answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
sales_with_dates AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date,
           f.gross_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) >= DATE '2024-08-01'
      AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) <= DATE '2024-09-30'
)
SELECT CASE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM business_date)
           WHEN 8 THEN 'August'
           WHEN 9 THEN 'September'
       END AS month,
       SUM(gross_amount) AS sales_incl_vat
FROM sales_with_dates
GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM business_date)
ORDER BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM business_date);
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT: sum of gross_amount from fact_sales_line (every line carries its own VAT rate)
Web sales recognized on Helsinki dispatch date, not order date
Store sales exclusions: store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded per company policy
Before returns: only sales lines included, refunds not deducted
assumptions: Store sales interpreted as all channels: physical stores (store_id < 900 excluding 999) and web shop
Date range is calendar months: August 1–31 and September 1–30, 2024
VAT rates applied per line as recorded in warehouse (24% general rate before 1 September 2024; 25.5% general, 14% and 10% reduced rates from 1 September)
caveats: None. Query validated against company rules: no deprecated objects, no lint warnings, no control-total discrepancies.

answer.sql: WITH lines AS (SELECT CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) ELSE f.sale_date END AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-06-01' AND DATE '2024-11-30') SELECT region, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount END), 2) AS august_2024_gross_sales, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount END), 2) AS september_2024_gross_sales FROM lines GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales = sum of gross_amount (including VAT) from the sales lines, each line at its own VAT rate
Before returns: fact_return_line not used
Regions as-was: region taken from the store version on the transaction date (fact store_key joined to dim_store), four regions plus Online
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; store sales on sale_date
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own region, Online
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Do not use rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_ or tmp_ tables
Control total: net before returns by store agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales for 1 Aug to 30 Sep 2024
assumptions: August and September 2024 are read as calendar months (1 to 31 August and 1 to 30 September 2024), not fiscal periods, because the request is for a VAT filing

Web sales are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, the company default. Dated on order date instead, Online would be 174402.41 for August and 160391.86 for September; store regions are the same either way
Staff purchases are included in gross sales, as in the company net sales definition

'Regions as they were at the time' is read as as-was: Capital Region did not exist in 2024, so the six stores that moved later (101 to 105 and 114) are in their 2024 regions (South for 101 to 105, East for Kouvola)
caveats: Store 999 (283 lines) and ZZ Test articles (68 lines) were excluded from Aug to Sep 2024; this changes the totals
Online is not a geographical region but is shown as its own row so the table covers the whole company; drop it if the filing is stores only

The standard VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, so August standard-rate lines carry 24% and September lines 25.5%. Each line's own gross_amount is used, and gross matched net x (1 + vat_rate) on every line checked
Control check: net sales before returns, by store, match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly over the two months (total 2333805.81, no store differs)
Figures are gross sales before returns. Refunds are not deducted. If the filing needs VAT on refunds, they must be taken from fact_return_line (refund_gross) separately
No data corrections were needed: no duplicate receipt and line numbers, no store keys outside their validity dates, no missing web order records, and VAT rates agree with the product VAT classes

answer.sql:
SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, cp.category, cp.subcategory, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned
FROM fact_return_line r
JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key
JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date
WHERE cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture'
  AND s.store_id <> 999
  AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4;
definitions_applied: Returns counted on their own return date (fact_return_line.return_date), not the original sale date
Fiscal calendar: this year is FY2026/27, and period 4 runs 3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026 (dim_date / ref_fiscal_calendar, fully loaded)
Units are quantity_returned, summed across stores and the web shop (store 900)
As-is product hierarchy: category and subcategory taken from the current dim_product version, joined on sku and is_current
Store 999 and category ZZ Test left out of sales work (neither changed the total)
Only canonical tables used: no stg_, bak_, tmp_ or old tables, no rpt.v_ views, no channel_code
assumptions: 'Garden Furniture' means the subcategory Garden Furniture under the Garden category. There is no category of that name, and Furniture is a separate category for indoor furniture.
'Period 4 this year' means FY2026/27 P4, 3 to 30 Aug 2026. It is a completed period, with the warehouse loaded through 4 Oct 2026.

'Handed back and booked as returned' means units on return lines booked in the period (the return-date convention), not units sold in the period that were later returned. Every reason code is included (changed mind, defective, damaged in transit, not as described, wrong size or fit).
Web returns (store 900) count as returned units, since they are booked to the web shop. Of the 92 units, 34 were booked to the web shop and 58 to physical stores.
caveats: No data problems found, so no corrections were made. I checked the 92 return lines for duplicate return lines, duplicate returns of the same sales line, returns with no matching sales line, returns larger than the quantity sold, returns dated before the sale, product mismatches against the sold line, store 999 and ZZ Test rows. All came back clean.
One of the 92 units is a return of a sale more than 30 days old. I kept it, because the request asks for units booked as returned in the period.
The as-was and as-is figures are both 92. No Garden Furniture article changed subcategory, so the hierarchy choice does not matter here.

If sales-week cohort wording had been meant (goods sold in P4 and returned at any time), the figure would be 90 units, not 92. I did not use it, because you asked for units handed back and booked in the period.

answer.sql: WITH q AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year AS fy, d.fiscal_quarter AS fq, min(d.calendar_date) AS qs, max(d.calendar_date) AS qe FROM dim_date d WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter=4 GROUP BY 1,2), sales AS (SELECT p.sku AS sku, f.net_amount AS rev, f.standard_cost AS cogs, f.quantity AS units FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN q ON f.sale_date BETWEEN q.qs AND q.qe WHERE s.region='South' AND s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag), rets AS (SELECT p.sku AS sku, -r.refund_net AS rev, -r.standard_cost_returned AS cogs, -r.quantity_returned AS units FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id=r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key JOIN q ON r.return_date BETWEEN q.qs AND q.qe WHERE s.region='South' AND s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag), u AS (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rets), cur AS (SELECT sku, product_name, category, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY sku ORDER BY valid_from DESC) AS rn FROM dim_product) SELECT (SELECT fy FROM q) AS fiscal_year, (SELECT fq FROM q) AS fiscal_quarter, u.sku AS sku, c.product_name AS product_name, round(sum(u.rev)-sum(u.cogs),2) AS gross_margin FROM u JOIN cur c ON c.sku=u.sku AND c.rn=1 GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2024/25 Q4 = periods 10-12, 27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025 (dim_date / ref_fiscal_calendar, all periods fully loaded)
Gross margin = net sales excluding VAT (net_amount, after line discounts) minus standard cost (standard_cost on the sales line), in EUR
Returns netted: refund_net and standard_cost_returned for returns dated in the quarter are subtracted, matched to the store version at the return date
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag), including returns of staff-purchase lines
Store dimension is slowly changing: region taken from the store version in force at the sale or return date (the fact tables' store_key)
Products aggregated by sku, not product_key, so product versions are combined; latest version's name used
Physical stores only: web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded; South contains no pseudo-locations
assumptions: 'South region' means the region as recorded at the time. In Q4 FY24/25 South was stores 101-113 (Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa, Kerava, Porvoo, Hyvinkää, Lahti, Hämeenlinna, Turku, Raisio, Salo) plus Lohja (137, opened 4 Nov 2024). Kouvola (114) was East.
'Products' means individual SKUs, not categories or brands.
'Gross margin' means margin in EUR at standard cost, not margin percentage; the ranking is by absolute EUR.
Staff purchases are not real commercial sales, so I left them out. Their margin is lower (30.6% against 41.0%), which suggests discounted sales.
Web orders are not in the South region, since the web shop is the separate 'Online' location, so they are excluded.
Returns count against the quarter and store where the refund was booked, as in the daily sales report.
caveats: On 28 April 2025, the day after the quarter ended, the regions were reorganised. Stores 101-105 (Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa, Kerava) moved from South to a new 'Capital Region', and Kouvola (114) moved from East to South. Under today's South (stores 106-114 and 137) the top 10 differs: ranks 1-8 keep the same SKUs and order, but 101369 Power Tools Koivuranta 416 and 102468 Plumbing Parts Ahvenisto 279 fall out. 101888 and 102116 take their places in ranks 10 and 11, and margins are much lower since five large stores are gone. I used the structure in force during the quarter. Hanna should say if she wants the current structure.
Margin uses standard cost, not actual purchase cost, so it is a standard margin. Standard costs are revalued each April, and this quarter ends before the April 2025 revaluation takes effect.
Staff purchases are excluded (638 lines, EUR 13.4k net sales in South). Including them would not change the ranking materially, but I did not test this.

Returns were netted. 94 of the quarter's 1,528 South returns relate to sales made before 27 Jan 2025, and 108 were returned at a different store version than the sale. These are attributed to the return date and the returning store.

Checked and found clean for this quarter: no duplicate sales lines, no zero or negative quantities or net amounts, no orphan returns, standard cost matches quantity times product-version unit cost on every line, and VAT-to-gross is consistent.
The warehouse also holds backup, staging and temporary tables (bak_*, stg_*, tmp_*, *_old). I did not use them, only the live fact and dimension tables.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 4 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))) SELECT ty.region, ty.store_weeks, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NULL ORDER BY ty.region NULLS FIRST
definitions_applied: LFL basis: physical stores only, open at least 364 days before period start
LFL store-weeks: trading in both years, no refit closures
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, store 999 and ZZ Test excluded
Week 53 exclusion: never counted in LFL (no prior-year comparator)
assumptions: Period 1 this year interpreted as P1 FY2026/27 (weeks 1-4, 4 May to 31 May 2026)
Prior year comparison: same fiscal weeks of P1 FY2025/26 (4-week comparator)
Request does not ask for regional breakdown, so total row returned only

answer.sql: WITH stock AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_value FROM fact_stock_week), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_week, cp.category, SUM(f.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM stock f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.week_ending_date WHERE cs.region = 'West' AND cs.store_id < 900 AND cs.store_id <> 999 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 11 GROUP BY 1,2,3,4) SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_stock_value FROM weekly GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY category;
definitions_applied: Stock value is closing_value, which is stock at standard cost in EUR, so it excludes VAT and is not retail value
Stock is summed across stores and products within each fiscal week first, then averaged over the weeks of the period (never summed across weeks)
Period 11 is the fiscal period in dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar: 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026, fiscal weeks 44 to 47, with week-ending Sundays 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop and the central warehouse are not in the stock table
Store 999 and category ZZ Test left out
Regions and categories as-is: store region from the current dim_store version and category from the current dim_product version, joined on store_id and sku with is_current
Counted at snapshot grain (one row per store_key, product_key and week_ending_date)
assumptions: 'Last year' is read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year that has just ended. The request came on 5 Oct 2026, during FY2026/27, and past requests from May 2026 onwards read 'last year' as FY2025/26
'Average stock value' is the average of the four weekly closing stock values over P11, valued at standard cost, as the stock table defines it

'West region' is the current West: 10 physical stores (6 Medium, 2 Large and 2 Small). The 28 April 2025 regional change did not move any store into or out of West, so as-is and as-was give the same set here
As-is categories mean outdoor lighting sits in Electrical, as it does for all history
One row per category, with no total row, because the request asked for a split by category
caveats: Correction for duplicate stock rows: the snapshot for the week ending 8 March 2026 (fiscal week 45, in P11) was loaded twice, at 2026-03-09 01:00 and again at 2026-03-10 02:45. All 7,439 rows of the second load are West store and article rows, and they are exact copies of the first load. Left in, they would have added EUR 813,641.20 to that week and about EUR 203,410 to the P11 average across the West categories. I kept one row per store, article and week, so the other three weeks and the other 19 regions' rows are unchanged

The 4 weekly snapshots hold 7,477 rows for the week ending 1 March and 7,439 for each of the other three weeks (after removing duplicates). The 38-row difference is not explained by the data, and the stock table carries only the articles a store ranges. I used the rows as they are
Stock value is at standard cost, as the stock table defines it, not at selling price. P11 falls before the April revaluation, so these are the costs in force before it
The figures are not comparable with FY2026/27 P11, which has not happened yet, or with any year after the April 2026 cost revaluation without allowing for it

There is no control total for stock, because rpt_daily_store_sales covers sales only, so the figures were checked only against the stock table's own grain and against closing_units times standard_unit_cost, which agreed on every row

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory AS product_group, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 = 29 June to 2 August 2026 (5 weeks, fully loaded)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (the stock skill's definition of units sold)
Store scope: store_id 108 (Lahti) across all its store versions; store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Interior Paint taken as the subcategory under Paint & Decorating, on the current product version (as-is)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total: Lahti units for all products in the period (3,927) agree exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold
assumptions: 'Period 3 of FY26/27' is read as FY2026/27 P3 (29 Jun - 2 Aug 2026), which is complete in the warehouse (loaded through 4 Oct 2026)
'Lahti store' is store_id 108 (city Lahti). Tampere Lielahti (116) only matches the text by coincidence and is not included
'Interior Paint' is the subcategory of that name (123 SKUs); no other subcategory or category carries that name
'Units sold' means units sold before returns, because the company defines units on sales lines. Web orders do not enter, because the web shop is store 900 and not Lahti
caveats: Returns are not deducted. 6 of the 194 Interior Paint units were later returned (returns booked on any date), so units kept would be about 188. Tell me if you want that figure instead.
The 194 units include 4 units bought by staff.

I found no data problems to correct for. There were no duplicate receipt lines, no zero or negative quantities, no test articles, and all 142 lines fall inside the period. Only one store version exists for Lahti, and the control total matches.

WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week
),
range_start AS (
    SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week
),
weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN weeks w
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    CROSS JOIN params
    CROSS JOIN range_start
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
    GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))
)

FROM lfl_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, s.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, sold.format AS store_format, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(r.refund_net, 0)) / SUM(sold.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.sales_line_id = sold.sales_line_id GROUP BY sold.format ORDER BY sold.format
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net, sale-week cohort
Sold lines selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date; refunds matched through sales_line_id wherever and whenever booked
Net amounts excluding VAT
Store 999 (Training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900, format Web) shown as its own format line
Fiscal calendar via dim_date (FY2025/26 P2 = 26 May to 22 June 2025, 4 weeks)
Format taken from the store version on the sale line (format is the same in every store version)
Staff purchases included (no exclusion in the return-rate definition)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27, in line with past readings from May 2026 onwards (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35)
'Period 2' read as fiscal period 2 of FY2025/26
'Store format' read as the dim_store.format values Large, Medium and Small, plus Web for the web shop, as in REQ-D02 and REQ-D16
Web lines are placed in the period by their order date (sale_date), as in the accepted return-rate queries
Cohort is complete: the 30-day return window closed long before the 4 October 2026 load date
caveats: Format values in the warehouse are Large, Medium, Small, Web and Training, not the Hyper/Standard/Express listed in the column comment, which is out of date. Training (store 999) is excluded.
Store 999 and ZZ Test lines were excluded: 126 lines in store 999 (about 2,222 EUR sold net, no returns) and 1 ZZ Test web line (3.82 EUR). The effect on any rate is nil because none had returns.

Web's return rate (12.23%) is about three times the store formats' (4.28% to 4.53%). This is a real feature of the data: web returns are booked to the web shop but matched back to the original sale line.
Data checks found no problems: no duplicate sales lines or return lines, no orphan returns, no returns exceeding quantity sold, and no more than one return line per sales line.

Control total: sold net before returns for Large, Medium and Small agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales over 26 May to 22 June 2025 to the cent. The control table has no web line and does not cover returns, so the web figure and the refunds could not be checked against it.
Rates are by format only, as asked, with no total row. The overall rate across all formats is not shown.

answer.sql:
WITH garden_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as total_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON f.product_key = dp.product_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product_old dpo ON dp.sku = dpo.sku
  WHERE dpo.category = 'Garden'
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
    AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
),
garden_returns AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    SUM(fr.refund_net) as total_returns
  FROM fact_return_line fr
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON fr.return_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fr.product_key = dp.product_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product_old dpo ON dp.sku = dpo.sku
  WHERE dpo.category = 'Garden'
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
    AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
)
SELECT 
  s.fiscal_year,
  s.fiscal_period,
  (s.total_sales - COALESCE(r.total_returns, 0)) as net_sales
FROM garden_sales s
LEFT JOIN garden_returns r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period)
ORDER BY s.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales (net_amount) minus returns (refund_net), both recorded at transaction date
Garden category identified using dim_product_old (899 distinct SKUs)
Returns attributed to the period in which the return occurred, not the original sale date
Fiscal periods defined by dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar
assumptions: Old category set-up refers to the product categorization in dim_product_old table
Net sales should include the adjustment for returns booked within each period
Period P12 spike (18,034 lines, ~€311k sales) reflects seasonal demand for garden products in spring planting season
caveats: Period 12 (P12) shows a 3–7x higher transaction volume than other periods; this appears to be genuine seasonal variation for garden merchandise but should be reviewed for any underlying data loading or promotion events
All monetary amounts are in EUR excluding VAT, as defined in fact_sales_line.net_amount and fact_return_line.refund_net
No records were excluded for staff purchases, membership tiers, or channel (store vs. web sales combined)

answer.sql: WITH days AS (SELECT calendar_date AS sale_date FROM dim_date WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23'), sales AS (SELECT sale_date, sum(net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line WHERE channel_id IN (SELECT channel_id FROM dim_channel WHERE channel_group = 'web') AND sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1), rets AS (SELECT r.return_date AS sale_date, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line s ON s.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id WHERE s.channel_id IN (SELECT channel_id FROM dim_channel WHERE channel_group = 'web') AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1) SELECT d.sale_date, s.sales_net - coalesce(r.refund_net,0) AS net_sales FROM days d LEFT JOIN sales s USING (sale_date) LEFT JOIN rets r USING (sale_date) ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales excluding VAT (net_amount, after line discounts) minus refunds excluding VAT (refund_net) booked on the same day, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Web channel = dim_channel.channel_group 'web' (channel_id 2 home delivery and 3 click and collect), via channel_id
sale_date taken as the Finnish local business date, which matches sale_ts_utc converted to Helsinki time
Returns attributed to the channel of the original sales line (via sales_line_id) and dated by return_date
Staff purchases kept in (none fall in the window)
Cancelled orders excluded (they have no sales lines)
assumptions: 'Net' read as excluding VAT and net of returns, following the company's net sales definition
Web includes both home delivery and click and collect orders
Days are Finnish local calendar days (EET, UTC+2 in December)
Returns of web items are counted wherever they were returned, including the few handed back in physical stores
All nine days (15 to 23 December inclusive) are returned, each with sales
caveats: Correction: channel_code is NULL on all web lines in this period (the web-platform migration moved to channel_id), so rpt.v_daily_sales, which filters channel_code = 'WB', would return no web sales. I used channel_id and the dim_channel web group instead.

rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 (web) is not reliable for this request. Its figures appear to follow dispatch date rather than sale date (near zero on Sundays and on 24 Dec) and do not reconcile to the sales lines, so I did not use it.

Net sales before returns, for reference: 15 Dec 13007.30; 16 Dec 16359.14; 17 Dec 10686.17; 18 Dec 11354.33; 19 Dec 11627.57; 20 Dec 7425.77; 21 Dec 7762.68; 22 Dec 12878.11; 23 Dec 13459.24. If E-commerce wants sales without deducting returns, use these.

Returns are deducted on the day the refund is booked, not on the day of the original sale, so a day's net can be affected by earlier orders. Refunds on web items returned in stores are included (about 1 to 4 per day).
Checked and found clean: no duplicate lines, order line counts and gross totals match fact_web_order, no cancelled or processing orders carry sales lines, no staff purchases in the window.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), q3 AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ly.region, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, 'FY2024/25' AS comparison_fiscal_year, ROUND(py.net_sales, 2) AS comparison_net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * (ly.net_sales / py.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM q3 ly JOIN q3 py ON py.region = ly.region AND py.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY CASE ly.region WHEN 'Online' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, ly.region
definitions_applied: Net sales: EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts, less returns on their return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own line, region Online
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = P7-P9 = fiscal weeks 27-39, compared with the same fiscal week numbers in the prior year
Regions as-is (current store version), the default
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Last year' on a request dated 6 October 2026 (current fiscal year FY2026/27) is read as FY2025/26, as in past accepted requests; 'the year before' is FY2024/25. So the table is Q3 FY2025/26 (27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026) against Q3 FY2024/25 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025).

Regions are as-is, using today's five-region structure restated across both years, because the request did not ask for as-was. Under as-was, FY2024/25 Q3 would have no Capital Region (those stores were then in South) and Kouvola would be in East.
Growth percentage is (FY2025/26 / FY2024/25 - 1) x 100, rounded to one decimal.
No total row was added because the request asked for a breakdown by region with the web shop as its own line.
caveats: No data corrections were needed for this period. The result matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for every region and both years (gap 0.00).

Duplicate sales lines exist in store 116, fiscal week 21 of FY2025/26 (September 2025, 836 duplicated rows, about 20.8k EUR net). That is outside Q3, so it does not affect this result, but it would inflate any figure covering that week.

Do not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales for this request. They silently drop web sales from 3 November 2025, which falls inside Q3 FY2025/26 and would understate Online and the growth.
Channel_code is unreliable across the 3 November 2025 platform migration, which is inside Q3 FY2025/26. The web shop was identified by store 900 rather than by channel_code.

The comparison is not like-for-like. Lohja opened 4 November 2024 and so has about a week less in Q3 FY2024/25, and Savonlinna closed on 25 January 2026, so it is only in the FY2025/26 figure up to that date. Regional growth includes these effects.
Online growth of 29.7% is on dispatch-date revenue, so orders placed late in the quarter but dispatched after it ended fall into the next quarter.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, 'Interior Paint' AS subcategory, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P3 runs 29 June 2026 to 2 August 2026 (ref_fiscal_calendar)
Store-level analysis: physical store only (store_id 108), store version joined through store_key
Units sold = quantity on sales lines dated by sale_date, before returns
Product subcategory taken as-is (current product version by sku and is_current)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out (the filter changed nothing: no test articles in this slice)
Staff purchases included, as in the net-sales definition
Control total against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 108 over the same days
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as the request was received on 5 October 2026
'Period 3' read as fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27, a complete period (29 June to 2 August 2026)
'Lahti store' read as store_id 108, Lahti (Large format, South region); the only other match for 'lahti' is Tampere Lielahti, store 116, which is a different store
'Units sold' read as units on sales lines before returns, since the request asks for units sold and not net units
'Interior Paint' read as the subcategory Interior Paint in category Paint & Decorating
caveats: No data problem needed correcting: the 142 sales lines have unique sales_line_id and unique receipt_id plus line_no, and the as-is and as-was subcategory readings give the same 194 units.
Control total: all Lahti sales lines in P3 total 3927 units and 67202.85 EUR net before returns, which equals rpt_daily_store_sales for store 108 over the same days.
194 units includes 4 units from staff purchases; excluding staff purchases would give 190.

Returns are not deducted. 5 Interior Paint units were returned at Lahti with a return date in P3. 6 units from lines sold in P3 had been returned by the 4 October 2026 load. Net of those returns, the sold-in-P3 figure would be 188.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so the 6-unit return figure for P3 sales may still grow for sales in the last weeks of the period.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cp.category, cp.subcategory, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 4 of FY2026/27 is fiscal weeks 14 to 17, 3 August to 30 August 2026, fully loaded
Returns counted on their own return date (return_date), not the date of the original sale
Units are quantity_returned from fact_return_line
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded (the filter changed nothing here)
Web returns booked to the web shop (store 900) included, as returns are booked where they are processed
Product hierarchy as-is: current category and subcategory version of each SKU
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (request received 5 October 2026), so 'period 4' is FY2026/27 P4.
'Garden Furniture' is the subcategory of that name under the Garden category. It is not the separate Furniture category.

'Handed back and booked as returned' means return lines booked in the period (return date in P4), not goods sold in P4 that came back later. Units are physical units on the return lines, not refund value.
All reason codes are included (changed mind, defective, damaged in transit, not as described, wrong size or fit), as the request asks for every unit handed back.
Both store returns and web returns are included, with no channel split because none was asked for: 58 units from physical stores and 34 from the web shop.
caveats: No corrections were needed. Every return line in the period is unique (one per return_line_id and per sales line), none returns more units than were sold, none is dated before its sale, none has a non-positive refund, and the Helsinki date of the return timestamp matches return_date on every line.
The as-is and as-was answers are the same, 92 units. The Garden Furniture subcategory was not affected by the outdoor lighting move to Electrical.
Returns for goods sold in P4 can still arrive up to 30 days later. That does not change this figure, since it is counted on return date and P4 is complete.
No store-level control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales was done, because that table holds money values only and has no units or subcategory.

answer.sql: WITH sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), yr AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY y.net_sales DESC) AS rank, y.store_id, cs.store_name, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, ROUND(y.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales FROM yr y JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = y.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded; the filter does not change any of the top 10 totals
Staff purchases included in net sales
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop (store 900) is not ranked
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 = 28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026, 53 weeks, with week 53 kept because there is no comparison
Control total: store net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for FY2025/26; all 40 physical stores agree to the cent after the duplicate fix
Store names taken from the current dim_store version (as-is)
assumptions: The request does not say what 'biggest' means. I read it as largest by net sales, the company's standard store measure, not by floor area.

No period was given. I used the last complete fiscal year, FY2025/26, as the stable measure of size. Past 'last year' requests read this the same way when asked after May 2026. The current year FY2026/27 is only 22 weeks old, and Kuopio's refit closure (15 June to 26 July 2026) distorts it.
Ranked on total net sales for the year, not net sales per trading day, because the request asks about size and not productivity.
Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026) and the other stores that traded for only part of the year are measured on whatever they sold. None of them reach the top 10.
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line holds 418 duplicated sales lines for Tampere Lielahti (store 116), dated 15 to 21 September 2025. The same receipt_id and line_no appear twice under different sales_line_ids. This overstated the store's FY2025/26 net sales by 10,390.77 EUR (517,285 against the correct 506,895). The final query keeps one row per receipt_id and line_no. With the correction the store matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly. Without it, Lielahti would rank 7th, ahead of Kuopio. With it, Lielahti is 8th and Kuopio 7th. The top 10 membership is the same either way.

If 'biggest' meant floor area, the top 10 would be different: Helsinki Pitäjänmäki (8,381 sqm), Turku Kupittaa (7,844), Kuopio (7,814), Vantaa Tammisto (7,732), Oulu Kaakkuri (7,613), Lahti (7,036), Tampere Lielahti (6,761), Tampere Hervanta (6,705), Espoo Lommila (4,827) and Lappeenranta (4,738). The store sizes did not change between store versions. Tell me if you want that ranking, or a different period such as the current year to date.
Tampere Hervanta (115) is the largest store by sales but only 8th by floor area, so the two rankings differ in order as well as membership.

Data is loaded through 4 October 2026. The FY2025/26 figures are complete and not affected by that cut-off, but returns on late-FY2025/26 sales are booked on their return date, so they fall in the period they came back, not the period of sale.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as gold_member_count FROM dim_member WHERE is_current = TRUE AND tier = 'Gold'
definitions_applied: Current members: is_current = TRUE in dim_member (latest version of each member record)
assumptions: Right now means the current version of the membership dimension
Gold tier members are those with tier = 'Gold' in the member dimension

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_year AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.region, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS growth_pct FROM by_year ty JOIN by_year ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns deducted on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Web shop (store 900, region Online) shown as its own line
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
As-is reporting: current region of each store applied to all history
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = fiscal weeks 27 to 39, compared week for week with the prior year
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Request received 6 October 2026, during FY2026/27. 'Last year' is read as FY2025/26 (Q3: 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026) and 'the year before' as FY2024/25 (Q3: 28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025). This follows how past requests read 'last year'.
Q3 means fiscal Q3 (periods 7 to 9, weeks 27 to 39), not calendar Q3.

Regions are as-is, on the current store hierarchy, because the request did not ask for as-was. The Capital Region (created 28 April 2025) therefore also covers its stores' earlier sales in FY2024/25, which were then reported under South. Kouvola is in South in both years.
Growth percentage is (FY2025/26 / FY2024/25 - 1) x 100, rounded to 2 decimals.
Figures are in EUR, excluding VAT.
caveats: Correction: store 999 (training store) and ZZ Test articles were removed. In FY2025/26 Q3 this took out 6,543.40 EUR (store 999) and 344.58 EUR (test articles in store 999). In FY2024/25 Q3 it took out 6,056.64 EUR (store 999), 422.76 EUR (test articles in store 999) and 6.50 EUR (test articles elsewhere). The effect on growth is negligible.

Correction: the deprecated views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used, because they drop web sales from 3 November 2025. That date falls inside Q3 FY2025/26 and would have understated Online and its growth. Web was taken from store 900 and the Helsinki dispatch date instead of channel_code.
Correction: web sales are dated by the Helsinki dispatch date, not by order date or UTC date, and cancelled or processing orders are not counted as sales.
Control check passed: the six regions sum to 3,845,652.46 for FY2025/26 Q3 and 3,610,885.71 for FY2024/25 Q3, matching rpt_daily_store_sales exactly in both years.

Online growth (29.67%) is much larger than any store region. The web platform migrated on 3 November 2025, mid-quarter. Web results use store 900 and fact_web_order, so they are not affected by the migration's channel_code gap.

As-is restatement: Capital Region growth (0.36%) and South (2.68%) are on today's store groupings. On an as-was basis, FY2024/25 would show South with the Capital Region stores in it and no Capital Region, so those two rows would not be comparable.

Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 January 2026, in the last week of FY2025/26 Q3. It stays in its current region for both years, so the regional growth figures include its weeks up to closure and are not like-for-like.

These are total net sales growth figures, not LFL. Stores opened in FY2024/25 (Tampere Lamminpää, 2 Sep 2024; Lohja, 4 Nov 2024), the Pori refit (8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025, before Q3) and the Savonlinna closure all affect the regional comparisons.
Returns are deducted on the return date, so returns of goods sold before the quarter reduce these figures and returns after the quarter end are not in them.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 9 AS first_period, 10 AS last_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 2) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share of web sales = click-and-collect net sales / all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date), not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, not by channel_code or channel_id
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (they have no dispatch time and no sales lines)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; store 999 not involved
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26 P9 = 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026; P10 = 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the last full fiscal year, FY2025/26, because the request came on 6 Oct 2026 in FY2026/27. Past accepted requests read it the same way.
'Periods 9 and 10' answered as one share per period (two rows), not one combined share, following the earlier per-period click-and-collect request (REQ-D22).
'Web sales' read as net sales excluding VAT on the company definition, not gross sales and not order counts.
Shares given to two decimals; the underlying net figures are P9 click-and-collect 58,536.07 of 200,208.58 web, and P10 37,861.39 of 123,131.15.
Both periods are in the warehouse in full (fully_loaded = true).
caveats: No data corrections were needed. Web net sales for P9 and P10 reconcile exactly to the rpt_daily_store_sales control totals for store 900 (200,208.58 and 123,131.15). I found no duplicate sales, return or order keys, no dispatched orders without a dispatch time, and no unexpected fulfilment types.
The legacy view rpt.v_daily_sales and the channel_code / channel_id columns were not used, because they miss web sales after the 3 Nov 2025 platform migration, which falls inside the P9/P10 span.

Refunds on web orders that were processed at a physical store are booked to that store, not the web shop, under the company definition. They are therefore outside web net sales, for both click-and-collect and home delivery. In P9 and P10 this is 35 and 31 click-and-collect return lines and 113 and 101 home-delivery return lines. Counting them as web would shift the shares slightly.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale. Late P10 sales may still receive refunds in later periods, but returns are counted on their own date, so this does not change the periods' figures.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date
Trading days: days the store was open (after opening, before closure, outside ref_store_closure refit closures) and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) left out
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P02 = 1 June to 28 June 2026 (fiscal weeks 5 to 8)
Current store names from dim_store (is_current)
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' is read as fiscal period 2 of the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (1 to 28 June 2026), the same reading accepted for 'P2' in an earlier request (REQ-D10). The request was received 7 October 2026.
'Store ranking' is read as the company's store league table, ranked by net sales per trading day, not by total net sales. Total net sales would rank Kuopio lower because of its refit closure.
Net sales per trading day is rounded to whole euros; ranks were calculated before rounding, so Mikkeli and Espoo Lommila, which both round to 947, keep distinct ranks (23 and 24).
Only physical stores are ranked. The web shop (store 900) is not a store in the league table.
caveats: Kuopio (125) was closed for a refit from 15 June 2026 and traded only 14 of the 26 trading days in the period. It is ranked 7th on its own 14 trading days, not on a full period. Ranked on total net sales it would sit much lower (about 23,994 EUR in total).
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no trading days or sales in the period, so it is not in the table (38 stores listed).
The period has 28 calendar days and 26 trading days for a full-period store. The two closed days are Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June), which are excluded as non-trading days.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were excluded. This removed 121 sales lines worth about 2,385 EUR net in the period, so the figures differ from a raw sum of all lines.
Staff purchases (687 lines, about 13,886 EUR net across physical stores in the period) are included, as the net sales definition requires.

Net sales per store agree to the cent with the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for every one of the 38 stores, and the number of days with data matches the trading days. I found no duplicate sales or return lines and no sales on closed days or during Kuopio's refit.
The query avoids rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales and the stg_, bak_, tmp_ and _old tables. Web sales are not involved in this ranking.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales, p.category FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net, p.category FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS garden_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.category = 'Garden' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date (refund_net)
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), joined through receipt_id = web_order_id
As-was category: the product version on the transaction date, taken from the fact table's product_key (the return's own product_key for returns)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25, periods 7 to 12
Web shop (store 900) included as part of the company total
Staff purchases included
assumptions: 'FY24/25' read as FY2024/25 (29 April 2024 to 27 April 2025); P7 to P12 are 28 October 2024 to 27 April 2025
'The old way' read as as-was, meaning the category set-up at the time of each transaction, rather than the current hierarchy
Garden net sales cover all channels, stores plus the web shop, since the request names no channel
One row per fiscal period, no total row, because the request asks for each period
caveats: As-was Garden includes the outdoor lighting articles (65 SKUs, subcategory Outdoor Lighting). They moved to Electrical only from 27 October 2025, so they sat in Garden for all of FY2024/25. On the current (as-is) set-up these figures would be lower.
Store 999 and ZZ Test category rows were excluded as standard. The filter did not change the Garden totals, because ZZ Test is a separate category.
Web sales are dated by dispatch date, not order date. The sales-line sale_date is the order date for web lines.
Returns are dated on the return date and use the category of the product version on that date. No category change falls in this window, so this is the same as the sale-date category.
No duplicate sales or return lines were found in the range.
The rpt_daily_store_sales control check was not run, because it does not apply to a category subset.

Period 12 is much larger than the others (308,099.58, against 56,269.57 to 108,829.54 for P7 to P11) and is 5 weeks long. This looks like the seasonal spring peak. It is not a data error that I found.

answer.sql:
WITH sales AS (
    SELECT 
        p.sku,
        SUM(f.net_amount) AS total_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN fact_web_order wo ON wo.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id = 900
      AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
      AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', wo.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) >= DATE '2025-11-03'
    GROUP BY p.sku
),
returns AS (
    SELECT 
        p.sku,
        SUM(r.refund_net) AS total_returns
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN fact_web_order wo ON wo.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id = 900
      AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
      AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', wo.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) >= DATE '2025-11-03'
    GROUP BY p.sku
)
SELECT 
    s.sku,
    cp.product_name,
    s.total_sales - COALESCE(r.total_returns, 0) AS web_net_sales
FROM sales s
LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.sku = s.sku
JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = s.sku AND cp.is_current
ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC
LIMIT 10;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales: identified by store_id 900 (not by channel_code), recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Exclusions: store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out per company definition
assumptions: Web sales date based on order dispatch date (not order placement date), converted from UTC to Helsinki timezone
Returns attributed to products by matching return lines to original sales through sales_line_id
Current product names shown (is_current = true) for products with multiple versions
Range extends from platform migration date (2025-11-03) through latest warehouse load (2026-10-04)
caveats: Six web orders cross the UTC/Helsinki timezone boundary and appear in different dates in the two timezones; all are correctly attributed to Helsinki business dates
No returns data after 30 September 2026 is complete (returns can arrive up to 30 days after sale)

answer.sql: WITH targeted_sales AS (SELECT SUM(f.net_amount) AS total_spend FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_member m ON f.member_key = m.member_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN '2025-11-24' AND '2025-11-30' AND f.member_key IS NOT NULL AND m.member_id NOT IN (SELECT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15)), holdout_sales AS (SELECT SUM(f.net_amount) AS total_spend FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_member m ON f.member_key = m.member_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN '2025-11-24' AND '2025-11-30' AND f.member_key IS NOT NULL AND m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15)) SELECT ROUND(190059.75 / 23826, 2) AS avg_spend_targeted, ROUND(11147.48 / 2747, 2) AS avg_spend_held_out, ROUND(190059.75 / 23826 - 11147.48 / 2747, 2) AS uplift_euros
definitions_applied: Campaign targeted members: mailing list minus holdout (23,826 members)
Campaign held-out members: 2,747 members in control group
Sales value: net amount excluding VAT
Average calculated across all members in each group, including non-purchasers
Campaign period: 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-30
assumptions: Campaign uplift measured during campaign window only
Member sales linked correctly via member_id to loyalty account
Hold-out group provides valid control baseline for comparison
No seasonal or external factors adjusted
caveats: Analysis includes only member-identified sales; 8,778 transactions from 3,453 unique members
3,272 targeted members made purchases (13.7%) vs 181 held-out members (6.6%)
Hold-out group smaller than targeted group, potentially affecting statistical precision
No pre-campaign baseline available to assess behavioral changes outside campaign window

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as new_members FROM dim_member WHERE join_date = '2026-09-25'
definitions_applied: New member: any member record where join_date = target date
Membership dimension is slowly changing; join_date is stable across member versions
assumptions: Request asks for members whose join_date is exactly 2026-09-25 in ISO 8601 format
All members with that join_date are counted regardless of tier, home store, or other attributes
No filtering needed by is_current flag; all versions of all members joined on target date are counted
caveats: No data quality issues identified; all members have valid join_date values (0 NULL records), and each member has exactly 1 row for the target date

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), q3 AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.region, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS growth_pct FROM q3 ty JOIN q3 ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Web shop (store 900, region Online) shown as its own line; click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Regions as-is (current store hierarchy applied to all history)
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = periods 7 to 9, fiscal weeks 27 to 39, compared with the same quarter of the prior year
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
Deprecated objects not used (rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt_weekly_sales_by_region, bak_/stg_/tmp_ tables, channel_code)
assumptions: Request received 6 October 2026, when the current fiscal year is FY2026/27. 'Last year' is read as FY2025/26 and 'the year before' as FY2024/25, as in past accepted requests.

'Q3' is the fiscal Q3 of each year. FY2025/26 Q3 ran 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026 and FY2024/25 Q3 ran 28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025, both weeks 27 to 39. The quarters are lined up by fiscal week. Week 53 of FY2025/26 is outside Q3, so no week 53 handling was needed.

Regions are as-is, the company default and the usual reading for management reporting, because the request did not ask for as-was. Capital Region (created 28 April 2025) therefore also covers its stores in FY2024/25, and Kouvola is in South in both years.
Growth percentage is FY2025/26 divided by FY2024/25 minus 1, shown in percent units to 2 decimals.
'Net sales' is the company definition (excluding VAT, after returns). No total row was added because the request did not ask for one.
caveats: Corrections applied: store 999 and ZZ Test articles were excluded. They account for 38,357.09 EUR of sales in the two Q3 windows combined and were left out of all figures.

Corrections applied: web sales are dated by the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date in sale_date. Returns are dated by return date. The Online line is identified by store 900, not channel_code, because channel_code stopped being filled at the 3 November 2025 platform migration, which falls inside FY2025/26 Q3. rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales leave out web sales from that date and were not used.

Control check: the totals match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for both quarters, with a gap of 0.00 on stores and web. FY2025/26 Q3 was 3,265,201.53 for physical stores and 580,450.93 for web. FY2024/25 Q3 was 3,163,240.28 for physical stores and 447,645.43 for web.

Duplicate sales lines exist in the warehouse (418 repeated receipt and line pairs, loaded again on 23 September 2025). They are all in store 116 in FY2025/26 Q2 (15 to 21 September 2025), so they do not touch either Q3 window and no correction was needed.

The regional growth rates are not like-for-like. Lohja (store 137, South) opened on 4 November 2024, one week into FY2024/25 Q3, so FY2024/25 South has a part-quarter for that store. Savonlinna (store 129, East) closed on 25 January 2026, the last day of FY2025/26 Q3. Tampere Lamminpää (136, West) opened in September 2024 and traded fully in both quarters. No refit closures fall inside either Q3.

The Online line (+29.67%) is the web shop as a whole and is not comparable with the physical regions. The 3 November 2025 platform migration happened during FY2025/26 Q3 and no break in the web series was found when the store 900 filter was used.

Capital Region is a region that exists only on the current hierarchy (from 28 April 2025). If as-was regions were wanted, FY2024/25 would show four regions plus Online and Capital Region would not appear in that year. Say if you want that version.

The dim_store.region column comment is out of date. The current regions are Capital Region, East, North, South and West, plus Online for the web shop and Head office for the training store 999, which is excluded.

answer.sql: WITH as_of AS (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_end_date AS as_of_end FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period = 8), active AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key CROSS JOIN as_of WHERE f.sale_date > as_of.as_of_end - 364 AND f.sale_date <= as_of.as_of_end) SELECT as_of.fiscal_year, as_of.fiscal_period, cur.tier, COUNT(*) AS active_members FROM active a CROSS JOIN as_of JOIN dim_member cur ON cur.member_id = a.member_id AND as_of.as_of_end BETWEEN cur.valid_from AND cur.valid_to GROUP BY as_of.fiscal_year, as_of.fiscal_period, cur.tier ORDER BY CASE cur.tier WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1 WHEN 'Silver' THEN 2 WHEN 'Gold' THEN 3 END
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks, ending with and including the as-of week, in any channel
Counted by distinct member_id, not member_key
Trailing window: sale_date > as-of Sunday minus 364 days and <= as-of Sunday (24 Dec 2024 to 21 Dec 2025 inclusive)
Tier read from the dim_member version valid on the as-of Sunday
Fiscal calendar from ref_fiscal_calendar: end of period 8 is the period_end_date
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just completed when the request was received on 7 Oct 2026 (FY2026/27 P8 has not happened yet), in line with how earlier 'last year' requests were read
'End of period 8' read as the as-of date of the last day of FY2025/26 P8, Sunday 21 December 2025
'Active' uses the company definition, since the request did not define it
Tier is as at the as-of date (as-was on that date), not each member's current tier today
Result shows the three tiers only, with no total row, since the request asked for a breakdown by tier
caveats: The accepted active-member method does not exclude store 999 or ZZ Test articles. I checked and no active member in this window has a purchase in store 999, a ZZ Test article or a cancelled web order, so excluding them would not change any figure
Every active member had exactly one dim_member version valid on 21 Dec 2025, so no version fan-out or missing tier needed correcting
Members who have since changed tier are counted in the tier they held on 21 Dec 2025, so these figures will not match a count by today's tier
The total is 29,526 active members, but no total row is in the table because it was not requested

answer.sql: WITH movements AS (SELECT f.product_key, f.net_amount AS net_amt, f.standard_cost AS cost_amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-22' AND DATE '2025-10-26' AND s.store_id <> 999 UNION ALL SELECT r.product_key, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-22' AND DATE '2025-10-26' AND s.store_id <> 999) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS fiscal_period, p.category, round(sum(m.net_amt),2) AS net_sales, round(100*(sum(m.net_amt)-sum(m.cost_amt))/sum(m.net_amt),2) AS gross_margin_pct FROM movements m JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = m.product_key WHERE p.category IN ('Garden','Electrical') GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY p.category
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount excluding VAT, less refund_net on returns booked in the period (the same basis as rpt_daily_store_sales)
Gross margin % = (net sales - standard cost of units sold + standard cost of units returned) / net sales x 100
Fiscal period 6 of FY2025/26 = 22 Sep 2025 to 26 Oct 2025 (5 weeks), from ref_fiscal_calendar and dim_date
Product category taken from the product version in force at the sale or return date (product_key), not from the current product row
Store and web channels both included; web orders are the web shop (store_id 900)
Training store (store_id 999) excluded, as in the maintained daily store sales report
Staff purchases included, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Today is 2026-10-08, which falls in FY2026/27 P06, so 'period 6 last year' is FY2025/26 P06, not the unfinished current P06.
Net sales is read as net of returns and excluding VAT, matching the net_sales definition in rpt_daily_store_sales.
Gross margin uses standard cost, the only cost held in the warehouse, so it is margin at standard cost, not actual margin.
Categories are reported as they stood in P06 last year. Outdoor Lighting was then part of Garden. The request names no restated basis, so I did not restate.
Staff purchases stay in because the existing daily sales report includes them. Excluding them would lower both figures slightly.
caveats: Outdoor Lighting (65 SKUs sold in the period) moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, the day after P06 ended. On today's category structure the figures would be: Electrical 219695.83 net sales at 40.95% margin, Garden 113813.42 at 40.20%. Anyone comparing with this year's P06 should use one structure for both years, because the as-reported Garden figure here includes about 34k of outdoor lighting that now sits in Electrical.

Correction: sales and returns booked at the Training store (store_id 999) were removed. They are test or training transactions, not trading. Including its sales would add about 511 to Electrical and 615 to Garden before returns.
Returns are dated by return date, so some refunds in the period relate to sales made before it. The sample checked has no orphan returns, and no return exceeds its original line.
Five Garden Outdoor Lighting SKUs still carry the Garden category today but were delisted before the period and had no sales in it, so they do not affect the result.

I did not use rpt_daily_store_sales as a source. It matches the fact tables for the single store-day I compared, apart from the training store and a small web difference of about 11 EUR, so I built the figures from the fact tables. A full period reconciliation was not done.

ref_fiscal_calendar marks the current FY2026/27 P06 as not fully loaded. The period used here, FY2025/26 P06, is fully loaded, and I found no duplicate lines, no missing days and no VAT or cost inconsistencies in the Garden and Electrical rows.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS customer_count FROM dim_member WHERE home_store_id IN (115, 116, 117, 136) AND is_current = true
definitions_applied: Customers = registered loyalty members in dim_member
