Tampere = retail stores with store_id in (115, 116, 117, 136); excludes web shop (900) and training store (999)
Current members only (is_current = true) - standard practice to exclude inactive/lapsed members
assumptions: Interpreted 'customers in Tampere' as members whose home_store is in Tampere, not customers who have visited Tampere stores
Counted only current/active members, excluding lapsed members (is_current = false)
caveats: This count includes members whose home store is Tampere but who may not have made recent purchases (3,244 inactive members with Tampere home store exist in the historical data)
If the requester meant customers who have actively shopped in Tampere, the count would be 11,967 (distinct members with any transaction at Tampere stores)
Web shop sign-ups (store_id 900) are excluded; if online-Tampere customers are wanted, that would need to be evaluated separately

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT web_order_id) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Business date is the Finnish (Europe/Helsinki) calendar date, not the UTC date
Web order means one row in fact_web_order, counted by distinct web_order_id
Placed orders include cancelled ones, because an order that is cancelled was still placed
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is Monday 1 December 2025, as the request states, and dim_date confirms it is a Monday and a trading day
The day is read in Finnish local time (UTC+2 in December), so it runs from 2025-11-30 22:00 UTC to 2025-12-01 22:00 UTC
Cancelled orders are counted, since the request asks how many were placed rather than fulfilled
caveats: Order timestamps are stored in UTC. Filtering on the UTC date gives 291 orders, which is 54 too few, because those orders were placed in the Finnish evening and early morning. I corrected for this by converting to Helsinki time.
The 345 orders include 19 cancelled ones. Excluding them gives 326 (239 delivered and 87 collected).
The 19 cancelled orders have no lines in fact_sales_line, so a count of web receipts in the sales table would give 326 rather than 345.

fact_sales_line.channel_code is NULL for these December 2025 web lines, so a filter on channel_code = 'WB' returns no rows for the day. The channel_id column identifies them instead (2 for delivered orders, 3 for collected orders).
Order ids are unique, with no duplicate orders found for the day.

answer.sql: WITH wk AS (SELECT calendar_date, fiscal_year, fiscal_week FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_period = 2 AND fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27','FY2025/26')), sales AS (SELECT w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, sum(f.net_amount) AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN wk w ON w.calendar_date = f.sale_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY 1,2), rets AS (SELECT w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, sum(x.refund_net) AS amt FROM fact_return_line x JOIN wk w ON w.calendar_date = x.return_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = x.store_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY 1,2), net AS (SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_week, s.amt - coalesce(r.amt,0) AS net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN rets r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_week)) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, t.fiscal_week, round(t.net_sales,2) AS net_sales_this_year, round(l.net_sales,2) AS net_sales_last_year, round((t.net_sales / l.net_sales - 1) * 100, 1) AS growth_pct FROM net t JOIN net l ON l.fiscal_week = t.fiscal_week AND l.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE t.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY t.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar: period 2 is fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (FY2026/27: 1-28 June 2026; FY2025/26: 26 May-22 June 2025)
Net sales means fact_sales_line.net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus fact_return_line.refund_net, with returns counted on the return date
Total company means all stores plus the web shop (store_id 900), which covers home delivery and click-and-collect
Web lines identified through the web shop store (store_id 900) rather than channel_code, because channel_code is empty from the web-platform migration onwards
Growth is (this year / last year - 1) x 100, compared week by week on the same fiscal week number
assumptions: 'This year' is the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (the request is dated 5 October 2026, so FY2026/27 started 4 May 2026) and 'last year' is FY2025/26
'Sales' is read as net sales, ex VAT and after returns, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Staff purchases are real sales and are included (about 1% of sales)
Weeks are compared by fiscal week number (5 to 8) in both years
Click-and-collect and home-delivery orders are all collected or delivered (none cancelled or still processing in these weeks), so all web lines are counted
caveats: Correction: from the web-platform migration, web lines in fact_sales_line have channel_code NULL (channel_id 2 or 3 instead). A filter on channel_code = 'WB' drops all web sales for FY2026/27 (about EUR 55,000-71,000 a week) and would make growth look far too low. The web shop is identified by store_id 900 instead. The view rpt.v_daily_sales has this flaw, so it was not used.
Correction: the Training store (store_id 999, Head office) has sales of EUR 200-900 a week in both years. It was excluded as non-trading activity.

Weeks 7 and 8 are distorted by Midsummer. In FY2026/27 the Midsummer closure (two non-trading days, 19-20 June) falls in week 7, but in FY2025/26 it falls in week 8 (20-21 June). Week 7 (-26.5%) and week 8 (+54.4%) are therefore not like-for-like. Weeks 7 and 8 combined are EUR 586,868 against EUR 551,168, up 6.5%. The whole period is EUR 1,295,948 against EUR 1,210,936, up 7.0%.

FY2025/26 was a 53-week year, so week 5 of FY2026/27 starts on 1 June 2026 and week 5 of FY2025/26 starts on 26 May 2025, 371 days earlier rather than 364. Last year's comparison weeks therefore sit one calendar week earlier than a strict same-week-last-year comparison would.

The set of trading stores differs between the years: 40 stores last year, 39 in weeks 5-6 this year (store 129 Savonlinna closed 25 January 2026) and 38 in weeks 7-8 (store 125 is shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026). Growth is total company, not like-for-like.
rpt_daily_store_sales gives different totals from the fact tables (for example its web figures differ), so the figures were built from fact_sales_line and fact_return_line instead.
Web returns are included in returns, using the web shop store key on the return line.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(f.sale_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, sum(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.sale_date >= DATE '2024-08-01' AND f.sale_date < DATE '2024-10-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Store sales = sales lines in physical stores only (channel ST, store_id below 900), as in the rpt.v_daily_sales view
Web shop (store_id 900, channel WB, including click-and-collect) excluded from store sales
Training store (store_id 999) excluded as a pseudo-location
Including VAT = gross_amount on the sales line (net_amount plus the line's own VAT rate)
Before returns = fact_sales_line only, fact_return_line not netted off
Store identity taken through the store_key on each line (dim_store version at the sale date)
Staff purchases kept in, in line with rpt_daily_store_sales (which includes them)
assumptions: August 2024 and September 2024 are read as calendar months (1-31 Aug, 1-30 Sep), not fiscal periods (P05 runs 26 Aug to 22 Sep)

Staff purchases count as store sales because the Data & Analytics daily store report includes them; they are a small share (about 1.2% of net sales, roughly EUR 13.7k net in August and EUR 13.1k in September)
Amounts are in EUR, by the sale_date on the line
No store filter (all stores, including the Vantaa Tammisto refit closure, which ended 11 Aug 2024)
caveats: Correction: 283 lines (EUR 7,633.94 gross) booked to the Training store (999) were excluded; they are not real sales. Of that, EUR 4,282.23 falls in August and EUR 3,351.71 in September.
Correction: web shop lines (EUR 334,806.10 gross over the two months) were excluded, since they are not store sales. Click-and-collect orders are also counted as web.
Staff purchases are included (EUR 16,949.92 gross in August and EUR 16,438.40 in September, regular stores). If Finance wants them out, subtract these amounts.
Vantaa Tammisto was closed for a refit from 8 Jul to 11 Aug 2024, so August has about 11 fewer trading days for that store, and the August figure is not like-for-like with other months.

Checked and found clean for these two months: no duplicate receipt lines, no lines where gross differs from net times (1 + VAT rate), no nulls or negative amounts, and no overlap with the staging load table. The totals reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales for every real store.
The result includes the VAT rate change on 1 Sep 2024 as recorded on the lines. I did not recompute VAT.

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT f.* FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-08-02' AND s.store_id <> 999), ret AS (SELECT r.* FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-08-02' AND s.store_id <> 999) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, ROUND(((SELECT SUM(net_amount) FROM sales) - (SELECT SUM(refund_net) FROM ret)) / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT receipt_id) FROM sales), 2) AS atv_eur
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales excluding VAT, after returns, divided by the number of receipts (a web order counts as one receipt)
Net sales after returns follows rpt_daily_store_sales: net_amount on the sale date minus refund_net booked on the return date
Fiscal periods from ref_fiscal_calendar: P01 to P03 of FY2026/27 run 2026-05-04 to 2026-08-02, fully_loaded = true
Company-wide scope: all physical stores, including store 129 Savonlinna, which closed on 2026-01-25 and has no sales in the window, plus the web shop (store 900)
Web scope: channel_id 2 (web home delivery) and 3 (click and collect); web lines are identified by channel_id because channel_code is NULL in this period
Receipts counted with COUNT(DISTINCT receipt_id)
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year FY2026/27, because the request was received on 2026-10-05. Periods 1 to 3 are 2026-05-04 to 2026-08-02 (13 weeks).

'ATV' means average transaction value, with the value taken excluding VAT and after returns, in line with the net sales definition used in rpt_daily_store_sales. The warehouse documents no ATV definition, so this is my reading.
Staff purchases are kept, as they are in rpt_daily_store_sales. Excluding them would give a slightly different figure.
Returns are deducted in the period they were booked. They are not matched back to the original sale date, and returns of web orders count in the same way.
Web orders in the sales data are all delivered or collected. I found no cancelled or processing orders with sales lines, so no web status filter was needed.
caveats: Correction: store 999 (Training store, head office) is excluded. It has 186 receipts and 7,806.26 EUR net in the window, and rpt_daily_store_sales also leaves it out. Including it would not belong in company results.

Correction: web lines were identified through channel_id (2 and 3) and the web-shop pseudo-store 900, not channel_code = 'WB'. In FY2026/27 channel_code is NULL on every line. The rpt.v_daily_sales view filters on channel_code = 'WB', so it would drop all web sales for this period.

Inputs behind the figure: net sales of 4,538,952.58 EUR before returns, 243,627.84 EUR of refunds booked in the window, and 80,983 receipts. That includes 12,962 web receipts (9,037 home delivery and 3,925 click and collect).
ATV before returns would be 56.04 EUR. Including VAT it would be 70.22 EUR before returns. The 53.04 figure is net of returns and excludes VAT.

rpt_daily_store_sales shows 13,004 web receipts for the window against 12,962 in the sales lines, a difference of 42 that I did not resolve. I used the sales lines, which reconcile exactly to the report for the physical stores (68,021 receipts).

No duplicate lines (same receipt and line number), no receipts spanning more than one store, and no null or negative amounts were found in the window. Slowly changing store versions were joined through store_key and did not affect the count.

answer.sql: SELECT ds.store_id, ds.store_name, dd.fiscal_year, dd.fiscal_period, SUM(fsl.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line fsl INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key WHERE ds.store_id = 108 AND dp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND dd.fiscal_period = 3 AND dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' GROUP BY ds.store_id, ds.store_name, dd.fiscal_year, dd.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Interior Paint identified by subcategory = 'Interior Paint' in the Paint & Decorating category
Sales units from fact_sales_line.quantity for completed transactions (not including returns)
Fiscal period 3 as defined in ref_fiscal_calendar (June 29 - Aug 2, 2026)
Lahti store identified as store_id 108
assumptions: 'This year' interpreted as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (April 2026 - March 2027)
Period 3 refers to fiscal period 3, not calendar period
All Interior Paint SKUs in the subcategory are included (123 products)
caveats: No data quality issues detected
Period 3 ends in the past (Aug 2, 2026); data is complete for this period
Interior Paint is a broad category containing 123 individual products; figure represents the total for all Interior Paint variants

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND p.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 9 AND 13
definitions_applied: Units sold from fact_sales_line.quantity (goods sold, before returns)
Interior Paint as product subcategory
Lahti store identified by store_id 108
Period 3 FY2026/27 mapped to fiscal weeks 9–13 (29 June–2 August 2026)
assumptions: Period 3 of FY2026/27 interpreted as fiscal period 3, running from fiscal week 9 to fiscal week 13
Units sold counted on the sale date, not the return date
caveats: None. Period 3 FY2026/27 is fully loaded as of the warehouse load date (4 October 2026)

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, ty.region, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: Like-for-like growth: net sales in LFL stores for the same fiscal weeks, week by week, against last year
LFL base: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop excluded
LFL opening rule: open at least 364 days before the first day of the period
LFL store-week: the store must have traded in that fiscal week in both years (open, not closed, no refit closure in ref_store_closure)
Week 53 never counts in LFL (not relevant to Q3 weeks 27 to 39)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT after returns, returns deducted on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = P7 to P9 = fiscal weeks 27 to 39, compared by fiscal week number, not calendar date
Regions as-is: current dim_store version (five regions including Capital Region applied to all history)
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' read as FY2025/26 Q3 (weeks 27 to 39, 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026), because the request was received on 5 Oct 2026 in FY2026/27 and past requests read 'last year' as FY2025/26. The comparator is FY2024/25 Q3 (weeks 27 to 39, 28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025).

'By region' read as one LFL row per region with no company total row, using regions as-is (current hierarchy), the company default. On the old four-region split, Capital Region would not exist for the earlier period.
Net sales for the LFL stores are given alongside the growth rate so the percentages can be traced.
Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026, the last day of week 39) is treated as having traded in all 13 weeks of the quarter and is kept in the East base. It had sales on all 7 days of week 39.
caveats: Lohja (store 137, South) is excluded from the LFL base. It opened on 4 November 2024, less than 364 days before the quarter began on 27 October 2025. It had sales in the quarter but no full year of history, so including it would have inflated South growth.
Tampere Lamminpää (store 136, West, opened 2 September 2024) is in the base, as it had been open more than 52 weeks before 27 October 2025.
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test lines were left out of net sales; 2,124 sales lines across the two Q3 windows were affected.
No refit closures fall in either Q3 window (Pori's refit ended 12 October 2025), so no store-weeks dropped out for refits. The base is 38 stores x 13 weeks = 494 store-weeks.

The query did not use the deprecated views rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, which omit web sales from 3 November 2025, nor rpt_weekly_sales_by_region (stale, old regions). Web is outside LFL anyway.
Store-level net sales for both quarters matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for every physical store, and no duplicate sales or return lines were found in the range.
Savonlinna's sales were down about 43% in its final week (week 39) before closing and it stays in the LFL base for that week, which weighs slightly on East.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(w.web_order_id) as web_orders FROM fact_web_order w WHERE DATE(w.order_ts_utc) = '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web orders are records in fact_web_order where order_ts_utc falls on the calendar date
Order date is the calendar date of order_ts_utc (order timestamp)
assumptions: Cyber Monday on 1 December 2025 refers to the calendar date 2025-12-01 (a Monday)
A web order is counted once per order_id, regardless of status or fulfilment type
caveats: Web orders include all statuses (delivered, collected, processing, cancelled) placed on this date

answer.sql: SELECT cs.store_id, cs.store_name, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Interior Paint' AS subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 AND cs.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cs.store_id, cs.store_name
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (metric dictionary, weeks-of-cover definition)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 = 29 Jun to 2 Aug 2026 (weeks 9-13, 5 weeks), from dim_date
Store scope: physical store only, store_id 108 (Lahti); web shop (900) and training store 999 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Product hierarchy as-is: current product version (dim_product is_current) for subcategory
Versioned dimensions joined through store_id/sku with is_current, not on natural keys alone
Staff purchases included (not excluded for unit counts)
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 108 over the same dates
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (request received 5 Oct 2026)
'Period 3' read as fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27, which is fully loaded (warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026)
'Interior Paint' read as the subcategory Interior Paint within the Paint & Decorating category

'Units sold' read as gross units on sales lines, before returns, as the company definition of units sold in the weeks-of-cover metric; the metric dictionary has no separate definition of units sold for a category request
'Lahti' read as store 108 Lahti; Tampere Lielahti (116) is a different store whose name matches a text search only
As-is and as-was give the same answer here: all Interior Paint lines sold in Lahti in the period sit in Interior Paint in both the version on the sale date and the current version
caveats: No data problems needing correction were found: no duplicate sales lines (sales_line_id and receipt_id + line_no both unique), no test-article lines, no zero or negative quantities in the selection

Control check: all Lahti sales in the period total 3,927 units and 67,202.85 EUR net before returns, matching rpt_daily_store_sales exactly across the same 35 days. The control table has no product dimension, so the 194 itself cannot be checked against it

Returns are not netted off: 5 Interior Paint units were returned at Lahti with a return date in the period (6 units from sales made in the period came back, some possibly after period end), which would give about 189 units net of returns by return date
The 194 units come from 142 lines on 137 receipts, covering 33 distinct articles, and include 'staff purchase' lines
Staging, backup and deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales etc.) were not used

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week),
range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week),
weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)),
store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900),
lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)),
web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')),
net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'),
lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region)))
SELECT NULL AS region, ty.store_weeks, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NULL;
definitions_applied: LFL growth definition: compares net sales in LFL stores for a period with the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
Physical stores only (store_id < 900); web shop excluded
Store eligibility: open at least 52 weeks before period start
Store-week trading requirement: must trade in both years for the week to count
Refit closures excluded using ref_store_closure
Week 53 never included in LFL comparison
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
assumptions: Period 4 this year interpreted as FY2026/27 P04 (weeks 14-17, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30) based on request date 2026-10-07 - the most recent completed period
Prior-year comparator: FY2025/26 P04 (same fiscal week numbers: weeks 14-17)
Total LFL growth returned (not broken by region) as the request did not ask for a breakdown
caveats: No data quality issues detected by query-check
152 store-weeks included in the LFL base for period 4
LFL growth is -0.03%, representing a minimal decline in like-for-like net sales

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY p.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (metric dictionary weeks-of-cover definition)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 5 = 31 Aug 2026 to 27 Sep 2026 (28 days, complete and loaded)
Pitäjänmäki = Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, store_id 102, found through the store_key on each sales line
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this store)
Products grouped by stable sku, named from the current product version (is_current)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total: units for store 102 over the period agree with rpt_daily_store_sales (3,740 units)
assumptions: Read 'period 5 of FY26/27' as fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27, a complete period
Read 'sold the most units' as units sold on sales lines before returns. Returns are not netted off
'Product' means the article (sku), not the product version
Pitäjänmäki is store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki); web orders are not part of a physical store, so the web shop is not included
caveats: Returns were not deducted. Netting them would not change the top three: the 3rd product had 1 unit returned in the period, leaving 41 against the 4th product's 30
Rank 3 is clear. The next product sold 30 units, so there is no tie at the cut-off
No data problems found. There were no duplicate sales lines for the store in the period, and the units total matches the rpt_daily_store_sales control (3,740)
Pitäjänmäki moved from South to the Capital Region in April 2025. This does not affect a single-store answer

answer.sql: SELECT p.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY p.subcategory ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period: Period 5 within the fiscal year (FY2026/27 P05 running 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27)
Units sold: Quantity column from fact_sales_line for sales transactions
Store: Nokia (store_id 118, West region) identified by current dimension version
Subcategory: Product classification from dim_product
assumptions: This year refers to FY2026/27, the fiscal year active as of the request date (2026-10-09)
Period 5 refers to fiscal_period = 5 in the fiscal calendar
The query includes both in-store (channel ST) and web (channel WB) sales, excluding returns
Current versions of dimensions used (is_current = true) to capture the names as they are known today

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, st.store_id, st.store_name, s.week_ending_date, s.closing_units FROM fact_stock_week s JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = s.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = s.product_key WHERE st.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND s.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Closing stock per store and SKU at the end of the fiscal week (fact_stock_week.closing_units), counted on the Sunday week-ending date
Fiscal week runs Monday to Sunday (dim_date fiscal_week_start_date and fiscal_week_end_date)
Store and product identified through their stable IDs (store_id 124, sku 100011) and joined to the fact table via the surrogate keys (store_key, product_key)
Closing units as at the end of the week, not a sum across weeks (stock is a point-in-time balance)
assumptions: Request received Thursday 2026-10-08, so 'last week' is the previous complete fiscal week, FY2026/27 week 22 (Monday 2026-09-28 to Sunday 2026-10-04), and 'end of last week' is the stock count on Sunday 2026-10-04
'Jyväskylä Palokka' is the store name of store_id 124 (store_key 30), the only store matching that name; SKU 100011 is 'Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570'
Kaisa asked for units on hand, so closing_units is reported rather than closing_value (46.64 EUR at standard cost)
caveats: The warehouse has no problem for this store and SKU. Each has a single dimension version, and there is exactly one stock row for the week with no duplicate loads. It matches the staging snapshot (11 units). Last week's receipts and adjustments were both 0, and no sales or returns were booked on the SKU in the store that week, so the opening 11 units carried through. Earlier weeks reconcile too: 13 units at 2026-09-20 less 2 units sold (21 and 24 September) gives 11 at 2026-09-27. The store has no planned closure.

Elsewhere in fact_stock_week there are duplicate rows (about 7,400 more rows than distinct store/product/week combinations). They do not touch this store and SKU, but a broader stock total over the table would need de-duplicating first.

ref_fiscal_calendar flags period FY2026/27 P06 (which contains week 22) as not fully loaded. The week 22 stock row for this SKU was loaded on 2026-10-05 and reconciles with sales, so I treated it as complete.

answer.sql: WITH web_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, w.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date JOIN fact_web_order w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 6 AND 8 AND (f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3))), sales AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, sum(net_amount) AS web_net, sum(CASE WHEN fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN net_amount ELSE 0 END) AS cc_net FROM web_lines GROUP BY 1, 2), refunds AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(r.refund_net) AS web_refund, sum(CASE WHEN w.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN r.refund_net ELSE 0 END) AS cc_refund FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN fact_web_order w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 6 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_period, round(100 * (s.cc_net - r.cc_refund) / (s.web_net - r.web_refund), 1) AS click_and_collect_share_pct FROM sales s JOIN refunds r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period) ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: periods taken from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar (P06 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, P07 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025, P08 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025)
Net sales: value excluding VAT, after line discounts, less refunds booked in the period (the definition used by rpt_daily_store_sales)
Web shop: sales lines with channel_code WB, or channel_id 2 (web home delivery) or 3 (click and collect)
Click and collect: web orders with fulfilment_type = click_and_collect in fact_web_order
Refunds counted on the return date, linked to web orders through the original sales line
All periods are fully loaded (fully_loaded = true in ref_fiscal_calendar)
assumptions: Last year means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (the request is dated 9 Oct 2026, which falls in FY2026/27 P06)
Periods 6 to 8 are fiscal periods, not calendar months
Share means click-and-collect net sales divided by total web net sales, in money terms and not in order counts
Sales are net of refunds, as the company's net sales definition has it; no staff purchases or cancelled orders fall in these web periods, so none were excluded
caveats: The channel field changes at the web-platform migration, with the first lines on 3 Nov 2025 (fiscal week 28, mid P07). Before then channel_id is NULL and all web lines carry channel_code WB, and from then on channel_code is NULL and channel_id is 2 or 3. Filtering on channel_id = 3 alone would miss all of P06 and the first week of P07, and filtering on channel_code = 'WB' alone would miss most of P07 and all of P08. I therefore identified web lines with both fields and click-and-collect through fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, which is available for the whole period.
The existing view rpt.v_daily_sales only picks up web lines with channel_code = 'WB', so it understates web sales from 3 Nov 2025 and is not suitable for this question. I did not use it.
Before returns the shares are 27.7%, 26.6% and 26.6% for P06, P07 and P08. If E-commerce wants gross sales before refunds, use those figures instead.
Click-and-collect refunds are a little higher in P06 and P07 than home-delivery refunds as a share of sales, so including refunds lowers the shares slightly.

Checked the sales lines in these periods: no duplicate lines, no non-positive amounts or quantities, every web line matches a web order, and net and gross agree with the VAT rate. No problem found there.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 18 AS week_start, 21 AS week_end) SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date INNER JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key INNER JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.week_start AND params.week_end AND s.store_id != 999 AND p.category != 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 10;
definitions_applied: Last period: most recent completed fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, 28 August to 27 September 2026)
Best-selling: ranked by units sold (quantity)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Exclusions: store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test
assumptions: Interpreted 'best-selling' as highest units sold by volume (standard retail metric for top products by volume)
caveats: Training store (999) and test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded from totals as per standard reporting rules
Net sales figures include staff purchases (15% discount) but otherwise follow company definition
Quantity figures represent gross sales before returns

answer.sql:
WITH date_range AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_period_label
  FROM dim_date d
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 27 AND 52
),
sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    d.fiscal_period_label,
    SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' 
    AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 27 AND 52
    AND p.category = 'Garden'
    AND s.store_id < 900
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_period_label
),
returns AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    d.fiscal_period_label,
    SUM(r.refund_net) AS return_amount
  FROM fact_return_line r
  JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
  JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' 
    AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 27 AND 52
    AND p.category = 'Garden'
    AND s.store_id < 900
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_period_label
)
SELECT 
  COALESCE(s.fiscal_year, r.fiscal_year) AS fiscal_year,
  COALESCE(s.fiscal_period, r.fiscal_period) AS fiscal_period,
  COALESCE(s.fiscal_period_label, r.fiscal_period_label) AS fiscal_period_label,
  COALESCE(s.net_sales, 0) - COALESCE(r.return_amount, 0) AS net_sales
FROM sales s
FULL OUTER JOIN returns r 
  ON s.fiscal_period = r.fiscal_period 
  AND s.fiscal_year = r.fiscal_year
ORDER BY COALESCE(s.fiscal_period, r.fiscal_period)
definitions_applied: Net sales definition: net amount excluding VAT, after line discounts and returns
Fiscal calendar: P7-P12 of FY2024/25 covers fiscal weeks 27-52 (28 October 2024 – 27 April 2025)
As-was product categorization: product versions valid on the transaction date
Store scope: physical stores only, excluding web shop (store 900) and training store (999)
Return attribution: returns allocated to the fiscal period of the original sale, not return date
assumptions: P7 to P12 of FY2024/25 interpreted as fiscal periods 7 through 12 of the fiscal year running 29 April 2024 to 27 April 2025
'Net sales' uses the company standard definition (excluding VAT, after returns)
'The old way, Garden as it was reported at the time (the old category set-up)' interpreted as as-was reporting using product versions and categories as they stood on each sale date
Garden category includes all products in the Garden category during this period; no product reorganizations occurred within Garden during FY2024/25
caveats: House rule filter applied: category 'ZZ Test' excluded (does not affect result as only Garden category included)
No product category changes affected Garden during this period (outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 October 2025, after FY2024/25 ended 27 April 2025)
Returns include both in-store and web returns processed during their respective return periods

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members_joined FROM dim_member WHERE join_date = '2026-10-03'
definitions_applied: Member: counted by distinct member_id from dim_member table
Join date: calendar date when member joined (join_date column)
Slowly-changing dimension: one row per member version; join_date is immutable across versions
assumptions: Request refers to calendar date 3 October 2026, not fiscal period
Count distinct member IDs (not rows) since the dim_member table stores multiple versions per member
caveats: No data quality issues found; all join_dates are non-null and valid
The warehouse is current through 2026-10-04; the requested date (2026-10-03) is fully loaded

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-10-04' AS as_of_end), tampere AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_id FROM dim_store WHERE city = 'Tampere' AND store_id < 900), ver AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.home_store_id FROM dim_member m, params p WHERE p.as_of_end BETWEEN m.valid_from AND m.valid_to), active AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key, params p WHERE f.sale_date > p.as_of_end - 364 AND f.sale_date <= p.as_of_end) SELECT COUNT(*) AS active_members_tampere FROM ver v JOIN active a USING (member_id) WHERE v.home_store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM tampere)
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks, as-of week included, in any channel, counted as distinct member_id
Member version valid on the as-of date (dim_member valid_from/valid_to), so one row per member
Physical stores only (store_id below 900) for store scope
Store 999 (training store) and the web shop (900) excluded from the Tampere stores
Home store taken from the member version valid on the as-of date
assumptions: The warehouse has no customer table, and 'customer' is not defined in the metric dictionary. I read 'customers' as loyalty members, the only identifiable customers we hold. Non-member shoppers and guest web orders cannot be counted.
I read 'customers we have' as active loyalty members, using the company's active-member definition, rather than everyone ever enrolled.

'In Tampere' means the member's home store is one of the four physical Tampere stores (Hervanta 115, Lielahti 116, Kaleva 117, Lamminpää 136). A member's home store is where they enrolled or last moved to, not where they live.
As-of date is Sunday 4 October 2026, the end of the last loaded fiscal week (FY2026/27 week 22), so the trailing window is 6 October 2025 to 4 October 2026.
Members whose home store is the web shop (900) are not counted in Tampere, even though their home store is not a physical Tampere one.
caveats: Correction: dim_store lists the web shop (900) and the training store (999) with city = Tampere. A plain filter on city = 'Tampere' would pull both in. I excluded them, so only the four physical Tampere stores count. Web-shop sign-ups (12,028 members, 4,698 of them active) are not included.

If Jukka means everyone enrolled with a Tampere home store, whether or not they have bought in the past year, the figure is 7,175 (Hervanta 2,788; Lielahti 1,721; Kaleva 1,692; Lamminpää 974). Active members by store: Hervanta 1,708; Lielahti 1,052; Kaleva 1,034; Lamminpää 647.
Members who shop in Tampere but have a home store elsewhere, or are online sign-ups, are not counted. A count by where people shop would give a different number.

I could not ask the requester which definition of 'customer' he wants, as the library's house rule says to do for an undefined metric. The active-member reading is the closest defined metric, and the answer should be confirmed with him.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_period = 2 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Total company includes the web shop (store 900) and all physical stores
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2026/27 P2 is fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (1 to 28 June 2026)
Prior-year comparison lined up by fiscal week number, not by calendar date: FY2025/26 weeks 5 to 8 (26 May to 22 June 2025)
Growth % = this year / last year - 1, in percent
Control total: weekly figures agree exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales (gap 0.00 in all 8 weeks)
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2, the current fiscal year; the request was received on 7 October 2026 and P2 is fully loaded and complete
'Same weeks last year' read as FY2025/26 fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (P2 of FY2025/26), matched by week number as in earlier accepted weekly comparisons
'Total company' read as stores plus the web shop, shown as one combined figure with no breakdown by channel or region
No week 53 is involved (it falls in P12 of FY2025/26), so no week was dropped from the comparison
caveats: Midsummer falls in different fiscal weeks in the two years. Midsummer Eve and Day (stores shut by company rule) were 20 and 21 June 2025, in FY2025/26 week 8, and 19 and 20 June 2026, in FY2026/27 week 7. So week 7 shows -32.2% and week 8 shows +76.4%. This is a calendar effect, not a drop in demand or a data fault. Taken together, weeks 7 and 8 are 591,343.83 this year against 535,679.88 last year (+10.4%).
Over the whole of P2, net sales are 1,294,647.64 against 1,195,882.70 last year, up 8.3%. That total is my own sum and was not asked for.

Web dispatch was heavily concentrated on Monday 22 June 2026 (web net sales about 34.5k against a usual 6 to 16k a day). Orders placed over Midsummer were dispatched in a batch, as web sales are recognised on dispatch. This lifts FY2026/27 week 8 and is legitimate under the company definition.

The number of trading physical stores differs between weeks (40 stores trading in the FY2025/26 weeks shown, 39 in week 6 and 38 in weeks 7 and 8 of FY2026/27). This is total-company net sales, not like-for-like, so the growth percentages include the effect of store closures and openings. I did not investigate which stores changed.

Store 999 and ZZ Test were excluded as required. They account for about 6.4k and 0.4k of sales lines in the two P2 windows (the 999 amount includes the lead-in and tail days I pulled); the control table agrees with the filtered figures, so the exclusion is consistent with the company definition.

I checked for duplicate sales lines (receipt_id + line_no). The only duplicates, 836 rows, are in FY2025/26 P5 (15 to 21 September 2025), which does not touch P2 in either year. I found no unmatched store or product keys in the P2 windows, and no cancelled or processing web lines in the range.

I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales (they leave out web sales from 3 November 2025). The deprecated tables were also not used. The figures are as-is, but no regional or category grouping is involved, so as-is and as-was make no difference here.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id=st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date<=d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date>=d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 4) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id<900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id=ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week=ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id=ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-05-04' - 364)), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id=n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week=d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27','FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_period=1 GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0*(ty.net_sales/ly.net_sales-1),2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty, lfl_sales ly WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores for the period vs the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week, physical stores only (store_id below 900)
LFL base rule: open_date on or before the first day of the period minus 364 days (4 May 2026 minus 364 = 5 May 2025)
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open/close dates and ref_store_closure refit weeks)
Net sales: excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their return date; web sales on the Helsinki dispatch date (web shop store 900 is not in LFL)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P1 = weeks 1-4, 4 to 31 May 2026; compared with FY2025/26 weeks 1-4, 28 April to 25 May 2025 (same fiscal weeks, not the same calendar dates)
Store-level control total: net sales for P1 in both years agree with rpt_daily_store_sales for every store (zero differences)
Not used: rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, stg_/bak_/tmp_ tables, channel_code
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (request dated 9 October 2026), so 'period 1' is FY2026/27 P1, which ran 4 to 31 May 2026 and is fully loaded.
'Like-for-like' taken as the company LFL definition, returned as one total (this year, last year, growth) since no breakdown was requested.
Comparison year is FY2025/26 P1, the same fiscal weeks 1 to 4.
Open and close dates taken from the current dim_store version, as in the accepted LFL queries.
caveats: LFL base is 38 stores x 4 weeks = 152 store-weeks in each year. Savonlinna (129) is out because it closed on 25 January 2026. No store was in a refit closure in either year's P1 (the Pori, Kuopio and Tammisto refits fall outside these weeks). Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) are in the base because both opened before 5 May 2025.

Most of the growth comes from week 1. Last year's week 1 (28 April to 4 May 2025) contained the May Day closure on Thursday 1 May 2025, when the stores were shut, whereas this year's week 1 (4 to 10 May 2026) had no closed day. Week 1 LFL growth is 25.6%, against 0.9%, 2.6% and 1.8% in weeks 2, 3 and 4. For weeks 2 to 4 combined, LFL growth is about 1.8%. The company definition does not adjust for holidays, so I did not adjust the headline figure.

No data corrections were needed. In P1 of both years, sales lines, return lines and web orders had no duplicate keys and no orphan returns, and net sales agree with rpt_daily_store_sales store by store.
Week 53 is not part of this comparison, since P1 does not contain it.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT f.sale_date, p.sku, f.net_amount, f.standard_cost FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id NOT IN (900, 999) AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END AS category, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) / SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS gross_margin_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 6 AND CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 3
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after line discounts and after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the date of the original sale
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), web identified by store 900
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns, with returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned
Gross margin percentage: gross margin divided by net sales, in percent
As-is reporting: categories taken from the current product version
Outdoor Lighting subcategory counted in Electrical for all history
Fiscal period 6: fiscal weeks 22 to 26, 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, Helsinki business dates
Web shop (store 900) included in the totals because the request is for category totals
assumptions: 'Last year' was read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just ended, following the readings accepted on earlier requests received in May 2026 (REQ-D04, REQ-D08, REQ-D28, REQ-D35). The request arrived on 8 Oct 2026, during FY2026/27. 'Period 6 last year' is therefore FY2025/26 P6. If FY2024/25 was meant, the figures will differ.
Categories are as-is (current hierarchy), the company default, because the request did not ask for as-was.
Net sales and margin cover all channels (stores and web), since the request gave no channel restriction.
Gross margin percentage is calculated after returns, on the company definition.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: Outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, the day after P6 ended. On the as-is basis used here, outdoor lighting sits in Electrical for all of P6. On the as-was basis, Electrical net sales would be 185,711.09 and Garden's would be about 33,782 higher than shown. The as-was Garden figure was not computed separately.

Correction: five outdoor-lighting SKUs (100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) were delisted before the move. They never received an Electrical version and still show Garden as their current category. I classified every Outdoor Lighting subcategory SKU as Electrical. They had no sales or returns in P6, so the figures are unchanged.

Correction: 418 receipt lines in fact_sales_line (sale dates 15 to 21 Sep 2025) were loaded twice, on 16 to 22 Sep and again on 23 Sep 2025. I removed the duplicates by receipt_id and line_no. They fall in P5, outside P6, so P6 is unaffected, but the query is protected against them.

Correction: web lines are counted only when the order was delivered or collected, dated by Helsinki dispatch date. The standard net_lines template would otherwise date cancelled or processing web lines by sale_date. No such lines fall in P6, so the figures are unchanged.
The Pori store (119) was shut for refit from 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025, which covers the first three weeks of P6. This lowers both categories' sales for the period and is not a data error.
The control total in rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to category subsets, so it was not used. query_check passed with no failed checks.

The warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026. P6 of FY2025/26 is fully loaded, but returns on goods sold in late P6 can still arrive up to 30 days later. Returns are dated by their return date, so this does not change the net sales definition.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900) as part of the total
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only); cancelled and processing orders excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Last completed fiscal period used for 'last month' (FY2026/27 P05, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store and day by day
Did not use channel_code, rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales or any stg_, bak_, tmp_ or _old table
assumptions: 'Last month' is not defined in the metric dictionary. I read it as the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (31 August to 27 September 2026, 4 weeks). This follows how past requests read 'last four weeks' and 'last period', and the wiki says to filter on fiscal columns rather than calendar months. The request came in on 9 October 2026.
'The whole company' is read as all physical stores plus the web shop. The result is a single total, because no breakdown was requested.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: If you meant calendar September 2026 (1 to 30 September) instead of fiscal P05, the whole-company net sales are 1,179,035.98 EUR. Of that, stores are 988,592.16 and the web shop is 190,443.82. Tell me if you want that version.
The P05 total of 1,109,546.52 EUR splits into stores 932,309.19 and web 177,237.33.
P05 is fully loaded in the warehouse. The warehouse runs through 4 October 2026, so nothing in the range is missing.
The net sales by store and day matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for 31 August to 30 September 2026. There were no differing days.
No duplicate sales or return lines were found, and no web lines lacked a delivered or collected order.
The store 999 and ZZ Test exclusion removes 3,186.61 EUR of line sales (before returns) from the 31 August to 30 September range. It changes the total slightly.
No corrections were needed for dashboard views. rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it omits web sales from 3 November 2025.

Campaign identification by exact name match

Order date determined from order_ts_utc (UTC timestamp)
All orders included regardless of final status
assumptions: Cyber Monday is 1 December 2025 (confirmed as Monday via dim_date)
All orders placed on that calendar date are counted
UTC date is the reference for order placement

Breakdown by status: delivered 193, collected 81, cancelled 17

Counted on the Helsinki order date, converted from order_ts_utc
Cancelled orders excluded; processing orders would be included (none that day)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Guest orders included
Test articles (ZZ Test) left out of reporting
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is Monday 1 December 2025, as the request states
Web shop orders means all web orders (home delivery and click-and-collect, logged-in and guest)
The day is the Helsinki calendar day (UTC+2 in December), not the UTC day

19 orders placed on the day were cancelled (13 home delivery, 6 click-and-collect) and are not counted.

No problems found in the data for this request, so no corrections were made.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ce.member_key) as members_contacted, SUM(fs.net_amount) as total_spending FROM (SELECT DISTINCT member_key FROM fact_campaign_exposure WHERE campaign_id = 19) ce LEFT JOIN fact_sales_line fs ON ce.member_key = fs.member_key AND fs.sale_date >= '2026-05-04' AND fs.sale_date <= '2026-05-24'
definitions_applied: Members contacted: individuals with at least one exposure record in fact_campaign_exposure for Spring Garden Launch 2026 (campaign_id = 19)

Spending question refers to the same 15,063 contacted members
Sales amounts are measured by net value (excluding VAT per fact_sales_line.net_amount definition)
Members who received multiple exposures count as one member

This 36-member (0.24%) discrepancy could indicate contact records for members outside the mailing list, or minor inconsistencies in member key versioning across the slowly-changing dim_member table.
Completeness: 2,443 of the 15,063 contacted members (16.2%) did not record a purchase during the campaign window; spending is zero for these members.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, count(DISTINCT member_id) AS member_count FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Current member version: dim_member.is_current = true, which is the row with valid_to = 9999-12-31
Members counted once each by member_id (stable loyalty number), not by member_key
Tier is the loyalty tier on the member's current version (Basic, Silver or Gold)
assumptions: 'At the moment' means the latest loaded version of each member, as of the request date 2026-10-07. The latest valid_from in dim_member is 2026-10-04.
A 'Gold-tier loyalty member' is anyone with a current dim_member row at tier Gold. I did not filter on marketing consent, home store or join date, because the request did not ask for it.
caveats: Counting every dim_member row with tier = 'Gold' would give 8,203. That figure counts historical versions and counts members who were Gold earlier but have since moved tier, so it overstates the answer. The 2,412 non-current Gold rows cover 2,233 members.

I checked the dimension for problems and found none. Each of the 60,000 members has exactly one current version and exactly one open-ended version. The tier values are clean (only Basic, Silver and Gold). No current version starts after the request date.
The staging table stg_member_updates holds 4,061 rows (3,939 of them current). Every one already matches the matching dim_member row on tier and validity dates, so it does not change the count.
Of the 5,791 current Gold members, 3,861 have given marketing consent. This is not part of the answer; I include it in case the figure is wanted for marketing contact.
The count is a snapshot of the warehouse as loaded. A tier change after the latest load on 2026-10-04 would not show up.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) DESC) AS rank, 'FY2024/25' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_quarter, cp.sku, cp.product_name, cp.brand, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost), 2) AS gross_margin_eur FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 10 AND 12 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name, cp.brand ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns (returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned)
Net sales excludes VAT; returns reduce sales on their own return date
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered/collected orders only); web (store 900, region Online) is not in the South region
As-is hierarchy: region taken from the current store version and product name, brand and category from the current product version, by sku
Fiscal Q4 = periods 10 to 12 = fiscal weeks 40 to 52 (27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025, 91 days)
Staff purchases included (company net sales definition)
assumptions: Q4 of FY24/25 is read as FY2024/25 periods 10 to 12 (27 January to 27 April 2025). The request names the year, so no relative reading was needed.

South is read as-is, the current company definition. That is ten stores: 106 Porvoo, 107 Hyvinkää, 108 Lahti, 109 Hämeenlinna, 110 Turku Kupittaa, 111 Turku Härmälä, 112 Raisio, 113 Salo, 114 Kouvola and 137 Lohja. The request did not ask for regions as they were at the time.
Products are ranked at the article (sku) level on euro gross margin, not margin percentage, and shown under their current name and brand.
Ranking is by gross margin in euros. Net sales and margin % were not asked for and are left out.
caveats: Region reorganisation of 28 April 2025: South as-is no longer contains the five stores that moved to the new Capital Region (101 Vuosaari, 102 Pitäjänmäki, 103 Lommila, 104 Tammisto, 105 Kerava). It does contain Kouvola (114, moved from East to South). Those stores were in South for most of this quarter, so the old-report South would give larger figures and a different list. As-was, ranks 9 and 10 would be Power Tools Koivuranta 416 (sku 101369) and Plumbing Parts Ahvenisto 279, and Indoor Lighting Havu 419 would drop out. Ranks 1 to 8 would be the same articles in the same order, apart from Plumbing Parts Ahvenisto 279 and Power Tools Havu Pro 689, which swap places.

Control check: net sales for the ten South stores over the same 13 weeks agree to the cent with rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store (gap 0.00 in all ten stores). I did not run a control for the product-level margin itself, since the control table has no product dimension.

I found no duplicate sales or return line keys in the range and no null costs, quantities or non-positive net amounts, so no data corrections were needed. Only deprecated objects were avoided (rpt.v_daily_sales, the bak_, stg_, tmp_ and _old tables were not used).
Margin uses standard cost, which is revalued each April. The quarter ends just before the April 2025 revaluation takes effect, and the cost on each line is the one recorded at sale.

Dates 27 Jan to 27 Apr 2025 are whole fiscal weeks, fully inside the warehouse load (through 4 Oct 2026). Returns booked after 27 April 2025 on sales in this quarter are not included, because returns count on their own return date.

definitions_applied: Net sales excluding staff purchases
Last week as the last completed fiscal week

Staff purchases excluded from reported units

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_year, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON f.product_key = dp.product_key INNER JOIN dim_product_old dpo ON dp.sku = dpo.sku WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 AND dpo.category = 'Garden' GROUP BY d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_year ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Garden category defined via dim_product_old (historical product dimension)
Net sales defined as net_amount from fact_sales_line (excluding VAT, after line discounts)
Fiscal periods mapped via dim_date calendar alignment
Sales matched to product SKU for historical category lookup
assumptions: Interpreted 'the old way' as using dim_product_old dimension for category classification
Matched current sales (in fact_sales_line via dim_product) to historical categories (dim_product_old) using SKU
Included all sales channels (store and web) in net sales total
caveats: All 3680 distinct product keys in the period matched successfully to dim_product_old; no unmapped products
Period 12 shows notably higher Garden sales (€325,651.60 vs €61–115k in P7–P11), consistent with spring/Easter seasonal demand

answer.sql: SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, cp.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 5 = fiscal weeks 18 to 21, 31 Aug 2026 to 27 Sep 2026 (28 days, complete in the warehouse)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store scope: physical store 102 Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, identified by stable store_id across both store versions
Products counted by stable sku, using the current product version for name
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included (as in net sales)
Control total check: daily units and receipt counts for store 102 match rpt_daily_store_sales on every day of the period
Warehouse objects not used: deprecated tables, staging, backups and rpt.v_daily_sales
assumptions: 'Period 5 this year' read as FY2026/27 P05, the current fiscal year, and the request was received on 7 Oct 2026, after P5 ended on 27 Sep 2026
'Units sold' read as units sold on sales lines, before returns; returns were not netted off
Web shop (store 900) not included, since the request is about a physical store; click-and-collect lines belong to the web shop and not to Pitäjänmäki
Products ranked at SKU level, not by subcategory or brand
Staff purchases kept in, as the company definition includes them in sales; only 2 of the units of the third-ranked item were staff purchases
caveats: No data problems requiring correction were found: no duplicate sales lines at sales_line_id or receipt_id + line_no level, and daily units and receipts reconcile exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales for store 102 over all 28 days
Store 102 has two dim_store versions (South until 27 Apr 2025, Capital Region from 28 Apr 2025); grouping by store_id handles both, and the region change does not affect this answer
No ties at the cut-off: third place has 42 units and fourth place has 30
