answer.sql:
WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week),
range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week),
weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)),
store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900),
lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)),
web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')),
net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'),
lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region)))
SELECT ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NULL ORDER BY ty.region NULLS FIRST;
definitions_applied: DEF-LFL-BASIS: Like-for-like compares net sales in LFL-eligible stores for fiscal weeks 14-17 of FY2026/27 with the same fiscal weeks in FY2025/26
DEF-LFL-OPEN: A store qualifies for LFL if open at least 52 weeks (364 days) before the first day of the period (2026-07-31)
DEF-LFL-BOTH-YEARS: A store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years
DEF-LFL-REFIT: Refit weeks from ref_store_closure are excluded for both years; 152 store-weeks comprise the LFL base
DEF-LFL-WEEK53: Week 53 is not LFL (no comparator week last year)
DEF-NET-SALES: Net sales exclude VAT and are measured after returns; store 999 and category ZZ Test are excluded
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop is not part of LFL
CAL-COMPARE: Fiscal weeks aligned by week number (not calendar dates)
assumptions: Period 4 without a fiscal year read as the most recent completed period: FY2026/27 P04 (fiscal weeks 14-17, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30), compared with FY2025/26 P04 (same fiscal week numbers, 2025-07-28 to 2025-08-24)
Request asks for company total (all stores), not regional breakdown
caveats: No data quality issues; query validates against rpt_daily_store_sales control total with zero gap
UTC/Helsinki day boundary spans 29 web order and sales line rows in this period; timestamps converted to Helsinki business dates per company standard

LFL includes 152 store-weeks across five regions (Capital Region, East, North, South, West); new stores (Tampere Lamminpää, Lohja) were not yet in the LFL base in period 4; Savonlinna had already closed

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 22 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal YTD: FY2026/27 weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026), the last completed fiscal week in the warehouse
Like-for-like (LFL) growth, week by week against the same fiscal week numbers of FY2025/26
LFL base: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the range, and a store-week counts only if the store traded in that week in both years
Refit and closure weeks removed for the store concerned in both years (ref_store_closure; Savonlinna's closure)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (store 900) excluded
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, less refund_net on the return date; staff purchases included
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Regions as-is (current dim_store version, five regions including Capital Region)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'How they are doing this year so far' is read as like-for-like net sales growth by region, because it is the company's growth measure and it ranks regions without the effect of store size, closures and refits. Raw net sales would mostly rank regions by size.
'This year so far' is read as FY2026/27 fiscal year to date through week 22 (ending Sunday 4 October 2026), not the calendar year.
Regions are as-is: Capital Region contains its five current stores in both years, and Kouvola is counted under South in both years.
Rank 1 is the highest LFL growth.
caveats: Data problem corrected: 418 lines of store 116 (West) for 15 to 21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 week 21) are in fact_sales_line twice, with the same receipt_id, line_no, timestamp and amount but different sales_line_ids. I kept one row per receipt line. The duplicates added 10,390.53 EUR of net sales to the prior-year figure. After the correction both years match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (this year 5,762,831.03, last year 5,753,182.50 for stores, weeks 1 to 22). Without the correction West's LFL growth would read 1.33% instead of 1.93%, which is still rank 4.

East is the only region below last year. Its reported net sales are down about 11.6% (959,424 against 1,085,463 EUR) because Savonlinna closed on 25 January 2026 and East has 7 stores instead of 8. On a like-for-like basis East is -0.19%.

Pori's refit weeks (8 September to 12 October 2025) fall in last year's weeks 20 to 22 and drop out of both years for Pori, which sits in West. Kuopio's refit (15 June to 26 July 2026) drops out of both years for Kuopio. Both reduce the sales base used in those regions' LFL figures.

If a ranking by plain net sales YTD (all stores, no LFL adjustment) is wanted instead, the order is West 1,815,139; South 1,309,214; East 959,424; Capital Region 948,668; North 730,386 EUR excluding VAT. It mostly reflects store count and size.
The LFL rankings of Capital Region (2.71%), South (2.11%) and West (1.93%) are close, so small differences between them should not be over-read.
Week 53 of FY2025/26 is not part of the comparison; it has no comparator week. The warehouse is loaded only through 4 October 2026, so week 23 onward is not included.

answer.sql: WITH stock_dedup AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_units, closing_value FROM fact_stock_week WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22'), weekly AS (SELECT sd.week_ending_date, cp.category, SUM(sd.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM stock_dedup sd JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = sd.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = sd.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE cs.region = 'West' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 11 AS fiscal_period, category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_stock_value FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot at standard cost (closing_value), summed across stores and products within each week, then averaged across the weeks of the period, never summed across weeks
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P11 = fiscal weeks 44-47, 23 Feb 2026 to 22 Mar 2026, four week-ending Sundays (1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026)
As-is reporting: region and category taken from the current store and product versions (is_current)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); store 999 and web shop 900 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Ranged articles only, no web stock (the stock table holds nothing for the central warehouse)
Query-check run on the final query: no deprecated objects, no lint warnings, unique at category grain
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27, because the request was received on 5 October 2026. Earlier accepted requests asked in a new fiscal year took the year just completed.
'Period 11' is fiscal period 11 (weeks 44-47), not calendar November.
'Average stock value' is the average of the four weekly closing values at standard cost (closing_value). Closing stock is a snapshot, so nothing is added across weeks.

'West region' is the current West region: 10 stores (Tampere Hervanta, Tampere Lielahti, Tampere Kaleva, Nokia, Pori, Rauma, Vaasa, Seinäjoki, Kokkola, Tampere Lamminpää). None of them changed region in the April 2025 reorganisation, so as-is and as-was give the same stores.
Category on the current product version (as-is). The outdoor lighting move from Garden to Electrical took effect on 27 October 2025, before P11, so as-is and as-was agree for this period.
Stock is valued at standard cost, not retail price.
No 'All' or total row was added, since the request asks for a split by category only.
caveats: Duplicate load corrected: the stock snapshot for the week ending 8 March 2026 was loaded twice (9 March 01:00 and 10 March 02:45). The second load re-inserted 7,439 store and article rows, all in 10 stores (the West stores), with identical units, values, receipts and adjustments. Summed as stored, that week would be overstated by about 0.8 million euro company-wide (3.69 million against about 2.87 million in the neighbouring weeks), and the West categories would be inflated. I removed the duplicates with SELECT DISTINCT before summing. The warehouse itself still holds the duplicate rows and needs fixing in the stock load.

Store-level rows were checked for the other three weeks: unique at store, article and week with no negative stock and no test or non-store rows. closing_value equals closing_units times standard unit cost on every row.

The week ending 1 March 2026 has 102 more store and article rows (27,263) than the later weeks (27,161), seen across all stores. I did not investigate the cause and left them in. It looks like articles being delisted, as 543 rows that week are delisted articles against 441 later. Because the weekly values are summed before averaging, this causes only a small difference week to week.
Stock value is at standard cost, which is revalued each April. The FY2025/26 standard costs apply to all four weeks.
The rpt_daily_store_sales control total applies to net sales only, so it was not used for this stock request.

answer.sql:
WITH active AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE f.sale_date > DATE '2025-12-21' - 364 AND f.sale_date <= DATE '2025-12-21'
      AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT m.tier, count(DISTINCT a.member_id) AS active_members
FROM active a
LEFT JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_id = a.member_id AND m.valid_from <= DATE '2025-12-21' AND m.valid_to >= DATE '2025-12-21'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CASE m.tier WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1 WHEN 'Silver' THEN 2 WHEN 'Gold' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks ending with, and including, the as-of week (sale_date > as-of Sunday - 364 and <= as-of Sunday), in any channel
Distinct member_id counted, not member_key
Tier read from the dim_member version valid on the as-of Sunday (valid_from <= date <= valid_to)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out of the purchases
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar from ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2025/26 P08 ends Sunday 21 December 2025
Deprecated objects (stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old tables, rpt.v_ views, channel_code) not used
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 on the request date, 7 October 2026), following the 12 to 27 May 2026 precedent (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35). 'End of period 8' is therefore Sunday 21 December 2025, the last day of FY2025/26 P08 (24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025).
The trailing window is 22 December 2024 to 21 December 2025 inclusive.

Web purchases are dated on sale_date (the order date), as in the accepted active-member queries (REQ-D29, D30). Cancelled and still-processing web orders have no sales lines, so they do not count as purchases.
Returns are ignored: a member counts as active if they made a purchase, even if they later returned it.
Every active member had a tier version valid on 21 December 2025, so the three tiers add up to all active members (29,526).
caveats: Duplicate loads in fact_sales_line: 418 receipt_id and line_no pairs in the window appear twice (for example store key 22 on 15 September 2025, loaded 16 and 23 September 2025). This does not change a distinct member count, so no correction was needed here. It would double-count sales values, receipts and units in any other request.
The window excludes store 999 and ZZ Test. In the window, no member-linked lines were in either, so this filter did not change the total.
Counts are as at the as-of date. Tier is the tier on 21 December 2025, not the member's current tier.
The figures are as-of 21 December 2025 and do not use data after that date (the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026).

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales) DESC) AS rank, n.sku, cur.product_name, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_product cur ON cur.sku = n.sku AND cur.is_current WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-03' AND DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY n.sku, cur.product_name ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Web sales = net sales (EUR excluding VAT) after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or channel_id (neither works across the 3 November 2025 migration)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (no dispatch, not sales)
Returns deducted on their own return date, booked to the web shop (store 900)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; store 999 excluded
Staff purchases included
Product ranked by stable SKU, shown with its current (as-is) name
Dispatch dates converted from UTC to Helsinki time
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales (they omit web sales from 3 November 2025)
assumptions: Top products ranked by web net sales in EUR excluding VAT after returns, not by units or gross value
Period runs from Monday 3 November 2025 (migration date) through Sunday 4 October 2026, the last day loaded in the warehouse; the current part-period FY2026/27 P6 is included
Dispatch on or after 3 November 2025 (Helsinki date) counts, so an order placed shortly before the migration but dispatched on or after 3 November is included
Rank is by SKU; product name and category are the current versions
'Products' means individual SKUs, not categories or subcategories
caveats: The platform migration emptied channel_code from 3 November 2025, so channel_code cannot identify web sales in this period; I used store_id 900 instead, and the legacy views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales would have left web sales out

Total web net sales over the period (EUR 2,150,090.07) matches rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly on all 336 days, so the underlying web figures reconcile; the control total covers all products, not this ranking by itself
296 web orders are still in processing status and have no sales lines, so they are not included; the last few days of the range will be understated until they are dispatched
Cancelled orders and test-article (ZZ Test) web orders were left out

Ranks 8 to 10 are close (EUR 7,411 / 7,130 / 6,890, with the next at 6,680), so the order of the lower places could change if the end date moved or late returns arrive; returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so recent sales may still be reduced
Sales on the last day (4 October 2026) depend on dispatch timestamps converted to Helsinki time; the week ending 4 October is complete in the warehouse

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(f.sale_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines (each line carries its own VAT rate)
Before returns: no refunds deducted
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop 900 excluded
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Store lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
VAT rate change on 1 Sep 2024 (24% to 25.5% general rate) handled through line-level rates
assumptions: August 2024 and September 2024 read as calendar months (1-31 Aug, 1-30 Sep 2024), not fiscal periods
Store sales read as sales in the physical stores; web shop sales left out
Figures are the sum of gross_amount as booked, in EUR including VAT
Reported as-is on the warehouse as loaded; no store or product hierarchy is involved in a monthly total
caveats: No data problems found and no corrections made: no duplicate sales lines, gross_amount agrees with net_amount x (1 + vat_rate) on every line, and the net amounts match rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales_before_returns) exactly for every store-day in both months.

The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, so September carries the higher rate on standard-rated goods. The fall from August to September is partly the VAT change and partly lower volume, since net sales fell from 1,101,807.91 to 964,016.09 excluding VAT.
Store 999 (training store) had 4,282.23 (Aug) and 3,351.71 (Sep) of gross sales; these are excluded.

If web sales are meant to be included, the gross web sales on dispatch date, excluding cancelled and processing orders, were 173,563.99 for August and 160,307.64 for September 2024. They are not in the figures above.
Returns are not deducted, as requested. Refunds are not shown here.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 22 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), dedup AS (SELECT * FROM (SELECT f.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) AS rn FROM fact_sales_line f) WHERE rn = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.net_sales/ly.net_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ROUND(100.0*(ty.net_sales/ly.net_sales-1),2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region=ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year=params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year=params.ty_year ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: LFL growth: LFL-store net sales this year against the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week, physical stores only
LFL base: a store must have been open at least 364 days before the first day of the range
A store-week counts only if the store traded in that week in both years (refit weeks from ref_store_closure and weeks after a closure drop out for that store, in both years)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns booked on their own return date
Staff purchases included
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900), so the web shop and the Online region are out
As-is regions: region taken from the current dim_store version, so the Capital Region includes its six stores for both years and Kouvola (114) sits in South
YTD: FY2026/27 fiscal weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026, the last completed week in the warehouse) against FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22, lined up by fiscal week number
Control total: weekly store net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'How they are doing' has no metric stated. I read it as like-for-like sales growth against last year, which is the company's growth measure and is not distorted by openings, closures or refits. The ranking is by that figure, highest first.
'This year so far' is the fiscal year to date, FY2026/27 weeks 1 to 22, through Sunday 4 October 2026. Week 22 is complete and the warehouse is loaded through it.
Regions are as-is (the current five regions), as the company reports unless as-was is requested.
Store openings and closures are taken from the current dim_store version (Tampere Lamminpää and Lohja are in the base because they opened in 2024). Week 53 is not in range.
caveats: Duplicate load found and corrected: in FY2025/26 week 21 (15 to 21 September 2025), store 116 has every sales line twice (418 receipt lines, 836 rows, with the second copies loaded on 2025-09-23 03:12). This overstates last year's net sales by 10,390.53 EUR against rpt_daily_store_sales. I kept the first-loaded row for each receipt_id and line_no, and after that the weekly totals match the control table. It affects the last-year comparator in the region where store 116 sits, and only slightly, but without the fix that region's growth would be understated. No other duplicates were found from 28 April 2025 onward, and none in returns.

Ranking by plain net sales would look very different. Year-to-date net sales over weeks 1 to 22, in EUR, were West 1,815,139, South 1,309,214, East 959,424, Capital Region 948,668 and North 730,386. Total (not like-for-like) growth against last year was North +3.80%, West +3.24%, Capital Region +2.71%, South +2.11% and East -11.61%. That order is driven mainly by region size and by store events, not by trading performance.

East's non-LFL fall of -11.6% is mostly structural. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 (weeks 7 to 12). Those store-weeks are removed in both years in the LFL figure, which leaves East at -0.19%.

West: Pori's refit (8 September to 12 October 2025, which falls in weeks 20 to 22 of last year) is removed from both years in the LFL figure, so West's LFL (+1.93%) is lower than its total growth (+3.24%). The 22,981 EUR of Pori's current-year sales in those weeks is outside the LFL base.
The gaps between regions in the middle of the table are small (South 2.11%, West 1.93%), so those two places are close.

The web shop (Online region), store 999 and the ZZ Test category were excluded as asked and as per house rules. Excluding the web shop is a scope choice from the request, and the filter on 999 and ZZ Test did not change any region total beyond what the control table shows.
rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt_weekly_sales_by_region were not used (the first omits web sales from 3 November 2025 and the second stopped refreshing in April 2025).

answer.sql: WITH store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27') AND fiscal_period = 4) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-08-03' - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty, lfl_sales ly WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores for the period vs the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
Net sales: excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop excluded from LFL
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
LFL base rule: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the period (open_date <= 2026-08-03 minus 364 days)
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open/close dates and ref_store_closure refit weeks)
Fiscal calendar: P4 is fiscal weeks 14 to 17 in both years (FY2026/27: 3 to 30 Aug 2026; FY2025/26: 28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025), aligned by fiscal week, not calendar date
As-is hierarchy (no regional or category breakdown requested, so no effect on the result)
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' is read as FY2026/27 P4, which is complete (ended 30 Aug 2026) and fully loaded.
'Last year' is read as FY2025/26 P4, the same fiscal weeks 14 to 17, in line with past requests asked during FY2026/27.
A single total was returned because no breakdown (by store or region) was requested.
Open and close dates were taken from the current dim_store version, as in the accepted LFL queries.
'Stores' was read as the physical store estate; the web shop is never part of LFL.
caveats: Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales in FY2026/27 P4, so it is excluded. 38 of the 39 physical stores are in the LFL base for all four weeks.
No refit closures fall in P4 in either year (Pori's refit was 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025 and Kuopio's ended 26 Jul 2026), so no store-weeks were dropped for refits. Week 53 is not involved.

Store-level net sales (stores below 900, store 999 and ZZ Test excluded) matched rpt_daily_store_sales store by store for P4 in both years, with no gaps. I found no duplicate sales or return lines in P4 in either year. No data corrections were needed.
Growth is essentially flat at -0.03% (about EUR 265 lower on roughly EUR 1.01 million).
rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, channel_code and all stg_, bak_, tmp_ and old tables were not used.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY ALL
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 = 29 June to 2 August 2026 (5 weeks, fully loaded)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date), as in the metric dictionary's weeks-of-cover definition
Store scope: Lahti is store_id 108 (physical store only; web orders and click-and-collect collected at Lahti are not included)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Interior Paint taken as the subcategory (Paint & Decorating category), on the current product version (as-is)
Staff purchases included (4 units)
Control total: all-product units for store 108 over the period (3,927) match rpt_daily_store_sales units_sold exactly (35 trading days)
assumptions: 'Period 3 of FY26/27' means fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27, i.e. FY2026/27 P03
'Lahti store' means store_id 108 Lahti, not Tampere Lielahti (116), whose name merely resembles it
'Units sold' means gross units sold, before returns, because the request asks for units sold, not net units; the company metric dictionary defines no returns-adjusted unit measure
'Interior Paint' means the subcategory of that name; the subcategory is the same on the as-was and current product versions, so as-is and as-was give the same answer
No year-on-year comparison or breakdown was requested, so a single figure is given
caveats: No data problems found that needed correcting: no duplicate sales lines, no test articles or training-store rows involved, and the control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales matched

Returns: 6 units of these sales were returned (5 of them within the period). Units net of returns would be 188 on a sale-week basis, or 189 if returns are counted on their return date. The 194 figure is before returns
Interior Paint units in Lahti are in-store sales only; web orders collected at Lahti are not counted (web is recognised in store 900)
I did not run the skill library's query_check script (no script runner in this session); I did the equivalent checks by hand
The 'caveats' reading of units as gross is a choice; if Supply chain wants stock-relevant net units after returns, use 188

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2024/25' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, f.vat_rate * 100 AS vat_rate_pct, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-26' AND DATE '2024-09-22' GROUP BY f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate DESC
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2024/25 P05 = 26 Aug 2024 to 22 Sep 2024 (4 weeks, fully loaded)
VAT from the lines: gross_amount minus net_amount, summed per line, never a flat rate on a net total
VAT rate taken from each line's own vat_rate (24% general rate before 1 Sep 2024, 25.5% from 1 Sep 2024; reduced 14% and 10% unchanged)
Stores = physical stores only (store_id below 900), so the web shop (900) is excluded
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Stores dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total: net sales before returns on the same lines (938,729.24) equals rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days and stores
assumptions: 'VAT charged' means VAT on sales to customers (output VAT on sales lines), before any VAT refunded on returns
'In the stores' means physical stores only, not the web shop
'Period 5 of FY24/25' means fiscal period 5 of FY2024/25, 26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024
The dictionary does not say how returns enter a figure including VAT, so refunds are left out of the table and reported in the caveats instead
As-is vs as-was does not apply because there is no split by region or category
caveats: Period 5 straddles the VAT rate change on 1 Sep 2024, which is why 24% and 25.5% both appear: the 24% VAT is on sales from 26 to 31 Aug and the 25.5% VAT is on sales from 1 to 22 Sep, so the two general-rate rows are not like-for-like

Refunds not netted: VAT on store refunds booked in the period (by return date, same exclusions) was 5,094.72 at 24%, 6,029.57 at 25.5%, 10.48 at 14% and 1.20 at 10% (total 11,135.97). Returns carry the rate of the original sale, so some 24% refunds were booked after 1 Sep. VAT charged net of refunds would be 180017.23-6029.57 = 173,987.66 at 25.5%, 54105.20-5094.72 = 49,010.48 at 24%, 817.62-10.48 = 807.14 at 14%, 150.67-1.20 = 149.47 at 10%
Exclusions: store 999 and ZZ Test lines were removed. In stores below 900 the only change is that store 999 is out, and no ZZ Test lines were in the physical stores in this period

Data checks on the 37,605 store lines in the period: no duplicate receipt/line keys, no nulls, gross_amount agrees with net_amount x (1 + vat_rate) on every line, every line's vat_rate agrees with its product's vat_class, and sale_date agrees with the Helsinki date of sale_ts_utc. No corrections to the data were needed
Web shop VAT (store 900) is not included, as the request asked for stores; the web lines in the period carry about 30,757 of VAT if wanted

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 107 AND cp.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY ALL
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2026/27, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (28 days, four weeks, fully loaded)
Units sold: quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (the weeks-of-cover definition of units sold)
Store scope: store_id 107 (Hyvinkää), identified by stable store_id across versions
As-is product hierarchy: current product version via sku and is_current
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither affects this figure)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 5' as fiscal period 5 of that year (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026)
'Cleaning Products' read as the subcategory of that name, which sits in the category Cleaning & Household; the whole category would be 221 units
'Units sold' is gross units on sales lines, not reduced by returns
Hyvinkää is the physical store 107; web orders are not part of any physical store
caveats: The 136 units include 4 units on 2 staff-purchase lines (132 units on non-staff lines)
No returns of Cleaning Products were booked at Hyvinkää in period 5, so the figure is the same before and after returns
Period 5 ended on 27 Sep 2026 and is fully loaded; the product subcategory is the same in the sale-date and current versions, so as-is and as-was agree
The Hyvinkää day totals in rpt_daily_store_sales (1626 units across all products) match fact_sales_line for the period
No data problems found that needed correcting

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-04-28' AS start_date, DATE '2026-05-03' AS end_date), sales_dedup AS (SELECT f.* FROM fact_sales_line f, params WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY f.receipt_id, f.line_no ORDER BY f.etl_loaded_at, f.sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r CROSS JOIN params JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND r.return_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date), store_sales AS (SELECT store_id, SUM(net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ROUND(ss.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_eur FROM store_sales ss JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date
Staff purchases included in net sales
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Store identity by stable store_id, names and sqm from the current dim_store version
Fiscal year FY2025/26 (28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026, including week 53) as 'last year' with no comparison
Control total: store results checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Biggest' is not defined in the metric dictionary, and I could not ask in the queue. I read it as largest by net sales, the way the company ranks stores in the league table, and not by shop floor area.
No period was given, so I used the last complete fiscal year, FY2025/26 (28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026, 53 weeks). The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026.
The ranking is total net sales for the year, not net sales per trading day, because the request is about size and not productivity.
The web shop is excluded because the request is about stores. It would otherwise be a separate line.
Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026) is not in the top 10 under any reading I tried.
caveats: Correction: store 116 Tampere Lielahti had duplicate sales lines in the warehouse for 15 to 21 September 2025. 418 lines were loaded twice under different sales_line_id values (same receipt_id and line_no), overstating its net sales by 10,390.53 EUR. I kept one copy of each. After that, all stores in the top 12 match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total exactly. Without the correction Lielahti would have ranked 7th, ahead of Kuopio, instead of 8th.

The ranking depends on how 'biggest' is read. By floor area (sqm, current store record) the top 10 would be: Helsinki Pitäjänmäki 8381, Turku Kupittaa 7844, Kuopio 7814, Vantaa Tammisto 7732, Oulu Kaakkuri 7613, Lahti 7036, Tampere Lielahti 6761, Tampere Hervanta 6705, Espoo Lommila 4827, Lappeenranta 4738. Tampere Hervanta, the largest by sales, is only 8th by area. If Leena meant floor area, the answer above is not the one she wants.

Kuopio was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 (6 weeks). It is 7th for FY2025/26 but would drop to about 14th on the current year to date (FY2026/27, 4 May to 4 October 2026). Pori (refit in 2025) also lost five weeks last year.
Totals are by calendar-year-length fiscal year including the 53rd week (27 April to 3 May 2026), as past requests without a comparison did. Every store has the extra week.
Other results change only slightly with a trailing 52-week window (6 October 2025 to 4 October 2026): the same ten stores appear, with Kuopio 9th and Tampere Kaleva 8th.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending), closing AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT c.category, ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM closing c LEFT JOIN sold s ON s.category = c.category ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Weeks of cover = closing stock units at the end of the fiscal week / average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks, for the same grouping
Closing stock is the snapshot at the end of the last fiscal week of the period, summed across stores and products
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date
Last period = last completed fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, ended Sunday 27 September 2026)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product category (current dim_product version via sku and is_current)
Stock only for ranged articles (as held in fact_stock_week); no web stock
assumptions: Read 'last period' as the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (fiscal_year FY2026/27, period 5, 27 July to 27 September 2026), because the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026 and P06 has only one week.
Read 'end of last period' as the closing snapshot on the period's last Sunday, 27 September 2026 (fiscal week 21), not an average over the period's weeks.

Read 'prior four fiscal weeks' literally as the four weeks before the snapshot week: Monday 24 August to Sunday 20 September 2026. The snapshot week itself (21 to 27 September) is not in the sales average.
Used the current category hierarchy (as-is), so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical for all dates.
Cover is computed from category totals across all stores, not as an average of store-level cover figures.
Weeks of cover is rounded to one decimal.
caveats: Web sales are left out of units sold and web stock is not in the stock snapshot (web orders are picked from the central warehouse). Cover therefore describes the physical store network only.
Units sold are gross of returns (sales-line quantity), as the company definition says.

Seasonal (48.8 weeks) and Furniture (29.5 weeks) have very low recent unit sales (524 and 168 units a week). Their cover is sensitive to the seasonal pattern and to a four-week window, and is not a forecast.

Checks run: fact_stock_week has no duplicate store/article rows at 27 September (27,143 rows, all unique, 38 stores); no negative closing units; and unit sales for the window total 69,438, equal to the units_sold control total in rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days and stores. No correction to the data was needed.
The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026. The stock snapshot for 4 October exists but is not the end of last period, so it was not used.

answer.sql: WITH first_version AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from, member_key) AS version_no FROM dim_member) SELECT fv.home_store_id AS store_id, cs.store_name, COUNT(*) AS new_members FROM first_version fv JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = fv.join_date LEFT JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = fv.home_store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE fv.version_no = 1 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: New member: counted on the join date, at the home store in the member's first version in dim_member (the enrolling store)
Online sign-ups are home_store_id 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop) and are shown as their own row
Members counted by distinct member_id (first version only), so later tier, home-store or consent changes do not add or move anyone
Fiscal year FY2025/26 from dim_date (28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026, 53 weeks, week 53 included because there is no comparison)
Store names taken from the current dim_store version (as-is)
Store 999 (training store) excluded; no members enrolled there in the period
assumptions: 'Last year' (asked 7 October 2026, in FY2026/27) is read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, as past accepted requests did. It is not read as calendar 2025.
Because the year is fiscal, it includes week 53 (27 April to 3 May 2026), as unpaired full-year totals do.

'Each store' is read as the enrolling (home) store at sign-up, with online sign-ups under the web shop (900). Stores with no sign-ups in the year would not be listed, but every store in the warehouse has some.
Output is a breakdown by store only, with no total or per-region rows because none were asked for.
caveats: Counts use the enrolling store from the member's first dim_member version, not the current home store. Using the current version would move members who later changed their home store.

If Jukka meant calendar 2025 (1 January to 31 December 2025), the numbers differ: there were 14,629 first-version sign-ups in calendar 2025 against 14,854 in FY2025/26 (all stores and online combined). I did not produce a per-store split for calendar 2025.

Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026, so its 113 sign-ups cover only the part of the year it traded. Stores 136 to 139 are newer openings, so their counts may cover less than a full year of trading.

Regions are not shown. The April 2025 region reorganisation (Capital Region) would change a regional roll-up, so regional totals should be checked against the as-is or as-was reading before they are quoted.
I did not run the query-check control-total comparison against rpt_daily_store_sales, since this is a member count and that table holds only net sales.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-11-03' AS start_date, DATE '2026-10-04' AS end_date), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT p.sku, w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT p.sku, r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), agg AS (SELECT n.sku, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT a.sku, cp.product_name, ROUND(a.web_net_sales, 2) AS web_net_sales FROM agg a JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = a.sku AND cp.is_current ORDER BY a.web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Web net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after line discounts and after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, from fact_web_order via receipt_id = web_order_id
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code (channel_code breaks at the 3 November 2025 migration)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Product = sku (stable natural key), named and categorised as-is from the current dim_product version
Helsinki time for day boundaries, using timezone('Europe/Helsinki', ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales
assumptions: 'Top 10 products' is ranked by web net sales in EUR excluding VAT, not by units or orders, since the request says 'web sales'.
A product is a sku, so all versions of an article are combined.

'Since the platform migration on 3 November 2025' is read as dispatch dates from 3 November 2025 (inclusive) through 4 October 2026, the last day loaded in the warehouse. The range includes the current part-period (FY2026/27 P06, week 1) because the request is open-ended.

Because web sales sit on the dispatch date, orders placed shortly before 3 November 2025 but dispatched on or after it are included, and orders placed near the end of the range but not yet dispatched are not.
Returns are netted on their return date within the range. This means a return of a pre-migration sale made after 3 November 2025 reduces the figure.
caveats: The legacy views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales silently drop web sales after 3 November 2025, and channel_code is no longer filled from that date. I did not use them and identified web by store_id 900, so any dashboard built on them will not match these figures.
Web sales are on the dispatch date, not the order date (sale_date on web lines is the order date). Orders that are cancelled or still processing are not included.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles are filtered out. Returns are deducted, so the figures are net of refunds booked to the web shop.

The query was checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 over the same range (all 336 days present, none outside it). The daily total of 2,150,090.07 EUR matches the control with a gap of 0.00. The check covers all web products, not just the top 10. No duplicate sales lines were found in the web data.
The figures are EUR excluding VAT.

The data runs only to 4 October 2026, so the last few days of returns on recent sales are not yet in. Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so the figures for recently dispatched products may drop a little.
Christmas Decorations Mäntylä 402 (sku 103747) shows a delisting date of 1 June 2026. Its sales in the range come from before then.
The tenth place is clear. The next product, Christmas Decorations Kuusela 620, is at 6,679.65, which is 210 EUR behind, so the top 10 is not a close tie.

answer.sql: SELECT cs.store_id, cs.store_name, 'Interior Paint' AS subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 (29 June to 2 August 2026, 5 weeks), taken from dim_date
Units sold are the quantity on fact_sales_line, dated by sale_date
Store resolved by natural key store_id 108 (Lahti); the fact's store_key was joined to dim_store
Product subcategory taken as-is from the current dim_product version (joined on sku and is_current)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (the filter changed nothing here)
Control total: all store 108 units and net sales before returns in P3 reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales (3,927 units, EUR 67,202.85)
Deprecated tables and views (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old) not used
assumptions: 'Lahti store' is store 108, whose store_name and city are both Lahti. Tampere Lielahti (store 116) only matches the text 'lahti' and was not included.
'Interior Paint' is the subcategory under Paint & Decorating (Exterior Paint is a separate subcategory).
'Period 3 of FY26/27' is FY2026/27 P03, which is complete and fully loaded.
'Units sold' means gross units sold, with returns not netted off. The company definitions give no net-units measure.
Staff purchases are included (4 of the 194 units). They are part of units sold, as for net sales.
The request came from Supply chain. I took it as a store-level sales volume and did not look at stock.
caveats: No corrections to the data were needed. The sales lines for the store and period had no duplicate rows, no negative or zero quantities, and one store version.
As-is and as-was subcategory gave the same result, because no Interior Paint article changed subcategory in this period.

The 194 units are before returns. Returns matched back to these sales lines total 6 units, which would give 188 net of returns. Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so the 6 may still rise for sales late in the period.
The 194 units come from 142 sales lines, and the largest single line is 4 units.
The Lahti store was open and not in a refit closure in P3, so the full 5 weeks apply.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 1) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 10 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share of web sales = click-and-collect net sales / all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date), not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is broken after the 3 Nov 2025 platform migration)
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (no dispatch)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar: periods from dim_date, FY2025/26 P9 = 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026 (5 weeks), P10 = 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026 (4 weeks)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request was received on 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and earlier accepted requests made in FY2026/27 took last year as FY2025/26.
'Periods 9 and 10' read as fiscal periods P9 and P10, with one share per period rather than one combined figure.
Share is of web net sales (money), not of web order counts, because the request says 'web sales'.
Net sales is after returns, per the company net sales definition.
caveats: Web sales were taken from store 900 and the dispatch date, not from channel_code or sale_date. channel_code is empty from 3 Nov 2025, which falls inside P9 and P10, and the legacy views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales leave out web from that date. Neither was used.
Timestamps were converted from UTC to Helsinki dates before assigning periods.

Web net in the share denominator was 200,208.58 EUR for P9 and 123,131.15 EUR for P10. Click-and-collect net was 58,536.07 EUR and 37,861.39 EUR. These totals match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly (200,208.58 and 123,131.15).

Refunds on web orders that were processed in physical stores (148 lines, 5,757.82 EUR net, in P9; 132 lines, 5,011.82 EUR net, in P10) are booked to those stores. They are not in web net sales, in line with the company definition and the control table. Including them would lower the web denominator slightly and move the shares a little.
Both periods are fully loaded and well past the 30-day return window, so the figures are final.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, fulfilment_type, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, w.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, w.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id=r.sales_line_id JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN n.fulfilment_type='click_and_collect' THEN n.net_sales END)/SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS click_and_collect_share_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (6,7,8) GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counted as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (not the order date); cancelled and processing orders excluded
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code or channel_id
Click-and-collect identified through fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, not through channel columns
Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 left out
Fiscal periods taken from dim_date (fiscal_year, fiscal_period)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year that just ended (the request was received 9 October 2026, in FY2026/27), following the 12 to 27 May 2026 precedents
Periods 6 to 8 of FY2025/26 are 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025 (P6, 5 weeks), 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025 (P7, 4 weeks) and 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025 (P8, 4 weeks), all fully loaded
'Share of the web shop's sales' means the company definition of the click-and-collect share, on net sales after returns
Refunds on a click-and-collect order were assigned to click-and-collect through the original sales line, and counted in the web shop only when booked to store 900
One share per period, with no breakdown by month or week
caveats: Neither channel_code nor channel_id works across the 3 November 2025 web-platform migration, which falls inside P7. I used fulfilment_type from fact_web_order to identify click-and-collect, so the shares are consistent across the migration.
Web sales were dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, not on sale_date (the order date). For click-and-collect the dispatch date is when the order was ready for collection.

Some refunds on web lines were processed in physical stores, not booked to the web shop. By the company definition these reduce those stores' net sales and are not in web net sales. They are not netted off here. They are small: for example, 11 click-and-collect and about 28 home-delivery refund lines in the busiest return stores.

The web net sales behind the shares match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in all three periods, both after returns and before returns. Net web sales were EUR 175,588.62 (P6), 154,977.27 (P7) and 225,265.08 (P8). Click-and-collect net sales were EUR 48,901.47, 39,403.04 and 60,899.16.
Before returns the shares would be slightly different: 27.88% (P6), 25.99% (P7) and 27.13% (P8). I reported the after-returns figures because net sales is the company definition.
No duplicate sales lines or return lines turned up in these periods, and I found no other data problem needing correction.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, returns on their own return date
Trading days: days after opening and before closure, outside refit closures, excluding closed holidays (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P2 = weeks 5-8, 1 June to 28 June 2026 (Helsinki business dates)
Current store version (is_current) for names and formats
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Store ranking' read as the store league table, ranked by net sales per trading day (the company definition), not by total net sales
'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2 (4 weeks, 1 to 28 June 2026), the current fiscal year; the period is fully loaded
Ties are not present at unrounded values; rank 1 is the highest net sales per trading day
Kuopio is ranked on the days it traded, as in the accepted P3 league table
Rank, store ID, store name and the ranking measure only; total net sales and trading days left out because they were not asked for
caveats: Kuopio (125) was closed for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it traded only 14 days in the period (1 to 14 June) against 26 for the other stores; its per-day figure covers a shorter, partly pre-closure stretch and is not strictly comparable
Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed holidays, so a full-period store has 26 trading days rather than 28
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales in the period, so it is not listed
Store-level net sales agree with rpt_daily_store_sales for all 38 stores over 1 to 28 June 2026 (gap 0.00 for every store)
Mikkeli (rank 23, 946.76) and Espoo Lommila (rank 24, 946.55) are separated by only 0.21 euro per trading day
Values are in EUR excluding VAT, rounded to 2 decimals; web sales are not part of the store ranking

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_cat AS (SELECT cp.category, d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') AND cp.category IN ('Garden','Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM by_cat ty JOIN by_cat ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Net sales: EUR excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered and collected orders only
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: period 8 is fiscal weeks 31 to 34, 4 weeks (24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025; 25 Nov to 22 Dec 2024)
Prior year lined up by fiscal week and period number, not by calendar date
As-is reporting: categories taken from the current product version, so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical in both years
Control total: my all-category period 8 net sales equal rpt_daily_store_sales for both years (1,435,696.60 and 1,373,188.97, gap 0.00)
assumptions: The request was received 5 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27. I read 'last year' as FY2025/26, the most recently completed fiscal year, and 'the year before' as FY2024/25. This matches how earlier accepted requests were read.
'Period 8' means fiscal period 8 of each fiscal year.
Net sales on the company definition (excluding VAT, after returns), because the request did not say otherwise.
As-is category hierarchy, because the request did not ask for as-was.
Web sales are included, since the category figures cover the whole company. Both categories are reported as separate rows, not combined.
caveats: Correction applied: outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, which is before FY2025/26 P8 but after FY2024/25 P8. I restated FY2024/25 on the current hierarchy so both years are like for like. This moves 19,504.55 EUR of FY2024/25 P8 outdoor lighting sales into Electrical.

On the old as-was categories, FY2024/25 P8 would show Electrical 142,914.41 and Garden 56,269.57, which would make Garden look about 35% down and Electrical about 20% up. That would come purely from the reclassification, not from trading. These as-was figures are my own derived estimate and were not produced by a separate query.
Garden is flat year on year (+0.1%, about 48 EUR). This is a December period, when garden sales are seasonally low.
Both periods are fully loaded and complete. Week 53 is not involved because it falls in period 12.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, because they omit web sales from 3 Nov 2025 onward, which falls inside FY2025/26 P8.
The control-total check was done on all categories together, since rpt_daily_store_sales has no product dimension. The Garden and Electrical rows are not individually reconciled to it.
I found no duplicate sales_line_id values in either period.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, params.fiscal_period AS fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM params JOIN lfl_sales ty ON ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales of LFL stores for the period against the same fiscal weeks last year, matched by fiscal week number

WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank;
definitions_applied: Store league table: ranking by net sales per trading day
Trading days: store open days in the period, excluding closed holidays and refit closures
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, excluding ZZ Test articles and staff purchases included
Physical stores only: store_id < 900, current store versions
assumptions: Period 2 this year interpreted as P2 FY2026/27 (June 1-28, 2026)
