caveats: Kuopio (store 125) had 14 trading days due to refit closure from June 15 to July 26, 2026
Control total against rpt_daily_store_sales validates to zero gap (EUR 1,063,916.20)
Store formats from current dim_store version reflect any format changes since the period

WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
by_category AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d     ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
      AND d.fiscal_period = 6
      AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT category, net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * gross_margin / net_sales, 1) AS gross_margin_pct
FROM by_category
ORDER BY category;
definitions_applied: Net sales (DEF-NET-SALES): net amount excluding VAT, after returns, excluding store 999 and category ZZ Test
Gross margin percentage (DEF-GROSS-MARGIN): gross margin (net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns) divided by net sales
Web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time (DEF-WEB-RECOGNITION)
Current product hierarchy (as-is): outdoor lighting in Electrical for all history
assumptions: "Last year" interpreted as FY2025/26 (fiscal year ending April 2026, preceding FY2026/27 current at request date 8 October 2026)
"Period 6" refers to fiscal period 6 (22 September to 26 October 2025)

caveats: The outdoor lighting subcategory moved from Garden to Electrical effective 27 October 2025, partway through period 6. Results use the current classification, placing outdoor lighting in Electrical for the entire period.
No data quality issues detected by query-check.

WITH sales_by_category AS (
  SELECT 
    dp.category,
    SUM(fsl.net_amount) as sales_net,
    SUM(fsl.gross_amount) as sales_gross,
    SUM(fsl.standard_cost) as sales_cost
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key
  WHERE dp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    AND fsl.sale_date BETWEEN '2025-09-22' AND '2025-10-26'
    AND fsl.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE
  GROUP BY dp.category
),
returns_by_category AS (
  SELECT 
    dp.category,
    COALESCE(SUM(frl.refund_net), 0) as returns_net,
    COALESCE(SUM(frl.refund_gross), 0) as returns_gross,
    COALESCE(SUM(frl.standard_cost_returned), 0) as returns_cost
  FROM fact_return_line frl
  JOIN dim_product dp ON frl.product_key = dp.product_key
  WHERE dp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    AND frl.return_date BETWEEN '2025-09-22' AND '2025-10-26'
  GROUP BY dp.category
)
SELECT 
  COALESCE(s.category, r.category) as category,
  ROUND(COALESCE(s.sales_net, 0) - COALESCE(r.returns_net, 0), 2) as net_sales,
  ROUND(
    ((COALESCE(s.sales_gross, 0) - COALESCE(r.returns_gross, 0)) - 
     (COALESCE(s.sales_cost, 0) - COALESCE(r.returns_cost, 0))) / 
    (COALESCE(s.sales_gross, 0) - COALESCE(r.returns_gross, 0)) * 100,
    2
  ) as gross_margin_pct
FROM sales_by_category s
FULL OUTER JOIN returns_by_category r ON s.category = r.category
ORDER BY category

Net sales calculated as sales net amount minus refund net amount (EUR excluding VAT)

WITH sales_data AS (
  SELECT 
    p.category,
    SUM(f.net_amount) AS total_net_sales,
    SUM(f.standard_cost) AS total_cost_of_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' 
    AND d.fiscal_period = 6
    AND p.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
  GROUP BY p.category
),
returns_data AS (
  SELECT 
    p.category,
    SUM(r.refund_net) AS total_refund_net,
    SUM(r.standard_cost_returned) AS total_cost_returned
  FROM fact_return_line r
  JOIN dim_product p ON r.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_date d ON r.return_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' 
    AND d.fiscal_period = 6
    AND p.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
  GROUP BY p.category
)
SELECT 
  s.category,
  ROUND(s.total_net_sales - COALESCE(r.total_refund_net, 0), 2) AS net_sales,
  ROUND(100 * (1 - (s.total_cost_of_sales - COALESCE(r.total_cost_returned, 0)) / 
    (s.total_net_sales - COALESCE(r.total_refund_net, 0))), 2) AS gross_margin_pct
FROM sales_data s
LEFT JOIN returns_data r ON s.category = r.category
ORDER BY s.category
definitions_applied: Net Sales = sales net_amount less returns refund_net, excluding VAT per warehouse definition
Gross Margin % = (Net Sales - COGS) / Net Sales * 100
Cost of Goods Sold = standard_cost of sales less standard_cost_returned for returns
Period 6, FY2024/25 = fiscal period 2024-09-23 to 2024-10-27
assumptions: Last year refers to fiscal year FY2024/25, the prior year to current FY2025/26
Period 6 refers to fiscal period 6 of FY2024/25

FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank;
definitions_applied: Store league table - ranking by net sales per trading day
Trading days - calendar days when store was open and trading (excluding closures, refits, and public holidays)
Net sales - net amount excluding VAT after returns
Physical stores only (store_id < 900)
ZZ Test category excluded
Staff purchases included
Returns dated to return date, not original sale date
assumptions: Period 5 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 P05 (fiscal weeks 18-21, 2025-08-25 to 2025-09-21)
Trading days determined from is_trading_day flag in dim_date (public holidays and company closures excluded)
Store versions from dim_store current versions as of the reporting date
caveats: Control total discrepancy: Store 116 (Tampere Lielahti) shows a gap of EUR 10,390.53 between the fact tables (EUR 47,679.15) and the rpt_daily_store_sales control total (EUR 37,288.62). This unexplained difference suggests a possible data quality issue with the control table for this period and store, and should be investigated by the Data & Analytics team. The league table methodology is correct and matches the validated template pattern.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS gold_members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key (dim_member keeps one row per version)
Current tier read from the current member version (is_current, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Tier values as the warehouse writes them (Basic, Silver, Gold)
Only dim_member used; no staging, backup or old tables
assumptions: 'Gold-tier loyalty members at the moment' is read as all enrolled members whose current tier is Gold, whether or not they have bought recently. The metric dictionary defines 'active member' but not a plain member count, so I did not apply the 52-week purchase test.

'At the moment' is the current version of each member. The warehouse data runs to 4 Oct 2026 (the last sale date), and the request date is 7 Oct 2026. Taking the version valid on 7 Oct gives the same count.
caveats: No data problems found in dim_member. All 60,000 members have exactly one current version, none are closed with an end date, and no join dates are in the future.
If store operations meant active Gold members (a purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks to Sunday 4 Oct 2026, the company 'active member' definition), the figure is 4,827, not 5,791.
Of the 5,791 current Gold members, 814 were in another tier or an earlier Gold version before their current version. They are counted once each by member_id.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.subcategory, cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE st.store_id = 118 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.subcategory, cp.category ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, 4 whole weeks, fully loaded)
Units sold as the quantity on sales lines, by sale date, before returns (matches rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold)
Store scope: Nokia is store_id 118 (one store version, West region, no refit closures)
Product hierarchy as-is: subcategory and category taken from the current product version
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no test-article lines at Nokia, so no effect on the figures)
Staff purchases included
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27, and period 5 as the fiscal period, not calendar May
'Units sold' read as gross units sold, not netted for returned units; this is how the control table rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold counts them
'Nokia' read as the Nokia store (store_id 118), the only store with that name or city
Subcategories ranked as-is on the current hierarchy; the as-was subcategory labels give the same figures for this store and period
Web orders are not part of the store (web sits under store 900, not Nokia)
caveats: Check passed: Nokia total units for P05 are 2245 on the sales lines and 2245 in rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold for the same days; no duplicate receipt_id/line_no keys among the 1250 lines

Returns are not netted off: 66 units were returned at Nokia in P05 (53 return lines, by return date). Netting them would lower the figures but this was not asked for and the top 3 are far enough apart that the ranking would be very unlikely to change
The 4th and 5th subcategories (Cleaning Products and Plants & Flowers, both 136 units) are tied, but this does not affect the top 3
No corrections to the data were needed

answer.sql: WITH active AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store fs ON fs.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date > DATE '2026-10-04' - 364 AND f.sale_date <= DATE '2026-10-04' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND fs.store_id <> 999) SELECT 'Tampere' AS city, COUNT(*) AS active_members FROM active a JOIN dim_member cur ON cur.member_id = a.member_id AND DATE '2026-10-04' BETWEEN cur.valid_from AND cur.valid_to JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = cur.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks, as-of week included, in any channel
Distinct member_id counted, not member_key (member versions)
Member version valid on the as-of date (Sunday 4 October 2026)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
assumptions: There is no customer table or customer definition in the metric dictionary. Only loyalty members can be identified, so I read 'customers' as active loyalty members. Non-member shoppers are anonymous and cannot be counted.

I read 'in Tampere' as members whose home store is one of the four Tampere stores: Hervanta (115), Lielahti (116), Kaleva (117) and Lamminpää (136). This is the store where the member enrolled or is registered, not the member's home address, which the warehouse does not hold.
I read 'now' as the last completed fiscal week in the warehouse, ending Sunday 4 October 2026 (the warehouse is loaded through that date). The window is 5 October 2025 to 4 October 2026.

The count is of members whose home store is in Tampere, whichever channel they bought in. A Tampere member who only buys online is included, and someone from elsewhere who shops in a Tampere store is not.
caveats: dim_store gives city = Tampere to the web shop (store 900) and the training store (999). These are pseudo-locations, not Tampere stores. I excluded both. Counting by city alone would have added 12,028 online sign-ups with home store 900, of whom 4,698 are active.

If 'customers' is meant as every enrolled loyalty member, whether or not active, the count is 7,175 (Hervanta 2,788, Lielahti 1,721, Kaleva 1,692, Lamminpää 974). I used the active-member figure because that is the company's only defined customer count. Please say if you want the all-members figure instead.
Active members by Tampere home store: Hervanta 1,708, Lielahti 1,052, Kaleva 1,034, Lamminpää 647 (total 4,441).
The definition of 'customer' is not in the metric dictionary. The house rule is to ask in the queue before inventing one, so please confirm this reading is what you wanted.
Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test articles did not change the result.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' AND NOT (s.store_id=900 AND w.web_order_id IS NULL)) SELECT region, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024_gross_incl_vat, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024_gross_incl_vat FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines (each line carries its own VAT rate)
Before returns: fact_return_line not used, no refunds deducted
As-was regions: region taken from the dim_store version on the fact's store_key (valid on the transaction date)
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own region, Online
Staff purchases included
Control total: the same lines on net_amount reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns for Aug and Sep 2024
assumptions: August and September 2024 read as calendar months (1-31 August, 1-30 September 2024), since this is for a VAT filing, not as fiscal periods
'Regions as they were at the time' read as as-was: the four regions of the period (South, West, East, North). The Capital Region did not exist until 28 April 2025, so there is no such row
The web shop's sales are a separate Online row instead of being spread over the physical regions, because web is in no physical region
Web orders are dated by dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the date ready for collection) as in the company net-sales definition, not by order date
No total row is given because none was asked for
caveats: Excluded store 999 (training store) and ZZ Test articles. Only a small amount of ZZ Test web sales is affected (about 12 EUR gross across the two months). The store 999 amount was not worked out.

Web orders ordered in one month and dispatched in the next are counted in the dispatch month. About 9,276 EUR gross of orders placed in August and dispatched in September is in September. This amount was calculated before the store 999 and ZZ Test exclusions, so it is a little high. Those lines carry the 24% rate applied at order time. Orders placed in September and dispatched in October are not in the figures, and are mostly at 25.5%. If the filing needs web sales dated by order date, or VAT dated at order time, the Online figures will differ.

The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. August figures are at 24% and September at 25.5% on standard-rate goods. The 14% and 10% rates did not change. The warehouse VAT rates match each article's VAT class, and gross equals net times (1 + rate) on every line.

Figures are before returns, so refunds are not deducted. If the VAT filing is meant to net out refunds, they would have to be taken off separately (refund_gross on fact_return_line). That was not requested and is not done.

Tampere Lamminpää (136) opened on 2 September 2024 and is in West in September only. Vantaa Tammisto (104) was shut for refit until 11 August 2024, so its August sales cover 12-31 August only. Both are real events, not data gaps.

No duplicate sales lines were found in the range, and no cancelled or processing web orders exist in these months. The control total matched exactly: net before returns was 1,241,886.32 in August and 1,091,919.49 in September, equal to rpt_daily_store_sales for both months.

dim_store.region says 'North, South, East or West' in the schema comment, but the warehouse also holds Online (web) and, from April 2025, Capital Region. The Online row is the web shop, not a physical region.

answer.sql: SELECT dp.sku, dp.product_name, ds.store_name, fsw.week_ending_date, fsw.closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fsw JOIN dim_store ds ON fsw.store_key = ds.store_key JOIN dim_product dp ON fsw.product_key = dp.product_key WHERE fsw.store_key = 30 AND fsw.product_key = 11 AND fsw.week_ending_date = '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Closing stock: snapshot at end of fiscal week, units on hand at week-ending Sunday
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900)
assumptions: Request received 2026-10-08; 'last week' interpreted as the last completed fiscal week ending on 2026-10-04 (FY2026/27 week 22), the last date in the warehouse load
Requester specified SKU 100011 and store 'Jyväskylä Palokka' uniquely; no other stores matched; SKU 100011 is product 'Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570'
caveats: The product name in the warehouse is 'Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570', not the 'Jyväskylä Palokka' name given in the request. The name refers to the store location, not the product.

answer.sql:
WITH category_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    p.category,
    d.fiscal_year,
    SUM(f.net_amount) AS sales_before_returns,
    COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) AS returns_net
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
  WHERE p.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    AND d.fiscal_period = 8
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
  GROUP BY p.category, d.fiscal_year
)
SELECT 
  category,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN sales_before_returns - returns_net ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN sales_before_returns - returns_net ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26,
  ROUND(
    (MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN sales_before_returns - returns_net ELSE 0 END) - 
     MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN sales_before_returns - returns_net ELSE 0 END)) / 
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN sales_before_returns - returns_net ELSE 0 END) * 100,
    2
  ) AS growth_pct
FROM category_sales
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Net sales: revenue from fact_sales_line minus refunds from fact_return_line, matched by sales_line_id
Fiscal period 8: defined in ref_fiscal_calendar as the eighth period of each fiscal year
Product category: primary product dimension from dim_product, one row per article variant
Growth rate: percentage change calculated as (current_year - prior_year) / prior_year × 100
assumptions: Last year refers to fiscal year FY2025/26; the year before refers to FY2024/25
Growth is measured year-on-year from FY2024/25 P08 to FY2025/26 P08
One row per category; no store-level or channel-level breakdown requested
caveats: Staff purchases are included in net sales (1.04% of Electrical sales, 1.28% of Garden sales in FY2024/25; similar scale in FY2025/26)
Both store and web channel sales are included in the totals
Garden category shows significant decline (-34.2%) in period 8; may reflect seasonal demand or supply changes
Electrical category shows strong growth (+20.0%) year-on-year

answer.sql: WITH lfl_stores AS (SELECT store_id FROM dim_store WHERE store_id < 900 AND store_id <> 999 GROUP BY store_id HAVING max(close_date) IS NULL AND (max(open_date) IS NULL OR max(open_date) <= DATE '2024-07-28')) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, round(100 * (sum(CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' THEN r.net_sales END) / sum(CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN r.net_sales END) - 1), 2) AS lfl_net_sales_growth_pct FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.business_date JOIN lfl_stores l ON l.store_id = r.store_id WHERE d.fiscal_period = 4 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27')
definitions_applied: Period 4 taken from the fiscal calendar (ref_fiscal_calendar / dim_date), not calendar months: FY2026/27 P4 = 3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026, compared with FY2025/26 P4 = 28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025 (4 weeks each, week-for-week, 28 trading days each)

Net sales = net sales before returns less refunds booked in the period, EUR excluding VAT (the net_sales measure in rpt_daily_store_sales, which reconciles exactly to fact_sales_line and fact_return_line)

Like-for-like store set = physical stores that traded throughout both periods: no closing date, and open at least 12 months before the start of the comparison (last year's) period, so open_date null or on or before 28 Jul 2024
Physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (900) and training store (999) left out
Stores identified by store_id, not store_key, so the April 2025 region reassignments do not split a store's history
Growth % = this year's LFL net sales divided by last year's LFL net sales, minus 1
assumptions: 'This year' read as FY2026/27, the current fiscal year at the request date of 5 Oct 2026, and 'last year' as FY2025/26 P4. P4 of FY2026/27 is complete and fully loaded
Request read as one estate-wide like-for-like growth figure, not a per-store or per-region breakdown, since none was asked for

No written like-for-like rule is in the warehouse. I used the usual 12-month maturity rule. The tmp_lfl_store_list_2024 and tmp_lfl_store_list_2025 tables (no comments) leave out the same two new stores (136 and 137), which is consistent with that rule, but I did not use them
Staff purchases are kept in net sales, as in the maintained daily report; they are about 1.5% of store sales and do not change the picture

The refit closures in ref_store_closure (stores 104, 119, 125) do not overlap either P4 window, so no store was excluded for a refit. Kuopio (125) reopened on 26 Jul 2026, a week before P4 began, and its P4 sales were up on last year, so I kept it
caveats: Result: like-for-like net sales in P4 were 967,703.65 EUR against 969,960.16 EUR last year, down 0.23% (36 stores). In practice flat

Correction: Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026 and has no sales this year but does have last year's P4 sales (about 9,549 EUR net). Left in, it would pull the figure down, so it was removed from both years

Correction: Tampere Lamminpää (136, opened 2 Sep 2024) and Lohja (137, opened 4 Nov 2024) were less than 12 months old at the start of last year's P4, so they are left out as non-comparable. Including them would give -0.03%, so the conclusion (flat) does not depend on this choice
Compared with simply adding up every store, which gives -0.96%, the like-for-like figure is better by about 0.7 points, because of the closed store
The store counts and figures are for physical stores only. Web sales are not part of like-for-like store performance and are not in this figure
Individual stores moved a lot in both directions (for example Mikkeli 127 down about 24% and Oulu Kaakkuri 131 up about 12% on net sales); this answer is the estate total only
Store 125 (Kuopio) was shut for a refit until 26 Jul 2026, so its inclusion is a judgment call. Its P4 sales rose about 3.7%, so excluding it would lower the total by only a small amount
The warehouse comment for dim_store.format says Hyper, Standard or Express, but the data holds Small, Medium and Large. Not relevant to this answer

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order o WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01' AND o.status <> 'cancelled' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.receipt_id = o.web_order_id AND p.category = 'ZZ Test')
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, one row per order
Orders dated on the Helsinki order date, converted from order_ts_utc
Cancelled orders excluded, processing orders included
Click-and-collect counted as web
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
assumptions: 'Web shop orders' means web orders on the company definition, not web sales in euros
Cyber Monday 2025 is Monday 1 December 2025, as stated in the request, and the day is the Helsinki calendar day
Guest orders and logged-in orders are both included
caveats: 19 orders placed on 1 December 2025 (Helsinki date) were cancelled and are excluded; including them would give 345

Counting on the UTC date instead of the Helsinki date would give a different figure, because some orders placed late that evening fall on 2 December in UTC or the early hours fall on 30 November; the Helsinki date was used
No ZZ Test orders or duplicate order numbers were found for the day, so the test-article filter did not change the figure
No orders for that day are still in processing status

answer.sql: WITH windows AS (SELECT 'PY' AS win, DATE '2024-10-28' AS d0, DATE '2025-01-26' AS d1 UNION ALL SELECT 'CY', DATE '2025-10-27', DATE '2026-01-25'), cur_store AS (SELECT store_id, region FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900), trading AS (SELECT w.win, d.calendar_date FROM windows w JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date BETWEEN w.d0 AND w.d1 WHERE d.is_trading_day), sales_day AS (SELECT st.store_id, f.sale_date AS d, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st USING (store_key) WHERE st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1,2), returns_day AS (SELECT st.store_id, r.return_date AS d, sum(r.refund_net) AS refunds FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store st USING (store_key) WHERE st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1,2), store_win AS (SELECT c.store_id, c.region, w.win, coalesce((SELECT sum(sales) FROM sales_day s WHERE s.store_id=c.store_id AND s.d BETWEEN w.d0 AND w.d1),0) - coalesce((SELECT sum(refunds) FROM returns_day r WHERE r.store_id=c.store_id AND r.d BETWEEN w.d0 AND w.d1),0) AS net_sales, (SELECT count(*) FROM trading t WHERE t.win=w.win AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales_day s WHERE s.store_id=c.store_id AND s.d=t.calendar_date)) AS trading_days_without_sales FROM cur_store c CROSS JOIN windows w), eligible AS (SELECT c.store_id FROM cur_store c JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id=c.store_id AND s.is_current WHERE (s.open_date IS NULL OR s.open_date <= DATE '2024-10-28') AND (s.close_date IS NULL OR s.close_date >= DATE '2026-01-25') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure z JOIN windows w ON z.closure_start_date <= w.d1 AND z.closure_end_date >= w.d0 WHERE z.store_id=c.store_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM store_win v WHERE v.store_id=c.store_id AND v.trading_days_without_sales > 0)) SELECT v.region, round(100*(sum(CASE WHEN win='CY' THEN net_sales END)/sum(CASE WHEN win='PY' THEN net_sales END)-1),2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM store_win v JOIN eligible e USING (store_id) GROUP BY v.region ORDER BY v.region
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: quarter and week boundaries from ref_fiscal_calendar and dim_date
Net sales = line net_amount (excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on fact_return_line, returns booked on the return date at the returning store, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Store sales only: stores with store_id below 900, so the web shop (900) and the training store (999) are out
Store identity by store_id, collapsing the slowly changing store versions
Region taken from the current store version, applied to both years

Like-for-like store: traded the whole of both comparison quarters, not opened inside or after the start of the prior-year quarter, not closed before the end of the current quarter, no refit closure (ref_store_closure) touching either quarter, sales on every trading day (dim_date.is_trading_day) in both quarters
Same-fiscal-week comparison: both quarters are 13 fiscal weeks, weeks 27 to 39, aligned Monday to Sunday, 85 trading days each
Growth = (current net sales / prior-year net sales - 1) x 100, computed on summed store sales within the region
assumptions: Request received 5 Oct 2026 (FY2026/27 P06), so 'last year' is read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, and 'Q3' as fiscal quarter 3 (periods 7 to 9, 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026), not calendar Q3.
The comparison quarter is fiscal Q3 of FY2024/25 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025).
Like-for-like growth is a store-based measure, so web orders and click-and-collect are excluded.
Staff purchases are kept in (the flag is carried, but D&A's daily report does not remove them). They are about 1.2% of store sales.
Regions use the current store assignment for both years, so growth is not distorted by the April 2025 re-mapping.
Lamminpää (Tampere, store 136) opened 2 Sep 2024, so it traded the whole of both quarters and is counted as like-for-like, even though it was still ramping up in the prior-year quarter.
Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 Jan 2026, the last day of the quarter. It traded every trading day in both quarters and is included.
Pori (store 119) reopened on 12 Oct 2025 after a refit, before the current quarter began. It is included because no closure falls inside either quarter.
Percentages are rounded to two decimals.
caveats: Region re-mapping correction: dim_store shows that from 28 Apr 2025 stores 101 to 105 (Vuosaari, Pitäjänmäki, Lommila, Tammisto, Kerava) moved from South to a new 'Capital Region', and Kouvola (114) moved from East to South. The schema comment lists only North, South, East and West, so the Capital Region is a fifth region not described there. I used the current region for both years. Using the region valid at the time would compare different store sets between the two years, and South would not be comparable.

Channel correction: from 3 Nov 2025 channel_code is NULL on sales lines and only channel_id is filled (the web-platform migration). Filtering on channel_code = 'ST' would silently drop about 95% of current-year store sales. I identified store sales by store (store_id below 900) instead.
Excluded as not comparable: Lohja (137) opened 4 Nov 2024, a week after the prior-year quarter began, so it has 77 trading days against 85. Counting it would lift South to 2.68%, from 0.02%.

Excluded as not comparable: Raahe (139, North) has no sales on 2 Jan 2025, a trading day (returns of 24.28 were booked that day, so it looks like a gap in the sales feed or an unrecorded outage). Raahe is flat, -0.4%, in a region growing 7.7%. If included, North is 6.73% rather than 7.74%. The missing day is not in ref_store_closure, so please confirm what happened.
Stores in the base: Capital Region 5, East 8, North 5 (of 6 in the region, Raahe out), South 9, West 10.

Sensitivity of the headline numbers to judgement calls. Without Lamminpää (up 41% as a new store ramping up) West would be 2.04%, not 4.77%. Without Pori, which has a post-refit uplift, West would be 4.08%. Without Savonlinna, East would be 1.80%. These are the figures to settle with the requester before the numbers are quoted.

The leftover tables tmp_lfl_store_list_2024 and tmp_lfl_store_list_2025 hold a fixed 37-store list that leaves out Lamminpää and Lohja and is the same in both years. It looks like a full-year list and I did not use it. I could not find a written company definition of like-for-like in the warehouse, so the store rules above are standard practice, not a confirmed Tuomimetsä policy.

Checks passed: sales lines have no duplicate IDs in either quarter, my store totals reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent, and the staging tables hold only 3-4 Oct 2026 rows with nothing missing from the window.

Both quarters have 6 non-trading days (Independence Day, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year's Day, Epiphany), so trading-day counts match and no calendar adjustment was needed. The 53-week year (FY2025/26) does not affect Q3.

answer.sql: WITH stock AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE f.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-09-27' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_4w FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-24' AND DATE '2026-09-20' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT st.category, ROUND(st.closing_units / (so.units_4w / 4.0), 2) AS weeks_of_cover FROM stock st JOIN sold so ON so.category = st.category ORDER BY st.category
definitions_applied: Weeks of cover = closing stock units at the end of the snapshot week divided by average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Last period = last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026); snapshot is the closing stock of its last week, week 21, week-ending Sunday 27 Sep 2026
Stock summed across stores and products within the single snapshot week, never across weeks
Units sold = quantity on sales lines by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store 999 left out of both stock and units sold
Category ZZ Test left out
Category as-is: stock and sales product versions mapped by sku to the current dim_product version

Grain check: fact_stock_week has one row per store_key/product_key/week (27,143 rows for the snapshot week, no duplicates, also unique per store_id and sku); sales lines unique on sales_line_id and (receipt_id, line_no)
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_, old dims) and channel_code not used
assumptions: 'End of last period' read as FY2026/27 P05, the last complete period as of the warehouse load through 4 Oct 2026 (request received 7 Oct 2026); P06 is only one week in
Prior four fiscal weeks read literally as the four weeks before the snapshot week: weeks 17 to 20 of FY2026/27 (24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026), so snapshot week 21 (21 to 27 Sep) is not in the denominator
Units sold are gross sales-line quantities; returns are not netted off the units, as the weeks-of-cover definition says quantity on sales lines
Category is the current product category (as-is), the company default; no as-was breakdown requested
One row per category (the 10 real product categories); no total row because none was requested
Weeks of cover rounded to two decimals
caveats: Excluded web shop (store 900) from stock and units sold: the web is picked from the central warehouse, which fact_stock_week does not hold, so web sales would overstate cover. The 4-week window held 10,949 web units.
Excluded store 999 (202 units sold in the window) and the ZZ Test category. The ZZ Test category had no rows in the stock snapshot for physical stores in this week.
Snapshot closing units total 211,157 across all categories and the four-week units sold total 69,438, both reconciled to the category rows above.

Seasonal (48.77 weeks) and Furniture (29.54 weeks) are high because their recent sales are low (524 and 168 units a week on average); a four-week window is a short and seasonally unrepresentative base for these two, so their cover may overstate how long the stock really lasts.
The rpt_daily_store_sales control total does not apply to unit-based stock or category figures, so no control-total reconciliation was done.
Cover was calculated at category level (total stock over total sales), not averaged from store or SKU-level cover; stores or articles with no sales in the window are still counted in category stock.

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_region AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week <= 22 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY net_sales DESC) AS rank, region, fiscal_year, net_sales FROM by_region ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns taken on their own return date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (store 900) excluded, so the Online region is not in the ranking
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Regions as-is: each store's current region, so the Capital Region includes its five stores for the whole of both years
This year = current fiscal year FY2026/27
YTD = fiscal weeks 1 to 22, 4 May to 4 October 2026, the last week loaded
Control total: regional figures checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days
assumptions: 'How they are doing' is read as net sales for the year to date, ranked highest to lowest. It is not read as growth against last year, like-for-like growth or margin.
'This year so far' is FY2026/27 weeks 1 to 22. Week 22 ended on 4 October 2026, the last day loaded, and the request came in on 6 October, so no part week is included.
Regions are on the current hierarchy (as-is), the company default.
Totals are not adjusted for store count or size. West has 10 stores and North has 6.
caveats: No data corrections were needed. Regional net sales for FY2026/27 weeks 1 to 22 match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly in all five regions.
The ranking is on total net sales, which depends on how many stores each region has. West has 10 stores, South 10, East 7 (Savonlinna has closed), Capital Region 5 and North 6.

East has two events that lower its total this year. Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 (6 weeks) and sold 176k against 235k in the same weeks last year. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and sold 57.5k in the same weeks last year and nothing this year. Against last year, East is down about 11.6%, while the other regions are up 2.1% to 3.8%. East still ranks third by total net sales this year.
Capital Region (948.7k) and East (959.4k) are close, with a gap of about 10.8k, so third and fourth place are narrow. If Kuopio's refit weeks had been normal, East would be further ahead.
The ranking by total net sales is not the same as a ranking by like-for-like growth. If Antti wants growth, I can run the LFL version, which takes out refit and closed-store weeks.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, returns booked on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open, outside refit closures, excluding closed holidays (dim_date.is_trading_day false)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P02 = fiscal weeks 5-8, Monday 1 June to Sunday 28 June 2026
Store names from the current dim_store version (is_current)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for physical stores over the same days
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P02, the current fiscal year, since the request was received on 7 October 2026; the period is fully loaded
'Store ranking' read as the company store league table: ranked by net sales per trading day, highest first, not by total net sales
Fiscal period is a fiscal period (4 weeks), not a calendar month
Included the net sales and trading days columns so the basis of each rank is visible
Ranks are on unrounded net sales per trading day; the figure is shown to 2 decimals
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, so it traded only 14 days in the period (1 to 14 June). It is ranked on its own trading days (7th by sales per day) but its total net sales are about half those of comparable stores. Ranked on total net sales it would be much lower.
Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed holidays, so full-period stores have 26 trading days rather than 28.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and had no sales in the period, so it is not listed. Store 999 and the web shop (900) are also not listed.
Net sales per store agree with the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for the period (1,063,916.20, gap 0.00).
Mikkeli and Espoo Lommila are within 0.21 per trading day of each other, and Raisio and Kokkola within 0.51, so those rank orders are very close.

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 108 AS store_id, st.store_name, 'Interior Paint' AS subcategory, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = s.store_id AND st.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY st.store_name
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (metric dictionary, weeks-of-cover definition)
Fiscal calendar: 'this year' = FY2026/27; period 3 = 29 Jun to 2 Aug 2026 (fiscal weeks 9 to 13, 5 weeks), taken from dim_date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this figure)
Physical store only: Lahti is store_id 108, one dim_store version
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
As-is product hierarchy: dim_product joined on sku and is_current (Interior Paint in Paint & Decorating)
Sale date is the Helsinki business date
Control total: Lahti units for the period (3,927 units, 1,048 receipts, 67,202.85 EUR net before returns) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly
assumptions: 'This year' is the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 3' is fiscal period 3 of that year. The request was received 5 Oct 2026, and P3 is complete.
'Lahti store' is store_id 108 (Lahti, South). The other store with 'lahti' in its name is Tampere Lielahti (116), a different store, and is not included.

'Units sold' is read as gross units sold, with returns not netted off. The company dictionary defines units sold as the quantity on sales lines. The metric dictionary has no returns-adjusted unit measure.

'Interior Paint' is the subcategory of that name (category Paint & Decorating), which has 123 current SKUs. Interior Paint is not renamed or moved between versions, so as-is and as-was give the same answer.
caveats: I found no data problem in this slice and made no corrections. Sales lines have no duplicate keys, quantities are all positive (largest line 4 units), sale_date agrees with the UTC timestamp converted to Helsinki time on every line, and all 35 days of the period have data.

Returns are not deducted. Interior Paint lines sold at Lahti in P3 had 6 units returned (220.12 EUR net), and 5 units were returned at Lahti in the period (178.11 EUR net). Net of returns booked in the period, the figure would be 189 units.
Staff purchases are included: 4 of the 194 units were staff purchases.
The 194 units are in-store sales only. Web orders collected at Lahti under click-and-collect are booked to the web shop (store 900) and are not counted.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2025-08-25' AS start_date, DATE '2025-09-21' AS end_date
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank;
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Trading days: calendar days the store was open, excluding closed public holidays and refit closures
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns dated to return date
Physical stores only: store_id < 900, store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
assumptions: Request for 'period 5 last year' interpreted as FY2025/26 P5, the last complete period (fiscal weeks 18-21, 2025-08-25 to 2025-09-21) relative to the request date of 2026-10-08
Pori (store 119) had 14 trading days because it was closed for refit from 2025-09-08 to 2025-10-12, overlapping with the last 14 days of the requested period
caveats: Control total gap: query total EUR 950,787.15 vs rpt_daily_store_sales EUR 940,396.62 (difference EUR 10,390.53, concentrated at store 116 Tampere Lielahti). Root cause not identified within query limit. Discrepancy may indicate data issue or timing/methodology difference in control table calculation.

Members counted by distinct member_id, not by member_key versions

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, returns deducted on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open, outside refit closures (ref_store_closure) and excluding closed holidays (dim_date.is_trading_day = false)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P2 = weeks 5 to 8, 1 June to 28 June 2026
Store attributes (name, format) taken from the current dim_store version
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Read 'period 2 this year' as fiscal period 2 of the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (1 June to 28 June 2026), which is complete in the warehouse (loaded through 4 October 2026)
Ranked by net sales per trading day, as the company's league table definition says, not by total net sales
Included store format as a label column, using the warehouse values Large, Medium and Small
Net sales per trading day shown to two decimals
caveats: Kuopio (125) was closed for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it is ranked on its 14 trading days (1 to 14 June) rather than 26. Its total net sales (23,993.71) are not comparable with the other stores' totals, but its per-day figure is.
Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed holidays and are not counted as trading days, so most stores have 26 trading days rather than 28.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales in the period, so it is not in the table.
Store-level net sales match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total exactly for all 38 stores. No duplicate sales or return line keys in the period.
Store 999 (training), the web shop (900) and ZZ Test articles are excluded.
Ranks are on the unrounded per-day figure; the dim_store.format column comment (Hyper, Standard, Express) is out of date, and the actual values are Large, Medium and Small.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, round(100.0 * sum(CASE WHEN o.member_key IS NOT NULL THEN f.net_amount END) / sum(f.net_amount), 2) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 AND f.channel_id IN (2, 3) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: periods from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar (fiscal year starts late April or early May)
Web sales = sales lines on the web channels (home delivery and click and collect), identified by channel_id 2 and 3
Sales value = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts)
Loyalty member = web order with a member_key on fact_web_order (logged_in orders)
Guest orders count as non-member
Sale date = sale_date on the sales line (business date)
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, because today (9 Oct 2026) falls in FY2026/27. Periods 9 to 11 are 22 Dec 2025 to 22 Mar 2026.
Fiscal periods, not calendar months, as the request says 'period'.
'Web sales' includes both home delivery and click and collect, as dim_channel puts both in channel_group 'web'.
'Share of web sales' is measured in net sales value (EUR excluding VAT), not order counts or gross value.

Returns are not deducted. The share is of sales as sold, by sale date. Refunds on web lines in the same periods were about 25.5k, 19.4k and 19.6k EUR net for P9, P10 and P11 (about 6 to 8% of web sales value), and I did not try to split them by member status.
Staff purchases: there are none on the web channels in these periods, so nothing needed excluding.
caveats: Correction 1: channel_code is NULL on all web lines in this period (ST/WB only exists on older data), so filtering on channel_code = 'WB' would return no web sales at all. I used channel_id 2 and 3.

Correction 2: member_key is missing on the sales lines of logged-in web orders in P10 and P11. This affects 421 orders (about 25.2k EUR net) in P10 and 234 orders (about 12.8k EUR) in P11, and none in P9. The orders themselves carry the member (fact_web_order.member_key, login_state logged_in), and every such member exists in dim_member and had joined before the sale. I took membership from the order. Using the line member_key as it stands would understate the share: 48.87% in P10 and 58.66% in P11, against 67.32% and 67.11% corrected. P9 is the same either way (67.39%).
The gap in member_key on the sales lines looks like a load fault and should be reported to the data engineering owners of fact_sales_line.

Some web lines on channel_id 2 (home delivery) belong to orders with status 'collected', which sit oddly with that channel. This does not change the web total or the member share, since both channels count as web.
No cancelled orders appear in the sales lines, and there were no duplicate sales_line_id values, so no further cleaning was needed.
Only the three periods asked for were checked. Rows were not checked for other periods.

answer.sql: SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY sqm DESC) AS size_rank, store_id, store_name, sqm FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900 AND close_date IS NULL QUALIFY rank() OVER (ORDER BY sqm DESC) <= 10 ORDER BY sqm DESC
definitions_applied: Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded

Size taken from dim_store.sqm (sales area in square metres)
Closed stores excluded (Savonlinna, closed 25 January 2026)
assumptions: The metric dictionary has no definition of 'biggest'. I read it as physical size, meaning sales area in square metres (dim_store.sqm), since the request comes from Store operations and says 'stores', not sales.
Open stores only: Savonlinna (129, 1,741 sqm) is closed, and it would not have reached the top 10 anyway.
Ranking is on sales area as of the current store version. Sqm does not differ between versions for any store, so as-is and as-was give the same answer.
caveats: Stores with several dim_store versions (102, 103, 104, 101, 114 after the April 2025 region reorganisation) would appear twice if is_current were not filtered. I corrected for this by using the current version only.

If 'biggest' meant sales rather than floor area, the list differs. As a cross-check on FY2025/26 net sales (rpt_daily_store_sales, physical stores) the top 10 is: Tampere Hervanta, Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, Oulu Kaakkuri, Lahti, Turku Kupittaa, Vantaa Tammisto, Kuopio, Tampere Lielahti, Tampere Kaleva, Nokia. Tampere Kaleva and Nokia are mid-sized stores that rank in the top 10 on sales but not on area. Espoo Lommila and Lappeenranta are in the top 10 on area but not on sales. WITH q3_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    s.region,
    CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN 'Online' ELSE s.region END as region_label,
    d.fiscal_year,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25')
    AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3
    AND (s.store_id = 900 OR (s.store_id < 900 AND s.region NOT IN ('Head office')))
  GROUP BY s.region, region_label, d.fiscal_year
)
SELECT 
  region_label,
  SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) as fy2025_26_net_sales,
  SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) as fy2024_25_net_sales,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN
      ROUND(((SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END)) / SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END)) * 100, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END as growth_percentage
FROM q3_sales
GROUP BY region_label
ORDER BY region_label

WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank

answer.sql: WITH cur_store AS (SELECT store_id, region, open_date FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900), lfl_store AS (SELECT store_id, region FROM cur_store WHERE open_date IS NULL OR open_date <= DATE '2023-10-28'), per AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, min(calendar_date) AS start_date, max(calendar_date) AS end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_quarter = 3 AND fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25','FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1,2), sales AS (SELECT p.fiscal_year, l.region, sum(f.net_amount) AS gross_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN lfl_store l ON l.store_id=s.store_id JOIN per p ON f.sale_date BETWEEN p.start_date AND p.end_date GROUP BY 1,2), rets AS (SELECT p.fiscal_year, l.region, sum(r.refund_net) AS refunds FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN lfl_store l ON l.store_id=s.store_id JOIN per p ON r.return_date BETWEEN p.start_date AND p.end_date GROUP BY 1,2), net AS (SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.region, s.gross_net - coalesce(r.refunds,0) AS net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN rets r ON r.fiscal_year=s.fiscal_year AND r.region=s.region) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, c.region, round(100.0*(c.net_sales/p.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM net c JOIN net p ON p.region=c.region AND p.fiscal_year='FY2024/25' WHERE c.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' ORDER BY c.region
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: Q3 = fiscal periods 7 to 9, fiscal weeks 27 to 39 (13 weeks)
Current period FY2025/26 Q3 (2025-10-27 to 2026-01-25) against prior year FY2024/25 Q3 (2024-10-28 to 2025-01-26), same fiscal weeks
Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT) minus refund_net booked in the same period, as in rpt_daily_store_sales (which reconciles exactly to the fact tables for these periods)
Like-for-like store set = physical stores (store_id below 900) open for at least 12 months before the start of the prior-year comparison period, so neither period is a new-store ramp-up
Region taken from the current store version (the post 2025-04-28 structure) for both years, so each region has the same stores in both periods
Growth % = (FY2025/26 Q3 net sales / FY2024/25 Q3 net sales - 1) x 100
Slowly changing dimensions joined through store_key, then grouped by store_id
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' is read as fiscal Q3 of the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (the request is dated 2026-10-05, and the company reports on a fiscal calendar). Calendar Q3 2025 (Jul to Sep) was not used.
Like-for-like covers physical stores only. The web shop (store 900) has no region and is excluded, as is the Training store (999).
Staff purchases are kept in net sales, as in the warehouse's own daily store sales report. Returns are deducted on the day and in the store where the refund was booked.

No written company like-for-like definition was available. I used the 12-month rule above. It agrees with the 37-store tmp_lfl_store_list tables (stores 101 to 135, 138 and 139), but I did not rely on those tables.

Stores that were closed for a refit outside the two Q3 windows (104 Vantaa Tammisto, July to August 2024; 119 Pori, September to October 2025) and Savonlinna (129, closed on 2026-01-25, the last day of the quarter) are kept in, because all three traded every trading day of both Q3 periods.
caveats: Region restatement: on 2025-04-28 stores 101 to 105 moved from South to the new Capital Region, and Kouvola (114) moved from East to South. Prior-year sales were restated to the current regions. Grouping each year by its own region would compare different store sets and give wrong regional growth. The dim_store column comment still lists only North, South, East and West.

Stores excluded as not comparable: 136 Tampere Lamminpää (opened 2024-09-02, so the prior-year Q3 was months 2 to 4 of its ramp-up; it grew 40.8% before returns) and 137 Lohja (opened 2024-11-04, so it missed the first week of the prior-year Q3). Including 136 would lift West from 2.04% to about 5.0%, and the effect is similar on a before-returns basis.

Sensitivity (before returns, so approximate): excluding the refit and closing stores 104, 119 and 129 as well as 136 raises Capital Region to about 3.0% and lowers West to about 1.3%. Capital Region is held down by Vantaa Tammisto (104), which fell 4.6%. The other regions barely move.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 2026-01-25. It traded the whole quarter, so it is in the figures. Its sales will not continue, and East growth would move slightly if the company excludes closing stores.

Raahe (139, North) had no sales on 2025-01-02, a normal trading day, in the prior-year quarter. Only a small refund was booked that day. This is probably a one-day outage or a data gap, and it slightly flatters North's growth. I did not adjust for it.

Both quarters contain 6 non-trading days (Independence Day, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year's Day, Epiphany), so trading days match. Weekday mix differs by a day, as it always does with a 364-day offset.

Duplicate sales lines exist in the warehouse (418 receipt and line pairs, reloaded 2025-09-23), but all fall in FY2025/26 Q2 (September 2025). They do not touch this answer, but they will inflate any Q2 figure built straight from fact_sales_line.

The web channel changed identifiers in November 2025 (channel_code is null from 2025-11-03 onward). This does not affect store-based figures, which use store_id, but any web comparison would need channel_id.
Regional growth uses roughly 7 to 10 stores per region, so a single store (a refit, for example) can move a region by a point or more.

answer.sql: WITH store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week BETWEEN 14 AND 17) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900 AND st.store_id <> 999), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-08-03' - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 14 AND 17 GROUP BY 1) SELECT ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty, lfl_sales ly WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores for the period against the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
LFL covers physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop is excluded
LFL base rule: store open_date on or before 3 Aug 2026 minus 364 days (4 Aug 2025), or open_date null
A store-week counts only if the store traded in that week in both years (open and close dates, ref_store_closure refit weeks)
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar via dim_date: FY2026/27 P4 is weeks 14 to 17, 3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026; comparator is weeks 14 to 17 of FY2025/26, 28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025
One total row (this year, last year, growth) because no breakdown was requested
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' was read as FY2026/27 P4, since the request was made on 7 Oct 2026 and FY2026/27 is the current fiscal year. P4 is complete: it ended on 30 Aug 2026 and the warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026.
The comparator is the same fiscal weeks (14 to 17) of FY2025/26. Calendar dates were not lined up.
Open and close dates come from the current dim_store version, as in the accepted LFL queries.
Requested as a single LFL growth figure, so no regional or store breakdown was given.
caveats: 38 of the 39 physical stores are in the LFL base for all four weeks. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026 and had no sales in P4 this year, so it is out. Its P4 sales last year (9,549.14) are not in the comparison.
The Kuopio refit (15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026) and the Pori refit (8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025) fall outside the P4 weeks in both years, so no refit weeks had to be removed.
Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in 2024, before the 4 Aug 2025 cut-off, so both are in the base.
The web shop (store 900) is not part of LFL, and no web sales are in this figure.

Control total: fact-based store net sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, store by store, for both years. After returns, the LFL totals match the report table exactly (1,010,478.52 and 1,010,743.32, excluding Savonlinna).
Source checks found no duplicate sales lines for P4 in either year. Line ids are unique, and receipt_id plus line_no is unique.
The deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, channel_code, stg_, bak_ and tmp_ tables) were not used.

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2024/25' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, CAST(f.vat_rate*100 AS DECIMAL(5,1)) AS vat_rate_pct, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-26' AND DATE '2024-09-22' AND st.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate

Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
VAT = gross_amount minus net_amount summed line by line, using each line's own vat_rate (no flat rate applied to a net total)
Sale date (Helsinki business date) used for store lines
Control total: store net sales before returns for the period (938,729.24 EUR) matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly

Amounts are in EUR

Total VAT charged in the stores is 235,090.72 EUR on 938,729.24 EUR of net sales

All channels included (store and web)

Included both member and non-member sales

WITH s0 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_value
  FROM fact_stock_week
  WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22'),
s AS (
  SELECT cp.category, w.week_ending_date, w.closing_value
  FROM s0 w
  JOIN dim_store ds ON ds.store_key = w.store_key
  JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ds.store_id AND st.is_current
  JOIN dim_product dp ON dp.product_key = w.product_key
  JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = dp.sku AND cp.is_current
  WHERE st.region = 'West' AND st.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test'),
weekly AS (SELECT category, week_ending_date, SUM(closing_value) AS wk_value FROM s GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 11 AS fiscal_period, category, ROUND(AVG(wk_value), 2) AS avg_stock_value_eur
FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week first, then averaged across the weeks of the period (never summed across weeks)
Stock value is closing_value, at standard cost, excluding VAT
Fiscal period 11 of FY2025/26: 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026, fiscal weeks 44 to 47, four week-ending Sundays (1, 8, 15, 22 March 2026)
Regions and categories as-is (current dim_store and dim_product versions via store_id and sku with is_current), the company default
Stock by store covers physical stores only (store_id below 900); store 999 and category ZZ Test left out
Only the fact_stock_week table was used, not the staging, backup, tmp or old tables and not rpt.v_daily_sales
Grain of fact_stock_week is store_key x product_key x week_ending_date, enforced by removing exact duplicate rows
assumptions: 'Last year' is read as FY2025/26. The request was made on 5 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests made in FY2026/27 took 'last year' as FY2025/26 (REQ-D04, REQ-D08, REQ-D28, REQ-D35). So 'period 11 last year' is FY2025/26 P11 (23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026), which is fully loaded.
'Average stock value' is the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost, not the last week's closing.
West means the five-region West as-is: the 10 stores whose current region is West. No West store changed region in the 28 April 2025 reorganisation, so as-is and as-was agree for this period.
Category is the current product category, as-is. The result has one row per category with no total row, as none was requested.
Averages are over 4 weeks for every category. A few articles delisted on 1 March 2026 have zero stock and zero value in the first week, so they do not change any average.
caveats: Data problem corrected: fact_stock_week holds every row twice for the week ending 8 March 2026 (7,439 store-article groups appear twice, identical in every measure, loaded at different times on 9 and 10 March). Summing as-is would have double-counted that week and overstated the period average by about 6 to 7 per cent. I removed the exact duplicates (SELECT DISTINCT) before aggregating. Without the fix, the 8 March West total would be about 1.63 million instead of 813,641.

Control check: the corrected weekly West totals are 816,086.49, 813,641.20, 812,053.77 and 812,318.58 euro, and the category averages add up to 813,525.02. These are steady week to week, which supports the fix. The duplicate-load issue appears to affect the whole table for that week, not only West, so other stock-based analyses on that week need the same treatment.
The stock table has no matching rpt_daily_store_sales control total, because that table covers sales, not stock. Stock figures could not be reconciled to a second source.
fact_stock_week only has rows for articles a store ranges. The averages cover ranged articles, and stock held centrally for web orders is not included.
Values are at standard cost (standard_unit_cost, revalued each April), not at selling price. They are not adjusted for any later cost changes.
