answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27') AND fiscal_period = 4) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-08-03' - 364)), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty, lfl_sales ly WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL): physical stores only, same fiscal weeks last year, store-weeks that traded in both years
LFL base rule: store open_date on or before the period start minus 364 days (3 Aug 2026 minus 364 days)
Refit and closure weeks removed for the store concerned in both years (ref_store_closure, close_date)
Net sales: excluding VAT, after returns, with returns booked on their return date
Web sales on the Helsinki dispatch date (web shop store 900 is not part of LFL, so web does not enter the result)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: P4 is weeks 14 to 17
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' read as FY2026/27 P4 (3 to 30 Aug 2026, weeks 14 to 17). The request was dated 5 Oct 2026 and P4 is complete.
'Last year' read as FY2025/26 P4 (28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025, same fiscal weeks 14 to 17), per the practice for requests made in FY2026/27.
'The stores' read as the LFL base across all physical stores combined, with one total and no breakdown by store or region, since none was asked for.
Regions, categories and store attributes are not used in the result, so as-is versus as-was does not affect it.
caveats: LFL base is 38 stores (152 store-weeks, all four weeks each). Savonlinna (129) is out because it closed on 25 Jan 2026 and did not trade this year.

Kuopio (125) is in the base for all four weeks: its refit ran 15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026, before P4, and last year's P4 was a normal trading period. Pori's refit (Sep to Oct 2025) and Tammisto's (2024) do not touch P4 either.
Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in 2024, more than 364 days before 3 Aug 2026, so both are in the base.
Store-level net sales agree with rpt_daily_store_sales for every physical store in both years (no differences over 0.50 EUR).
No duplicate rows were found in the sales lines, return lines or web orders for the periods used, so no data correction was needed.
Growth is flat at -0.03% (about -265 EUR on roughly 1.01 million EUR). Individual store-weeks swing by 25 to 100% either way, so the flat total hides large week-to-week and store-to-store movement.
dim_store.format now holds Small, Medium and Large, not the Hyper, Standard and Express named in the column comment. This did not affect the result because the format column was not used.

answer.sql: WITH sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week<=22), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id=st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date<=w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date>=w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id<900), lfl AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id=ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week=ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id=ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-05-04' - 364)), agg AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) ns FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date JOIN lfl l ON l.store_id=n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week=d.fiscal_week JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id=n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND d.fiscal_week<=22 GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.ns/ly.ns DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ty.fiscal_year, ty.ns AS net_sales_this_year, ly.ns AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0*(ty.ns/ly.ns-1),2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM agg ty JOIN agg ly ON ly.region=ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: This year = current fiscal year FY2026/27
YTD = fiscal weeks 1 to 22, 4 May to 4 October 2026, the last completed fiscal week (the warehouse is loaded through that date)
Compared with the same fiscal weeks 1 to 22 of FY2025/26, lined up by fiscal week, not by calendar date
Like-for-like (LFL) growth, physical stores only, web shop (store 900) excluded
LFL base: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the range (open_date <= 2026-05-04 minus 364 days)
LFL store-weeks: only weeks in which the store traded in both years; refit closures from ref_store_closure and closed-store weeks removed for the store in both years
Net sales = net amount excluding VAT after returns, with returns booked on their return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Regions as-is (current dim_store version), including the Capital Region for all history
Staff purchases included in net sales
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store and day by day, for weeks 1 to 22 of both years
Deprecated objects not used (rpt.v_daily_sales, bak_, stg_, tmp_ and old tables)
assumptions: 'How they are doing' has no metric in the data dictionary. I read it as like-for-like net sales growth year to date, the company's standard way of comparing stores. LFL stops the ranking being skewed by the two stores opened in 2024, the closed store, and refit closures. Net sales this year and last year are shown so the base is visible.
'This year so far' = FY2026/27 YTD through the last completed fiscal week (week 22, ended Sunday 4 October 2026). The comparison year is FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22.
'Five store regions' = North, South, East, West and Capital Region, as-is. Online and Head office are not included.
Figures are for the LFL store-weeks only, so they are lower than total regional net sales. The growth percentages are the ranking basis.
Ranking is by LFL growth percentage, highest first. Ranking by absolute net sales would put West first and North last.
Opening-rule test uses the start of the whole range, 4 May 2026, as in the accepted LFL queries.
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line has 418 duplicated lines (same receipt_id and line_no, different sales_line_id, same amounts and store) all in FY2025/26 week 21 (15 to 21 September 2025), loaded 16 to 23 September 2025. I kept one row per receipt_id and line_no. Without this fix, last year's West is overstated by about 10,000 EUR and West shows 1.33% LFL growth instead of 1.93%. The ranking does not change, but West's growth would be understated. The other regions were not affected (the duplicates fall in West stores in the LFL base).
After the de-duplication, store-level net sales for weeks 1 to 22 of both years match rpt_daily_store_sales with no differences by store and day, so the figures reconcile to the control total.
Week-22 LFL for East is slightly negative (-0.19%), so East is the only region below last year. The gap between West (1.93%) and South (2.11%) is small.

The LFL base drops store-weeks that did not trade in both years. This removes Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026), Pori's refit weeks in FY2025/26 and Kuopio's refit weeks (15 June to 26 July 2026) for the stores concerned, in both years. Regions with those stores are therefore compared on fewer store-weeks.
The two stores opened in 2024 (Tampere Lamminpää 136, Lohja 137) are in the base, because both opened more than 364 days before 4 May 2026.

Part-year, absolute net sales growth would differ from LFL growth, which handles the closed store, the refit stores and week 53 properly. No net sales growth figure that includes non-comparable stores is shown.
The metric reading is my assumption and should be confirmed with Antti Rautiainen (FP&A) if he meant total net sales growth, gross margin or something else.

definitions_applied: Active membership defined by dim_member's valid_from and valid_to dates at the reference date
Reference date set to the last day of fiscal period 8, FY2025/26 (2025-12-21)
Tier sourced from the member's record version valid on the reference date

Period 8 refers to fiscal period (not calendar period)

answer.sql:
-- Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day for P2 FY2026/27
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date     -- FY2026/27 P2
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank;
definitions_applied: DEF-STORE-LEAGUE: Stores ranked by net sales per trading day
DEF-NET-SALES: Net amount excluding VAT, after returns; returns deducted on return date, not sale date
DEF-NET-SALES-SCOPE: Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: Physical stores only (store_id < 900)
CAL-CLOSED-DAYS: Stores closed on Finnish public holidays (is_trading_day false)
REG-STORE-EVENTS: Store openings and closures; Kuopio refit closure mid-period
REG-REFITS: Refit closures from ref_store_closure excluded from trading-day count
REG-STAFF-PURCHASE: Staff purchases included in net sales
assumptions: Period 2 this year interpreted as FY2026/27 P02 (the most recent completed period as of the request date 9 October 2026), running 1-28 June 2026, fiscal weeks 5-8
All 38 physical stores in the warehouse have current (is_current = true) versions as of this date
Net sales per trading day calculated as total net sales divided by trading days the store was open
caveats: Store 125 (Kuopio) had only 14 trading days in the period due to a refit closure (15 June to 26 July 2026); it is included in the league table with its actual trading days and ranked accordingly
All other stores had the full 26 trading days in the period (28 calendar days minus two closed holidays: Midsummer Eve on 21 June and Midsummer Day on 22 June)
Control total verified against rpt_daily_store_sales: 1,063,916.20 EUR with zero gap
Some store names contain special characters (é, ä) which may display differently depending on encoding

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending), closing AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7 AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT c.category, ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM closing c LEFT JOIN sold s ON s.category = c.category ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Last period = last completed fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026)
Weeks of cover = closing stock units at end of fiscal week / average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Closing stock is a week-end snapshot, summed across stores and products within the single week (never across weeks)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store 999 excluded; no web stock in fact_stock_week
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product hierarchy (current category per sku via is_current), so outdoor lighting is in Electrical
Stock rows are only for articles the store ranges
assumptions: Last period read as FY2026/27 P05, the last complete period as of the request date 7 Oct 2026. P06 is only partly loaded.
End of the period = the last fiscal week, week ending Sunday 27 Sep 2026 (FY2026/27 week 21).
The request gives no store breakdown, so one figure per category across all physical stores: total closing units divided by total average weekly units sold.
Prior four fiscal weeks = the four whole weeks before the snapshot week, 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026 (the stock skill's literal reading). The units-sold window does not include the snapshot week itself.
Categories on the current (as-is) hierarchy; no as-was split was asked for.
Weeks of cover is not additive across categories, so no overall total row is given.
caveats: Window choice moves some categories. If the four weeks ending on the snapshot date (31 Aug to 27 Sep, P05 itself) are used for sales instead, cover is: Bathroom & Plumbing 11.6, Cleaning & Household 7.5, Electrical 8.5, Furniture 28.6, Garden 18.5, Home Textiles & Decor 11.7, Kitchen & Dining 13.8, Paint & Decorating 13.5, Seasonal 42.0, Tools & Hardware 7.6. Garden and Seasonal differ most.

Seasonal (48.8 weeks) and Furniture (29.5) show long cover because recent sales are low relative to stock. Cover is based on the last four weeks of sales only, so seasonal articles in off-season look overstocked on this measure.

No data problems found in the stock snapshot for 27 Sep 2026: one row per store, article and week (27,143 rows, no duplicates), 38 physical stores, no negative units, no ZZ Test rows. Savonlinna (129) closed in Jan 2026 and has no stock, as expected. No corrections were needed.

The sales side was checked for duplicate sales_line_id and found none. Closing units summed over the categories equal the snapshot total of 211,157 units. No control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales applies to a stock or category-level units figure.

Cover is units-based, not value-based, and is computed on the whole category across all stores, so individual stores may be much tighter or looser than the category figure. Only the stores' ranged articles are in stock, so cover for articles not ranged in a store is not shown.
The sales side is not net of returns, following the definition (quantity on sales lines).

answer.sql: WITH lines AS (SELECT p.sku, cp.product_name, f.quantity FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT sku, product_name, SUM(quantity) AS units_sold FROM lines GROUP BY sku, product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 5 (fiscal weeks 18 to 21, 31 August to 27 September 2026)
Units sold: quantity on sales lines, by sale date
Store 102 Helsinki Pitäjänmäki selected by stable store_id across store versions
Store 999 and category ZZ Test left out
Product names and categories as-is (current dim_product version, keyed on sku)
Control total: daily units and receipts checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 5 this year' is FY2026/27 P05, the current fiscal year and the last completed period at the request date (7 October 2026). It is fully loaded.
'Units sold' is gross quantity on sales lines, before returns, as the metric dictionary defines units sold. It is not net of returns.
Staff purchases are included, as they are in sales reporting.
Products are counted by sku, so the different versions of an article are combined.
Helsinki Pitäjänmäki is read as store_id 102. It is a physical store, so web lines are not part of it.
caveats: No data correction was needed. The 28 daily unit and receipt totals for store 102 match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, with no duplicate sales lines and no test-article units in the store.

Returns would not change the ranking. Only one returned unit was booked in the period for the top-5 articles (sku 102244), so its net figure would be 41, still third and still well ahead of fourth place (30 units).
Store 102 changed region from South to Capital Region on 28 April 2025. This does not affect the answer, because the store is selected by store_id.

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT w.week_ending_date, SUM(w.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week w JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = w.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = w.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.week_ending_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS average_closing_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week first, then averaged across the weeks of the period
Stock value at standard cost (fact_stock_week.closing_value)
Stock by store covers physical stores only (store_id below 900); store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Category as-is: Paint & Decorating taken from the current product version (dim_product.is_current)
Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 = fiscal weeks 9 to 13, 29 June to 2 August 2026, selected through dim_date on the week-ending Sunday
Snapshot grain checked: one row per store_key, product_key and week_ending_date, no duplicates
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27, so period 3 is FY2026/27 P3, which is complete and fully loaded
'Average stock' read as the average of the five weekly closing stock values in the period, not the last week's closing
'Whole chain' read as all physical stores (38 stores with stock rows). The web shop is excluded because web orders are picked from the central warehouse, which is not in fact_stock_week
Category read as-is (current hierarchy), the default for management reporting. The as-was figure is identical, because no Paint & Decorating article changed category in this period
Value at cost is the warehouse's closing_value at standard cost. It equals closing units times standard unit cost on every row checked
caveats: No data correction was needed. The five snapshots for P3 have no duplicate rows, no nulls and no negative units. closing_value matches units times standard cost on every Paint & Decorating row

The five weekly closing values (EUR) are 341,138.89 for w/e 5 July, 341,742.53 for 12 July, 344,245.91 for 19 July, 349,160.39 for 26 July and 346,046.42 for 2 August. The last week's closing alone would be 346,046.42
The week ending 5 July has 61 extra rows (25 in Paint & Decorating) for articles delisted on 1 July 2026, all with zero units and zero value. They do not change the result
Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 but still has stock rows, so its stock is included in the weeks it was closed. Its stock was not removed
Stock is only held for the articles each store ranges, and the central warehouse is not covered, so this is store stock only
The store-level control against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to stock figures, so none was done

answer.sql: WITH cal AS (SELECT calendar_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period=2 AND is_trading_day), st AS (SELECT store_id, store_name, open_date, close_date FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900), trading AS (SELECT st.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM st CROSS JOIN cal c WHERE (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= c.calendar_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= c.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure x WHERE x.store_id = st.store_id AND c.calendar_date BETWEEN x.closure_start_date AND x.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), agg AS (SELECT store_id, SUM(net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-06-01' AND DATE '2026-06-28' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY a.net_sales / t.trading_days DESC) AS rank, st.store_id, st.store_name, t.trading_days, ROUND(a.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, ROUND(a.net_sales / t.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM st JOIN trading t USING (store_id) JOIN agg a USING (store_id) ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Store counts and store-level analyses cover physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Trading days: days in the period when the store was open, outside refit closures (ref_store_closure) and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P2 taken from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar (Monday 1 June to Sunday 28 June 2026, weeks 5 to 8)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales, store by store, same days
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old tables) not used

WITH sales_data AS (
  WITH sales_by_week AS (
    SELECT 
      d.fiscal_year,
      d.fiscal_week,
      SUM(fsl.net_amount) AS sales_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line fsl
    INNER JOIN dim_date d ON fsl.sale_date = d.calendar_date
    WHERE d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 5 AND 8 
      AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27')
    GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week
  ),
  returns_by_week AS (
    SELECT 
      d.fiscal_year,
      d.fiscal_week,
      SUM(frl.refund_net) AS returns_amount
    FROM fact_return_line frl
    INNER JOIN dim_date d ON frl.return_date = d.calendar_date
    WHERE d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 5 AND 8 
      AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27')
    GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week
  )
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(s.fiscal_year, r.fiscal_year) AS fiscal_year,
    COALESCE(s.fiscal_week, r.fiscal_week) AS fiscal_week,
    COALESCE(s.sales_amount, 0) - COALESCE(r.returns_amount, 0) AS net_sales
  FROM sales_by_week s
  FULL OUTER JOIN returns_by_week r 
    ON s.fiscal_year = r.fiscal_year AND s.fiscal_week = r.fiscal_week
)
SELECT 
  this_year.fiscal_week,
  ROUND(this_year.net_sales, 2) AS sales_2026_27,
  ROUND(last_year.net_sales, 2) AS sales_2025_26,
  ROUND((this_year.net_sales - last_year.net_sales) / last_year.net_sales * 100, 1) AS growth_pct
FROM sales_data this_year
LEFT JOIN sales_data last_year 
  ON this_year.fiscal_week = last_year.fiscal_week 
  AND this_year.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
  AND last_year.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
WHERE this_year.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
ORDER BY this_year.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: sum of line net amounts minus refunds, EUR excluding VAT
Fiscal week boundaries from dim_date calendar (fiscal weeks 5-8 = period 2)
Returns: refund amounts processed in the same fiscal week as the sale week
assumptions: This year = FY2026/27, Last year = FY2025/26
Total company sales = all channels (store and web) combined
Growth percentage = (FY2026/27 - FY2025/26) / FY2025/26 * 100
caveats: Store closure: Kuopio (store 125) was closed for refit from 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-26, spanning most of fiscal week 7 (2026-06-15 to 2026-06-21). The -26.3% decline in week 7 this year is partly attributable to this closure and is not a like-for-like comparison.
No store closures occurred during period 2 of FY2025/26, so the year-on-year comparison for week 7 is affected by this planned maintenance.

answer.sql: WITH s_agg AS (SELECT p.sku, sum(f.net_amount - f.standard_cost) AS margin_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.region = 'South' AND f.channel_code = 'ST' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-27' AND DATE '2025-04-27' GROUP BY p.sku), r_agg AS (SELECT p.sku, sum(r.refund_net - r.standard_cost_returned) AS returned_margin FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id WHERE s.region = 'South' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-27' AND DATE '2025-04-27' GROUP BY p.sku) SELECT c.sku, c.product_name, c.category, round(a.margin_before_returns - coalesce(r.returned_margin, 0), 2) AS gross_margin_eur FROM s_agg a LEFT JOIN r_agg r USING (sku) JOIN dim_product c ON c.sku = a.sku AND c.is_current ORDER BY gross_margin_eur DESC LIMIT 10

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_year AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM by_year ty JOIN by_year ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.category
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered or collected orders only)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: period 8 compared with period 8 of the prior year (same fiscal weeks 31-34)
As-is product hierarchy (current product version, via is_current)
Growth % = (FY2025/26 net sales / FY2024/25 net sales - 1) x 100
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 and 'the year before' as FY2024/25, because the request is dated 5 October 2026 (FY2026/27 is the current fiscal year). This matches how past requests read 'last year'.
Period 8 is fiscal weeks 31-34 in both years: 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025 and 25 Nov to 22 Dec 2024. Both are complete and loaded. Week 53 is not in P8, so no week 53 adjustment was needed.
Garden and Electrical are shown as two rows, because the request names two categories. No combined total row was added.
As-is hierarchy used because the request did not ask for as-was.
Web sales (store 900) are included, as in company net sales. Category is not limited to physical stores.

caveats: Outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 October 2025 (start of FY2025/26 P7). Under the as-is hierarchy it sits in Electrical in both years. This is the only reason Electrical and Garden are comparable. As-was, the FY2024/25 P8 figures would be Electrical 142,914.41 and Garden 56,269.57, giving Electrical +19.8% and Garden -34.6%. That movement is a category reclassification, not trading.
The as-is reclassification moved 19,504.55 EUR of FY2024/25 P8 net sales from Garden to Electrical. The Garden-to-Electrical shift would otherwise distort both growth rates.

The category-level figures cannot be reconciled directly to rpt_daily_store_sales, which has no category dimension. The all-category P8 company total from the same net-sales logic (excluding store 999 and ZZ Test) matched the control exactly in both years: 1,373,188.97 for FY2024/25 and 1,435,696.60 for FY2025/26.

Source checks on Garden/Electrical sales lines for fiscal weeks 29-36 of both years found no duplicate sales_line_id or receipt_id and line_no pairs, and no negative or zero-quantity lines. The query found no web lines for cancelled or processing orders in P8, so the dispatch-date rule changed nothing here.

The library's net-sales template dates web lines with no delivered or collected order by their order date. No such lines fall in P8, so it did not affect these figures, but it would overstate web sales in other periods.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week

Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered and collected orders only
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)

Same fiscal week comparison, not same calendar dates
Control total against rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store and day by day

assumptions: This year means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (period 2 ran 1 June to 28 June 2026)
Last year means FY2025/26 (period 2 ran 26 May to 22 June 2025). This follows how requests asked in May 2026 and later were read
Period 2 of this year is complete, because the warehouse is loaded to 4 October 2026
Total company sales are net sales (excluding VAT, after returns), as the company default. The request did not ask for gross
Weeks are paired by fiscal week number (5 to 8) in each year
Growth is this year over last year, in percent
caveats: Growth in weeks 7 and 8 reflects the calendar and a store closure, not trading performance. Midsummer (stores shut for two days) falls in week 7 this year (19 and 20 June 2026) but in week 8 last year (20 and 21 June 2025). That is why week 7 shows -32.2% and week 8 shows +76.4%. Weeks 7 and 8 combined: 591,343.83 this year against 535,679.88 last year, +10.4%. Period 2 as a whole: 1,294,647.64 against 1,195,882.70, +8.3%

The Kuopio store (125) was closed for a refit from 15 June 2026 to 26 July 2026, so it has no sales in weeks 7 and 8 this year. It sold about 7,200 to 12,200 per week in the same weeks last year. This is total company, not like-for-like, so the closure is left in the figures and lowers this year's weeks 7 and 8

Web sales are counted on the dispatch date, so they will not match web sales by order date. Web is 52,105.04, 60,691.84, 44,949.11 and 72,985.45 in weeks 5 to 8 this year, against 40,688.20, 35,416.55, 44,352.25 and 30,548.35 last year. Web growth is much faster than store growth
Test data removed: store 999 sales (about 200 to 900 a week) and a few ZZ Test lines in other stores (under 4 a week). Removing them changes the totals slightly
Control check passed. My net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales for every store (including the web shop, store 900) on every day of both periods, with no differences
Returns reduce net sales on their return date. Returns from late June 2026 sales could still arrive for up to 30 days, but they land in later weeks and do not change these four weeks

answer.sql:
WITH lfl_stores AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.store_id, s.region
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN '2024-10-28' AND '2025-01-26'
    AND s.store_id < 900
  INTERSECT
  SELECT DISTINCT s.store_id, s.region
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN '2025-10-27' AND '2026-01-25'
    AND s.store_id < 900
),
q3_fy2425_sales AS (
  SELECT lfl.region,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.sale_date BETWEEN '2024-10-28' AND '2025-01-26' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END)
    - SUM(CASE WHEN r.return_date BETWEEN '2024-10-28' AND '2025-01-26' THEN r.refund_net ELSE 0 END) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
  JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN lfl_stores lfl ON s.store_id = lfl.store_id
  WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN '2024-10-28' AND '2025-01-26'
    AND s.store_id < 900
    AND f.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE
  GROUP BY lfl.region
),
q3_fy2526_sales AS (
  SELECT lfl.region,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.sale_date BETWEEN '2025-10-27' AND '2026-01-25' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END)
    - SUM(CASE WHEN r.return_date BETWEEN '2025-10-27' AND '2026-01-25' THEN r.refund_net ELSE 0 END) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
  JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN lfl_stores lfl ON s.store_id = lfl.store_id
  WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN '2025-10-27' AND '2026-01-25'
    AND s.store_id < 900
    AND f.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE
  GROUP BY lfl.region
)
SELECT 
  q1.region,
  ROUND(q1.net_sales, 2) as net_sales_q3_fy2425,
  ROUND(q2.net_sales, 2) as net_sales_q3_fy2526,
  ROUND(((q2.net_sales - q1.net_sales) / q1.net_sales * 100), 2) as lfl_growth_pct
FROM q3_fy2425_sales q1
JOIN q3_fy2526_sales q2 ON q1.region = q2.region
ORDER BY q1.region
definitions_applied: Like-for-like stores: stores with sales in both Q3 FY2024/25 (2024-10-28 to 2025-01-26) and Q3 FY2025/26 (2025-10-27 to 2026-01-25)
Net sales: sum of fact_sales_line.net_amount minus fact_return_line.refund_net
Store exclusion: physical stores only (store_id < 900, excluding online channel)
Staff purchase exclusion: transactions flagged staff_purchase_flag = TRUE excluded from sales
assumptions: Q3 last year interpreted as Q3 FY2024/25, comparing to current Q3 FY2025/26
Like-for-like growth calculated as percentage change in net sales between comparable periods
Staff purchases excluded as non-customer transactions not representative of demand
caveats: 39 stores across all regions had sales in both Q3 periods (East 9, North 6, South 15, West 10)
No store closures (refits) during either Q3 period
Fiscal year runs from late April to late April; Q3 is Oct-Jan spanning two calendar years

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT f.week_ending_date, sum(f.closing_value) AS chain_stock_value FROM fact_stock_week f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN ref_fiscal_calendar c ON f.week_ending_date BETWEEN c.period_start_date AND c.period_end_date WHERE p.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND s.store_id < 900 AND c.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND c.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY f.week_ending_date) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, round(avg(chain_stock_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 from ref_fiscal_calendar: 29 June to 2 August 2026, 5 weeks
Stock value at standard cost (fact_stock_week.closing_value)
Average stock as the mean of the five weekly closing-stock totals (weeks ending 5, 12, 19, 26 July and 2 August 2026)
Category taken from the product version in fact_stock_week.product_key (dim_product.category = 'Paint & Decorating', all four subcategories)
Whole chain: all physical stores (store_id below 900); the web shop (900) and training store (999) have no Paint & Decorating stock rows
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, since the request arrived on 2026-10-08 and the company year starts in May
'Period 3' read as fiscal period 3 (P03) of the company fiscal calendar, not calendar month 3
'Average stock' read as the simple average of weekly closing stock values across the period, not an average of opening and closing
Zero-stock lines are kept in the weekly totals; they add no value, so the result is the same either way
Closing value at standard cost is used as it stands in the warehouse; the stock-value column agrees with units times the product version's standard unit cost on every row checked for the period
caveats: No data corrections were needed. In the period, there are no duplicate store and SKU rows, no negative stock, no stock values that disagree with units times standard cost, and no rows outside their store or product version dates. Every week has the same 38 stores (closed store 129 has no rows)
Week ending 5 July has 25 more rows than the other four weeks. These are 25 store and SKU lines for three articles delisted on 1 July 2026, shown at 0 units and EUR 0; they do not affect the value

Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 but still carries stock in the data (about EUR 17.5k of Paint & Decorating in the closure weeks). It is included as real inventory on hand. If supply chain wants it excluded, the average would be lower by about EUR 17.5k
Standard costs are revalued each April, so the period uses the post-April 2026 costs; the figure is not comparable with a stock value at an earlier cost basis
Period 3 is 5 weeks long, so the average covers five weekly counts

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS gold_tier_members FROM dim_member WHERE tier = 'Gold' AND is_current = TRUE

answer.sql: WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25','FY2025/26') AND fiscal_quarter = 3), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN wk w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2025-10-27' - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT cs.region, d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.region, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores for the period vs the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week, physical stores only
LFL store base: open at least 364 days before the first day of the period (open_date <= 2025-10-27 minus 364 days)
LFL store-week: the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open_date, close_date and ref_store_closure checked)
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, minus refunds (refund_net) on their return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900) excluded from LFL
Regions as-is: current dim_store version, so Capital Region covers stores 101-105 in both years
Fiscal calendar: fiscal_year and fiscal_quarter from dim_date, weeks 27 to 39 of each year compared by fiscal week, not calendar date
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
Open and close dates taken from the current dim_store version
assumptions: The request was received on 5 October 2026 (FY2026/27). I read 'Q3 last year' as Q3 of FY2025/26: weeks 27 to 39, 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026. This follows the 12 to 27 May 2026 precedent that took 'last year' as FY2025/26 (REQ-D04, REQ-D08).
The comparator is Q3 of FY2024/25: weeks 27 to 39, 28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025.
Regions are as-is, the management-reporting default. The requester did not ask for as-was.
One row per region, because the request asks for a breakdown by region. There is no total row.
Both quarters have 13 weeks and week 53 is not in the range, so it does not affect the result.

Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026, which is the last Sunday of week 39. I counted it as trading in all 13 weeks, which the rule (close_date on or after the week's Sunday) gives. It has sales in all 13 weeks in both years.
Percentages are net sales growth, rounded to 2 decimals.
caveats: Lohja (137) is left out of the LFL base. It opened on 4 Nov 2024, which is after 28 Oct 2024 (the opening-rule cut-off of 2025-10-27 minus 364 days). It did not trade in week 27 of the comparator year, and it joins the base on 3 Nov 2025 (week 28), after the quarter starts. This follows the REQ-D08 precedent. 38 stores are in the base: Capital Region 5, East 8, North 6, South 9, West 10.

Tampere Lamminpää (136) opened on 2 Sep 2024, so it is in the base. Its sales grew from about 70.6k to 98.0k (about 39%) as a young store, which lifts the West figure of 4.77%. The result is correct under the rule, but the West number is flattered by that one store.
Neither refit closure (Pori 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025, Tammisto 8 Jul to 11 Aug 2024) overlaps Q3 in either year. No store-weeks dropped out for refits.

I found 418 duplicated sales lines: the same receipt_id and line_no loaded twice with different sales_line_id, on 15 to 21 Sep 2025 (fiscal week 21 of FY2025/26). They fall outside both Q3 windows, so they do not affect this answer. They would double-count any sales query covering that week.
Store-level net sales (sales plus returns) for Q3 of both years match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for every physical store, so no unexplained gap.
I did not use channel_code or rpt.v_daily_sales. The deprecated objects are not involved, since web is not in LFL.
Returns are booked on their return date, so some Q3 sales may still be returned after the quarter. This is the company definition and was not adjusted.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Web shop (store 900) included, as the request is for total company
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: period 2 of FY2026/27 (weeks 5 to 8) against the same fiscal weeks of FY2025/26, lined up by fiscal week and not by calendar date
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales) for the same days: all 8 weeks agree to the cent
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, and used no channel_code
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' is read as FY2026/27 P2 (1 June to 28 June 2026, fiscal weeks 5 to 8). It is the current fiscal year and is complete in the warehouse, which is loaded through 4 October 2026.
'The same weeks last year' is read as fiscal weeks 5 to 8 of FY2025/26 (26 May to 22 June 2025), compared week by week, not as the same calendar dates.
'Total company' is read as all physical stores plus the web shop (store 900), with store 999 and ZZ Test left out.
Growth percentage is this year divided by last year, minus 1, rounded to 1 decimal place.
Regions are not involved, so the as-is or as-was question does not arise.
caveats: Weeks 7 and 8 are not like for like because of Midsummer. The stores were shut on Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day on 19 and 20 June 2026, which fall in FY2026/27 week 7, but on 20 and 21 June 2025, which fell in FY2025/26 week 8. That is why week 7 shows -32.2% and week 8 shows +76.4%. Read these two weeks together: they total 591,343.83 this year against 535,679.88 last year, which is +10.4%.

This is a total-company comparison and not like-for-like (LFL). The store base differs: 39 stores traded last year, and this year 38 traded in weeks 5 and 6 and 37 in weeks 7 and 8. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026, and Kuopio (125) has been in a refit since 15 June 2026. The web shop's share of sales also grew.

Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test test transactions changes the weekly totals only slightly (a few hundred euro at most a week). I found no duplicate sales or return lines, no orphan keys and no undispatched web lines, so I made no other corrections.
Returns are booked on their own return date. These figures are the net sales as booked in the warehouse for those weeks, and returns arriving later for sales in these weeks will fall in later weeks.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (section 9), before returns
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P5 = 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (last complete period)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Subcategory as-is (current product version via sku and is_current)
Store-level control total against rpt_daily_store_sales units_sold for the same days
Physical store only (store_id 118); web shop (store 900) not included
Store identified by natural key store_id, not store_key
assumptions: 'Nokia' means store 118 Nokia (the only store matching the name, city Nokia, West region, format Medium).
'Period 5 this year' means FY2026/27 P5, the last complete period (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026).
'Units sold' means units on sales lines, before returns, matching how the company defines units sold and the units_sold column in rpt_daily_store_sales.
Subcategories reported as-is, on the current product hierarchy.
Staff purchases left in, as they count in sales and units sold.
caveats: Control total agrees: 2245 units for Nokia over P5 in both fact_sales_line (after excluding ZZ Test) and rpt_daily_store_sales. No duplicate sales_line_id values; no test articles or store 999 lines affected the Nokia figures.

The ranking is on units before returns. If returns were netted off (7, 5 and 9 units returned in Fixings & Fasteners, Indoor Lighting and Storage Boxes), the top two would stay the same, but third place would change: Cleaning Products (136 sold, 2 returned = 134) would pass Storage Boxes (139 sold, 9 returned = 130).
Third place is close on a gross basis too: Storage Boxes 139, then Plants & Flowers and Cleaning Products both on 136.
