answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
store_data AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id) AS receipts,
           SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
    WHERE s.store_id < 900
      AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 13
),
web_data AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT wd.web_order_id) AS orders,
           SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN web_dispatch wd ON wd.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = wd.dispatch_date
    WHERE s.store_id = 900
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 13
)
SELECT 
    'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year,
    'P01-P03' AS periods,
    ROUND((sd.net_sales + wd.net_sales) / (sd.receipts + wd.orders), 2) AS atv
FROM store_data sd
CROSS JOIN web_data wd
definitions_applied: ATV as net sales before returns divided by transaction count (modified from company definition)
Exclusions: staff purchases, store 999 (training store), test articles (category ZZ Test)
Web orders included in ATV calculation (deviates from company standard which excludes them)
Net sales and web orders both aligned to dispatch date in Helsinki time
Web orders: only delivered or collected orders counted; cancelled and processing orders excluded
assumptions: Periods 1 to 3 this year interpreted as FY2026/27 P01-P03 (most recent completed periods per established pattern: REQ-D03, REQ-D06, REQ-D12)
Web orders should be in it too: interpreted as including web orders in the ATV denominator, overriding the company definition which excludes web orders
Web revenue and orders both counted by dispatch_date (when delivered or collected), ensuring revenue and transaction counts align to the same period
Request received 2026-10-05; warehouse loaded through 2026-08-02 (end of P03), so the period is fully complete
caveats: This result deviates from the company ATV definition, which excludes web orders. The standard store-only ATV for the same period is €55.52 (€3,719,186.33 ÷ 66,984 receipts).
Web is included: 13,004 orders contributing €771,530.75 in net sales.
Timing: web revenue is recognized on dispatch date (Helsinki time), not order date. A small portion of orders placed in P1-P3 may dispatch into P4 or later, and vice versa.
No data problems detected. Query validated for deprecated objects, house rules, and row count.

answer.sql: SELECT dp.category, ROUND(AVG(fsw.closing_value), 2) AS average_stock_value FROM fact_stock_week fsw INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsw.store_key = ds.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsw.product_key = dp.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsw.week_ending_date = dd.calendar_date WHERE ds.region = 'West' AND dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND dd.fiscal_period = 11 GROUP BY dp.category ORDER BY dp.category
definitions_applied: Average stock value: arithmetic mean of closing_value across all store/product/week observations
West region: stores with region = 'West' from dim_store
Period 11 last year: FY2024/25 period 11 (2025-02-24 to 2025-03-23)
Stock value: closing_value in EUR from fact_stock_week, calculated at standard cost
assumptions: Last year means the previous fiscal year (FY2024/25) from today's date (2026-10-15)
Average is unweighted arithmetic mean across all 29,058 individual stock records (10 stores × 3,118 products × 4 weeks, minus unavailable combinations)
All West region stores and their current store master data versions are included
caveats: Calculation includes 14 zero-value records (store/product combinations with no stock), which contribute zeros to the average
Average is calculated per individual product snapshot; products delisted during the period are included if in stock on their recorded dates
Stock values use the product version and standard cost effective on each week-ending date; cost revaluations (April) do not apply within a single period

answer.sql: WITH web_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2), web_returns AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(r.refund_net) AS returns_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_period, round(w.sales_net - coalesce(r.returns_net, 0), 2) AS net_sales FROM web_sales w LEFT JOIN web_returns r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period) ORDER BY w.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Fiscal calendar: dim_date / ref_fiscal_calendar, periods starting on Mondays (P05 = 25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025, P06 = 22 Sep to 26 Oct, P07 = 27 Oct to 23 Nov, P08 = 24 Nov to 21 Dec)
Web shop = pseudo-store 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop), covering home delivery and click and collect
Sales dated by sale_date (Helsinki local date), refunds dated by return_date (when booked)
Staff purchases: none on web lines in these periods, so nothing to exclude
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (request dated 6 Oct 2026, which falls in FY2026/27), not calendar 2025 or the current year
'Net' read as net sales per the company definition: excluding VAT and after returns
Returns are deducted in the period the refund was booked, even if the original sale fell in an earlier period
Both web fulfilment types (home delivery and click and collect) are included; cancelled orders have no sales lines so add nothing
caveats: Correction 1, channel migration: from 3 Nov 2025 the sales lines carry channel_id (2 = home delivery, 3 = click and collect) and a NULL channel_code. Filtering on channel_code = 'WB' (as rpt.v_daily_sales does) drops all web sales from 3 Nov, which would understate P07 and P08 and leave out the whole of P08 after that date. I identified web sales by store 900 instead, which works on both sides of the change.

Correction 2, returns booked at stores: 501 refunds on web sales lines in these periods were booked at physical stores (store_key of the store, not the web shop), about 17k EUR net. Store sales are always returned at their own store, so this looks like web orders handed back in stores. The company convention books a refund where it is made, which would leave these out of web net sales and charge them to the stores. I deducted them from the web shop because the sale was a web sale. Taking only refunds booked at the web shop would give 145,626.90 / 175,588.62 / 154,977.27 / 225,265.08 less nothing for stores' share, i.e. higher web net sales in every period.

rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 does not match the fact table (for example P05 net sales before returns 158,717 against 158,124 in fact_sales_line; P08 243,086 against 249,085). The daily pattern also looks like a store's (near-zero Sundays, receipt counts well below the web order counts). I did not use it for the web shop.

Checks that came back clean: no duplicate sales lines or reloads, order and line totals reconcile to fact_web_order for all delivered and collected orders, gross matches net plus VAT on every line, sale dates match Helsinki local dates, and all four periods are flagged fully loaded.
P08 includes the Black Friday and Cyber Monday spikes (28 Nov, 1 Dec) and the pre-Christmas rise, so it is much higher than the other periods. Nothing in the data suggests these are errors.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-08-31' AS start_date, DATE '2026-09-27' AS end_date), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
definitions_applied: Net sales = net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only); cancelled and processing orders excluded
Whole company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: 'last period' = last completed fiscal period
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Last month' was read as the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (fiscal_period 5, fiscal weeks 18 to 21), 31 August to 27 September 2026 (28 days, 4 whole fiscal weeks). The company has no calendar-month definition and reports in fiscal periods; a request received 9 October 2026 gives P05 as the last completed period.
'Whole company' read as stores plus web shop, shown as one figure (no breakdown asked for).
Figure is in EUR, excluding VAT, after returns.
caveats: If you meant calendar September (1 to 30 September 2026) rather than the fiscal period, the same definition gives 1,179,035.98 EUR (including 190,443.82 from the web shop), from rpt_daily_store_sales. That window is not whole fiscal weeks.
The figure is made up of store sales 983,903.11 plus web sales dispatched in the period 195,624.31, minus returns booked in the period 69,980.90.

Store 999 and ZZ Test articles are excluded as per company rule. The control table rpt_daily_store_sales shows no difference with or without store 999 for this period, so the filter did not change the total.
The total matches the rpt_daily_store_sales control total exactly (gap 0.00).
Web orders cancelled or still processing are not counted as web sales. None of them fell in the period.
The deprecated views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used; they leave out web sales from 3 November 2025.
Warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026; the period is fully loaded.
No duplicate sales or return line keys were found.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2024-08-01' AS august_start,
           DATE '2024-08-31' AS august_end,
           DATE '2024-09-01' AS september_start,
           DATE '2024-09-30' AS september_end
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
sales_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date,
           s.region,
           f.gross_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30'
)
SELECT s.region,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.business_date BETWEEN p.august_start AND p.august_end THEN s.gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.business_date BETWEEN p.september_start AND p.september_end THEN s.gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024
FROM sales_lines s
CROSS JOIN params p
GROUP BY s.region
ORDER BY s.region;
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT: sum of gross_amount from sales lines
Net sales scope: store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
As-was reporting: regions as they existed on the transaction date
Sales before returns: refunds not included
assumptions: August and September 2024 interpreted as calendar months 2024-08-01 to 2024-09-30
Regions reported as-was (at the time), not as-is (current)
Online line represents web shop sales (store 900) on dispatch date
Gross sales requested explicitly; VAT included per requirement
caveats: Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded per company definition
VAT rate changed from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024; each line carries its own rate
Online sales include click-and-collect orders picked up in Aug/Sep and home delivery orders dispatched in Aug/Sep
No Capital Region in this period; region reorganization occurred 28 April 2025
Five regions in result; the four physical regions (East, North, South, West) plus Online (web shop)

answer.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, COUNT(DISTINCT h.member_id) AS members_held_out FROM campaign_holdout h JOIN dim_campaign c ON c.campaign_id = h.campaign_id WHERE c.campaign_name = 'Black Week 2025' GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name
definitions_applied: Holdout members counted as distinct member_id in campaign_holdout, which holds member_id and not member_key
Campaign identified through dim_campaign by name (Black Week 2025, campaign_id 15)
No deprecated, staging, backup or tmp tables used
assumptions: 'Black Week 2025 mailing' means the dim_campaign row named Black Week 2025 (campaign_id 15, 24-30 Nov 2025, email+sms+push). There is only one campaign with that name; the earlier Black Week 2024 is a separate campaign.
'Held out' means members listed in campaign_holdout for that campaign, not members who were merely not contacted.
caveats: The count matches dim_campaign.holdout_size (2747). campaign_holdout has 2747 rows and 2747 distinct member_ids for this campaign, so there are no duplicates to remove.
No held-out member was contacted in the campaign: none of the 2747 appears in fact_campaign_exposure for campaign 15 (checked via member_id through dim_member).
All 2747 held-out member_ids exist in dim_member. 181 of them have since lost marketing consent, but they were held out at the time and are still counted.

The held-out share is 2747 of 26573 on the mailing list (about 10.3%), slightly above the nominal holdout_pct of 0.100. The table's own holdout_size agrees with the count, so I used the figure as recorded.
The contacted members (23818) plus the holdout (2747) come to 26565, which is 8 fewer than mailing_list_size (26573). This does not affect the holdout count.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, count(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id (natural key), not by member_key version
Tier read from the current member version (is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
dim_member used as the canonical member table; stg_member_updates and other staging, bak_ and tmp_ tables not used
assumptions: 'Members on the Gold tier' means all enrolled loyalty members whose current tier is Gold, not only active members (those who bought in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks). The metric dictionary defines 'active member' separately and the request did not ask for it.
'Right now' means the current version of each member in the warehouse, which is the position at the latest load (4 October 2026), since the request was received on 8 October 2026.
caveats: The warehouse holds data only up to 4 October 2026 (latest sale date and latest member version start), so the figure is as at that load, not as at 8 October 2026.

dim_member keeps one row per version, and 2,233 other members held Gold in an earlier version but have since moved to another tier. Counting version rows instead of distinct members would overstate the figure (8,203 Gold rows against 5,791 members currently Gold).
Checks found no data problems: every member has exactly one current version, is_current agrees with valid_to = 9999-12-31 for all rows, and no member has overlapping versions on 8 October 2026.
If Marketing wants Gold members who are active, or who have marketing consent, the number will be lower; that needs a separate request.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, w.week_ending_date, w.closing_units AS units_in_stock FROM fact_stock_week w JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = w.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = w.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND w.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Closing stock is the end-of-fiscal-week snapshot in fact_stock_week, read at one store and one SKU for one week
Fiscal weeks run Monday to Sunday, and the snapshot is dated on the week-ending Sunday
Store and article resolved through the version keys (dim_store store_key 30, dim_product product_key 11), with store_id and sku as the stable natural keys
Store 999 and category ZZ Test exclusions checked; neither applies (store 124, category Garden)
Deprecated tables (stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old) not used
assumptions: 'End of last week' on a request dated Thursday 8 October 2026 is read as the last completed fiscal week, FY2026/27 week 22 (Monday 28 September to Sunday 4 October 2026), so the snapshot dated 4 October 2026

'SKU 100011 Jyväskylä Palokka' is read as article 100011 (Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570, category Garden) in store 124 Jyväskylä Palokka; the store name matched exactly one store and the SKU matched exactly one product version
caveats: No data problems found, so no corrections were made.
The snapshot has exactly one row for this store, article and week at its grain (no duplicate loads), and the loaded timestamp is 5 October 2026.

Consistency check against sales: closing stock went 16 to 13 to 13 to 11 to 11 over the weeks ending 6, 13, 20 and 27 September and 4 October. Units sold were 3, 0, 2 and 0 in the weeks ending 13, 20 and 27 September and 4 October, with no receipts or adjustments, so the 11 units is consistent.
The figure is units on hand in the store at the end of Sunday 4 October 2026. It does not include stock at the central warehouse, which fact_stock_week does not cover.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (they have no sales lines)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern)
UTC timestamps converted to Helsinki time
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' was read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year that ended 3 May 2026, as accepted requests from May 2026 onward did. The request was received on 6 October 2026, in FY2026/27. If FY2024/25 was meant, the figures will differ.
'Periods 5 to 8' was read as fiscal periods P5 to P8 of FY2025/26: 25 August to 21 December 2025, fiscal weeks 18 to 34. P5 and P6 are 4 and 5 weeks, P7 is 4 weeks and P8 is 4 weeks.
'Web shop' was read as all web sales, home delivery and click-and-collect together.
One row per period was given because the request says 'in each of periods 5 to 8'. No total row was added.
caveats: Web returns processed in physical stores are not in these figures. Returns are booked where they are processed, and 'Where processed' is the company rule. Web-order items returned at a store sit under that store, not store 900. These total about 5,495 (P5), 4,784 (P6), 4,901 (P7) and 4,545 (P8) EUR net. If those refunds are also meant to reduce web sales, the four figures would be lower by those amounts.

The 3 November 2025 platform migration falls in P7 and channel_code is empty from that date. The query uses store_id 900, so it is not affected. The legacy view rpt.v_daily_sales would have left out web sales from that date and was not used.
The figures match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for store 900 to the cent in all four periods (145,626.90 / 175,588.62 / 154,977.27 / 225,265.08).
Duplicate sales lines exist (418 receipt/line pairs, loaded twice, 15 to 21 September 2025), all in store 116. They do not touch web sales, so no correction was needed.
Test articles (ZZ Test) and store 999 are excluded, and the filter is built into the query. I did not measure how much it removed from web sales.
Period 6 is 5 weeks long, so its figure is not directly comparable with the 4-week periods without adjusting for length.

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS tampere_loyalty_members FROM dim_member m JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = m.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE m.is_current AND s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900
definitions_applied: Customer = loyalty member, counted once per member_id (stable ID), not per dim_member version row
Current member version only (dim_member.is_current = true), so each member is counted once and sits at their latest home store
Tampere = member's home store (home_store_id) is a physical store whose current dim_store city is Tampere: Hervanta (115), Lielahti (116), Kaleva (117), Lamminpää (136)
Pseudo-locations excluded (store_id >= 900)
assumptions: Warehouse has no customer table, so 'customers' means loyalty members; non-member shoppers cannot be identified or located
'In Tampere' means the member's home store is a Tampere store, since dim_member holds no address or city
Count is all current members with a Tampere home store, active or not, and regardless of marketing consent
Tampere means the city of Tampere only; Nokia (118) is a separate city and is not included
caveats: Correction: dim_store gives the web shop (store 900) and the Training store (999) the city 'Tampere' because they are booked at head office. I excluded them. A plain city = 'Tampere' filter would have included the web shop pseudo-location, whose 12,028 online sign-ups are not Tampere customers.

Correction: dim_member is slowly changing with several rows per member (60,000 members; for the Tampere stores, 11,516 version rows against 7,175 current members). I counted current versions only, because counting version rows or members who were ever at a Tampere store would overstate the figure.

The 12,028 members who signed up online (home_store_id 900) have no store or city, so any of them living in Tampere are not in the 7,175. The true number of Tampere-resident members is probably higher.
Of the 7,175, 4,841 have marketing consent; if the figure is for a mailing or campaign, use that number instead. Lamminpää (opened September 2024) accounts for 974 of the total.

The figure rests on home store, not residence, so members who live in Tampere but registered at another store (or the reverse) are misplaced. The same person holding more than one loyalty number could not be checked.
Figures are as of the 2026-10-08 request; the latest member join date in the warehouse is 2026-10-04.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), period_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ly.fiscal_year AS prior_fiscal_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS prior_net_sales, ty.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS growth_pct FROM period_sales ty JOIN period_sales ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.category
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on the return date, not the sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected orders count
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
As-is reporting: current product version for category (outdoor lighting in Electrical for all history)
Fiscal calendar: period 8 compared with period 8 of the prior year, matched by period number
Growth % = (this year / prior year - 1) x 100
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Request received 5 October 2026 (FY2026/27), so 'last year' is read as FY2025/26 and 'the year before' as FY2024/25. This follows how earlier accepted requests read the phrase.
Period 8 is the fiscal period: FY2025/26 P8 runs 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025 and FY2024/25 P8 runs 25 Nov to 22 Dec 2024. Both are complete and fully loaded, and neither includes week 53.
Garden and Electrical are product categories, reported as-is on the current hierarchy because the requester did not ask for as-was.
Growth is FY2025/26 P8 against FY2024/25 P8, shown as a percentage.
Web sales are included in each category because the request did not limit it to stores.
caveats: Outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 October 2025 (FY2025/26 P7). answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year

WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-11-03' AS start_date, DATE '2026-10-04' AS end_date),

  SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
  WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net
  FROM fact_return_line r
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
  WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT n.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS web_net_sales
FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current
WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date

ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC
LIMIT 10

WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2025-12-21' AS as_of_date
),
as_of AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_week_end_date AS as_of_end
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date = params.as_of_date
),
active AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    CROSS JOIN as_of
    WHERE f.sale_date > as_of.as_of_end - 364
      AND f.sale_date <= as_of.as_of_end
      AND s.store_id != 999
      AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT cur.tier, COUNT(*) AS active_members
FROM active a
CROSS JOIN as_of
JOIN dim_member cur ON cur.member_id = a.member_id
                   AND as_of.as_of_end BETWEEN cur.valid_from AND cur.valid_to
WHERE cur.tier IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY cur.tier
ORDER BY cur.tier
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks ending with the as-of week, in any channel
Loyalty tier from the member version valid on the as-of date
Exclusions: store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test per house rules

Null tier members (if any existed) excluded from the breakdown
caveats: The trailing 52-week window captures sales from 2024-12-23 to 2025-12-21
Store 999 (training/test store) excluded per house rules for member definitions
ZZ Test category purchases excluded per house rules
No material difference observed between including and excluding these categories for member counts, suggesting minimal training/test activity in period

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, s.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, l.format AS store_format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY l.format ORDER BY l.format

Web returns at 12.23% are about three times the store rates. Web refunds follow the original web line even when the return was posted to the web shop. This is a real channel difference on the company definition, not a data error.

WITH params AS (

),
sold_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.sale_date, cp.subcategory, f.net_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s     ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p   ON p.product_key = f.product_key

    WHERE s.store_id <> 999

      AND cp.category = 'Garden'

      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week
),
refunds AS (
    SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net 
    FROM fact_return_line 
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT l.subcategory,
       ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct

Garden subcategories shown are those with sales in the period; if a subcategory had no sales, it does not appear

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date
Trading days: days the store was open (after opening, before closure), outside ref_store_closure refit closures, and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
A store that traded for only part of the period stays in the table with its own trading days
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) left out
Test articles (category ZZ Test) left out; staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P02 is fiscal weeks 5 to 8, 1 June to 28 June 2026
Dimensions joined on store_key and product_key (version at the transaction date); store name and format taken from the current version
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: "Period 2 this year" is read as FY2026/27 P02. The request arrived on 9 October 2026, which falls in FY2026/27, and P2 (1 to 28 June 2026) is complete in the warehouse, which is loaded through 4 October 2026.
Ranking is on net sales per trading day, highest first, using the unrounded value. The per-day figure in the table is rounded to 2 decimals.
Store names and ids are the current ones; the league table does not group by region or format, so as-is versus as-was makes no difference to it.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026, so it has no trading days or sales in June 2026 and is not listed.
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 to 26 July 2026 per the skill notes, but ref_store_closure runs 15 June 2026 onward, so 15 to 28 June fall in this period. It is ranked on its 14 trading days, not 26. Its net sales (23,993.71) cover only those days, so compare its per-day figure (1,713.84) with the other stores, not its total.
Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed holidays and are not counted as trading days, so a store open throughout has 26 trading days, not 28.
The store total (1,063,916.20 EUR) matches rpt_daily_store_sales for physical stores over 1 to 28 June 2026 with zero gap, both in total and store by store.
Savonlinna is not listed because it was closed for the whole period. No zero rows were added.
Sales were taken on the Helsinki business date (sale_date), and returns by their own return_date, so there is no UTC day-edge distortion.
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_ and _old tables) were not used.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns booked on their own return date
Fiscal calendar: P2 of FY2026/27 (weeks 5 to 8, 1 to 28 June 2026) against P2 of FY2025/26 (weeks 5 to 8, 26 May to 22 June 2025), matched by fiscal week number, not calendar date
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900) as part of the total
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), not the order date; cancelled and processing orders carry no sales
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Natural-key and version-key handling: sales and returns joined to dim_store and dim_product on the version keys carried by the fact rows, so no row multiplication
Control total: store and web figures checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days and matched to the cent in all 8 weeks
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, channel_code, stg_, bak_, tmp_ and _old tables) not used
Growth % = (this year / last year - 1) x 100, rounded to one decimal
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2 (1 to 28 June 2026), which is a complete period; 'last year' read as FY2025/26 P2 (26 May to 22 June 2025), in line with how past requests were read in May 2026 onward
'Total company sales' read as net sales excluding VAT (the company default), stores plus web, with no breakdown by region or channel since none was asked for
Each fiscal week is compared with the same-numbered fiscal week last year (weeks 5, 6, 7, 8), as the company rule requires
This is total company growth, not like-for-like: no store-week adjustments were made for refits, openings or closures
Net sales are not shown including VAT, as the request did not ask for that
caveats: Week 7 and week 8 are not comparable like for like because Midsummer falls in different fiscal weeks. Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (20 and 21 June 2025) fell in last year's week 8, and the equivalent days (19 and 20 June 2026) fall in this year's week 7. The stores were shut on those days, which is why last year's week 8 (210,207) and this year's week 7 (220,624) are low. This drives the -32.2% in week 7 and the +76.4% in week 8. Over the whole period the effects offset: this year 1,294,648 against last year 1,195,883, growth 8.3% (computed from the weekly figures, not in the table).

Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a refit from 15 June 2026 to 26 July 2026, which covers this year's weeks 7 and 8 and the end of week 7's comparison. Total company growth is not adjusted for this, so it also pulls this year's weeks 7 and 8 down. Savonlinna (store 129) closed in January 2026 and has no sales this year against a full period last year, which depresses growth in all four weeks. Pori and Tammisto refits do not fall in P2 of either year.

Filters changed the totals slightly: removing store 999 and ZZ Test articles took 2,385.03 EUR off this year's period sales before returns (1,372,772.47 before the filter) and 2,226.03 EUR off last year's (1,286,692.08 before the filter).

No data defects found: sales lines, return lines and web orders have no duplicate keys, every fact row matches a store and product version, no web sales line belongs to a cancelled or undispatched order, VAT amounts are consistent with the stated rates, and the total agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent in every week. No corrections were needed.

Web sales grew strongly (for example week 8: 72,985 against 30,548) which lifts the total growth in all weeks; this is real web net sales on the dispatch date, but web returns are booked on the return date and may arrive after the period for goods dispatched late in the period.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines
Order date in Helsinki time (UTC converted with timezone('Europe/Helsinki', ...))
Cancelled orders excluded, processing orders would be included
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (checked, no effect)
Click-and-collect counted as web
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 read as Monday 1 December 2025, as the request states
Orders counted on the placement date, not the dispatch date, per the company rule for web orders
All fulfilment types and both login states (logged-in and guest) included
caveats: No data corrections were needed. fact_web_order has one row per web_order_id (94,876 rows, 94,876 distinct ids), so there are no duplicate orders.
326 non-cancelled orders on 1 December 2025 (Helsinki): 239 delivered and 87 collected. None are still processing.
19 cancelled orders on the day were excluded; including them would give 345.
None of the 326 orders contain a ZZ Test article or a store 999 line, so the test filter did not change the total.
Day boundaries are Helsinki midnight (UTC+2 in December). Cutting the day at midnight UTC instead would give 274, which is wrong for reporting.

answer.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(r.net_sales) DESC) as rank, d.region, SUM(r.net_sales) as net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r INNER JOIN dim_store d ON r.store_id = d.store_id INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON r.business_date = dd.calendar_date WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.is_current = TRUE AND d.region NOT IN ('Online', 'Head office') GROUP BY d.region ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store sales from rpt_daily_store_sales table
Physical stores only: excluded Online and Head office regions
This year = fiscal year FY2026/27 (04 May 2026 to 04 Oct 2026)
Performance metric: net sales in EUR (excluding VAT)
assumptions: Interpreted 'how they are doing' as net sales performance (standard retail metric)
Interpreted 'this year so far' as FY2026/27 from start to latest available data (04 Oct 2026)
Used current store dimension (is_current = TRUE) to ensure accurate region assignment
Each store assigned to one region; no cross-region allocation
caveats: All five physical store regions have complete data with 152 trading days in the fiscal period
West region has 10 stores and dominates performance; North region has 6 stores
Net sales include returns already accounted for in the daily store sales figures
Data current as of 04 October 2026; any transactions after this date are not included

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT p.sku, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key LEFT JOIN fact_web_order w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND st.store_id <> 999 AND coalesce(w.status, 'x') <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.sku), refunds AS (SELECT p.sku, sum(rl.refund_net) AS refunds_net FROM fact_return_line rl JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = rl.product_key JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = rl.store_key WHERE rl.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND st.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY p.sku), names AS (SELECT DISTINCT sku, product_name FROM dim_product) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, rank() OVER (ORDER BY s.sales_net - coalesce(r.refunds_net,0) DESC) AS rank, s.sku, n.product_name, round(s.sales_net - coalesce(r.refunds_net,0), 2) AS net_sales_eur FROM sold s LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sku) JOIN names n USING (sku) QUALIFY rank <= 10 ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal period: FY2026/27 P05 (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27), from ref_fiscal_calendar
Net sales: line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT) less refund_net on returns dated in the period, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Product identity: one row per sku, with the SKU's several dim_product versions rolled up
Training store (store_id 999) excluded as non-trading
Cancelled web orders excluded; all web lines in the period were delivered or collected
Web channels identified by channel_id (1 = store, 2 = web home delivery, 3 = click and collect), because channel_code is null in this period
assumptions: 'Last period' means the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05. Today is 2026-10-08 and P06 (from 2026-09-28) is still running and not fully loaded.

'Best-selling' means highest net sales value in EUR excluding VAT, after returns. Ranked by units sold instead, the list would be dominated by low-price items such as fixings and fasteners, batteries and storage boxes, and would look quite different.
Staff purchases are kept in, because they are real sales. They total about 715 lines in the period and change no rank materially.
Web and store sales are combined into one total per product, because the request does not ask for a channel split.
Refunds are attributed to the period of the return date, not the original sale date, so a period-P05 return of an earlier sale reduces P05.
caveats: Correction: 139 sales lines (EUR 2,690.92 net) from the Training store (store_id 999) were left out. It is a test location, not a trading store.
Correction: sales lines were grouped by sku and not by product_key. 105 SKUs have several dim_product versions, and grouping by product_key would split their sales across rows.

Correction: channel_code is null on all lines in this period, so a filter on channel_code = 'WB' would find no web sales. Web sales (EUR 193,492 net, about 16% of the period total) were included via channel_id 2 and 3.

Returns reorder the list. Before returns, Home Office Peltola 918 ranked 2nd and Outdoor Lighting Kultala 862 3rd. After returns they swap, 2nd and 3rd. Living Room Havu Pro 936 has no returns and moves up from 8th to 5th. Home Office Peltola 918 lost EUR 1,162.80 to refunds and Home Office Tuulikki 821 lost EUR 727.45.

Places 2 and 3 are close (EUR 7,476.52 against 7,465.18, a gap of EUR 11.34), as are places 5 and 6 (EUR 5,410.67 against 5,409.16, a gap of EUR 1.51). Their order could change with a small change of definition.

Several high-ranking items sell few units at high prices. Living Room Havu Pro 936 sold 11 units, Power Tools Nordhem 370 sold 31 and Power Tools Selkämaa 638 sold 22. Value ranking favours them over high-volume low-price lines.

The warehouse has no written definition of 'best-selling'. Net sales after returns was chosen as the closest to the company's 'net sales' definition in rpt_daily_store_sales. Pekka should confirm whether he meant units or value.
Backup, staging and tmp tables were not used. Only the main fact and dimension tables were used.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.standard_cost) as gross_margin_eur FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE s.region = 'South' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND f.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY gross_margin_eur DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin calculated as gross_amount (revenue including VAT) minus standard_cost
South region as defined in dim_store
Q4 of FY2024/25 spans 27 January 2025 to 27 April 2025
Staff purchases excluded from calculation
assumptions: Gross margin interpreted as absolute amount in EUR, not margin percentage
Ranking by total (summed) gross margin across all transactions for each product in the period
Staff purchases excluded as non-commercial transactions
Product identified by current SKU and product_name from dim_product
caveats: Seven sales lines in this period have negative margins (gross_amount < standard_cost, totalling -18.88 EUR). These are included in the calculation as legitimate transactions, likely caused by standard cost revaluations or minimal pricing adjustments.
Standard costs are revalued each April; transactions analysed span from late January to late April 2025, so cost values reflect two different valuation dates.
Gross margin excludes VAT in the cost basis (standard_cost is direct cost per unit) but includes VAT in revenue, so margin percentage is higher than after-VAT margin would be.
No returns (from fact_return_line) are deducted in this analysis; this reflects the sales invoice perspective rather than net-of-returns contribution.

answer.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date AS d0, period_end_date AS d1 FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period=5), sales AS (SELECT st.store_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS gross_net FROM (SELECT f.* FROM fact_sales_line f, p WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1 AND f.channel_code='ST' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY f.receipt_id, f.line_no ORDER BY f.etl_loaded_at, f.sales_line_id)=1) f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key=f.store_key GROUP BY 1), ret AS (SELECT st.store_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS refunds FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key=r.store_key, p WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1 GROUP BY 1) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY sales.gross_net - coalesce(ret.refunds,0) DESC) AS rank, p.fiscal_year, p.fiscal_period, d.store_id, d.store_name, sales.gross_net - coalesce(ret.refunds,0) AS net_sales FROM sales LEFT JOIN ret USING(store_id) JOIN (SELECT store_id, store_name FROM dim_store WHERE is_current) d USING(store_id), p WHERE sales.store_id < 900 ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2025/26 P05 = Monday 2025-08-25 to Sunday 2025-09-21, 4 weeks, fully loaded)

Net sales = store-channel line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns booked in the period (by return date, at the store that took the return); same definition as the Data & Analytics report rpt_daily_store_sales
Store sales = channel ST only; web shop (store 900) and the training store (999) excluded
Store identity by store_id (all versions of a store rolled up), names from the current dim_store version
Receipt lines de-duplicated on receipt_id + line_no (earliest load kept)
League rank = descending net sales, rank() so ties would share a rank
assumptions: Today is 2026-10-08 (request date), so the current fiscal year is FY2026/27 and 'last year' means FY2025/26; period 5 is therefore 25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025
'Store league table' means all physical stores ranked by net sales (EUR excl. VAT) for the period
Staff purchases are kept in net sales, as the existing Data & Analytics daily report does (about 16,200 EUR net across all stores, 1.6% of store sales)
Returns are netted off in the period they are booked, not the period of the original sale
Only the columns asked for are shown: rank, fiscal year and period, store ID and name, net sales; no region, format or like-for-like columns
caveats: Duplicate loading in Tampere Lielahti (116): 418 sales lines for this period appear twice in fact_sales_line (same receipt and line number, new line id, reloaded on 2025-09-23), adding 10,390.53 EUR of net sales. They were removed; before the correction the store would have shown 47,679 EUR and ranked 5th instead of 7th. The Data & Analytics daily report already excludes them. No other store had duplicates.

Pori (119) was shut for a planned refit from 2025-09-08, so it traded only 14 of the 28 days (weeks 1 and 2 of the period). Its 16,057.86 EUR and 26th place are not comparable with the other stores; on full trading it would rank higher. It is shown unadjusted.
Savonlinna (129) has a close date of 2026-01-25. It was trading during this period and is included, but the store has since closed.
Stores 136 Tampere Lamminpää and 137 Lohja opened in late 2024, so they are fully trading in this period; they would not count as like-for-like against a year earlier.

Store regions were redrawn from 28 April 2025 (for example Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa and Kerava moved from South to Capital Region, Kouvola from East to South). No region is shown here, but any regional roll-up should use the region in force at the time.
The data dictionary describes store formats as Hyper, Standard and Express, while the warehouse holds Small, Medium and Large. Format is not used in this answer.
Old and backup tables (bak_*, *_old, tmp_*, stg_*) were not used.
Net sales are for physical stores only. Web orders (about 158,000 EUR net in the period) and click-and-collect are not attributed to stores.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending), closing AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, c.category, ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM closing c LEFT JOIN sold s ON s.category = c.category ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Last period = last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (weeks 18-21, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026)
Closing stock = snapshot on the last week-ending Sunday of the period (27 Sep 2026), summed across stores and articles
Weeks of cover = closing stock units / average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks, for the same grouping (category)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product hierarchy: current category per SKU (outdoor lighting counted in Electrical)
Stock covers ranged articles in physical stores only; web stock is not in the table
assumptions: 'Last period' read as FY2026/27 P05, the last complete period as of the request date of 7 Oct 2026 (warehouse loaded through 4 Oct 2026; P06 has only one week).
'End of last period' read as the closing snapshot of 27 Sep 2026, the final week-ending Sunday of P05.

'Prior four fiscal weeks' read literally per the stock skill: the four weeks before the snapshot week, 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026 (fiscal weeks 14-17 of FY2026/27). This is not the four weeks of P05 itself, which would include the snapshot week.
Category is the company-wide figure across all physical stores, with no store breakdown, since the request asks for category only.
Category on the current (as-is) hierarchy, as the company default, since the request did not ask for as-was.
Units sold are gross sales quantities, not net of returns, per the company definition of units sold in the weeks-of-cover metric.
caveats: No data problems needing correction were found. The 27 Sep 2026 snapshot has 27,143 rows, unique at store, article and week with a single ETL load, and no negative stock. The sales lines for 24 Aug to 27 Sep have no duplicate keys or non-positive quantities.

Filters applied: store 999 and web (store 900) rows are out of both stock and sales, and ZZ Test articles are out of both. In the sales window these removed 1,680 non-store lines and 18 test-article lines.

Seasonal (48.8 weeks) and Furniture (29.5 weeks) are far above the other categories because their recent sales rates are low relative to stock. Seasonal cover is probably overstated as a forward-looking figure, since the sales window is late summer and seasonal demand is lumpy. A four-week trailing rate is a poor guide for these two.
A different reading of 'prior four weeks' (the four weeks of P05 itself, 31 Aug to 27 Sep) would give somewhat different weeks of cover. The other reading was not computed.
Stock is the ranged-article snapshot only, so articles not ranged in a store are not in cover. Units sold in a store for an article it does not range would still be in the denominator.
The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales was not applied: it covers net sales by store, not units by category.

answer.sql:
WITH q3_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    s.store_id,
    s.region,
    SUM(r.net_sales) AS net_sales
  FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r
  JOIN dim_date d ON r.business_date = d.calendar_date
  JOIN dim_store s ON r.store_id = s.store_id
  WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
    AND r.store_id < 900
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, s.store_id, s.region
),
lfl_stores AS (
  SELECT store_id, region
  FROM q3_sales
  GROUP BY store_id, region
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) = 2
),
lfl_regional_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    qs.fiscal_year,
    lfl.region,
    SUM(qs.net_sales) AS regional_net_sales
  FROM q3_sales qs
  JOIN lfl_stores lfl ON qs.store_id = lfl.store_id AND qs.region = lfl.region
  GROUP BY qs.fiscal_year, lfl.region
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT 
    region,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN regional_net_sales END) AS q3_2024_25_sales,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN regional_net_sales END) AS q3_2025_26_sales
  FROM lfl_regional_sales
  GROUP BY region
)
SELECT 
  region,
  ROUND(((q3_2025_26_sales - q3_2024_25_sales) / q3_2024_25_sales * 100), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM pivoted
ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Like-for-like: only stores that had sales in both Q3 FY2024/25 and Q3 FY2025/26
Growth rate: (current year sales - prior year sales) / prior year sales * 100
Net sales: net of returns, excluding VAT, from rpt_daily_store_sales
Regions: Capital Region, East, North, South, West
assumptions: Last year means fiscal year FY2025/26; comparison is Q3 FY2025/26 versus Q3 FY2024/25
Store sales exclude web channel and staff purchases (store_id < 900 filters to physical stores)
All stores in both periods are like-for-like; no store closures or openings between the two periods
caveats: No data quality issues found; all regions had complete sales data for both comparison periods

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, ROUND(SUM(f.gross_amount), 2) AS web_sales_gross_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 4 AND 6 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2

Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Cancelled and processing orders excluded: only status delivered or collected, which have dispatch times and sales lines

VAT-inclusive value taken by summing gross_amount from the lines, since each line carries its own VAT rate; no flat rate applied

answer.sql: WITH cur AS (SELECT store_id, region FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900), lines AS (SELECT d.store_id, f.sale_date AS d, f.net_amount AS amt FROM (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) = 1) f JOIN dim_store d USING (store_key) WHERE d.store_id < 900 UNION ALL SELECT d.store_id, r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store d USING (store_key) WHERE d.store_id < 900), x AS (SELECT c.region, l.store_id, CASE WHEN l.d BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-10-04' THEN 'TY' WHEN l.d BETWEEN DATE '2025-04-28' AND DATE '2025-10-05' THEN 'LY' END AS yr, l.amt FROM lines l JOIN cur c USING (store_id)) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY sum(CASE WHEN yr='TY' AND store_id NOT IN (119,125,129) THEN amt END) / sum(CASE WHEN yr='LY' AND store_id NOT IN (119,125,129) THEN amt END) DESC) AS rank, region, round(sum(CASE WHEN yr='TY' THEN amt END), 2) AS net_sales_ytd_eur, round(100 * (sum(CASE WHEN yr='TY' AND store_id NOT IN (119,125,129) THEN amt END) / sum(CASE WHEN yr='LY' AND store_id NOT IN (119,125,129) THEN amt END) - 1), 2) AS like_for_like_growth_pct FROM x WHERE yr IS NOT NULL GROUP BY region ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal year FY2026/27 year to date: fiscal weeks 1 to 22, 4 May 2026 to 4 October 2026
Comparison period: the same fiscal weeks of FY2025/26 (28 April 2025 to 5 October 2025), aligned by fiscal week because FY2025/26 was a 53-week year

Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excl. VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net, with refunds counted on the return date and in the store where they were booked (same basis as rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales)
Stores only: store_id below 900 (web shop 900 excluded, training store 999 excluded)
Regions as currently defined in dim_store (is_current = true), which gives five regions after the April 2025 reorganisation: Capital Region, South, East, West, North
Like-for-like (LFL) stores: stores trading in full in both periods, so excluding the three stores in the list below
Ranking by LFL growth in net sales vs the same fiscal weeks last year
assumptions: 'How they are doing this year so far' is read as sales performance against last year, not size. I ranked by LFL net sales growth versus the same fiscal weeks of last year, because regions differ greatly in size and some stores were closed or refitted. If a ranking by absolute net sales was wanted, the order is West (1,815,139), South (1,309,214), East (959,424), Capital Region (948,668), North (730,386). The YTD net sales column shows these totals.

'This year' is the current fiscal year FY2026/27, not the calendar year. YTD runs to the last complete fiscal week (week 22, ending Sunday 4 October 2026). The warehouse is loaded through 4 October. FY2026/27 P06 is flagged not fully loaded because the period runs to 1 November.
The net_sales_ytd_eur column covers all stores in each region that traded this year, including the Kuopio store that was shut for a refit. The growth column uses LFL stores only.
Staff purchases in real stores are kept in sales (same as the Data & Analytics daily report). Only the training store 999, where most of the staff-flagged lines sit, is excluded.
Regions are restated on today's mapping for both years, so last year's figures are not distorted by the reorganisation.

LFL excludes the stores wholly: Pori (119, West) because of the refit 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025 that falls in last year's comparison period, Kuopio (125, East) because of the refit 15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026 in this year's period, and Savonlinna (129, East) because it closed on 25 Jan 2026 and has no sales this year.
caveats: Duplicate load corrected: store 116 Tampere Lielahti (West) has 418 sales lines (836 rows, 178 receipts, about EUR 20.8k net in total) loaded twice for 15 to 21 September 2025, the second load on 23 September 2025. I removed the second copy of each. This affects only last year's comparison base for West; without the correction West's comparison base would be overstated by about EUR 10.4k, and its LFL growth would look about 0.6 points worse. The reporting table rpt_daily_store_sales already carries the de-duplicated figures, and my totals match it exactly.

Region reorganisation corrected: from 28 April 2025 the Helsinki-area stores (101 to 105) moved from South to a new 'Capital Region', and Kouvola (114) moved from East to South. The warehouse schema describes four regions (North, South, East, West), but the data holds five. Last year's sales lines carry the old store version, so grouping by the region on the sale line would have put them in the wrong region. I mapped every store to its current region in both years.

East looks worst, but only part of that is a trading problem. Its total net sales are down 14.8% on last year (959k vs 1,126k), but that includes the Kuopio refit closure (6 weeks) and the closed Savonlinna store. On a like-for-like basis East is down 4.73%, which is still the weakest region.

The like-for-like gaps between regions are small, apart from East. North is flat (-0.04%) and Capital Region, West and South are down about 1.3 to 2.0%. Ranks 3 and 4 (West -1.86% and South -1.97%) are close enough that I would not read much into their order.
Pori (119, West) is excluded from LFL growth because of last year's refit. Its total sales are still in the West YTD net sales figure.

Returns are booked in the period of the return, not the period of the original sale, so net sales follow the same basis as the daily sales report. Web-shop returns are excluded because they are booked on the web-shop pseudo-location.

The warehouse tables contain unmaintained backup, staging and temporary tables (bak_*, stg_*, tmp_*, *_old), which I did not use. The channel_code column on the sales lines is empty for the recent data I checked, so I identified stores by store_id, not by channel.

answer.sql:
-- Like-for-like (LFL) net sales growth, Q3 FY2025/26 by region
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week
),
range_start AS (
    SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week
),
weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN weeks w
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    CROSS JOIN params
    CROSS JOIN range_start
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
    GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year, cs.region))
)
SELECT ty.region, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM lfl_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY ty.region;
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in stores open 52+ weeks before period start, store-weeks trading in both years
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, excluding store 999 and test articles
Physical stores only: store_id < 900
Refit closures excluded: weeks outside ref_store_closure closure windows counted
Week 53 excluded: LFL uses fiscal weeks 27-39 only
Fiscal week comparison: FY2025/26 weeks 27-39 vs FY2024/25 weeks 27-39
As-is hierarchy: current region assignment as of the reporting date
assumptions: Q3 last year interpreted as Q3 FY2025/26 (weeks 27-39 of fiscal year beginning 28 April 2025)
Prior-year comparator is same fiscal week numbers in FY2024/25
Request asks for breakdown by region, so company total row (region NULL) excluded
Web shop (store 900) not included in LFL; LFL is physical stores only
caveats: Savonlinna (store 129) closed 25 January 2026 (week 39). The LFL base includes it only for weeks it traded in both years; it appears in the LFL calculation for weeks 27-38 of FY2025/26, where it traded in both years.
Region assignment is as-is (current as of reporting date). The April 2025 region reorganisation affecting Capital Region is reflected in current assignments.
All sales figures are net of VAT and net of returns, per company net sales definition. Returns are booked on return date, not original sale date, by sale-week cohort.
