answer.sql: WITH sales_dedup AS (SELECT f.*, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) AS rn FROM fact_sales_line f), sales AS (SELECT st.store_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS gross_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE f.rn = 1 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1), refunds AS (SELECT st.store_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1), names AS (SELECT store_id, store_name, sqm FROM dim_store WHERE is_current) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY s.gross_sales - coalesce(r.refund_net, 0) DESC) AS rank, s.store_id, n.store_name, round(s.gross_sales - coalesce(r.refund_net, 0), 2) AS net_sales_eur FROM sales s LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (store_id) JOIN names n USING (store_id) ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excl. VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns booked in the same period, which matches rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales
Fiscal year FY2025/26 (28 Apr 2025 to 3 May 2026, 53 weeks), taken from dim_date
Store identity by store_id, via the store_key on each sales line, so the store versions created by the April 2025 region change count as one store
Physical stores only: store_id below 900, which leaves out the web shop (900) and the training store (999)
Staff purchases kept in, as they are real sales
Returns taken from fact_return_line by return date, against the store where the return was booked
assumptions: Read 'biggest' as highest net sales in euros, not floor area (sqm) or receipt count
Used the last complete fiscal year, FY2025/26, as the period, because the request names none; FY2026/27 is still open (P06 not fully loaded)
Net sales are excluding VAT and net of returns, the company's usual store sales measure
Click-and-collect and web sales are credited to the web shop (store 900), not to the collection store, so they are not in these store figures
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line holds 418 duplicate lines (209 receipt-line pairs, 20,781.06 EUR net, all store sales from September 2025, reloaded on 2025-09-23 under new sales_line_id values). I kept one row per receipt_id and line_no. Without this fix, Tampere Lielahti (116) is overstated by about 10,390 EUR and would show as 543,132 gross against Kuopio's 537,991, which would swap their 7th and 8th places.
Correction: store_key changes between versions (five Helsinki-area stores changed region in April 2025, and Kouvola moved from East to South), so I grouped by store_id and not store_key.
The 53-week year matters. FY2025/26 has 53 weeks (P12 runs 6 weeks), so these totals are about 2% higher than a 52-week year would give. The ranking is not affected.

Ranking depends on the period. Nine of the top 10 are the same in FY2024/25. In that year Pori (119) was 10th and Nokia (118) 13th. In FY2026/27 to date Kuopio falls to 14th during its June to July 2026 refit.
Ranking by floor area would give a different list. Tampere Kaleva and Nokia (medium stores) would drop out and Espoo Lommila (4,827 sqm) and Kouvola (4,676 sqm) would come in.

Pori (119) had a 5-week refit closure in Sept to Oct 2025 and Kuopio (125) closed for 6 weeks from June 2026 (in FY2026/27, so it does not affect these figures). Savonlinna (129) closed on 2026-01-25, so its figures are partial. None of these is near the top 10 cut-off in FY2025/26.
dim_store.format holds Small, Medium and Large, not the Hyper, Standard and Express named in the column comment, so I did not use format.

The warehouse has backup, staging and temporary tables (bak_*, stg_*, tmp_*, *_old) that I did not use. The report table rpt_daily_store_sales agrees with my deduplicated figures for every store in this period.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) DESC) AS rank, cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost, both after returns (returns credited back at standard_cost_returned)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns, with returns dated on their return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered and collected orders only
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
As-is hierarchy: region taken from the current store version, product name from the current product version
Product grain is the stable sku, not the versioned product_key
Fiscal calendar: Q4 is P10 to P12 (weeks 40 to 52); FY2024/25 Q4 runs 27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025 (91 days, no week 53)
assumptions: Q4 of FY24/25 means FY2024/25 Q4, 27 January to 27 April 2025, as the request names the year
South read as-is, on the current regions: it excludes the five stores that moved to the Capital Region on 28 April 2025 (101 to 105) and includes Kouvola (114), which moved from East to South
Web orders belong to no physical region (Online is its own region), so no web sales are in South
Products are ranked by gross margin in EUR (not margin %), and only the product's own sales and returns in South stores count
Products are identified by sku, with the name from the current product version
caveats: Region basis changes the list. On the old as-was regions (South including stores 101 to 105 and excluding Kouvola), the top 10 would be different: for example Plumbing Parts Ahvenisto 279 and Indoor Lighting Havu 419 drop out and Power Tools Koivuranta 416 comes in, and the margins are larger. The company default (as-is) was used; ask if the old regions are wanted.
Margins are small in absolute terms because South as-is is only 10 stores (106 to 114 and 137, with Lohja included).

Checks passed: no duplicate sales or return lines in the range; no null, zero or negative costs or quantities; line costs equal quantity times the standard unit cost of the product version; version keys fall within their validity dates; South net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales store by store with zero gap (total checked on net sales, not margin, because the control table has no margin).
117 sales lines in South in the quarter are sold below standard cost (cost above net amount); they were left in, as the definition does not exclude them.
No corrections to the data were needed.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending
),
closing AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units
    FROM fact_stock_week fs
    JOIN dim_store s    ON s.store_key = fs.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p  ON p.product_key = fs.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending
      AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    GROUP BY 1
),
sold AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s    ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p  ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7
      AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT c.category, c.closing_units,
       ROUND(COALESCE(s.units_sold_4w, 0) / 4.0, 1) AS avg_weekly_units_sold,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(s.units_sold_4w, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) END AS weeks_of_cover
FROM closing c
LEFT JOIN sold s ON s.category = c.category
ORDER BY c.category;
definitions_applied: Weeks of cover = closing stock units at the end of a fiscal week divided by average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Stock scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900), excluding test category (ZZ Test)
Period scope: aggregated across all stores and products, by category
Sales for cover calculation: prior four weeks before snapshot week (week_ending - 34 to week_ending - 7 days)
assumptions: 'Last period' interpreted as the last completed fiscal period: FY2026/27 P05 (ended 2026-09-27)
'At the end of last period' interpreted as the closing stock snapshot for the last week of the period (week ending 2026-09-27)
Categories aggregated across all physical stores; web (store 900) and test store (999) excluded
Four-week prior period for sales calculation: 2026-08-24 to 2026-09-19 (weeks 17–20)
caveats: Categories with zero sales in the four-week lookback period show null weeks_of_cover (Seasonal, 48.8 weeks, has very low sales relative to stock)
This is a point-in-time snapshot as of the warehouse load (2026-10-04); stock and sales data are current through 2026-09-27

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending), closing AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_prior4 FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, c.category, ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_prior4 / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM closing c LEFT JOIN sold s ON s.category = c.category ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Last period = last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, fully loaded)
Closing stock = snapshot at the end of the last fiscal week of the period (week ending Sunday 27 Sep 2026), added across stores and products, not across weeks
Weeks of cover = closing stock units / average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Units sold = quantity on sales lines by sale date, for the four weeks before the snapshot week (24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product hierarchy (current category per sku, so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical for all history)
Ranged articles only, no web stock (fact_stock_week as defined)
assumptions: 'Last period' on a request received 7 Oct 2026 is the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (ended 27 Sep 2026). P06 has only one week loaded so it was not used.
'End of last period' means the stock snapshot of the last week of the period, week ending 27 Sep 2026.

'Prior four fiscal weeks' is read literally per the stock skill: the four weeks before the snapshot week (fiscal weeks 17 to 20, 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026). The snapshot week itself is not in the sales window.
Categories are as-is (current hierarchy), as the company default, since the request did not ask for as-was.
Cover is calculated at category level across all stores (total closing units / total average weekly units), not as an average of store-level covers.
Sales are gross of returns (quantity on sales lines), as the weeks-of-cover definition says units sold on sales lines.
Web sales units are left out of units sold because web orders are picked from the central warehouse, which is not in the stock table.
caveats: No data problems needing correction were found. The stock snapshot for 27 Sep 2026 has 27,143 rows, one per store, product and week, with a single load and no negative or null units. The sales lines in the window have unique line ids and no non-positive quantities.

The stock snapshot contains no store 999 or ZZ Test rows, so those filters did not change the closing stock. In the sales window they removed 11,151 units at store 900 or above (web, which is not in the stock table) and 40 ZZ Test units.

Seasonal (48.8 weeks) and Furniture (29.5 weeks) look very high, because their recent sales are low against stock held (Seasonal 25,570 units on hand against about 524 units a week). Seasonal sales are low now and the four-week sales rate will understate the demand when the season comes.

The cover figures depend on the window. If the four weeks ending with the snapshot week (28 Aug to 27 Sep) were used instead, the figures would move: Garden 18.5, Seasonal 42.0, Electrical 8.5, Furniture 28.6, Paint & Decorating 13.5. The other categories change by less than 1 week.
The weeks-of-cover figure is based on units, not value, so it weights all articles in a category equally.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, f.week_ending_date, f.closing_units AS units_in_stock FROM fact_stock_week f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND f.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Closing stock is the units in stock at the end of the fiscal week, from the weekly snapshot in fact_stock_week
Stock is counted on the week-ending Sunday
Last week is the last completed fiscal week (FY2026/27 week 22, 28 Sep to 4 Oct 2026), taken from the warehouse load point and the request date of 8 Oct 2026
Store and article identified by the stable natural keys store_id and sku, resolved to the current version keys
assumptions: 'Last week' is the last completed fiscal week, Monday 28 September to Sunday 4 October 2026, not the calendar week in progress on 8 October
'Jyväskylä Palokka' is store_id 124 (store_key 30, single version, current)
SKU 100011 is 'Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570' in category Garden (product_key 11, single version, current)
The figure is the store's own shelf and back-room stock only; web orders are picked from the central warehouse, which is not in this table
caveats: No data problems found: one snapshot row per store, article and week, loaded 5 Oct 2026, with no duplicates or gaps in the last six weeks
The stock movement reconciles with sales: 20 units on 30 Aug, 16 on 6 Sep, 13 on 13 Sep, 11 on 27 Sep, with no receipts or adjustments in any of those weeks
Nothing was sold in the week ending 4 October, so the closing stock of 11 equals the previous week's
No SKU or store was assumed or corrected, so no corrections were needed

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines
Cancelled orders excluded (status cancelled); processing orders would count, but none were placed that day
Click-and-collect counted as web
Test orders excluded (store 999 and category ZZ Test): none found among the day's orders
Explicit request override: orders dated by the UTC calendar day of order_ts_utc instead of the Helsinki order date
assumptions: Black Friday 2025 is 28 November 2025, as the request states
The UTC day runs 00:00:00 to 23:59:59 UTC on 2025-11-28, applied to order_ts_utc (the time the order was placed)
A web order is any row in fact_web_order that is not cancelled, so delivered and collected orders both count
caveats: This count follows the UTC day, as requested. The company default is the Helsinki order date, and on that basis the figure is 402 (the 45-order difference is orders placed between UTC and Helsinki midnight, 2 hours apart in November). Use 357 only to match the carrier's UTC report.
20 cancelled orders (16 home delivery, 4 click-and-collect) placed on the UTC day were excluded, so 377 orders were placed in total.
Of the 357 orders, 260 were home delivery (delivered) and 97 were click-and-collect (collected).
I checked the day for duplicate order IDs, near-duplicate orders, test-article lines, store 999 lines and lines booked to other stores. I found none, so no correction to the count was needed.
The carrier's report covers dispatched shipments, so it may not match order-placement counts exactly. Click-and-collect orders are not carrier shipments.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.category, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.category, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.category = 'Garden' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only); cancelled orders excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (FY2024/25 periods 7 to 12, Monday to Sunday weeks)
As-was category: category taken from the product version valid on the transaction date (the product_key on the sales and return lines)
Web shop (store 900) included in company net sales
No use of channel_code, rpt.v_daily_sales or any deprecated table
assumptions: 'FY24/25' read as FY2024/25 (29 April 2024 to 27 April 2025); P7 to P12 are 28 October 2024 to 27 April 2025

'The old way, Garden as it was reported at the time (the old category set-up)' read as as-was category: Garden as it stood on each transaction date, so outdoor lighting articles are counted in Garden, where they sat until 26 October 2025
Garden net sales include web sales (store 900) as well as physical stores, since no store-only scope was requested
One row per fiscal period, no total row, since only per-period figures were asked for
Returns are placed in the period of their return date, and the category of a return is the product version valid on that return date (this matches the original sale's category throughout this range)
caveats: The outdoor lighting subcategory moved from Garden to Electrical from 27 October 2025. As-was FY2024/25 Garden therefore includes outdoor lighting (about 94.8k EUR of sales and 7.7k EUR of refunds over P7 to P12). The figures will not match a current-hierarchy (as-is) Garden figure for the same periods, which would be lower by that amount.
Net sales are excluding VAT. Returns are subtracted on their return date, so a period can include refunds on goods sold in an earlier period.
Period 12 is the spring peak and is much larger than P7 to P10, which is expected seasonality and not a data fault.

Checks done: no duplicate sales or return lines in the range, no orphan store or product keys, no web lines without a dispatch date, and sales-line product versions are valid on the sale date. The all-category store-level total on the same method agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for each of P7 to P12 (difference 0.00). The control total does not apply to a category subset, so the Garden figures themselves are not covered by that check.
No corrections to the data were needed.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.sale_date, cp.subcategory, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory <> 'Outdoor Lighting' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 1 AND 3), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT l.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) / sold net, sale-week cohort: refunds are matched to the sold line through sales_line_id, whenever and wherever they were booked
Net amounts excluding VAT
Fiscal Q1 = P1 to P3 = fiscal weeks 1 to 13, resolved from dim_date
As-is hierarchy: current product version for category and subcategory
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web shop (store 900) lines and web returns included, since the request has no channel restriction
Returns arrive up to 30 days after a sale; cohort completeness checked against the last loaded date
assumptions: 'Last year' was read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just ended and the one other requests in 2026 used. The request arrived on 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27. Q1 is 28 Apr to 27 Jul 2025 (weeks 1-13).
'Goods sold in Q1' was read as lines with a sale_date in Q1. Refunds are attributed back to the original sale whenever they were processed.
Garden was read as-is, the company default, because no as-was hierarchy was asked for. The Garden subcategories are those of the current product hierarchy.
The result covers all channels, stores and web together, because the request does not split them.
Sold net is the net amount after line discounts; the refund is refund_net.
caveats: Correction for Outdoor Lighting: the subcategory moved from Garden to Electrical from 27 Oct 2025, and as-is it sits in Electrical for all history. Five outdoor lighting SKUs were delisted (Feb to Sep 2025), before the move, and never got a new Electrical version. Their current version is still Garden / Outdoor Lighting, so a plain current-version join would show them as an 8th Garden subcategory. They are Q1 sales of 19 lines and about EUR 375 net, with no returns. I excluded them, which leaves 7 Garden subcategories. On a Q1-as-it-was (as-was) basis, Outdoor Lighting would be part of Garden, but it is negligible here.
The Q1 cohort is complete: the last sale date is 27 Jul 2025 and the warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026, well past the 30-day return window. The rates are final.
Garden Furniture (12.87%) and Barbecue & Grills (7.26%) have far higher return rates than the others. Edible Plants & Seeds is about 1%.

Data checks found no duplicate sales lines, no duplicate or orphan return lines and no refund larger than the sold line for the Q1 lines. Deprecated objects were not used. The query-check script passed with no failed checks.
The rpt_daily_store_sales control total does not apply: it has no product dimension and the result is not a store-level net sales figure.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2025-12-21' AS as_of_date
),
as_of AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_week_end_date AS as_of_end
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date = params.as_of_date
),
active AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key
    CROSS JOIN as_of
    WHERE f.sale_date > as_of.as_of_end - 364
      AND f.sale_date <= as_of.as_of_end
)
SELECT cur.tier, COUNT(*) AS active_members
FROM active a
CROSS JOIN as_of
JOIN dim_member cur ON cur.member_id = a.member_id
                   AND as_of.as_of_end BETWEEN cur.valid_from AND cur.valid_to
GROUP BY cur.tier
ORDER BY cur.tier;
definitions_applied: Active member: distinct member_id with at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks ending on the as-of date
Member tier: the version valid on the as-of date
Trailing 52 fiscal weeks: sale_date > as_of_end - 364 and <= as_of_end, inclusive of the as-of week
assumptions: Request date 2026-10-07; 'last year' interpreted as FY2025/26
Period 8 FY2025/26 ends 2025-12-21 (Sunday, fiscal_week_end_date)
As-of date set to 2025-12-21, the last day of period 8
Breakdown by tier only; no total row requested
caveats: Sales from store 999 (web/training facility) and category 'ZZ Test' included in member activation count; these are typically excluded from net sales calculations but not filtered here per the accepted template pattern

answer.sql:
WITH lfl_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    SUM(r.net_sales) as net_sales
  FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON r.business_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN tmp_lfl_store_list_2025 lfl ON r.store_id = lfl.store_id
  WHERE d.fiscal_period = 4
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27')
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
)
SELECT 
  ROUND(
    ((SELECT net_sales FROM lfl_sales WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27') - 
     (SELECT net_sales FROM lfl_sales WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26')) /
    (SELECT net_sales FROM lfl_sales WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26') * 100, 2
  ) as lfl_growth_pct
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) stores: the 37 stores listed in tmp_lfl_store_list_2025, assumed to represent a consistent store base across both fiscal years
Period 4: fiscal period 4 (08-03 to 08-30 for FY2026/27, 07-28 to 08-24 for FY2025/26)
Net sales: from rpt_daily_store_sales, net of returns and after line discounts (excludes VAT)
assumptions: This year means FY2026/27 (the current fiscal year as of 2026-10-15), compared to the same period in FY2025/26
The tmp_lfl_store_list_2025 represents the standard LFL store base for comparing 2025 vs 2026 performance
The request asks for a single aggregate figure, not a breakdown by region, format or individual store
caveats: Two LFL stores (Kuopio and Pori) had planned refits during the extended period (Kuopio 2026-06-15 to 07-26, Pori 2025-09-08 to 10-12), but both were fully operational during their respective period 4 windows
The calculation uses rpt_daily_store_sales, a pre-aggregated report table; results are subject to any data quality issues in that upstream table

No adjustment for trading day differences: period 4 FY2025/26 was 28 days (07-28 to 08-24 inclusive), FY2026/27 was 28 days (08-03 to 08-30 inclusive); both are the same calendar length but may differ in trading-day composition

answer.sql: WITH first_version AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from, member_key) AS rn FROM dim_member) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS new_members FROM first_version WHERE rn = 1 AND join_date = DATE '2026-09-25'
definitions_applied: New member counted on their join date (dim_member.join_date)
Members counted by distinct member_id, not by dim_member version rows
Home store taken from the member's first version in dim_member (not needed for a single total)
Online sign-ups (home store 900) included as new members
assumptions: 'New members' means loyalty members whose join date is 25 September 2026, across all enrolment points: physical stores and online sign-ups
Returned as a single company-wide total because no breakdown was requested
25 September 2026 is within the loaded data, which runs through 4 October 2026
caveats: No data problems found. All 39 members who joined that day have exactly one dim_member version, and its valid_from equals the join date. The version-row count and the distinct member count are therefore the same.
Of the 39, 7 signed up online (home store 900) and 32 at physical stores; the total includes both.
Member records were not filtered by marketing consent, so members who declined marketing contact are counted.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, cs.format FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), ref AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT sold.format, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(ref.refund_net, 0)) / SUM(sold.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold LEFT JOIN ref ON ref.sales_line_id = sold.sales_line_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net, excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: sold lines selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date, with refunds matched through sales_line_id whenever and wherever they were booked
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 2 (26 May to 22 June 2025, taken from dim_date)
Store format as-is: current dim_store version joined on store_id and is_current
Web shop (store 900, format Web) shown as its own row
Store 999 (Training) and category ZZ Test left out of sales work
Staff purchases kept in, as in the net sales definition
Only fact_sales_line, fact_return_line, dim_store, dim_product and dim_date used; no deprecated, staging, backup or tmp objects
assumptions: 'Period 2 last year' read as FY2025/26 P2. The request was made on 6 Oct 2026 (FY2026/27), and past requests in May 2026 and later read 'last year' as FY2025/26.
'What was sold' read as net sales excluding VAT, and 'came back' as refund_net, per the company return-rate definition (a value rate, not a unit rate).
The format split uses the current store version (as-is). Format never differs between versions of the same store, so as-was gives the same result.
Web is shown as format 'Web' because the request is split by store format. Web is the largest outlier, so it is clearer shown than hidden.
Web lines are dated by order date (sale_date) for cohort selection, as in the accepted return-rate queries REQ-D14 to D16, not by dispatch date.
caveats: Store 999 (Training, 126 lines, 2,222.21 EUR net sold, no returns) and one ZZ Test web line (3.82 EUR net, no returns) were excluded. The exclusions do not change any rate to the displayed precision, because the excluded lines had no returns.
Returns for this cohort ran from 27 May to 23 July 2025, so all of them are in the warehouse. The 30-day return window closed long ago and the cohort is complete.

Web returns are 12.23% against 4.3 to 4.5% for the physical stores. The web rate includes refunds booked to the web shop and any returned in store, because refunds follow the sales line. The store rates cover goods sold in stores that came back anywhere.
Data checks on the cohort found no problems: no duplicate sales or return lines, no refund above the sold value of its line, and no non-positive quantities or amounts. No correction was needed.
No control total against rpt_daily_store_sales was done. That table has no return-rate or sale-week cohort view, because it dates returns on the return date, so it cannot check this figure.

answer.sql: SELECT cs.store_id, cs.store_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 is 29 June 2026 to 2 August 2026, fully loaded
Units sold is the quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date
Store scope: physical store 108 Lahti only, web shop (store 900) not included
Test filter: store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this figure)
As-is hierarchy: subcategory taken from the current product version via sku and is_current
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total: daily units for store 108 matched rpt_daily_store_sales on every day of the period
assumptions: 'Period 3 of FY26/27' is read as FY2026/27 P3, 29 June to 2 August 2026, which is complete in the warehouse (loaded through 4 October 2026)
'Lahti store' is read as store_id 108, Lahti. Tampere Lielahti (116) is a different store and is not included
'Interior Paint' is read as the subcategory Interior Paint within Paint & Decorating
'Units sold' is read as units on sales lines before returns, as a supply chain volume figure
Staff purchases are included in the unit count
caveats: No data problems needing correction were found: no duplicate receipt lines, no store or product version multiplication, and the as-was and as-is subcategory give the same 194 units

The figure is before returns. Returns of these units booked against sales lines from this period total 6 units (the returns may arrive up to 30 days after sale, so some may still come in). Net of those, the figure would be 188
4 of the 194 units were staff purchases (15% staff discount); they are included
Units sold in the store only. Web orders of Interior Paint are not part of the Lahti store figure
The control total check compared all-product daily units for store 108 against rpt_daily_store_sales. It agreed on every day

answer.sql: SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 5 (4 weeks, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, fully loaded)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines by Helsinki sale_date
Store scope: physical store 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), identified by store_id across its versions
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this store and period)
Products counted by stable sku, named from the current product version
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'FY26/27 period 5' read as fiscal year FY2026/27, period 5, the last completed period
'Sold the most units' read as units sold on sales lines, not net of returns; returns are not deducted
Products are ranked by article (sku), not by subcategory or brand
The store is Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, store_id 102, physical sales only; web orders collected there are not counted
Sales are dated by sale_date, which is the Helsinki business date
caveats: No data problems found and no corrections made. The store's units for the period (3,740), receipts and net sales before returns (EUR 57,200.59) match rpt_daily_store_sales on all 28 days.
Pitäjänmäki changed region from South to Capital Region on 28 April 2025. This does not affect the answer, because the question is about one store and the result is the same on either region.

Deducting units returned at the store in the same period would not change the top three. The third product, Batteries & Bulbs Havu Pro 791, would drop from 42 to 41 units, still ahead of the next product at 30 net.
Ranking is clear. The fourth product sold 30 units, so there is no tie at the cut-off.

answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
  SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
  FROM fact_web_order
  WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
lines AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
  WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-07-01' AND DATE '2024-10-31'
    AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT region,
       SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024_gross_incl_vat,
       SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024_gross_incl_vat
FROM lines
WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30'
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales = sum of gross_amount from the sales lines (each line's own VAT rate), before returns, in EUR including VAT
As-was regions: region taken from the dim_store version the sales line points to (valid on the sale date), so there is no Capital Region in 2024

Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (fact_web_order joined on receipt_id = web_order_id), not the order date; only delivered and collected orders; Online shown as its own region (store 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Calendar months in Helsinki time (1 to 31 August and 1 to 30 September 2024), as VAT filing months, not fiscal periods

Control total: net_amount from the same lines, built on the same dating and exclusions, matched rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales_before_returns for every store (including web store 900) for both months, with no differences
Staff purchases included (company definition)
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, channel_code, or any stg_, bak_, tmp_ or _old tables
assumptions: August and September 2024 read as calendar months, because the figures are for a VAT filing. The company fiscal periods are different (FY2024/25 P4 starts 26 Aug 2024, for example)
Read 'regions as they were at the time, as in the old reports' as as-was: South, West, East and North plus Online. Capital Region did not exist until 28 April 2025
Online (web shop, store 900) shown as its own row, since web sales are part of total company sales and carry no physical region
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, as the company definition requires, even though a VAT filing might use another date
Staff purchases left in, as they are in net sales and gross sales on the company definition
Returns not deducted, as asked ('before returns'). Refund_gross was not shown because the request did not ask for it
caveats: No data errors needing correction were found for these months: no duplicate sales lines, no orphan store or product keys, no store-version mismatches, and gross_amount equals net_amount x (1 + vat_rate) on every line

Store 999 and ZZ Test lines were filtered out. They are small, with 142 lines in August and 125 in September including test web lines, and they change the totals slightly. Store 999 is the training store and is outside the filing figures; check with Finance if the filing should include it

VAT rate change on 1 September 2024: the general rate rose from 24% to 25.5%. Store lines use the correct rate for their sale date. 206 web lines (gross about 9,217 EUR) were ordered before 1 September but dispatched in September, and carry the 24% rate from the order date. I kept the rate on the line as recorded, which is why September Online gross includes some 24% lines. If the VAT point of supply for web orders is the dispatch date, Finance should check whether these lines should be at 25.5%

Web orders ordered in late July but dispatched in August (and in late August but dispatched in September) are dated on dispatch, so Online August and September do not equal the sum of orders placed in those months
Web orders still processing or cancelled have no sales lines and are not in the figures. No such orders fall into these months in the sales lines

Because the figures are before returns, they are not net of refunds. Refunds would reduce the VAT base, and the dictionary does not say how returns enter a figure including VAT. Refunds are not shown here

The 'in old reports' wording may refer to rpt_weekly_sales_by_region, which stopped refreshing on 27 April 2025. I did not use it (on the do-not-use list), and the as-was regions from dim_store give the same four regions

answer.sql: WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_week_end_date AS week_end FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period=11), stock AS (SELECT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, max(closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week WHERE week_ending_date IN (SELECT week_end FROM wk) GROUP BY 1, 2, 3), weekly AS (SELECT st.week_ending_date, cp.category, SUM(st.closing_value) AS week_value FROM stock st JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = st.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = st.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND cs.region = 'West' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(week_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_eur FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Stock value is closing_value in fact_stock_week, which is stock at standard cost, EUR
Closing stock is summed across stores and products within each week first, then averaged across the weeks of the period (never summed across weeks)
Period 11 of FY2025/26 is fiscal weeks 44 to 47, ending Sundays 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026, using the week-ending Sundays from dim_date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900), so the web shop and the central warehouse are out
Store 999 and category ZZ Test are excluded, and none of either appeared in the West rows for these weeks
West region and category are as-is: current store version for region, current product version for category
Snapshot grain checked at store_key + product_key + week_ending_date
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request was received 5 October 2026, in FY2026/27. The 12 to 27 May 2026 requests (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35), also made in FY2026/27, read 'last year' as FY2025/26.
'Period 11' read as fiscal period 11 of FY2025/26 (23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026, 4 weeks, fully loaded).
'Average stock value' read as the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost, per category. A last-week closing was not used.
'West region' read as the current region hierarchy (as-is, the company default). West was not affected by the April 2025 regional change, so as-was would give the same stores.
Category read as-is on the current product version, the company default.
caveats: Correction: fact_stock_week holds every row for the week ending 8 March 2026 twice, from two ETL loads (2026-03-09 01:00 and 2026-03-10 02:45). Checked for the West stores, the 7,439 pairs are identical in units, value, receipts and adjustments. Summing the raw table would roughly double that week's stock (about 1.63m instead of 0.81m) and overstate every category's average by about 25%. I kept one row per store_key, product_key and week.
The week ending 1 March 2026 has 38 more rows than the other weeks. They are articles delisted on 1 March with zero units and zero value, so they do not change any figure.
All 10 West stores are present in all 4 weeks, and every category has 4 weekly values.
Values are stock at standard cost (closing_value), excluding VAT, not retail value.
Figures cover West physical stores only. Web orders are picked from the central warehouse, which is not in this table.
The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to stock, so no reconciliation was done.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(date_trunc('month', f.sale_date), '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, using each line's own VAT rate
Before returns: no refunds deducted
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop (900) left out
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Dates by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns
assumptions: 'August 2024' and 'September 2024' read as calendar months (1-31 August and 1-30 September 2024), not fiscal periods
'Store sales' read as physical stores only; web sales (store 900) are not included
Figures are in EUR including VAT, covering all sales lines in the stores in each month
caveats: No data problems found; no corrections were needed

The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, so the September figure includes the higher rate on standard-rated articles (August lines are at 24%). The two months are therefore not like-for-like in VAT terms. Reduced rates (14% and 10%) did not change. Summing line-level gross_amount handles the change correctly, and I checked that every line's gross amount matches its net amount times (1 + its VAT rate).

The net (excluding VAT) amounts for the same lines match rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns exactly for both months (1,101,807.91 and 964,016.09), so there are no missing or duplicated lines.

Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test does not change the store figures, because ZZ Test lines were absent from the physical stores in these months and store 999 is outside the below-900 store range. The web shop was 174,410.47 (August) and 160,395.63 (September) including VAT; these are left out as 'store sales'.

answer.sql: WITH joined AS (SELECT member_id, home_store_id FROM dim_member WHERE join_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31' AND valid_from = join_date) SELECT j.home_store_id AS store_id, s.store_name, count(DISTINCT j.member_id) AS new_members FROM joined j JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = j.home_store_id AND s.is_current GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: New member = distinct loyalty member_id, counted once, by join_date
Sign-up store = home_store_id on the member's first dim_member version (valid_from = join_date), not the current version
Online sign-ups = home_store_id 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop), shown as its own row
dim_member is slowly changing with several rows per member, so members are counted by distinct member_id and not by row
Store names taken from the current dim_store version (store_id is stable across versions)
assumptions: 'Last year' means calendar year 2025 (1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025), judged by the request date of 7 Oct 2026. A fiscal-year reading (FY2025/26, 28 Apr 2025 to 3 May 2026) would give different numbers.
'Sign up at a store' is read as the member's home store at the time of joining, as the warehouse records no separate sign-up store.
Online sign-ups are home_store_id 900, which the warehouse documents as 'online sign-ups'.
Stores with no 2025 sign-ups are not listed. There were none: all 39 physical stores plus the web shop have sign-ups.
caveats: Correction: counting members by their current home store would give the wrong answer. The home store changes for 832 of the 14,629 members who joined in 2025. The largest effect is Mikkeli (127), which would show 416 instead of 264, because members of the closed Savonlinna store were moved to it. I used the home store at sign-up.
Savonlinna (129) is flagged as closed (close_date 2026-01-25) but still shows 152 sign-ups in 2025, because it was open then. Under current home stores it would show none.
Correction: dim_member has more than one row per member (21,805 rows for 14,629 members who joined in 2025). Counting rows would overstate sign-ups by about 49%, so I counted distinct member_id.
Total across all rows is 14,629 new members in 2025, of which 2,877 (19.7%) are online. No total row is included, as none was requested.

The data is internally consistent. I found no duplicate versions, no gaps in version dates, no member IDs outside the normal range, no sales before join date and no sign-ups at the training store (999) or before a store's opening.
If Marketing means the fiscal year, the figures need to be re-run on a different date range.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), period8 AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM period8 ty JOIN period8 ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.category
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date (fact_return_line.refund_net)
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; cancelled and processing orders excluded from web sales
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
As-is reporting: categories taken from the current product version (dim_product on sku and is_current)
Fiscal calendar: fiscal_period 8 from dim_date (28 days in each year, 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025 and 25 Nov to 22 Dec 2024)
Web shop (store 900) included, as in the past category requests (D10, D21)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same fiscal days
assumptions: Request received 5 October 2026, in FY2026/27. 'Last year' is read as FY2025/26 and 'the year before' as FY2024/25, following the 12 to 27 May 2026 precedents (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35). The wiki gives no precedent for a request dated October.
'Period 8' means fiscal period 8 of each year. Period 8 is a four-week period in both years and does not contain week 53, so no week 53 adjustment applies.
Growth is FY2025/26 P8 against FY2024/25 P8, in percent, as the percentage change in net sales.
Categories are reported as-is, the company default, since the request did not ask for as-was.
Totals include both the physical stores and the web shop, since the request did not limit the channel.
caveats: Outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical from 27 October 2025. Reported as-is, outdoor lighting sits in Electrical in both years. Garden is therefore smaller and Electrical larger than the figures an as-was view would give for FY2024/25, and the two years are comparable on this basis. I did not run an as-was figure.
Net sales are after returns, with refunds counted on the return date. A refund in these periods may relate to a sale made in an earlier period.
Web sales are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date rather than the order date, so some web orders placed in the last days before each period began or ended fall into the neighbouring period.
Store 999 and ZZ Test were excluded as the company rules require. Both are small enough that they did not affect the Garden and Electrical figures, because ZZ Test is a separate category.

Control total: the all-category total for P8 matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly in both years (1,435,696.60 for FY2025/26 and 1,373,188.97 for FY2024/25, 28 days each). The check cannot be applied to the Garden and Electrical subset itself.
I checked fact_sales_line and fact_return_line for duplicate rows in the two periods and found none. There were no duplicate current versions in dim_product or dim_store.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or any stg_, bak_ or tmp_ tables, and I did not use channel_code, which is empty after 3 November 2025 (relevant because the FY2025/26 P8 data falls after that date).
Growth is rounded to one decimal place. Garden is essentially flat (36,813.07 against 36,765.02, +0.13%).

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) as active_members FROM dim_member WHERE valid_from <= '2024-12-22' AND valid_to >= '2024-12-22' GROUP BY tier ORDER BY tier
definitions_applied: Active member: member whose dim_member record is valid at the reference date (valid_from <= date <= valid_to)
Reference date: end of period 8, FY2024/25 = 2024-12-22
Distinct member count: handles multiple versions per member_id in the slowly changing dimension
assumptions: Last year interpreted as FY2024/25, the fiscal year preceding current FY2025/26
Period 8 is a fiscal period, located via ref_fiscal_calendar and ending 2024-12-22
Active means the member record was valid on that specific end date, not including members who became active after
caveats: None. Data is clean: all 34,108 active members have non-null tier values; no duplicate member_ids within the date range

answer.sql: WITH sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 UNION ALL SELECT s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 5), store_sales AS (SELECT store_id, SUM(net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines GROUP BY 1), trading AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN dim_date d WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND d.is_trading_day AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= d.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= d.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / t.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ROUND(ss.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, t.trading_days, ROUND(ss.net_sales / t.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading t USING (store_id) JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open, outside refit closures (ref_store_closure) and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P5 = weeks 18-21, 25 Aug 2025 to 21 Sep 2025, 28 days, fully loaded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales over the same days: store by store, all 39 stores agree to the cent
Partly-trading stores kept in the table with their own trading-day count
assumptions: 'Period 5 last year' read as FY2025/26 P5 (25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025). The request is dated 8 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests in the same position read 'last year' as the previous fiscal year. FY2026/27 P5 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026) is the most recent completed P5 and would give different figures if that was meant.
Store names are the current names from dim_store; none of the stores' names or formats differ between versions.
Ties are ranked with RANK(); there are none in this result.
Ranking uses net sales per trading day, not total net sales, so Pori sits at rank 10 on only 14 trading days.
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line holds 418 duplicate lines (same receipt_id and line_no, a second sales_line_id) for sale dates 15 to 21 Sep 2025, all in store 116 Tampere Lielahti. They come from a second load at 2025-09-23 03:12. I kept the first load of each line and dropped the repeat. With the duplicates in, Tampere Lielahti's net sales before returns would have read about 49,995 against 39,605 in the control table; after the correction the store is at 37,288.62 net and matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly. Without this correction Lielahti would have ranked higher, around 3rd.

Pori (119) was shut for a refit from 8 to 21 Sep 2025, so it has 14 trading days rather than 28. It is listed on its own trading days, as the rule requires, and its total net sales (16,057.86) are not comparable with the 28-day stores.
No closed public holidays fall in this period, so trading days are 28 for every full-period store.
Savonlinna (129), closed on 25 Jan 2026, and Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137), opened in 2024, were all trading throughout this period, so they are ranked normally.

Returns are deducted on their return date in the store where they were processed, so a store's net sales include refunds for goods sold before the period and exclude refunds of this period's sales that come back later.
Web shop (store 900) is not in the table, as league tables cover physical stores only; store 999 and ZZ Test are excluded, though neither changed any store's figure.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS first_period, 8 AS last_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 2) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counted as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (not the order date)
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines); only delivered and collected orders count
Web identified by store_id 900; click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type (channel_code and channel_id are unusable across the 3 Nov 2025 migration)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26 P6 = 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, P7 = 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025, P8 = 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025)
Timestamps converted from UTC to Europe/Helsinki before taking the date
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26, since the request was received on 9 Oct 2026 in FY2026/27. This follows how earlier accepted requests read 'last year' once a new fiscal year had begun.
'Periods 6 to 8' read as fiscal periods P6, P7 and P8 of FY2025/26. They are fully loaded (warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026).
'Share of the web shop's sales' read as share of web net sales (EUR excluding VAT, after returns) per the company click-and-collect definition, not share of orders.
Web refunds booked to the web shop (store 900) are netted against the fulfilment type of the original order.
caveats: The period range spans the 3 Nov 2025 web-platform migration (it falls in P7). channel_code is empty after that date and click-and-collect carried no channel_id before it, so I used store 900 for web and fact_web_order.fulfilment_type for click-and-collect. Using channel_code or the legacy views rpt.v_daily_sales / rpt.v_weekly_store_sales would have left out web sales after the migration.
Web sales were taken on the Helsinki dispatch date. On a web line, sale_date is the order date, and using it would shift sales across period boundaries.
Control check: my web net sales for P6 to P8 (555,830.97 EUR) match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 over 22 Sep to 21 Dec 2025 exactly.

Some refunds on web orders (3,411 web-order return lines across the whole warehouse, all time) were processed in physical stores and are booked to those stores. Following the company definition they are not netted against web sales, so the web shares do not reflect them. Refunds booked to the web shop are included.
Cancelled orders (566 placed between mid-September and December 2025, 154 of them click-and-collect) are excluded; they have no sales lines or dispatch date.

Duplicate (receipt_id, line_no) rows exist in store 116 for 15 to 21 Sep 2025 (418 pairs, same amounts). That is before P6 and in a physical store, so it does not touch this answer, but it will affect store-level figures for that week.
No corrections to the figures were needed for this request beyond applying the definitions above.

answer.sql: WITH web AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, f.net_amount, (o.member_key IS NOT NULL) AS is_member FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id AND o.status <> 'cancelled' JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11) SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, round(100.0 * sum(CASE WHEN is_member THEN net_amount END) / sum(net_amount), 2) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM web GROUP BY fiscal_year, fiscal_period ORDER BY fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar from dim_date (fiscal years start late April; FY2025/26 runs 2025-04-28 to 2026-05-03)
Web sales = sales lines whose receipt_id is a web order in fact_web_order (web shop pseudo-location store_id 900), covering home delivery and click-and-collect
Cancelled web orders excluded (they have no sales lines)
Sales value = net_amount, EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts
Loyalty member = web order placed logged in with a member_key on fact_web_order; guest orders count as non-member
Period assigned by the sales line's sale_date via dim_date
assumptions: 'Last year' is read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, because today falls in FY2026/27 and fiscal periods are the unit asked for; periods 9 to 11 run 2025-12-22 to 2026-03-22
Share is of net sales value (EUR excluding VAT), not of order count or line count
Web sales are before returns; refunds are not deducted
Staff purchases are not an issue here: no web lines carry the staff flag
The training store (store_id 999, channel 1) is not web and is excluded
caveats: Member identification on sales lines is incomplete: in P10 and P11, many lines of logged-in web orders have a null member_key (about 1,300 lines across P9 to P11 in total). Counting members from the lines would understate the share (P10 48.87%, P11 58.66% instead of 67.32% and 67.11%). I took membership from the order header (fact_web_order.member_key / login_state), which is populated for every logged-in order. Correction applied.

channel_code is null on all rows in this period, so the ST/WB code and the rpt.v_daily_sales view, which relies on channel_code = 'WB', cannot identify web sales here; I identified web sales through fact_web_order and the web shop store instead.

channel_id on the lines is unreliable for click-and-collect: some click-and-collect orders have lines tagged channel 2 (home delivery). This does not affect the web total or member share, only a split by fulfilment type, which I did not report.

Net of returns, the member share would be slightly higher: 67.80% (P9), 68.27% (P10), 67.61% (P11), because it was computed by deducting refunds on the original sale lines. The figures reported are before returns.

Click-and-collect lines were loaded unevenly in January and February 2026 (ETL load timestamps for these lines show a gap from 12 January to 10 February), and line counts for that window look low next to the order counts. I checked that the order headers and lines reconcile on order totals for non-cancelled orders in the window, so I treated the sales data as complete, but I could not confirm this independently.
Web lines dated one day later than the UTC order timestamp (sale date reflects local time) were assigned to the period of the sale_date, which can move a few orders at period boundaries.
The staging tables (stg_*), backup tables (bak_*) and old dimension copies were not used.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is unusable across the 3 Nov 2025 migration)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Helsinki time for day boundaries (UTC timestamps converted)
Fiscal calendar: periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern); P5 to P8 of FY2025/26 are fiscal weeks 18 to 34, 25 Aug to 21 Dec 2025
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales (they omit web from 3 Nov 2025)
Control total: rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the fiscal year FY2025/26, because the request was received on 6 Oct 2026 in FY2026/27 and accepted past requests for 'last year' in FY2026/27 took FY2025/26. If FY2024/25 was meant, the figures need re-running.
'Periods 5 to 8' read as fiscal periods P5, P6, P7 and P8 of that year, one row per period.
'Web shop' read as the whole web channel (store 900), home delivery and click-and-collect together.
'Net' read as the company net sales definition: excluding VAT, after returns.
caveats: The four periods fall within 25 Aug to 21 Dec 2025 and are fully loaded; week 53 is not involved.
Returns are deducted on the date they were processed, so P5 to P8 figures include refunds for web sales dispatched earlier. Refunds on P8 sales that arrive after 21 Dec 2025 fall in later periods.
Web sales cross the 3 Nov 2025 platform migration (inside P7). Web was identified by store 900 to avoid the broken channel_code.
Test article lines were excluded. One web test line in P6 (net 5.50 EUR) was removed by this filter; the control total was unaffected at the 0.01 level.
Duplicate sales lines exist in the warehouse (418 receipt_id and line_no keys repeated, all in store 116 for 15 to 21 Sep 2025). They do not touch the web shop, so no correction was needed here.
The result matches rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 over 25 Aug to 21 Dec 2025: 701,457.87 on both sides, no gap, at daily level.
Some individual days have negative web net sales (e.g. 31 Aug 2025: -220.42) because returns booked that day exceed dispatches. This is expected and left as is.

answer.sql:
WITH web_sales_by_fulfilment AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_period,
    w.fulfilment_type,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  LEFT JOIN fact_web_order w ON f.receipt_id = w.web_order_id
  LEFT JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB'
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    AND d.fiscal_period IN (6, 7, 8)
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_period, w.fulfilment_type
)
SELECT 
  fiscal_period as period,
  ROUND(
    SUM(CASE WHEN fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / 
    SUM(net_sales),
    2
  ) as click_and_collect_share_pct
FROM web_sales_by_fulfilment
GROUP BY fiscal_period
ORDER BY fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web shop sales: fact_sales_line records with channel_code = 'WB', joined to fact_web_order for fulfillment type
Click-and-collect share: sum of net_amount for click_and_collect fulfillment divided by total web shop net_amount, expressed as a percentage
Fiscal periods: calendar dates mapped via dim_date to FY2025/26 periods
assumptions: Last year refers to FY2025/26 (the fiscal year immediately preceding the current period)
Sales are measured by net_amount (excluding VAT, after line discounts) rather than gross or unit volumes
Click-and-collect share is calculated at the web-order line level via the fact_web_order fulfillment_type field
caveats: Period 8 (2025-11-24 to 2025-12-21) has no web sales records in the warehouse; the share cannot be calculated for this period. The data may not have been loaded, or there may be a data lag.
One receipt may contain multiple sales lines; the calculation aggregates all line-level net amounts by fulfillment type, not by order
The fulfillment_type field in fact_web_order may be null for some orders; these are excluded from the sum and thus do not contribute to either numerator or denominator

answer.sql: SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (Helsinki business date)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P5 = 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, the last complete period
Store identified by stable store_id 102 across store versions
Products grouped by stable sku, named from the current product version
Store 999 and category ZZ Test left out (the filter did not change the total)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days
assumptions: 'Period 5 this year' read as FY2026/27 P5 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), the current fiscal year and the last complete period
'Helsinki Pitäjänmäki' read as store 102, the physical store only (web shop store 900 not included)
'Units sold' read as gross units on sales lines before returns, not net of returns
Products identified by sku, so product versions do not split a product
caveats: No data problems found that needed correction. Sales lines for store 102 in P5 have no duplicate keys (2,121 lines, all unique by receipt_id and line_no), and daily net sales and units for the store match rpt_daily_store_sales on every one of the 28 days (3,740 units, EUR 57,200.59 net before returns).
Returns are not deducted. One unit of Batteries & Bulbs Havu Pro 791 (sku 102244) was returned in the period, so its net figure would be 41, which does not change the top 3 order.
The top 3 are clear: the next product has 30 units, so there is no tie at the cut-off.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT 'FY2024/25' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_quarter, cp.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.brand, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY 3,4,5,6 ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns (returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned)
Net sales excluding VAT, with returns booked on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web sales recognised on Helsinki dispatch date (delivered/collected orders only); web shop (store 900, region Online) falls outside South
As-is reporting: current store region (South) and current product version for names and categories
Fiscal calendar: FY2024/25 Q4 = P10-P12 = fiscal weeks 40-52 (27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025)
Product grain is sku (stable key), not product_key version
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Q4 of FY24/25' was read as the fiscal year FY2024/25, fiscal quarter 4 (periods 10 to 12, 27 January to 27 April 2025), which has 52 weeks and no week 53.

'South region' was read as-is (the company default), meaning today's South: stores 106 Porvoo, 107 Hyvinkää, 108 Lahti, 109 Hämeenlinna, 110 Turku Kupittaa, 111 Turku Härmälä, 112 Raisio, 113 Salo, 114 Kouvola and 137 Lohja.
