Kouvola (114) was East then and is included.
'Top 10 products' was read as individual articles (sku) ranked by gross margin in EUR, not margin percentage.
Product names and categories come from the current product version; margin comes from the standard cost on each sales and return line.
Net sales and gross margin are in EUR excluding VAT; no ties at the cut-off (10th is 978.84, 11th is 935.46).
caveats: Region basis changes the list. Under the as-was reading (South as it stood in Q4 FY24/25, including stores 101-105 and excluding Kouvola) the ranking differs: the first six are the same, but Power Tools Havu Pro 689 moves up to 7th, and Power Tools Koivuranta 416 (101369) enters the top 10 while Indoor Lighting Havu 419 drops out. The margin figures are also higher (rank 1 is 3,866.86). The figures above are as-is.
Regional reorganisation of 28 April 2025: the dim_store.region column comment ('North, South, East or West') is out of date; there are now five regions plus Online.

Net sales and margin were reconciled to rpt_daily_store_sales for all ten South stores over the quarter; the difference is 0.00 in every store. There were no duplicate sales or return line IDs in the period, no null or zero costs, and every sales line's standard_cost equals quantity times the product version's standard unit cost.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were excluded on both the sales and return sides; they do not enter the South figures anyway.

Figures are margin after returns. Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so a return booked in May 2025 against a Q4 sale reduces Q2 FY25/26, not these Q4 figures; this is the company convention (returns on their own date).

Absolute values are small (the best product earns 2,927 EUR of margin in the quarter) because the ranking is at individual-article level across 2,638 active articles in the South; the top 10 are a thin slice of the region's total margin.

answer.sql: SELECT f.vat_rate, ROUND(SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount), 2) AS vat_charged FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 18 AND 21 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category != 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate
definitions_applied: Net VAT on store sales: difference between gross_amount and net_amount on fact_sales_line
Store sales only: store_id < 900, channel_code = ST
Exclusions: store 999 (excluded by store_id < 900), category ZZ Test
VAT rates: 10%, 14%, 24% (before 1 Sept 2024), 25.5% (from 1 Sept 2024)
assumptions: Physical stores only (store_id < 900); web sales (store 900) excluded per request for 'stores'

Current product version used for exclusion of ZZ Test category

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, s.format FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, l.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY l.format ORDER BY CASE l.format WHEN 'Large' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Small' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END
definitions_applied: Return rate: refund_net divided by sold net_amount (excluding VAT), on the sale-week cohort
Returns matched to the original sales line through sales_line_id, whenever and wherever they were booked
Sold lines selected by the fiscal period of sale_date
Store 999 (training store) excluded
Category ZZ Test (test articles) excluded
Staff purchases included
Web shop (store 900, format Web) shown as its own format
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 P2 = fiscal weeks 5 to 8, 26 May to 22 June 2025
Store format taken from the store version on the sale date, which is the same as the current version for every store
assumptions: 'Period 2 last year' read as FY2025/26 P2, because the request came in on 6 Oct 2026, during FY2026/27. Earlier accepted requests read 'last year' as the previous fiscal year in the same way.
'What came back' read as the value returned (refund_net) divided by the value sold (net_amount), both excluding VAT, not units or number of lines.
'Share of what was sold' read as the standard company return rate, with returns counted against the period in which the goods were sold, not the period in which the refund was booked.

Web orders are included as a fourth format, 'Web', because they were sold in the period and the store formats alone would leave them out. Web lines are dated by order date, as in earlier accepted web-versus-store return-rate requests.
No total row, because the request asked for a split by format.
caveats: The Web rate (12.23%) is much higher than the store formats (4.28 to 4.53%). It is a different channel, and Leena may want to read the three store formats separately.
The cohort is complete. P2 ended 22 June 2025, returns arrive within about 30 days, and the warehouse is loaded to 4 October 2026, so no late returns are missing.

The store-side sold value reconciles exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns for the period (1,101,367.56 EUR). The control table has no return-cohort view, so the returned amounts could not be checked against it.
Corrections made: 126 sales lines in store 999 and 1 web test-article line (category ZZ Test) were excluded. Together they total about 2,226 EUR of sales and have no returns.
No duplicate sales or return lines were found, no return exceeds its sold line, and there are no cancelled web orders in the period.
Rates are on sold value excluding VAT. A rate on units or on value including VAT would differ slightly.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key (dim_member keeps one row per version)
Current tier taken from the current member version (is_current = true, valid_to 9999-12-31)
Loyalty tier values Basic, Silver and Gold as in dim_member
dim_member used directly; staging (stg_member_updates) and backup tables not used
assumptions: 'At the moment' read as the current state of the warehouse, which is loaded through Sunday 4 October 2026 (the latest member versions are all open-ended and valid on that date)

'Gold-tier loyalty members we have' read as everyone currently enrolled in the programme whose current tier is Gold, whether or not they have bought recently. The metric dictionary defines only 'active members' (a purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks), and the request does not say 'active'
caveats: dim_member has 8,203 Gold version rows, but only 5,791 distinct members are Gold today. The rest are past Gold versions: 2,412 non-current rows, covering 2,233 members who moved tier or changed home store or consent. Counting rows or counting Gold at any point in time would overstate the answer. Each member has exactly one current version, so the 5,791 is not inflated by version fan-out.

If Store operations meant active Gold members on the company definition (at least one purchase in the 52 fiscal weeks to Sunday 4 October 2026, tier on that date), the figure is 4,827 instead of 5,791. I did not use it as the headline because the request did not say 'active'. Please confirm which one is wanted.
The count includes members who joined as recently as 4 October 2026 and online sign-ups (home store 900). No members were excluded.

answer.sql:
WITH web_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    SUM(f.gross_amount) AS gross_sales_incl_vat
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN fact_web_order w ON f.receipt_id = w.web_order_id
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
