Web shop (store 900) included, since the request is not limited to physical stores
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request was received on 8 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests received from May 2026 onward read 'last year' as FY2025/26. So 'period 6 last year' is FY2025/26 P6.
Categories are as-is (current hierarchy), the company default, because the request did not ask for as-was.
Total across all channels, web included, with no split by store, region or channel, because none was asked for.
Gross margin percentage rounded to one decimal place, net sales to cents.
caveats: Outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, the day after P6 ended. On the as-is hierarchy used here, outdoor lighting is in Electrical for all of P6. Electrical net sales of 219,493.00 therefore include 33,781.91 of outdoor lighting that was in Garden when it was sold. On the as-was hierarchy, Electrical is 185,711.09 (margin 41.7%) and Garden is 148,587.85 (margin 39.5%). Garden is the same on both views (114,805.94) only because the as-is view moves the lighting out; the as-was Garden figure above includes the lighting. Margin on the moved outdoor lighting alone is 37.3%.

Duplicate sales lines exist in the warehouse. 418 lines for the sale dates 15 to 21 September 2025 were loaded a second time on 23 Sep 2025 under new sales_line_id values. These are exact copies of the earlier lines, and fall in P5, not P6. They do not affect the figures above, but anyone summing P5 net sales from fact_sales_line without removing them would overstate it.

The P6 net sales figures are checked in total: all-category net sales for FY2025/26 P6 on the same logic is 1,293,219.69, which matches rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent. No category-level control table exists, so the Garden and Electrical split itself is not checked against a control.
Net sales are after returns booked in P6, so returns in P6 for goods sold in earlier periods reduce this period, and returns for P6 sales that arrive after 26 Oct 2025 do not appear in it.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines, so orders that are still processing are included
Cancelled orders are not counted as web orders
Click-and-collect orders count as web orders
Store 999 and category ZZ Test left out of reporting (no test orders fell on this day)
Day boundary set by the request: UTC calendar day on order_ts_utc, not the Helsinki day
assumptions: Black Friday 2025 is 28 November 2025, as the request states
The UTC day is 2025-11-28 00:00:00 to 23:59:59 UTC, applied to order_ts_utc, the time the order was placed
The request asks for orders placed, so I counted by order timestamp, not dispatch time
caveats: The request asks for UTC, which differs from the company default of Helsinki time. I followed the request. On the Helsinki order date the same count would be 402, so the two figures should not be mixed.
377 orders were placed on that UTC day. I excluded 20 cancelled orders, which leaves 357 (97 collected plus 260 delivered). None were still processing.

I checked for duplicate order ids and duplicate order content on the day and found none. Every non-cancelled order has sales lines that match its line_count. No ZZ Test or store 999 lines are on orders placed on 27 to 29 November, so no test-order correction was needed.
No correction to the data was needed.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key WHERE f.sale_date >= '2025-11-03' GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net_amount field from fact_sales_line, excluding VAT and line discounts
Web platform: all transactions from 2025-11-03 onwards
assumptions: Post-migration transactions (2025-11-03 onwards) with NULL channel_code represent web platform sales, as the platform migration coincides exactly with the shift from explicit channel codes to NULLs
caveats: DATA QUALITY ISSUE: The warehouse channel_code field becomes NULL for all transactions starting exactly 2025-11-03. Before this date, channel_code values were recorded as 'ST' (store) or 'WB' (web). After this date, no channel codes are captured. This coincides with the stated platform migration date. Without explicit channel identification post-migration, the answer assumes all post-migration transactions represent web-platform sales, but this assumption should be verified with the E-commerce team or by examining the ETL load logic.

answer.sql: WITH q1 AS (SELECT (SELECT min(period_start_date) FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_quarter=1) AS start_date, (SELECT max(period_end_date) FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_quarter=1) AS end_date), sold AS (SELECT p.subcategory, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold, sum(coalesce(r.quantity_returned,0)) AS units_returned FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON r.sales_line_id = f.sales_line_id CROSS JOIN q1 WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN q1.start_date AND q1.end_date AND p.category = 'Garden' GROUP BY p.subcategory) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_quarter, subcategory, round(100.0 * units_returned / units_sold, 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold ORDER BY subcategory
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar from ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2025/26 Q1 = periods 1-3, 2025-04-28 to 2025-07-27
Product category and subcategory as at the sale date (product_key on the sales line, slowly changing dimension version)
Returns attributed to the original sale via fact_return_line.sales_line_id, so returns count against the quarter the goods were sold in, whenever the return was booked
Return rate = units returned / units sold, in percent
Sales lines from all channels (store and web) and staff purchases are included, consistent with how rpt_daily_store_sales counts sales
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (today is in FY2026/27), so Q1 is 2025-04-28 to 2025-07-27 rather than calendar Jan-Mar 2025

'Return rate' read as units returned divided by units sold; the value-based rate (refund net / net sales) is close for every subcategory (e.g. Garden Furniture 12.85%, Outdoor Lighting 7.16%) and does not change the ranking
'Goods sold in Q1' read as a sales cohort: every return of a Q1 sale is counted regardless of return date
Rows are limited to the Garden category as it was at the time of sale, which is eight subcategories
Staff purchases and web sales are kept in; nothing in the request says to exclude them
caveats: Outdoor Lighting was moved from Garden to Electrical on 2025-10-27 (a product dimension reclassification, after Q1). I kept it as Garden because that is where it sat when the goods were sold. If you want Garden as it is organised today, drop that row; the other seven rows are unaffected either way. A join to current product versions (is_current) would wrongly lose about 65 of the 70 lighting SKUs.
The Q1 sales cohort is fully matured. The longest gap between a sale and its return in the cohort is 34 days, and the data runs to October 2026, so no late returns are missing.
Returns are joined by sales_line_id, one return row per sales line, so there is no fan-out. No return exceeds the quantity or value sold, and none predates its sale.

226 pairs of lines in Q1 show identical receipt, product, quantity, amount and timestamp under different line numbers. I treated them as genuine repeat scans and did not remove them; they are about 0.3% of lines.
Several subcategories have small bases (Barbecue & Grills 2,057 units, Outdoor Lighting 1,757, Garden Furniture 2,915), so their rates move noticeably with a few returns.

answer.sql: WITH dedup AS (SELECT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, MAX(closing_value) AS closing_value, COUNT(*) AS copies FROM fact_stock_week WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3), weekly AS (SELECT cp.category, d.week_ending_date, SUM(d.closing_value) AS weekly_value FROM dedup d JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = d.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = d.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE cs.region = 'West' AND s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 11 AS fiscal_period, category, ROUND(AVG(weekly_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot at standard cost (closing_value), added across stores and articles within each week and then averaged across the weeks of the period, never summed across weeks
Fiscal period 11 is fiscal weeks 44 to 47, Monday 23 Feb 2026 to Sunday 22 Mar 2026, with week-ending Sundays 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is reporting: region and category taken from the current version of the store and the article
Only ranged articles appear in the stock snapshot, and web stock is not held there
Values are at standard cost excluding VAT
assumptions: 'Last year' on a request received 5 Oct 2026 (in FY2026/27) means the fiscal year FY2025/26, as past requests read it in FY2026/27. So period 11 last year is FY2025/26 P11, not FY2024/25 P11.
'Average stock value' means the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost, summed over the West stores and articles in each category.

'West' means the current West region (as-is), the company default. Category is also as-is. For this period the as-was answer would be the same, because the April 2025 region change and the October 2025 outdoor lighting move to Electrical both came before March 2026.
Value is closing_value at standard cost in EUR, not retail value.
caveats: Correction: the week ending 8 March 2026 was loaded twice, on 9 and 10 March. 7,439 store-article rows in 10 stores appeared twice with identical values. I kept one row per store, article and week. Without this, that week would be overstated by about EUR 0.81 million company-wide, and the period average with it.
Articles delisted on 1 March 2026 are in the 1 March snapshot but not in later weeks, so the weekly totals fall slightly. This is genuine ranging, not a data error, and it is included as recorded.
The figures are an average of four weekly closings. They are not the closing stock at the end of the period, which would be the 22 March snapshot.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT n.business_date, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND n.business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Web net sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date (sale_date)
Net sales = net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce web net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect counted as web, dated on the ready-for-collection date (Helsinki)
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
UTC timestamps converted to Helsinki time before taking the date
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales (web, store 900)
assumptions: 'Daily web sales (net)' read as the company definition of web net sales: excluding VAT, after returns, on dispatch date
Range 15 to 23 December 2025 read as calendar dates, both ends inclusive, Helsinki business days
Click-and-collect included in web, as company definition says
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT
caveats: Dates are dispatch dates in Helsinki time, so a day's figure is not the value of orders placed that day. Dispatched orders include some placed in the days before.

Web net sales are net of returns on the return date. Returns of web orders processed in physical stores (64 return lines, about 1,964 EUR net over 15 to 23 Dec) are booked to those stores under the company definition and are not deducted here. Returns booked to the web shop total about 6,843 EUR net over the same days.
21 December (Sunday) is low at 611.75 EUR because few orders were dispatched that day (18 orders). The same happened on Sunday 14 December. This is the normal pattern and not a data gap.
The total over the nine days, 93,720.40 EUR, matches rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly, with no gap on any day.
No duplicate sales lines, duplicate return lines, orphan web lines or test-article lines were found for these orders, so no data corrections were needed.

The UTC and Helsinki day boundaries differ for some rows: 19 dispatch timestamps fall in the range only by UTC date. Helsinki dates were used throughout. I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, which leaves out web sales after the November 2025 migration.

answer.sql: WITH stock_dedup AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_units, closing_value, receipts_units, adjustment_units FROM fact_stock_week WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22'), weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM stock_dedup fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE cs.region = 'West' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_eur FROM weekly GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot, added across stores and products within each week, never across weeks
Period average = average of the weekly closings (4 weeks, week-ending 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026)
Stock value = closing_value at standard cost, EUR
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P11 = 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026, fiscal weeks 44 to 47
As-is reporting: current region and current product category via is_current versions
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); store 999 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Stock table covers ranged articles in physical stores only; there is no web stock
assumptions: 'Last year' in a request received on 5 October 2026 (FY2026/27) is read as FY2025/26, as in past accepted requests; 'period 11' is FY2025/26 P11
'Average stock value' is read as the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost, summed over all West stores in each week
West region as-is: the 10 West stores (115 to 123 and 136 Tampere Lamminpää) each have a single, unchanged version, so as-is and as-was give the same region
Category as-is. The outdoor lighting move to Electrical took effect on 27 October 2025, before this period, so as-is and as-was categories agree here
Values are in EUR at standard cost (not retail value) and exclude VAT
caveats: Correction: the stock snapshot for week ending 8 March 2026 was loaded twice for the West stores (7,439 store/article keys, 14,878 rows, loads on 9 and 10 March). The duplicate rows are identical in every value. I removed them with SELECT DISTINCT over the key and value columns without etl_loaded_at. Without this the West average would be inflated for that week and the period average overstated by about 25% of that week's value.
The week ending 1 March 2026 has 38 extra West store/article rows with zero closing units. They have no value and do not change the figures.

No control total exists for stock, since rpt_daily_store_sales covers sales only, so the figures were checked against the source rows only (no orphan keys, no nulls, no negative units, and closing_value equals units times standard cost on every West row).

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE DATE(order_ts_utc) = '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web order: one row per completed order from fact_web_order
Cyber Monday 2025: calendar date 1 December 2025
Orders placed: defined by order_ts_utc timestamp (time order was submitted)
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is 1 December 2025
All orders with any UTC time on 2025-12-01 are counted, regardless of order status
order_ts_utc timestamp represents when the order was placed, as per the schema documentation
caveats: The count includes all orders regardless of final status (delivered, collected, processing, or cancelled). If the request intended to count only successfully completed orders, clarify the status filter.
Times are stored in UTC; if there are regional time zone considerations for determining the Cyber Monday window, the count may differ
No data quality issues detected

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(net_sales) as net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales WHERE business_date >= '2026-09-01' AND business_date < '2026-10-01'
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales before returns minus returns (both excluding VAT)
Whole company = all 39 physical and pseudo-stores including the web shop (store 900)
Last month = calendar month of September 2026
assumptions: Last month interpreted as the calendar month immediately before the request date (2026-10-09), i.e., September 2026
Whole company includes both store channel (38 physical locations) and web channel
caveats: Data available through 2026-10-04 only; request arrived 2026-10-09. September data is complete (30 days, all trading days represented).
Six days in September showed net negative sales (returns exceeded forward sales), which is normal business variance.
Slight reconciliation difference (1,338 EUR) between fact_sales_line and rpt_daily_store_sales may be due to timing or reporting adjustments; rpt_daily_store_sales is the authoritative source.

answer.sql: WITH first_version AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from, member_key) AS version_no FROM dim_member) SELECT f.home_store_id AS store_id, cs.store_name, COUNT(DISTINCT f.member_id) AS new_members FROM first_version f JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = f.home_store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE f.version_no = 1 AND f.join_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-04-28' AND DATE '2026-05-03' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: New member: counted on the join date, at the home store in the member's first dim_member version (the store where they enrolled)
Members counted by distinct member_id, not by member_key or version rows
Online sign-ups sit under store 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop), shown as its own row
Last year read as the fiscal year FY2025/26, 28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026 (week 53 included, since there is no comparison)
Store names taken from the current dim_store version
Deprecated objects (stg_member_updates, dim_store_old, bak_ and tmp_ tables) not used
assumptions: 'Last year' means FY2025/26, because the request was received on 7 October 2026, in FY2026/27. Past requests in May 2026 and later read it the same way (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).
'Each store' means every store with at least one sign-up in the year, including Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026, enrolled 113 members) and the stores opened in 2024 (Tampere Lamminpää, Lohja).
The count is of members who joined (first appeared in the loyalty scheme) in the year, whatever their current tier, home store or consent status.
caveats: Each member is counted once, at the enrolment store. Members who later changed home store are not moved: a later version's home_store_id would have given a different split.
Calendar-year 2025 would give a different figure; the figures cover FY2025/26 (28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026), which is 53 weeks long.
Total across all rows is 14,854 new members (stores 11,922, web shop 2,932). That total was not asked for and is not in the table.

Checks run on dim_member found no problems: no duplicate versions, every member has exactly one current version, and the first version's valid_from equals the join date for every member counted. No corrections to the data were needed.
Store 999 (training store) has no sign-ups in the year and does not appear.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-03' AND DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (from dispatch_ts_utc), not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or channel_id
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders have dispatch dates and sales lines)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Product identified by stable sku, named from the current product version (as-is)
UTC timestamps converted to Helsinki dates
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: Top 10 means ranked by web net sales in EUR excluding VAT, after returns; not by units or by sales before returns.
Since the platform migration on 3 November 2025 means from 3 November 2025 inclusive, by Helsinki dispatch date.
The end of the range is 4 October 2026, the last date loaded in the warehouse (the request was received 8 October 2026), so the figures cover 3 Nov 2025 to 4 Oct 2026.
Products are grouped by sku (as-is, current product version), so versions of the same article are combined.
Returns are those booked to the web shop (store 900), the same convention as the accepted web sales requests.
Orders placed before 3 November 2025 but dispatched on or after it count in full, because web sales follow the dispatch date.
caveats: Do not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales for this. They are built on channel_code, which stops being filled from the 3 November 2025 migration, so they silently leave out web sales in this period. I identified web by store 900 instead.

Web lines are dated by dispatch date in Helsinki time, not by sale_date, which on web lines is the order date. This moves 522 lines (about 13,452 EUR) that were ordered before 3 November but dispatched after it into the window.
Test-article lines (category ZZ Test) in web orders were excluded (9 lines, 25.50 EUR in the window).

Web purchases returned in physical stores are booked to those stores, not to the web shop. They are not netted off these web figures. They come to about 2,000 return lines and roughly 70,000 EUR net across all products in the window, so product net sales could be somewhat lower if they were counted. I followed the accepted store-900 convention.

The sales fact table holds 418 duplicated store lines for 15 to 21 September 2025, loaded twice. They are outside this window and not web, so they do not affect this result, but they would inflate any store-sales query covering those dates.

Control check: web sales before returns (2,359,008.09 EUR) and returns booked to the web shop (208,918.02 EUR) match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 from 3 Nov 2025 to 4 Oct 2026 exactly (net 2,150,090.07 EUR).
Returns lag sales by up to 30 days, so recent sales may still be returned and these figures can fall slightly.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week BETWEEN 14 AND 17) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-08-03' - 364)), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27','FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_period = 4 AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 14 AND 17 GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty, lfl_sales ly WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: P4 = fiscal weeks 14 to 17 (3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026), compared with the same fiscal weeks 14 to 17 of FY2025/26 (28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025), week by week, not by calendar date
LFL base: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop excluded
LFL opening rule: open_date <= first day of the period minus 364 days (3 Aug 2026 - 364 = 4 Aug 2025); Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) both qualify
LFL store-week: kept only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open and not closed by close_date, no overlap with ref_store_closure)
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns; returns deducted on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Open and close dates taken from the current dim_store version
Result given as one total (this year, last year, growth), with no breakdown, since none was requested
Control total: store-level net sales for P4 in both years checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'This year' is the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, so 'period 4' is FY2026/27 P4 (fiscal weeks 14 to 17). It is complete, since the warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026 and the last complete period is P5.
The comparator is the same fiscal weeks of FY2025/26 (P4, weeks 14 to 17), which is the LFL definition.
Regions and hierarchy do not affect the figure because no breakdown was asked for.

Growth is reported as one percentage figure. Underlying net sales in the LFL store-weeks are about EUR 1,010,479 this year and EUR 1,010,743 last year, a difference of about EUR 265. Unrounded growth is about -0.026%.
caveats: Growth is essentially flat at -0.03%, so rounding matters. Unrounded it is about -0.026%.

The LFL base is 38 stores x 4 weeks = 152 store-weeks. Savonlinna (129) is out because it closed on 25 Jan 2026 and has no FY2026/27 trading. Kuopio (125) is fully in: its refit ran 15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026, before P4 started on 3 Aug. Pori's (119) refit was Sep to Oct 2025, outside P4 of last year. No refit weeks fell inside P4 in either year.

I found no data problems needing correction. Sales and return lines have no duplicate keys in the P4 windows of either year. Per-store net sales in P4 of both years match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (differences of 0.00). Every LFL store-week has sales on all 7 days. No closed public holidays fall in these weeks.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales (they drop web sales from 3 Nov 2025), the channel_code column, or any stg_, bak_, tmp_ or _old tables.
Web is excluded from LFL by definition. Web sales would otherwise have been dated on their Helsinki dispatch date, as in the standard net-sales pattern.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 4 AS period_no, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, params.period_no AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM params JOIN lfl_sales ty ON ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) net sales growth, physical stores only
LFL base: store open at least 52 weeks (364 days) before the first day of the period
LFL store-weeks: only fiscal weeks in which the store traded in both years
Refit closures taken out per store in both years (ref_store_closure)
Closed store (Savonlinna 129) dropped from the base
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, returns dated on their return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal weeks aligned by week number (weeks 14 to 17), not by calendar date
Web shop (store 900) excluded
Reported as-is (current store dimension version)
Checked against the rpt_daily_store_sales control total
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales
assumptions: Read 'period 4 this year' as FY2026/27 P4 (3 to 30 August 2026, fiscal weeks 14 to 17). It is fully loaded; the warehouse runs through 4 October 2026.
Read 'last year' as FY2025/26 P4 (28 July to 24 August 2025, weeks 14 to 17).
Read 'the stores' as the physical stores in the LFL base, in line with the company LFL definition. The web shop is not part of LFL.
Gave one company-wide LFL figure, because no breakdown by region or store was asked for.
Net sales are in EUR excluding VAT. Growth is in percent.
caveats: Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and is out of the LFL base. It had EUR 9,549.14 of net sales in P4 last year. The all-store control total for last year is EUR 1,020,292.46, which is that amount above the LFL figure. This year's LFL net sales equal the control total exactly (EUR 1,010,478.52), because no other store dropped out.

No other store was removed. The Pori (Sept to Oct 2025), Kuopio (June to July 2026) and Tammisto (July to Aug 2024) refits do not overlap weeks 14 to 17 in either year. Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) had been open more than 52 weeks before 3 August 2026, so both are in the base (38 stores, 152 store-weeks).

Lohja (137) is still ramping up after its November 2024 opening: its net sales rose about 25% (EUR 10,333 to EUR 12,956), which helps the total. Mikkeli (127) fell about 26% (EUR 27,002 to EUR 19,921), in every week of P4 and the weeks before it, with no gaps or zero-sales days. I treated that as real trading, not a data fault, and left it in.
Growth is essentially flat at -0.03% (EUR 265 lower on about EUR 1.01m). That is a rounding-level difference, not a real decline, and the 38 stores' individual results vary much more than that.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles are excluded as house rules require. Sales lines are unique by sales_line_id and receipt line in the period, so there was no duplicate-row problem.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(f.sale_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.sale_date >= DATE '2024-08-01' AND f.sale_date < DATE '2024-10-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Store sales means the store channel only (channel_code = 'ST'); web orders (channel WB, pseudo-store 900) are excluded
Pseudo-locations are excluded: store_id 900 (web shop) and 999 (Training store); only real stores (store_id below 900) count
Sales including VAT is the sum of gross_amount on fact_sales_line
Before returns means fact_return_line is not netted off
Calendar months by sale_date (1-31 August 2024, 1-30 September 2024)
assumptions: August and September 2024 are calendar months, not fiscal periods

Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag = true) are kept in. They are real till sales, and the Data & Analytics daily store sales report (rpt_daily_store_sales) includes them. Excluding them would give 1,347,937.57 for August and 1,189,220.09 for September less the 4,282.23 and 3,351.71 Training store amounts, so treat that as an alternative reading only if Finance defines store sales without staff purchases
Sales are assigned to a month by sale_date. For these two months sale_date matches the Helsinki-time date of sale_ts_utc on every line
All stores that traded in the period are included, whether or not they are comparable (like-for-like) stores
caveats: Correction: the store channel in fact_sales_line contains sales booked to the Training store (store_id 999), which is not a trading store. These are removed: 4,282.23 in August (158 lines) and 3,351.71 in September (125 lines). Without this correction the store channel would show 1,369,364.12 for August and 1,212,263.87 for September
Web shop sales (store_id 900, channel WB) are not store sales and are excluded: 174,410.47 in August and 160,395.63 in September including VAT
Vantaa Tammisto (store 104) was closed for a refit from 2024-07-08 to 2024-08-11 and has no sales until 12 August, so its August figure covers about three weeks only
Tampere Lamminpää (store 136) opened on 2 September 2024, so it contributes to September only (19,657.54), and is not in August

Checks that found no problem: no duplicate sales_line_id or (receipt_id, line_no) pairs, gross_amount equals net_amount times (1 + vat_rate) on every line, there are no zero or negative lines, every day in both months has sales from every expected store, and there are no sales on non-trading days. The figures reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales, which matches net sales before returns from the fact table for real stores (1,101,807.91 for August and 964,016.09 for September, excluding VAT)
The figures are in EUR including VAT at the rates on the sales lines, and are not net of returns

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27','FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Total company scope: all physical stores plus the web shop (store 900), shown as one total
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Fiscal calendar: period 2 is weeks 5 to 8, Monday to Sunday
Prior-year comparison lined up by fiscal week number, not by calendar date
Growth % = this year / last year - 1, in percent
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales: all four weeks in both years match to the cent
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' means FY2026/27 P2 (weeks 5 to 8, 1 to 28 June 2026). It is fully loaded; the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026.
'Same weeks last year' means FY2025/26 weeks 5 to 8 (26 May to 22 June 2025), matched by fiscal week number as in earlier accepted requests.
Week 53 of FY2025/26 is outside this period, so the comparison needs no week 53 treatment.
'Total company' includes web, as in the earlier total-company weekly request.
The table gives one row per week and no period total row, because none was asked for.
caveats: The midsummer holidays fall in different fiscal weeks in the two years. In FY2025/26 the stores were shut on Midsummer Eve and Day (20 and 21 June 2025), in week 8. In FY2026/27 they were shut on 19 and 20 June 2026, in week 7. Weeks 7 and 8 are therefore not like for like. Week 7 shows -32.2% and week 8 shows +76.4%, and both come from the holiday shift, not from underlying trading. Weeks 5 and 6 are unaffected.

The holiday effect largely cancels over the whole period. Period 2 totals 1,294,647.64 this year against 1,195,882.70 last year, which is +8.3%. I did not add this as a row, because no total was asked for.

I found 418 receipt lines that were loaded twice in the sales fact table (same receipt and line number, loaded again on 23 September 2025). They are all for 15 to 21 September 2025, so none affects period 2 in either year and no correction was needed. Anyone reusing the sales table for September 2025 should de-duplicate on receipt_id and line_no.
Store 999 and ZZ Test lines were removed (248 sales lines in the eight weeks used). I did not measure how much this changes the weekly totals.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, because they miss web sales from November 2025. They would not affect these dates, but they are not safe to use.
I found no other problems in the period: no orphan store, product or sales-line keys, no duplicate return lines, and no processing or cancelled web orders with sales lines.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS sales, 0 AS ret FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, 0, r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test') SELECT n.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, ROUND(SUM(sales)-SUM(ret),2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku=n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date >= DATE '2025-11-03' AND n.business_date <= DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Web sales are recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or channel_id, which do not work across the 3 November 2025 migration
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, less web-shop returns (refund_net) on their own return date
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; store 999 excluded
Click-and-collect counted as web
Products grouped by stable sku, named from the current dim_product version
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or any deprecated, stg_, bak_ or tmp_ table
assumptions: 'Web sales' means net sales after returns in EUR excluding VAT, the company default; ranking is by that figure
'Since the platform migration on 3 November 2025' means dispatch dates from Monday 3 November 2025 to the end of the warehouse load, Sunday 4 October 2026 (inclusive)
'Products' means articles (sku), not product versions
Orders placed before 3 November but dispatched on or after it are included, as web sales follow the dispatch date (522 such lines)
Only the top 10 are listed; no ties at the cut-off (10th is 6889.60, 11th is 6679.65)
caveats: The ranking shifts under other readings. Before returns, Bedroom Peltola 793 is first (15533.23) and Christmas Decorations Kuusela 620 and Barbecue & Grills Poutaranta Home 851 sit just outside the top 10. If you want net sales to include refunds booked in physical stores on web-sold items, there are 3,411 such return lines over the whole history, and Home Office Peltola 918 drops out of the top 10 (Christmas Decorations Kuusela 620 enters). I used the company definition, where a return reduces net sales at the store where it was processed, so only web-shop returns are deducted here.
Returns deducted are those processed at the web shop and dated within the window, so a few may relate to sales made before 3 November 2025.
19 web lines on test articles (ZZ Test) were excluded.
The window ends on 4 October 2026, when the warehouse load ends; the request came on 8 October, so 5 to 8 October are not in the data.
I did not use channel_code or rpt.v_daily_sales: they leave out web sales from 3 November 2025.
Seasonal items (Christmas decorations, sauna and winter) and garden furniture dominate the list, so the result depends on the window covering one Christmas and one spring and summer season.
I did not run a rpt_daily_store_sales control total because this is a product-level analysis and that table has no product dimension.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Fiscal calendar: period 3 of FY2026/27 = 29 June to 2 August 2026 (weeks 9 to 13, 5 weeks, fully loaded)
Store scope: physical store Lahti (store_id 108); store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out (no effect on this figure)
Interior Paint = dim_product.subcategory, taken as-is on the current product version
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Versioned dimensions joined by natural key with is_current, so no row multiplication
Control check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 108 over the same dates
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 3' as fiscal period 3 (P3) of that year (request received 5 October 2026)
'Lahti store' read as store_id 108, Lahti, city Lahti (the other name match, Tampere Lielahti, is a different store)
'Interior Paint' read as the subcategory of that name within Paint & Decorating, which has 123 SKUs
'Units sold' read as gross units on sales lines, before returns; the metric dictionary has no net-of-returns unit measure and the weeks-of-cover definition uses sales-line quantity
Staff purchases kept in the unit count (4 of the 194 units)
caveats: No data problems found and no corrections made: 142 sales lines, with no duplicate line ids or receipt-line pairs, on 35 consecutive trading days from 29 June to 2 August 2026
All Lahti sales in the period (all products) reconcile exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales: 3,927 units, EUR 67,202.85 net before returns and 1,048 receipts
6 Interior Paint units sold in Lahti in this period were later returned (booked to the return date); they are not deducted from the 194, so net of returns the figure would be 188
The two Interior Paint SKUs that have more than one product version (100963 and 101047) kept the same subcategory in every version, so as-is and as-was give the same answer

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT sale_date AS business_date, sum(net_amount) AS net_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line WHERE channel_id IN (2,3) AND sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1), rets AS (SELECT r.return_date AS business_date, sum(r.refund_net) AS returns_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1) SELECT s.business_date AS sale_date, s.net_before_returns - coalesce(r.returns_net, 0) AS web_net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN rets r USING (business_date) ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales net of VAT (net_amount, after line discounts) minus refunds net of VAT booked on the day, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Web = channel_id 2 (web home delivery) and 3 (click and collect), i.e. the web shop pseudo-store 900; channel_code is NULL on current rows so it was not used
Sale date = sale_date, the Finnish local date (sale_ts_utc runs from 22:00 or 23:00 UTC the evening before)
Returns dated by return_date and taken from the web shop (store_id 900), where the warehouse books web returns
Cancelled web orders carry no sales lines, so they are not in the figures
Fact tables used as the source, not the rpt views or tables
assumptions: Read 'net' as the company's net sales: excluding VAT and after returns. Before returns, the figures are 13007.30, 16359.14, 10686.17, 11354.33, 11627.57, 7425.77, 7762.68, 12878.11 and 13459.24 for 15 to 23 December.
Web sales means both home delivery and click and collect, since both are in the web channel group.
Days are Finnish local dates, taken as sale_date, and both ends of the range are included (15 to 23 December 2025, nine days).
Refunds are counted on the day the refund was booked, not the day of the original sale.
caveats: rpt.v_daily_sales filters web lines on channel_code = 'WB'. That code is NULL on all lines in this period (only channel_id is filled), so the view returns no web sales. I queried fact_sales_line by channel_id instead.

rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 does not reconcile with the fact tables on the sales side. For example, 15 December shows 11714.52 before returns, against 13007.30 in fact_sales_line. Its returns_net does match the fact table, and the sales gap does not match a UTC-date cut either. I did not use that table and did not find the cause.

41 refunds on web-order lines (about 1,960 EUR net over the nine days) were booked in physical stores (for example 101, 102, 115, 131), not at the web shop. I treated them as store returns, in line with the warehouse booking convention. If they are charged back to web, the daily figures fall by that amount: 12386.51, 15711.65, 9504.43, 10321.11, 10489.65, 5967.71, 6786.48, 11904.22 and 12681.03.
The warehouse stores timestamps in UTC. Grouping by the UTC date of sale_ts_utc instead of sale_date would move web orders across midnight and give different daily totals.
No duplicate lines (sales_line_id and receipt/line are unique) and no staff purchases among the web lines. Every non-cancelled web order in the period has lines in the sales fact.

answer.sql: SELECT cs.format AS store_format, COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id) AS receipts, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts, dated by sale_date
ATV is a store measure: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop (store 900) left out
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) excluded from ATV
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Returns not deducted, because ATV uses net sales before returns
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2026/27 P4 = Monday 3 August 2026 to Sunday 30 August 2026 (4 weeks)
Format taken from the current dim_store version (format is the same in every store version)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales_before_returns and receipts)
assumptions: 'Period 4 of FY26/27' is read as FY2026/27 P4, which is complete (the last complete period is P5).
'Average basket value' is read as ATV (average transaction value), as the request states, using the company definition.
'Store format' is read as dim_store.format with the values present in the warehouse: Large, Medium and Small. The schema comment (Hyper, Standard, Express) is out of date.
No total company row is given because the request asks only for a breakdown by format.
caveats: The dim_store.format column comment is out of date. The actual values are Large, Medium, Small, plus Web (store 900) and Training (store 999), which are both excluded from ATV.

Exclusions: staff-purchase receipts removed (99 Large, 138 Medium, 43 Small in P4). Store 999 had 32 staff-flagged receipts and 23 test-article receipts, and the web shop had one test-article receipt. Test-article receipts and store 999 were left out. Staff receipts raise the three formats' net sales before returns by about 5,544 (Large), 7,273 (Medium) and 1,979 (Small) EUR.

The control total with rpt_daily_store_sales agrees store by store for 3 to 30 August 2026, for both net sales before returns and receipt counts. The report table includes staff purchases, so the check was run on all non-test lines, before the staff exclusion.
I found no duplicate lines in fact_sales_line for the period (48,107 lines, all unique by sales_line_id and by receipt_id + line_no).
The Small format counts 12 trading stores in P4. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and Kuopio's refit (15 June to 26 July 2026) ended before P4, so no store in P4 had closure effects.
Receipts: Large 6,508, Medium 8,641, Small 2,598. Net sales before returns used for ATV (EUR excluding VAT): Large 394,865.46, Medium 520,763.45, Small 131,841.05.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or any staging, backup or tmp table.

answer.sql: WITH sl AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sl f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 22) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-05-04' - 364)), lfl_sales AS (SELECT cs.region, d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27','FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 22 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ROUND(ty.net_sales,2) AS lfl_net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales,2) AS lfl_net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales in LFL stores versus the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
Net sales: excluding VAT, after returns, with returns booked on their return date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (900) left out; store 999 and category ZZ Test left out
Regions as-is: current dim_store version, so the Capital Region holds stores 101 to 105 in both years and Kouvola (114) sits in South in both years
LFL store-week rule: a store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years, using open_date, close_date and ref_store_closure
LFL opening rule: open_date on or before the first day of the range minus 364 days (4 May 2026 minus 364 = 5 May 2025)
YTD: FY2026/27 weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026), the last completed fiscal week, against FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22
Control total: store-by-store, week-by-week net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Read 'how they are doing' as like-for-like net sales growth, the company's standard measure of trading performance, and ranked the regions on it from highest to lowest

Read 'this year so far' as FY2026/27 year to date through week 22 (ending Sunday 4 October 2026, the end of the loaded data), compared with FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22. Period 6 is only partly complete, but YTD runs through the last completed week
Read 'five store regions' as North, South, East, West and the Capital Region (Online/web excluded)
Regions taken as-is, on the current store hierarchy
Comparison year is last year (FY2025/26), the usual reading in the request history
caveats: Duplicate loads corrected: 418 sales lines (209 receipt lines loaded twice, each pair with identical store, product, date and amount but different sales_line_id and etl_loaded_at) fall in 15 to 21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 week 21). I kept one row per receipt_id and line_no. After this, the store-by-store, week-by-week net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales for weeks 1 to 22 of both years with no differences. Without this correction last year's base would be overstated for the affected stores' regions and their growth understated

Ranking depends on the measure. On raw net sales for all stores (not like-for-like), the order differs: North +3.8%, West +3.2%, Capital Region +2.7%, South +2.1%, East -11.6%. West drops to fourth on LFL only because Pori's refit weeks (8 September to 12 October 2025) are taken out of both years; the large East fall is mainly Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026, East had 8 stores last year and 7 now) and the Kuopio refit (15 June to 26 July 2026)

East is the only region with negative LFL growth (-0.19%), and that is after removing Savonlinna's trading weeks and Kuopio's refit weeks. The gap between North, Capital Region, South and West is small (about 0.1 to 1.7 points), so ranks 2 to 4 are close
Week 22 data is the last loaded week; period 6 of FY2026/27 has only its first week, so figures are YTD weeks, not complete periods

Net sales are excluding VAT and include staff purchases; returns are deducted on their return date, so recent weeks may still receive returns for sales already made (returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale)
Not used: rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, rpt_weekly_sales_by_region, channel_code, and all stg_, bak_ and tmp_ tables

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns (returns credited back at standard_cost_returned)
Net sales excluding VAT, after line discounts; staff purchases included
Returns dated on their own return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered/collected orders); not relevant to South, since web is in region Online
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
As-is hierarchy: current store region (dim_store is_current) and current product version
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25 Q4 = periods 10 to 12, weeks 40 to 52, 27 Jan to 27 Apr 2025
Products identified by stable sku
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Q4 of FY24/25 read as fiscal quarter 4 of FY2024/25 (P10 to P12, 27 January 2025 to 27 April 2025), not calendar Q4

South read as-is, meaning the current region of each store. This is the five-region structure since 28 April 2025: Kouvola (114) is in South for all history, and the five stores that moved to the Capital Region (101 to 105) are not counted as South even though they were South during this quarter
The 10 South stores counted are 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 113, 114 and 137. Lohja (137) opened in November 2024 and trades for most of the quarter
Products ranked by gross margin in EUR, not margin percentage
The product name, category and brand are those on the current product version
Web orders are not in South, because the web shop (store 900) is in region Online
caveats: The result reflects the current South (Kouvola in; Vuosaari, Pitäjänmäki, Lommila, Tammisto and Kerava out). On the regions as they stood in Q4 FY24/25 the answer would differ, because the Capital Region did not exist until 28 April 2025
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were excluded. No warehouse problems were found in the range (no duplicate sales or return keys, no zero or mismatched costs on the top SKUs)
Net sales for the South stores over the quarter (593,853.56 EUR excluding VAT) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, store by store
Margin is at standard cost, and standard costs are revalued each April; lines carry the cost in force on the sale date

In the Smart Home / Indoor Lighting group, the 10th product (sku 101888) is Indoor Lighting Havu 438. Its gross margin of 978.84 is clearly ahead of the 11th (Smart Home Tuulikki 855, 935.46), so the top 10 is not a tie

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members_joined FROM dim_member WHERE join_date = '2026-10-03'
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id to account for slowly changing dimension
Join date treated as the date member enrolled in the loyalty program
assumptions: The request refers to calendar date 3 October 2026
Counted distinct member_ids to avoid duplicates from dimension versioning
Included all members regardless of tier or home store
caveats: No data quality issues detected
All 29 members have is_current = TRUE, confirming these are active current records

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS tampere_members FROM dim_member m JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = m.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE m.is_current AND s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900
definitions_applied: Customer = loyalty member (dim_member); the warehouse has no identity for non-member shoppers
Customer location = the city of the member's home store (home_store_id)
Current member version only (is_current = true), counted as distinct member_id
Tampere stores = store_ids 115 Hervanta, 116 Lielahti, 117 Kaleva and 136 Lamminpää (the Lamminpää store opened 2024-09-02)
Pseudo-locations excluded: 900 (web shop) and 999 (training store), which carry city = Tampere in dim_store
assumptions: Read 'customers in Tampere' as loyalty members whose home store is in Tampere, as of the latest data (sales run to 2026-10-04, the latest member change is 2026-10-04)
No activity filter applied, so the figure includes members who have never bought or have not bought recently
Marketing consent not filtered, since the request did not ask for it
Tampere means the city of Tampere only; Nokia (store 118) and other neighbouring towns are not included
caveats: dim_member is slowly changing and has 89,314 rows for 60,000 members. Counting every version with a Tampere home store gives 7,515 members, because members who moved are counted more than once or under an old store. I used the current version only, which gives 7,175.

dim_store lists the web shop (store 900) and the training store (999) under city Tampere. Joining on city alone would pull in the 12,028 online sign-up members, whose location is unknown. These are excluded.
12,028 members have the web shop as home store (online sign-ups), so their city is unknown. Some of them probably live in Tampere and are not in the 7,175.
Non-member shoppers (including web guest orders) cannot be located and are not counted.

For context only, since no activity definition was given: of the 7,175 members, 5,395 have ever made a purchase and 4,438 purchased in the 12 months to 2026-10-08. Of the 7,175, 4,841 have marketing consent. Neither figure is used in the answer.
Tables named bak_*, *_old, stg_* and tmp_* were not used.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period)
SELECT params.fiscal_year, params.fiscal_period, cs.format,
       ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv
FROM fact_sales_line f
JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
JOIN dim_store cs  ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current
JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
JOIN dim_date d    ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE s.store_id < 900
  AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag
  AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
  AND d.fiscal_period = params.fiscal_period
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY 3
definitions_applied: ATV (average transaction value) = net sales before returns excluding VAT / number of distinct sales receipts
ATV is a store measure: physical stores only (store_id below 900), so web shop (900) and training store (999) are out
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) excluded from ATV
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Sales dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date), no web lines involved
Fiscal period from dim_date: FY2026/27 P4 = 3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026 (weeks 14-17)
Store format taken from the current store version (format is identical in every version of a store)
Net amount excluding VAT after line discounts (net_amount)
assumptions: 'Average basket value' read as ATV, the company's average transaction value metric
'Period 4 of FY26/27' read as fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 (3 to 30 August 2026)
Web shop and training store have their own formats (Web, Training) but are left out because ATV is a store measure that excludes web orders
Returns not deducted, as the ATV definition uses net sales before returns
Values rounded to 2 decimals in EUR

Control check: receipts and net sales before returns by format (staff receipts included) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for P4 (Large 6,607 receipts / 400,409.69; Medium 8,779 / 528,036.85; Small 2,641 / 133,820.18).
