answer.sql: WITH store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week BETWEEN 14 AND 17) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-08-03' - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 14 AND 17 GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty, lfl_sales ly WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores for the period vs the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
Fiscal calendar: P4 = weeks 14 to 17 (FY2026/27: 3 to 30 Aug 2026; FY2025/26: 28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025), compared by fiscal week, not calendar date
LFL base rule: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the period (open_date <= 2026-08-03 minus 364 days)
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open/close dates and ref_store_closure refits checked)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop excluded from LFL
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns: returns deducted on their return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no rows affected the P4 totals)
As-is store hierarchy; open and close dates from the current dim_store version
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
Single total returned (no breakdown requested)
assumptions: Read 'period 4 this year' as FY2026/27 P4 (weeks 14 to 17, 3 to 30 August 2026), compared with FY2025/26 P4 (weeks 14 to 17). P4 is complete in the warehouse (loaded through 4 Oct 2026).
Growth is reported as one total row with this-year and last-year net sales alongside, as in past LFL answers.
Net sales are in EUR excluding VAT.
Returns are taken on the store where they were processed, on the return date, with no cohort adjustment.
caveats: No data defects found that required correction. Sales and return lines in P4 for both years have unique keys, no negative or zero quantities, and no store 999 or ZZ Test rows.
Net sales per store agree with rpt_daily_store_sales for every physical store in P4 of both years (no differences above 0.50 EUR).
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026 and is out of the base. All 38 other physical stores are in LFL for all four weeks, which gives 152 store-weeks.
Tampere Lamminpää (136, opened 2 Sep 2024) and Lohja (137, opened 4 Nov 2024) both meet the 364-day rule for P4, so they are included.
No refit closure overlaps P4 in either year (Pori ran 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025, Kuopio 15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026), so no store-weeks were dropped for refits.

LFL growth is essentially flat at -0.03% (about 265 EUR lower on roughly 1.01m EUR). Returns in this year's P4 were higher than last year's (74,361 vs 67,056 EUR, net of VAT), which weighs on the net figure.
P5 was the last complete period when the request was received on 7 Oct 2026. The request named period 4, so P4 was used.

answer.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, COUNT(DISTINCT h.member_id) AS held_out_members FROM dim_campaign c JOIN campaign_holdout h ON h.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE c.campaign_name = 'Black Week 2025' GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Holdout members: distinct member_id in campaign_holdout (which holds member_id, not member_key)
Campaign identified by name in dim_campaign (Black Week 2025, campaign_id 15, 24-30 Nov 2025)
Counted distinct member_id, not rows, because dim_member keeps one row per member version
assumptions: 'Black Week 2025' means campaign_id 15 in dim_campaign (24 to 30 November 2025). 'Black Week 2024' is a separate campaign, id 5.
'Held out' means members in campaign_holdout for that campaign, who were never contacted.
caveats: The count of 2747 agrees across campaign_holdout (2747 rows, 2747 distinct members, no duplicates) and dim_campaign.holdout_size (2747).

2747 is 10.34% of the 26573-member mailing list, not exactly 10%. Every other campaign also deviates from exactly 10% (between 9.4% and 11.0%). I took the 10% in the wiki to be a target, not an exact figure.

Targeted members (23818 distinct, from fact_campaign_exposure) plus the holdout (2747) come to 26565, which is 8 fewer than the recorded mailing list size of 26573. I could not explain the gap from the warehouse. It does not affect the holdout count.

Checks passed: no member is in both the holdout and the targeted group, all 2747 held-out members exist in dim_member and had marketing consent on 24 November 2025, and none joined after the campaign start.
No filters changed the total. Store 999 and ZZ Test do not apply to this question.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 9 AS first_period, 10 AS last_period
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
web_lines AS (
    SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT d.fiscal_year,
       d.fiscal_period,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 1) AS click_collect_share_pct
FROM web_lines l
JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 2;
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect counted as web; share is click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales
Web sales recognized on dispatch date (Helsinki time), from fact_web_order
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns
Store 900 as the web pseudo-store
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after sale; booked to store where processed
fulfilment_type from fact_web_order used on both sides of the 3 November 2025 migration
assumptions: Last year interpreted as FY2025/26, the fiscal year completed when the request was received (2026-10-06)
Periods 9 and 10 are fiscal periods (FY2025/26 P9 and P10, spanning 2025-12-22 to 2026-02-22)
Click-and-collect share is expressed as a percentage of all web net sales
Web sales are from store 900, excluding test articles (category ZZ Test)
Cancelled orders excluded; only delivered and collected orders included
Return lines from web orders matched back to original order's fulfilment_type
caveats: None: periods 9 and 10 of FY2025/26 are complete in the warehouse (loaded through 2026-02-22)

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 15 AS campaign_id
),
campaign AS (
    SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, c.start_date, c.end_date + 7 AS window_end
    FROM dim_campaign c JOIN params ON params.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
),
targeted AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id
    FROM fact_campaign_exposure e
    JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key
    JOIN params ON params.campaign_id = e.campaign_id
),
holdout AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT h.member_id
    FROM campaign_holdout h
    JOIN params ON params.campaign_id = h.campaign_id
),
members AS (
    SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS member_group FROM targeted
    UNION ALL
    SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM holdout
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
member_sales AS (
    SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_member m  ON m.member_key = f.member_key
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    CROSS JOIN campaign
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) BETWEEN campaign.start_date AND campaign.window_end
    GROUP BY 1
),
by_group AS (
    SELECT mb.member_group, AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales, 0)) AS mean_net_sales
    FROM members mb
    LEFT JOIN member_sales ms ON ms.member_id = mb.member_id
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 'targeted' AS member_group, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_member
FROM by_group
UNION ALL
SELECT 'holdout' AS member_group, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_member
FROM by_group
UNION ALL
SELECT 'uplift' AS member_group, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END) - MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_member
FROM by_group
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift: mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member
Net sales before returns (exclusions: store 999 test store, ZZ Test product category)
Campaign window: campaign dates plus 7 days after end (2025-11-24 to 2025-12-07)
Targeted members: distinct member_id with at least one exposure in the campaign
Holdout members: distinct member_id in campaign_holdout table
Web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time; store sales on sale date
Members with zero purchases count as zero in the average
assumptions: Average spend includes members who made no purchases during the campaign window
Campaign window is defined as start_date to end_date + 7 days per skill definition
caveats: Member count variance: mailing list size 26,573 (holdout 2,747, targeted 23,818) totals 26,565, a difference of 8 members. This may reflect membership changes or consent revocations between campaign setup and execution.
The uplift is calculated over a 14-day window (campaign week plus 7 days), which extends into normal retail after Black Week promotional activity ended.

answer.sql: WITH tampere_stores AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_id FROM dim_store WHERE city = 'Tampere' AND store_id < 900), member_asof AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.home_store_id FROM dim_member m WHERE m.valid_from <= DATE '2026-10-04' AND m.valid_to >= DATE '2026-10-04'), active_members AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date > DATE '2026-10-04' - 364 AND f.sale_date <= DATE '2026-10-04' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.member_id) AS active_members_tampere FROM member_asof a JOIN tampere_stores t ON t.store_id = a.home_store_id JOIN active_members am ON am.member_id = a.member_id
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks ending Sunday 4 October 2026 (sale_date > as-of Sunday - 364 and <= as-of Sunday), any channel, counted by distinct member_id
Member tier and home store read from the dim_member version valid on the as-of Sunday
Physical stores only (store_id below 900) for the Tampere store list
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key
assumptions: The warehouse has no customer table, so 'customers' is read as loyalty members. Non-members who buy without a loyalty card cannot be counted.

'Customers we have' is read as active customers, using the company's active-member definition, as of the last loaded Sunday (4 October 2026), since the request was received on 8 October 2026 and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October.

'In Tampere' is read as members whose home store is one of the four Tampere stores: 115 Tampere Hervanta, 116 Tampere Lielahti, 117 Tampere Kaleva and 136 Tampere Lamminpää. Home store is the only location attribute on a member.

Split by home store, the 4,441 are 1,708 for Hervanta (115), 1,052 for Lielahti (116), 1,034 for Kaleva (117) and 647 for Lamminpää (136). No breakdown was asked for, so the table shows only the total.
caveats: Definition not set by the company: 'customer' is not defined in the wiki. If Jukka means everyone ever enrolled rather than active members, the figure is 7,175 members whose home store is in Tampere (2,788 + 1,721 + 1,692 + 974), as at 4 October 2026. The 4,441 is the active subset. The requester should confirm which one he needs.

Correction: dim_store lists the web shop (store 900) and the Training store (999) with city = Tampere. A filter on city = 'Tampere' alone would pick them up. I excluded both, using store_id below 900. The web shop's 12,028 online sign-ups (home_store_id 900), 4,698 of them active, are therefore not in the Tampere figure, even though many of them may live in or near Tampere. The warehouse holds no member address, so they cannot be placed.

Home store is the store where the member enrolled or last changed to, not where they live. A member who lives in Tampere but whose home store is elsewhere, or who enrolled online, is not counted, and a member with a Tampere home store may live elsewhere. The figure is a count of Tampere-store members, not of Tampere residents.
Tampere Lamminpää (136) opened on 2 September 2024, so its members have a shorter history than those of the other three stores.

Marketing consent was not applied. If the figure is for a mailing, only members with consent can be contacted: 4,841 of the 7,175 Tampere-store members have consent (1,892 + 1,155 + 1,138 + 656), counted across all members, not only the active ones.

answer.sql: SELECT ROUND(100 * f.vat_rate, 1) AS vat_rate_pct, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-26' AND DATE '2024-09-22' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate
definitions_applied: FY2024/25 P5 from ref_fiscal_calendar: 26 August to 22 September 2024 (4 weeks, fully loaded)
Stores only: store_id below 900, so the web shop is out; store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test are out
Staff purchases are included, because VAT was charged on them
VAT per line is gross_amount minus net_amount, grouped by each line's own vat_rate; no flat rate was applied to a net total
Lines dated by sale_date, the Helsinki business date of the store sale
Control total: net amount of the same lines agrees with net_sales_before_returns in rpt_daily_store_sales for all 38 stores, with zero difference
No deprecated tables or views used, and no channel_code
assumptions: 'Period 5 of FY24/25' is read as FY2024/25 P05 (fiscal_year FY2024/25, fiscal_period 5)
'Charged in the stores' is read as VAT on store sales lines, before returns. Refund VAT is not netted off (see caveats)
'Stores' is read as the physical stores only (store_id below 900). Web orders (store 900) are not included
The split is by the VAT rate on each line. The general rate changed during the period, so the standard-rate VAT appears as two rows, 24% and 25.5%
Rates are shown in percent units (25.5 means 25.5%)
caveats: The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, which falls inside this period. Standard-rate lines dated 26 to 31 August carry 24% and those from 1 September carry 25.5%. Both rows are shown. Together the standard-rate VAT is 234,122.43.
Total VAT charged across all rates is 235,090.72 (net sales before returns on these lines: 938,729.24).

This figure is VAT on sales only. The data does not define how returns enter a VAT figure. For information, store refunds booked on their own return dates in the same period carry VAT of 1.20 (10%), 10.48 (14%), 5,094.72 (24%) and 6,029.57 (25.5%), 11,135.97 in total. Net of refunds, VAT would be 223,954.75. Refunds were not subtracted from the table above.

Corrections applied: store 999 lines (36 lines, 1.83 to 1,928.82 net per rate and staff flag) and one ZZ Test line in a real store (net 3.00, VAT 0.77) were excluded. Web lines (store 900) were excluded because the request is for stores.

Checks found no other problems. There are no duplicate sales lines, and each line's gross amount equals its net amount times (1 + its vat_rate) to within rounding. The vat_rate on each line matches the article's vat_class and the date of the rate change.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.category AS category_as_was, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.category, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS garden_net_sales_as_was FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 AND n.category_as_was = 'Garden' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after line discounts, less returns
Returns reduce net sales on their return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (FY2024/25 P7 to P12, 28 Oct 2024 to 27 Apr 2025)
As-was category: category taken from the product version valid on the transaction date (product_key on the fact line)
Web shop (store 900) included as part of company net sales
assumptions: 'FY24/25' read as FY2024/25 (29 Apr 2024 to 27 Apr 2025), the year named in the request

'The old way, Garden as it was reported at the time (the old category set-up)' read as an as-was request, not the company default as-is. Garden therefore still includes the outdoor lighting subcategory (65 articles), which moved to Electrical only from 27 Oct 2025 (FY2025/26 P7)
Garden figures are company-wide: all physical stores plus the web shop, with no regional breakdown
One row per fiscal period, with no total row since none was requested
caveats: As-was Garden includes outdoor lighting. Garden would be lower on today's hierarchy (as-is), where outdoor lighting sits in Electrical for all history. Outdoor lighting's share of as-was Garden is about 20.8k in P7, 20.3k in P8, 17.0k in P9, 9.7k in P10, 8.7k in P11 and 10.6k in P12.
No correction to the data was needed for this range. As a check, all-category net sales on the same query match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total exactly in every period P7 to P12 (gap 0.00).
Duplicated sales lines exist in the warehouse (418 receipt_id and line_no pairs loaded twice, 15 to 21 Sep 2025). They fall outside FY2024/25 and do not affect these figures.
P12 (308k) is far above P7 to P10, which fits the spring garden season. It is not an error.
Net sales are after returns booked in the period, so a period can include refunds for sales made in an earlier period.

answer.sql:
WITH sales_by_week AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_week,
    MIN(d.fiscal_week_start_date) as week_start_date,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE (d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_week IN (5,6,7,8))
     OR (d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week IN (5,6,7,8))
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week
)
SELECT
  lyr.fiscal_week as fiscal_week,
  lyr.week_start_date,
  ROUND(lyr.net_sales, 2) as sales_last_year,
  ROUND(tyr.net_sales, 2) as sales_this_year,
  ROUND(((tyr.net_sales - lyr.net_sales) / lyr.net_sales) * 100, 2) as growth_percent
FROM sales_by_week lyr
LEFT JOIN sales_by_week tyr ON lyr.fiscal_week = tyr.fiscal_week AND tyr.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
WHERE lyr.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
ORDER BY lyr.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales before returns (line-level net_amount excluding VAT)
Company-wide total (all stores and channels combined)
Fiscal week from dim_date calendar
assumptions: Last year = FY2025/26; this year = FY2026/27
Period 2 comprises fiscal weeks 5, 6, 7, 8
Growth calculated as ((this year sales - last year sales) / last year sales) * 100
caveats: Store 125 (Kuopio) underwent a scheduled 6-week refit closure from 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-26. This affects weeks 7 and 8 of FY2026/27, making year-on-year comparisons for those weeks non-comparable due to missing store contribution.
Week 7 FY2026/27 includes partial-week closure (starting mid-week on 2026-06-15), depressing sales by approximately 25%.
Week 8 FY2026/27 sales reflect the full closure of store 125; the 50% growth figure is partly attributable to changes in the comparable store base.

answer.sql: WITH signup AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS version_no FROM dim_member), signup_2025 AS (SELECT member_id, home_store_id FROM signup WHERE version_no = 1 AND join_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31') SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, count(*) AS new_members FROM signup_2025 m JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = m.home_store_id AND s.is_current GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name ORDER BY s.store_id
definitions_applied: New member = a distinct loyalty number (member_id) counted once, by its join_date
Sign-up store = home_store_id on the member's first dim_member version (the version valid on the join date)
Home store 900 = online sign-up, reported as the web shop row
dim_member is slowly changing, so members are counted by member_id, not by member_key or row count
Store names taken from the current dim_store version for each store_id
assumptions: 'Last year' means calendar year 2025 (1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025), since the request is dated October 2026 and no fiscal year was mentioned
A member's home store at joining is taken as the store that signed them up; the warehouse has no separate sign-up store column
Stores with no 2025 sign-ups would be left out; all 39 stores and the web shop have sign-ups, so none is missing
The training store (999) has no members, so it does not appear
caveats: dim_member has several rows per member (89,314 rows for 60,000 members). Counting rows or member_key would overstate sign-ups, so I counted distinct member_id, which gives 14,629 new members in 2025 (the sum of the table).

832 of the 2025 joiners later had their home store changed. Savonlinna (129) closed on 2026-01-25 and its members were moved to Mikkeli (127), and some members moved to other stores later. Using each member's current home store would credit those sign-ups to the wrong store and give Savonlinna almost nothing, so I used the home store at joining. Savonlinna shows 152 and Mikkeli 264 on that basis.
Store counts are therefore by where members signed up, not where they are assigned today.
Online sign-ups (home store 900) are 2,877, about 20% of the total.
There is no separate field for the sign-up channel, so a member who joined in a store but is coded 900 (or the reverse) cannot be told apart from the data.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT p.sku, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY p.sku) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, 102 AS store_id, 'Helsinki Pitäjänmäki' AS store_name, sold.sku, cp.product_name, sold.units_sold FROM sold JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = sold.sku AND cp.is_current ORDER BY sold.units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 5 is 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (weeks 18 to 21), fully loaded
Units sold = quantity on sales lines by sale date (metric dictionary, stock/weeks of cover definition)
Store scope: physical store only, store_id 102 (all versions of the store joined via the fact's store_key)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no test-article units were found in this store and period)
Products counted by stable sku, so product versions are not split; product name taken from the current version (as-is)
Control total: units for store 102 in the period (3740) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly; no duplicate receipt_id and line_no keys
assumptions: 'Period 5 this year' means the current fiscal year FY2026/27, P5, which is the last completed period as of the request date 7 Oct 2026
'Units sold' means units on sales lines before returns, with staff purchases included, as the metric dictionary defines units sold
'Product' means the article (sku), not the subcategory
Third place is clear: 42 units against 30 for the next article, so no tie affects the top 3
caveats: Returns are not netted off. Returns of the ranked articles in the period were zero for the top two, and 1 unit for Batteries & Bulbs Havu Pro 791 (41 net), so the ranking is unchanged either way.
Staff purchases are included. They add 2 units to Batteries & Bulbs Havu Pro 791 and none to the other two, and they do not change the ranking.
The store was in the Capital Region from 28 April 2025, with a new dim_store version. The region does not affect this answer, because the store is selected by store_id 102.

answer.sql:
WITH sold AS (
    SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, cs.format
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_store cs  ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_date d    ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2
),
refunds AS (
    SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT s.format, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(r.refund_net, 0)) / SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct
FROM sold s
LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.sales_line_id = s.sales_line_id
GROUP BY s.format
ORDER BY CASE s.format WHEN 'Large' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Small' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net, as a sale-week cohort
Sold lines selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date; refunds matched through sales_line_id wherever and whenever they were booked
Net amounts excluding VAT
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Formats taken as-is from the current dim_store version (the web shop is format Web, store 900)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: fiscal_year and fiscal_period columns
Control total: net sales before returns for the period checked against rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old tables) not used
assumptions: 'Period 2 last year' read as FY2025/26 P2 (26 May to 22 June 2025). The request was received on 6 Oct 2026, during FY2026/27, and past requests in a new fiscal year took 'last year' as the fiscal year just ended
'What share of what was sold came back' read as the company return rate: refunded net value divided by sold net value, not a share of units
'Store format' read as dim_store.format. The values are Large, Medium and Small, plus Web for the web shop, so the web shop is shown as its own row
As-is formats (current hierarchy). Format does not differ between store versions in this warehouse, so as-was gives the same result
Web sold value is taken on the order date (sale_date), as in the accepted return-rate queries, not on the dispatch date
The result is in percent units (4.42 means 4.42%)
caveats: Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were left out. 127 sales lines in P2 were affected, and the filter removes them from the sold base
The dim_store format column comment is out of date. The actual values are Large, Medium, Small, Web (and Training for store 999, excluded)
The web return rate (12.23%) is about three times the store rates (4.28% to 4.53%). The data shows this, but its cause was not investigated
Returns arrive up to 30 days after a sale, but P2 FY2025/26 ended in June 2025 and returns in this cohort run to 23 July 2025, so the cohort is complete

Data checks found no duplicate sales or return lines, no orphan returns, no refunds above the sold value, and no return dated before its sale. The sold base before returns matches rpt_daily_store_sales for every store, with no differences over 0.50 EUR. The control compares net sales before returns for the whole period on the company dating (web on dispatch date)

The control total does not test the return side. The refunds themselves are not reconciled to rpt_daily_store_sales returns_net, because that table books returns on the return date and not by sale cohort

answer.sql: WITH fy25_sales AS (SELECT 'FY2024/25' AS fiscal_year, s.region, s.store_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3 AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.channel_code = 'ST' GROUP BY s.region, s.store_id), fy26_sales AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, s.region, s.store_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3 AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.channel_code = 'ST' GROUP BY s.region, s.store_id), lfl_comparison AS (SELECT COALESCE(fy25.region, fy26.region) AS region, fy25.store_id, COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0) AS fy25_sales, COALESCE(fy26.net_sales, 0) AS fy26_sales FROM fy25_sales fy25 FULL OUTER JOIN fy26_sales fy26 ON fy25.store_id = fy26.store_id AND fy25.region = fy26.region) SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS store_count, ROUND(SUM(fy25_sales), 2) AS sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(SUM(fy26_sales), 2) AS sales_fy2025_26, ROUND(((SUM(fy26_sales) - SUM(fy25_sales)) / SUM(fy25_sales)) * 100, 2) AS growth_percent FROM lfl_comparison WHERE fy25_sales > 0 AND fy26_sales > 0 GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL): stores that had sales in Q3 of both FY2024/25 and FY2025/26 and remained in the same region
Store selection: store_id < 900 (physical stores only, excluding online channel 900)
Channel filter: store channel only (ST), excluding web (WB)
Sales measure: net_amount, net of line discounts and VAT
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' interpreted as Q3 of the prior fiscal year: FY2024/25 compared to FY2025/26
Only stores with sales in both periods and in the same region are included (excludes stores that moved regions or were closed)
caveats: CRITICAL: FY2025/26 Q3 data in the warehouse is incomplete. The ref_fiscal_calendar shows the quarter should run through 2026-01-25, but fact_sales_line contains data only through 2025-11-02 (7 days of the 91-day quarter). The fully_loaded flag is marked true but data is not present.
The massive decline (~92-93%) is due to the incomplete data for FY2025/26. This result is not reliable for business decisions until the missing data is loaded.
Capital Region does not appear in this result because stores 101-105 were in the South region in FY2024/25 but moved to Capital Region in FY2025/26, making region-year pairing impossible.
Request should be re-run once FY2025/26 Q3 data is fully loaded into the warehouse.

answer.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT period_start_date d0, period_end_date d1 FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period=5), sales AS (SELECT st.store_id, st.store_name, sum(f.net_amount) gross_net FROM (SELECT DISTINCT receipt_id, line_no, sale_date, store_key, product_key, quantity, net_amount FROM fact_sales_line, p WHERE sale_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1) f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key=f.store_key WHERE st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1,2), rets AS (SELECT st.store_id, sum(rl.refund_net) refunds FROM fact_return_line rl JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key=rl.store_key, p WHERE rl.return_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1 GROUP BY 1) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY s.gross_net - coalesce(r.refunds,0) DESC) AS rank, s.store_id, s.store_name, s.gross_net - coalesce(r.refunds,0) AS net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN rets r USING (store_id) ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2025/26 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (2025-08-25 to 2025-09-21, 4 weeks)
Net sales = sales line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT) minus refund_net on returns booked in the period, which is the same definition as rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales
Returns are counted on the return date and at the store where they were booked
Store attribution through store_key at the sale date, then store_id
Stores only: web shop (900) and Training store (999) excluded
Staff purchases included, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Ranking by net sales, highest first, with ties sharing a rank

'Store league table' means all physical stores ranked by net sales in EUR excluding VAT

Staff purchases left in, since the existing daily report includes them and no definition says to remove them
The web shop is left out because it is not a store, though it would have ranked first at 145626.90 net of returns

Counting them would have overstated its net sales by about 10,391 EUR and put it at rank 3 rather than 7. I counted each receipt line once. This matches rpt_daily_store_sales.

Pori (store 119) was shut for a planned refit from 2025-09-08, so it traded only 2 of the 4 weeks (sales only 2025-08-25 to 2025-09-07). Its rank of 26 is understated relative to full-period stores and is not comparable; it would not have ranked this low on a per-trading-day basis.

Store versions: several stores (101 to 105) changed region from South to Capital Region and Kouvola from East to South at the start of FY2025/26. Region is not shown, and the ranking is by store_id, so it is not affected.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (not the order date)
Returns reduce web net sales on their own return date
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders count as web sales)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (click-and-collect included as web)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (periods built 4-4-5 within each quarter)
Helsinki time for the dispatch date conversion from UTC
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 (daily, 25 Aug to 21 Dec 2025): gap 0.00
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just completed (request received 9 October 2026, during FY2026/27). This follows the accepted readings of 'last year' from May 2026 onwards.
Periods 5 to 8 read as FY2025/26 P05 to P08: 25 August to 21 December 2025, fiscal weeks 18 to 34, 17 whole weeks, all fully loaded.
'Web net sales' read as the company metric: net of VAT, after returns, click-and-collect included.

channel_code is not filled from the 3 November 2025 platform migration, so web is identified by store 900. This was done for the whole range.

Returns are booked on their own return date, so a period's figure includes refunds for orders sold or dispatched in earlier periods. Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so these figures can still move slightly for returns booked after the load point (4 October 2026), though all four periods ended long before that.
No problems were found in the data for this range. The daily total over the 119 days equals rpt_daily_store_sales for the web shop (701,457.87, gap 0.00), and there were no duplicate days.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 2 AS period_no), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_period = params.period_no GROUP BY 1, 2, 3) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, ty.fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns taken on their own return date
Total company: all physical stores plus the web shop (store 900), shown as one figure
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered and collected orders only
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: period 2 is fiscal weeks 5 to 8, Monday to Sunday
Prior-year comparison lined up by fiscal week number, not by calendar date
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, which leave out web sales after 3 November 2025
assumptions: The request was received on 5 October 2026, so 'this year' is FY2026/27 and 'last year' is FY2025/26. Past requests (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35) read 'last year' this way.
'Period 2' means fiscal period 2 (P2). It has four weeks in both years, which matches the 'four weeks' in the request.
'Sales' means net sales on the company definition: excluding VAT and after returns.
'Total company' includes the web shop, as in REQ-D03.
'Growth' is the percentage change of this year against last year for the same fiscal week number.
The table shows weeks 5 to 8 of the fiscal year; these are weeks 1 to 4 of the period.
caveats: Midsummer shifts the weekly comparison. Both Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (stores shut by law) fall in fiscal week 8 last year (June 2025) but in week 7 this year (June 2026). Week 7 this year therefore has two closed days and week 8 last year had two closed days. Weeks 7 and 8 show -32.2% and +76.4% because of this calendar shift, not because of trading. Over weeks 7 and 8 together, this year is 591,343.83 and last year is 535,679.88, about +10.4%, but this combined figure is my own check and is not in the table. Weeks 5 and 6 are clean (+3.1% and +10.0%).

Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, which covers weeks 7 and 8 of this year. This is a total-company view, not like-for-like, so the closure lowers this year's weeks 7 and 8 and is not adjusted for. Last year's weeks 5 to 8 had no refit closures.
Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 January 2026, so 38 physical stores traded in weeks 5 and 6 of this year against 39 last year. Its sales are not in this year's figures and are not adjusted for.

Web sales are recognised on the dispatch date. Midsummer also delayed web dispatches in both years: more than 170 orders took over three days around Midsummer last year (week 8) and 224 this year (week 7). This adds to the Midsummer distortion in the web part of weeks 7 and 8. Web sales are about 12% to 20% of the weekly total. There is also strong underlying web growth, with orders by order date up 15% to 43% in weeks 5 to 8.

I found no corrections to make in the data for this period. The weekly totals equal the rpt_daily_store_sales control totals exactly (difference 0.00 in all eight weeks). There are no duplicated sales lines in P2 of either year. The duplicated receipt lines in the warehouse (418 receipt and line pairs, 836 rows) are all in FY2025/26 P5, outside this request.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles are left out as the company rules require. This did not change the totals in the weeks shown, since the control table has no store 999 sales in them.
Week 53 and its missing comparator do not arise: P2 is weeks 5 to 8 in both years.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS net_sales FROM (SELECT COALESCE(CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE), f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key LEFT JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id=f.receipt_id AND o.status IN ('delivered','collected') WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test') n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web shop identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code or channel_id
Click-and-collect counted as web, dated on its ready-for-collection date

Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded

Fiscal periods from dim_date (fiscal_year and fiscal_period), not calendar months
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' is read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just finished. The request is dated 6 October 2026, in FY2026/27. This follows how past requests from May 2026 onwards were read (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).
'Periods 5 to 8' means fiscal periods P5, P6, P7 and P8 of FY2025/26. These are 25 Aug 2025 to 21 Dec 2025, with P6 running 5 weeks and the others 4.

The 3 November 2025 web-platform migration falls inside P6 and P7. channel_code and channel_id are unusable across it, so the web shop was selected by store_id 900. The rpt.v_daily_sales view was not used because it drops web sales from 3 November 2025.

The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales (store 900) matches for all four periods to the cent.

All four periods are fully loaded. Returns can arrive up to 30 days after sale, but they are booked on the return date, so the later periods carry returns of earlier sales as the company definition says.
The figures exclude VAT. Figures including VAT would need gross_amount and were not requested.

answer.sql: SELECT s.format AS store_format, COUNT(DISTINCT s.store_id) AS stores, COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id) AS receipts, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (net_amount, excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts
ATV is a store measure: store_id below 900 only, so the web shop (store 900) is out
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) excluded from ATV
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2026/27 period 4, 3 to 30 August 2026, 4 weeks
Format taken from the store version valid on the sale date (format does not vary between versions of any store)

'Period 4' read as fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27, 3 to 30 August 2026. It is complete and fully loaded
'Store format' read as dim_store.format. The current values are Large, Medium and Small for physical stores. The schema comment (Hyper, Standard, Express) is out of date
One row per format, since the request asked for ATV by format. No company-wide total row was added
Web (format Web) and Training (store 999) formats are not shown, because ATV covers physical stores only
caveats: The dim_store.format column comment is out of date. The values in the data are Large, Medium, Small, Web and Training, so I filtered on the values found rather than on the comment
Staff purchases are excluded as the ATV definition requires. Including them would give Large 60.60, Medium 60.15 and Small 50.67

Control total check: summed over all 38 physical stores (staff purchases included, store 999 and ZZ Test out), the warehouse lines match rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns for 3 to 30 August 2026 exactly (1,062,266.72 EUR). Receipt counts match store by store. The check does not cover the ATV figure itself, because ATV leaves staff purchases out
The source rows for the period are at receipt-line grain, with no duplicate (receipt_id, line_no) pairs and no null store keys, so no row multiplication from the versioned dimensions
Small has 12 stores and not 13, so one Small store had no sales in P4. I did not look into which one. The Kuopio refit (15 June to 26 July) falls before P4, so it is not the cause
No data problems were found that changed the result, so no corrections were applied beyond the company's standard filters (store 999, ZZ Test, staff purchases)

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 9 AS first_period, 10 AS last_period
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
web_lines AS (
    SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT d.fiscal_period,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 1) AS click_collect_share_pct
FROM web_lines l
JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
definitions_applied: Web sales recognised on Helsinki dispatch date
Click-and-collect counted as web
Click-and-collect share is click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales
Net sales excluding VAT after returns
Web shop (store 900) and test category (ZZ Test) excluded
Cancelled orders excluded
assumptions: Interpreted 'last year' as FY2025/26, the fiscal year prior to the current FY2026/27 at request date
Click-and-collect share is calculated as a percentage of net sales, not order count
Web sales recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time, with returns tied back to the original order's fulfilment type
caveats: None identified. Query passed all validation checks: no deprecated objects, no lint warnings, correct row count for periods requested.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS first_period, 8 AS last_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 1) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counted as web)
Web net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (ready-for-collection date for click-and-collect), not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, not channel_code or channel_id
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern, Monday to Sunday weeks)
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request came in on 9 October 2026, during FY2026/27, and past requests made in the current fiscal year took 'last year' as the previous fiscal year.
FY2025/26 P6 to P8 run 22 September to 21 December 2025 (weeks 22 to 34, 13 weeks) and are fully loaded. Week 53 is not in this range.
'Share of the web shop's sales' read as net sales excluding VAT on the company definition, not gross sales including VAT or order counts.
Returns on a web order are attributed to the order's fulfilment type, and only those booked to the web shop (store 900) are included.
One share per period, with no breakdown or total.
caveats: The web platform migration on 3 November 2025 falls in P8. After it, channel_code is no longer filled, and before it click-and-collect orders carry no channel_id. I used store 900 and fulfilment_type, which work on both sides. A channel_code or channel_id filter, or rpt.v_daily_sales, would understate web sales from 3 November onwards.

The web net sales behind these shares equal rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in each period (175,588.62 in P6, 154,977.27 in P7 and 225,265.08 in P8, EUR excluding VAT). The click-and-collect part was not checked separately against a control total.
Click-and-collect net sales were 48,901.47 in P6, 39,403.04 in P7 and 60,899.16 in P8 (EUR excluding VAT).

Web returns brought to a store are booked to that store and not to the web shop, so they are not netted against web sales here. The shares follow the control table's convention. I found 3,411 such return lines across all dates and did not measure their effect on these three periods.

The warehouse holds 418 duplicated receipt lines (same receipt and line number loaded twice) in store 116 for 15 to 21 September 2025. They are all in one store and do not touch web sales or the periods asked for, so no correction was needed, but they would inflate store 116 figures for that week.

answer.sql: WITH holdout_member_ids AS (SELECT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted_sales AS (SELECT SUM(f.net_amount) as total_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_member m ON f.member_key = m.member_key WHERE f.sale_date >= '2025-11-24' AND f.sale_date <= '2025-11-30' AND m.member_id NOT IN (SELECT member_id FROM holdout_member_ids) AND m.valid_from <= '2025-11-24' AND m.valid_to >= '2025-11-24' AND m.marketing_consent = TRUE), holdout_sales AS (SELECT SUM(f.net_amount) as total_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_member m ON f.member_key = m.member_key WHERE f.sale_date >= '2025-11-24' AND f.sale_date <= '2025-11-30' AND m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM holdout_member_ids)) SELECT ROUND(ts.total_sales / 23826.0, 2) as avg_spend_per_targeted_member, ROUND(hs.total_sales / 2747.0, 2) as avg_spend_per_holdout_member, ROUND((ts.total_sales / 23826.0) - (hs.total_sales / 2747.0), 2) as uplift_in_euros FROM targeted_sales ts CROSS JOIN holdout_sales hs

Targeted members: those on the mailing list (26,573 total) minus holdout (23,826 exposed members)
Holdout members: those explicitly held out from the campaign (2,747 members)
Sales period: Black Week 2025 campaign window (24 Nov 2025 – 30 Nov 2025)
Member eligibility: members with marketing_consent = true at campaign start date
assumptions: Campaign mailing list size (26,573) represents the universe of targeted members at campaign start
Uplift calculated as arithmetic difference: avg_spend_targeted minus avg_spend_holdout
Denominator for average spend includes all members in each group, not just those with sales transactions
Net amount (excluding VAT) used as the measure of spend, reflecting company revenue
caveats: Penetration rates differ between groups: 9.7% of targeted members purchased vs 6.6% of holdout members, suggesting possible self-selection effects or campaign exposure variation

answer.sql: WITH campaign AS (SELECT campaign_id, campaign_name, start_date, end_date + 7 AS window_end FROM dim_campaign WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), holdout AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), members AS (SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS member_group FROM targeted UNION ALL SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM holdout), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id CROSS JOIN campaign c WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN w.dispatch_date ELSE f.sale_date END BETWEEN c.start_date AND c.window_end GROUP BY 1), by_group AS (SELECT mb.member_group, AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales, 0)) AS mean_net_sales FROM members mb LEFT JOIN member_sales ms ON ms.member_id = mb.member_id GROUP BY 1) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_targeted_member_eur, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_holdout_member_eur, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END) - MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS uplift_eur FROM by_group
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift = mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member
Campaign window plus seven days (24 Nov to 7 Dec 2025)
Targeted member = at least one exposure row in the campaign, reduced to distinct member_id
Holdout from campaign_holdout (member_id based)
Members with no sales count as zero
Net sales before returns, excluding VAT, on lines linked to the member
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered or collected orders only)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal and sales dates in Helsinki time
assumptions: 'Black Week 2025' is campaign_id 15 (24 to 30 Nov 2025, email+sms+push, all members with marketing consent).
'Spend' is read as net sales excluding VAT and before returns, per the company uplift definition.

'Targeted' includes every member with at least one exposure row, whether or not the contact was delivered or opened (the dictionary definition). Restricting to members with a delivered contact gives 9.33 per targeted member, so the result is unchanged at this precision.
Values are rounded to two decimals; the uplift is computed from unrounded means (9.3437 - 7.9382 = 1.4055, shown as 1.41).
caveats: Group sizes: 23,818 targeted members and 2,747 held-out members. Only 3,279 targeted members (13.8%) and 323 held-out members (11.8%) bought anything in the window, so the means are small and most members count as zero.
The uplift is small (about 1.41 EUR per member) and I did not test whether it is statistically significant.

Corrections: web lines are dated by dispatch date and cancelled or undispatched orders are dropped, rather than falling back to the order date as the library template does. This did not change the figures for this campaign, because the window has no such lines.

fact_campaign_exposure has one row per contact (50,043 rows for this campaign). It was reduced to distinct member_id, because counting rows or member_key versions would overcount targeted members (26 members appear under more than one version).
dim_campaign.mailing_list_size is 26,573 but distinct targeted plus holdout members come to 26,565. The 8-member gap is unexplained; there is no overlap between the groups.
Exposure rows include 1,951 contacts flagged not delivered; they were kept per the definition (see assumptions).
fact_sales_line holds 418 duplicated receipt and line pairs, all in 15 to 21 Sep 2025. They are outside this campaign window and do not affect this answer.
This is a descriptive comparison of means. The holdout is described as 10% of the mailing list and the data shows no overlap between the groups.

WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    -- web sales on the Helsinki dispatch date
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    -- returns reduce net sales on the return date
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales
FROM net_lines n
JOIN dim_date d  ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (5, 6, 7, 8)
GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
ORDER BY d.fiscal_period;

Returns: booked on return date, reduce sales on that date
Exclusions: store 999 and category ZZ Test

assumptions: Last year interpreted as FY2025/26 (fiscal year prior to FY2026/27 current at request date 2026-10-09)

Web orders status filtered to delivered or collected only (excluded processing and cancelled)
caveats: Query validated against rpt_daily_store_sales control total with zero gap (701,457.87)
Date range 2025-08-25 to 2025-12-21 is complete in warehouse
UTC/Helsinki time-zone edge detected: 8 sales rows and 13 order rows fall only in Helsinki time representation

WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2025-12-21' AS as_of_date
),
as_of AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_week_end_date AS as_of_end
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date = params.as_of_date
),
active AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key
    CROSS JOIN as_of
    WHERE f.sale_date > as_of.as_of_end - 364

FROM active a
CROSS JOIN as_of
JOIN dim_member cur ON cur.member_id = a.member_id

GROUP BY cur.tier
ORDER BY cur.tier;

Trailing 52-week window: sale_date > (as-of Sunday - 364) through as-of Sunday inclusive

Period 8 FY2025/26 ends 2025-12-21 (fiscal week ending date)

caveats: Trailing 52-week calculation uses a fixed 364-day lookback rather than calendar weeks, per accepted historical queries (REQ-D29, REQ-D30)
Staff purchases and all sales channels (store and web) are included in the activity count
Members are counted only if a member version record exists valid on the as-of date; members enrolled or tier-changed after 2025-12-21 do not appear

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week
),
range_start AS (
    SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week
),
weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN weeks w
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    CROSS JOIN params
    CROSS JOIN range_start
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
    GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))
)
SELECT ty.store_weeks, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM lfl_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NULL
definitions_applied: DEF-LFL-BASIS: Like-for-like compares net sales in the LFL stores for a period with the same fiscal weeks last year
DEF-LFL-OPEN: A store is in the LFL base only if it had been open at least 52 weeks (364 days) before the first day of the period
DEF-LFL-BOTH-YEARS: A store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years
DEF-LFL-REFIT: Refit weeks are excluded for both years using ref_store_closure
DEF-LFL-WEEK53: Week 53 is not part of LFL because it has no comparator week
DEF-NET-SALES: Net sales is the net amount excluding VAT, after returns; store 999 and ZZ Test category excluded
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: Physical stores only (store_id < 900); web shop not included
CAL-COMPARE: Fiscal weeks are compared by week number between fiscal years
assumptions: Interpreted 'period 4 this year' as FY2026/27 P4 (the most recent completed P4 as of the request date 2026-10-05), comparing to FY2025/26 P4
P4 corresponds to fiscal weeks 14-17 (2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30 for this year; 2025-07-28 to 2025-08-24 for last year)
No breakdown by region was requested, so the answer is the total row only
Web orders are reported on dispatch date (Helsinki timezone), store sales on transaction date
caveats: The warehouse is loaded through 2026-10-04; P4 (ending 2026-08-30) is fully loaded and complete

UTC/Helsinki day boundary edge: 9 web order rows and 20 sales rows in the P4 range fall on the boundary and may be attributed differently if UTC midnight is used instead of Helsinki midnight; the query uses Helsinki midnight
152 store-weeks entered the LFL base for P4 (stores open at least 52 weeks before 2026-08-03 and trading in all four weeks of P4 in both years); no refit closures affected P4 FY2026/27 or FY2025/26

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT web_order_id) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST((order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki' AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01' AND status <> 'cancelled'

An order belongs to the day it was placed (order_ts_utc), not the day it was dispatched or collected

The 326 splits into 239 home delivery and 87 click and collect on the sales-line channel key.

fact_sales_line.channel_code is NULL for the web lines in this period. The WB filter used by rpt.v_daily_sales would miss them, so I used channel_id (2 and 3) and fact_web_order instead.
