Result includes all sales regardless of staff purchase flag status
No returns deducted; figure represents gross unit sales

answer.sql:
WITH net_lines AS (
  SELECT f.sale_date, f.store_key, f.product_key, f.net_amount, 0 AS refund_net
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT r.return_date, r.store_key, r.product_key, 0 AS net_amount, -r.refund_net
  FROM fact_return_line r
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
  WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT cs.region, SUM(nl.net_amount + nl.refund_net) AS net_sales
FROM net_lines nl
INNER JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = nl.sale_date
INNER JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = nl.store_key
INNER JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current
WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 22
GROUP BY cs.region
ORDER BY net_sales DESC
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns (returns reduce sales on their return date, not the sale date)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900), excluding training store 999
Product scope: excludes test articles (category ZZ Test)
As-is hierarchy: current region names (Capital Region as one of five regions)
Fiscal period: FY2026/27 weeks 1-22 (2026-05-04 through 2026-10-04)
assumptions: 'How they are doing' interpreted as net sales, the primary retail performance metric
'This year so far' interpreted as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 through the last loaded data (2026-10-04)
'Stores only, no web shop' applied by filtering to physical stores (store_id < 900, excluding web at 900 and training at 999)
Ranking determined by net sales in descending order
caveats: Data current through 2026-10-04; FY2026/27 continues through 2027-05-02 but is incomplete
The five regions include Capital Region, which was created on 2026-04-28 when six stores moved from South/East
Net sales verified against rpt_daily_store_sales control total: 5,762,831.03 EUR (sum of all regions)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales) DESC) AS rank, cp.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS web_net_sales_eur FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date >= DATE '2025-11-03' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory ORDER BY web_net_sales_eur DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date (sale_date)
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is not filled from the 3 Nov 2025 migration)
Cancelled and still-processing orders are not web sales (only delivered/collected orders with a dispatch time count)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Staff purchases included
Product as-is: lines grouped by stable sku, named from the current product version
Timestamps converted from UTC to Europe/Helsinki before dating
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales (they leave out web sales from 3 Nov 2025)
assumptions: 'Products' means individual articles (sku), not categories, subcategories or brands.
'Web sales' means net sales in EUR excluding VAT after returns, per the company definition; ranked by value, not units or order count.
'Since the platform migration on 3 November 2025' is read as from 3 November 2025 inclusive, up to the end of the loaded data (4 October 2026), by Helsinki dispatch date.
Orders placed before 3 November 2025 but dispatched on or after it count as web sales of the period; refunds booked on or after 3 November 2025 count even if the original sale was dispatched earlier.
Product names, categories and subcategories are as-is (current product version).
The request did not ask for margin, VAT-inclusive figures or order counts, so none are given.
caveats: Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or rpt.v_daily_sales: channel_code is empty from the 3 Nov 2025 migration and the legacy views silently drop web sales after that date.
Web net sales for the period total 2,150,090.07 EUR and match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly (after excluding ZZ Test).
19 web test-article lines (category ZZ Test, 61.27 EUR net) were excluded; they do not affect the top 10.

Refunds follow the company rule (booked where processed). 1,621 refunds on web-sold lines (67,513.71 EUR net) were processed in physical stores and so reduce store net sales, not web sales, in this answer. If they were charged back to web, the ranking would change: sku 103415 Home Office Peltola 918 would drop out of the top 10 and 103861 Christmas Decorations Kuusela 620 would enter, with 100528 and 103928 moving down or up a place and 103390 and 100529 swapping places 3 and 4.
102 refunds (4,478.51 EUR net) on or after 3 Nov 2025 relate to web sales dispatched before 3 Nov 2025; they reduce the figures here, as the return-date rule requires.
Orders still processing or cancelled have no sales lines and are not in the figures; the data runs to 4 Oct 2026, so the latest dispatches and returns may still be incomplete.
The gap between 10th (6,889.60) and 11th (6,679.65) is small, so the tenth place is sensitive to the points above.
Unrelated to this request: fact_sales_line has duplicated receipt/line rows (418 keys) for store 116 in 15-21 Sep 2025, loaded twice; web data is not affected.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, p.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND f.staff_purchase_flag = false GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name, p.category ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Last period: most recent fully-loaded fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, 31 Aug – 27 Sep 2026)
Best-selling: ranked by unit quantity
Staff purchases excluded from ranking
assumptions: Last period interpreted as the most recent complete fiscal period with fully_loaded = true
Best-selling ranked by units sold, not by net sales or gross revenue
Staff purchases excluded as they do not represent customer demand
Returns not netted out: figures show gross units sold (demand signal), not net retained units
caveats: Current period (P06, FY2026/27) is not fully loaded; using previous complete period instead
Return rate in this period was 2.73%; net units retained would be slightly lower
Tools & Hardware category dominates top 10 (6 of 10 SKUs), suggesting strong category demand or possible data concentration

answer.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount, f.staff_purchase_flag, s.format FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 AND s.store_id < 900), staff_receipts AS (SELECT DISTINCT receipt_id FROM p WHERE staff_purchase_flag) SELECT format, round(sum(net_amount) FILTER (WHERE receipt_id NOT IN (SELECT receipt_id FROM staff_receipts)) / count(DISTINCT receipt_id) FILTER (WHERE receipt_id NOT IN (SELECT receipt_id FROM staff_receipts)), 2) AS avg_transaction_value_eur FROM p GROUP BY format ORDER BY CASE format WHEN 'Large' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Average transaction value = net sales divided by number of distinct receipts
Net sales = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts), before returns
Transaction = one receipt (receipt_id)
Store format taken from dim_store through the sale line's store_key (the store version at the sale date)
Fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 = 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30 (ref_fiscal_calendar / dim_date, fully loaded)
Physical stores only: pseudo-locations with store_id of 900 or above (web shop, training store) excluded
Staff purchases excluded: receipts with any staff_purchase_flag line
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' read as fiscal period 4 of the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (the request is dated 2026-10-06, which falls in FY2026/27 P06), not calendar April
ATV measured on net sales excluding VAT; the request did not say whether to use gross
ATV measured before returns, since a return is not a transaction and refunds are booked against other receipts
Staff purchases left out because they are not customer transactions; the request did not say either way
Web orders left out because the request is by store format and the web shop is not a store format
All 38 physical stores that traded in the period are included; none were closed or in a refit closure
caveats: The warehouse formats are Large, Medium and Small (8, 18 and 12 stores trading in P4). The column comment on dim_store.format says Hyper, Standard or Express, which does not match the data. I used the values in the data.
fact_sales_line.channel_code is NULL for the P4 rows, despite the column comment saying ST/WB. I did not rely on it and identified the web shop and training store through store_id of 900 and above.
Training store (999) has real-looking sales rows in the period (EUR 1,885 net, 55 receipts) and the web shop has EUR 209,106 net on 3,229 receipts. Both are excluded.
Including staff purchases would give 60.60 (Large), 60.15 (Medium) and 50.67 (Small), so the exclusion moves each figure by 0.07 to 0.12 EUR.

Checks run on the P4 sales lines found no duplicate receipt-and-line pairs, no receipts spanning more than one store or date, no sales on non-trading days or during refit closures, and no VAT mismatches. Receipt counts and net sales by store agree exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales (before returns).
Store regions changed on 2025-04-28 for several stores, but formats did not change, so the format grouping is unaffected.

answer.sql: WITH cal AS (SELECT min(period_start_date) AS p_start, max(period_end_date) AS p_end FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period BETWEEN 1 AND 3), sales AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key CROSS JOIN cal WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN cal.p_start AND cal.p_end AND s.store_id <> 999) SELECT round(sum(net_amount) / count(DISTINCT receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM sales
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) divided by the number of distinct receipts, the same basis as rpt.v_daily_sales (sum of net_amount over distinct receipts)
A web order counts as one transaction (receipt_id equals web_order_id), the same as a store receipt
Fiscal calendar from ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2026/27 periods 1 to 3 run 2026-05-04 to 2026-08-02 (13 weeks, with P3 being 5 weeks)
Stores joined through the dim_store surrogate key (store_key), as the fact tables require
Channels identified by channel_id (1 store, 2 web home delivery, 3 click and collect), not by channel_code
Sales are before returns, so refunds are not deducted from the numerator
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (the request is dated 2026-10-05, so P1 to P3 are complete and the warehouse marks them fully_loaded). A calendar-year reading would be a different date range.
ATV is measured on net sales excluding VAT. Including VAT it would be 70.22.
ATV is measured before returns. The warehouse has no written ATV definition, so this is my reading. Net of returns it would be 53.04 (refunds of 243,627.84 net, which match rpt_daily_store_sales).
Staff purchases are included, as in the company's own daily sales report. Excluding them gives 56.17.
Web orders are dated by sale_date, the local date on the sales lines.
caveats: Correction: the Training store (store_id 999, 174 receipts and 7,805.99 EUR net in the period) was excluded. It is a test location, not real trading, and the warehouse has no flag for it other than its name and format 'Training'.

Correction: web sales lines in this period have a NULL channel_code, because the code was replaced by channel_id after the web-platform migration. The existing views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales pick web lines up with channel_code = 'WB', so they would drop all web orders from the figure. I used channel_id 2 and 3 instead, giving 12,962 web receipts and 771,031.31 EUR net.
Cancelled web orders (531 in the period) have no sales lines, so they are not in the figure. Only delivered and collected orders appear.
Result basis: 80,983 receipts (68,021 in physical stores, 12,962 web) and 4,538,952.58 EUR net sales.

The physical-store figures match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, day by day. Store 900 (web) differs because that report books web orders on a different business date, and it also includes some days with nearly no web activity. Its period totals are not a clean basis for ATV, which is why I used the fact table.
Using the report's own figures (4,295,824.18 net after returns over 81,025 receipts) would give about 53.0, which is a different measure from the 56.05 reported here.

I checked for duplicate lines, receipts spanning dates or stores, zero or negative lines, and VAT inconsistencies, and found none. Lines loaded into the staging tables are all present in the fact table.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-29' AS period_start_date, DATE '2026-08-02' AS period_end_date), weekly_chain_totals AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS weekly_total_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date BETWEEN params.period_start_date AND params.period_end_date AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY fs.week_ending_date) SELECT ROUND(AVG(weekly_total_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_eur FROM weekly_chain_totals;
definitions_applied: Closing stock: snapshot at end of fiscal week
Period average: average of weekly closings, never sum across weeks
Scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900)
Stock value: at standard unit cost in EUR
Category: Paint & Decorating (includes Brushes & Rollers, Exterior Paint, Interior Paint, Wallpaper & Decor Film)
assumptions: Period 3 this year read as FY2026/27 P03 (most recent completed fiscal period as of request date 2026-10-08)
Period 3 covers fiscal weeks 9-13 (2026-06-29 to 2026-08-02)
Average stock for whole chain: sum of Paint & Decorating products across all physical stores per week, then average across weeks
caveats: Data complete: all 5 weeks of period 3 present in warehouse
No data quality issues identified in query-check
Web stock excluded (central warehouse not in fact_stock_week)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE fs.week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-06-29' AND DATE '2026-08-02' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' GROUP BY 1) SELECT ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 3 of FY2026/27 is 29 June to 2 August 2026 (fiscal weeks 9 to 13, 5 weeks)
Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week, then averaged across the 5 weeks, never summed across weeks
Closing value at standard cost (fact_stock_week.closing_value)
As-is category hierarchy (current dim_product version via sku and is_current)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); store 999 and the web shop excluded; no web stock exists in the snapshot
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Stock is counted on week-ending Sundays, so the 5 snapshots are 5, 12, 19 and 26 July and 2 August 2026
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, so period 3 is 29 June to 2 August 2026
'Average stock' is read as the average of the 5 weekly closing stock values in the period, as the company definition has it
'Whole chain' means all physical stores that hold stock in the snapshot (38 stores); the web shop holds no stock in the table
'Value at cost' is the standard cost in closing_value, not the latest purchase price
The Sunday 28 June closing belongs to period 2 (fiscal week 8), so it is not included
caveats: I checked the source rows for the 5 weeks at store, article and week level and found no duplicates, no negative stock, and no mismatch between closing_value and units times standard cost, so no corrections were needed
Using the category as it was on the date instead of the current one gives the same figure, because no Paint & Decorating articles changed category
Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 but still carries stock in the snapshot, so its stock is included for all 5 weeks
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no stock rows in the period, so it adds nothing
Weekly closing value ranged from 341,139 to 349,160 EUR across the 5 weeks
Standard unit costs are revalued each April, so the value is at the FY2026/27 standard costs

answer.sql:
SELECT 
  dp.category,
  SUM(CASE WHEN dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN fsl.net_amount ELSE 0 END) AS net_sales_fy2024_25,
  SUM(CASE WHEN dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN fsl.net_amount ELSE 0 END) AS net_sales_fy2025_26,
  ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN fsl.net_amount ELSE 0 END) - 
          SUM(CASE WHEN dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN fsl.net_amount ELSE 0 END)) / 
         SUM(CASE WHEN dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN fsl.net_amount ELSE 0 END) * 100, 2) AS growth_percent
FROM fact_sales_line fsl
INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key
INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date
WHERE dd.fiscal_period = 8
  AND dd.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
  AND dp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
GROUP BY dp.category
ORDER BY dp.category
definitions_applied: Net sales: sum of fact_sales_line.net_amount (excluding VAT, after line discounts)
FY2024/25: fiscal year 2024/25 (the year before)
FY2025/26: fiscal year 2025/26 (last year)
Period 8: fiscal period 8 in each fiscal year (late November to late December)
Growth: percentage change from FY2024/25 to FY2025/26
assumptions: Last year interpreted as FY2025/26 (most recent completed fiscal year)
The year before interpreted as FY2024/25 (prior fiscal year)
Both periods use fiscal calendar period 8 for seasonal comparability
All sales channels included (store and web)
All store formats and regions included without subdivision
caveats: Both fiscal periods are fully loaded in the warehouse
Net sales figures exclude returns; fact_return_line is not subtracted from sales
Staff purchases are included in the net sales figures (staff_purchase_flag not filtered)
Garden category shows significant decline of 34.21%, warrant review for causes (promotional timing, inventory, supply)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' AND NOT (s.store_id=900 AND w.web_order_id IS NULL) UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period=5 GROUP BY 1,2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Cancelled and processing web orders excluded (no dispatch)
Whole company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Last period = last completed fiscal period (FY2026/27 P5)
Fiscal calendar columns used rather than calendar months
Control total against rpt_daily_store_sales
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, channel_code, stg_/bak_/tmp_ tables) not used
assumptions: 'Last month' read as the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P5 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), following the wiki convention for 'last period' and the fiscal-calendar rule. The warehouse is loaded to 4 Oct 2026 and P6 is only partly complete.
'Whole company' read as all physical stores plus the web shop, shown as one total, with no breakdown.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: If you meant calendar September (1 to 30 Sep 2026), the figure on the same definition is 1179035.98, not 1109546.52. P5 covers 31 Aug to 27 Sep.
Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test articles is the standing rule. The data has no store 999 or ZZ Test lines in this period that change the total, so no correction was needed for that.
The dashboard views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales leave out web sales from 3 Nov 2025 and were not used. Web net sales in P5 are 177237.33, included in the total.

Checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for P5: the total and every store (including web, store 900) agree exactly, with a difference of 0.00 at store level. I did not find duplicate sales or return lines in the range.
No web order lines in the range were missing a dispatched order, so none were dropped.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 4 of FY2026/27 is 3 August to 30 August 2026 (4 weeks)
A return counts on its own return date (return_date), not the date of the original sale
Units returned is quantity_returned from fact_return_line
Product category and subcategory as-is (current product version)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out (no effect on this figure)
Web returns are booked to the web shop (store 900) and are included
Did not use channel_code, deprecated tables or the rpt views
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as of the request date 5 October 2026. P4 is complete (the last complete period is P5).

'Garden Furniture' read as the subcategory Garden Furniture within the Garden category. There is no other category or subcategory of that name; Furniture and Bathroom Furniture are different categories and were not included.

'Handed back and booked as returned' read as rows in fact_return_line dated by return date, in all channels (stores and web). Of the 92 units, 58 were booked in physical stores and 34 on the web shop (store 900).
Units returned are not netted against units sold. This is a count of returned units, not a return rate.
caveats: No data problems affecting this figure were found, so no corrections were made. The 92 return lines are 92 distinct return_line_ids and 92 distinct sales lines, so there are no duplicates. No return is dated before its sale, none exceeds the quantity sold, none is orphaned from its sales line, and none has a null reason code. Every line has quantity 1.
As-was and as-is give the same 92, so the 2026/27 outdoor-lighting and region reclassifications do not affect it.
The count includes the web shop returns (34 units). For stores only, the figure is 58.
The count was not checked against rpt_daily_store_sales, which carries refund values rather than units and has no product dimension. This control total does not apply to a product subset.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so the 92 units are those booked in P4, not the returns on goods sold in P4.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), gross_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT region, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024_gross_incl_vat, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024_gross_incl_vat FROM gross_lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, before returns (the request asked for gross instead of the net default, so I followed it)
Each line carries its own VAT rate: 24% general rate in August 2024, 25.5% from 1 September 2024, reduced rates 14% and 10% unchanged; no flat rate applied
As-was regions: region taken from the dim_store version on the fact's store_key, valid on the transaction date (four regions plus Online in 2024)
Company date convention: store lines on sale_date, web lines on the Helsinki dispatch date (UTC converted to Europe/Helsinki)
Web orders counted only if delivered or collected
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own region, Online
Returns excluded (before returns)
assumptions: August and September 2024 are calendar months (1-31 August, 1-30 September 2024), not fiscal periods, because the figures are for a VAT filing
'Regions as they were at the time, as in the old reports' is an as-was request, so I used the pre-reorganisation regions (South, West, East, North). The Capital Region only exists from 28 April 2025
Web sales appear as a separate Online row because Online is its own region in the warehouse. Marjatta can drop that row if the filing covers stores only
Web sales are dated by dispatch, per the company definition. The brief did not ask for order-date timing
caveats: Online is dated by dispatch, not order date. Using order date would give August 173,402.41 and September 160,391.86 for Online. Orders placed late in August and dispatched in September carry the 24% rate set at order time. A web line therefore does not always have the VAT rate of the month it is reported in. If the VAT point of supply is the order date, the Online row should be re-cut.
Cancelled and still-processing web orders are excluded as non-sales. None appeared in the date range.
Store 999 and ZZ Test lines were removed. This changes the total only if those lines exist in the period.
No duplicate sales lines were found (sales_line_id and receipt_id with line_no are both unique). No days with zero trading were missing.

Check: net sales before returns by month (stores and web separately) reconcile exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales on the same definition (August stores 1,101,807.91, web 140,078.41; September stores 964,016.09, web 127,903.40).
Line VAT rates are consistent with product VAT class and date: 24% before 1 September 2024 and 25.5% from then on for standard-rated items.
The figures are before returns. Refunds including VAT are not netted off and would reduce the VAT base for the filing. They are not shown here.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-29' AS start_date, DATE '2026-08-02' AS end_date), weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_at_cost FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week, then averaged across weeks, never summed across weeks
Stock value is closing_value, at standard cost in EUR
Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 is 29 June to 2 August 2026, fiscal weeks 9 to 13, with weeks ending Sunday 5, 12, 19 and 26 July and 2 August
Physical stores only (store_id below 900): the web shop holds no stock in this table, and store 999 is excluded
Category ZZ Test is excluded from reporting (no Paint & Decorating test rows were present)
Product category as-is: each article's current dim_product version, per the management reporting default
Versioned dimensions joined on sku with is_current, so no rows multiply
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 3' means fiscal period P3 of that year (29 June to 2 August 2026). The request was received on 8 October 2026.

'Average stock' means the average of the five weekly closing stock values in the period, each summed over the whole chain. It is not the last week's closing and not the average of the opening and closing figures.
'Whole chain' means all physical stores (38 stores with Paint & Decorating stock in the period). The web shop is not included because it holds no store stock.
'Value at cost' is the standard cost value (closing_value) held in the warehouse, not the latest purchase price.
caveats: No correction was needed. fact_stock_week had no duplicate rows at the store, product and week grain for these five weeks, and no negative units were present.
P3 is fully loaded in the warehouse (fully_loaded = true).
The weekly chain totals were 341138.89, 341742.53, 344245.91, 349160.39 and 346046.42 EUR. The average of the five is 344466.83 EUR.
Paint & Decorating is the same category under the current and the historical product version for every row in the period, so as-is and as-was give the same figure.
The first week of the period had 2,699 store-article rows and the four later weeks had 2,674. This is a change in what stores range, not a data fault.
Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026. Its stock stays in the weekly snapshot and is included in the figure.
The figure is at standard cost, which is revalued each April. It will not match a valuation at actual purchase cost.
The control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply, because it covers net sales and not stock.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (5, 6, 7, 8) AND (f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales identified by channel_code = WB or channel_id in (2, 3) (Web home delivery or Click and collect)
Net sales excluding VAT from fact_sales_line
Last year interpreted as FY2025/26 (current fiscal year is FY2026/27)
assumptions: Last year means the most recent complete fiscal year (FY2025/26), not the prior calendar year
Web net sales comes from fact_sales_line.net_amount (excluding VAT), matching the column definition
caveats: Data quality issue: channel_code field transitions from populated (periods 5-6) to mixed/null (periods 7-8). Channel identification switched to channel_id during this period. Query corrected by using (channel_code = 'WB' OR channel_id IN (2, 3)) to capture all web sales consistently.
Period 7 has both channel_code and channel_id patterns in the data; the result combines both identification methods.

answer.sql: WITH contacted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure x JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = x.member_key WHERE x.campaign_id = 19), sales AS (SELECT sum(f.net_amount) AS net_sales_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key WHERE m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM contacted) AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-05-24'), refunds AS (SELECT coalesce(sum(r.refund_net), 0) AS refunds_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = r.member_key WHERE m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM contacted) AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-05-24') SELECT 19 AS campaign_id, 'Spring Garden Launch 2026' AS campaign_name, (SELECT count(*) FROM contacted) AS members_contacted, s.net_sales_before_returns - r.refunds_net AS net_spend_eur_ex_vat FROM sales s, refunds r
definitions_applied: Campaign identified as dim_campaign campaign_id 19, Spring Garden Launch 2026 (window 2026-05-04 to 2026-05-24)
Members counted by member_id (the stable loyalty number), not member_key, because a member has one row per version
Contacted = member has at least one row in fact_campaign_exposure for the campaign (one row per contact made); holdout members have none
Member spend matched through member_id across all member versions, in all channels (store, web home delivery, click and collect)
Spend is net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after line discounts, less refund_net on returns booked in the window (company net sales definition, as in rpt_daily_store_sales)
Dates are sale_date and return_date inclusive of 4 and 24 May 2026 (FY2026/27 P01, fully loaded)
assumptions: 'Contacted' means a contact was made, whether or not it was delivered; a count of members with at least one delivered contact is given in the caveats
'Spend' is read as net sales excluding VAT and net of refunds, in EUR, matching the company's net sales definition
Staff purchases are included (flagged lines are 117 lines, EUR 2,540.79 net)
Guest web orders (no member_key) cannot be attributed to a member and are excluded
Returns are counted when booked in the window, even if the original sale was earlier
4 to 24 May is read as inclusive of both days, matching the campaign window
caveats: Member versions: dim_member has several versions per member, so 15,063 member_keys in the exposure table are 15,001 distinct members. Joining spend on member_key only would miss purchases booked under a different version, so everything is matched on member_id.
rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used. Web lines carry a NULL channel_code, so those views leave web out. fact_sales_line was queried directly.
Delivery: 14,814 of the 15,001 members had at least one delivered contact. 187 members had only undelivered contacts. They are counted as contacted but would drop out of a delivered-only count.
Holdout: the 1,597 held-out members (matches dim_campaign.holdout_size) are not among the contacted members; none appears in the exposure table.

Spend basis: net sales before returns were EUR 191,576.08 (8,142 lines, 2,626 buying members) and refunds booked in the window were EUR 8,231.32, giving EUR 183,344.76. Gross spend including VAT before returns was EUR 239,917.96. Say if a different basis is wanted.
Not all of the 15,001 contacted members bought in the window; 2,626 did.
This is spend by contacted members, not spend caused by the campaign. Nothing here compares them with the holdout, and the holdout is the right comparison for any uplift claim.

answer.sql: WITH lfl AS (SELECT store_id FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900 AND close_date IS NULL AND (open_date IS NULL OR open_date <= DATE '2024-07-28')), sales AS (SELECT store_id, sum(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-03' AND DATE '2026-08-30' THEN net_sales END) AS this_year, sum(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-28' AND DATE '2025-08-24' THEN net_sales END) AS last_year FROM rpt_daily_store_sales WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-28' AND DATE '2026-08-30' GROUP BY store_id) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, round((sum(this_year) / sum(last_year) - 1) * 100, 2) AS lfl_net_sales_growth_pct FROM sales JOIN lfl USING (store_id)
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 4 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2026/27 P04 (2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30) against FY2025/26 P04 (2025-07-28 to 2025-08-24), both 4 weeks, compared week for week
Like-for-like store set: physical stores only (store_id below 900), open for at least 12 months before the start of the comparison-year period, trading in both periods, not closed
Net sales: rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales, which is EUR excluding VAT after returns (returns booked on the return date)
Web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Stores identified by store_id, not store_key, so store versions and the April 2025 region re-mapping do not affect the result
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' means FY2026/27 P04 and 'last year' means FY2025/26 P04, because the request was received 2026-10-05, and P04 is fully loaded in both years

Like for like needs a store open at least 12 months before the start of the prior-year period (open on or before 2024-07-28). The warehouse gives no formal definition, and this matches the 2025 store list left in the warehouse (tmp_lfl_store_list_2025), apart from Savonlinna
Net sales are measured after returns and include staff purchases, as in the Data & Analytics daily report. Staff purchases are about 2% of store sales
The result is a single growth figure for the whole like-for-like store group, since no breakdown by store or region was requested
Store 125 Kuopio was kept in the set. Its 6-week refit ended 2026-07-26, a week before P04 began, so it traded all 28 days of both periods
caveats: 36 stores are in the like-for-like set. Savonlinna (129) is excluded because it closed on 2026-01-25 and had no sales in this year's P04. Tampere Lamminpää (136, opened 2024-09-02) and Lohja (137, opened 2024-11-04) are excluded because they had been open less than 12 months at the start of last year's P04 and were still ramping up
Excluding Kuopio (125), which has just come back from a refit and may be getting a reopening lift, the figure is -0.41% rather than -0.23%. The reported figure keeps it in
Like-for-like net sales were about EUR 967.7k this year against EUR 970.0k last year, effectively flat. The figure is a slight decline
The web shop (900) is not included. The rpt_daily_store_sales and fact_sales_line totals reconcile to the cent for every store, and no duplicate lines were found in either period

This year's P04 starts on 2026-08-03 and last year's on 2025-07-28 because of the 53-week fiscal calendar. The periods were compared on fiscal weeks, not calendar dates, so the calendar dates shift by 6 days
The tmp_lfl_store_list_2024 and tmp_lfl_store_list_2025 tables in the warehouse were not used. They are undocumented working tables, and the 2025 list still includes closed Savonlinna
FY2026/27 P06 is not fully loaded in the warehouse. It does not affect this P04 answer

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, 'Garden Furniture' AS subcategory, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line AS r JOIN dim_product AS p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN ref_fiscal_calendar AS d ON d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 WHERE p.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND r.return_date BETWEEN d.period_start_date AND d.period_end_date GROUP BY d.fiscal_year
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 = 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30 (4 weeks, ref_fiscal_calendar; matches dim_date)
Garden Furniture = dim_product subcategory 'Garden Furniture' (category Garden)
Returned units = SUM(quantity_returned) on fact_return_line, dated by return_date
Product version taken from the return line's product_key (version at the return date)
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as the request date is 2026-10-05 and that year started 2026-06-29. Period 4 is the one that ended 2026-08-30, and it is fully loaded.
'Period' means the company's 4-4-5 style fiscal period, not a calendar month or a quarter.
'Handed back and booked as returned' means units on booked return lines, counted by the date of the return, not the date of the original sale.
Web returns are included. Of the 92 units, 34 were booked at the web shop and 58 at physical stores. Both are booked returns, and the request did not limit the channel.
All return reason codes are included (changed mind, defective, damaged in transit, not as described, wrong size or fit). The request did not exclude any.
Only the fact tables were used. The staging, backup and tmp tables were ignored.
caveats: No correction to the figure was needed. I checked for duplicate return lines (none), the staging return table (all 141 rows are already in the fact table, so nothing is double-counted), orphan product keys (none), return lines with no matching sale (none), returns dated before the sale (none), returns larger than the quantity sold (none), and return timestamps that fall on a different date than return_date (none).

Garden Furniture has no category or subcategory changes across its product versions. The October 2025 move of Outdoor Lighting from Garden to Electrical does not affect it. The figure is the same whether the product version at the return date or the current version is used.
All 92 units come from 92 separate return lines (one unit per line). The units are 37 changed mind, 20 defective, 14 not as described, 14 wrong size or fit and 7 damaged in transit.
Of the 34 web-shop units, the originating web orders include some collected via click-and-collect. I did not separate these from home delivery. If you want in-store returns only, the figure is 58.

The sales lines carry channel_id and a null channel_code for recent data, so I did not use channel_code to split web from store. The store/web split above comes from the return line's store (the web shop is a pseudo-location).

answer.sql:
WITH period_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    w.fulfilment_type,
    SUM(w.order_total_gross) as sales
  FROM fact_web_order w
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON DATE(w.order_ts_utc) = d.calendar_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    AND d.fiscal_period IN (6, 7, 8)
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, w.fulfilment_type
),
period_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    fiscal_year,
    fiscal_period,
    SUM(sales) as total_sales
  FROM period_sales
  GROUP BY fiscal_year, fiscal_period
)
SELECT 
  ps.fiscal_period as period,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN ps.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN ps.sales ELSE 0 END) / pt.total_sales, 2) as click_and_collect_share_pct
FROM period_sales ps
INNER JOIN period_totals pt ON ps.fiscal_year = pt.fiscal_year AND ps.fiscal_period = pt.fiscal_period
GROUP BY ps.fiscal_period, pt.total_sales
ORDER BY ps.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web shop sales measured from fact_web_order using order_total_gross (EUR including VAT)
Fulfilment types: click_and_collect vs home_delivery
Fiscal periods: periods 6, 7, 8 within FY2025/26
Share calculated as click_and_collect sales divided by total web shop sales per period
assumptions: Last year refers to fiscal year FY2025/26 (the most recent complete fiscal year before current FY2026/27)
Web shop sales defined as all orders recorded in fact_web_order table regardless of status
Order timestamp used to assign order to fiscal period
All orders are at web channel (fulfilment_type values apply only to web orders)
caveats: No data quality issues detected in web order records for the requested periods
Shares are calculated on order value (gross amount including VAT), not order count

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 107 AND p.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY ALL
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 = 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27 (4 weeks, fully loaded) per ref_fiscal_calendar
Store identified by stable store_id 107 via dim_store, not by store_key
Product group taken from dim_product.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products', joined on the product_key version in force at the sale date
Units sold = sum of fact_sales_line.quantity
Store channel only (channel_id 1, 'Store'); web and click-and-collect lines are booked to other locations and are not in Hyvinkää's lines
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as of the request date 2026-10-05 (the fiscal year starts 2026-05-04). 'Period 5' is read as fiscal period 5, not calendar month 5.
'Cleaning Products' means the subcategory of that name, not the whole category 'Cleaning & Household'. If the whole category was meant, the figure is 221 units.
'Units sold' is the gross quantity on sales lines. No returns of Cleaning Products were booked at Hyvinkää in the period, so net and gross are the same.
Staff purchases are included (2 lines, 4 units, flagged staff_purchase_flag = true) because they are units sold and the daily store sales report includes them. Excluding them gives 132.
caveats: No correction to the figure was needed. The store's daily line totals match rpt_daily_store_sales for every day of the period, there are no duplicate receipt lines, there are no unloaded rows in the staging table, and Hyvinkää had no planned closure and trading every day.
Hyvinkää is listed with format 'Medium', which is not one of the three formats the column comment gives (Hyper, Standard, Express). This does not affect the answer.

dim_product has 65 Outdoor Lighting SKUs with two versions that disagree on category (Electrical vs Garden). This does not touch Cleaning Products, but anyone counting that subcategory by category will get inconsistent results.
The channel_code column is null on these lines, although the comment says ST or WB. Channel was taken from channel_id (1 = Store) instead, so the figure is unaffected.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or channel_id
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Click-and-collect counted as web, with the dispatch date as the ready-for-collection date
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: fiscal_year and fiscal_period
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' was read as FY2025/26. The request was received on 9 October 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests in May 2026 read 'last year' as FY2025/26 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).

FY2025/26 P5 to P8 run 25 Aug 2025 to 21 Dec 2025: P5 25 Aug to 21 Sep (4 weeks), P6 22 Sep to 26 Oct (5 weeks), P7 27 Oct to 23 Nov (4 weeks), P8 24 Nov to 21 Dec (4 weeks). Week 53 is not in this range.
'Periods 5 to 8' means one row per period, in the same way that other period requests were returned by period.
Online and the web shop are the same thing here, so only store 900 is included.
Regions and categories are not involved, so the as-is versus as-was question does not arise.
caveats: Correction: one test-article web line (ZZ Test, net EUR 5.50, P6) was removed under the standing ZZ Test rule. It changes P6 by EUR 5.50.
Web sales are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date. Orders placed near a period boundary fall into the period of their dispatch.

Net sales are after returns, with each refund booked to the period of its return date. The sales and refund amounts by period were: P5 158717.41 and 13090.51, P6 193190.55 and 17601.93, P7 167120.98 and 12143.71, P8 243086.38 and 17821.30. They are not shown in the table.
The totals match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in all four periods: net sales before returns, returns and net sales all agree.

The web platform migrated on 3 November 2025, inside P7. channel_code is empty after that date, so web was taken from store_id 900 and not from channel_code. rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it drops web sales from that date.
P6 is a 5-week period and the other three have 4 weeks, so P6 is not directly comparable to them without adjusting for weeks.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT. The request did not ask for VAT-inclusive figures.
The warehouse checks showed one row per receipt line (receipt_id, line_no) and no duplicated lines on web orders.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: FY2026/27 period 5 from ref_fiscal_calendar and dim_date: 31 August 2026 to 27 September 2026, fully loaded
Units sold: the quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date, as in the weeks-of-cover definition
Pitäjänmäki is store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), matched on the store_key on the sales line
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Products grouped by the stable sku, with the name from the current product version
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 5 of FY26/27' means fiscal year FY2026/27, fiscal period 5 (the last complete period).

'Sold the most units' means units sold at the till. Units returned afterwards are not deducted, because the company definition of units sold is the sales-line quantity. The request did not ask for net-of-returns units.
Staff purchases are included, as they are in the company's sales definitions. Excluding them would take 2 units off the third product (40 instead of 42) and would not change the top three.
Products are ranked by article (sku), not by product version. Only physical store 102 sales are counted, so there are no web lines.
caveats: No data problem found that needed correcting. Store 102 total units for the period (3,740, from 2,121 sales lines) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly. The 28 days have no duplicate sales_line_ids.
The gap to fourth place is wide (42 units against 30), so the top three do not depend on tie-breaks or on the staff-purchase and returns choices above.
Pitäjänmäki moved from the South region to the Capital Region on 28 April 2025. This does not affect a single-store, single-period answer.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(f.sale_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Including VAT: sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, each line at its own VAT rate (no flat rate applied to net)
Before returns: no refunds deducted (fact_return_line not used)
Staff purchases included
Store sales dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Control total: net_sales_before_returns in rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: August 2024 and September 2024 are calendar months (1-31 August, 1-30 September 2024), as the request names the months, not fiscal periods.
Store sales means the physical stores only. The web shop is not included, since a company total was not asked for.
Staff purchases stay in, as in company net sales, because the request did not ask to remove them.
Figures are in EUR including VAT, with no returns taken off.
Store and product hierarchy does not affect the figures, so as-is versus as-was does not apply.
caveats: VAT rate change: the general rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. The data carries this correctly (August standard-rate lines at 24%, September at 25.5%; reduced rates of 14% and 10% unchanged), and gross_amount was summed from the lines. The September figure includes the higher rate, so it is not directly comparable with August on a VAT-inclusive basis.
Store 999 and ZZ Test lines were left out. They are small: store 999 and test lines came to about 4,282 incl. VAT in August and 3,352 in September. The web shop's lines were also excluded.

Control check: the same lines on a net (excluding VAT) basis match rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns exactly, store by store and day by day (1,101,807.91 for August and 964,016.09 for September, with no differences in net amount or receipt count). No duplicate sales lines were found. The VAT-inclusive figures themselves have no control table.

The monthly figures are not directly comparable: August has 37 stores trading and September 38, and September is one day shorter, so September is about 11.4% lower despite the higher VAT rate. This was not investigated further.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, s.format AS store_format, COUNT(DISTINCT s.store_id) AS stores, COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id) AS receipts, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 3
definitions_applied: ATV: net sales before returns (excluding VAT) divided by distinct sales receipts, dated by sale_date
ATV is a store measure: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop (store 900) left out
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2026/27 P4 = weeks 14 to 17, 3 to 30 August 2026
Store format taken from the version valid on the sale date (format is the same in every store version, so as-is and as-was agree)
Control total against rpt_daily_store_sales (receipts and net_sales_before_returns, store by store)
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (request dated 6 October 2026), and 'period 4' as fiscal period 4 of that year, which is complete (ended 30 August 2026)
Breakdown is one row per store format, as requested; no chain total row added
ATV is shown in EUR excluding VAT, rounded to 2 decimals
Formats filtered by what the data holds (Small, Medium, Large), not by the out-of-date column comment (Hyper, Standard, Express)
caveats: The dim_store.format column comment is out of date. The real values in the stores are Small, Medium and Large, and the format column also holds Web and Training for the web shop and store 999. I did not filter on the comment's values.
No store was closed or in a refit during P4 (3 to 30 August 2026), so all 38 physical stores are included for the full period (8 Large, 18 Medium, 12 Small).

Checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for 3 to 30 August 2026: receipt counts and net sales before returns match for every store and every trading day once store 999 and ZZ Test are excluded. No correction was needed.

No problems found in the source rows for the period: no duplicate sales lines, no receipts spanning more than one store, no receipts mixing staff and non-staff lines, and no receipts with a non-positive net value.
ATV is calculated after removing staff-purchase receipts, so it will not tie to rpt_daily_store_sales net sales; the control check was done on the figures including staff receipts.

answer.sql: WITH signup AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from, member_key) AS version_no FROM dim_member) SELECT s.home_store_id AS store_id, d.store_name, count(*) AS new_members FROM signup s JOIN (SELECT store_id, store_name FROM dim_store WHERE is_current) d ON d.store_id = s.home_store_id WHERE s.version_no = 1 AND s.join_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: New member = a distinct loyalty number (member_id), counted once however many dim_member versions it has
Sign-up date = join_date
Sign-up store = home_store_id on the member's first dim_member version (earliest valid_from), not the current version
Online sign-ups = home_store_id 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop), shown as its own row
Store names taken from the current dim_store version
assumptions: 'Last year' read as calendar year 2025 (1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025), since the request came on 7 Oct 2026 and is from Marketing/CRM. If a fiscal year was meant, FY2025/26 runs 28 Apr 2025 to 3 May 2026 and the counts would differ.

A member's 'store' is the home store recorded when they signed up. The warehouse has no separate sign-up store field, so this is the home store on the first version, which starts on the join date for every member.
Online sign-ups are home_store_id 900, as the column comment states, and they appear as one row labelled Tuomimetsä web shop.
Stores with no sign-ups in 2025 are not listed. All 39 physical stores and the web shop had sign-ups, so none are missing.
caveats: dim_member holds one row per member version (89,314 rows for 60,000 members), so counting rows would overstate sign-ups by about 50%. I counted distinct member_id on the first version only.

Using the current home store would give wrong store figures. In 2025, 1,017 of the 4,975 members who signed up at a physical store have since changed home store. Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 Jan 2026 and none of its 152 members from 2025 still show it as their home store, so it would have shown zero. I attributed members to the store they joined.
Savonlinna (129) is a closed store and still appears in the table with 152 sign-ups, because they happened while it was open.
The 40-row total is 14,788 new members in 2025, of which 2,877 (about 19%) were online. No total row is given in the table because it wasn't requested.

No sign-up store field exists. If a member's first recorded home store was not where they signed up (for example, a data-entry default), the store attribution could be slightly off. I could not check this against the sales data in the query budget.

answer.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date AS d0, period_end_date AS d1 FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period = 2), sales AS (SELECT s.store_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN p ON f.sale_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1 WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY s.store_id), refunds AS (SELECT s.store_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN p ON r.return_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1 WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY s.store_id), names AS (SELECT store_id, store_name FROM dim_store WHERE is_current) SELECT p.fiscal_year, p.fiscal_period, rank() OVER (ORDER BY round(sales.amt - coalesce(refunds.amt, 0), 2) DESC) AS rank, sales.store_id, names.store_name, round(sales.amt - coalesce(refunds.amt, 0), 2) AS net_sales FROM sales CROSS JOIN p LEFT JOIN refunds USING (store_id) JOIN names USING (store_id) ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 2 of FY2026/27 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar: Monday 1 June to Sunday 28 June 2026 (4 weeks)
Net sales = line net sales (excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refunds booked in the period (excluding VAT), the same definition as rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales
Refunds are counted on the date the return was booked, not the date of the original sale
Stores identified by store_id through the store_key version in effect on the sale or return date; names taken from the current store version
Only physical stores counted (store_id below 900): web shop 900 and Training store 999 excluded
Rank 1 = highest net sales
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' means fiscal period 2 of the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (the request is dated 9 Oct 2026 and the fiscal year began 4 May 2026). The calendar-year reading gives the same dates.
'Store league table' means stores ranked by net sales for the period, highest first
Staff purchases are included in net sales, as in the team's daily store sales report
Total net sales for the period was used as the ranking basis, with no adjustment for store size or trading days
Savonlinna (store 129, closed 25 Jan 2026) has no sales in the period and is not listed
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a planned refit from 15 June 2026 to 26 July 2026 and traded only 14 of the 26 trading days in the period. Its rank of 24 is not comparable with the other stores, which traded all 26 days. It would rank higher over a full period.

Web shop (900) and Training store (999) are excluded: they are not stores. The web shop's 230,731 net sales would otherwise top the table. The Training store had 2,381 of sales, nearly all staff purchases.
Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (19 and 20 June) are non-trading days, so all stores have 26 trading days rather than 28. This affects every store equally.

Checks found no data problems in this period: no duplicate sales or return lines, no staging rows missing from the fact tables, no returns without a matching sale, and store-level totals tie exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales.

Store versions changed on 28 April 2025, when several stores moved to the Capital Region and Kouvola moved to South. This does not affect the period 2 figures because stores are grouped by store_id, but regional views would differ if built on the old versions.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected orders count
Whole company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: last completed fiscal period
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: The warehouse has no definition of 'month'. I read 'last month' as the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, 4 weeks), because the company reports in fiscal periods. Past requests read 'last four weeks' as the last period, and the fiscal-calendar skill says to filter on fiscal columns rather than calendar months.
Whole company means all physical stores plus the web shop, so web is included.
The figure is net of returns, in EUR excluding VAT, with returns booked on their return date.
caveats: If you meant calendar September 2026 (1 to 30 Sep), the same definition gives 1179035.98 EUR. P05 ends on 27 September, so the two differ by the last 3 days of September plus the 31 Aug to 31 Aug start day included in P05 only. Tell me if you want the calendar month instead.
Correction: store 999 (2690.92 EUR of sales in the period) and one ZZ Test line outside store 999 (6.00 EUR) were removed, as the company definition requires.

Correction: web revenue is dated by Helsinki dispatch date, not order date, and the do-not-use view rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it omits web sales from 3 Nov 2025. Web contributed 177237.33 EUR of the total.
The result matches the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for the same days exactly (1109546.52 EUR, web 177237.33 EUR). I found no duplicate sales, return or web order keys in the period.

The period is fully loaded (warehouse loaded through 4 Oct 2026). Returns on goods sold in P05 can still arrive for up to 30 days, but they reduce net sales in the period they are booked, so P05 itself will not change for returns yet to come on its own dates only if those dates fall inside P05.
On 31 Aug 37 of the 38 stores reported sales in the control table; I did not investigate the missing store (a refit or closure is likely), and the total is as the warehouse records it.

answer.sql:
WITH period_dates AS (
  SELECT period_start_date, period_end_date
  FROM ref_fiscal_calendar
  WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period = 2
),
sales_in_period AS (
  SELECT 
    fsl.sales_line_id,
    fsl.net_amount,
    ds.format
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key
  INNER JOIN period_dates pd ON fsl.sale_date BETWEEN pd.period_start_date AND pd.period_end_date
),
sales_by_format AS (
  SELECT 
    format,
    SUM(net_amount) as total_sales_net
  FROM sales_in_period
  GROUP BY format
),
returns_by_format AS (
  SELECT 
    sip.format,
    SUM(frl.refund_net) as total_refunds_net
  FROM fact_return_line frl
  INNER JOIN sales_in_period sip ON frl.sales_line_id = sip.sales_line_id
  GROUP BY sip.format
)
SELECT 
  sbf.format,
  CASE 
    WHEN sbf.total_sales_net > 0 
    THEN ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(rbf.total_refunds_net, 0) / sbf.total_sales_net, 2)
    ELSE 0
  END as return_share_pct
FROM sales_by_format sbf
LEFT JOIN returns_by_format rbf ON sbf.format = rbf.format
ORDER BY sbf.format
definitions_applied: Net amounts used for both sales and returns (excluding VAT, after discounts)
Return share calculated as total refund net amount divided by total sales net amount
Returns tracked back to their original sales line to determine store format at sale point
assumptions: Last year interpreted as FY2025/26, the most recent complete fiscal year
Period 2 interpreted as fiscal period 2 (P02), not calendar period
Share interpreted as return rate: percentage of sales value that was refunded
Returns linked to sales by sales_line_id to ensure we count returns from P02 sales regardless of return date
Store format determined by the store where the original sale occurred
caveats: Store format values in warehouse (Large, Medium, Small, Training, Web) do not match schema documentation which specifies Hyper, Standard, Express
Training format has zero returns despite sales activity; this may reflect operational policy or sample size (56 receipts)
Web format shows significantly higher return rate (12.23%) compared to physical stores (4.28-4.53%), which should be verified with business owners
Return data relies on sales_line_id matching; any orphaned return lines would not be included

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT p.sku, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net, sum(f.standard_cost) AS sales_cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-27' AND DATE '2025-04-27' AND s.region = 'South' GROUP BY p.sku), returned AS (SELECT p.sku, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net, sum(r.standard_cost_returned) AS refund_cost FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-27' AND DATE '2025-04-27' AND s.region = 'South' GROUP BY p.sku), names AS (SELECT sku, max(product_name) AS product_name FROM dim_product GROUP BY sku) SELECT sold.sku, names.product_name, round(sold.sales_net - coalesce(returned.refund_net, 0) - (sold.sales_cost - coalesce(returned.refund_cost, 0)), 2) AS gross_margin_eur FROM sold JOIN names USING (sku) LEFT JOIN returned USING (sku) ORDER BY gross_margin_eur DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: Q4 of FY2024/25 is fiscal periods 10-12, 2025-01-27 to 2025-04-27 (ref_fiscal_calendar, fully loaded)
Gross margin = net sales excluding VAT minus standard cost of units sold, after deducting returns (refund_net less standard_cost_returned)
Store versions as at the transaction date (fact store_key joined to dim_store), so a store's region is the one it had when the sale or return happened
Products grouped by SKU across product versions (dim_product.sku, not product_key)
Return side counted by return date and the store where the return was booked, as in rpt_daily_store_sales (net sales = sales before returns minus returns)
Web shop (900) and Training store (999) are not in the South region
assumptions: Gross margin is a EUR amount (net sales less standard cost, net of returns), not a percentage; ranking is by EUR margin
South means the region as it stood during Q4 FY24/25: stores 101-113 and Lohja (137, opened 2024-11-04). Kouvola (114) was East then, so it is excluded
Staff purchases are included, matching rpt_daily_store_sales, which includes them. Excluding them gives the same top 10 in the same order, with small changes to a few values
Standard cost is used as the cost of goods, since the warehouse carries no actual cost
Online sales are not attributed to South, even for click-and-collect orders
caveats: Regions were redrawn on 2025-04-28, the day after the quarter ended. Stores 101-105 (Helsinki Vuosaari, Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, Espoo Lommila, Vantaa Tammisto, Kerava) moved from South to a new Capital Region, and Kouvola moved from East to South. Joining on the current dim_store row would give a different South (the 5 capital-area stores out, Kouvola in) and a different top 10. In that version SKU 101888 enters the top 10, 101369 drops out, and the values fall to 2927 for the top product against 3867. I used the region as it was at the time. Say if you want the current structure restated back over the quarter

The warehouse has several backup, staging and temp tables (bak_*, stg_*, dim_*_old, tmp_*) and the rpt schema views. I did not use any of them. The staging tables hold only October 2026 loads and no Q4 rows

I checked for duplicate sales or return lines, orphan returns, standard cost not matching quantity times the unit cost, and product or store version mismatches in this quarter's South data. I found none. The sales and returns lines reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales for every South store
The dim_store.format comment says Hyper/Standard/Express but the data holds Small/Medium/Large, and the dim_member.home_store_id comment is unrelated. Neither affects this answer
Standard unit costs are revalued each April. Since the quarter ends 27 April, the cost carried on each line is the standard cost version in force on the sale date
Margins are at standard cost, not actual purchase cost, so they can differ from the finance gross margin

answer.sql: WITH cur AS (SELECT store_id, region FROM dim_store WHERE is_current), sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN 'Web shop' ELSE c.region END AS line, f.net_amount AS amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN cur c ON c.store_id = s.store_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25','FY2025/26') AND s.store_id <> 999), refunds AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, CASE WHEN orig_store.store_id = 900 THEN 'Web shop' ELSE c.region END AS line, -r.refund_net AS amount FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN cur c ON c.store_id = s.store_id JOIN fact_sales_line o ON o.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_store orig_store ON orig_store.store_key = o.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25','FY2025/26') AND s.store_id <> 999), allrows AS (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM refunds), agg AS (SELECT line AS region, round(sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year='FY2025/26' THEN amount END),2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26, round(sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year='FY2024/25' THEN amount END),2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25 FROM allrows GROUP BY line) SELECT region, net_sales_fy2025_26, net_sales_fy2024_25, round(100.0*(net_sales_fy2025_26/net_sales_fy2024_25 - 1),1) AS growth_pct FROM agg ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: Q3 = fiscal periods 7 to 9 (FY2025/26 Q3: 2025-10-27 to 2026-01-25; FY2024/25 Q3: 2024-10-28 to 2025-01-26), both 13 weeks
Net sales = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net, by sale date and return date
Region taken from the current store version (dim_store.is_current), applied to both years
Web shop = store 900, covering home delivery and click-and-collect, shown as its own line outside the regions
Training store 999 excluded
Channel identified by store 900 and channel_id, not by channel_code (null after the web-platform migration)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (today is 2026-10-06, in FY2026/27), so Q3 is Oct 2025 to Jan 2026; 'the year before' is FY2024/25 Q3

Regions restated to today's structure for both years: the 28 April 2025 change created the Capital Region (five stores moved from South) and moved Kouvola from East to South, so the earlier year is comparable
Staff purchases are included, as in the Data & Analytics report table rpt_daily_store_sales, which I reconciled to for stores
Refunds of web-sold lines are charged to the web line, including those booked at a store; other refunds go to the region of the store that booked them, on the return date
Growth percentage = FY2025/26 divided by FY2024/25, minus 1, in percent, rounded to one decimal
Cancelled and processing web orders: none appear in the quarters, so nothing was excluded
caveats: Region restatement: on the warehouse's own stored regions, the earlier year would show Capital Region stores under South and Kouvola under East; I restated using current regions via store_id. A naive join on store_key gives wrong regional growth.
Channel code change: from 2025-11-03 channel_code is null and channel_id (1, 2, 3) is used instead; a filter on channel_code = 'WB' misses most web lines in FY2025/26. I identified web by store 900.
Training store 999 had about 6.5k EUR (FY2024/25) and 6.9k EUR (FY2025/26) of mostly staff-flagged sales in the quarter. These were excluded.

Web growth of 28.0% is boosted by click-and-collect: in FY2024/25 it was inside the old WB code, and in FY2025/26 it is channel_id 3 (about 139.6k EUR sales before refunds). Both years are included, so the comparison is like for like, but the web line is not a pure home-delivery figure.

Not like-for-like store growth: Tampere Lamminpää (136, opened 2024-09-02) and Lohja (137, opened 2024-11-04) were open for only part of, or all of, FY2024/25 Q3, so they lift West and South growth. Savonlinna (129, East) closed on 2026-01-25, the last day of FY2025/26 Q3, so East includes it in both years. No refit closures overlap either quarter.

The web line differs from rpt_daily_store_sales (about 2.7k EUR higher in the report for FY2024/25 sales before returns, 3.4k lower for FY2025/26), probably because of the date boundary between UTC and local time.
