'Units sold' is read as units on sales lines (quantity), before returns, as in the company definition of units sold used for weeks of cover and in rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold.
Staff purchases are included, as the units-sold definition does not exclude them (none appeared on this SKU in the week).
The figure covers store 131 only, with no web sales; web is store 900 and was not requested.
caveats: The request pairs the SKU with 'Oulu Kaakkuri', which is a store name. I treated it as a store-level request. If the question was meant for the whole company or for a product with that name, the figure would differ; no product named 'Oulu Kaakkuri' exists.

4 units of this SKU were returned at store 131 in the same week (return date 28 September to 4 October). Net of those returns the figure would be 13. I report 17 because the request asks for units sold.

No sales of this SKU in store 131 on Wednesday 30 September, which is consistent with a low-volume item (daily lines are sparse in the preceding weeks as well). The store's total units for that day match rpt_daily_store_sales (97), so it is not a load gap.

No data problem required correction: no duplicate lines were found (sales_line_id and receipt_id plus line_no are unique in the week), and the store's daily units and net sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales on all 7 days.

answer.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date AS p_start, period_end_date AS p_end FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period = 2), stores AS (SELECT store_id, max(CASE WHEN is_current THEN store_name END) AS store_name FROM dim_store WHERE store_id < 900 GROUP BY store_id), sales AS (SELECT s.store_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN per ON f.sale_date BETWEEN per.p_start AND per.p_end WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY s.store_id), refunds AS (SELECT s.store_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS refunds_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN per ON r.return_date BETWEEN per.p_start AND per.p_end WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY s.store_id), trading AS (SELECT st.store_id, count(*) AS trading_days FROM stores st JOIN per ON true JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date BETWEEN per.p_start AND per.p_end AND d.is_trading_day WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY st.store_id), agg AS (SELECT per.fiscal_year, per.fiscal_period, st.store_id, st.store_name, round(sa.sales_net - coalesce(rf.refunds_net, 0), 2) AS net_sales, round((sa.sales_net - coalesce(rf.refunds_net, 0)) / tr.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM stores st JOIN sales sa ON sa.store_id = st.store_id LEFT JOIN refunds rf ON rf.store_id = st.store_id JOIN trading tr ON tr.store_id = st.store_id CROSS JOIN per) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY net_sales_per_trading_day DESC) AS rank, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, store_id, store_name, net_sales, net_sales_per_trading_day FROM agg ORDER BY rank, store_id
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount (excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns booked in the period, the same definition as rpt_daily_store_sales
Fiscal period from ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2026/27 P02 = 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-28 (4 weeks, fully loaded)
Stores identified by store_id (stable across dim_store versions), with the current store_name
Physical stores only: web shop (900) and the head-office training location (999) are not stores and are excluded
Trading days from dim_date.is_trading_day (Midsummer Eve and Day, 19-20 June, are closed), minus the dates of planned refit closures in ref_store_closure
Returns are attributed to the store where the return was booked, on the return date
assumptions: 'This year' is read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (request dated 2026-10-07), so period 2 is 1-28 June 2026, not the calendar year or the prior fiscal year
'Ranking' means store net sales in EUR excluding VAT, after returns, highest first

Staff purchases are included in net sales, as in the maintained daily store report (rpt_daily_store_sales). Excluding them would shift individual figures slightly (for example Tampere Lamminpää by about 254 EUR) but would not change the top of the ranking

Because Kuopio was closed for part of the period, stores are ranked on net sales per trading day. The 37 stores that traded the whole period all had 26 trading days, so their order is the same as on total net sales
The net_sales column shows the actual period total for every store, including Kuopio's part-period figure
caveats: Correction for Kuopio (store 125): the store was closed for a refit from 2026-06-15, with no sales after 14 June, so it traded only 14 of the 26 trading days. On total net sales (23993.71 EUR) it would rank 24th. Per trading day (1713.84 EUR) it ranks 7th. I ranked on the per-day figure. If you want a ranking on plain period totals, move Kuopio to 24th. Ranks 8 to 24 for the other stores then move up one place.
The closure runs to 2026-07-26, so Kuopio will be short in period 3 as well.
Excluded the web shop (900, 253566.50 EUR gross of returns) and the Training pseudo-location (999, 2381.03 EUR, almost all staff purchases) because they are not stores. They are not in the ranking.

Staff purchases (about 1 percent of store net sales in the period) are left in the figures. Tampere Lamminpää (136) has the largest staff share, about 254 EUR. If Finance excludes staff sales from store rankings, tell me and I will rerun.

The ranking is on absolute sales, so store size drives it. Format and sqm are not normalised, and the warehouse format labels (Large, Medium, Small) differ from the schema comment (Hyper, Standard, Express).
Store 129 Savonlinna closed on 2026-01-25 and has no sales in the period, so it is not listed.
Period 2 is fully loaded. The query also checked for duplicate sales lines and found none. The totals reconcile exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales (excl. VAT) minus standard cost, both after returns; returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned
Returns reduce net sales and margin on their own return date, in the store where they were processed
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered/collected orders only); none fall in South, since the web shop is store 900 / Online
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Regions as-is: current dim_store version, so South = stores 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 113, 114 and 137
Products grouped by sku and named from the current dim_product version
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25 Q4 = periods 10 to 12, 27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025 (13 weeks)
Staff purchases included in net sales and margin
Control total: South store-level net sales before returns, returns and net sales agree with rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent for all 10 stores over the same days
assumptions: 'Q4 of FY24/25' is read as fiscal year FY2024/25 (the year starting 29 April 2024), the fiscal year as written in the request, not a calendar quarter

'South region' read as-is, the management-reporting default, so Kouvola (114) is in South for the whole quarter and the five stores that moved to the Capital Region on 28 April 2025 (101 to 105) are not
'Product' read as article (sku), not product version, subcategory or brand
Ranked by absolute gross margin in EUR, not margin percentage
Margin figures are in EUR excluding VAT
caveats: Region basis changes the answer: the South region was redefined on 28 April 2025, the day after this quarter ended. As-was, South would include stores 101 to 105 and exclude Kouvola (114). I used the as-is current South; the as-was list was not computed.
The 10th place margin (978.84) is well clear of 11th place (Smart Home Tuulikki 855, 935.46), so the cut-off is not a tie.

No data defects were found in this range. There were no duplicate sales or return lines, no null or non-positive costs, and line costs match quantity times the dim_product standard cost. All sales lines join to a current product version.
Margin uses standard cost, not actual purchase cost, so it is a standard-cost margin.

Returns are booked where processed and on the return date, so some refunds in the quarter may relate to sales made before 27 Jan 2025, and returns on sales from late in the quarter can arrive after 27 Apr 2025 and are not included.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS this_year_net_sales, ly.net_sales AS last_year_net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900) as one figure, no regional or channel split
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only); cancelled and processing orders excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: weeks run Monday to Sunday; period 2 is fiscal weeks 5 to 8
Same fiscal week compared with the same fiscal week last year, not the same calendar dates
Growth = this year / last year - 1, in percent
Control total: weekly net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales and agree to the cent in all 8 weeks
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, channel_code, stg_, bak_, tmp_ tables) not used
assumptions: 'This year' is FY2026/27, the current fiscal year on 5 October 2026, so period 2 is 1 to 28 June 2026 (weeks 5 to 8)
'Last year' is FY2025/26 (the reading used for requests made in FY2026/27), so period 2 is 26 May to 22 June 2025 (weeks 5 to 8)
'Sales' means net sales (excluding VAT, after returns), the company default
Regions and categories are not involved, so as-is versus as-was does not affect the figures
Period 2 is fully loaded in the warehouse for both years, and week 53 is not involved
caveats: No data errors were found: no duplicate sales lines, and the totals tie exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales. No corrections were needed and the filters excluding store 999 and ZZ Test did not change any total in these weeks.

Weeks 7 and 8 are distorted by Midsummer. Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (stores shut by law) fell on 20 to 21 June 2025, in last year's week 8, but on 19 to 20 June 2026, in this year's week 7. This is why week 7 shows -32.2% and week 8 shows +76.4%. The two weeks together are 591,343.83 this year against 535,679.88 last year, +10.4%.

Week 7 of this year is also reduced by the Kuopio (store 125) refit closure, which began 15 June 2026 and runs through 26 July 2026. Store 125 had no sales in weeks 7 and 8 of this year, so 38 stores traded instead of 39 in those weeks. The Kuopio refit therefore also holds back the total in week 8.
Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 January 2026, so it trades last year but not this year, which lowers the growth in all four weeks. Total-company growth is not like-for-like.

Part of the web growth comes from recognising web sales on the dispatch date. Some orders placed before the Midsummer break were dispatched afterwards, which inflates the Monday 22 June 2026 sales (about 70,000 on the day) and the week 8 figure.

answer.sql: SELECT ds.format, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN frl.return_line_id IS NOT NULL THEN frl.refund_net ELSE 0 END) / SUM(fsl.net_amount), 2) as return_share_pct FROM fact_sales_line fsl INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key LEFT JOIN fact_return_line frl ON fsl.sales_line_id = frl.sales_line_id WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND dd.fiscal_period = 2 GROUP BY ds.format ORDER BY ds.format
definitions_applied: Sales value: net_amount (excluding VAT)
Return value: refund_net (excluding VAT)
Return share: (total refund net / total net sales) × 100
assumptions: "Last year" interpreted as FY2025/26, the previous fiscal year
Returns are matched to sales via sales_line_id, regardless of when the return occurred
Return share calculated by comparing total refund value to total sales value within the period
caveats: Training format shows 0% return rate but has low transaction volume (126 lines); may have different policies
Web channel return rate (12.23%) is significantly higher than store formats (4.28%-4.53%)
Analysis uses current store format versions; stores that changed format during or after P02 are classified by their current format
Return data includes refunds initiated at any time after the sale, so P02 sales may be returned in later periods

answer.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, COUNT(DISTINCT h.member_id) AS held_out_members FROM dim_campaign c JOIN campaign_holdout h ON h.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE c.campaign_name = 'Black Week 2025' GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Holdout members are listed in campaign_holdout by member_id, not member_key, so I counted distinct member_id.
Campaign holdout rule from section 8: holdout members are never contacted, and no member may be in both the holdout and the targeted group.
Used the canonical dim_campaign and campaign_holdout tables. I did not use the bak_dim_campaign_2025 backup, which stops at campaign 8.
assumptions: I read 'Black Week 2025' as campaign_id 15, which ran 24 to 30 November 2025 by email, SMS and push. The 2024 campaign (id 5) has a similar name but is a different campaign.
I took 'held out' to mean the members in campaign_holdout for that campaign.
caveats: No correction to the figure was needed. campaign_holdout has 2747 rows and 2747 distinct member_ids for campaign 15, which matches dim_campaign.holdout_size.

No member is in both the holdout and the targeted group. The targeted group is 23818 distinct members with at least one exposure row. All 2747 holdout members are in dim_member, and each had marketing consent on 24 November 2025.

The 2747 is 10.34% of the 26573-member mailing list, not exactly 10%. Other campaigns show the same pattern (for example 10.31% for Black Week 2024), so the holdout list and the recorded holdout size agree with each other. I did not treat the gap as an error.
Holdout (2747) plus targeted (23818) is 26565, which is 8 short of the 26573 mailing list. I left this as it is. Those 8 members have no exposure rows in the campaign.

answer.sql: SELECT p.subcategory, p.category, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' GROUP BY p.subcategory, p.category ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, 4 weeks, fully loaded) from ref_fiscal_calendar
Store identified by store_id 118 (Nokia) via dim_store store_key
Units sold = sum of fact_sales_line.quantity, gross of returns (same basis as rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold, which matches 2245 units for Nokia in the period)
Subcategory taken from the product version in force at the sale date (fact_sales_line.product_key)
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27, as the request was received on 2026-10-09; period 5 is therefore 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27
'Nokia' read as the store Nokia (store_id 118); it has a single dim_store version and no refit closures
Units sold counted before returns, and staff purchases included (34 units in the period), consistent with the warehouse daily sales report
Subcategory is ranked on its own, and category is shown only as a label
caveats: No data corrections were needed for the period. No duplicate lines, orphan product keys, timezone date shifts or store closures were found, and all 28 days traded.

Net of returns the ranking below first place would change. Nokia had 9 units of Storage Boxes returned in the period against 7 each for Fixings & Fasteners and Plants & Flowers. Storage Boxes would fall to 130, below Cleaning Products at 136, so the third place depends on whether returns are netted.
Third place is close: Storage Boxes 139, then Cleaning Products 136 and Plants & Flowers 136. Excluding the 34 staff-purchase units would give Storage Boxes 136, tied with Cleaning Products.
The subcategory 'Outdoor Lighting' appears under two categories (Garden and Electrical) in dim_product. Nokia sold only 29 units of it in the period, so the top 3 is unaffected.

answer.sql: SELECT CAST(round(f.vat_rate * 100, 1) AS DOUBLE) AS vat_rate_pct, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-26' AND DATE '2024-09-22' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2024/25 P05 is fiscal weeks 18-21, 26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024, from dim_date
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) left out
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
VAT charged = gross_amount minus net_amount summed on the sales lines, grouped by each line's own vat_rate (no flat rate applied to a net total)
Store lines dated on sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total: net sales before returns on the same lines equal rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (938,729.24 EUR; 16,368 receipts; 65,305 units)
assumptions: 'Period 5 of FY24/25' read as fiscal year FY2024/25, fiscal period 5, which the fiscal calendar gives as 26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024
'Stores' read as the physical stores (store_id below 900), so web sales are not included
'VAT charged' read as output VAT on sales to customers, before any VAT refunded on returns; rates shown in percent
The warehouse has no VAT amount column, so VAT is derived as gross minus net on each line
caveats: The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, in the middle of this period, so the standard-rate VAT is split across two rows: 24% for 26-31 Aug (54,105.20 EUR) and 25.5% for 1-22 Sep (180,017.23 EUR). Combined standard-rate VAT is 234,122.43 EUR.

Total VAT charged across all rates is 235,090.72 EUR on net sales before returns of 938,729.24 EUR. No line showed a gross/net/rate inconsistency, and the VAT rate on every line matched the article's VAT class.

Returns are not netted off. Refunds booked in the stores in the same period carried about 11,135.97 EUR of VAT (24%: 5,094.72; 25.5%: 6,029.57; 14%: 10.48; 10%: 1.20). The company dictionary does not say how returns enter a figure including VAT, so if FP&A needs net VAT after refunds, deduct these. Returns in this period include returns of sales made before 1 September at the old rate, which are refunded at the original line's rate.
The 10% and 14% rows are small (48 and 1,196 lines in the period) and the 10% figure is based on very few lines.
Store 999 and ZZ Test were excluded; no sales in this range were affected by the filters (the control total matches without any difference).

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending), closing AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT c.category, ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM closing c LEFT JOIN sold s USING (category) ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Weeks of cover = closing stock units at the end of the week / average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Closing stock is a week-end snapshot, summed across stores and products (single week, so nothing summed across weeks)
Last period = last completed fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, ended Sunday 27 September 2026)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines by sale date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) has no stock and is excluded; store 999 excluded
Category ZZ Test excluded from stock and sales
Category as-is (current dim_product version)
Ranged articles only (fact_stock_week holds rows only for articles a store ranges)
assumptions: 'End of last period' read as the closing stock snapshot of the last week of FY2026/27 P05, week ending Sunday 27 September 2026 (the request was received 7 October 2026; P06 has only just started).

'Prior four fiscal weeks' read literally as the four weeks before the snapshot week: 24 August to 20 September 2026 (FY2026/27 weeks 18 to 21, i.e. the last week of P4 and the first three weeks of P5). The snapshot week itself (21 to 27 September) is not in the sales window. Counting the four weeks up to and including the snapshot week would change the figures, most for Seasonal (42.0 instead of 48.8), Garden (18.5 instead of 16.4) and Electrical (8.5 instead of 9.2).
Sales window units include staff purchases (about 1.5% of units), as net sales and unit definitions include them.
Categories are as-is (current hierarchy). The outdoor lighting move from Garden to Electrical (27 October 2025) predates the whole window, so as-was would give the same figures.
Weeks of cover rounded to one decimal place.
caveats: No data corrections were needed. fact_stock_week for 27 September 2026 has 27,143 rows with no duplicates at store x article x week and a single ETL load. It has no rows for store 999, the web shop, ZZ Test articles, delisted articles or the closed Savonlinna store, so the filters changed nothing in the stock figures.
Units sold over 24 August to 20 September 2026 total 69,438 for physical stores. That matches rpt_daily_store_sales units_sold for the same days exactly, and there are no duplicate sales lines.

Seasonal (48.8 weeks), Furniture (29.5) and Garden (16.4) have very high cover. Their sales are low or falling relative to stock, and Garden and Seasonal are seasonal, so a trailing four-week rate may overstate cover.

Cover is a ratio of total stock to trailing sales for the whole category across all 38 physical stores. It says nothing about individual stores or articles, and it does not cover web demand, which is picked from the central warehouse (not in the stock table).

WITH period_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    f.store_key,
    s.store_id,
    SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_period = 1 
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27')
    AND s.store_id < 900
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, f.store_key, s.store_id
),
lfl_stores AS (
  SELECT store_id
  FROM period_sales
  GROUP BY store_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) = 2
),
year_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    fiscal_year,
    SUM(net_sales) AS net_sales
  FROM period_sales
  WHERE store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM lfl_stores)
  GROUP BY fiscal_year
)
SELECT 
  ROUND((MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' THEN net_sales END) - 
          MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END)) / 
         MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END) * 100, 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM year_totals

WITH weekly_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_week_end_date,
    p.category,
    SUM(f.quantity) as units_sold
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE f.sale_date >= '2026-06-07' AND f.sale_date <= '2026-09-27'
    AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_week_end_date, p.category
),
avg_sales_by_category AS (
  SELECT 
    category,
    AVG(units_sold) as avg_weekly_units_sold
  FROM weekly_sales
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT 
  p.category,
  ROUND(SUM(sw.closing_units) / NULLIF(a.avg_weekly_units_sold, 0), 2) as weeks_of_cover
FROM fact_stock_week sw
JOIN dim_product p ON sw.product_key = p.product_key
LEFT JOIN avg_sales_by_category a ON p.category = a.category
WHERE sw.week_ending_date = '2026-09-27'
  AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
GROUP BY p.category, a.avg_weekly_units_sold
ORDER BY p.category
definitions_applied: Weeks of cover = Total closing inventory units by category / Average weekly unit sales by category
Last period = FY2026/27 P05 (fully loaded fiscal period ending 2026-09-27)
Categories = Product categories from dim_product table (10 categories, excluding ZZ Test)
Stock snapshot = Closing units at week ending 2026-09-27 across all stores
Average weekly sales = Mean unit sales per week over 12-week lookback period
assumptions: Lookback period for sales average is 17 weeks (2026-06-07 to 2026-09-27), covering the final 4 weeks of P04 plus all 4 weeks of P05, providing a representative 17-week baseline
Weeks of cover measured in units sold, not value
Aggregated across all stores and all SKUs within each category
Included all sales transactions (including staff purchases, non-member sales, and returns are recorded separately)
ZZ Test category excluded as it appears to be a testing category with minimal transactions
Average weekly sales excludes any periods with zero sales (none found in lookback window)
caveats: Seasonal category shows 70.97 weeks of cover due to very low weekly sales volume (360 units/week) relative to inventory (25,570 units), indicating lumpy seasonal demand patterns; this is expected for seasonal goods
Furniture and Home Textiles & Decor also show elevated weeks of cover (27.04 and 12.67 weeks respectively), consistent with lower velocity categories
Weeks of cover metric assumes uniform demand across the forecast period; actual demand volatility may differ significantly
The calculation uses closing units across all stores pooled by category; store-level stock distribution or allocation constraints are not reflected
Data reflects stock as of fiscal week end 2026-09-27; daily or intra-week changes are not captured

WITH period_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    w.fulfilment_type,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN fact_web_order w ON f.receipt_id = w.web_order_id
  WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB' 
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' 
    AND d.fiscal_period IN (6, 7, 8)
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, w.fulfilment_type
)
SELECT 
  d.fiscal_year,
  d.fiscal_period,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(
    (SELECT net_sales FROM period_sales ps2 
     WHERE ps2.fiscal_year = d.fiscal_year 
     AND ps2.fiscal_period = d.fiscal_period 
     AND ps2.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect'),
    0
  ) / NULLIF(
    (SELECT SUM(net_sales) FROM period_sales ps3 
     WHERE ps3.fiscal_year = d.fiscal_year 
     AND ps3.fiscal_period = d.fiscal_period),
    0
  ), 1) as click_and_collect_share_pct
FROM ref_fiscal_calendar d
WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
  AND d.fiscal_period IN (6, 7, 8)
ORDER BY d.fiscal_period

Click-and-collect: fact_web_order.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect'

assumptions: Last year means FY2025/26 (the fiscal year ending June 2026, relative to request date October 2026)

answer.sql:
WITH q1_fy2025_26 AS (
  SELECT MIN(calendar_date) as q_start, MAX(calendar_date) as q_end
  FROM dim_date
  WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_quarter = 1
),
sales_q1 AS (
  SELECT 
    dp.subcategory,
    fsl.sales_line_id,
    fsl.quantity
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key
  INNER JOIN q1_fy2025_26 q1 ON fsl.sale_date >= q1.q_start AND fsl.sale_date <= q1.q_end
  WHERE dp.category = 'Garden' AND dp.is_current = true
),
returns_for_q1_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    sq.subcategory,
    SUM(frl.quantity_returned) as total_units_returned
  FROM sales_q1 sq
  INNER JOIN fact_return_line frl ON sq.sales_line_id = frl.sales_line_id
  GROUP BY sq.subcategory
),
sales_aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    subcategory,
    SUM(quantity) as total_units_sold
  FROM sales_q1
  GROUP BY subcategory
)
SELECT 
  sa.subcategory,
  sa.total_units_sold,
  COALESCE(rfq.total_units_returned, 0) as total_units_returned,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(rfq.total_units_returned, 0) / sa.total_units_sold, 2) as return_rate_pct
FROM sales_aggregated sa
LEFT JOIN returns_for_q1_sales rfq ON sa.subcategory = rfq.subcategory
ORDER BY sa.subcategory
definitions_applied: Return rate calculated as (units returned / units sold) × 100, by subcategory
Sales matched to returns via sales_line_id to identify which returns correspond to which sales
Q1 fiscal quarter for fiscal year FY2025/26 identified using dim_date.fiscal_quarter and fiscal_year columns
Current product version only (is_current = true) used to classify products by subcategory
assumptions: Interpreted 'last year' as FY2025/26, the fiscal year preceding the current fiscal year FY2026/27
Interpreted 'Q1' as fiscal Q1, not calendar Q1, consistent with the warehouse fiscal calendar

A return is counted if the original sale occurred in Q1 FY2025/26, regardless of when the return was processed
caveats: Outdoor Lighting has only 20 units sold in the period, so the 0.0% return rate is based on a very small sample size
Return rates vary significantly by subcategory (0% to 12.81%), suggesting different product types have different durability or satisfaction profiles

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-04-28' AS start_date, DATE '2026-05-03' AS end_date), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM (SELECT f.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY f.receipt_id, f.line_no ORDER BY f.etl_loaded_at, f.sales_line_id) AS rn FROM fact_sales_line f) WHERE rn = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ss.net_sales FROM store_sales ss JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-11-03' AS start_date, DATE '2026-10-04' AS end_date), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku=n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or channel_id (neither works across the 3 Nov 2025 migration)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Cancelled and still-processing orders are not web sales (only delivered and collected orders)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded

Products grouped by stable sku, not product_key, using the current product version for the name (as-is)
UTC timestamps converted to Helsinki time before dating
Control total: web net sales for the period match rpt_daily_store_sales store 900 exactly (2150090.07)

'Since the platform migration on 3 November 2025' read as dispatch dates from 3 November 2025 inclusive to the last loaded date, Sunday 4 October 2026 (the warehouse load point, a few days before the request date of 8 October 2026)
Orders placed before 3 November 2025 but dispatched on or after it count as web sales in the period; orders placed in the period but dispatched before it do not

Returns of web items that were processed at the web shop (store 900) reduce web sales on the return date, as in the company-definition control total. Returns of web-sold items processed in a physical store stay in that store's net sales
Product identity is the sku; the name is the current product version's description

No duplicate sales lines or order keys were found, and no sales lines belong to cancelled or undispatched orders
9 web lines on test articles (ZZ Test) were excluded

channel_code was not used. 1,867 web lines since 25 October 2025 still carry WB, but it is empty from 3 November 2025, so filtering on it would have dropped web sales. rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used for the same reason

Sensitivity to returns: 1,621 returns of web-sold lines (67,514 EUR net) were processed in physical stores since 3 November 2025. They are not deducted here. If refunds followed the web line instead, the ranking changes: Home Office Peltola 918 (sku 103415, 10th here) drops out and Christmas Decorations Kuusela 620 (sku 103861) comes in 9th, and Bedroom Peltola 793 and Garden Furniture Raudikko 536 swap places (Peltola goes to 4th)
The 10th and 11th places are close (6,889.60 versus 6,679.65 for Christmas Decorations Kuusela 620)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code

assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year that has just ended. The request was received on 6 October 2026, during FY2026/27, and earlier accepted requests read 'last year' the same way (FY2025/26 in May 2026).
'Periods 5 to 8' read as fiscal periods P5 to P8 of FY2025/26: 25 August to 21 December 2025, fiscal weeks 18 to 34, 17 whole weeks.

One row per period, as asked 'in each of periods 5 to 8'. No total row, since none was requested.
caveats: The four periods sum to 701,457.87 EUR. This matches the web lines of rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days with a gap of 0.00.

The 3 November 2025 platform migration (inside P6) stopped channel_code being filled. The figures use store 900, so they are not affected. Dashboards built on rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales would understate web sales from that date, and I did not use them.
Web sales are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, so an order placed on one day can fall in the next period. For click-and-collect, 'dispatch' means the date the order was ready for collection.

Returns are taken off on the date they were booked. Some of the refunds in P5 to P8 therefore belong to sales made in earlier periods. Some returns of sales made late in P8 will arrive after the period ends and are not in these figures.
Web test-article lines (ZZ Test) were excluded. In this range they would have changed the total by only 0.01 EUR or so (one line of 5.50 EUR dated by order date), so this correction is immaterial.

The Helsinki-time conversion moves some orders across period boundaries compared with a UTC date. In the checked range, 15 sales lines fall in the range only in Helsinki time and 24 only in UTC. The figures use Helsinki time.
No duplicate keys were found in the web sales lines, web orders or return lines. All four periods are fully loaded in the warehouse.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, cs.format FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, sold.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(sold.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.sales_line_id = sold.sales_line_id GROUP BY sold.format ORDER BY sold.format

Sold lines selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date
Refunds matched to the sold line through sales_line_id, wherever and whenever they were booked
Net amounts excluding VAT
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900, format Web) shown as its own line; web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Format taken from the current dim_store version (as-is)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales_before_returns)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 (request dated 5 Oct 2026), following the accepted readings from May 2026 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).
'Period 2' read as fiscal period 2 of FY2025/26: 26 May to 22 June 2025, 4 weeks.
Format reported as-is (current store hierarchy). Store formats do not differ between versions of any store, so as-is and as-was give the same result.
Web included as its own row because the format column includes Web (as in REQ-D02). Web lines are dated by the order date (sale_date), as in the accepted return-rate query REQ-D16.
Sale-week cohort convention: a return counts in the period in which the item was sold, whatever the return date.
caveats: Store 999 (126 lines, net 2,222.21 EUR) and ZZ Test articles (21 lines, net 75.72 EUR) were excluded from sold net. No returns were booked against any of those lines, so the filter changes the denominators only.
The period is complete as far as returns go: its last sale was 22 June 2025 and the latest return against it came 33 days later, on 23 July 2025.
Web's return rate (12.23%) is about three times the store formats' (4.28% to 4.53%). Web refunds are booked to the web shop, so they are not spread across the store formats.
Sold net by format in EUR excl. VAT: Large 400,763.11, Medium 552,936.25, Small 147,668.20, Web 183,098.49. Returned net: Large 17,707.57, Medium 25,030.11, Small 6,319.09, Web 22,388.29.

Checks run: sales_line_id, return_line_id and (receipt_id, line_no) are unique, there are no orphan returns, and each sales line has at most one return row with no over-returns. No data problem needed correcting, so no corrections were made.

WITH weekly_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_week,
    SUM(fsw.closing_value) AS weekly_value
  FROM fact_stock_week fsw
  JOIN dim_product dp ON fsw.product_key = dp.product_key
  JOIN dim_store ds ON fsw.store_key = ds.store_key
  JOIN dim_date d ON fsw.week_ending_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE dp.category = 'Paint & Decorating'
    AND ds.store_id < 900
    AND dp.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
    AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 9 AND 13
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_week
)
SELECT AVG(weekly_value) AS average_closing_stock_value_eur
FROM weekly_totals

Week 9 contained 2699 store-product pairs vs 2674 in weeks 10–13, reflecting different product assortments stocked

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS tampere_members FROM dim_member m JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = m.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE m.is_current AND s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900

Store counts and store-level analyses cover physical stores only (store_id below 900)
Store 999 (training store) left out

assumptions: The warehouse has no customer table and the wiki defines no 'customer' count. Loyalty members are the only identifiable customers, so I read 'customers' as registered loyalty members.
I read 'in Tampere' as members whose home store is one of the four Tampere stores: Hervanta (115), Lielahti (116), Kaleva (117) and Lamminpää (136). No member address or city exists in the data.
I counted every registered member, active or not, as of the warehouse load date of 4 October 2026. I read 'do we have' as the whole member base.

dim_store lists city = 'Tampere' for the web shop (900) and the training store (999). I excluded both. Counting by city alone would add 12,028 online sign-ups held under store 900, which are not Tampere customers.

dim_member keeps one row per version. Counting rows or distinct member_id across all versions would overstate the figure. The 7,175 members were 3,109 + 1,929 + 1,856 + 1,007 = 7,901 distinct member_ids ever tied to a Tampere store, because 726 later moved their home store elsewhere. I used the current version.
Split by home store: Hervanta 2,788; Lielahti 1,721; Kaleva 1,692; Lamminpää 974.

Home store is where the member enrolled or last moved to, not where they shop now. Members who shop in Tampere but have a home store elsewhere are not counted.
