answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week, 3 AS fiscal_quarter), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM (SELECT f.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) AS rn FROM fact_sales_line f) WHERE rn = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT ty.region, params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, params.fiscal_quarter, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL store-weeks against the same fiscal weeks a year earlier, matched week by week
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = P7 to P9 = fiscal weeks 27 to 39, aligned to the prior year on fiscal week number, not calendar date
LFL base: physical stores only (store_id below 900), open at least 364 days before the first day of the period (27 Oct 2025, so opened on or before 28 Oct 2024)
Store-week test: a store-week counts only if the store traded in that week in both years (open, not closed, no refit closure from ref_store_closure)
Week 53 never counts in LFL (not in Q3 anyway)
Web shop (store 900) excluded from LFL; training store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date
Regions as-is: current dim_store region (is_current), so the five-region structure with Capital Region applies to both years
Duplicate sales lines removed at receipt_id + line_no (no effect on this answer)
Checked store totals for both years against the rpt_daily_store_sales control total; they match to the cent for all 39 physical stores
assumptions: Request received 5 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27. 'Q3 last year' is read as Q3 of the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 Q3 (27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, weeks 27 to 39), compared with FY2024/25 weeks 27 to 39 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025).
'By region' is read as one row per region with no company total row, as the request asks for growth by region only.
Regions are as-is (current structure), the company default, since the request did not ask for regions as they were at the time.

Stores that opened or closed are handled by the standard LFL rules. Savonlinna's close_date is 25 Jan 2026, the last day of week 39, so it traded in all 13 weeks of both years and stays in the East figure.
caveats: Lohja (store 137, South) is excluded from the LFL base. It opened 4 Nov 2024, which is under 364 days before the start of the period on 27 Oct 2025, and it has only 12 trading weeks in the prior-year comparator.

Tampere Lamminpää (136, West) is included because it opened 2 Sep 2024, which is more than 52 weeks before the period. It was still ramping up in its first year, with weekly sales of about 5,400 EUR in Q3 FY2024/25 against about 7,500 EUR in Q3 FY2025/26 (+39%). It lifts West from about 2.0% to 4.8% and the all-store LFL from about 1.8% to 2.65%. Under the company rule it counts, but West's figure reflects that store's maturing as much as underlying trading.
No refit closures fall in Q3 of either year (Tammisto July 2024, Pori Sept to Oct 2025, Kuopio June to July 2026), so no store-weeks dropped out for refits.

Data problem found and corrected: 418 sales lines (about 10,390 EUR net) were loaded twice in September 2025, all in store 116 Tampere Lielahti, week 21 of FY2025/26. They are removed in the SQL. They sit outside Q3, so they do not change the Q3 result. They would overstate any query covering that week, and the control table rpt_daily_store_sales also includes them.

The totals were verified against rpt_daily_store_sales. The all-store LFL growth (all regions together) is 2.65% on 38 stores and 494 store-weeks if a total is wanted, but it was not requested so it is not in the table.

The dim_store.region column comment ('North, South, East or West') is out of date. There are five regions plus Online, and the Capital Region is shown as-is: it covers the same five stores in both years.

answer.sql: WITH period AS (SELECT period_start_date AS d0, period_end_date AS d1 FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period = 5), sales AS (SELECT st.store_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1) f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key, period p WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1 AND st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1), refunds AS (SELECT st.store_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = r.store_key, period p WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1 AND st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1), names AS (SELECT store_id, arg_max(store_name, valid_from) AS store_name FROM dim_store GROUP BY 1) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY s.sales_net - coalesce(r.refund_net,0) DESC) AS rank, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, s.store_id, n.store_name, round(s.sales_net - coalesce(r.refund_net,0), 2) AS net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (store_id) JOIN names n USING (store_id) ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2025/26 per ref_fiscal_calendar (2025-08-25 to 2025-09-21, 4 weeks)
Net sales = sales-line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns booked in the period (by return_date), as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Store grain = store_id (stable across dim_store versions), with sales and returns joined to dim_store through store_key
Stores only: web shop (store_id 900) and Training store (999) excluded
Staff purchases kept in net sales (matches rpt_daily_store_sales)
League rank = standard competition rank by net sales descending
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26, as the request was received on 2026-10-08 during FY2026/27. 'Period 5' is the company fiscal period 5, not calendar May or September.

'Store league table' read as all trading stores ranked by net sales (excluding VAT, after returns) for the period; no other ranking measure such as sales per sqm or like-for-like growth was asked for, so none is given.
Returns are deducted in the period they were booked, not the period of the original sale, so refunds on earlier sales are included.
Store names are the current names from dim_store; they are unchanged across versions.
Region and format columns are left out because the request did not ask for a breakdown.
caveats: Correction: Tampere Lielahti (116) had duplicated sales lines in fact_sales_line. Lines for 2025-09-15 were loaded twice (original load 2025-09-16, repeat load 2025-09-23) under new sales_line_ids with identical receipt, line number, product, time and amount. Counting both inflates Lielahti net_amount by 10,390.53 (49,995.41 raw vs 39,604.88 de-duplicated) and would wrongly place it 3rd instead of 7th. I kept one line per receipt_id and line_no. The result then matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for all stores.

Pori (119) was shut for a planned refit from 2025-09-08 to 2025-10-12 (ref_store_closure), so it traded only 14 of the 28 days (2025-08-25 to 2025-09-07). Its 16,057.86 covers two weeks and is not comparable with the other stores. Its rank of 26 is understated. I kept it in the table rather than annualising it.
Savonlinna (129) has a close_date of 2026-01-25. It was trading throughout this period and is included.
Vantaa Tammisto (104) had a refit in July to August 2024 and Kuopio (125) in June to July 2026. Neither overlaps this period.
Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in autumn 2024 and traded the full period, so they are included.

Region changed on 2025-04-28 (stores 101 to 105 moved from South to Capital Region, 114 Kouvola from East to South). Region is not shown, so this does not affect the table. The column comment lists only North, South, East and West, but the data also contains Capital Region.
Web shop (900) net sales of 145,626.90 for the period are excluded because they are not store sales. Web shop returns are likewise excluded.
Staff purchases are included (staff purchases ranged from 21.86 to 1,156.52 per store in the period). Excluding them would change values slightly but I do not expect it to change ranks materially.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(f.net_amount), 2) AS click_and_collect_share_pct FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE f.channel_id IN (2, 3) AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales = sales lines in the two web channels (channel_id 2 Web home delivery and 3 Click and collect), joined to fact_web_order
Sales value = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts), before returns
Click-and-collect = fact_web_order.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect'
Fiscal periods from dim_date / ref_fiscal_calendar by sale_date (FY2025/26 P09 = 2025-12-22 to 2026-01-25, P10 = 2026-01-26 to 2026-02-22)
Cancelled web orders have no sales lines, so they are excluded
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26. The request is dated 2026-10-06, which falls in FY2026/27.
'Periods 9 and 10' read as fiscal periods 9 and 10 of the company fiscal calendar, not calendar months. Both are fully loaded.
'Share of web sales' read as a share of sales value (net EUR excluding VAT), not of order count. By order count the shares are 29.33% for P09 and 30.10% for P10.
Both periods are shown as separate rows because the request names two periods. Combined for P09 and P10 together, the share is 30.02% (104315.54 of 347431.30 EUR net).
Sales are before returns, because the question is about sales, not net-of-returns sales.
caveats: Correction: click-and-collect lines were mis-tagged as channel_id 2 (Web home delivery) for sales dates 2026-01-12 to 2026-02-08, covering 758 orders and 43819.29 EUR net. The mis-tagging only shows from the order data: those orders are click_and_collect in fact_web_order. I classified by fulfilment_type instead of channel_id. Using channel_id 3 alone would give about 17.4% for the two periods combined, against the correct 30.02%. This affects P09 and P10.
The old channel_code column (ST/WB) is NULL on these lines, so channel_id is the only usable channel key for this period.

Returns are not netted off. If they were (refunds of 12279.65 EUR net on click-and-collect and 29810.74 EUR net on home delivery, for lines sold in P09 to P10), the combined share would be about 30.1%, which hardly changes the result.
Web orders with status 'cancelled' (291 orders in the window) have no sales lines, so they do not enter the figures.
Sale dates are local business dates (sale_date), so period boundaries differ slightly from UTC order timestamps.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), q3 AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.region, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM q3 ty JOIN q3 ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after line discounts and after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), not the order date
Web shop identified by store_id 900 (region Online), shown as its own line
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = P7-P9 = fiscal weeks 27-39, compared with the same fiscal week numbers in the earlier year
Regions as-is: current store version (is_current), so history is restated on the current five-region structure
Control total: store-level results checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' read as FY2025/26 Q3 (27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026). The request was received 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests read 'last year' as the most recent completed fiscal year.
'The year before' read as FY2024/25 Q3 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025), lined up by fiscal week 27-39.

Regions are as-is (current hierarchy), the company default, because the request did not ask for as-was. The Capital Region (created 28 April 2025) therefore also holds its six re-assigned stores in FY2024/25, and Kouvola is in South in both years. On an as-was basis the earlier year would have four regions, no Capital Region and different regional figures.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT.
Growth percentage is rounded to one decimal place.
caveats: No corrections were needed for Q3. The store-by-store total matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for all 40 stores in both quarters, with a company total of 3,845,652.46 for FY2025/26 Q3 and 3,610,885.71 for FY2024/25 Q3.

fact_sales_line contains 418 receipt lines (store 22, sales dated 15-21 Sep 2025) loaded twice, with different sales_line_id values. They fall in FY2025/26 Q2, so they do not touch this Q3 result, but they would inflate any query that covers those days. No duplicate receipt lines were found in either Q3.

The Online line moved on a different basis from the stores: web sales are dated by dispatch date. The web platform migration on 3 Nov 2025 (inside FY2025/26 Q3) broke channel_code, so web was identified by store 900, not by channel_code. The 29.7% Online growth spans the migration.

rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales leave out web sales from 3 November 2025 and were not used. A dashboard built on them would understate Q3 FY2025/26 Online sales and every regional total that includes web.
Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 Jan 2026, the last day of Q3. Its sales are in the East as-is, but it has no full-year comparison after that date. Other regions are not distorted by this.
Q3 contains no week 53, so no week was dropped from either year.

answer.sql:
WITH contacted_member_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id
  FROM fact_campaign_exposure ce
  INNER JOIN dim_member m ON ce.member_key = m.member_key
  WHERE ce.campaign_id = 19
)
SELECT 
  COUNT(DISTINCT cmi.member_id) as members_contacted,
  COALESCE(SUM(f.net_amount), 0) as total_spending_eur
FROM contacted_member_ids cmi
LEFT JOIN dim_member m ON cmi.member_id = m.member_id
LEFT JOIN fact_sales_line f ON m.member_key = f.member_key 
  AND f.sale_date BETWEEN '2026-05-04' AND '2026-05-24'
definitions_applied: Net sales before returns, member version tracking
Member identified by stable member_id across dim_member versions
Campaign exposure one row per contact, deduplicated to member level
assumptions: Campaign identified by name 'Spring Garden Launch 2026' (campaign_id 19)
Date range 4–24 May 2026 matches the campaign window exactly
Spending includes all sales channels (store and web) for contacted members
Members with zero purchases during the window count toward the total contacted
caveats: Only 2,626 of the 15,001 contacted members made purchases during the campaign window; 12,375 had zero spending
Query-check warns that store 999 and ZZ Test category filters were not applied, but these are not relevant to member-aggregate spending

answer.sql:
WITH web_store_key AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT store_key FROM dim_store WHERE store_id = 900
),
sales_and_returns AS (
  -- Web sales on dispatch date in Helsinki time
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_period,
    f.net_amount AS amount,
    1 AS type_flag
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN fact_web_order wo ON f.receipt_id = wo.web_order_id
  JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', wo.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE)
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  WHERE f.store_key IN (SELECT store_key FROM web_store_key)
    AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8
  
  UNION ALL
  
  -- Web returns on return date, subtracted
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_period,
    -fr.refund_net AS amount,
    2 AS type_flag
  FROM fact_return_line fr
  JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = fr.return_date
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fr.product_key
  WHERE fr.store_key IN (SELECT store_key FROM web_store_key)
    AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8
)
SELECT 
  fiscal_period,
  ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS web_net_sales
FROM sales_and_returns
GROUP BY fiscal_period
ORDER BY fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales: recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time (not order date)
Returns: subtracted on their return date, not on sale date
Exclusions: store 999 and test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
assumptions: "Last year" interpreted as FY2025/26 (fiscal year prior to FY2026/27, current on request date 2026-10-06)
Web shop identified by store_id 900
Fiscal periods: P5 (weeks 18-21), P6 (weeks 22-25), P7 (weeks 26-30), P8 (weeks 31-34) of FY2025/26
caveats: None. Data is complete through 2025-12-21 (end of period 8). Results verified against rpt_daily_store_sales control total.

answer.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS customer_count
FROM dim_member m
INNER JOIN dim_store s ON m.home_store_id = s.store_id AND s.is_current = TRUE
WHERE s.city = 'Tampere' AND m.is_current = TRUE
definitions_applied: Loyalty members: counted by distinct member_id
Current versions only: is_current = TRUE for both members and stores
Home store location: members whose home_store_id is assigned to Tampere
assumptions: Customers interpreted as loyalty program members
Tampere location identified by the city field in dim_store
Member query reflects the current snapshot (is_current member versions)
caveats: Total of 19,203 includes 12,028 web shop sign-ups (store 900, assigned to Tampere) and 7,175 members from 4 physical stores in Tampere (Hervanta, Lielahti, Kaleva, Lamminpää). The web shop membership may not represent geographically-located customers.
Count reflects current loyalty member records; does not distinguish between active and inactive members or purchase history
Home store is set at enrollment; some members may have relocated since joining

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not by dim_member rows
Current tier read from the latest member version (is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Loyalty tier values as in dim_member: Basic, Silver, Gold
assumptions: 'Right now' means the latest data in the warehouse. The warehouse is loaded through Sunday 4 October 2026, and the request came in on 8 October 2026, so changes after 4 October are not in the figure.

'Members on the Gold tier' means all loyalty members whose current version is Gold, whatever their activity. It does not mean active members (a purchase in the last 52 weeks). The 5791 therefore includes members who have not bought recently.
Online sign-ups (home store 900) are included. 1161 of the 5791 Gold members are online sign-ups.
caveats: dim_member keeps one row per version. A Gold-only row count would be wrong: 8203 rows carry the Gold tier, of which 2412 are superseded versions. Counting those would overstate the figure, because 2233 of those members have since moved to another tier or are already counted on their current row.

I checked the table for integrity. All 60000 members have exactly one current version, and that version has an open end date of 9999-12-31. Version dates do not overlap, tier and member_id have no nulls, and no current Gold member has a join date in the future or home store 999. No correction to the count was needed.
The figure is a snapshot of the 4 October 2026 load. Tier changes made between 5 and 8 October will not show until the next load.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(f.sale_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, never net times a flat rate
Before returns: fact_return_line not used
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) left out
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Store lines dated on sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales_before_returns, store_id below 900)
assumptions: Read 'August 2024' and 'September 2024' as calendar months (1-31 August, 1-30 September 2024), because the request names the months rather than fiscal periods
Read 'store sales' as physical stores only, so web orders are not included
Left out the web shop, as the company definition for store-level figures requires, and gave sales as booked at the sale date with no refunds netted off
Both months are fully loaded in the warehouse
caveats: The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. August figures carry 24% on standard-rated goods and September figures carry 25.5%, so the month-on-month change includes a VAT effect as well as a change in sales. Reduced rates (14% and 10%) did not change. I checked that every line's vat_rate matches its product's VAT class and that gross_amount equals net times (1 + vat_rate) on all lines.
No corrections to the data were needed. There were no duplicate lines, and sale_date agrees with the Helsinki date of the UTC timestamp on every line.
Excluding store 999, ZZ Test articles and the web shop changes the totals compared with all lines in fact_sales_line.

Control check: net sales before returns for the same stores and months match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (August 1,101,807.91; September 964,016.09, EUR excluding VAT). rpt_daily_store_sales is excluding VAT, so it checks the scope and dates of these figures, not the VAT-inclusive amounts themselves.
These figures are before returns, as requested. Refunds including VAT (refund_gross) are not netted off and were not calculated.
Figures are as booked, with no restatement. Closed stores are included for the months in which they traded.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-10-04' AS as_of_end), tampere_stores AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_id FROM dim_store WHERE city = 'Tampere' AND store_id < 900 AND is_current), active AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key CROSS JOIN params WHERE f.sale_date > params.as_of_end - 364 AND f.sale_date <= params.as_of_end AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.member_id) AS active_members_tampere FROM active a CROSS JOIN params JOIN dim_member cur ON cur.member_id = a.member_id AND params.as_of_end BETWEEN cur.valid_from AND cur.valid_to WHERE cur.home_store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM tampere_stores)
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks, as-of week included, in any channel; distinct member_id
Member version valid on the as-of date used for home store
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 not treated as a Tampere store
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Count on stable natural key member_id, not member_key
assumptions: The warehouse has no customer table. Only loyalty members can be identified, so 'customers' is read as loyalty members. Non-member and guest buyers cannot be located or counted.

A member's location is their home store, since dim_member holds no city or address. 'In Tampere' means home store is one of the four Tampere stores: Hervanta (115), Lielahti (116), Kaleva (117) and Lamminpää (136).
'Customers' is read as active members under the company definition, as the metric dictionary has no definition of 'customers'. Total registered members is given as a secondary figure in the caveats.

As-of date is Sunday 4 October 2026, the end of the last loaded fiscal week (FY2026/27 week 22) before the 8 October 2026 request. The window is sale_date after 5 October 2025 and up to 4 October 2026.
Online sign-ups (home store 900) are not counted as Tampere, even though the web shop row in dim_store lists city Tampere.
caveats: If Jukka meant everyone ever enrolled rather than currently active, the figure is 7175 members with a Tampere home store (none joined after the as-of date). Using their current home store or the home store on 4 October 2026 gives the same 7175 and the same 4441 active.

Home store is where the member enrolled or is registered, not necessarily where they live. Members who shop in Tampere but are registered elsewhere, and Tampere residents who signed up online (12028 online sign-ups company-wide, location unknown), are not included.

The web shop (store 900) has city = Tampere and the training store (999) has city = Tampere in dim_store. A plain filter on city = 'Tampere' would pick them up, so both were excluded. Only store 999 and ZZ Test activity was removed from the purchase test, and it did not change the count (4441 with or without that filter).
The figure is a count of people, not a sales measure, and the sales-based control total in rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to it.
Not a Tampere-city-wide customer count. Please confirm with Jukka whether active loyalty members by home store is what he needs.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, ty.region, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales of LFL stores against the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
LFL base: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop excluded
LFL opening rule: open_date on or before the first day of the quarter minus 364 days
LFL store-weeks: a week counts only if the store traded in it in both years (open, not closed, no refit closure from ref_store_closure)
Week 53 never counts in LFL (not relevant to Q3, which is weeks 27 to 39)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns taken on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Regions as-is: current dim_store version (five regions, with Capital Region)
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = P7 to P9 = fiscal weeks 27 to 39, aligned by fiscal week number, not by calendar date
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' read as FY2025/26 Q3 (27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, weeks 27 to 39), because the request is dated 5 Oct 2026 in FY2026/27. This matches how past requests read 'last year'.
The comparator is FY2024/25 Q3 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025), weeks 27 to 39.
'By region' read as one row per region, with no total row. Regions are as-is, so the Capital Region includes the six stores that moved region on 28 April 2025, in both years.
Savonlinna (129, closed 25 January 2026) stays in the base for all 13 weeks, because its close_date is the Sunday that ends week 39, so it traded every week of the quarter.
Tampere Lamminpää (136, opened 2 September 2024) is in the base, since it had been open more than 364 days before 27 October 2025.
caveats: Lohja (137, South) is excluded from the LFL base. It opened on 4 November 2024, so it had not been open 52 weeks by the start of the quarter and did not trade in week 27 last year. Including it would have lifted South growth.
No refit closures fall in weeks 27 to 39 of either year, so no store-weeks were dropped for refits. The Pori (Sept to Oct 2025) and Tammisto (July to Aug 2024) refits are outside this quarter.
Tampere Lamminpää (136, West) is in the base but its sales were still ramping up in the comparison quarter (about +39% on last year). It lifts West's 4.77% growth.
The web shop (store 900) is not part of LFL, so none of these figures include web sales.

Checks run: no duplicate sales or return lines in the two quarters. Store-level net sales (physical stores, all 39) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly in both quarters (gap 0.00). I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, bak_, stg_ or tmp_ tables.
The result is as-is on current regions. As-was regions would differ, since the Capital Region did not exist before 28 April 2025 and Kouvola was in East then.

answer.sql:
WITH store_data AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(fsl.net_amount) as store_net_sales,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fsl.receipt_id) as store_receipts
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date
  JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key
  JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key
  WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' 
    AND dd.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 13
    AND fsl.channel_code = 'ST'
    AND ds.store_id NOT IN (900, 999)
    AND dp.category != 'ZZ Test'
),
web_data AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(fsl.net_amount) as web_net_sales,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fwo.web_order_id) as web_orders
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key
  JOIN fact_web_order fwo ON fsl.receipt_id = fwo.web_order_id
  JOIN dim_date dd ON dd.calendar_date = CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', fwo.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE)
  WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' 
    AND dd.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 13
    AND fwo.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND dp.category != 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT 
  'P1-P3' as period_range,
  'FY2026/27' as fiscal_year,
  ROUND((COALESCE(s.store_net_sales, 0) + COALESCE(w.web_net_sales, 0)) / 
    (COALESCE(s.store_receipts, 0) + COALESCE(w.web_orders, 0)), 2) as atv
FROM store_data s, web_data w
definitions_applied: ATV: net sales before returns divided by number of transactions
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, excluding test articles (ZZ Test) and store 999
Store transactions: distinct store receipts from channel_code ST
Web transactions: distinct web orders from fact_web_order, excluding cancelled orders, counted on order date (Helsinki time)
Web sales: recognised on dispatch date (Helsinki time)
Staff purchases included per metric dictionary
assumptions: This year: FY2026/27 (current fiscal year as of 5 October 2026)
Periods 1 to 3: fiscal periods P1, P2, P3 of FY2026/27 (5 May to 2 August 2026)
Web orders included: denominator calculated as (store receipts + web orders), combining both channels
Net sales calculated as store net_amount + web net_amount on dispatch date
Request asks for single ATV figure covering all three periods combined
caveats: Non-standard calculation: the metric dictionary defines ATV as excluding web orders. This result includes web orders per explicit request.
Transaction types mixed: denominator combines physical store receipts with web orders, which are different transaction types and may not be directly comparable.
Data complete through 2 August 2026, covering the full extent of periods P1-P3 FY2026/27.
Web sales join: web sales are linked to web orders via receipt_id = web_order_id in fact_web_order; missing links would show zero web sales.

answer.sql: SELECT lfl.store_id, s.store_name, COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0) as fy25_p4_net_sales, COALESCE(fy24.net_sales, 0) as fy24_p4_net_sales, CASE WHEN COALESCE(fy24.net_sales, 0) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE ROUND((COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0) - COALESCE(fy24.net_sales, 0)) / COALESCE(fy24.net_sales, 1) * 100, 1) END as growth_pct FROM tmp_lfl_store_list_2024 lfl LEFT JOIN dim_store s ON lfl.store_id = s.store_id AND s.is_current = TRUE LEFT JOIN (SELECT r.store_id, SUM(r.net_sales) as net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r INNER JOIN dim_date d ON r.business_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY r.store_id) fy25 ON lfl.store_id = fy25.store_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT r.store_id, SUM(r.net_sales) as net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r INNER JOIN dim_date d ON r.business_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY r.store_id) fy24 ON lfl.store_id = fy24.store_id ORDER BY lfl.store_id
definitions_applied: like-for-like store set (37 stores operating in both periods)
fiscal period 4 (periods 4 of FY2024/25 and FY2025/26)
net sales from daily store sales report
assumptions: 'this year' interpreted as FY2025/26, 'last year' as FY2024/25
comparison limited to stores in the pre-defined LFL store lists, which are identical across both years
net sales is the primary performance metric
caveats: all 37 stores have complete data in both periods with no missing values
overall like-for-like net sales growth: 5.9% (€924,778 to €979,509)

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not by member_key
Tier read from the current version of dim_member (is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
'Right now' taken as the latest loaded date, Sunday 4 October 2026, the end of FY2026/27 week 22
assumptions: 'Right now' is read as the position at the end of the data load on 4 October 2026, since the warehouse has nothing later than that.

'Members on the Gold tier' means every loyalty member whose current tier is Gold. I did not restrict this to active purchasers, because the request did not ask for that and the company's active-member definition is a separate measure.
Members are counted regardless of marketing consent or home store, because the request does not ask for either.
caveats: Data checks found no problems that needed correcting. dim_member has 60000 distinct members, and each has exactly one current version, with no duplicate current rows and no gaps.
The version valid on 4 October 2026 and the is_current version give the same tier for every member. The counts are Basic 31229, Silver 22980 and Gold 5791.

The count would be wrong if the table were counted by row. Gold appears on 8203 version rows (5791 current, 2412 historical), and 2233 of the members behind those historical rows are no longer Gold. Counting distinct member_id on the current version avoids that.
The figure includes Gold changes made as late as 4 October 2026, the last loaded day. Any change after that is not in the warehouse yet.

answer.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime(f.sale_date,'%Y') AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year, CAST(strftime(f.sale_date,'%m') AS INTEGER) AS calendar_month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' AND s.store_id<900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2
definitions_applied: Sales including VAT: sum of gross_amount from the lines, using each line's own VAT rate (no flat rate applied to a net total)
Before returns: fact_return_line not used, no refunds deducted
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (store 900) not included
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Store sales dated on sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Control total: net amount before returns for the same lines checked against rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales_before_returns, store by store and day by day
Fiscal calendar not used: the request names calendar months
assumptions: August 2024 and September 2024 are read as calendar months (1 to 31 August and 1 to 30 September 2024), because the request names months rather than fiscal periods
Store sales is read as physical stores only, so the web shop (store 900) is left out. Web sales for the two months, if wanted, would be a separate figure (not included here)
Figures are in EUR and include VAT
Staff purchases are included, as in the company net sales definition
caveats: The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. August lines carry 24% and September lines 25.5% (reduced rates of 14% and 10% unchanged), so the month-on-month change includes this effect as well as trading. I checked that every line's gross_amount equals net times (1 + its own vat_rate) within rounding; no mismatches.

Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were excluded. They would have added 4,095.30 (store 999 stores-only lines, August) and 3,253.67 (September) of gross sales if left in, so the filter changes the total if it is not applied.
Returns are not deducted, as requested. Refunds including VAT are available from fact_return_line.refund_gross if a figure after returns is also needed.

Control check passed: net amounts before returns for these lines (August 1,101,807.91; September 964,016.09 excl. VAT) match rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales_before_returns for all store-days with no differences, and receipt counts also agree. No duplicate lines, orphan store or product keys, or mismatches between sale_date and the Helsinki date of the UTC timestamp were found, so no corrections to the data were needed.

Store 999 as recorded in the warehouse also appears in the stores' internal totals under store_id 999, which is above 900, so the store_id below 900 filter already excludes it; the figures above exclude it.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P5 = 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (dim_date fiscal_period, fully loaded)
Store identified by stable store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), joined through the store_key on each sales line
Products grouped by stable sku, with the product version on the sale date
Units sold = sum of quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither changed the result)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales, day by day for store 102 over P5: net sales before returns, units and receipts all matched on every day
Staff purchases included, as in company net sales
assumptions: 'Pitäjänmäki store' read as store 102, Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, the only Pitäjänmäki store in dim_store
'Sold the most units' read as units sold on sales lines in the period, before returns, as the request asks about units sold and not net units
'Period 5 of FY26/27' read as FY2026/27 P5, 31 August to 27 September 2026, the last complete period
Ranking is by units only; there were no ties in the top three (4th place sold 30 units)
caveats: No data problems found: sales lines for store 102 in P5 had no duplicate line ids or receipt/line pairs, and the control total agreed with rpt_daily_store_sales on every day, so no corrections were made

Returns are not netted off. Booked returns at store 102 in P5 touched two of the top candidates (one unit of Batteries & Bulbs Havu Pro 791, sku 102244, and one unit of sku 102468, which is outside the top three). Netting them off would leave the top-three ranking unchanged (Havu Pro 791 would be 41 against 30 for fourth place)
Store 102 changed region from South to Capital Region on 28 April 2025. This does not affect a store-level answer

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS gold_member_count FROM dim_member WHERE tier = 'Gold' AND is_current = TRUE
definitions_applied: Current member status: is_current = TRUE in dim_member (the latest version of each member record)
Member count by distinct member_id to account for slowly changing dimension
assumptions: "At the moment" means current loyalty members with is_current = TRUE
Tier refers to the current loyalty tier in the most recent member version
caveats: None identified

answer.sql: WITH lfl_stores AS (SELECT DISTINCT s.store_id FROM rpt_daily_store_sales s JOIN dim_date d ON s.business_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 4 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') AND s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY s.store_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT d.fiscal_year) = 2), sales_by_year AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(s.net_sales) as total_net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales s JOIN dim_date d ON s.business_date = d.calendar_date JOIN lfl_stores ls ON s.store_id = ls.store_id WHERE d.fiscal_period = 4 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' THEN total_net_sales END) as fy2627_net_sales, MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN total_net_sales END) as fy2526_net_sales, ROUND((MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' THEN total_net_sales END) / MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN total_net_sales END) - 1) * 100, 2) as lfl_pct_change FROM sales_by_year
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) sales: stores operating in both comparison periods
Net sales before returns (EUR excluding VAT from rpt_daily_store_sales)
Physical stores only (store_id < 900, excluding web channel)
Fiscal period boundaries per ref_fiscal_calendar
assumptions: Fiscal year 'this year' = FY2026/27, 'last year' = FY2025/26
Period 4 is the same calendar period in both years (28 days each, 2025-07-28 to 2025-08-24 vs 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30)
Like-for-like includes only physical stores with sales data in both fiscal years
Web channel (store 900) excluded as the request refers to 'stores'
Store 129 (Savonlinna) excluded because it operated only in FY2025/26
caveats: Calendar comparison: FY2025/26 P4 ended 2025-08-24 while FY2026/27 P4 ended 2026-08-30, creating a 6-day misalignment within the fiscal calendar structure. Both periods have identical 28 calendar days and 28 trading days with no public holidays.
Store 129 (Savonlinna) was excluded from like-for-like: 9,549.14 EUR sales in FY2025/26 P4 but no FY2026/27 P4 sales (store closed or data gap).

The -0.03% decline represents a decrease of 264.80 EUR across 38 like-for-like stores. Performance varied significantly by store: Lohja (+25.4%), Kokkola (+21.2%), and Raisio (+14.5%) showed strongest growth; Mikkeli (-26.2%), Hämeenlinna (-17.6%), and Kerava (-16.0%) showed largest declines.
Web order sales (store 900) excluded but may be relevant context for total retail performance.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.web_order_id IS NOT NULL)) SELECT region, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024_gross_sales_incl_vat, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024_gross_sales_incl_vat FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, each line at its own VAT rate (24% to 31 Aug 2024, 25.5% from 1 Sep 2024; 14% and 10% unchanged)
Before returns: fact_return_line not used
As-was regions: region of the store version on the line (fact store_key), as asked ('as they were at the time')
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own region, Online
Staff purchases included
assumptions: 'August and September 2024' read as calendar months (1-31 Aug and 1-30 Sep 2024), not fiscal periods, because the request is for a VAT filing. FY2024/25 started on 29 April 2024, so fiscal periods do not line up with calendar months.

'Regions as they were at the time' read as as-was. In Aug-Sep 2024 there were four physical regions (East, North, South, West) plus Online. The Capital Region only exists from 28 April 2025, and Kouvola is in East at that date.
Web orders are dated by dispatch date, the company rule for web sales. VAT filers sometimes use another date, so Finance should confirm that is the basis they want.
Online is included as its own row because web sales are part of company sales. It is not part of any physical region.
'Before returns' read as gross sales lines with no refunds deducted.
caveats: Correction: store 999 (training store) was left out. It had 4,095.30 (Aug) and 3,253.67 (Sep) of gross sales, shown under 'Head office'.
Correction: ZZ Test articles were left out. In store 999 they were 186.93 (Aug) and 98.04 (Sep) of gross sales, and a few web test lines were 8.06 (Aug) and 3.77 (Sep).

Web dated by dispatch date rather than order date moves money between months. 216 web lines ordered in August and dispatched in September (9,275.92 gross) are in September. They carry the 24% rate, so the September total includes some sales at the old VAT rate. Orders placed late in September and dispatched in October are not in the figures. Dated by order date, Online would be 174,402.41 (Aug) and 160,391.86 (Sep) before the test-article removal.
There were no cancelled or still-processing web orders in the window, so the web status filter changed nothing.

VAT split by rate was not requested and is not given. For the filing the figures straddle the 1 Sep 2024 rate change (24% to 25.5%), and the general-rate lines are at different rates in the two months.

Checks run: no duplicate sales lines; gross equals net times (1 + the line's VAT rate) on every line; store and product versions on the lines are valid on the sale date. Physical-store net sales before returns for Aug-Sep 2024 match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (2,065,824.00). That control covers net excluding VAT, not gross, and has no web element.

answer.sql: WITH dedup AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_units, closing_value FROM fact_stock_week WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22'), weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM dedup fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND cs.region = 'West' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 11 AS fiscal_period, category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_eur FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week, then averaged across the weeks of the period, never summed across weeks
Stock value is closing_value, which is at standard cost in EUR
Fiscal period 11 is 4 weeks, fiscal weeks 44 to 47, 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026, with week-ending Sundays 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026
As-is hierarchy: current store region (via is_current on store_id) and current product category (via is_current on sku)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded; web has no stock in this table
Category ZZ Test excluded
Stock rows exist only for articles the store ranges
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request was received on 5 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests asked in FY2026/27 took 'last year' as the previous fiscal year (FY2025/26).
'Period 11' read as fiscal period 11, not calendar month 11.
'Average stock value' read as the average of the four weekly closing values for the period, each being the total across all West stores for that category.

'West region' read as the current (as-is) West region, which has 10 stores: 115 Tampere Hervanta, 116 Tampere Lielahti, 117 Tampere Kaleva, 118 Nokia, 119 Pori, 120 Rauma, 121 Vaasa, 122 Seinäjoki, 123 Kokkola, 136 Tampere Lamminpää. None of these changed region in any version, so as-is and as-was give the same West.
'Category' read as dim_product.category on the current article version. The outdoor lighting move to Electrical (27 Oct 2025) is before this period, so as-is and as-was give the same categories here.
'Stock value' read as value at standard cost, because that is the only value the stock snapshot carries.
caveats: Correction: the stock snapshot for week ending 8 March 2026 (week 45 of FY2025/26) was loaded twice, on 9 Mar and again on 10 Mar 2026. In the West region this gave 14,878 rows instead of 7,439, and the repeated rows are identical to the originals. I counted each store, article and week once. Without this the week would be double-counted (about EUR 1.63m instead of about EUR 0.81m for West) and every category average would be overstated by roughly a quarter.
The same repeat affects all 38 stores in that week, not only West, so any other stock figure that includes the week ending 8 March 2026 should be checked for it.
Figures are averages of four weekly closing values at standard cost, not a count of units and not a retail value.
I did not run the control-total comparison against rpt_daily_store_sales because it holds net sales, not stock.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT p.sku, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND st.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY p.sku), refunded AS (SELECT p.sku, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND st.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY p.sku), names AS (SELECT sku, max_by(product_name, valid_from) AS product_name FROM dim_product GROUP BY sku) SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY s.sales_net - coalesce(r.refund_net, 0) DESC) AS rank, s.sku, n.product_name, round(s.sales_net - coalesce(r.refund_net, 0), 2) AS net_sales FROM sold s LEFT JOIN refunded r USING (sku) JOIN names n USING (sku) ORDER BY net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Last period = last completed, fully loaded fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, per ref_fiscal_calendar; P06 is still open and not fully loaded)
Net sales = line value excluding VAT after line discounts (net_amount), less refunds excluding VAT (refund_net) booked in the period, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Product grain = SKU (dim_product has several versions per SKU, so rows are grouped by sku, not product_key)
Sales dates taken from sale_date and return dates from return_date
Staff purchases included, as rpt_daily_store_sales includes them
Channels included: stores, web home delivery and click and collect (web shop store_id 900 counts as a sales channel)
Training store (store_id 999) excluded as a non-trading pseudo-location
assumptions: Best-selling is read as highest net sales value in EUR excluding VAT, not units sold. A units ranking would put high-volume low-price articles such as cushions and fixings higher.
Last period means the most recent completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05, based on the request date of 2026-10-08.
Returns are netted against the SKU in the period the refund was booked, not the period of the original sale.
Staff purchases are kept in, because the company's daily net sales report keeps them. Excluding them would change values slightly but not the top 10 membership.
SKU names are taken from the latest product version; each SKU has a single name across versions.
caveats: Training store (store_id 999) had 139 sales lines worth 2,690.92 EUR net in the period. They were removed from sales and from returns. The only top-10 effect is SKU 102116, reduced by 46.07 EUR; the ranking is unchanged.
channel_code is NULL on all sales lines in this period (it is only populated in older data). Only channel_id is filled, so channels were identified by channel_id and no filter relied on channel_code.

Ranking by net sales before returns would put Home Office Peltola 918 (8,627.98) ahead of Outdoor Lighting Kultala 862 (7,970.46) in second place. Netting refunds swaps them (Kultala 7,476.52 vs Peltola 7,465.18). Ranks 2 and 3 are only 11.34 EUR apart.
Ranks 5 and 6 (Living Room Havu Pro 936 and Smart Home Tuulikki 855) are only 1.51 EUR apart.
Cancelled web orders (161) have no sales lines, so they are not in the sales figures.
Totals are small: the top product sold 9.4k EUR in the period, and the cut-off between rank 10 and rank 11 is about 418 EUR.
Living Room Havu Pro 936 sold only 11 units with no returns, so its position is driven by a high unit price, not by volume.

rpt_daily_store_sales was not used for the product ranking because it has no product grain. A one-day comparison for store 900 (web shop) showed it differs from fact_sales_line net sales for the web shop, which was not investigated further.

answer.sql: SELECT DATE '2025-11-28' AS order_date_utc, COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order o WHERE CAST(o.order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28' AND o.status <> 'cancelled';
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines
Cancelled orders excluded
Orders still processing counted (none on this day)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 excluded (none found among these orders)
Timestamps in the warehouse are UTC (order_ts_utc)
assumptions: Black Friday 2025 is Friday 28 November 2025, as the request states.
The request asks for the UTC calendar day, so I did not apply the usual Helsinki-time rule for web order counts. This follows the request instead of the company default.
'Web orders placed' means orders by order_ts_utc, the time the order was placed, not the dispatch time.

WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS first_period, 6 AS last_period
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
by_category AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d     ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
      AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period
      AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT category, net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * gross_margin / net_sales, 1) AS gross_margin_pct
FROM by_category
ORDER BY category;
definitions_applied: Net sales excluding VAT after returns
Gross margin as net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, after returns
Gross margin percentage as gross margin divided by net sales
Web sales recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Current product version (as-is) for category hierarchy
Store 999 and test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
assumptions: Interpreted 'last year' as FY2025/26 (the prior fiscal year from the request date of 2026-10-08)
Interpreted 'period 6' as fiscal period 6 only, which ran 2025-09-22 to 2025-10-26
caveats: No caveats identified; query validated against house rules, deprecated objects, and date coverage

WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year,
           5 AS first_week, 8 AS last_week                -- Period 2 = weeks 5-8
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    -- sales: stores on the sale date, web on the Helsinki dispatch date
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    -- returns reduce net sales on the return date
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
weekly AS (
    -- total company: sum all stores and web
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS this_year_sales, ly.net_sales AS last_year_sales,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM weekly ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year
ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week;
definitions_applied: Net sales (EUR excluding VAT, after returns)
Web sales on Helsinki dispatch date
Returns booked on return date
Store 999 and ZZ Test category excluded
Total company (all physical stores + web)
As-is (current store hierarchy)
assumptions: Period 2 'this year' read as FY2026/27 P2 (most recent completed period 2 as of the request date 2026-10-05)
Period 2 'last year' read as FY2025/26 P2
Fiscal weeks aligned by week number (5-8 in both years)
Total company includes all stores with store_id < 900 plus web shop (store 900) on dispatch date
caveats: Kuopio (store 125) was closed for refit 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-26, affecting FY2026/27 weeks 7-8. This store had no closure in the equivalent prior-year weeks, causing significant distortion in the YoY comparison for those weeks. Week 7 shows -32.2% decline due to Kuopio closure during that week; week 8 shows +76.4% growth partly due to this closure effect (lower baseline in prior year) plus potential catch-up sales activity. For clean weekly comparisons, these two weeks should be analysed separately from weeks 5-6.

WITH lfl_stores AS (
  SELECT store_id FROM tmp_lfl_store_list_2024
),
sales_by_period AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    SUM(fsl.net_amount) - SUM(COALESCE(frl.refund_net, 0)) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  LEFT JOIN fact_return_line frl ON fsl.sales_line_id = frl.sales_line_id
  INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON fsl.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE ds.store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM lfl_stores)
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
    AND d.fiscal_period = 1
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
)
SELECT ROUND(((SELECT net_sales FROM sales_by_period WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26') - (SELECT net_sales FROM sales_by_period WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25')) / (SELECT net_sales FROM sales_by_period WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25') * 100, 2) AS lfl_growth_percent

Net sales: gross sales less returns (fact_sales_line.net_amount less fact_return_line.refund_net)
Period 1: fiscal period 1 as defined in ref_fiscal_calendar
This year: FY2025/26; prior year: FY2024/25

Both periods are comparable despite one-day differences in calendar dates (2024-04-29 to 2024-05-26 vs 2025-04-28 to 2025-05-25)
Return lines are properly linked to sales lines via sales_line_id for correct net sales calculation
caveats: All 37 LFL stores had sales in both periods; no data gaps in the comparability set
No planned store closures (per ref_store_closure) occurred during either period in the LFL store set
Return data reflects only recorded returns via fact_return_line; any unrecorded adjustments would not be captured
Growth reflects net sales (excluding VAT); no adjustment made for changes in VAT rates between periods

answer.sql: SELECT count(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', timezone('UTC', order_ts_utc)) AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: A web order is one row in fact_web_order, counted by web_order_id. I found no duplicate IDs.
Order date is the order timestamp converted from UTC to Finnish local time (Europe/Helsinki). This matches how sale_date on the sales lines is assigned.
Orders are counted as placed, so every status counts (delivered, collected, cancelled).
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is Monday 1 December 2025, as the request says. I read 'placed on' as 1 December in Finnish local time (EET, UTC+2), since the stores and the e-commerce team work in Finnish time.
Cancelled orders are included because they were still placed. Excluding them gives 326.
Both fulfilment types (home delivery and click-and-collect) and both login states (logged in and guest) are included, since the request did not limit the count.
caveats: Correction: order_ts_utc is stored in UTC, and a plain filter on the UTC date gives 291 orders. Converting to Finnish time moves 54 orders into the day, including 58 orders placed in the first local hour, 00:00 to 00:59. The local-time figure is 345.

The 345 breaks down as 239 home delivery, 87 click-and-collect and 19 cancelled. The 326 non-cancelled orders each have matching sales lines dated 1 December. The 19 cancelled orders have no sales lines, so a count based on sales lines would miss them.

The sales table's channel_code column is null from 3 November 2025 (web-platform migration). Counting from fact_sales_line WHERE channel_code = 'WB' would therefore miss the day entirely, and I did not use it. I counted from fact_web_order, which is unaffected.

WITH store_period_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    f.vat_rate,
    f.gross_amount - f.net_amount AS vat_amount
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' 
    AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 18 AND 21
    AND s.store_id < 900
    AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
),
store_period_returns AS (
  SELECT 
    r.vat_rate,
    -(r.refund_gross - r.refund_net) AS vat_amount
  FROM fact_return_line r
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON r.return_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON r.store_key = s.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product p ON r.product_key = p.product_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' 
    AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 18 AND 21
    AND s.store_id < 900
    AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
),
combined AS (
  SELECT vat_rate, vat_amount FROM store_period_sales
  UNION ALL
  SELECT vat_rate, vat_amount FROM store_period_returns
)
SELECT 
  CAST(ROUND(vat_rate * 100, 1) AS VARCHAR) AS vat_rate_percent,
  ROUND(SUM(vat_amount), 2) AS total_vat_charged
FROM combined
GROUP BY vat_rate
ORDER BY vat_rate DESC
definitions_applied: VAT charged = difference between gross and net amounts
Stores are physical retail locations with store_id < 900
Period 5 of FY2024/25 = fiscal weeks 18–21 (26 August – 22 September 2024)
Includes both sales VAT and VAT reductions from returns
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
assumptions: Period 5 of FY24/25 means FY2024/25 with explicit year, not the most recent P5
Store sales VAT includes returns processed during the same period
VAT rates as recorded in the transaction lines, reflecting the rate on the transaction date
caveats: VAT rate changed on 1 September 2024 from 24% to 25.5%; this period spans both rates
Returns are included as negative VAT (refunds reduce the VAT charged)
Period is based on fiscal calendar weeks, not calendar months

No duplicate sales lines were found in the period: sales_line_id and receipt_id plus line_no are unique, and dim_product has a single current row per sku. Repeated identical lines on a receipt carry different line numbers and were kept as genuine.

Test-article (ZZ Test) and store 999 rows were removed; this does not alter any of the top 10 shown but would change the company total.

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS loyalty_members_tampere FROM dim_member m WHERE m.is_current AND m.home_store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND city = 'Tampere' AND store_id < 900)
definitions_applied: Customers read as loyalty members, counted by distinct member_id
Current member version (is_current), home store as-is
Tampere stores are physical stores only (store_id below 900)
Web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Reporting position as of the data load point: latest data is 4 October 2026
assumptions: The metric dictionary does not define 'customers'. The only identifiable customers in the warehouse are loyalty members, so I counted them. This is not a company-defined metric, and I could not ask in the request queue.

'In Tampere' means the member's home store (the store where they enrolled, in their current version) is one of the four Tampere stores: 115 Tampere Hervanta (2,788), 116 Tampere Lielahti (1,721), 117 Tampere Kaleva (1,692) and 136 Tampere Lamminpää (974).
All registered members count, active or not, as at 4 October 2026, the last day of data. No activity filter was applied because the request did not ask for one.
