Web lines dated on the Helsinki dispatch date from fact_web_order (status delivered or collected); cancelled and processing orders have no sales lines
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included (they count in net sales)
Members with no sales in the window count as zero spend and do not change the total
Web shop identified by store_id 900 and dispatch join, not by channel_code
No deprecated, staging, backup or tmp tables or views used
assumptions: Spring Garden Launch 2026 is campaign_id 19 (window 4 to 24 May 2026), the only campaign with that name and year
'Contacted' means the member has at least one exposure row, as in the company definition of a targeted member. This includes contacts that were not delivered
'Spend' means net sales excluding VAT before returns, on the members' own lines, summed across all stores and the web shop

The date range is exactly 4 to 24 May 2026 as the requester specified, which is the campaign window itself. The company's standard uplift window of the campaign plus seven days was not applied because the request names explicit dates
Spend is the total for all contacted members. No holdout comparison or uplift was asked for, so none is given
caveats: The mailing list size (16,624) less the holdout (1,597) gives 15,027 members expected to be contacted. The exposure table shows 15,001 distinct members, 26 fewer. I could not tell from the warehouse why. The 15,001 is what the exposure data supports
Of the 15,001 contacted members, 14,814 had at least one delivered contact, and 1,266 exposure rows were undelivered. All 15,001 are counted as contacted

Only 2,605 of the 15,001 contacted members bought anything in the window. The 190,687.59 EUR is made up of 155,518.67 EUR in stores and 35,168.92 EUR on the web, and includes 2,540.79 EUR of staff purchases
Figures are before returns. Refunds in the window are not deducted, because the request asks for spend and company convention for campaign analysis is net sales before returns

Checks: no member is both contacted and in the holdout, all exposure rows fall inside 4 to 24 May 2026, and there were no duplicate keys in the sales, member, store or product tables for the period. The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to a member subset, so it was not run
Store 999 and ZZ Test filters were applied. Whether they change this total was not tested separately
The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so the 4 to 24 May 2026 range is fully covered

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE s.store_name = 'Hyvinkää' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND p.category = 'Cleaning & Household' GROUP BY s.store_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Units sold: quantity from fact_sales_line (initial sales transactions at point of sale)
Cleaning Products: category 'Cleaning & Household' from dim_product
Current fiscal year: FY2026/27 (based on current date 2026-10-15)
Fiscal period 5: 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27 per ref_fiscal_calendar
assumptions: Request for 'this year' interpreted as current fiscal year FY2026/27
Request for 'Cleaning Products' mapped to product category 'Cleaning & Household', the only cleaning-related category in the warehouse
Units sold counted as all sales transactions, not net of subsequent returns
caveats: Of the 221 units sold, 5 units were subsequently returned within the same fiscal period (2 for wrong size/fit, 2 for not as described, 1 customer changed mind). These returns are not subtracted from the sales count as they represent completed transactions.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0), 2) AS net_revenue, ROUND(SUM(f.standard_cost) - COALESCE(SUM(r.standard_cost_returned), 0), 2) AS cost_of_goods, ROUND((SUM(f.net_amount) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0)) - (SUM(f.standard_cost) - COALESCE(SUM(r.standard_cost_returned), 0)), 2) AS gross_margin FROM fact_sales_line f LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id AND r.return_date >= '2025-01-27' AND r.return_date <= '2025-04-27' INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND s.region = 'South' AND f.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin: net revenue minus cost of goods sold, both net of returns
Net revenue: sum of net_amount (sales excluding VAT after discounts) less sum of refund_net (returns processed in Q4)
Cost of goods: sum of standard_cost less sum of standard_cost_returned (returns processed in Q4)
Staff purchases excluded from margin calculation
Q4 FY2024/25 fiscal period: 27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025
assumptions: Gross margin requested as absolute amount in EUR, not as a percentage
Return attribution: returns are counted against the quarter in which the return was processed, not the original sale quarter
Region filter applies to store region at time of sale
All calculations use net_amount (excluding VAT) for consistency with warehouse conventions
caveats: 1,311 return lines out of 41,212 sales lines in the period were deducted from gross margin
Results reflect only sales to non-staff customers in stores with South region classification

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, st.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM (SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) AS rn FROM fact_sales_line WHERE sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-08-25' AND DATE '2025-09-21') f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.rn = 1 AND st.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), rets AS (SELECT r.return_date AS business_date, st.store_id, -r.refund_net AS net_sales FROM (SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY return_line_id ORDER BY return_ts_utc) AS rn FROM fact_return_line WHERE return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-08-25' AND DATE '2025-09-21') r JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE r.rn = 1 AND st.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), net AS (SELECT store_id, sum(net_sales) AS net_sales FROM (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rets) GROUP BY 1), trading AS (SELECT st.store_id, count(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store st JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-08-25' AND DATE '2025-09-21' WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900 AND d.is_trading_day AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.calendar_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY n.net_sales / t.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.region, round(n.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, t.trading_days, round(n.net_sales / t.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM net n JOIN trading t USING (store_id) JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day, physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) excluded
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT after returns; sales on sale_date, returns deducted on their own return date
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Trading days: days after opening, before closure, outside ref_store_closure refit closures, and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
A store that traded only part of the period is still listed, ranked on its own trading days (Pori)
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P5 = 25 Aug 2025 to 21 Sep 2025 (weeks 18 to 21, 28 days)
Regions shown as-is (current dim_store version, five regions including Capital Region)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales (net sales and net sales before returns)
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_ tables, channel_code) not used
assumptions: 'Period 5 last year' read as FY2025/26 P5 (25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025), because the request was made on 8 Oct 2026 (FY2026/27) and past requests in this situation took last year as the previous fiscal year (FY2025/26).
Ranking is by net sales per trading day, descending; ties would share a rank (none occurred).

Region is the current (as-is) region. As-was would put stores 101 to 105 in South and 114 in East, which is how the original four-region structure worked before 28 April 2025, but that structure no longer applies in the period requested, which started after the change.

Net sales per trading day is net sales for the store over the period divided by its own trading days, so Pori (14 trading days) is ranked on that basis even though its total is lower than stores trading the full 28 days.
No web sales are included, since the league table covers physical stores only.
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line contains duplicate rows for Tampere Lielahti (store 116) from 15 to 21 Sep 2025. A re-load on 23 Sep 2025 (etl_loaded_at 03:12) re-inserted 418 lines that had already been loaded the day after each sale, under new sales_line_ids. Left in, they would add EUR 10,390.53 to the store's net sales and wrongly lift it from rank 7 to rank 4 or so (EUR 49,995.41 before returns versus the correct EUR 39,604.88). I kept one row per receipt_id + line_no (the earliest load). After this fix every store matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (difference 0.00 for all 39 stores, net sales and net sales before returns).

Pori (119) was shut for a refit from 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025, so it traded only 14 of the 28 days in this period (25 Aug to 7 Sep). Its figure is per those 14 trading days and it is ranked 10th on that basis; its period total of EUR 16,057.86 is not comparable with the full-period totals of other stores.
No public holidays or other closed days fall within 25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025, so no store lost trading days to holidays.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026, after this period, so it was fully trading in P5 FY2025/26 and is listed. Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in 2024 and were open for the whole period.
The league table uses the later region assignment (as-is). Stores 101 to 105 are shown as Capital Region and 114 Kouvola as South, as in current management reporting.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after sale, but this table deducts returns on their own return date within the period, so it is not a sale-week cohort measure.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as web_orders_placed FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28'
definitions_applied: Web order = one row in fact_web_order table
Order placed = order_ts_utc date in UTC timezone
Black Friday 2025 = 28 November 2025
assumptions: Counted all orders with order_ts_utc on 28 November 2025 UTC, including cancelled orders
order_ts_utc timestamp used to determine the order placement date, not dispatch or any other date
No filtering by status; 'placed' includes all orders regardless of whether they were later cancelled, collected, or delivered
caveats: All 377 orders have valid order_ts_utc values; no NULL timestamps detected
Breakdown: 260 delivered, 97 collected, 20 cancelled; all included in the count as they were all placed on 28 November
Mix of member logins (283) and guest orders (94)
Fulfilment methods: 276 home delivery, 101 click-and-collect

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS this_year_net_sales, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS last_year_net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), not the order date
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store_id 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar: fiscal weeks and period 2 from dim_date (weeks 5 to 8, Monday to Sunday)
Comparison with the same fiscal week last year, not the same calendar dates
Growth % = this year / last year - 1
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, channel_code or any deprecated table
assumptions: "This year" is the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and "last year" is FY2025/26. This matches how past requests from May 2026 onward read it.

"Period 2" is FY2026/27 P2, 1 to 28 June 2026, weeks 5 to 8. It is complete, because the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026. The comparison is FY2025/26 P2, 26 May to 22 June 2025, weeks 5 to 8.
"Total company" includes the web shop (click-and-collect included) and excludes store 999. History is not restated, so the question of as-is versus as-was does not arise at total-company level.
Sales are net of VAT and net of returns, which is the company definition. The request did not ask for gross or before-returns figures.
Weeks are shown by fiscal week number (5 to 8), each lined up with the same fiscal week of the prior year.
caveats: No correction to the data was needed. In P2 of both years, sales lines have no duplicate keys, every line joins to a store and a product, and web lines all belong to delivered or collected orders. My store-level net sales (stores only, before web) agree with rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (difference 0.00 in every week, with no store off by more than 5 cents).
Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test removed about 2,385 EUR of sales lines in FY2026/27 P2 and 2,226 EUR in FY2025/26 P2, before returns. This is a small change to the totals.

The weeks 7 and 8 growth figures (-32.2% and +76.4%) are mainly a holiday-timing effect, not a trading trend. Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (stores shut by company rule) fall in week 7 this year (19 to 20 June 2026) but in week 8 last year (20 to 21 June 2025). Week 7 this year and week 8 last year each have two shut days. Weeks 7 and 8 together are the fairer comparison: 591,343.83 EUR this year against 535,679.88 EUR last year, +10.4%. The whole period is 1,294,647.64 EUR against 1,195,882.70 EUR, +8.3%.

Kuopio (store 125) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, which covers weeks 7 and 8 of this year. Last year it traded. This lowers this year's weeks 7 and 8 and is not adjusted for. Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 January 2026, so it has sales last year and none this year. This is a total-company comparison, not like-for-like, so both effects stay in the figures.

Web sales are dated by the Helsinki dispatch date, so web sales in week 5 can come from orders placed in the previous week. Web sales were 52,105 EUR in week 5, 60,692 EUR in week 6, 44,949 EUR in week 7 and 72,985 EUR in week 8 this year. Last year they were 40,688 EUR, 35,417 EUR, 44,352 EUR and 30,548 EUR. Part of the total growth comes from the web.

answer.sql: WITH stock AS (SELECT DISTINCT f.store_key, f.product_key, f.week_ending_date, f.closing_value FROM fact_stock_week f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE s.region = 'West' AND f.week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22'), weekly AS (SELECT p.category AS category, st.week_ending_date AS week_ending_date, SUM(st.closing_value) AS weekly_value FROM stock st JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = st.product_key GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(weekly_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_eur FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 11 runs 2026-02-23 to 2026-03-22 (4 weeks, ref_fiscal_calendar, fully loaded)
Stock value = closing_value in fact_stock_week, closing stock at standard cost in EUR
Region = dim_store.region of the store version carried on the stock row (store_key)
Category = dim_product.category of the product version carried on the stock row (product_key)
Average stock value = mean of the four week-ending closing stock totals (Sundays 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026) per category
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26. The request came on 2026-10-05, which falls in FY2026/27.
'Period 11' means fiscal period 11 (the fiscal calendar, not calendar month 11).
Average stock value is the average over the period of the weekly closing stock totals for the whole West region, per category. It is not an average per store or per SKU.
The week ending Sunday 2026-02-22 is left out. It closes the day before period 11 starts.
Values are in EUR at standard cost, the same basis as the warehouse's closing_value. They are not retail value and do not include VAT.
West is the 10 stores with region = 'West' in dim_store (store_id 115 to 123 and 136). The web shop and the training store are not in the region.
caveats: Correction made: the stock snapshot for the week ending 2026-03-08 is loaded twice for the West region (7,439 rows twice, 14,878 in all, loaded 2026-03-09 01:00 and again 2026-03-10 02:45). The copies are identical row for row. I kept one copy. Without this, that week would count double and every category average would be inflated by about 25%, so the West total would read about 1.02 million instead of 813,525.
Other regions have no duplicate loads in this period. West is the only region affected.

Checks that found nothing: closing_value equals closing_units times standard_unit_cost on every row, every stock row matches a product version, there are no negative stock quantities, and no West store was closed for a refit in the period (the only recent closure is store 125 in June 2026).
The ten category averages add up to 813,525.02 EUR, the average total West stock value in the period.
The numbers show West stock at the end of each week, not an average of daily balances.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, s.format FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, s.format AS store_format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold s LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.sales_line_id = s.sales_line_id GROUP BY s.format ORDER BY s.format
definitions_applied: Return rate = refunded net (refund_net) divided by sold net, both excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: sold lines are selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date, then every refund on those lines is added through sales_line_id, whenever and wherever it was booked
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test left out
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 period 2 runs 26 May 2025 to 22 June 2025 (4 weeks)
Format taken from the store version on the sale line; the web shop (store 900) is format Web
Staff purchases kept in, as in net sales
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old tables) not used
assumptions: 'Period 2 last year' was read as FY2025/26 P2. The request is dated 6 October 2026, which falls in FY2026/27, and past requests asked in FY2026/27 read 'last year' as FY2025/26.
'What share of what was sold came back' was read as the company's return rate, by value: refunded net divided by sold net. It is not a share of units or of lines.
'Split by store format' was read as the formats Large, Medium and Small plus Web, which is a format value in the warehouse. The web shop is shown as its own row, not folded into the stores.
The training format (store 999 only) has no row because store 999 is excluded from all sales reporting.
caveats: The 'Training' format (store 999, 126 lines, 2,222.21 EUR net) was excluded. The test-article exclusion (ZZ Test) also removed one web line, about 3.82 EUR net, which lowers the Web sold total slightly (183,102.31 to 183,098.49).
The dim_store.format column comment is out of date. The real values are Large, Medium, Small, Web and Training.

The period is fully complete. The latest return is dated 276 days after 1 January 2026, and the longest gap between a sale and its return is 56 days, so the rates are final. Some returns arrive later than the 30 days the wiki mentions.

Return rate here is a sale-week cohort figure. It counts a refund in the period the item was sold, not the period it came back, so it will not match net sales, where a return reduces sales on its own return date.

Web has a much higher return rate (12.23%) than the stores (4.28% to 4.53%). Web returns are booked to the web shop, but I attributed each refund to the format of the original sale line, so no web refund is counted against a store.

I found 418 duplicated receipt_id and line_no pairs in fact_sales_line, all in September 2025 (about 836 rows, 178 receipts). None are in the period 2 window, so no correction was needed. I found no duplicate sales_line_id, no orphan returns, no refund larger than its sold line, and no VAT mismatches in the period.

As a check on the control totals, sold net per format agrees with the line-level data. The rpt_daily_store_sales control check was not run, because it only holds net sales per store per day and has no format or refund-by-sale-week view.

answer.sql: WITH cur_region AS (SELECT store_id, CASE WHEN store_id = 900 THEN 'Web shop' ELSE region END AS region_line FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 999), movements AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cr.region_line, f.net_amount AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN cur_region cr ON cr.store_id = s.store_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') UNION ALL SELECT d.fiscal_year, cr.region_line, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN cur_region cr ON cr.store_id = s.store_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25')) SELECT region_line AS region, round(sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN amt END), 2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26_q3, round(sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN amt END), 2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25_q3, round(100.0 * (sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN amt END) / sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN amt END) - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM movements GROUP BY region_line ORDER BY CASE region_line WHEN 'Web shop' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, region_line
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns
Returns are booked on the return date and in the store or web shop where the refund was made, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Web shop = store_id 900, covering home delivery and click-and-collect, shown as its own line and not added to any region
Four sales regions: North, South, East, West, plus Capital Region (the newest region, created 2025-04-28)
assumptions: Last year read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (the request is dated 2026-10-06, in FY2026/27), and Q3 as fiscal Q3, not calendar Q3. The year before is FY2024/25.
Net sales read as sales net of returns, excluding VAT, matching the company's daily net sales report
Staff purchases are included, because the daily net sales report includes them (about 1.2 % of sales)
Every store is assigned to its current region in both years, so the two years are comparable
Web shop identified by store_id 900 and not by channel_code, because channel_code is empty on lines after the web-platform migration
Totals across regions and the web shop were not requested and are not shown
caveats: Correction: the regions were redrawn on 2025-04-28. Stores 101 to 105 moved from South to Capital Region and store 114 Kouvola moved from East to South. Fact rows carry the region of the store version at the sale date, so the prior year would show the old regions. I restated both years on the current regions. Using the regions as stored on each row would show a very different South, Capital Region and East.
Correction: store 999 (Training store, head office) has test sales in both quarters, about 0.9 k EUR in total, and is excluded. It is not a region.

Correction: the channel coding changed at the web-platform migration. Older web lines carry channel_code WB, newer ones only carry channel_id (2 home delivery, 3 click and collect). I identified web by the web shop store (900), which captures both. The existing view rpt.v_daily_sales filters on channel_code = 'WB' and would miss the newer web lines and understate the web shop for FY2025/26.
Correction: web returns, booked to the web shop (store 900), are netted off the web line, not any region.

Not like-for-like: Tampere Lamminpää (136, West) opened 2024-09-02 and Lohja (137, South) opened 2024-11-04. Lohja traded for only part of the FY2024/25 Q3 window, which flatters growth in South. These stores added about 97 k EUR of gross sales in the earlier quarter. Pori (119) was shut for a refit until 2025-10-12, before the FY2025/26 Q3 window. Savonlinna (129) closes on 2026-01-25, the last day of the quarter, so it traded the whole quarter.
The 28.1 % growth for the web shop is partly the migration effect on coding. It is calculated on all web lines of both years.
Refunds are deducted in the period they are made, so some FY2025/26 refunds relate to sales from earlier periods (about 9.5 k EUR in stores, 5.2 k EUR on web).

Reconciliation with rpt_daily_store_sales: the returns agree exactly, but before-returns sales differ from the fact table on 91 store-days in FY2025/26 Q3 (about 3.4 k EUR in total, 0.08 %). I did not trace the cause and used the fact tables.
The warehouse holds backup, old and staging tables (bak_, _old, stg_, tmp_), which I did not use.
The first column set uses fiscal_year in the column names because the table has one column per fiscal year (both are fiscal quarter 3).

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28'
definitions_applied: Web orders are counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines, so orders still processing would be included (none fall on this day)
Cancelled orders are not counted as web orders (status <> 'cancelled')
Click-and-collect is counted as web, so those orders are included (101 placed that UTC day, 97 of them not cancelled)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test are excluded from sales work. I checked orders placed 27 to 29 November 2025 and none had a store 999 or ZZ Test line, so this filter changed nothing

The requester asked for the UTC calendar day, which differs from the company default of the Helsinki day. I followed the request and used the UTC day: order_ts_utc cast to a date with no timezone conversion
The result has one row per web_order_id. I checked there are no duplicate order ids in fact_web_order
assumptions: 'Black Friday 2025 (28 November)' means Friday 28 November 2025, counted on the UTC calendar day from 00:00:00 to 23:59:59 UTC
'Placed' means the order timestamp (order_ts_utc), not the dispatch time
Cancelled orders are excluded from 'web orders placed', as the company definition says
caveats: The count is by UTC day as requested. By the Helsinki order date (the company default) the same non-cancelled orders on 28 November 2025 number 350. The Helsinki-day count is not the same set of orders, because Helsinki midnight falls 2 hours before UTC midnight in November, so the two days overlap by 22 hours. The company-standard figure is therefore different from the carrier-aligned 357.
Including the 20 cancelled orders placed on that UTC day, fact_web_order holds 377 rows. Cancelled orders are not web orders under the company definition, so they are left out.
No data problems affected this figure. There were no duplicate order ids, no test orders and no processing orders on the day, so no corrections were needed.

answer.sql: WITH cur AS (SELECT store_id, region AS region_now FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900), sales AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS d, st.store_id, f.net_amount AS amt, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY f.receipt_id, f.line_no ORDER BY f.etl_loaded_at, f.sales_line_id) AS rn FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key WHERE st.store_id < 900 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-04-28' AND DATE '2026-10-04'), rets AS (SELECT r.return_date AS d, st.store_id, -r.refund_net AS amt, 1 AS rn FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = r.store_key WHERE st.store_id < 900 AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-04-28' AND DATE '2026-10-04'), allrows AS (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rets), mapped AS (SELECT a.store_id, a.amt, a.rn, CASE WHEN a.d >= DATE '2026-05-04' THEN 'CY' WHEN a.d <= DATE '2025-09-28' THEN 'PY' END AS yr, CASE WHEN a.d >= DATE '2026-05-04' THEN a.d ELSE a.d + 371 END AS cy_date FROM allrows a WHERE a.d >= DATE '2026-05-04' OR (a.d BETWEEN DATE '2025-04-28' AND DATE '2025-09-28')), clean AS (SELECT * FROM mapped WHERE rn = 1 AND NOT (store_id = 129) AND NOT (store_id = 125 AND cy_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-06-15' AND DATE '2026-07-26') AND NOT (store_id = 119 AND cy_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-14' AND DATE '2026-10-18')) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY lfl_growth_pct DESC) AS rank, region, lfl_growth_pct FROM (SELECT c.region_now AS region, round(100*(sum(CASE WHEN yr='CY' THEN amt END)/sum(CASE WHEN yr='PY' THEN amt END)-1),2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM clean cl JOIN cur c USING (store_id) GROUP BY 1) ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal year: FY2026/27 year to date, from 2026-05-04 (start of P01) to 2026-10-04, the last complete fiscal week in the warehouse (it falls in the still-open P06)
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, with refunds (refund_net, booked on the return date) deducted; staff purchases included, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Stores only: web shop (store 900, channel WB) and the Training store (999) excluded
Region: the current region of each store (dim_store is_current), applied to both years
Comparison base: the same fiscal weeks of FY2025/26, matched by day (prior-year date = this-year date minus 371 days, same weekday)
Like-for-like: stores closed, or closed for a refit, in either period left out for the affected dates in both years
assumptions: 'How they are doing' is read as growth in net sales against the same weeks last year, like-for-like, because a raw YTD total mostly ranks regions by size. Ranked from highest growth to lowest.
'This year so far' is read as the fiscal year to date. Weeks 1 to 5 of P06 are open, so I included the one complete week after P05 (28 Sep to 4 Oct) rather than stopping at 27 Sep.
Five regions means North, South, East, West and the Capital Region, which exists in the warehouse from 28 Apr 2025.
Staff purchases are kept in net sales because the team's own daily store report includes them.

Prior-year Pori refit days (8 Sep to 4 Oct 2025 in the window) are left out, together with the matching days this year (14 Sep to 4 Oct 2026). Kuopio's refit days (15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026) are left out, together with the matching prior-year days.
caveats: Duplicate sales lines: 418 receipt lines in Sept 2025 at Tampere Lielahti (West) were loaded twice (second load on 2025-09-23). I kept one copy of each. Left in, West's prior-year base is overstated and its growth looks 0.7 points lower in the naive figure, and West and South swap places (naive West +2.63%, South +2.11%).
Savonlinna (East) closed on 2026-01-25. It has 60,143 EUR of prior-year sales and none this year, so I excluded it from both years. Left in, it drags East down.

Kuopio (East) was closed for a refit from 15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026 (6 weeks) and Pori (West) from 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025 (5 weeks). I removed those weeks from both years. Without any of these corrections, East shows -11.6%, which is mostly closures and not trading.

Store regions were redrawn on 28 Apr 2025: Capital Region was created from five South stores, and Kouvola moved from East to South. I used the current mapping for both years. The prior-year window starts after the change, so this does not alter the figures, but any comparison with earlier years would need restating.

East is the only region below last year, at -0.19% after the corrections. That is within noise, so East is effectively flat. The gaps between West, South and Capital Region are about 0.2 to 0.8 points, so their order is not firm.
Warehouse tables with bak_, stg_, tmp_ or _old names were not used. The web shop sits in the same sales table as the stores and was filtered out by store number.
Fiscal P06 is not fully loaded, so the 4 October cut-off excludes the incomplete remainder of the period.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date, w.order_member_key, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_member_key IS NOT NULL THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_amount), 1) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.dispatch_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (from fact_web_order.dispatch_ts_utc), not the order date
Net sales excluding VAT (net_amount)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders have been dispatched)
Guest web orders counted as non-member
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date, FY2025/26 periods 9 to 11 (weeks 35 to 47, 22 Dec 2025 to 22 Mar 2026)
Click-and-collect counted as web
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 (request dated 9 Oct 2026), in line with how earlier requests were read
'Periods 9 to 11' read as FY2025/26 P9, P10 and P11, 22 December 2025 to 22 March 2026, all complete in the warehouse
'Share of web sales from loyalty members' read as the company member-share definition applied to web only: member net sales before returns over all web net sales before returns, excluding VAT
Returns are not netted off; the member-share definition is before returns
Result shown as one row per period, with no total across the three periods
caveats: Correction: in fact_sales_line, logged-in web orders lost their member_key on many lines in fiscal weeks 42 to 45 (P10 weeks 42 and 43, P11 weeks 44 and 45). That is 299, 407, 465 and 138 lines in those weeks, 706 in P10 and 603 in P11. Using the line-level member_key would understate the member share (P10 about 51.8% and P11 about 55.8%, against 67.5% and 66.7% here). I took membership from fact_web_order.member_key, which is filled for every logged-in order. Guest orders have no key, and no order key is missing from dim_member.
One ZZ Test web line in P11 was excluded. It is too small to change any rounded figure.
The shares are before returns. A net-of-returns basis would differ slightly, and returns arriving after the period would not all be in yet.
Orders placed but not yet dispatched or cancelled have no sales lines and are not counted. Web sales are dated by dispatch, so some P9 sales come from orders placed before 22 December 2025.
I did not run query_check.py or the rpt_daily_store_sales control total. The control table has no member dimension, so it cannot check a member share.

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) DESC) AS rank, cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns (returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned)
Net sales excluding VAT, with returns booked on their own return date
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: Q4 = periods 10 to 12 (weeks 40 to 52) of FY2024/25, 28 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025 by dim_date (91 days, 3 periods)
As-is reporting: South region taken from the current store version (dim_store is_current)
As-is reporting: product name taken from the current product version (dim_product is_current), grouped by sku
Online (store 900) is its own region, so web sales are not in South
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Q4 of FY24/25' read as FY2024/25 Q4 (P10 to P12), written FY2024/25 in the warehouse

'South region' read as the current (as-is) South, which includes Kouvola (114, moved from East on 28 April 2025) and Lohja (137) and excludes the five stores that became the Capital Region (101 to 105)
'Products' read as individual articles (sku), not subcategories or brands
Ranked on gross margin in EUR (absolute), not margin percentage
Week 53 is not relevant because FY2024/25 has 52 weeks
Stores that were later closed are not an issue for South because Savonlinna (129) is not a South store
caveats: As-is vs as-was: on the regions as they stood during Q4 FY24/25 (before the 28 April 2025 reorganisation), South included stores 101 to 105 and excluded Kouvola. This answer uses the current hierarchy, so those five stores are out and Kouvola is in. A request for 'as they were then' would give a different list.
Net sales for the South stores in the quarter reconcile exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales (EUR 593,853.56 on both).
No duplicate sales or return line IDs were found in the period, and no current-version duplicates in dim_product or dim_store.
Margin uses standard cost, which is revalued each April. The quarter ends on 27 April 2025, so all of it is on the pre-April 2025 cost.
Margin is in EUR excluding VAT.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Trading days: days after opening, before closure, outside refit closures (ref_store_closure) and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) not listed
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 2 = fiscal weeks 5 to 8, 1 to 28 June 2026
Store versions: stores identified by stable store_id, names from the current dim_store version
Control total: store net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' is read as FY2026/27 P2 (1 June to 28 June 2026), the current fiscal year as of the request date 2026-10-07, and a fully loaded period; the same reading was accepted for a 'P2' request in July 2026
'Store ranking' is read as the company store league table, ranked by net sales per trading day, rank 1 = highest
Stores are ranked using their own trading days, so a store that traded only part of the period is still listed
Ties are not present; ranking uses unrounded net sales per trading day
Net sales and trading days are shown beside the ranking measure for context; per-day figure rounded to 2 decimals
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it traded only 14 of the period's 26 trading days. It is ranked on those 14 days (rank 7) and its total net sales (23,993.71) are not comparable with the other stores' totals.
Two closed holidays in the period (Midsummer Eve 19 June and Midsummer Day 20 June) are not counted as trading days, so a full-period store has 26 trading days, not 28.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and had no sales or trading days in the period, so it does not appear.
The ranking is of physical stores only; the web shop (store 900) is not ranked. Click-and-collect and other web sales are not credited to stores.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles are excluded; this does not change any physical-store figure in the period.
Store net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for every store in the period (gap 0.00), and the sales and return lines had no duplicate keys.
Mikkeli (rank 23) and Espoo Lommila (rank 24) are within 0.21 euro per trading day of each other, so their order is marginal.

answer.sql:
WITH dedup AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_units, closing_value
    FROM fact_stock_week
    WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22'
),
weekly AS (
    SELECT cp.category, w.week_ending_date, SUM(w.closing_value) AS closing_value
    FROM dedup w
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = w.store_key
    JOIN dim_store cs  ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = w.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND cs.region = 'West' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 11 AS fiscal_period, category,
       ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_eur
FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P11 = weeks 44 to 47, 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026 (ref_fiscal_calendar), four week-ending Sundays
Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week first, then averaged across the four weeks, never summed across weeks
Stock value is closing_value, at standard cost, EUR
Region and category as-is (current dim_store and dim_product versions, joined on store_id/sku with is_current), so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical
West region means the 10 current West stores (physical stores only, store_id below 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Canonical fact_stock_week used; no staging, backup or tmp tables, no deprecated views
Grain check done at store_key x product_key x week_ending_date before aggregating
assumptions: 'Last year' asked on 5 Oct 2026 (current year FY2026/27) read as FY2025/26, following the past readings for requests made in the same fiscal year (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35)
'Period 11' read as the fiscal period (FY2025/26 P11, 4 weeks), not calendar month 11
'Average stock value' read as the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost, per category
Region as-is, because management reporting is as-is by default and the request did not ask for as-was
Web shop and central warehouse stock are not part of the West region and are not in fact_stock_week
caveats: Duplicate load found and corrected: the week ending 2026-03-08 (week 45) appears twice in fact_stock_week, loaded on 2026-03-09 01:00 and 2026-03-10 02:45, with 7,439 store x article rows duplicated across the chain (all values identical). Left as is, the double-counted week would inflate the P11 average. I kept one row per store_key, product_key and week. Raw P11 rows 116,185, deduplicated 108,746
No other grain problems: after deduplication no store x SKU x week has more than one product version
Week ending 2026-03-01 has 38 more store x article rows chain-wide than the other weeks; I read this as normal range changes and did not adjust it
Figures are not checkable against rpt_daily_store_sales, which holds sales only
Week 53 is not in P11, so the comparison-year question does not arise; no comparison with an earlier year was requested or given

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order o WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web orders are counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines, so orders still processing are included
Orders are counted on the order date in Helsinki time (order_ts_utc converted from UTC), not on the UTC date or the dispatch date
Cancelled orders are excluded
Click-and-collect orders are counted as web orders
Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 are left out of all reporting
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is read as Monday 1 December 2025, as the request states
The count includes both logged-in and guest orders
The count includes home delivery and click-and-collect orders
'Placed' means the order date, not the dispatch date
caveats: The count is by Helsinki order date. Finland was on UTC+2 that day, so the day runs from 22:00 UTC on 30 November to 22:00 UTC on 1 December. A count on the UTC date would give a different number.
I excluded 19 cancelled orders from the 345 orders placed that day (5 guest, 14 logged-in). Including them would give 345.
No test-article or store 999 lines were on any order placed that day, so the test exclusion did not change the total.
I checked that fact_web_order has no duplicate order ids at all and that each of the 326 orders has sales lines and a dispatch time. No other correction was needed.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.category AS category_as_was, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.category, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS garden_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.category_as_was = 'Garden' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after line discounts, less returns booked on their own return date (refund_net)
As-was category: category taken from the dim_product version on each fact row (product_key), not the current version, as the request asked for the old set-up
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (join to fact_web_order, delivered or collected orders); web shop store 900 included as part of the company total
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25 (29 Apr 2024 to 27 Apr 2025, 52 weeks), periods 7 to 12 (28 Oct 2024 to 27 Apr 2025)
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, bak_, stg_, tmp_ tables, old dims) not used
assumptions: "Garden as it was reported at the time" read as the as-was product hierarchy: the category on the product version valid on the transaction date. For FY2024/25 this keeps the Outdoor Lighting subcategory in Garden, because it only moved to Electrical on 27 October 2025.
"Garden net sales" read as the company total (stores plus the web shop), with no region or channel split and no Garden/subcategory breakdown
"P7 to P12 of FY24/25" read as FY2024/25 periods 7 to 12, one row per period; FY2024/25 has 52 weeks, so no week 53 issue
Returns are attributed using the product version on the return line (version at the return date) and booked on the return date, per the company net sales definition
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT
caveats: No corrections were needed for FY2024/25 P7 to P12. I checked these data points: no duplicate sales lines, return lines, product keys or store keys in the range, and no unmatched store or product keys. Every web line has an order with a dispatch time, and the range has no processing or cancelled orders with lines.

The warehouse does hold 418 duplicated receipt and line pairs (836 rows, loaded twice, 16 Sep and 23 Sep 2025), but they are all store sales dated 15 to 21 September 2025, outside this range, so they do not affect these figures. They would double count any query that covers those dates.

The as-was Garden figures are higher than the as-is figures (Outdoor Lighting counted in Electrical) in every period. The difference is the Outdoor Lighting subcategory: P7 19,631.07, P8 19,504.55, P9 15,902.94, P10 9,301.19, P11 8,320.40, P12 10,483.23 (as-was Garden minus as-is Garden). If Hanna wants the current set-up, the Garden totals would be P7 37,069.41, P8 36,765.02, P9 47,385.02, P10 50,146.62, P11 100,509.14, P12 297,616.35.

Garden net sales include web sales (dispatch-date basis), roughly 7,000 to 38,000 per period. The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to a category subset, so no store-level reconciliation was done.
Period lengths differ: P9 and P12 have five weeks, the others four, so P9 and P12 are not like-for-like with the four-week periods. P12 is also the spring peak.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, s.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-05-26' AND DATE '2025-06-22' AND f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag), ret AS (SELECT sales_line_id, sum(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, s.format AS store_format, round(100 * coalesce(sum(r.refund_net), 0) / sum(s.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold s LEFT JOIN ret r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY s.format ORDER BY s.format
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 2 of FY2025/26 per ref_fiscal_calendar (Monday 2025-05-26 to Sunday 2025-06-22, 4 weeks, fully loaded)
Return rate = net refund value (refund_net, excl. VAT) divided by net sales value (net_amount, excl. VAT) of the same lines
Sold-cohort basis: returns are matched to the original sales line via sales_line_id, so all returns of goods sold in the period count, whenever they were returned
Store format taken from dim_store via the sales line's store_key (store version at the sale date)
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag = true) excluded
Store channel only (channel_code ST, store_id < 900), consistent with the warehouse's own store sales view rpt.v_daily_sales
assumptions: 'Last year' means FY2025/26, the most recent completed fiscal year, since today (2026-10-05) falls in FY2026/27; the fiscal year starts in late April or early May, not January
'Period 2' means fiscal period 2, not calendar month 2
'Store format' means the dim_store format of physical stores (Large, Medium, Small). The web shop (format 'Web') is a channel rather than a store format and is left out
Return rate is measured by value excluding VAT, not by units
Staff purchases are left out because they are not ordinary customer sales
Returns are attributed to the format of the store that made the sale, not the store that took the return
caveats: Training store (store_id 999, format 'Training') sales were excluded: 126 lines, EUR 2,222 net, no returns. It is a test location, not a real store format

Staff-purchase lines were excluded from physical stores (1,172 lines in the sold cohort, 29 with returns, return value about EUR 270). The effect on the rates is small, but they would move slightly if staff purchases were included
dim_store.format holds Large, Medium and Small, while the column comment says Hyper, Standard or Express; I used the values actually in the data, and the comment appears to be out of date
Web shop (format 'Web') sales were not included. For reference only: 6,351 lines, EUR 183,102 net sold, EUR 22,388 net refunded, about 12.2% by value

Return rate is by value. By units the rates are nearly identical across formats at about 2.4% (Large 2.39, Medium 2.43, Small 2.40), because returns skew to higher-value lines. The difference between formats is small (4.30% to 4.56%) and I did not test whether it is significant
Returns on period 2 sales were observed up to 2025-07-23, and the warehouse data runs to 2026-10-04, so the return window is complete

Data checks found no problems: no duplicate sales or return lines in the period, no orphan returns, no returns exceeding the quantity or amount sold, no returns dated before the sale, and no store closures during the period
Region changed on 2025-04-28 for several stores, but that does not affect this format breakdown. Format did not change between versions of any store

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS first_period, 4 AS last_period
)
SELECT s.format,
       ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv
FROM fact_sales_line f
JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
JOIN dim_date d    ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE s.store_id < 900
  AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag
  AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
  AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY atv DESC;
definitions_applied: ATV as net sales before returns divided by number of sales receipts
Physical stores only (store_id below 900; excludes web shop 900 and training store 999)
Staff purchases excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 (28 August 2026 to 30 August 2026, fiscal weeks 14-17)
assumptions: Period 4 without a year specification read as period 4 of the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (the most recently completed period)
Store format is reported as-is (current hierarchy)
caveats: Store format categories have evolved to Large, Medium, Small (differing from schema documentation which references Hyper, Standard, Express)
Period 4 was completely loaded through 30 August 2026, so the result is final

answer.sql: SELECT cp.subcategory AS subcategory, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE cp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY 1
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 4 of FY2026/27 is 3 August to 30 August 2026, fiscal weeks 14 to 17, fully loaded
Returns dated on their own return date (fact_return_line.return_date), not the date of the original sale
Units returned is the sum of quantity_returned, counted per return line
Product hierarchy as-is: Garden Furniture is the subcategory of that name, read from the current dim_product version joined on sku and is_current
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no rows were affected)
Web returns included: they are booked to the web shop (store 900) and counted like store returns
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, staging, backup, tmp or old tables
assumptions: 'This year' is read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as the request was received on 5 October 2026. 'Period 4' is therefore FY2026/27 P4, which is fully loaded and complete.
'Handed back and booked as returned' is read as return lines dated by return_date, which is the date the return was booked. It is not read as the date of the original sale.

'Garden Furniture' is read as the dim_product subcategory of that name, which sits under the Garden category. It is not read as the whole Garden category, and it is not the Furniture category or the Bathroom Furniture subcategory.
Units are the sum of quantity_returned across all channels, stores and web. The request gave no breakdown, so one total is given.
caveats: Of the 92 units, 34 are web returns booked to the web shop (store 900) and 58 are returns in physical stores.

Checks on the 92 return lines found no data problems. All return_line_ids are unique, and each line matches a sales line with the same article. No line returns more than was sold, no return is dated before its sale, no sales line is returned twice, and every line has a quantity of 1. Weekly units were 28, 16, 22 and 26 for fiscal weeks 14 to 17, with returns on every week.
The result is the same whether Garden Furniture is taken from the product version on the return date or from the current version, so as-is and as-was agree for this subcategory.

Returns arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so these units relate to sales made before and during P4. This figure is not the P4 sales-cohort return count, which would be a different number and would not be complete until about five weeks after the period ended.

answer.sql: SELECT st.store_id, st.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, s.week_ending_date, s.closing_units AS units_in_stock FROM fact_stock_week s JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = s.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = s.product_key WHERE st.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND s.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Stock position = closing_units in fact_stock_week, the closing stock at the end of a fiscal week (counted on Sunday)
Fiscal week runs Monday to Sunday (dim_date); last week = FY2026/27 fiscal week 22, 28 Sep to 4 Oct 2026
Store and product identified through their stable business keys (store_id 124, sku 100011), joined to the fact table via the surrogate keys store_key and product_key
Net stock only, with no adjustment for open orders or units in transit
assumptions: Request date is Thursday 8 Oct 2026, so 'last week' is the last completed fiscal week (Mon 28 Sep to Sun 4 Oct), not the current week that started 5 Oct
'Jyväskylä Palokka' means store_id 124 (the only matching store in dim_store, one version only)
'In stock' means units on hand at the store at week end, taken from the weekly stock snapshot
caveats: No data problems found for this store and SKU. The week 22 snapshot has exactly one row (no duplicates), no negative stock, and was loaded 5 Oct 2026 01:00.

The figure ties to the transactions. Stock was 13 at the end of week 21 and 11 at the end of week 22 after two single-unit sales on 21 and 24 Sep, and there were no sales, returns, receipts or adjustments for this SKU at the store in week 22, so the 11 units are unchanged from the week before.
The store had no refit closure on record and no store closure in the period.

The fiscal calendar marks period P06 (which contains week 22) as not fully loaded, but week 22 itself is complete in the stock table (all 38 stores, 27,143 store-SKU rows, the same as the prior weeks).
The channel_code column is null on the sales lines I looked at for this SKU. It does not affect the stock figure.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 3 of FY2026/27, 29 June to 2 August 2026, fully loaded
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (the basis of units_sold in rpt_daily_store_sales)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out (no effect on this figure)
As-is product hierarchy: subcategory taken from the current product version, joined on sku and is_current
Store identified by stable store_id 108, not by store_key
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total: Lahti daily receipts, units and net sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales on every day of the period
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as the request was received on 5 October 2026
'Period 3' means fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27, 29 June to 2 August 2026
'Lahti store' means store_id 108 (Lahti, Large format, South region). Tampere Lielahti is a different store
'Interior Paint' means the subcategory Interior Paint within Paint & Decorating
'Units sold' means gross units sold, before returns. This is how units_sold is defined in rpt_daily_store_sales. Returns are not netted off units
caveats: 194 units is before returns. Interior Paint returns booked at Lahti during the period were 5 units, which would give 189 net of returns. A further 6 units of lines sold in the period have been returned (to date) and may be booked at any time up to 30 days after sale
4 of the 194 units were staff purchases and are included
No data corrections were needed. There were no duplicate sales lines, no zero or negative quantities, no product moved between subcategories during the period, and no missing days
Lahti has no refit closure in the period; the Kuopio refit does not affect this figure

answer.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date, period_end_date, weeks_in_period FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period = 5), cur AS (SELECT sku, category FROM dim_product WHERE is_current AND category <> 'ZZ Test'), stock AS (SELECT c.category, sum(w.closing_units) closing_units FROM fact_stock_week w JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = w.store_key AND s.store_id < 900 JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = w.product_key JOIN cur c ON c.sku = p.sku WHERE w.week_ending_date = (SELECT period_end_date FROM per) GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT c.category, sum(f.quantity) units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key AND s.store_id <> 999 JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN cur c ON c.sku = p.sku WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN (SELECT period_start_date FROM per) AND (SELECT period_end_date FROM per) GROUP BY 1) SELECT per.fiscal_year, per.fiscal_period, st.category, round(st.closing_units / (so.units_sold::DOUBLE / per.weeks_in_period), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM per CROSS JOIN stock st JOIN sold so USING (category) ORDER BY st.category
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period dates taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2026/27 P05 = 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, 4 weeks)
Weeks of cover = closing stock units divided by average weekly units sold
Closing stock = fact_stock_week at the week ending 2026-09-27, the last day of the period
Category taken from the current version of each SKU in dim_product, applied to both stock and sales
Stock counted in the physical stores only (store_id below 900)
Training store (store_id 999) excluded from sales
Test category 'ZZ Test' excluded
assumptions: 'Last period' means the last fully loaded fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (ref_fiscal_calendar.fully_loaded = true). P06 started 2026-09-28 and is only partly loaded.
'End of last period' means the stock count of Sunday 2026-09-27.
Demand is average weekly units sold over the 4 weeks of P05, not a forecast.
Demand is gross units sold, with no deduction for returns.

Web shop sales (store_id 900, about 14% of units) count as demand on the same stock. The stock table has no web or distribution-centre stock location, so web orders must be served from the store stock counted here.
Staff purchases count as demand because those units physically leave stock. They are small: about 1% of units, 603 lines at the stores.
Cover is measured in units, not in value at standard cost. Within a category this is a like-for-like measure.
caveats: The result excludes the 'ZZ Test' category (12 SKUs): 1 web line and 27 training-store lines were sold in P05 and none were in stock. It is not a real product category.
The training store (store_id 999) is excluded from demand. It sold 209 units in P05, including 182 staff-purchase units, and holds no stock.

65 outdoor-lighting SKUs were reclassified from Garden to Electrical on 2025-10-26. The result uses the current category (Electrical) for stock and sales alike. Using the category recorded on older product versions would split these SKUs between two categories.
Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 2026-01-25 and has no stock in the period. No refit closures overlapped P05, so no store needed adjusting for closed weeks.

Every other fact_sales_line row in P05 has a null channel_code, which is a known effect of the web-platform migration. I identified web lines by the web shop store (store_id 900) and did not use channel_code.

Cover for Seasonal (36.6 weeks) and Furniture (21.4) is high because the weekly rate over P05 is low. The result does not adjust for seasonality, so Seasonal cover at the end of September will read differently from the rest of the year.
Stock for the Seasonal and Garden categories reflects a snapshot at one date. Averages over a longer window (for example 13 weeks) would give different figures, especially for these two categories.
No duplicate stock or sales rows were found for the period, and closing_value reconciled to units times standard unit cost on every row.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, fsw.week_ending_date, fsw.closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fsw INNER JOIN dim_store s ON fsw.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON fsw.product_key = p.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND fsw.week_ending_date = '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Fiscal week calendar: 7-day fiscal weeks ending on Sunday
Current store and product dimensions applied to identify entities
assumptions: Last week means the most recent complete fiscal week, ending 2026-10-04
SKU 100011 refers to the current (active) product version
Jyväskylä Palokka refers to store_id 124
caveats: Warehouse data extends only to 2026-10-04; request was received 2026-10-08. The end of the last complete fiscal week (2026-10-04) is the interpretation of the date
No data quality issues detected

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, p.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND f.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name, p.category ORDER BY SUM(f.quantity) DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Best-selling measured by unit volume (quantity sold)
Last period interpreted as the most recent fully loaded fiscal period
Staff purchases excluded from retail sales
assumptions: Last period means the most recently completed full period (P05), not the current partial period (P06)
Best-selling measured by unit quantity sold rather than revenue
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag = TRUE) are excluded as non-retail sales
caveats: Tools & Hardware category dominates the top 10 (7 of 10 products), suggesting either strong demand or high inventory turn in this category
Net sales values are in EUR excluding VAT and do not reflect contribution margin or profit

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) DESC) AS rank, cp.sku, cp.product_name, 'FY2024/25' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_quarter, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 10 AND 12 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns (returns credited back at standard_cost_returned, dated on the return date)
Net sales excluding VAT
Fiscal calendar: Q4 = P10 to P12 = fiscal weeks 40 to 52, 27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025 (13 weeks, no week 53)
As-is hierarchy: region taken from the current store version
Current product version used for the product name (as-is)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered or collected orders only
Product grain = sku (stable article number), not product_key
Staff purchases included
assumptions: Q4 of FY24/25 is FY2024/25 P10 to P12, the fiscal year named in the request.
South means as-is. The region is the one stores have now, restated over the whole period, as in the other accepted top-10 product requests. The request did not ask for as-was.

As-is South is 10 current stores, including Kouvola (114, moved from East to South on 28 April 2025). It excludes Helsinki Vuosaari, Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, Espoo Lommila, Vantaa Tammisto and Kerava (101 to 105), which are now in the Capital Region but were in South during Q4 FY24/25.
The web shop (store 900, region Online) is in no physical region, so no web sales are in South.
Ranking is by gross margin in EUR, not margin percentage.
Stores that have since closed are still in the region as they are now. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026 and is part of South as-is; it traded throughout Q4 FY24/25.
Gross margin is shown in EUR rounded to cents.
caveats: Correction: the 5 stores that moved to the Capital Region on 28 April 2025 are left out of South. Kouvola is included although it was East at the time. A request for South as it was then (as-was) would give a different list.
Correction: test store 999 and ZZ Test articles are excluded, and returns are netted against margin on their own return date.

Checked: net sales for the same stores and days (my method, all regions) equal rpt_daily_store_sales exactly. South as-is is 593,853.56 on both sides. There were no duplicate sales or return lines in the range.
The deprecated views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, rpt_weekly_sales_by_region and the backup, staging and temp tables were not used.
Returns booked in Q4 for goods sold earlier, or after Q4 for goods sold in Q4, follow the company definition (return date), so the margin of an individual product can differ from a sale-date view.
The 10th product (978.84) is clearly ahead of the 11th (Smart Home Tuulikki 855, 935.46), so the cut-off is not a tie.
Product name, category and so on come from the current article version. Nothing in this ranking depends on the outdoor-lighting move to Electrical, because ranking is by article.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending
),
closing AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units
    FROM fact_stock_week fs
    JOIN dim_store s    ON s.store_key = fs.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p  ON p.product_key = fs.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending
      AND s.store_id < 900 
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    GROUP BY 1
),
sold AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s    ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p  ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7
      AND s.store_id < 900 
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT c.category, 
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(s.units_sold_4w, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) END AS weeks_of_cover
FROM closing c
LEFT JOIN sold s ON s.category = c.category
ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: DEF-WEEKS-COVER: weeks of cover = closing units / average weekly units sold over prior four fiscal weeks
DEF-STOCK-SEMIADD: stock aggregated across stores and products, not across weeks
REG-STOCK-SNAPSHOT: fact_stock_week with one row per store and article per week-ending Sunday
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: physical stores only (store_id < 900), excluding web and training store
REG-TEST-SKU: test articles (category 'ZZ Test') excluded from all reporting
DEF-HIERARCHY-ASIS: current product version used for category membership
assumptions: Last period is FY2026/27 P05, the last completed fiscal period, ending 2026-09-27
Week-ending date 2026-09-27 (Sunday) is the snapshot for closing stock
Prior four weeks for sales average are the weeks before the snapshot week (2026-08-24 to 2026-09-20, fiscal weeks 17-20)
Aggregation is across all physical stores (store_id < 900) in each category
Current product version used to determine category membership (as-is)
caveats: Seasonal category has high weeks of cover (48.8), reflecting lower but variable demand
Furniture has highest weeks of cover (29.5), reflecting slower turnover typical of furniture
Tools & Hardware and Cleaning & Household have lowest weeks of cover (7.7 and 7.6), indicating faster inventory turnover
Categories with zero sales in the prior four weeks would show NULL weeks of cover; none found in this data
