answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS first_period, 6 AS last_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_category AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1) SELECT category, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * gross_margin / net_sales, 1) AS gross_margin_pct FROM by_category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, returns taken on their return date
Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost, both after returns (returned units credited back at standard cost)
Gross margin %: gross margin divided by net sales
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
As-is hierarchy: categories taken from the current product version
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 6 (22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, 5 weeks, fully loaded)
Web shop (store 900) included in the company total
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27, matching how requests in the current fiscal year were read before.
'Period 6' read as fiscal period 6 of that year (22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025).
Reported as-is, because no as-was view was requested: outdoor lighting is counted in Electrical for the whole period.
Net sales are excluding VAT, per the company definition.
Web sales are included, since the request is not limited to stores.
Gross margin % is after returns and is shown to one decimal place.
caveats: Outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, the day after P6 ended. Reported as-is, Electrical includes 33,781.91 of net sales (gross margin 12,586.84) that was in Garden at the time. Garden as-was would be 148,587.85 net sales at 39.4% margin. Electrical as-was would be 185,711.09 at 41.6%. Electrical as-is is 219,493.00 at 41.0%. Garden as-is is unchanged at 114,805.94 at 40.2%.

Duplicate load found in fact_sales_line: 418 sales lines (net 10,390.53) were loaded twice on 23 Sep 2025, with the same receipt_id and line_no but new sales_line_ids. They are all dated 15 to 21 Sep 2025, which is before P6, so they do not affect these figures. Any query that includes the week before P6 should deduplicate on receipt_id and line_no.

The company-wide net sales for P6 built with this method (1,293,219.69, of which web 175,588.62) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly. The control total covers all categories, so it checks the method, not the category split.
Do not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales. They leave out web sales from 3 Nov 2025 and were not used. P6 falls before that date.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, cp.subcategory, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1 AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory <> 'Outdoor Lighting'), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT l.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net (net_amount), both excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: sold lines selected by the fiscal period of the sale date, refunds matched back to the sold line through sales_line_id whenever and wherever they were booked
As-is product hierarchy (current dim_product version for category and subcategory)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar: Q1 = P1 to P3 = fiscal weeks 1 to 13
Physical stores and the web shop (store 900) both included in the sold lines
Staff purchases included (as in net sales)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026), the fiscal year just ended before the current FY2026/27, as in the accepted request REQ-D16 (Q1 sales last year)
'Q1' therefore means FY2025/26 Q1: P1 to P3, fiscal weeks 1 to 13, 28 April 2025 to 27 July 2025
'Goods sold in Q1' read as the sale-week cohort, so returns count against the sale whenever they came back, as in REQ-D14 to REQ-D16
'Garden' read as the current (as-is) Garden category, in line with management reporting practice
Web sales included alongside the stores, with no channel split, because none was asked for
Rate is on net value (refund_net / net_amount), the company definition, not on units
caveats: Outdoor Lighting was moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 October 2025. As-is, it belongs to Electrical for all history, so it is not a Garden subcategory in this answer. Four delisted outdoor lighting articles (SKUs 100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917 are in the delisted group in the warehouse) were never given a new product version and still show category Garden in dim_product. 19 sold lines in Q1 (about EUR 375 net) belong to such articles. I excluded them by filtering out subcategory 'Outdoor Lighting' so that the whole subcategory is treated as Electrical, consistently. Counting them as Garden would have added an eighth Outdoor Lighting row to the table.
Store 999 and ZZ Test were filtered out. In Q1 FY2025/26 this did not remove any Garden lines, since test articles sit in a separate category.
The cohort is complete: Q1 sales ended 27 July 2025, the last matched return was booked on 22 August 2025 (within the 30-day return window), and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026.
No duplicate sales lines or return lines were found (sales_line_id is unique in the Q1 range; no sales line has more than one return row; no orphan returns; no refund exceeds the quantity sold).
The rpt_daily_store_sales control total does not apply: it has no product dimension and is on a net-sales-after-returns basis, so no control comparison was made.
Rates are on value excluding VAT. A units-based return rate could differ.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, round(100.0 * sum(CASE WHEN o.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN f.net_amount END) / sum(f.net_amount), 2) AS click_and_collect_share_pct FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE (f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)) AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 6 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 periods 6 to 8 (22 Sep 2025 to 21 Dec 2025)
Web shop = sales lines with channel_code 'WB' (before the web-platform migration) or channel_id 2 or 3 (after it)
Click-and-collect identified through fact_web_order.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect', which works for both generations of channel coding
Sales measured as net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) on sale_date
Share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales in the period, in percent
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the last full fiscal year, FY2025/26, because today (9 Oct 2026) falls in FY2026/27 and the company reports on a fiscal calendar
'Periods 6 to 8' read as fiscal periods 6, 7 and 8, with one share per period
'Sales' read as net sales excluding VAT before returns, measured on the date of the sale
Cancelled orders are not counted; they have no sales lines anyway
Staff purchases are not an issue for the web channel, because none of the web lines in the window carries the staff flag
caveats: The web-platform migration changed how lines are coded: older lines use channel_code 'WB' with channel_id empty, newer lines have channel_code empty and channel_id 2 (home delivery) or 3 (click and collect). Filtering on channel_code = 'WB' alone, as the rpt.v_daily_sales view does, drops roughly two thirds of web lines in these periods and gives a wrong share. I included both codings.

Click-and-collect cannot be identified from channel_code, since the old code WB covers both fulfilment types; I took it from fact_web_order.fulfilment_type instead. Every web sales line matched an order.
Checks found no duplicate lines, no mismatch between line totals and order totals, and sale_date matches the Helsinki-local date of the timestamp.

Returns are not deducted. Netting each returned line's refund_net against its original sale gives slightly different shares: 27.08% for P6, 26.01% for P7 and 26.83% for P8. Tell me if you want net-of-returns figures instead.
Periods 6 to 8 of FY2025/26 are fully loaded in the warehouse, so there is no partial-period risk.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, cp.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period: FY2026/27 P05 (fiscal weeks 18 to 21, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), from dim_date
Units sold: the quantity on sales lines, by sale date
Store scope: Helsinki Pitäjänmäki is store_id 102, counted by store_id across store versions
Products counted by sku, so versions of one article are merged
Store 999 and category ZZ Test left out (no ZZ Test sales at store 102 in the period, so no effect)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total: store 102 units in the period equal rpt_daily_store_sales (3740 units, 28 days)
assumptions: Pitäjänmäki is Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, store 102.
'Period 5 of FY26/27' is FY2026/27 P05, which is complete and fully loaded.

'Sold the most units' means gross units sold on sales lines. Returns are not netted off. Netting them off does not change the top three: the returned units in the period were 1 for the third product and 0 for the first two, against 30 units for the fourth.
Products are identified by sku, with the name taken from the current product version.
Ranking is by units only, not by sales value.
caveats: Fiscal period and store dimension checks found no data problems: no duplicate receipt lines, no non-positive quantities, and the fact total agrees with the control table.
Pitäjänmäki moved from South to the Capital Region on 28 April 2025. This does not affect a single-store request.
Fourth place is 30 units, well clear of the top three, so there is no tie at the cut-off.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open, outside refit closures (ref_store_closure) and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P02 = Monday 1 June to Sunday 28 June 2026 (weeks 5 to 8, 4 weeks)
As-is store names from the current dim_store version
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P02, since the request arrived on 9 October 2026 and FY2026/27 began on 4 May 2026; P02 is fully loaded
Ranked by net sales per trading day (company league table definition), not by total net sales
A store that traded for only part of the period stays in the table with its own trading days
Net sales per trading day is rounded to 2 decimals; ranking uses the unrounded value
Trading days are 26 for a full-period store: 28 days minus Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June), both closed holidays
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026 (ref_store_closure) and traded only 14 days in the period (1 to 14 June). It is ranked on those days, at 7th, so its net sales of 23,993.71 are not comparable with the other stores' full-period totals.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales or trading days in the period, so it is not listed.
The store totals reconcile exactly (gap 0.00 for every store) to rpt_daily_store_sales for 1 to 28 June 2026.
rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, which leave out web sales from 3 November 2025, were not used. This does not affect the league table, which covers physical stores only.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were filtered out. I did not measure whether the filter changes any store figure.

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS tampere_loyalty_members FROM dim_member AS m JOIN dim_store AS s ON s.store_id = m.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE m.is_current AND s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900
definitions_applied: Customer = loyalty member (dim_member); non-member shoppers cannot be identified in the warehouse
Member location = home store (home_store_id) at the member's current version (is_current = true)
Tampere = the city of the member's home store in dim_store, using the current store version
Members counted once by member_id (stable loyalty number), not by member_key version rows
Real stores only: pseudo-locations with store_id 900 or above (web shop, training store) excluded
assumptions: 'Customers' means loyalty programme members, the only identifiable customer population in the warehouse
'In Tampere' means the member's home store is one of the four Tampere stores: Hervanta (115), Lielahti (116), Kaleva (117) and Lamminpää (136); the warehouse holds no member address or city

Counted all current members, whether or not they have bought recently, since no activity window was given and no 'active member' definition is in the schema. As a rough comparison, 4,438 of these members bought anything in the 12 months to 8 Oct 2026
Counted as of the request date (8 Oct 2026), using the latest member records in the warehouse
caveats: The warehouse records the city 'Tampere' for the web shop (store 900) and the training store (999) as well. Online sign-ups carry home store 900, so the 12,028 members who joined online are not counted as Tampere customers.

Counting every version row in dim_member instead of one row per member would give about 3,000 extra rows for members who changed tier or home store. Counting current versions per member_id avoids that double counting.

Home store is where a member signed up or is assigned, not necessarily where they live; members may live in Tampere but be assigned to another store or online, and the reverse. For a different reading, 7,632 distinct members bought in the four Tampere stores in the 12 months to 8 Oct 2026, which is a different population from the 7,175 above.
The count by home store is Hervanta 2,788, Lielahti 1,721, Kaleva 1,692 and Lamminpää 974; Lamminpää opened on 2 Sep 2024, so its base is younger.
The dim_store comments say formats are Hyper, Standard or Express, but the data shows Large and Medium for the Tampere stores. This does not affect the count.
Backup, staging and old copies of tables (bak_, stg_, _old, tmp_) were not used. The staged member updates (stg_member_updates) were checked and all already appear in dim_member.

answer.sql: WITH first_version AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS version_no FROM dim_member) SELECT join_date, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS new_members FROM first_version WHERE version_no = 1 AND join_date = DATE '2026-10-03' GROUP BY join_date
definitions_applied: New member: counted on the join date, by distinct member_id
Versioned member dimension: one count per member_id, taken from the first version in dim_member, not per member_key
Canonical table dim_member used; stg_ and bak_ tables not used
assumptions: Read 'joined' as new loyalty members whose join_date is 3 October 2026, a calendar date with no time-zone conversion
Counted all members including the 9 online sign-ups under home store 900, since the request has no channel or store restriction
No breakdown by store, region or tier given, since only a total was asked for
caveats: No data problem found for this date. There was one version per member, no duplicate member_id and valid_from equal to join_date for all 29, so no correction was needed
The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so 3 October is fully covered
Counting rows in dim_member would overcount for members who later change tier, home store or consent, so the count is by distinct member_id on the first version
The 29 includes 9 online sign-ups (store 900) and 20 who enrolled in physical stores

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending), closing AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, c.category, ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM closing c LEFT JOIN sold s ON s.category = c.category ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Last period = last completed fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026)
Closing stock is the snapshot at the end of the last fiscal week (Sunday 27 Sep 2026), summed across stores and products, not across weeks
Weeks of cover = closing stock units / average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Units sold = quantity on sales lines by sale date (Helsinki business date)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) excluded because web is picked from the central warehouse and has no stock rows
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Category as-is (current product version), so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical
Weeks of cover for a category computed on category totals (summed stock over summed sales), not as an average of store-level ratios
assumptions: 'End of last period' is the stock count at the end of the last week of P05, Sunday 27 September 2026 (request received 7 Oct 2026; P06 is incomplete).

'Prior four fiscal weeks' is read literally as the four weeks before the snapshot week, 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026 (fiscal weeks 17 to 20), per the stock skill. The snapshot week itself (week 21) is not in the sales average. Counting the period's own four weeks (18 to 21) would give somewhat different cover figures.
Cover is for all physical stores combined, one row per category, as the request gave no store breakdown.
Category is as-is: the current category of each article. No articles changed category in the stock snapshot for that week, so as-was would give the same result.
Units sold are gross of returns, as the definition uses sales-line quantity.
caveats: Store stock only: web orders are fulfilled from the central warehouse, which is not in fact_stock_week, and web sales are left out of the sales side, so cover does not reflect central warehouse stock.

Checks run on the source data found no problems needing correction: no duplicate rows in the stock snapshot (27,143 rows, unique on store, article and week, one load), no duplicate sales lines in the four-week window, no test-category or store 900/999 rows in the stock week, no negative or null closing units, and every unit sold in the window belongs to an article ranged in that store at the snapshot.
The 999 training store, 40 ZZ Test lines and web lines were present in the sales window and were removed.

Seasonal (48.8 weeks) and Furniture (29.5 weeks) have very high cover because of low sales volume relative to stock. Seasonal demand is out of season in September, so a four-week trailing average understates its forward demand and overstates cover.
Weeks of cover is a backward-looking rate: it assumes the past four weeks' sales rate continues.

I did not run the query_check script or the control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales, because that table does not apply to category-level unit figures. The checks above were run as separate queries.

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, p.sku, p.product_name, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN ref_fiscal_calendar c ON c.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND c.fiscal_period = 5 WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN c.period_start_date AND c.period_end_date GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 from ref_fiscal_calendar (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, 4 weeks, fully loaded)
Store identified by stable store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), covering both SCD versions (store_key 3 and 4)
Product identified by stable sku, summing across product versions
Units sold = sum of fact_sales_line.quantity by sale_date
assumptions: FY26/27 read as the warehouse label FY2026/27
Units sold counted gross, before returns, as the request asks what sold rather than net sales
Staff purchases left in, since they are real units sold through the till
Ranking by unit quantity only, not value
caveats: Store has two dimension versions (keys 3 and 4, change on 2025-04-28); joining on store_key alone would miss one, so I used store_id
Product has several versions, so I grouped by sku
Checked for duplicate sales lines in the period: none (2,121 lines, all with distinct sales_line_id and receipt/line pairs)
Staff purchases are 55 units in the store's period total, 2 of them on SKU 102244; excluding them leaves the top three unchanged, with 102244 on 40 units, still ahead of the fourth product on 30
Returns against these three are 0, 0 and 1 units. Net of returns, the ranking and the top three are unchanged (52, 44, 41)
No refit closure is recorded for store 102, so the store traded for the full period
I did not check the ETL load dates beyond confirming they fall within the period (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-28)

answer.sql: SELECT f.vat_rate, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND f.sale_date >= '2024-08-26' AND f.sale_date <= '2024-09-22' GROUP BY f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate DESC
definitions_applied: Stores identified as store_id < 900 in dim_store (physical retail locations, excluding pseudo-locations)
Period 5 FY2024/25 = 26 August to 22 September 2024 per ref_fiscal_calendar
VAT charged calculated as gross_amount minus net_amount (includes all sales lines, staff purchases excluded from scope implicitly as they may have different VAT treatment)
assumptions: VAT rates expressed as percentages (25.5 = 25.5%, etc.)
Request interpreted as all sales in physical stores during the period, regardless of whether a member card was used
Staff purchases included (staff_purchase_flag = true lines counted, as the request specifies 'stores' not 'customer sales')
caveats: Data quality: 8,357 lines (25% of store sales) carry a 0.2400 (24%) VAT rate on 'standard' VAT class products during a period when Finnish standard VAT was 25.5%. This rate does not align with Finnish VAT rules in effect 26 Aug–22 Sep 2024. These lines were counted as presented in the warehouse.
VAT rates are those applied at point of sale; actual remittance to tax authorities may differ if adjustments, credits or corrections are processed after the period end

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key WHERE s.store_id<900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id<900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'), sales AS (SELECT store_id, sum(net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-06-01' AND DATE '2026-06-28' GROUP BY 1), trading AS (SELECT cs.store_id, count(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN dim_date d WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id<900 AND d.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period=2 AND d.is_trading_day AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date<=d.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date>=d.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id=cs.store_id AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.net_sales/t.trading_days DESC) AS rank, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, t.trading_days, ROUND(s.net_sales,2) AS net_sales, ROUND(s.net_sales/t.trading_days,2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM sales s JOIN trading t USING (store_id) JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id=s.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date at the store that processed it
Staff purchases included in net sales
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop (store 900) is not listed
Trading days: days the store was open (after open_date, before close_date), outside ref_store_closure refit closures, and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Fiscal period 2 of FY2026/27 from dim_date / ref_fiscal_calendar (1 June to 28 June 2026)
Store name and open/close dates taken from the current dim_store version
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2 (1 to 28 June 2026), the current fiscal year on the request date of 9 October 2026. P2 is complete and fully loaded.
Net sales are after returns, per the company definition, although the request did not say so.
Ties are ranked with RANK on net sales per trading day; there are none in this result.
Stores are listed by the current store name and are not broken down by region or format because the request did not ask for it.
caveats: Two closed holidays fall in the period (Midsummer Eve 19 June and Midsummer Day 20 June), so a full-period store has 26 trading days, not 28.

Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it is ranked on its 14 trading days (1 to 14 June). Its net sales (23,993.71) cover only those days, which is why it ranks 7th on the per-day figure despite a low total. Its rank rests on a half-period.
Control total: per-store net sales agree with rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent for every store over 1 to 28 June 2026. Total sales before returns (1,116,824.94) also match the control table.
No duplicate sales lines were found in the period, and no store 999 or ZZ Test rows fell in the store range, so the exclusion filters did not change any total.
Net sales are excluding VAT and include staff purchases.
No data problem needed correcting for this request.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) as new_member_signups FROM dim_member WHERE join_date = '2026-09-25'
definitions_applied: New members: distinct member records where join_date equals the specified date (25 September 2026)
Slowly changing dimension: counted distinct member_id to avoid double-counting members with multiple versions
assumptions: join_date in dim_member represents the signup date
Date interpreted as 2026-09-25 in ISO format
Counted distinct member_id to handle the slowly changing dimension structure
caveats: No data quality issues detected; all records are current (is_current = true) and consistent
All new members signed up as Basic tier on their join date

answer.sql:
WITH cm AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key=e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id=19),
s AS (SELECT f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key=f.member_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN '2026-05-04' AND '2026-05-24' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM cm)),
r AS (SELECT r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key=r.member_key JOIN fact_sales_line sl ON sl.sales_line_id=r.sales_line_id WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN '2026-05-04' AND '2026-05-24' AND NOT sl.staff_purchase_flag AND m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM cm))
SELECT 'Spring Garden Launch 2026' AS campaign_name, 19 AS campaign_id, (SELECT count(*) FROM cm) AS members_contacted, (SELECT sum(net_amount) FROM s) - (SELECT coalesce(sum(refund_net),0) FROM r) AS net_spend_eur
definitions_applied: Net sales: EUR excluding VAT, net_amount after line discounts, less refunds (refund_net) booked in the window
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag), along with refunds of staff-purchase lines
Member counted by member_id (stable loyalty number), not by member_key version
Both channels counted: store, web home delivery and click and collect (channel_id 1, 2, 3)
Contacted = member has at least one row in fact_campaign_exposure for campaign 19
Campaign window 4 to 24 May 2026 matches dim_campaign start and end dates for campaign 19
Spend attributed via the member_key on the sales line, mapped to member_id
assumptions: The 2026 campaign is campaign_id 19, not the 2024 (id 1) or 2025 (id 9) Spring Garden Launch
Contacted means a contact was made (any row in fact_campaign_exposure), whether or not delivered; 14,814 members had at least one delivered contact
Spend means all purchases by the contacted members in the window, store and web, not only garden products, and not only purchases attributable to the campaign
Spend is net of returns because the company reports net sales that way, with returns taken by return date and not matched to the original sale date
Sale dates (sale_date) are taken as Helsinki local dates; sale_ts_utc is consistent with that
caveats: Members are counted by distinct member_id. The 31,685 contact rows sit on 15,063 member_key versions but only 15,001 people. Counting member_key would overstate the contacted figure by 62.

The mailing list size recorded in dim_campaign (16,624) less the holdout (1,597) is 15,027, which is 26 more than the 15,001 members actually in the contact table. I did not find why. The contact table is used as the record of who was contacted.
No holdout member appears in the contact table, and every contacted member had marketing consent.

fact_sales_line.channel_code is NULL for the whole May 2026 window, so channel_code = 'ST' or 'WB' filters return nothing. Channel was taken from channel_id instead, otherwise web sales would be missed.
Staff purchases were removed: EUR 2,541.79 net of sales plus EUR 2.72 of related refunds. Including staff purchases and ignoring returns, spend would be EUR 191,576.08.
Spend before returns and excluding staff is EUR 189,035.29, and refunds on those lines were EUR 8,228.60. Anyone who wants gross spend rather than net should use 189,035.29.
2,597 of the 15,001 contacted members bought in the window (excluding staff purchases), so the average per contacted member is low and most of the spend sits with a minority.
Spend is not an uplift figure. No comparison was made with the 1,597 held-out members, so this shows what contacted members spent, not what the campaign caused.
Cancelled web orders have no sales lines, so they do not affect the total. Guest web orders have no member_key and cannot be attributed to contacted members, so they are excluded.

I could not reconcile rpt_daily_store_sales to the fact tables (gross EUR 1,093,547 against about EUR 1,092,419 to 1,093,887 depending on staff treatment), so the fact tables were used directly rather than the report table. The bak_*, stg_*, tmp_* and *_old tables were ignored.

answer.sql: SELECT 'Gold' AS tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold'
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not by dim_member row
Tier read from the current member version (is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
dim_member only; no other tables, so the store 999 and ZZ Test exclusions are not relevant
assumptions: 'Right now' means the current version of each member. The warehouse holds data up to 4 October 2026, and the request came in on 8 October 2026.

'Members on the Gold tier' means all enrolled loyalty members whose current tier is Gold, whether or not they have bought recently. The metric dictionary defines only 'active members' (a purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks), not total members. I did not apply the activity test because the request did not ask for it.
No marketing-consent filter was applied.
caveats: The number is as of the latest warehouse load, 4 October 2026. Tier changes after that date are not included.

dim_member keeps one row per version. Counting all rows with tier = 'Gold' would give 8,203 and overcount, because 2,412 of those are superseded versions (2,233 members who have since moved tier). Only current versions were counted. Each member has exactly one current version, and no Gold member has a later version.

If Marketing wants Gold members who have bought in the past 52 weeks (the company's 'active member' definition), the figure is 4,827, as of Sunday 4 October 2026, with tier read from the current version. That differs from 5,791 because 964 Gold members have made no purchase in that window. The 4,827 is a side check only, and is not the answer given.
A Gold member can have been on a different tier earlier. The count reflects tier today, not tier at any past date.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Only delivered and collected orders count; cancelled and processing orders are excluded
Click-and-collect counted as web
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is not filled from the 3 Nov 2025 migration)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
UTC timestamps converted to Helsinki time before taking the date
Fiscal periods from dim_date (4-4-5 weeks; periods 5 to 8 are fiscal weeks 18 to 34)
assumptions: The request was received on 6 October 2026, in FY2026/27, so 'last year' is read as FY2025/26. This follows the accepted readings for requests made in FY2026/27 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).
'Periods 5 to 8' means FY2025/26 P05 to P08, 25 August to 21 December 2025 (17 fiscal weeks). I gave one row per period because the request names the periods individually.
'Net' means net sales on the company definition: excluding VAT and after returns.
Figures are in EUR.
caveats: The web shop's channel_code is not filled from 3 November 2025 (the platform migration), which falls in P7. I identified web by store 900, so the periods are consistent. A filter on channel_code, or the views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, would understate web sales from that date. In my query results channel_code WB was on all of P5 and P6, on 1,426 of 6,203 lines in P7, and on none in P8.
Web sales are dated by dispatch, not order date. Orders placed near a period boundary can land in the neighbouring period. Orders still processing or cancelled have no dispatch and are excluded.
One test-article web line (ZZ Test, EUR 5.50 net, in P6) was excluded. It does not change the P6 figure beyond rounding.
The result matches the rpt_daily_store_sales control totals for store 900 exactly in all four periods: 145,626.90; 175,588.62; 154,977.27; 225,265.08.
No duplicate sales lines were found for store 900 in these periods.

Returns arrive up to 30 days after a sale and reduce net sales on the return date. The 17 weeks are complete as of the warehouse load point (4 October 2026), but some returns booked in January 2026 for P8 sales fall in P9, not P8, by definition.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 131 AND p.sku = 101624 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-28' AND DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date
Fiscal week runs Monday to Sunday (FY2026/27 week 22)
Last week = last completed fiscal week as of the request date
sale_date is the Helsinki business date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out
Natural keys (store_id, sku) used so store and product versions are not multiplied
Control total against rpt_daily_store_sales units_sold
assumptions: 'Oulu Kaakkuri' in the request is a store name (store 131, Oulu Kaakkuri), not a product name. SKU 101624 is Fixings & Fasteners Raudikko 251, so the question is read as units of SKU 101624 sold in store 131
'Last week' on 2026-10-08 means the last completed fiscal week, Monday 28 September to Sunday 4 October 2026 (FY2026/27 week 22, period 6), which is the last day loaded in the warehouse
Units sold means units on sales lines and is not reduced by returns; staff purchases are included (there were none for this SKU in the week)
caveats: The request mixed up a store name and a product name: Oulu Kaakkuri is store 131 (Oulu, North, Large); SKU 101624 is Fixings & Fasteners Raudikko 251. The answer is for this SKU in this store only. If chain-wide sales of the SKU were wanted, say so and it will be rerun
4 units of this SKU were returned in store 131 in the same week. They are not netted off the 17 sold. Net of those returns the figure would be 13, although the returns may relate to earlier sales
The week is the first week of period 6 and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so the week is fully loaded
The 17 units are spread over 8 sales lines and 7 trading days with no store closure. The weekly total for store 131 across all SKUs (864 units) matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly
fact_sales_line holds 418 duplicate (receipt_id, line_no) keys in September 2025. None fall in the requested week and none involve these lines, so no correction was needed

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, cs.format, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY cs.format ORDER BY cs.format
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts
Physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Fiscal period from dim_date (FY2026/27 P4 = 3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026, weeks 14 to 17)
Format taken from the current store version (format is the same in every version of a store)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales (net sales before returns and receipts)
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27, period 4 (3 August to 30 August 2026), which is fully loaded
'Store format' read as dim_store.format: Large, Medium, Small
Web is not shown as a format because ATV is a store-only measure
ATV is in EUR excluding VAT, rounded to 2 decimals
caveats: No data problems found in the period: no duplicate sales lines, no receipts spanning several stores, dates or staff flags, and no non-positive amounts.

Per-store receipts and net sales before returns, with staff purchases included, matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly before the staff-purchase exclusion was applied. I did not run the query_check script, since no script runner was available.
The dim_store column comment says formats are Hyper, Standard and Express. The actual values are Large, Medium and Small, and the results use those.
Small covers 12 stores, not 13: Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales in the period.
Receipts per format in the period: Large 6,508 (8 stores), Medium 8,641 (18 stores), Small 2,598 (12 stores).

answer.sql: WITH periods AS (SELECT fiscal_year, period_start_date AS s, period_end_date AS e, CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' THEN 'cur' ELSE 'prior' END AS side FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_period = 4 AND fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27')), lfl_stores AS (SELECT DISTINCT st.store_id FROM dim_store st WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900 AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= (SELECT min(s) FROM periods)) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= (SELECT max(e) FROM periods)) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c, periods p WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= p.e AND c.closure_end_date >= p.s) AND (SELECT count(DISTINCT f.sale_date) FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store d ON d.store_key = f.store_key, periods p WHERE d.store_id = st.store_id AND f.sale_date BETWEEN p.s AND p.e) = 56), sales AS (SELECT p.side, sum(f.net_amount) AS v FROM periods p JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sale_date BETWEEN p.s AND p.e JOIN dim_store d ON d.store_key = f.store_key WHERE d.store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM lfl_stores) GROUP BY 1), refunds AS (SELECT p.side, sum(r.refund_net) AS v FROM periods p JOIN fact_return_line r ON r.return_date BETWEEN p.s AND p.e JOIN dim_store d ON d.store_key = r.store_key WHERE d.store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM lfl_stores) GROUP BY 1), net AS (SELECT s.side, s.v - coalesce(r.v, 0) AS net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (side)) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, round((max(CASE WHEN side = 'cur' THEN net_sales END) / max(CASE WHEN side = 'prior' THEN net_sales END) - 1) * 100, 2) AS lfl_net_sales_growth_pct FROM net
definitions_applied: Like-for-like stores: physical stores open and trading on every day of both compared periods
Fiscal period 4 compared with fiscal period 4 of the prior fiscal year (fiscal calendar, Monday-to-Sunday weeks, 4 weeks each)
Net sales: line net_amount excluding VAT, after line discounts, minus refund_net on returns booked in the period
Returns attributed to the store and date where the return was booked (as in rpt_daily_store_sales)
Stores only: web shop (store_id 900) and training store (999) excluded
Current store versions identified by store_id, joining facts through store_key
Refit closures from ref_store_closure checked against both periods
assumptions: 'This year' is fiscal year FY2026/27 (period 4 ran 3-30 Aug 2026, fiscal weeks 14-17), and 'last year' is FY2025/26 P04 (28 Jul-24 Aug 2025). The request was dated 5 Oct 2026, so both periods are complete and fully loaded.

The comparison is fiscal-period to fiscal-period. FY2025/26 was a 53-week year, so last year's period starts six days earlier on the calendar. Both periods are four Monday-to-Sunday weeks, with no public holidays or non-trading days in either.
'Stores' means the physical store estate. Web sales are not included.
'How did the stores do' is read as net sales growth, as one figure for the whole like-for-like estate. No breakdown by store or region was asked for.

Stores 136 (opened 2 Sep 2024) and 137 (opened 4 Nov 2024) are counted as like-for-like. Both traded on every day of both periods. Neither opened within the 12 months before the prior-year period began, as stores that trade through the whole of both periods would. Excluding both gives -0.23%.
Kuopio (125) is included. Its refit ended on 26 Jul 2026, before period 4 began on 3 Aug 2026, and it traded on every day of the period. Excluding it gives -0.19%.
Staff purchases are kept in net sales, as in the reporting table. They were about 1.4% of store sales in each period. Excluding them (before returns) gives about +0.16%.
Growth is the percentage change in total net sales across the like-for-like stores, not an average of store-level growth rates.
caveats: Result covers 38 stores. Savonlinna (129) is excluded because it closed on 25 Jan 2026 and has no sales in period 4 this year. Its P4 2025 net sales were about 9,549 EUR, and leaving it in would show a decline of about 1.0%.

Overall like-for-like net sales were flat (-0.03%): about 1,010,479 EUR this year against 1,010,743 EUR last year. Individual stores moved much more. For example, Vantaa Tammisto-area and Helsinki Pitäjänmäki stores such as 102 and 131 grew by 10% or more, while 109, 119 and 127 fell by 10% to 24%. The overall figure hides this spread.

Pori (119) fell about 10% (net of returns). Its refit ran 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025, after last year's period 4, so the comparison is pre-refit against post-refit. It traded on every day of both periods, so it stays in the like-for-like set.

The stale temporary tables tmp_lfl_store_list_2024 and tmp_lfl_store_list_2025 were not used. They list Savonlinna as a like-for-like store and leave out 136 and 137, which does not fit the current position.
In FY2026/27 fact_sales_line.channel_code is null on every line, where earlier data uses ST and WB. Stores were therefore identified through dim_store.store_id (below 900), not the channel code.

Reported sales cover only stores whose lines join to dim_store through store_key. All lines in both periods matched, there were no duplicate sales or return lines, VAT and net/gross amounts were consistent, and the store-level totals agreed with rpt_daily_store_sales.
Store regions changed on 28 Apr 2025 for stores 101-105 and 114 (Capital Region and South). This does not affect the total, but any regional cut must account for it.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, w.order_member_key, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_member_key IS NOT NULL THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END)/SUM(l.net_amount),1) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=l.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Web = store_id 900, not channel_code
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Guest web orders count as non-member
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Net amounts excluding VAT
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26, 4-4-5 pattern)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' asked on 9 October 2026 (FY2026/27 is current) is read as FY2025/26, following how past requests asked in the current fiscal year were read
'Periods 9 to 11' means FY2025/26 P9 (22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026), P10 (26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026) and P11 (23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026), shown as one row per period

Click-and-collect orders are web and are included
Shares are rounded to one decimal place
caveats: Correction: in roughly February and March 2026 some web sales lines of logged-in orders are missing their member_key (1,237 such lines in Feb 2026 and 72 in Mar 2026), although fact_web_order.member_key shows the order was placed by a member. answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order o WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01' AND o.status <> 'cancelled'

'Placed' means the order date (order_ts_utc), not the dispatch date

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, cp.subcategory, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1 AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory <> 'Outdoor Lighting'), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT l.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net (net_amount), both excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: refunds are matched to the original sales line through sales_line_id and counted against the period the item was sold, whenever it came back
Sold lines selected by fiscal period of sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Fiscal Q1 = periods 1 to 3 = fiscal weeks 1 to 13 (28 Apr 2025 to 27 Jul 2025)
As-is hierarchy: current product version (dim_product is_current) for category and subcategory
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900) lines included alongside the physical stores, with refunds following the line
Staff purchases included (not excluded for return rate)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (the fiscal year just ended; the request was received 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27). Past requests in FY2026/27 read 'last year' this way.
'Q1' read as fiscal Q1 (P1 to P3, 28 Apr to 27 Jul 2025), not calendar Q1
'Goods sold in Q1' read as the sale-week cohort: returns are attributed back to the sale, however late they came, which is the company return-rate definition
Garden subcategories read as-is on the current hierarchy, so outdoor lighting counts as Electrical and is not a Garden subcategory
Web and store sales are combined in one rate per subcategory because no channel split was requested
Rate is expressed in percent of net value (excluding VAT), rounded to two decimals
caveats: Correction: 19 sold lines (net EUR 375.00) sit on five delisted outdoor lighting articles (SKUs 100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) whose only dim_product version still says Garden / Outdoor Lighting, because they were delisted before the 27 Oct 2025 move to Electrical and never got a new version. I treated them as Electrical (as-is) and left them out, so Garden shows no Outdoor Lighting row. Under the same rule the 1,445 lines (EUR 50,443) on re-versioned outdoor lighting articles are also out.
The cohort is complete: the last Q1 sale was 27 Jul 2025, more than 30 days before the warehouse load point (4 Oct 2026), and the latest matching return is dated 22 Aug 2025.
Data checks found no duplicate receipt/line keys, no duplicate return lines, no returns without a sale, no returns before the sale and no over-returned lines in the cohort.

The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to a category-level, sale-cohort measure, so it was not run. The query-check script and the library's SQL scripts were not available in this session, so the checks were done by hand with SQL.
Return rate is by value excluding VAT, not by units, and Garden Furniture (12.87%) has the highest rate by a wide margin.

assumptions: This year is FY2026/27, the fiscal year containing the request date (2026-10-07)
Ranking is by net sales (descending: highest first)
The Tuomimetsä web shop (store_id 900) is included as a sales channel
Stores with zero sales in the period are excluded

Two stores (Savonlinna and Training store) had zero sales and are not shown

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, cp.category, cp.subcategory, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' GROUP BY ALL
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 4 = Monday 3 August to Sunday 30 August 2026 (weeks 14-17, fully loaded)
Returns counted on their own return date (fact_return_line.return_date), not the sale date and not the sale-week cohort used for return rate
Units = quantity_returned from fact_return_line
As-is product hierarchy: current product version (dim_product is_current) for category and subcategory
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this figure)
Web returns (booked to web shop store 900) and store returns both included
Warehouse tables used: fact_return_line, dim_product, dim_store, dim_date. No deprecated, staging, backup or tmp objects
Control total: all P4 refunds (excluding store 999 and test articles) of 74,361.18 EUR net match rpt_daily_store_sales returns_net exactly, store by day

'Garden Furniture' read as the Garden Furniture subcategory of the Garden category
'Handed back and booked as returned' read as units on return lines (quantity_returned), dated by return date, not refund value and not units sold in P4 that were returned later
Returns of all reason codes counted (changed_mind, defective, damaged_in_transit, not_as_described, wrong_size_or_fit)
All channels counted: 58 units returned in stores and 34 units booked to the web shop
Returns of items sold before P4 count if they were returned in P4
caveats: No data problems found, so no corrections made. Checked: no duplicate return lines, no return line without a matching sale, no return larger than the quantity sold, no return dated before its sale, no returns booked to store 999 or test articles, no sale line returned more than once.
The Helsinki date of the return timestamp gives the same 92 units as return_date, so there is no day-edge issue.
Every Garden Furniture return in P4 sits on a Garden Furniture version of the article, so as-is and as-was give the same 92. No article moved category in that period.

answer.sql: WITH store_sales AS (SELECT s.region, SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key WHERE f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.region NOT IN ('Online', 'Head office') GROUP BY s.region) SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY net_sales DESC) as rank, region, net_sales FROM store_sales ORDER BY rank

Store channel only (channel_code = 'ST')
Current store versions (store_key to current dim_store)
Five retail regions (excludes Online web shop and Head office training store)
assumptions: Performance measured by cumulative net sales
Request for FY2026/27 answered with most recent available complete data
NULL channel_code records excluded; only explicit 'ST' store sales included

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE tier = 'Gold' AND is_current GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id (dim_member keeps one row per version)
Current tier read from the latest member version (is_current, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Warehouse loaded through 4 October 2026, so 'at the moment' is the latest loaded state
assumptions: 'At the moment' means the current tier of each member, as of the latest load (4 October 2026). The request date was 7 October 2026.

'Gold-tier loyalty members' means every member whose current version has tier Gold, whether or not they have bought recently. I did not apply the 'active member' definition (a purchase in the trailing 52 weeks), because the request did not ask for active members.

Counting raw rows without the is_current filter would give 8,203 Gold rows. That is wrong because of the historical versions. Another 2,233 members were Gold at some earlier point, and most of them appear in other tiers now.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 9 AS first_period, 10 AS last_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 1) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share of web sales = click-and-collect net sales / all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date)
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type
Cancelled and processing orders excluded from web sales (only delivered and collected orders have dispatch dates and sales lines)
Category ZZ Test excluded (and store 999)
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern, Monday to Sunday weeks)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year that ended 3 May 2026. This follows how earlier requests asked in FY2026/27 were read (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35). The request was received 6 October 2026, during FY2026/27.
Periods 9 and 10 read as FY2025/26 P9 (22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, 5 weeks) and P10 (26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026, 4 weeks).
Reported one share per period, as the request names two periods and the earlier equivalent request (REQ-D22) was answered by period. No combined P9-P10 figure is given.
Share is by net sales value (web sales), not by order count, because the request says 'share of web sales'.
Web returns are attributed to the fulfilment type of the original order.
caveats: Both periods are fully loaded and fall after the 3 November 2025 web-platform migration. channel_code and channel_id were not used because neither works across the migration. rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it omits web sales after the migration.
Web net sales per period (P9 200,208.58 EUR, P10 123,131.15 EUR) match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly, so the denominator ties to the control total.
Click-and-collect net sales were 58,536.07 EUR in P9 and 37,861.39 EUR in P10.
No duplicate sales lines were found for web orders dispatched in P9-P10 (sales_line_id and receipt_id + line_no both unique). No web lines were attached to physical stores.

Web orders returned in physical stores are booked to those stores under the company definition, so they are not deducted from web net sales or from the share. In P9-P10 these are roughly 150 return lines. Only returns booked to the web shop (store 900, which includes postal returns) reduce web sales. This is the accepted company treatment and the figures reconcile to the control total. A view that deducted in-store returns of web orders would change the share slightly.
Orders still processing or cancelled carry no dispatch date or sales lines, so they are not in web sales. This is the company definition.

answer.sql: SELECT d.calendar_year AS year, d.calendar_month AS month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' AND s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines (each line carries its own VAT rate)
Before returns: no refunds deducted
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included (company net sales definition)
Store lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales_before_returns)
assumptions: 'Store sales' means physical stores only, so web orders (store 900) are left out
'August 2024' and 'September 2024' are read as calendar months (1-31 Aug, 1-30 Sep 2024), not fiscal periods, because the request names calendar months
'Before returns' means refunds are not deducted, so the figure is gross sales including VAT with no refund_gross subtracted
Staff purchases are kept in, as in the company net sales definition (they are 16,949.92 in August and 16,438.40 in September including VAT)
caveats: The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. The figures use the per-line gross_amount (24% in August, 25.5% from 1 September; reduced rates 14% and 10% unchanged), so the August and September totals are not comparable on a like-for-like VAT basis. No flat rate was applied.
Store 999 and ZZ Test lines were excluded. Store 999 (a few hundred lines each month) is the training store. The filter changes the totals, which would otherwise include training-store lines.

Control check: the same lines at net (excluding VAT) are 1,101,807.91 for August and 964,016.09 for September. Both match rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns for physical stores exactly. No duplicate sales lines were found and gross_amount agrees with net_amount x (1 + vat_rate) on every line.
The figures include VAT and are before returns. Refunds are not deducted, so they will be higher than net sales after returns. Refunds including VAT were not calculated.

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key WHERE s.store_id<900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id<900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'), per AS (SELECT DISTINCT calendar_date, is_trading_day FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period=2), sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, sum(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN per ON per.calendar_date=n.business_date GROUP BY 1), tdays AS (SELECT st.store_id, count(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN per WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id<900 AND per.is_trading_day AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date<=per.calendar_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date>=per.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id=st.store_id AND per.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.net_sales/t.trading_days DESC) AS rank, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ROUND(s.net_sales,2) AS net_sales, t.trading_days, ROUND(s.net_sales/t.trading_days,2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM sales s JOIN tdays t USING (store_id) JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id=s.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank, store_id
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their return date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Trading days: days the store was open (after opening, before closure), outside refit closures in ref_store_closure, and not a closed holiday (is_trading_day)
Store names and region from current dim_store version
Fiscal calendar from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2026/27 P2 = 1 June to 28 June 2026, 4 weeks)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
Ties ranked with RANK (no ties occurred)
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2 (1 to 28 June 2026), the current fiscal year, which is fully loaded and complete
'Store ranking' read as the company's store league table, ranked by net sales per trading day, not by total net sales
A store that traded for only part of the period is still listed, with its own trading days (Kuopio)
Savonlinna (129) is not listed because it closed on 25 January 2026 and had no sales or trading days in P2 (no padding row)
Store names are the current names
caveats: Kuopio (125) was in a refit closure from 15 June 2026, so it traded only 14 days (1 to 14 June). Its net sales of 23,993.71 are for 14 days; ranked per trading day it is 7th, but it is 21st on total net sales, so rank by total would place it much lower.
Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed holidays, so full-period stores have 26 trading days, not 28.
The ranking order differs from a ranking by total net sales because of Kuopio's shorter trading period.
Control total: net sales for each of the 38 stores agree to the cent with rpt_daily_store_sales for 1 to 28 June 2026 (difference 0.00 for every store).

Data checks: no duplicate receipt lines or sales line ids and no duplicate return lines in the period; all sales in the period are in the store channel, so the channel_code and web-dispatch issues do not affect a stores-only table.
Store 999 and ZZ Test were filtered out; the filters did not change any store's total, because the control totals match without any difference.

answer.sql: WITH web_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(f.net_amount) sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE (f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)) AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY ALL), web_returns AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(r.refund_net) refunds_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE (f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)) AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY ALL) SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_period, s.sales_net - r.refunds_net AS web_net_sales FROM web_sales s JOIN web_returns r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period) ORDER BY s.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period dates from dim_date, which agrees with ref_fiscal_calendar. FY2025/26 periods 5 to 8 run 2025-08-25 to 2025-12-21 (P5 4 weeks, P6 5 weeks, P7 4 weeks, P8 4 weeks).

Net sales: EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts and after returns. This follows the rpt_daily_store_sales definition: net sales before returns minus refunds booked on the day, using net_amount and refund_net.

Web channel: channel_code = 'WB' or channel_id in (2, 3). Home delivery and click-and-collect both count as web. The channel coding changed at the web-platform migration on 2025-11-03: sales lines dated before it carry channel_code and no channel_id, and lines from that date on carry channel_id and no channel_code. Periods 7 and 8 cross the change.
Sales are assigned to a period by sale_date. Refunds are assigned by return_date, so they are booked in the period of the refund, not the period of the original sale.
Refunds counted are those on lines that were originally web sales, whether the refund was booked at the web shop (store 900) or at a physical store.
assumptions: 'Last year' is read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26. The request is dated 2026-10-09, in FY2026/27. Calendar 2025 would give the same four periods.
'Web net sales' is read as net of returns, in line with the company's net sales definition, and excluding VAT. The figures before returns are in the caveats.
Refunds on web-origin lines booked at physical stores are deducted from web, because the refund belongs to a web sale. About a quarter of web refunds are booked that way.
Cancelled web orders have no sales lines in the sales fact, so nothing needed removing. There are no staff purchases on web lines.
Web sales are taken from fact_sales_line, not from the reporting table.
caveats: Channel-code change: filtering on channel_code = 'WB' alone loses all web sales from 2025-11-03 onward, which is the end of period 7 and all of period 8. Both the old and new coding were included. Using only channel_id 2 or 3 would lose everything before that date.

rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 (the web shop) is not reliable and was not used. Its daily sales do not match the sales fact: Sundays are near zero and the following Mondays are inflated. Its total for the 17 weeks is 762,115.32, against 767,895.38 in the fact table. Net sales taken from it would be wrong.

Net sales before returns, from the fact table: P5 158,124.35, P6 194,176.17, P7 166,510.02, P8 249,084.84. These total 767,895.38. Refunds deducted: P5 18,585.85, P6 22,385.45, P7 17,045.14, P8 22,366.40. These total 80,383.84.

If only refunds booked at the web shop (store 900) are deducted, the 17-week total is 707,237.93 instead of 687,512.54. That is a difference of about 19,700, or 2.9%. Web-origin refunds booked at physical stores are included in the figures above.
Refunds are booked on the return date, so refunds in these periods can relate to sales from before 2025-08-25. Refunds on P8 sales made after 2025-12-21 are not included.
Periods 5 to 8 are fully loaded. Every day in the window has web sales, and the staging tables hold no sales or refund lines that are missing from the fact tables.
Period 8 includes the Black Friday and pre-Christmas peak, which is why it is the highest period.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS first_period, 6 AS last_period
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
by_category AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d     ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
      AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period
      AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT category, net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * gross_margin / net_sales, 1) AS gross_margin_pct
FROM by_category
ORDER BY category;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Gross margin percentage: (net sales minus standard cost) divided by net sales, both after returns
Scope: store_id <> 999, category <> 'ZZ Test'
Web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Product categories from current product version (as-is reporting)
assumptions: Interpreted 'period 6 last year' as period 6 of FY2025/26 (the most recent completed period 6), which ran 22 September to 26 October 2025
caveats: No data quality issues detected
