answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week BETWEEN 14 AND 17) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-08-03' - 364)), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27','FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 14 AND 17 GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty, lfl_sales ly WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores for the period against the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week, physical stores only (web shop excluded)

Fiscal calendar from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar: P4 is fiscal weeks 14 to 17 in both years, fully loaded
Regions and hierarchy not needed (one total, no breakdown asked)

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, cp.brand, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS net_sales, ROUND(SUM(n.cost),2) AS cost, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost),2) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10

Fiscal calendar: Q4 of FY2024/25 = periods 10 to 12, 27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025 (weeks 40 to 52)
Regions as-is (current dim_store version), so South means stores 106 to 114 and 137, excluding the six stores that moved to Capital Region on 28 Apr 2025 and including Kouvola (114)
Products as-is on the current product version per sku (name, category, subcategory, brand)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900, region Online) is not part of South
Store-level control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
Ranking by absolute gross margin in EUR, not margin percentage
assumptions: 'Q4 of FY24/25' read as FY2024/25 fiscal Q4 (P10 to P12), not calendar Q4

'South region' read as-is, the company default for management reporting, using today's region hierarchy applied to all history; the as-was South (which included Helsinki Vuosaari, Pitäjänmäki, Espoo Lommila, Vantaa Tammisto and Kerava, and excluded Kouvola) would give a different list
'Top 10 products' read as individual SKUs (articles), ranked by gross margin in EUR
Staff purchases are included, as in the company net sales definition
Q4 FY2024/25 is fully loaded, so no part-period issue
caveats: The result uses as-is regions. Kouvola (East before 28 Apr 2025) is counted in South and the five Capital Region stores are not, even though they were South at the time. An as-was South request would need a re-run.
Returns are booked on their return date, so some Q4 margin is reduced by returns of goods sold before 27 Jan 2025, and returns of late-Q4 sales that arrive after 27 Apr 2025 are not in this quarter.
Top 10 sums are small in absolute terms (the largest is about EUR 2,927) because the South stores' sales for one quarter are spread across thousands of SKUs.

Checks found no data corrections needed: no duplicate sales or return lines in the quarter, no null, zero or negative costs or net amounts, line costs match quantity times unit cost, and net sales for the ten South stores match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly over 27 Jan to 27 Apr 2025 (zero difference for every store). Margin figures themselves are not in the control table.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.sale_date, s.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT l.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Return rate: returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net, excluding VAT

Sold lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date) in the fiscal period

No cancelled web orders appear among the P2 lines. All lines are delivered or collected

answer.sql: WITH fy2025_sales AS (SELECT CASE WHEN f.channel_code = 'WB' THEN 'Web' WHEN s.region = 'Online' THEN 'Web' WHEN s.region IS NULL THEN 'Unclassified' ELSE s.region END as region, SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date LEFT JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key AND s.is_current = TRUE WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3 GROUP BY CASE WHEN f.channel_code = 'WB' THEN 'Web' WHEN s.region = 'Online' THEN 'Web' WHEN s.region IS NULL THEN 'Unclassified' ELSE s.region END), fy2024_sales AS (SELECT CASE WHEN f.channel_code = 'WB' THEN 'Web' WHEN s.region = 'Online' THEN 'Web' WHEN s.region IS NULL THEN 'Unclassified' ELSE s.region END as region, SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date LEFT JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key AND s.is_current = TRUE WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3 GROUP BY CASE WHEN f.channel_code = 'WB' THEN 'Web' WHEN s.region = 'Online' THEN 'Web' WHEN s.region IS NULL THEN 'Unclassified' ELSE s.region END) SELECT COALESCE(fy25.region, fy24.region) as region, ROUND(COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0), 2) as net_sales_fy2025, ROUND(COALESCE(fy24.net_sales, 0), 2) as net_sales_fy2024, CASE WHEN COALESCE(fy24.net_sales, 0) > 0 THEN ROUND(((COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0) - COALESCE(fy24.net_sales, 0)) / COALESCE(fy24.net_sales, 0) * 100), 2) ELSE NULL END as growth_pct FROM fy2025_sales fy25 FULL OUTER JOIN fy2024_sales fy24 ON fy25.region = fy24.region WHERE COALESCE(fy25.region, fy24.region) NOT IN ('Head office', 'Unclassified') ORDER BY CASE WHEN COALESCE(fy25.region, fy24.region) = 'Web' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, COALESCE(fy25.region, fy24.region)

assumptions: Last year refers to fiscal year FY2025/26; earlier year refers to FY2024/25

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week
),
range_start AS (
    SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week
),
weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN weeks w
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    CROSS JOIN params
    CROSS JOIN range_start
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
    GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))
)
SELECT ty.region, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM lfl_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY ty.region;
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales in LFL stores compared week-by-week to same fiscal weeks prior year
LFL base: physical stores only, excludes web shop and store 999
52-week opening rule: store must be open 52+ weeks before the period start
Store-week trading rule: week counts only if store traded in both years
Refit weeks: excluded for affected store in both years via ref_store_closure
Week 53 exclusion: never part of LFL (no comparator in prior year)
Net sales: EUR excluding VAT, after returns (return reduces sales on return date)
assumptions: Q3 last year interpreted as Q3 of FY2025/26 (weeks 27-39, 25 October 2025 to 25 January 2026), compared to Q3 FY2024/25 same fiscal weeks (28 October 2024 to 26 January 2025)
Regions reported as-is: current store version geography at sale date
caveats: Savonlinna (store 129) closed 25 January 2026, last day of Q3 period; included in LFL for weeks it traded
No refit closures affected Q3 FY2025/26 (Pori refit was September-October 2025, weeks 25-26; Kuopio refit was June-July 2026, week 27 onwards of next period)
Store openings (Tampere Lamminpää in Sept 2024, Lohja in Nov 2024) already passed the 52-week opening rule for Q3 FY2025/26

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cp.category, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0*SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost)/SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS gross_margin_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 6 AND cp.category IN ('Garden','Electrical') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered/collected orders)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns (returned units credited at standard_cost_returned)
Gross margin %: gross margin divided by net sales
As-is reporting: category taken from the current product version (is_current), so outdoor lighting is in Electrical for all history
Fiscal period 6 taken from dim_date.fiscal_year and fiscal_period (22 September to 26 October 2025, 5 weeks)
Staff purchases included
Web shop (store 900) included in company totals
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request was dated 8 October 2026, during FY2026/27, and past requests in May 2026 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35) read it as the previous fiscal year, so P6 means FY2025/26 P6.
Reported as-is (current hierarchy), the management default, because the request did not ask for as-was.
Figures cover stores and the web shop together. The request did not limit them to a channel, and company-level category reporting includes web.
No comparison was requested, so only FY2025/26 P6 is shown. FY2025/26 P6 has 5 weeks and does not include week 53.
caveats: Outdoor lighting was in Garden until 26 October 2025. The last day of P6 is 26 October 2025, so as-was reporting would put outdoor lighting in Garden for all of P6. I used as-is, so outdoor lighting (EUR 33,781.91 net sales, EUR 12,586.84 gross margin in P6) is counted in Electrical. Read as-was, Garden would be higher and Electrical lower by those amounts.

Five outdoor lighting SKUs (100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) were delisted before the 27 October 2025 move and still sit in Garden in the current product dimension. They have no sales or returns in P6, so they do not change the figures.
Test data (store 999 and ZZ Test) was excluded. It does not affect Garden or Electrical, since test articles are in category ZZ Test.

Net sales by store for the period (all categories) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly across every store. Category-level figures cannot be checked against that table, because it has no category dimension.
I checked the P6 Garden and Electrical sales lines for duplicate lines, null or zero costs, cost mismatches against standard unit cost, VAT mismatches and web orders not yet dispatched. I found none.

Returns arrive up to 30 days after a sale. Returns booked in P6 reduce P6 net sales whatever sale date they relate to, and returns on P6 sales that arrive after 26 October 2025 are not in this figure.

answer.sql: WITH sales_data AS (SELECT ds.format, SUM(fsl.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line fsl INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND dd.fiscal_period = 2 AND ds.store_id < 900 GROUP BY ds.format), return_data AS (SELECT ds.format, SUM(frl.quantity_returned) as units_returned FROM fact_return_line frl INNER JOIN fact_sales_line fsl ON frl.sales_line_id = fsl.sales_line_id INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND dd.fiscal_period = 2 AND ds.store_id < 900 GROUP BY ds.format) SELECT s.format, ROUND(COALESCE(r.units_returned, 0) * 100.0 / s.units_sold, 2) as return_rate FROM sales_data s LEFT JOIN return_data r ON s.format = r.format ORDER BY s.format
definitions_applied: Return rate: units returned divided by units sold, expressed as a percentage
Fiscal period 2: the warehouse fiscal period, not calendar month
Store format classification: physical store formats (Large, Medium, Small) from dim_store, excluding training locations and web channel
assumptions: Last year refers to fiscal year FY2025/26 (the fiscal year preceding the current FY2026/27)
Return rate is calculated by unit count, not by value
Returns attributed to the format of the store where the original sale occurred
Excluded staff purchases and non-store channels to focus on retail store performance
caveats: Store formats in the current database (Large, Medium, Small, Training, Web) differ from the schema documentation which specifies Hyper, Standard, Express. The data appears to have been recategorised or the schema documentation is outdated.
Return rate is based on items sold during period 2 but returned at any time. A full post-purchase window analysis is not available from the warehouse.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P3 is 29 June to 2 August 2026 (weeks 9 to 13), filtered on dim_date.fiscal_year and fiscal_period
Units sold are the quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (store sale date)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no rows in scope, so no effect on the total)
Interior Paint taken from the current product version (as-is); the SKUs have never changed subcategory, so as-was gives the same figure
Store identified by the stable store_id 108 through dim_store, counting no duplicated versions
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for Lahti on every day of the period
assumptions: 'Period 3 this year' read as FY2026/27 P3, the current fiscal year, which is complete (ended 2 August 2026) and fully loaded
'Units sold' read as units sold before returns, the same basis as units_sold in rpt_daily_store_sales
'Lahti' read as store_id 108 Lahti (Large format, South). Tampere Lielahti (116) is a different store and was not included
Interior Paint read as the subcategory 'Interior Paint' in Paint & Decorating (123 SKUs)
Staff purchases are included, as in net sales; they account for 4 of the 194 units
caveats: The data needed no corrections: no duplicate sales lines, no test-article rows in scope, and no day-level mismatch with rpt_daily_store_sales for store 108 (receipts, units, and net sales before returns agree on all 35 days).
The control table has no product dimension, so it confirms the store-level totals but cannot confirm the Interior Paint subset itself.

194 is before returns. Returns of Interior Paint booked at Lahti in the period total 5 units (net 189 if netted on the return date, as net sales are). Returns booked against units sold in the period total 6, since some come back after the period ends.
The figure covers store sales only. Web orders are not part of a store's sales.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE st.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar: 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, 4 weeks, fully_loaded = true
Store identified by store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), joined through the store_key of both of its versions (keys 3 and 4) so the 2025-04-28 version change does not split the store
Products grouped by stable sku rather than the product_key version
Units sold = sum of fact_sales_line.quantity
Sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales: 28 days and 3,740 units, the same as the fact table for this store and period
assumptions: 'Sold the most units' means gross units sold from sales lines, before returns, as the request asks about sales and not net sales
Staff purchases are included because they are real units sold. Excluding them leaves the top three and their order unchanged (52, 44, 40)
'Period 5 of FY26/27' means the warehouse's FY2026/27 P05
'Pitäjänmäki store' means the one store with that name, store_id 102
caveats: No data problem needed correcting for this question. The sales lines have no duplicate sales_line_ids, there are no zero or negative quantities, and the store traded on all 28 days of the period.
Returns were not netted off. They are small in the top three: 1 unit returned on Havu Pro 791, none on the other two. The ranking stays the same either way.
The third place has a clear gap: Havu Pro 791 has 42 units against 30 for the fourth-placed products (Storage Boxes Vesikko 753 and Batteries & Bulbs Havu Pro 384), so there is no tie at the cut-off.
The warehouse holds old and backup tables (dim_product_old, bak_* and others). I did not use them.

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT sum(f.net_amount) AS v FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30' AND s.store_id <> 999), returns AS (SELECT sum(r.refund_net) AS v FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30' AND s.store_id <> 999) SELECT round(sales.v - returns.v, 2) AS net_sales_eur FROM sales, returns
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net sales (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refunds (refund_net), the same definition as rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales
Company-wide = all 38 trading stores plus the web shop (store_id 900)
Refunds counted on the date the return was booked (return_date), as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Staff purchases left in, as in the Data & Analytics daily report
Training store (store_id 999) excluded as a pseudo-location, not a real store
Sales and returns joined to dim_store through store_key, the version-aware surrogate key
assumptions: 'Last month' means calendar September 2026 (1-30 Sep), as the request was received on 9 October 2026
'Whole company' means stores plus web, not stores only
Amounts are in EUR excluding VAT, matching the company's net sales definition
Web sales are dated by sale_date (Helsinki local date), which is the fact table's own date
caveats: Web shop lines have a NULL channel_code and are identified by the web pseudo-store (store_id 900) in dim_store. A filter on channel_code = 'WB' (as in rpt.v_daily_sales) misses them, so I did not use it.

rpt_daily_store_sales agrees exactly with the fact tables for physical stores, but its web shop (store 900) figures differ from the fact tables. Its daily web sales are shifted, with near-zero Sundays and large Mondays, which suggests a different dating rule. For September, web sales before returns are 209,990.40 in the report against 205,567.52 in the fact table. Using the report would give about 1,179,036, which is 4,423 higher than my figure. I used the fact tables.
Net sales of 1,174,613.10 is sales of 1,248,875.34 less refunds of 74,262.24. Of the sales, 1,043,307.82 is stores and 205,567.52 is web. Of the refunds, 54,715.66 is stores and 19,546.58 is web.
The training store (999) booked 3,084.66 of sales in September, almost all staff purchases. I excluded it. It had no refunds.
Staff purchases are included. In the real stores they come to 13,499.45 of September sales.
If the company's fiscal period 5 is meant instead (FY2026/27 P05, 31 Aug-27 Sep, the last fully loaded fiscal period), net sales are 1,107,414.30. The fiscal period P06 is still loading.

Checks on September data found no duplicate lines, orphan keys, VAT inconsistencies, cancelled web orders or rows waiting in the staging tables. All 38 open stores have sales on all 30 days. Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 Jan 2026 and has no September sales.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line AS f INNER JOIN dim_product AS p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date AS d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE p.sku = 101624 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week = 22 GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Last week interpreted as the most recent fiscal week in the warehouse data (fiscal week 22 of FY2026/27, Sept 28 - Oct 4, 2026)
Sales line quantity summed across all channels and store types for the specified SKU
assumptions: Last week refers to the most recent fiscal week with complete sales data, not the calendar week
SKU 101624 is the correct identifier, despite the product name mismatch noted in caveats
caveats: Product name mismatch: The request refers to 'Oulu Kaakkuri', but SKU 101624 is 'Fixings & Fasteners Raudikko 251' in the warehouse. Verified no product with 'Kaakkuri' in the name exists. This may indicate a data entry error in the request or the warehouse.
The most recent sales data in the warehouse extends only to October 4, 2026. The request arrived on October 8; if more recent sales are expected, the warehouse may not be fully loaded.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS members_held_out FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15
definitions_applied: Campaign holdout: Members who were on the campaign mailing list but deliberately excluded from contact (holdout group for measurement purposes)
Black Week 2025: Marketing campaign run from 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-30 (campaign_id 15)
assumptions: Identified the Black Week 2025 campaign by exact name match in dim_campaign.campaign_name
Counted actual member holdout records from the campaign_holdout table (not the pre-calculated holdout_size, though both match)
caveats: The campaign data reflects the mailing list composition at the time the campaign was set up; any member record changes (tier upgrades, deactivations, consent changes) made after campaign setup would not be reflected in the holdout count

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT f.week_ending_date, SUM(f.closing_value) AS chain_stock_value FROM fact_stock_week f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.week_ending_date WHERE p.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY f.week_ending_date) SELECT ROUND(AVG(chain_stock_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 3 of FY2026/27 runs 2026-06-29 to 2026-08-02 (5 weeks, fiscal weeks 9 to 13)
Stock value at standard cost: fact_stock_week.closing_value (closing units x standard unit cost)
Product category from the product version in force at the week-ending date (dim_product.category = 'Paint & Decorating')
Average stock: the mean of the five weekly closing stock values for the fiscal period, each summed across all stores
Whole chain: all 38 stores that hold stock, no store or region filter
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as at the request date of 2026-10-08, so period 3 is 29 June to 2 August 2026.

'Average stock' means the average of the weekly closing stock values over the 5 weeks of the period (week endings 5, 12, 19 and 26 July and 2 August). The warehouse holds stock only as weekly closing snapshots, so the average is not daily-weighted.
'Value at cost' means standard cost, as held in the warehouse (closing_value).
'Whole chain' means all stores summed; the web shop and pseudo-locations hold no Paint & Decorating stock in the data.
Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 and still shows stock. I kept it in, since the goods were still held and belong to the chain's stock.
caveats: I found no errors in the stock data for this period and made no corrections. I checked that no store, SKU and week appears twice, that no units or values are negative, that closing_value equals closing units x standard unit cost on every row, that the period is fully loaded, and that all 38 stores appear in all 5 weeks.
25 store-SKU rows (3 delisted SKUs, delisted 2026-07-01) show zero stock at the week ending 5 July and disappear from later weeks. They carry no value, so they do not change the figure.
The weekly chain totals are: 341,138.89 (5 Jul), 341,742.53 (12 Jul), 344,245.91 (19 Jul), 349,160.39 (26 Jul) and 346,046.42 (2 Aug) euros. The average moves little across the period.

The figure is at standard cost, not purchase or latest cost. Standard costs are revalued each April, so the figure is not comparable with a period before the April revaluation without allowing for that.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS gold_members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key, because dim_member keeps one row per version
Tier read from the current member version (is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Report as-is: the member's tier today
assumptions: 'At the moment' means each member's current tier, in the latest version of dim_member. The warehouse is loaded to 4 October 2026, three days before the request date.

'Gold-tier loyalty members' means every enrolled member whose current tier is Gold, whether or not they have bought recently. The metric dictionary defines 'active member' but not 'member', and the request does not say 'active'.
Staff and test members were not separated out, because dim_member has no flag for them.
caveats: I checked dim_member before counting. All 60,000 members have exactly one current version, and that version is the one with valid_to = 9999-12-31. I found no duplicate or overlapping current versions and no invalid date ranges. The count needed no correction.
If Store operations meant only members who have bought in the last 52 fiscal weeks (the company's 'active member' definition, as of Sunday 4 October 2026), the Gold figure is 4,827 instead of 5,791.

7,210 distinct members have held Gold at some point. 1,419 of them have since moved to another tier and are not counted. Counting rows in dim_member without filtering to the current version would overstate the number.
The figure comes from the warehouse load, which runs to 4 October 2026. Tier changes made after that are not included.

answer.sql: WITH first_version AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS version_no FROM dim_member) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS new_members FROM first_version WHERE version_no = 1 AND join_date = DATE '2026-09-25'
definitions_applied: New member: counted on their join date
Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key, so version rows are not double-counted
Join date taken from the member's first version in dim_member
Date used as the calendar date 2026-09-25 (join_date is a date, with no UTC conversion)
assumptions: Read "new members who signed up on 25 September 2026" as loyalty members whose join_date is 2026-09-25.
Gave one total across all channels, store and online, because the request asks for a single figure and no breakdown by store.
caveats: No corrections to the data were needed. Each of the 39 members has a single join_date and one version row, with no duplicate versions.
None of the 39 joined at the training store 999, so no exclusion was needed.
31 of the 39 enrolled at physical stores and 8 signed up online (home store 900), so the total includes online sign-ups. Subtract those 8 if Marketing wants store enrolments only.
The warehouse holds data up to 4 October 2026, so 25 September 2026 is fully loaded.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 2) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 6 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2;
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Net sales = net amount excluding VAT, after returns; a return reduces net sales on its own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date), not on sale_date
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders have dispatch dates and sales lines)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is not filled from the 3 November 2025 migration, which falls inside P7)
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27, as accepted requests in May 2026 did. Periods 6 to 8 are therefore FY2025/26 P6 (22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025), P7 (27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025) and P8 (24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025).
'Sales' means net sales on the company definition, not order counts or sales including VAT.
Refunds are taken as booked to the web shop (store 900) on their return date, as in the accepted click-and-collect share reading (REQ-D22). Each refund is assigned to its order's fulfilment type.
One share per period, with no total across P6 to P8.
caveats: No correction was needed for the requested periods. The only duplicated sales-line keys (418 keys, each loaded twice) are in FY2025/26 P5 store lines. P6 to P8 are unaffected, and no web lines are duplicated.
The web net sales behind each share match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for store 900 exactly in all three periods: 175,588.62 in P6, 154,977.27 in P7 and 225,265.08 in P8.

Some web orders were returned in physical stores, and those refunds are booked to the store, not to the web shop. They are not in these figures. Counting them against the web order would move the shares slightly, to about 27.51% in P6, 25.32% in P7 and 27.01% in P8, so the conclusions do not change.
The 3 November 2025 platform migration is inside P7. Neither channel_code nor channel_id works across it, so web and click-and-collect were identified by store 900 and fulfilment_type.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, but net sales book them on the return date. P8 is fully loaded, so no period is affected by late returns.

answer.sql: SELECT s.closing_units FROM fact_stock_week AS s INNER JOIN dim_product AS p ON s.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_store AS st ON s.store_key = st.store_key WHERE p.sku = 100011 AND st.store_id = 124 AND s.week_ending_date = '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Fiscal week definition from dim_date: fiscal weeks end on Sunday
Last week from request date 2026-10-08: fiscal week 22 ending 2026-10-04
Current product and store versions: is_current = TRUE
Stock closing units at fiscal week end: closing_units from fact_stock_week
assumptions: Last week refers to the most recent completed fiscal week before the request date (2026-10-08), which ended 2026-10-04
The store reference Jyväskylä Palokka was matched to store_id 124 (Jyväskylä Palokka)
The request asks for closing stock units (not receipts or adjustments)
caveats: The request combined a product SKU (100011) with a store name in one phrase; these are separate entities — the product is Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570, the store is Jyväskylä Palokka
Stock data is point-in-time as of fiscal week end; no intra-week granularity is available

answer.sql: SELECT st.format AS store_format, round(100 * sum(coalesce(r.refund_net, 0)) / sum(f.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON r.sales_line_id = f.sales_line_id WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-05-26' AND DATE '2025-06-22' AND st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY st.format ORDER BY st.format
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 2 of FY2025/26 runs 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22 (ref_fiscal_calendar, fully loaded)
Return rate = refunds excluding VAT (fact_return_line.refund_net) divided by net sales excluding VAT (fact_sales_line.net_amount) of the same lines
Returns are matched to the original sales line through sales_line_id, so a return counts in the period the goods were sold, not the period it was booked
Store format taken from dim_store through the sales line's store_key (the store version in force on the sale date)
Physical stores only: web shop (store 900) and Training store (999) excluded
assumptions: 'Last year' means the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26, because the request date (2026-10-05) falls in FY2026/27; period 2 is 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22

'Goods sold in period 2' means sales lines dated in that period, with every later return of those lines counted, whenever it was booked. Returns of P2 sales were booked from 2025-05-27 to 2025-07-23, all of it well in the past, so the figures are complete
Return rate measured by value (refunds excluding VAT over net sales excluding VAT). No company definition of return rate was available
The return is attributed to the format of the store where the goods were sold, even if the goods were returned at another store (102 returned lines of P2 sales were booked at a different store key)
Staff purchases kept in, as in the Data & Analytics daily sales report (rpt_daily_store_sales, whose before-returns net sales for stores equal the fact table total including staff purchases)
Rows are the store formats that exist in the data. The warehouse column comment says Hyper, Standard and Express, but the data holds Large, Medium and Small, so I used the data values
caveats: Format labels do not match the schema comment: dim_store.format holds Large, Medium and Small, not Hyper, Standard and Express. If Commercial uses the Hyper/Standard/Express names, a mapping is needed, and I have not assumed one (Large, Medium and Small are the only physical-store formats in the data)
Web shop excluded because it is not a store format. For information, its return rate on the same basis is 12.23%, far above the stores. Including it in any blended rate would distort the figure
Training store (999) excluded: it has 126 sales lines (about 2.2k EUR net) in the period, no returns, and is not a real store
Staff purchases are included. Excluding them would give Large 4.45%, Medium 4.56% and Small 4.30%, and staff lines return less than customer lines. The result moves by 0.03 percentage points or less

Differences between the three formats are small (4.28% to 4.53%), so I would not read a ranking into them. Unit-based rates are 2.37% (Large), 2.44% (Medium) and 2.39% (Small), which order the formats differently from the value-based rates
Stores moved from the old region to Capital Region at 2025-04-28 (store versions), but format did not change in any version, so format attribution is unaffected by the slowly changing store dimension
The staging return table overlaps with fact_return_line (141 return lines in both). Each return line appears only once in the fact table, so there was no double counting
The two non-fact-style tables I did not use (backup, old and staging copies) were left out on purpose
FY2026/27 period 6 is not fully loaded in the warehouse, but this does not affect a P2 FY2025/26 analysis

answer.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, count(DISTINCT h.member_id) AS members_held_out FROM dim_campaign c JOIN campaign_holdout h ON h.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE c.campaign_id = 15 GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name
definitions_applied: Held out = a member listed in campaign_holdout for the campaign, counted by member_id (not member_key)
Black Week 2025 = dim_campaign campaign_id 15, 24-30 Nov 2025, email+sms+push
Counted distinct loyalty numbers (member_id), so members with several dim_member versions are not double counted
assumptions: 'Black Week 2025' means campaign 15 in dim_campaign, the only campaign with that name (the 2024 edition is campaign 5)
The question asks for the number of members in the holdout group, not those who would have been mailed
Used the live dim_campaign and campaign_holdout tables and ignored the bak_, stg_ and tmp_ tables
caveats: No correction was needed. campaign_holdout has 2747 rows for campaign 15, all distinct members, and this matches dim_campaign.holdout_size (2747).
All 2747 held-out members exist in dim_member and had marketing consent on the campaign start date (24 Nov 2025). None of them has a contact recorded in fact_campaign_exposure for this campaign.

The holdout is 10.3% of the 26573-member mailing list (list size includes the holdout), a little above the nominal 10% (dim_campaign.holdout_pct = 0.100). I read this as normal variation in the draw, not an error.

The mailing list is not the same as everyone consented on 24 Nov 2025. Using the campaign's own target-group rule (consent at campaign start), I count about 33080 members, and about 6515 of them are neither on the exposure list nor held out. I did not investigate this because it does not change the holdout count, but whoever uses the list size as a denominator should know the gap exists.

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT sum(f.net_amount) AS gross_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30' AND s.store_id <> 999), refunds AS (SELECT sum(r.refund_net) AS refunds FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30' AND s.store_id <> 999) SELECT sales.gross_sales - refunds.refunds AS net_sales_eur FROM sales, refunds
definitions_applied: Net sales = line value in EUR excluding VAT after line discounts (net_amount), minus refunds excluding VAT (refund_net)
Whole company = all physical stores plus the web shop (store 900), web home delivery and click and collect both included
Returns deducted on the date the refund is booked (return_date), including refunds on sales made in earlier months, as in rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales = net_sales_before_returns - returns_net)
sale_date taken as the local (Helsinki) calendar date; it matches the UTC-to-Helsinki date for every row, so no timezone shift was needed
Sales and returns linked to dim_store through store_key (the version of the store at the sale date), not by store_id alone
assumptions: 'Last month' read as calendar September 2026, since the request arrived on 9 October 2026 and September is fully loaded (sales data runs to 4 Oct 2026)
Staff purchases kept in net sales: they are real sales and are included in rpt_daily_store_sales. No company definition in the schema says to exclude them
Web orders counted from the sales lines. Only delivered and collected orders have sales lines; cancelled and processing orders have none
Result is a single company-wide figure with no breakdown, as the request asks for one number
caveats: Corrected: the Training store (store_id 999, a pseudo-location) is excluded. It had 160 sales lines in September worth EUR 3,084.66 net (about 2,957.51 of it staff purchases). It is not a real store and has no returns, so the figure excludes it

Do not use rpt_daily_store_sales for this figure. Its store rows match the fact table, but its web shop (store 900) rows do not. Daily web figures swing from near zero on Sundays to roughly double on Mondays, which looks like weekend sales booked on the next working day. September web sales before returns are EUR 209,990.40 in that report against EUR 205,567.52 in the fact table, a EUR 4,422.88 gap. I used the fact tables

Do not use the view rpt.v_daily_sales / v_weekly_store_sales without checking it. It adds a store branch (store_id < 900) and a web branch (channel_code = 'WB'), but channel_code is NULL on every September sales line, so the web branch returns nothing and web sales are missing from the view

September gross net sales before returns are EUR 1,248,875.34 (stores 1,043,307.82, web 205,567.52). Refunds booked in September are EUR 74,262.24, of which EUR 17,611.92 is for sales made before September. Net sales are EUR 1,174,613.10

If 'month' means the fiscal period rather than the calendar month, the last full fiscal period is FY2026/27 period 5 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, 4 weeks). Its net sales on the same basis are EUR 1,107,414.30. Period 6 started on 28 Sep and is not fully loaded
If staff purchases were excluded, September net sales would be about EUR 1,161,882 (staff sales of EUR 13,499.45 in stores, less EUR 768.22 of refunds on staff purchases)
Web sales are shown in the web shop's own pseudo-location (store 900), not under any physical store. Click-and-collect sales are counted as web, not under the collection store

No duplicate sales or return lines, no orphaned store keys and nothing waiting in the staging tables were found for September. Every store has sales on all 30 days. The backup, old and tmp tables were not used

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS gold_members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not by member_key (dim_member keeps one row per version)
Current tier taken from the current member version (is_current, valid_to 9999-12-31)
Loyalty tiers are Basic, Silver and Gold
Company data is as of the warehouse load point, Sunday 4 October 2026
assumptions: 'Gold-tier loyalty members' is read as all enrolled members whose current tier is Gold, whether or not they have bought recently. The metric dictionary defines only 'active member', not a plain member headcount, and I could not ask in the queue.

'At the moment' is read as the latest data in the warehouse. The last sales are dated 2026-10-04 and the latest member versions start on 2026-10-04, so this is the position at the end of Sunday 4 October 2026, three days before the request date.
Staff and test accounts are not excluded, because dim_member carries no flag for them.
caveats: A plain count of dim_member rows with tier = 'Gold' gives 8,203. That is wrong, because it counts every historical version of a member. Of those rows, 2,412 are superseded versions, 2,233 distinct members once held Gold at some point, and 5,791 hold it now. I used the current version only.

Checks on dim_member: each member has exactly one current version, no version date ranges overlap or leave gaps, there are no duplicate member_keys and no unexpected tier values. Counting Gold on 4 October 2026 or on 7 October 2026 by validity dates also gives 5,791.

If the question is about active Gold members, meaning at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks to 4 October 2026 (the company definition of an active member), the figure is 4,827. The 5,791 includes members who have not bought in that window.
Members who changed tier after 4 October 2026 are not reflected, since the warehouse holds no later data.

answer.sql: SELECT d.store_name, dd.fiscal_year, dd.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key JOIN dim_store d ON f.store_key = d.store_key JOIN dim_date dd ON f.sale_date = dd.calendar_date WHERE p.product_name LIKE 'Interior Paint%' AND d.store_id = 108 AND dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND dd.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY d.store_name, dd.fiscal_year, dd.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 defined by ref_fiscal_calendar (2026-06-29 to 2026-08-02)
Sales measured from fact_sales_line; quantity field represents units sold at point of sale
Interior Paint defined as all products with product_name matching 'Interior Paint%' pattern
assumptions: Interior Paint category includes all Interior Paint variants (123 SKUs with different brand/colour combinations)
Lahti store identified by store_id 108 and store_key 13
Sales measured at point of transaction (gross of returns)
Period 3 determined by fiscal calendar alignment with calendar dates
caveats: 5 units of Interior Paint were returned from Lahti store within the same period; figure shown is gross sales at point of sale, not net of returns
Sales include all channels (store and web) routed through Lahti location

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory AS subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 107 AND cp.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Units sold = sum of quantity on sales lines, by Helsinki sale_date (metric dictionary, stock section)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P05, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (fiscal weeks 18 to 21), complete
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither affects this figure)
As-is product hierarchy via the current product version (is_current)
Store scope: physical store 107 Hyvinkää only; web shop (store 900) not included
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total: store 107 units and net sales before returns for the period agree with rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27; 'period 5' read as fiscal period 5 (P05), the last completed period as of 5 Oct 2026
'Cleaning Products' read as the subcategory of that name, which sits in the category Cleaning & Household; the whole category would be 221 units
'Units sold' read as units on sales lines, before returns, not net of returns
Sales dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
caveats: No data problems needed correcting in this query: no duplicate sales lines, and Hyvinkää's total units (1,626) and net sales before returns (27,297.68 EUR) for the period match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, with sales on all 28 days.
136 units includes 4 units bought by staff.
No Cleaning Products units were returned at Hyvinkää during the period, so net-of-returns units would also be 136.
Hyvinkää's store_id is 107; web orders are booked to the web shop (store 900), so any web sales of cleaning products to Hyvinkää customers are not in this figure.
If Mika meant the whole Cleaning & Household category rather than the Cleaning Products subcategory, the figure is 221 units.

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS tampere_loyalty_members FROM dim_member m JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = m.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE m.is_current AND s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900
definitions_applied: Customer = loyalty member (dim_member), the only identifiable customer record
Current member version only (is_current = true), counted once per member_id
Tampere = member's home store is one of the four Tampere stores (Hervanta, Lielahti, Kaleva, Lamminpää)
Home store resolved through store_id to the current dim_store version
Real stores only (store_id < 900)
assumptions: Read 'customers' as loyalty members, since non-members and guest web buyers cannot be counted or located
Read 'in Tampere' as having a Tampere store as home store, with no purchase-activity filter, so lapsed members are included
Counted as of the latest data (4 Oct 2026)
Counted people, not marketing-reachable contacts, so members without marketing consent are included
caveats: Excluded online sign-ups (home store 900): the web shop is listed under city Tampere in dim_store, but those 12,028 members have no real location. Including them would give a wrong figure.
Excluded the Training store (999), also listed under Tampere. It has no members.

dim_member holds several versions per member (89,314 rows for 60,000 members), so counting rows would overstate the figure. I counted the current version per member_id only. Home-store counts across all versions would be 11,921 rows.
The count includes lapsed members: 4,443 of the 7,175 bought something in the 12 months to 4 Oct 2026.
Only 4,841 of the 7,175 have marketing consent, which matters if the number is meant for campaign planning.
Split by home store: Hervanta 2,788, Lielahti 1,721, Kaleva 1,692, Lamminpää 974.
People who live in Tampere but joined at a store elsewhere, or who are not members, are not counted. The warehouse holds no customer address.
The same person could hold more than one member_id; this cannot be detected in the warehouse.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, cs.format FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT l.format AS store_format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) / sold net, excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: sold lines selected by the fiscal period of the original sale date, refunds matched through sales_line_id whenever they were booked
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar: period 2 = 26 May 2025 to 22 June 2025 (4 weeks, no week 53)
Store format taken from the current dim_store version (format is the same in every version)
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own format, Web
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27), and 'period 2' as P2 of that year, 26 May to 22 June 2025, as past requests read it
'What was sold' read as net value excluding VAT (sold net after line discounts), and 'came back' as refund_net excluding VAT, so the share is a value share, not a unit share

Web is included as a format row because dim_store.format has a Web value for the web shop; web sales are dated by sale_date (the order date), as in the accepted return-rate requests, not by dispatch date
Staff purchases are included
Formats are Large, Medium, Small and Web; the Hyper/Standard/Express values in the column comment are out of date
caveats: The P2 sales cohort is complete: the last sale was 22 June 2025 and returns arrive up to 30 days later, with data loaded through 4 October 2026
Web returns are 12.23%, about three times the store formats, so a combined figure that includes web would be higher than any store format. If you only want physical stores, drop the Web row
Checks run: no duplicate sales lines, no duplicate or orphaned return lines, no refunds larger than the original line, and no cancelled web orders in the cohort

No data corrections were needed beyond the standard exclusions (store 999, ZZ Test), which cover only the training store and test articles. I did not run the rpt_daily_store_sales control total, because it covers net sales after returns on return dates, not the sale-week cohort return rate

answer.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT period_start_date AS a, period_end_date AS b FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period=2), sales AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, d.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store d ON d.store_key=f.store_key, p WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN p.a AND p.b AND d.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag), sold AS (SELECT format, sum(net_amount) AS sold_net FROM sales GROUP BY 1), returned AS (SELECT s.format, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net FROM sales s JOIN fact_return_line r USING(sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1) SELECT sold.format AS store_format, round(100*returned.refund_net/sold.sold_net, 2) AS return_share_pct FROM sold JOIN returned USING(format) ORDER BY CASE sold.format WHEN 'Large' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Last year's period 2 = FY2025/26 P02 (2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22) from ref_fiscal_calendar; the current fiscal year is FY2026/27
Return share = refund_net divided by net_amount (both EUR excluding VAT) on the same sales lines
Sales lines linked to their returns through sales_line_id
Store format taken from dim_store via the store_key on the sales line (format is the same across store versions)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900)
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag = false)
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year before the request date (6 Oct 2026), i.e. FY2025/26. Period 2 is the fiscal period, not calendar month 2.

'What came back' means refunds on lines sold in period 2, whenever the refund was booked. The last refund on these lines was booked on 2025-07-23, so every return window is complete. If the question means refunds booked during period 2 divided by period 2 sales, the figures are Large 4.65, Medium 4.79, Small 4.33.
The share is by value (EUR excluding VAT). Units were not used.
The web shop is left out because it is not a store format. Leena is in Store operations and the question asks for a split by store format. The web shop's return share is far higher, at about 12.2%.

Staff purchases are left out because they are not customer sales and their return rate is much lower (about 2.0 to 2.5%). Including them would move each figure by about 0.01 to 0.03 percentage points.
caveats: Correction: the 'Training' store (store_id 999) has sales lines in period 2 (about EUR 2,222 net, mostly flagged as staff purchases). These are test data and were excluded. It has no returns.
Correction: the web shop (store_id 900, format 'Web') was excluded from the store-format split.
Correction: staff purchases were excluded, as described above.
The format labels in the warehouse are Large, Medium and Small. The column comment says Hyper, Standard or Express, so the comment is out of date. I used the labels the data holds.
I found no duplicate sales or return lines for this period. Every return links to an existing sales line and none returns more than was sold.
Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 2026-01-25. It was open throughout period 2 last year and stays in the Small figure.
Several Helsinki-area stores changed region on 2025-04-28 and Kouvola changed from East to South. This does not affect a split by format.

answer.sql: WITH first_version AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS version_no FROM dim_member) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS new_members FROM first_version WHERE version_no = 1 AND join_date = DATE '2026-09-25'
definitions_applied: New member: counted on the join date, taken from the member's first version in dim_member
Members counted by distinct member_id (not member_key), so later versions do not add rows
Online sign-ups (home store 900) count as new members
dim_member used as the member source; stg_ and bak_ tables not used
assumptions: 'Signed up on 25 September 2026' is read as join_date = 2026-09-25, the company definition of a new member
The total across all enrolling stores and online is wanted, with no breakdown by store or region
join_date is a plain date, so no UTC-to-Helsinki conversion is needed
caveats: No data problems found for this date: there were 39 rows with that join date, all distinct member_ids, all first versions, and no member had a second version with the same join date
The 39 include 8 online sign-ups (store 900) and 31 sign-ups at physical stores
dim_member has join dates up to 4 October 2026, so 25 September is inside the loaded range

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-08-25' AS start_date, DATE '2025-09-21' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line WHERE sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-08-25' AND DATE '2025-09-21' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open (after opening, before closure), outside refit closures in ref_store_closure, and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
A store that traded for only part of the period stays in the table with its own trading days
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P05 = fiscal weeks 18 to 21, Monday 25 August 2025 to Sunday 21 September 2025 (28 days, no week 53)
Store name and format taken from the current dim_store version (as-is)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales: after the duplicate correction, result and control both total 940,396.62 and match store by store
assumptions: 'Period 5 last year' was read as FY2025/26 P05. The request was received on 8 October 2026, in FY2026/27, and requests since May 2026 that said 'last year' were accepted as FY2025/26.
If the requester meant P5 of the current year (FY2026/27 P05, 31 August to 27 September 2026), the table would need to be rerun on those dates.
'Store league table' was taken to mean ranking by net sales per trading day, as the company definition says. Ties are not an issue because ranks are strictly ordered at this precision.
The table is not restricted by format or region, so all 39 physical stores that traded in the period are listed.
Net sales per trading day is shown to 2 decimals. Net sales is shown to the cent.
caveats: Correction: duplicate sales lines at Tampere Lielahti (store 116). 418 lines dated 15 to 21 September 2025 were loaded a second time on 23 September 2025 under new sales_line_ids, with the same receipt_id and line_no and the same amounts. They added 10,390.53 EUR of net sales (47,679.15 against the true 37,288.62). I kept the first-loaded copy of each receipt_id and line_no. Without the correction Lielahti would rank 3rd instead of 7th and the stores ranked 3 to 6 would each sit one place lower.
After the correction the league table agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales for all 39 stores. The duplicates should be removed from fact_sales_line at source. Only store 116 was affected in this period.

Pori (119) was shut for a refit from 8 September 2025, so it has 14 trading days against 28 for every other store. It is ranked on its own trading days, which put it 10th. Its total net sales (16,057.86) are not comparable with the other stores.
The period has no closed public holidays, so every store open the whole period has 28 trading days.
Savonlinna (129), later closed (25 January 2026), traded the whole of this period and is included. Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) were already open (opened September and November 2024).
Rank is by net sales per trading day, so a store with higher total net sales can rank below a store with lower total (Pori is the clear example).

answer.sql: WITH sales_by_year AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, s.store_id, s.store_name, s.region, SUM(r.net_sales) AS period_net_sales, SUM(r.receipts) AS period_receipts, SUM(r.units_sold) AS period_units FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r INNER JOIN dim_date d ON r.business_date = d.calendar_date INNER JOIN dim_store s ON r.store_id = s.store_id AND s.is_current = TRUE WHERE d.fiscal_period = 4 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26') AND r.store_id < 900 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, s.store_id, s.store_name, s.region), lfl_stores AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_id FROM sales_by_year GROUP BY store_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) = 2), lfl_sales AS (SELECT * FROM sales_by_year WHERE store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM lfl_stores)), regional_summary AS (SELECT s24.region, SUM(s24.period_net_sales) AS net_sales_p4_fy2024_25, SUM(s26.period_net_sales) AS net_sales_p4_fy2025_26, COUNT(DISTINCT s24.store_id) AS store_count FROM lfl_sales s24 INNER JOIN lfl_sales s26 ON s24.store_id = s26.store_id AND s24.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND s26.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' GROUP BY s24.region) SELECT region, net_sales_p4_fy2024_25, net_sales_p4_fy2025_26, ROUND(((net_sales_p4_fy2025_26 - net_sales_p4_fy2024_25) / net_sales_p4_fy2024_25 * 100), 1) AS net_sales_pct_change, store_count FROM regional_summary ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Like-for-like comparison: stores operating in both Period 4 FY2024/25 and Period 4 FY2025/26
Physical stores only: web shop (store 900) excluded from comparison
Period 4: 27 July to 24 August (4 weeks, aligned to fiscal calendar)
Net sales: revenue excluding VAT, after line discounts
Percentage change: calculated as ((current period - prior period) / prior period) × 100
assumptions: Request interprets 'this year' as FY2025/26 and 'last year' as FY2024/25
Web shop sales excluded as they are not comparable to physical stores
Like-for-like comparison includes only stores that had sales data in both periods
Store status determined using is_current flag from dim_store; no partial-year exclusions applied beyond store opening/closing dates
caveats: 37 of 39 physical stores operated in both periods; stores 136 (Tampere Lamminpää, opened 2 Sep 2024) and 137 (Lohja, opened 4 Nov 2024) excluded as they opened after Period 4 FY2024/25
Store 129 (Savonlinna) included in comparison despite closing 25 Jan 2026, as it was operating during both Period 4s
Capital Region shows strongest like-for-like growth (+17.9%), driven by Vantaa Tammisto (+73.8%) and Helsinki Pitäjänmäki (+14.0%)
North region shows minimal growth (+0.2%), with declines at Kemi (-14.7%) and Kajaani (-14.3%) offsetting gains elsewhere
Web shop (store 900) achieved 34.9% growth (EUR 115.2k to 155.4k) in the same period, suggesting channel-specific demand trends

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS web_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 4 AND 6 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Figures including VAT: sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, using each line's own VAT rate
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders count as web sales)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: Q2 = periods 4 to 6
Before returns: no refunds deducted
assumptions: Q2 of FY24/25 is FY2024/25 (29 April 2024 to 27 April 2025), periods 4 to 6, as the request states: P4 29 Jul to 25 Aug 2024, P5 26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024, P6 23 Sep to 27 Oct 2024.
The request asks for sales before returns, so refunds (refund_gross) are not deducted. Company net sales is normally after returns, but the request explicitly asks otherwise.
Dispatch date is used for web sales because that is the company recognition rule. For click-and-collect orders this is the ready-for-collection date.
Staff purchases are included, as in the company net sales definition.
caveats: No data problem found for this range, so no correction was made. Checked: no duplicate sales lines on web, every web line has a matching web order, all web lines in the period belong to delivered or collected orders, and the gross figures equal net times (1 + each line's VAT rate) to the cent.
The net equivalents (126242.65, 122660.57, 153786.32) match the web shop (store 900) net_sales_before_returns in rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for the three periods.
The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, inside P5. Summing gross_amount line by line handles this. Multiplying a net total by one flat rate would be wrong.
The deprecated view rpt.v_daily_sales was not used; it drops web sales from 3 November 2025 (outside this range, but it is unreliable for web).

Duplicate receipt and line numbers exist in the warehouse for store sales in the week of 15 to 21 September 2025 (418 pairs). They are outside this request's range and are not web lines, so they do not affect these figures.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales of LFL stores vs the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns booked on their own return date
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop excluded from LFL
LFL base: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the period
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (refit and closure weeks dropped, using ref_store_closure and close_date)
Week 53 never LFL (not relevant to P4)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: period 4 = fiscal weeks 14 to 17, compared by fiscal week number rather than calendar date
Current store dimension version (as-is) for open and close dates and stores
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as of the request date 5 October 2026, so 'last year' is FY2025/26
Period 4 is FY2026/27 weeks 14 to 17 (3 to 30 August 2026), compared with FY2025/26 weeks 14 to 17 (28 July to 24 August 2025); P4 is fully loaded, since the warehouse runs to 4 October 2026
'The stores' is read as the whole LFL store base, so the answer is one total row; no breakdown by region or store was asked for
Growth is on net sales in EUR excluding VAT
caveats: Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and is excluded from LFL, although it traded in P4 last year (about EUR 9,549 net)

No refit weeks fell in P4 in either year. Kuopio's 2026 refit ended on 26 July, so it counts for all four weeks; Pori's refit was in autumn 2025. The base is therefore 38 stores x 4 weeks = 152 store-weeks in each year
Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in autumn 2024, over 364 days before the period, so both are in the base

LFL is effectively flat at -0.03% (EUR 1,010,478.52 against EUR 1,010,743.32, a difference of about EUR 265), so store-level results differ a lot: for example Lohja +25.4%, Kokkola +21.2%, Mikkeli -26.2%, Hämeenlinna -17.6%, Kerava -16.0%
Net sales were reconciled to rpt_daily_store_sales for P4 of both years store by store with no gap above EUR 0.50, and there were no duplicate sales lines. No data corrections were needed
The deprecated rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales views were not used

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(frl.quantity_returned) as units_returned FROM fact_return_line frl INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON frl.product_key = dp.product_key WHERE dp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND frl.return_date >= '2026-08-03' AND frl.return_date <= '2026-08-30'
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 runs 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30 per ref_fiscal_calendar
Garden Furniture is subcategory under the Garden category in dim_product
Returned units are recorded in fact_return_line.quantity_returned for items handed back and booked as returned
assumptions: This year refers to FY2026/27, the current fiscal year (request received 2026-10-05)
