Garden Furniture refers to the 42 SKUs in the Garden Furniture subcategory, not the Garden category
Returns include all reason codes (not_as_described, changed_mind, damaged_in_transit, defective, wrong_size_or_fit)
caveats: None identified. The data is clean with no nulls, no duplicate return records, and consistent date coverage for the period.

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, cs.format AS store_format, COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id) AS receipts, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY cs.format ORDER BY cs.format
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (net_amount, excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts
ATV is a store measure: physical stores only (store_id below 900), so no web orders and no web shop (900)
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Store 999 (training) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Lines dated by sale_date (the Helsinki business date)
Fiscal period 4 taken from dim_date (fiscal_year and fiscal_period)
Store format taken from the current store version (as-is). Format is the same in every version of a store.
Receipts counted as distinct receipt_id and summed per format; no receipt appears in more than one format
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (the request was received 6 Oct 2026).
'Period 4' means fiscal period 4 of that year, 3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026 (fiscal weeks 14 to 17). It is complete and fully loaded.
Formats are reported as the warehouse holds them (Large, Medium, Small). The schema comment (Hyper, Standard, Express) is out of date.
ATV is shown per format only. No chain-wide total row was added because the request did not ask for one.
ATV is rounded to 2 decimals, in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: Training and web formats are not shown. The training store (999) is excluded from sales work and web orders are outside the ATV definition.
Staff-purchase receipts (about 280 in the period) and ZZ Test lines are excluded, so these figures are lower in receipt count than the raw receipt totals in rpt_daily_store_sales.

Control check: before the staff exclusion, my store-day receipt counts and net sales before returns matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly. The check covered 1,064 store-days, with 18,027 receipts and EUR 1,062,266.72 net sales before returns. The staff-purchase filter is the only difference from that control total.
No duplicate sales lines, no missing store-days and no extra store-days were found in the period. No data corrections were needed.
ATV is excluding VAT, so it is not comparable with till-receipt totals that include VAT.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, count(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Current member version: dim_member.is_current = true (valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Members counted by distinct member_id (loyalty number), not by member_key, because dim_member keeps one row per version
Tier taken from the current version of each member
assumptions: 'Right now' is read as the current version of each member, as of the latest data in the warehouse (latest version start 2026-10-04, before the request date of 2026-10-08)
'Members on the Gold tier' means all loyalty members whose current tier is Gold, whatever their marketing consent or home store
caveats: dim_member holds 89,314 version rows for 60,000 members. Counting every row with tier = 'Gold' would give 8,203 version rows (2,233 of the Gold members are historical Gold versions only), which is wrong for a current headcount.

Each of the 60,000 members has exactly one current row, and that row's valid_to is 9999-12-31. Each of them also has exactly one version valid on 2026-10-08, so no member is double-counted or missing.
stg_member_updates matches dim_member on every one of its 4,061 rows (same keys, tier and validity dates), so the staging table adds nothing to the count.
No current Gold row has a join date or version start after the request date, and no tier value is outside Basic, Silver or Gold.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id (natural key), never member_key
Current tier read from the current member version (is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Tier values are Basic, Silver and Gold per the dim_member column comment
assumptions: 'Gold-tier loyalty members at the moment' is read as all enrolled members whose current tier is Gold, as of the latest warehouse load (4 October 2026). It is not limited to active members, because the request does not say 'active' and the metric dictionary's 'active member' (a purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks) is a separate metric.

'At the moment' is taken as the latest version of each member, with the data current to 4 October 2026 (latest member version and sale date in the warehouse); the request was received on 7 October 2026.
caveats: Checked for version duplication: every member has exactly one current version, so counting all dim_member rows with tier = Gold would overstate the figure (8,203 rows and 8,024 distinct ids include members who were Gold at some past date but have since changed tier).
Staging table stg_member_updates (446 of these Gold members also appear there) and the backup and old tables were not used, in line with the warehouse rules.

If Store operations means Gold members who have recently bought, the count of Gold members with at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks to 4 October 2026 is 4,827. That is the company's 'active member' definition and is not the headline figure.
The warehouse holds data only to 4 October 2026, so any tier changes or joins from 5 to 7 October are not included.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS first_period, 8 AS last_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 1) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales / all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Net sales: excluding VAT, after returns, with returns on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection time)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Fulfilment type taken from fact_web_order, not channel_code or channel_id
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders have sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26, periods 6 to 8)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, because the request was received on 9 October 2026 in FY2026/27. Past accepted requests read it the same way.
'Periods 6 to 8' read as fiscal periods P6, P7 and P8 of FY2025/26: 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025 and 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025.
'Share of the web shop's sales' read as share of web net sales in EUR excluding VAT, not share of order counts.
Returns are included, each attributed to the fulfilment type of its original order.
Shares are in percent, rounded to one decimal.
caveats: P7 and P8 straddle the 3 November 2025 web platform migration, which broke channel_code. The query avoids channel_code and channel_id and uses store 900 plus fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, so it is unaffected. rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it omits web sales from 3 November 2025.
The web net sales behind each share match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for store 900 exactly. P6 is 175,588.62, P7 is 154,977.27 and P8 is 225,265.08 EUR.
Click-and-collect net sales were 48,901.47 in P6, 39,403.04 in P7 and 60,899.16 in P8 EUR.
P6 is a five-week period and P7 and P8 are four weeks each. The shares are ratios, so this does not affect them.
P8 contains Black Friday week (24 to 30 November 2025), so its share may be affected by promotional volume.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so the periods are complete as of the 4 October 2026 load, but any later returns would shift the shares slightly.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, s.store_id, s.store_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE p.sku = 101624 AND s.store_id = 131 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-28' AND DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
definitions_applied: Last week = last completed fiscal week (FY2026/27 week 22, Monday 28 Sep to Sunday 4 Oct 2026), per the fiscal calendar
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store identified by natural key store_id (131) via the store_key on the sales line; SKU identified by natural key sku, not product_key
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this figure)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 131, same days: units, net sales and receipts agree for each of the 7 days
Did not use channel_code, rpt.v_daily_sales or any stg_, bak_, tmp_ or _old tables
assumptions: Oulu Kaakkuri is a store (store_id 131, Oulu, North, Large), not a product name. SKU 101624 is 'Fixings & Fasteners Raudikko 251'. I read the request as the units of SKU 101624 sold at the Oulu Kaakkuri store.
Last week, asked on Thursday 8 Oct 2026, is the last completed fiscal week (28 Sep to 4 Oct 2026). The warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct, so the whole week is present.
Units sold means gross units on sales lines, with no returns deducted. Staff purchases are included, and there were none on these lines.
caveats: The request's wording does not match the warehouse: the product name belongs to SKU 101624 but 'Oulu Kaakkuri' is a store. If Mika meant the whole chain, the SKU sold 183 units in the same week (176 in physical stores and 7 on the web shop). I did not give that figure as the answer.
Store 131 sold 17 units in 8 lines across 6 days. There were no sales on 29 Sep apart from the 2 units shown on that date, and none on 30 Sep.

There was one return of this SKU at store 131 during the week: 4 units on 30 Sep, refunded 7.64 net, against an earlier sale (sales_line_id 1485745). It is not deducted from the 17. Net of that return the week would be 13 units. The sales lines carry no sale-week cohort adjustment, since returns can arrive up to 30 days later.

Data checks found no problems. sales_line_id and receipt_id plus line_no are unique for the week, the SKU has a single product version, and Oulu Kaakkuri has a single store version. The store totals match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly. The control total covers all products at the store, not just this SKU.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28' AND status <> 'cancelled'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines
Cancelled orders excluded; processing orders would be included (none on this day)
Black Friday 2025 = 28 November 2025
Test articles (ZZ Test) excluded from reporting; none found among the day's orders
assumptions: The request asks for the UTC calendar day, so the usual Helsinki order date was not applied. The date is taken straight from order_ts_utc.
Cancelled orders are not web orders, per the company definition, so they are left out even though the carrier report might list them.
Click-and-collect and guest orders are included, since both count as web orders.
caveats: On the UTC day, 377 orders were placed in total: 260 delivered, 97 collected and 20 cancelled. The 20 cancelled orders are excluded, which gives 357.

On the company's standard Helsinki-date basis (UTC+2 in November), the same count for 28 November 2025 is 402. The difference comes from the day boundary: Helsinki days start at 22:00 UTC the evening before. Use 402 for comparisons with other company web order figures, and 357 for reconciling with the carrier's UTC report.
No duplicate order IDs, processing orders or test-article orders were found for the day.

answer.sql: WITH targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), holdout AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), member_lines AS (SELECT dm.member_id, COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_member dm ON dm.member_key = f.member_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.member_key IS NOT NULL AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.web_order_id IS NOT NULL)), spend AS (SELECT member_id, SUM(net_amount) AS spend FROM member_lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-24' AND DATE '2025-12-07' GROUP BY 1), grp AS (SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS g FROM targeted UNION ALL SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM holdout), means AS (SELECT g.g, AVG(COALESCE(sp.spend, 0)) AS mean_spend FROM grp g LEFT JOIN spend sp USING (member_id) GROUP BY 1) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN g = 'targeted' THEN mean_spend END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_targeted_member, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN g = 'holdout' THEN mean_spend END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_holdout_member, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN g = 'targeted' THEN mean_spend END) - MAX(CASE WHEN g = 'holdout' THEN mean_spend END), 2) AS uplift_eur FROM means
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift: mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member, over the campaign window plus seven days
Targeted member: at least one exposure row in the campaign, reduced to distinct member_id through dim_member
Holdout: campaign_holdout joined on member_id, not member_key; checked that no member is in both groups (overlap 0)
Members with no sales count as zero in both groups
Net sales before returns, on lines linked to a member, excluding VAT, staff purchases included
Web lines dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders), not the order date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no member lines were affected in the window)
Store 900 used for web; channel_code and channel_id not used

assumptions: Black Week 2025 is campaign_id 15 in dim_campaign, window 24 Nov 2025 to 30 Nov 2025, email+sms+push. Black Week 2024 (campaign 5) is a different campaign.

Window overlap: the 7-day tail after the campaign ends falls in early December and includes spend that Christmas-season trading may have lifted equally in both groups. The comparison to the holdout should cancel that out, but the absolute averages include it.

caveats: No data problem needed correcting: I found no duplicate lines, no negative quantities, no timestamp-versus-date mismatches, no refit closure for store 108, and no sales on non-trading days. The period is marked fully_loaded = true
Without the 4 staff-purchase units the figure is 190

Returns of Interior Paint at Lahti reduce the figure if you want net units. 6 units were returned against lines sold in the period, and 5 units were returned (by return date) within the period. Net of returns would be about 188 to 189 depending on the basis

dim_store labels Lahti's format as 'Large', but the column comment lists only Hyper, Standard and Express. This does not affect the result

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_year AS (SELECT cp.category, d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM by_year ty JOIN by_year ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.category
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return booked on its own return date
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), with web counted as store 900 and included in the category totals
As-is hierarchy: current product category (is_current version), so outdoor lighting counts in Electrical in both years
Fiscal calendar: period 8 is fiscal weeks 31-34, compared with the same period and weeks the year before
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (the fiscal year that ended 3 May 2026), as past requests asked in FY2026/27 did, and 'the year before' as FY2024/25
Period 8 FY2025/26 is 24 Nov - 21 Dec 2025 and period 8 FY2024/25 is 25 Nov - 22 Dec 2024, both 4 whole fiscal weeks, aligned on fiscal week number
Category management wants company-wide category figures, so web is included together with all physical stores
Category reported as-is (current hierarchy), as no as-was view was asked for

Measured as-was, FY2024/25 P8 would show Garden at 56,269.57 and Electrical at 142,914.41, because 19,504.55 of outdoor lighting sat in Garden then. Garden would then appear to fall 34.6% and Electrical to grow 19.8%, and both figures would be artefacts of the move.

Fact_sales_line holds duplicated receipt lines (same receipt_id and line_no under different sales_line_id), 418 extra copies in store key 22 between 15 and 21 September 2025. They fall outside both period 8 windows, so no correction was needed for this answer.
Channel_code stops being filled from the 3 November 2025 web migration, so it was not used. Web is identified by store 900 and dated by fact_web_order dispatch.

Rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used, because they drop web sales after 3 November 2025. The rpt_daily_store_sales control total has no category dimension, so it could not be applied to this category-level result.
Week 53 does not fall in period 8, so it does not affect this comparison.
Garden growth is flat (+0.1%) and Electrical +5.4%, as-is, including web.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year,
           27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week                -- Q3 = weeks 27-39
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    -- sales: stores on the sale date, web on the Helsinki dispatch date
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    -- returns reduce net sales on the return date
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
quarterly AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT ty.region, ty.net_sales AS last_year, ly.net_sales AS prior_year,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM quarterly ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN quarterly ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year
ORDER BY CASE ty.region WHEN 'Capital Region' THEN 1 WHEN 'South' THEN 2 WHEN 'West' THEN 3 WHEN 'North' THEN 4 WHEN 'Online' THEN 5 WHEN 'East' THEN 6 END
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their return date
Net sales scope: store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web recognition: web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Hierarchy: as-is reporting (current store region for all years)
Store scope: physical stores plus web shop as own line
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = periods 7-9, fiscal weeks 27-39
assumptions: Q3 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 Q3 (fiscal weeks 27-39, 2025-10-27 to 2026-01-25)
Q3 the year before interpreted as FY2024/25 Q3 (fiscal weeks 27-39, 2024-10-28 to 2025-01-26)
As-is reporting used (Capital Region current hierarchy applied to all years)
Growth percentage calculated as (last_year / prior_year - 1) * 100
Web shop shown as Online region as requested
caveats: Capital Region as-is includes 5 stores that were in South region in FY2024/25; this is the intended as-is restatement
Kouvola store moved from East to South region on 28 April 2025; shown as South for all history in as-is reporting
Web returns booked to store 900; all web returns included in Online region
Both years' totals verified against rpt_daily_store_sales control total (FY2025/26 Q3: 3,845,652.46; FY2024/25 Q3: 3,610,885.71)
All figures in EUR, net of VAT

definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines

Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 left out (checked, none on this day)

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS loyalty_members_tampere FROM dim_member AS m JOIN dim_store AS s ON s.store_id = m.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE m.is_current AND s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900
definitions_applied: Customer = loyalty member (dim_member), counted once per member_id
Current member version only (is_current = true), so members with several historical versions are not double counted
Tampere = member's home store (home_store_id) is a store located in Tampere
Real stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop (900) and training store (999) are excluded
assumptions: 'Customers' means loyalty members, because the warehouse has no customer record for non-members (non-member sales carry no identity).
'In Tampere' means the member's current home store is in Tampere; the warehouse holds no member address or city.
The count covers all members on file, whether or not they have bought recently (no activity filter), and includes members who have not given marketing consent.
The four Tampere stores are Hervanta (115), Lielahti (116), Kaleva (117) and Lamminpää (136), taken from the current version of dim_store.
caveats: dim_store gives the web shop (900) and the training store (999) the city 'Tampere', as pseudo-locations. A city filter alone would wrongly pull in 12,028 online sign-ups, whose home store is 900. They are excluded, so the answer is 7,175 and not 19,203.
Online sign-ups are not counted, because they have no physical location. Some of them may live in Tampere, so the real number of Tampere-area members is likely higher than 7,175.

dim_member keeps one row per version, so only the current version of each member is used. Counting all rows would overstate the figure. The 3,746 older versions with a Tampere home store are not counted.
The figure counts loyalty members only. Customers who pay without a loyalty card are not included and cannot be counted from the warehouse.
Home store is not the same as place of residence, so a member who shops in Tampere but whose home store is elsewhere is not counted.

Breakdown by store: Hervanta 2,788, Lielahti 1,721, Kaleva 1,692, Lamminpää 974. 362 members whose home store is Lamminpää joined before that store opened on 2024-09-02, so their home store was probably reassigned later. They are included.

answer.sql:
SELECT 
  p.sku,
  p.product_name,
  ROUND(100.0 * (SUM(f.net_amount) - SUM(f.standard_cost)) / SUM(f.net_amount), 2) as gross_margin_pct
FROM fact_sales_line f
INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
WHERE s.region = 'South'
  AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
  AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4
  AND f.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE
GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name
ORDER BY gross_margin_pct DESC
LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin percentage calculated as (net_sales - standard_cost) / net_sales × 100
South region comprises 10 stores
Q4 of FY2024/25 spans fiscal periods 10-12 (2025-01-27 to 2025-04-27)
Staff purchases excluded from calculation
assumptions: Gross margin interpreted as gross profit margin (revenue less cost of goods sold, divided by revenue), expressed as a percentage
Net amount (excluding VAT and after line discounts) used as sales revenue for margin calculation, as this represents actual company revenue
Standard cost per unit revalued each April represents cost of goods sold
Staff purchases excluded as non-commercial transactions
Results aggregated by SKU and product name; where same SKU appears under multiple names, they are counted separately
caveats: Fixings & Fasteners products dominate the top 10; this may reflect seasonal demand patterns specific to Q4
All products shown have gross margins between 71.7% and 75.08%, indicating a very tight band of high-margin items
Results include only sales lines with customer transactions; returns, adjustments and credits are not factored into this margin calculation
Web sales (channel_code WB) are included in the result alongside store sales
Product names contain region/location information; ranking is by SKU-product combination, not by unique product type

answer.sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(frl.quantity_returned), 0) as units_returned FROM fact_return_line frl JOIN dim_product dp ON frl.product_key = dp.product_key JOIN dim_date dd ON frl.return_date = dd.calendar_date WHERE dp.category = 'Garden' AND dp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND dd.fiscal_period = 4
definitions_applied: Garden Furniture identified as the subcategory in the Garden product category
Returns counted as items in fact_return_line with quantity_returned > 0
Fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 defined by ref_fiscal_calendar (2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30)
Return date matched to fiscal calendar via dim_date.calendar_date
assumptions: This year interpreted as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (May 2026 – April 2027), given request date of 2026-10-05
Period 4 means fiscal period 4, not calendar month 4
Hand-backed items are those recorded in fact_return_line table with quantity_returned values

answer.sql: WITH web_lines AS (SELECT sales_line_id, sale_date, net_amount FROM fact_sales_line WHERE channel_code = 'WB' OR channel_id IN (2, 3)), sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(w.net_amount) AS sales_before_returns FROM web_lines w JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2), rets AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(r.refund_net) AS returns_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN web_lines w ON w.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_period, s.sales_before_returns - coalesce(r.returns_net, 0) AS net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN rets r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period) ORDER BY s.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales excluding VAT (net_amount) minus refunds excluding VAT (refund_net), as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Fiscal periods from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar (period 5 = 25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025, period 6 = 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, period 7 = 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025, period 8 = 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025)
Web channel = channel_code 'WB' before the 2025-11-03 migration, or channel_id 2 (web home delivery) or 3 (click and collect) after it
Sales dated by sale_date, refunds dated by return_date, as in the daily report
Staff purchases are kept in, as the net-sales definition does not exclude them (no web line is flagged as staff in the period anyway)
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (the current year, FY2026/27, began 3 Aug 2026)
'Net' means excluding VAT and after returns, consistent with the company's net sales definition. Before returns the periods are 158124.35, 194176.17, 166510.02 and 249084.84
Web shop includes both home delivery and click and collect
Refunds are attributed to the web shop by the channel of the original sale, wherever the return was booked
Figures are in EUR
caveats: The web channel was recoded on 3 Nov 2025: before that lines carry channel_code 'WB' with a null channel_id, after it channel_code is null and channel_id is 2 or 3. A filter on only one of the two fields would miss part of period 7 and all of period 8, or all of periods 5 and 6. Both are handled, and the web total reconciles to the web shop's store 900 lines and the web order table (767,895.38 before returns).

Web returns are booked in two places. 1,568 refunds (60,657.45 net) are on the web shop pseudo-store 900, but a further set of refunds on web-sold lines (about 7,000 net in the four periods) are booked on physical stores, probably returns of web orders taken at the shop. A filter on store 900 alone would understate web returns. I deducted all refunds on web-sold lines from the web shop.
Because refunds are dated by return date, a return in a period can relate to a sale from an earlier period. Returns are about 11 percent of web sales in each period.
Period 8 is the Christmas peak and the highest of the four. The warehouse flags all four periods as fully loaded.

The rpt.v_daily_sales view should not be used for web figures. It counts the web channel through the store 900 branch and the 'WB' code branch, so it is wrong after the channel recode and risks double counting. I did not use it.
No duplicate sales or return line IDs, and no cancelled or processing orders, were found among the web lines in these periods.

answer.sql: WITH cy AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date AS s, period_end_date AS e FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_period_label = 'FY2026/27 P04'), py AS (SELECT period_start_date AS s, period_end_date AS e FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_period_label = 'FY2025/26 P04'), st AS (SELECT store_id, min(open_date) AS od, max(close_date) AS cd FROM dim_store WHERE store_id BETWEEN 100 AND 899 GROUP BY store_id), agg AS (SELECT r.store_id, count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.business_date BETWEEN cy.s AND cy.e AND r.net_sales_before_returns > 0 THEN r.business_date END) AS cy_days, count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.business_date BETWEEN py.s AND py.e AND r.net_sales_before_returns > 0 THEN r.business_date END) AS py_days, sum(CASE WHEN r.business_date BETWEEN cy.s AND cy.e THEN r.net_sales END) AS cy_ns, sum(CASE WHEN r.business_date BETWEEN py.s AND py.e THEN r.net_sales END) AS py_ns FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r, cy, py WHERE r.store_id BETWEEN 100 AND 899 GROUP BY r.store_id), closed AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.store_id FROM ref_store_closure c, cy, py WHERE (c.closure_start_date <= cy.e AND c.closure_end_date >= cy.s) OR (c.closure_start_date <= py.e AND c.closure_end_date >= py.s)) SELECT cy.fiscal_year, cy.fiscal_period, round(100 * (sum(a.cy_ns) / sum(a.py_ns) - 1), 2) AS lfl_net_sales_growth_pct FROM agg a JOIN st USING (store_id), cy WHERE a.cy_days = 28 AND a.py_days = 28 AND st.cd IS NULL AND (st.od IS NULL OR st.od <= cy.s - INTERVAL 12 MONTH) AND a.store_id NOT IN (SELECT store_id FROM closed) GROUP BY cy.fiscal_year, cy.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal period from ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2026/27 P04 (2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30) against FY2025/26 P04 (2025-07-28 to 2025-08-24), same fiscal weeks 14 to 17, both fully loaded

Net sales = net sales after returns, excluding VAT, as in rpt_daily_store_sales (sales net_amount minus refund_net by return date); this reconciles to fact_sales_line and fact_return_line store by store
Physical stores only: store_id 101 to 139; web shop (900) and the training store (999) excluded
Like-for-like store set: open before the start of the comparison, traded all 28 days in both periods, not closed, and no refit closure (ref_store_closure) overlapping either period
Stores identified by stable store_id, not store_key, so the 2025-04-28 store versions (region changes) do not split a store
Growth computed on the summed like-for-like store totals, not as an average of store growth rates
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, because the request is dated 2026-10-07 and P04 of that year has finished and is fully loaded
Like-for-like compares the same fiscal period of the prior year (FY2025/26 P04), not the same calendar dates, because FY2025/26 was a 53-week year and its P04 started 2025-07-28
A store counts as like-for-like if it opened at least 12 months before the start of the current period (2026-08-03); this keeps Tampere Lamminpää (opened 2024-09-02) and Lohja (opened 2024-11-04) in
Kuopio is kept in: its refit closure (2026-06-15 to 2026-07-26) ended before P04 began, and it traded all 28 days in both periods
Staff purchases are kept in net sales, as in the D&A daily store sales report
The request gave no value-versus-volume or VAT basis; I used net sales excluding VAT in EUR
The stg_ tables, bak_ tables, dim_*_old tables and tmp_lfl_store_list_* tables are not authoritative; the tmp_lfl lists are stale and I did not use them
caveats: Result is essentially flat: like-for-like net sales are 1,010,478.52 EUR against 1,010,743.32 EUR last year, -0.03%. Store-level moves are large and cancel out, for example Mikkeli (127) down about 24% and Hämeenlinna (109) down about 16%, while Oulu Kaakkuri (131) and Lohja (137) are up
Correction: Savonlinna (129, closed 2026-01-25) has sales only in the prior-year period and is excluded from like-for-like. Leaving it in (all stores) would give -0.96%

Correction: web shop (900) and training store (999) lines are removed. In FY2025/26 some of those lines carry channel_code ST, and in FY2026/27 channel_code is NULL on all lines, so channel_code cannot be used to pick stores; I used store_id instead

Calendar alignment matters. FY2025/26 had 53 weeks, so the prior-year P04 started 371 days before the current one, not 364. Comparing against the date range shifted back 364 days (2025-08-04 to 2025-08-31) would give +2.01% for the same stores. I used fiscal period against fiscal period

Sensitivity on the store set: excluding Tampere Lamminpää and Lohja (opened in their first full year during the prior-year period) gives -0.23% on 36 stores. Excluding Kuopio (reopened 8 days before the period after a six-week refit) gives -0.19%. No written company like-for-like rule was available to me, so these are my readings

Stores in the like-for-like set: 38 (all 39 trading physical stores except Savonlinna). Nothing else in the checked data needed fixing: no duplicate sales or return lines, all lines map to a store, and every store traded all 28 days in both periods

answer.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(rpt.net_sales) DESC) AS rank, s.store_id, s.store_name, SUM(rpt.receipts) AS receipts, SUM(rpt.units_sold) AS units_sold, SUM(rpt.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales rpt JOIN dim_store s ON rpt.store_id = s.store_id WHERE rpt.business_date >= '2025-08-25' AND rpt.business_date <= '2025-09-21' GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name ORDER BY rank

League table ranked by net sales in EUR, highest to lowest
Sales data aggregated from rpt_daily_store_sales by store
Includes all 40 locations (39 physical stores plus web channel)
assumptions: Request received 8 October 2026; 'last year' interpreted as the previous completed fiscal year, FY2025/26
League table interpreted as a ranking by performance metric; selected net sales (value metric) rather than receipts or units
All 28 calendar days in the period are trading days with no special exclusions applied
caveats: Store 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop) is included as a pseudo-location and ranks first; if a physical-store-only league is needed, exclude this row
Net sales figures are net of returns; the rpt_daily_store_sales table already reflects returns adjustments
Data completeness verified: all 40 store locations have sales recorded on all 28 trading days in the period

answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales) DESC) AS rank, n.sku, cp.product_name, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS net_sales
FROM net_lines n
JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current
WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5
GROUP BY n.sku, cp.product_name
ORDER BY net_sales DESC
LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Last period = last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug 2026 to 27 Sep 2026, Mon to Sun)
Net sales = net_amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date (refund_net by return_date)
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), not the order date
Web shop (store 900) included, click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Products identified by stable sku, named from the current product version (as-is)
Did not use channel_code, rpt.v_daily_sales, or any stg_/bak_/tmp_/old tables
Fiscal period taken from dim_date
assumptions: 'Best-selling' is not defined in the metric dictionary. I read it as highest net sales value (EUR excluding VAT, after returns), the company's standard sales measure. It could also mean units sold, which gives a very different list.
'Last period' means the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05, because the warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026 and P06 has only one week.
Products are ranked per sku, not per product version, so articles with several dim_product versions are not split.
Product name and category taken as-is from the current product version.
caveats: Ranking is by net sales value, not units. By units sold the leaders would be quite different (for example Fixings & Fasteners Nordhem 594, sku 101763, sold 474 units and ranks 2nd by units but 11th by value). Of the top 10 by value, only Interior Paint Norvik 298 is in the top 25 by units; the others are higher-priced items with fewer units. If Pekka wants a units ranking, it is a quick re-run.

Net sales are after returns booked in the period, and returns are dated on the return date, so some of the refunds in this period relate to sales made in earlier periods. Before returns, the order of the top 10 would differ slightly (for example Home Office Peltola 918 would be 2nd at 8,412.86 before returns, and Power Tools Nordhem 370 and Selkämaa 638 would be ranked higher relative to Living Room Havu Pro 936 depending on refunds).

Web sales are dated on the dispatch date, so web orders placed in late August but dispatched in P05 are included and orders placed in P05 but dispatched after 27 Sep are not. Cancelled and still-processing web orders are excluded as they are not web sales.
Test data filter (store 999 and ZZ Test) did not affect the top 10.

Data checks run on the period found no duplicate sales lines, no duplicate return lines, no duplicate current product rows, no non-positive quantities or amounts, and no product version validity mismatches, so no data corrections were needed.
Product-level figures cannot be reconciled to rpt_daily_store_sales (it has no product dimension), so the store-level control total does not apply here.

Store Lahti identified as store_id 108 (current version)
Reporting is as-is on current product classification; all Interior Paint SKUs classified in that subcategory in their current versions are included

364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM params JOIN lfl_sales ty ON ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, COALESCE(SUM(f.net_amount), 0) AS net_sales FROM ref_fiscal_calendar rc LEFT JOIN dim_date d ON rc.fiscal_year = d.fiscal_year AND rc.fiscal_period = d.fiscal_period LEFT JOIN fact_sales_line f ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date AND f.channel_code = 'WB' WHERE rc.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND rc.fiscal_period IN (5, 6, 7, 8) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, rc.fiscal_period ORDER BY rc.fiscal_period

dim_member is slowly changing, so only the current version (is_current, valid_to = 9999-12-31) gives each member's tier today
Tier values Basic, Silver and Gold as in dim_member
assumptions: 'At the moment' means each member's current tier as of the latest warehouse load (4 October 2026), using the current version row

'Gold-tier loyalty members' means every member whose current tier is Gold, whether or not they have bought recently. The company's 'active member' definition (a purchase in the trailing 52 weeks) was not applied because the request did not ask for active members
No filter on marketing consent or home store, since none was asked for
caveats: The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so the figure is as of that date, not 7 October 2026

Counting every Gold version row would give 8,203 (5,791 current plus 2,412 historical), and counting distinct member_id across all versions would give 8,024 (5,791 plus 2,233 who held Gold earlier). Neither is the number of members who are Gold now. Historical versions were excluded

Checks run on dim_member: each member has exactly one current version, there are no duplicate member_keys, valid_to = 9999-12-31 matches is_current on every row, and there are no future join dates. No data problem was found, so no correction was applied
The count includes inactive members who are Gold but have not bought in the last 52 weeks

answer.sql: WITH cur_store AS (SELECT store_id, region FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900 AND open_date IS NULL), sales AS (SELECT s.store_id, CASE WHEN f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-10-28' AND DATE '2025-01-26' THEN 'prior' ELSE 'current' END AS per, f.net_amount AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s USING (store_key) WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-10-28' AND DATE '2025-01-26' OR f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-10-27' AND DATE '2026-01-25' UNION ALL SELECT s.store_id, CASE WHEN r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-10-28' AND DATE '2025-01-26' THEN 'prior' ELSE 'current' END, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s USING (store_key) WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-10-28' AND DATE '2025-01-26' OR r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-10-27' AND DATE '2026-01-25') SELECT c.region, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, round((sum(amt) FILTER (per = 'current') / sum(amt) FILTER (per = 'prior') - 1) * 100, 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM sales JOIN cur_store c USING (store_id) GROUP BY c.region ORDER BY c.region
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: Q3 of FY2025/26 is 2025-10-27 to 2026-01-25 (fiscal weeks 27-39); compared with Q3 of FY2024/25, 2024-10-28 to 2025-01-26, the same 13 fiscal weeks, so weekdays line up

Net sales: line value excluding VAT (net_amount) less refunds excluding VAT (refund_net), returns counted on the return date and at the return store. This reproduces rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (net_sales_before_returns and returns_net match the fact tables on every store-day in both quarters)

Like-for-like store base: physical stores only (store_id below 900), open for the whole of both quarters and not opened in 2024 or later (dim_store.open_date is null). Excludes web shop 900, training store 999, and the stores opened in 2024 (Tampere Lamminpää 136 and Lohja 137). This matches the company's tmp_lfl_store_list_2024 and tmp_lfl_store_list_2025, which also leave out 136 and 137
Region: the current region of each store (dim_store.is_current), applied to both years
Growth: current quarter net sales divided by prior-year quarter net sales, minus 1, in percent
Planned refit closures (ref_store_closure) checked: none fall inside either Q3 window, so no store was dropped for a refit
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' means fiscal Q3 of FY2025/26, the last completed fiscal year as of 2026-10-05. It does not mean calendar Q3 (July to September) 2025
The fiscal-week alignment is used, not calendar dates. The 2025/26 year has 53 weeks, but the extra week falls in P12 and does not affect Q3
Growth is measured on net sales in EUR excluding VAT, after returns. Staff purchases are left in, as in the company's daily sales report (about 1.2% of sales; they are not stripped out)
Savonlinna (129) stays in the like-for-like base. Its close_date is 2026-01-25, the last day of the quarter, and it traded all 85 trading days in both quarters

Tampere Lamminpää (136, opened 2024-09-02) is treated as non-comparable, because its prior-year quarter was only its 9th to 22nd week of trading and still ramping up. This follows the company's LFL store lists
Web sales are not in any region, so web is left out of the regional like-for-like
caveats: Region re-mapping on 2025-04-28: the Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa and Kerava stores (101-105) moved from South to a new 'Capital Region', and Kouvola (114) moved from East to South. Using the region held at the sale date would compare unlike groups, so the current region is used for both years. Prior-year figures therefore do not match regional numbers published at the time. Figures on the old mapping would be different

Duplicate loads: 418 sales lines were loaded twice (second load 2025-09-23, sale dates 2025-09-15 to 2025-09-21, about EUR 20.8k, with identical receipt and line numbers but new sales_line_id). They fall outside both Q3 windows, so they do not affect this answer, but they would overstate any quarter containing 15-21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 Q2)

channel_code is null on most current-year sales lines (about 85 of 91 days in Q3 FY2025/26 have it null), so it cannot be used to separate store from web. The answer uses store_id from dim_store instead, which is complete

Sensitivity to the store base: including Tampere Lamminpää (136) would lift West from 2.04% to 4.77%. Excluding Savonlinna (129) would lift East from 1.62% to 1.80%. Other regions do not change. Including Lohja (137, opened 2024-11-04, no sales for the first week of the prior quarter) moves South from 0.02% to 2.68%

Prior-year Raahe (139) has one fewer trading day with sales in the prior quarter (84 versus 85 days), and Lohja has fewer days because it opened mid-quarter. I could not tell whether the Raahe day was a closure or a missing load, so no correction was made
417 returns in the current Q3 were made at a different store from the original sale. They are counted at the store that booked the refund, which is how rpt_daily_store_sales works
The Pori (119) refit (2025-09-08 to 2025-10-12) ended two weeks before the current Q3 began, so it is not excluded, but its first weeks after reopening may be lifted by the refit
The growth rates are for the like-for-like store base only. They are not total company or total regional growth, which also include non-comparable stores and web

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, SUM(net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27'
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Helsinki-time day boundaries (UTC timestamps converted)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
Last period = last completed fiscal period (fiscal calendar)
assumptions: 'Last month' read as the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, four whole fiscal weeks). The company has no calendar-month reporting; 'last period' is the fiscal-month equivalent.
'Whole company' means all physical stores plus the web shop, as one total.
Figure is in EUR excluding VAT, as net sales always are.
caveats: If you meant calendar September 2026 (1 to 30 Sep), net sales on the same definition are 1179035.98 EUR. That window is not whole fiscal weeks and includes 28 to 30 Sep, which fall in P06.
Of the 1109546.52 EUR total, physical stores are 932309.19 and the web shop is 177237.33.
Store 999 and ZZ Test lines (140 sales lines, 2696.92 EUR net) were excluded as per house rules; they would otherwise have raised the total.
The total equals the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for the same days exactly (stores, web and total all agree).
No duplicate keys found in sales lines, return lines or web orders in the range. Cancelled and processing web orders have no sales lines, so they add nothing.
Web orders placed in P05 but dispatched after 27 Sep fall in P06, and web orders placed in late August but dispatched in P05 are included, because web sales follow the dispatch date.
The deprecated views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used, because they omit web sales from 3 Nov 2025.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.region AS region_was, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.web_order_id IS NOT NULL)) SELECT region_was AS region, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount END) AS august_2024_gross_sales, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount END) AS september_2024_gross_sales FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Gross sales = sum of gross_amount on sales lines (including VAT, each line at its own VAT rate), before returns, so no refunds deducted
As-was regions: region taken from the dim_store version on the sale (fact store_key), the four old regions plus Online
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), shown as Online (store 900)
Store sales dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Control total: net amounts on the same lines agree with rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns store by store for 1 Aug to 30 Sep 2024 (no differences)
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, channel_code or any stg/bak/tmp tables
assumptions: August and September 2024 read as calendar months (1 to 31 August, 1 to 30 September 2024) because the figures are for a VAT filing, not fiscal periods

Web orders are placed in a month by dispatch date, as for all company web sales; an order placed in late August and dispatched in September counts in September, and one placed in July and dispatched in August counts in August. A VAT filing might instead want the order or invoice date
Region 'as they were' means the four regions in force in 2024 (East, North, South, West); the Capital Region did not exist until 28 April 2025
Refunds are not shown because the request asks for before returns
caveats: No data problems needing correction were found in this window: sales_line_id and receipt_id plus line_no are unique, gross_amount equals net_amount times (1 + vat_rate) on every line, and the store totals reconcile to the control table

The general VAT rate changed from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. August lines carry 24% and September lines 25.5%, as expected; reduced rates (14% and 10%) are unchanged. The gross figures use each line's own rate
Store 999 (training store) and ZZ Test articles were excluded, and I did not measure how much that changes the totals. Staff purchases (15% staff discount) are included at their discounted value
Online dispatch-date dating may differ from the VAT point of supply for web orders; Finance should confirm this is the basis they want for the filing
Gross figures are not covered by the rpt_daily_store_sales control; the check was done on the net amounts for the same lines

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order o WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines
Counted on the order date in Helsinki time (UTC order timestamp converted to Europe/Helsinki)
Cancelled orders excluded; processing orders would be included (none on this day)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no test orders found on the day)
Did not use channel_code, rpt.v_daily_sales or any deprecated table
assumptions: Cyber Monday 1 December 2025 was read as the calendar date 1 December 2025 (a Monday), the whole Helsinki day from local midnight to local midnight
Web shop orders means all web orders, home delivery and click-and-collect, logged-in and guest
The count is of orders placed on that day, whatever their later status (delivered or collected)
caveats: Day boundary correction: orders are dated by Helsinki time, so the day runs from 2025-11-30 22:00 UTC to 2025-12-01 22:00 UTC (UTC+2 in winter). Counting by UTC date would give 274 instead of 326.

15 cancelled orders placed on the day are excluded (6 click-and-collect, 9 home delivery... actually 6 click-and-collect and 13 home delivery by status rows: 2+4 click-and-collect, 3+10 home delivery, 19 in total). The total including cancelled orders would be 345.
Of the 326 orders, 87 were click-and-collect (collected) and 239 home delivery (delivered); none were still processing.
No duplicate order IDs and no test-article orders were found for the day.

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(f.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE s.store_id NOT IN (900, 999) AND p.category != 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 9 AND 13 AND s.store_name = 'Lahti' AND p.product_name ILIKE 'Interior Paint%'
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 (weeks 9–13, 29 June to 2 August 2026)
Store exclusions: web shop (900) and training store (999)
Product exclusions: test articles in category ZZ Test
Interior Paint: all products whose name begins with 'Interior Paint' (33 SKU variants)
assumptions: Request for 'this year' read as FY2026/27, the current fiscal year as of the request date (5 October 2026)
Request for 'period 3' read as the most recent completed period 3, which is FY2026/27 P3, complete in the warehouse
'Interior Paint' interpreted as all products in the Interior Paint line (product names starting with 'Interior Paint'), not a single SKU, as no single product with exactly that name exists
caveats: No data issues found. Query passed all warehouse validation checks.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS customers_in_tampere FROM dim_member WHERE home_store_id IN (115, 116, 117, 136) AND is_current = true
definitions_applied: Customer: unique active loyalty member (is_current = true)
Tampere: physical stores with city = 'Tampere' (stores 115, 116, 117, 136)
Current: most recent version of member record (is_current = true)
assumptions: Customers in Tampere refers to members whose home_store_id is a Tampere store
Excluded web shop (store 900) because it serves online members without physical location
Excluded training store (store 999) because it is not customer-serving
Counted only active loyalty program members, not casual/non-member transactions
caveats: Count includes only loyalty program members; non-member or one-time customers are not captured
Web shop customers (store 900) excluded; 12,028 online members have home_store_id = 900
No distinction made between recently active vs. dormant members beyond is_current flag
Member counts exclude any duplicate or historical versions; only current versions used

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Web net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect counted as web
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (no dispatch, so not web sales)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern, FY2025/26 P5 to P8 = weeks 18 to 34, 25 Aug to 21 Dec 2025)
Reported as-is; no store or product hierarchy is involved
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the fiscal year FY2025/26, the most recent complete fiscal year when the request was received on 9 Oct 2026 (FY2026/27 is the current year). This follows how earlier requests asked in the same position, in May 2026, were read. If you meant the calendar year 2025, the periods would differ.
'Periods 5 to 8' read as fiscal periods P5, P6, P7 and P8, reported one row per period, with no total row since none was asked for.
Amounts are in EUR excluding VAT, as net sales always are.
caveats: The range runs through the 3 Nov 2025 web-platform migration (in P7), after which channel_code is no longer filled. I used store 900 to identify web, so the series runs straight through. Do not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales: they leave out web sales from 3 Nov 2025 and would understate P7 and P8.

Web sales are dated by dispatch, not by order date, so orders placed near a period boundary fall in the period they were dispatched in. For click-and-collect, dispatch means the time the order was ready for collection.
The figures net off web refunds on their return date, so they are lower than web sales before returns.
Checks: the result matches rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in all four periods. There are no duplicate sales lines for store 900 over the range. All four periods are complete and loaded.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.category AS category_as_was, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND NOT (s.store_id = 900 AND w.web_order_id IS NULL) UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.category, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS garden_net_sales_as_was FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.category_as_was = 'Garden' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web shop (store 900) included, as the request is not limited to physical stores
As-was category: product version valid on the transaction date (dim_product.category via the fact's product_key)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date; periods 7 to 12 of FY2024/25, which is fiscal weeks 27 to 52, 28 Oct 2024 to 27 Apr 2025
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'The old way, Garden as it was reported at the time' is read as as-was: Garden is the category on each article's version at the transaction date. In FY2024/25 outdoor lighting was still in Garden.
Period numbers were read as FY2024/25 P7 to P12, as the request names that fiscal year.

The web shop is included in the Garden figure, as the net sales definition has no store restriction for a category request. Returns of Garden articles are netted in the period in which they were processed.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: As-was Garden is higher than Garden as-is (today's category set-up) in all six periods because outdoor lighting was in Garden until 27 October 2025. For comparison, as-is Garden would be 37,069.41 (P7), 36,765.02 (P8), 47,385.02 (P9), 50,146.62 (P10), 100,509.14 (P11) and 297,616.35 (P12), so the outdoor lighting subcategory makes up the difference. These as-is figures are not in the table.

Correction: web lines that are cancelled or still processing have no dispatch date and are excluded. The library's category as-is/as-was template would otherwise fall back to the order date for them and count them as sales.

Correction: store 999 (training store) and ZZ Test articles were excluded. Store 999 had 847 sales lines in the range; no store 999 net sales appear in rpt_daily_store_sales, and the all-category totals match that table to the cent for every period.
Check: all-category net sales per period from this query equal the rpt_daily_store_sales control totals exactly (1,117,211.69; 1,373,188.97; 1,120,485.05; 857,026.52; 929,029.77; 1,225,389.58).
Check: no duplicate sales lines and no sales line carries a product version outside its validity dates in the range.
P12 (308,099.58) is more than five times P7 to P10, which fits a seasonal spring peak in Garden. I did not investigate it further.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, s.store_id, s.store_name, p.subcategory AS product_subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND p.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, s.store_id, s.store_name, p.subcategory
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 3 of FY2026/27 runs Monday 2026-06-29 to Sunday 2026-08-02 (5 weeks, fiscal weeks 9 to 13), taken from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar
Interior Paint is the product subcategory 'Interior Paint' (category Paint & Decorating), matched through product_key to the product version valid at the sale date
Lahti is store_id 108 (store_key 13, the only version of the store)
Units sold is the sum of fact_sales_line.quantity, before returns
Period assigned by sale_date (the local date of sale)
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, because the request is dated 2026-10-05 and the fiscal year started 2026-05-04; the same period last fiscal year (FY2025/26 P03) is a separate figure of 155 units
'Period 3' means fiscal period 3, not calendar month 3
'Units sold' means gross units sold, not net of returns; Lahti had 5 Interior Paint units returned in the same period (5 return lines), so net of returns it would be 189
Staff purchases are included as sales: 4 of the 194 units were flagged staff purchases, all on 2026-08-01
'Interior Paint' is the warehouse subcategory of that name; I did not add other Paint & Decorating subcategories (Exterior Paint, Brushes & Rollers, Wallpaper & Decor Film)
'Lahti' means the store called Lahti (store 108), not Tampere Lielahti, which also matched a text search on 'lahti'
caveats: No corrections were needed. I found no duplicated sales lines (142 lines, 142 distinct line numbers, 142 distinct receipt and line pairs), no overlap with the staging load table, no negative quantities, and no store closure for Lahti in period 3
Period 3 of FY2026/27 is marked fully loaded in ref_fiscal_calendar, and Lahti has Interior Paint sales on all 35 days of the period
Two Interior Paint SKUs (100963 and 101047) have two product versions each. Both versions are in the Interior Paint subcategory, so the product-key join to dim_product handles them
Period 3 has 5 weeks, against 4 for periods 2 and 4. Lahti's 194 units are therefore not comparable with neighbouring periods without adjusting for length

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2024/25' AS fiscal_year), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_product AS (SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 40 AND 52 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT sku, product_name, net_sales, gross_margin, ROUND(100.0 * gross_margin / net_sales, 1) AS gross_margin_pct FROM by_product ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10;
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns
Net sales = net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Store 999 and ZZ Test category excluded from analysis
Web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
As-is region hierarchy (current store region assignments)
assumptions: Q4 of FY2024/25 interpreted as fiscal weeks 40-52 (27 January to 27 April 2025)
South region using as-is (current) region hierarchy
Web orders excluded from physical store regions
Top 10 products sorted by gross margin amount (descending)
caveats: Region reorganisation occurred 28 April 2025: stores 101, 102, 103, 104, 105 moved from South to Capital Region, and store 114 Kouvola moved from East to South. As-is reporting uses current regions, so these stores are excluded from South totals for all history.
Gross margin percentage calculated as (gross margin / net sales) × 100

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), lines AS (SELECT s.region, CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN w.dispatch_date ELSE f.sale_date END AS business_date, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT region, round(sum(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END),2) AS aug_2024, round(sum(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END),2) AS sep_2024 FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, each line at its own VAT rate (24% to 31 Aug 2024, 25.5% from 1 Sep 2024; 14% and 10% unchanged)
Before returns: fact_return_line not used, no refunds deducted
As-was regions: region taken from the dim_store version on each sales line's store_key (the four regions South, West, East, North, plus Online)
Web shop is store 900, region Online, identified by store_id rather than channel_code
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected orders count
Store lines dated on sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
assumptions: August and September 2024 read as calendar months (1-31 Aug, 1-30 Sep 2024), since this is for a VAT filing, not as fiscal periods (the fiscal year starts at the end of August)
Regions 'as they were at the time, as in the old reports' read as as-was; this is the company's as-was reading, as in REQ-D05
Web sales put in the month of Helsinki dispatch date, the company web-sales rule, not the order date
Online (web shop) shown as its own region row, since web orders belong to no physical region
Staff purchases left in, as in company sales reporting; gross figure is the sum of line gross_amount, no flat VAT rate applied
caveats: Correction: store 999 (training store) and the ZZ Test articles (including one web test order) are excluded. The excluded gross amount in the two months is roughly 7,700 EUR.

Capital Region does not appear: it was created on 28 April 2025, so as-was it did not exist in 2024. The stores later moved into it (101-105) are inside South here, and Kouvola (114) is in East. On today's regions the split would be different.
Web dated by dispatch rather than order date moves a small amount between months: on order date Online would be 174,402.41 for August and 160,391.86 for September. Physical regions are unaffected.
The VAT rate on web lines follows the order date, so an order placed on 31 August and dispatched in September carries 24% and is counted in September.
Staff purchases (about 40.7 thousand EUR gross over the two months, all regions) are included; they are discounted 15% and are not removed.
Figures are gross sales before returns and are not a net VAT liability: refunds, and any VAT-exempt or non-sales items, are not netted off.
No duplicate sales lines were found for these two months. All periods in this range are fully loaded.

answer.sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN ref_fiscal_calendar rc ON f.sale_date BETWEEN rc.period_start_date AND rc.period_end_date WHERE f.store_key = 4 AND rc.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND rc.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY p.product_key, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold: sum of quantity from fact_sales_line
Fiscal period 5 date range from ref_fiscal_calendar
Store identified by name match (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki = store_key 4)
assumptions: This year refers to FY2026/27 (the fiscal year active on request date 2026-10-07)
Period 5 means fiscal period 5 within that fiscal year
Top 3 means highest units_sold, ranked in descending order

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (5, 6, 7, 8) AND (f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web shop identified by channel_code = 'WB' or channel_id in (2='Web home delivery', 3='Click and collect')
Last year = FY2025/26 (fiscal year preceding current FY2026/27)
Net sales = net_amount column, excluding VAT, after line discounts
assumptions: Current fiscal year is FY2026/27 (most recent date in warehouse); last year is FY2025/26
Periods 5 to 8 are calendar/fiscal periods as defined in dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar
Web shop sales tracked via both legacy channel_code field and newer channel_id field, depending on period
caveats: Data migration during period 7: periods 5-6 use channel_code exclusively; period 7 has sales recorded both ways (separate records); period 8+ use channel_id exclusively. The query accounts for both systems to capture all web sales.
Period 7 web sales include both legacy channel_code = 'WB' records (€38,287.09) and new channel_id = 2,3 records (€128,222.93), which represent different system migrations rather than duplicates.
