answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, s.format, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY s.format ORDER BY s.format
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts
Physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (store 900) excluded
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2026/27 period 4 (Monday 3 August to Sunday 30 August 2026, 28 days)
Format taken from the store version on the sale date (format is the same in every version of a store)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns
assumptions: 'Period 4 of FY26/27' read as FY2026/27 P4, a completed period within the warehouse load (through 4 October 2026)
'Average basket value' read as the company's ATV (average transaction value), as the request says
Formats are the values actually in dim_store: Large, Medium and Small. The column comment (Hyper/Standard/Express) is out of date.
Web is not shown as a format row because ATV is a store measure that excludes web orders
Store 999's 'Training' format is not shown because store 999 is excluded from all sales reporting
caveats: No data problems needing correction were found for this period: no duplicate sales lines, no null formats, no receipts spanning stores, no test-article lines in P4 store sales, and no receipts mixing staff and non-staff lines.

Control check passed: net sales before returns per store (all stores, ZZ Test out, staff included) matched rpt_daily_store_sales for 3 to 30 August 2026 with zero differences. The check does not cover the ATV figure itself, since staff purchases are removed from ATV.
Excluding staff purchases removed 666 lines on 280 receipts (EUR 14,796.76 net) from the ATV calculation.
The training store (999) had 127 lines on 55 receipts in P4 and was excluded.
ATV is before returns, so returns do not affect it.
Underlying figures: Large 8 stores, 6,508 receipts, EUR 394,865.46; Medium 18 stores, 8,641 receipts, EUR 520,763.45; Small 12 stores, 2,598 receipts, EUR 131,841.05.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT period_start_date AS start_date, period_end_date AS end_date FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period = 3), weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot (week-ending Sunday): summed across stores and articles within each week, then averaged across the weeks, never summed across weeks
Stock value at standard cost (fact_stock_week.closing_value)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P3 = 29 June to 2 August 2026, fiscal weeks 9 to 13, five weekly snapshots (5, 12, 19, 26 July and 2 August 2026)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded; web has no stock in this table
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product hierarchy: category taken from the current version of each article (dim_product is_current)
Ranged articles only (fact_stock_week holds rows only for articles a store carries)
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27, so 'period 3' is FY2026/27 P3 (fully loaded; the warehouse runs through 4 October 2026).
'Average stock' read as the average of the five weekly closing stock values in the period, not the last-week closing.
'Paint & Decorating' read as the product category of that name (all four subcategories: Interior Paint, Exterior Paint, Brushes & Rollers, Wallpaper & Decor Film).
'Whole chain' read as all physical stores (38 stores with stock rows in each week), excluding the web shop.
caveats: No corrections were needed. Checks on the five weeks: no duplicate rows at store x article x week, 38 stores in every week, no negative units or values, and closing_value equals closing_units x standard_unit_cost on every row.
The first week (5 July) has 25 more rows than the others (2,699 against 2,674). They are zero-stock rows for articles with no row in later weeks, so they add nothing to the value.
Value is at standard cost, which is revalued each April, and is not the retail value.
Kuopio (store 125) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 but still has stock rows, and its stock is included in the chain figure.
The average of the weekly snapshots is 344,466.83 EUR. The weekly totals ranged from 341,138.89 to 349,160.39 EUR.

answer.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, count(DISTINCT h.member_id) AS held_out_members FROM dim_campaign c JOIN campaign_holdout h ON h.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE c.campaign_id = 15 GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name
definitions_applied: Holdout members counted as distinct member_id from campaign_holdout (which holds member_id, not member_key)
Campaign identified in dim_campaign by name (current table, not the bak_dim_campaign_2025 backup)
assumptions: 'Black Week 2025' means campaign_id 15 (24 to 30 November 2025, email+sms+push); it is the only campaign with that name for 2025
'Held out' means the members listed in campaign_holdout for that campaign, with no restriction on tier, consent or activity
caveats: No corrections were needed. campaign_holdout has 2,747 rows and 2,747 distinct member_ids for this campaign, so there are no duplicates, and the count matches dim_campaign.holdout_size (2,747).
The holdout is 10.3% of the mailing list of 26,573 (2,747 / 26,573), a little above the nominal 10% holdout_pct recorded in dim_campaign.
None of the 2,747 held-out members appears among the 23,818 distinct targeted members in fact_campaign_exposure for this campaign, and all exist in dim_member.
Black Week 2024 (campaign 5) is a different campaign, with 1,928 held out, so do not mix the two up.

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, f.net_amount AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE p.category = 'Garden' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12), rets AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, -r.refund_net AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE p.category = 'Garden' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12) SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, round(sum(amt), 2) AS net_sales FROM (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rets) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net sales (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refunds (excluding VAT), the same definition as rpt_daily_store_sales
Refunds are booked in the period of the return date, not the original sale date
Fiscal periods from the company fiscal calendar (dim_date / ref_fiscal_calendar): FY2024/25 P07 = 2024-10-28 to 2024-11-24, P12 = 2025-03-24 to 2025-04-27
Garden category 'as reported at the time': the category of the product version in force on the sale or return date (product_key on the fact lines), so Outdoor Lighting is part of Garden
All real channels included: stores and the web shop (store_id 900)
Staff purchases included, as in the daily store sales report
assumptions: 'Old category set-up' is read as the pre-27 October 2025 hierarchy, where Outdoor Lighting (about 70 SKUs) sat under Garden. Since 27 October 2025 it sits under Electrical. The fact tables' product_key points to the version valid on the sale date, so no remapping was needed and I did not use today's category.
'Net sales' means net of returns, in EUR excluding VAT.
Garden covers all channels (all stores plus web), with no like-for-like or store-format filter, since none was requested.
Staff purchases are left in because the company's own daily sales report includes them and no exclusion was requested.
Periods are the fiscal periods P7 to P12 of FY2024/25 (late October 2024 to 27 April 2025), reported one row per period.
caveats: Correction: the 'Training store' pseudo-location (store_id 999) is excluded. It holds about 1,175 EUR of Garden sales in the range and is not real trading. The company's daily store sales report does not carry it either.

Correction: Garden is taken from the product version valid at the time of sale. Using today's dim_product would move Outdoor Lighting out of Garden and understate each period. Outdoor Lighting is 22.9k, 21.5k, 18.7k, 10.8k, 9.2k and 11.7k of gross Garden line sales in P7 to P12.
The figures are not comparable with Garden as it is defined now (without Outdoor Lighting). Any like-for-like comparison with FY2025/26 needs the same category set on both sides.
Net sales falls from P7 and then jumps in P11 and P12 (109k and 310k), because the spring season starts. P12 is a 5-week period and P7 to P10 are 4-week periods (P9 has 5 weeks).
No duplicate sales or return lines, orphaned returns, product keys outside their validity dates, or cancelled web orders were found in the range.

Reconciliation: the store-level sales in my base data match rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent over the whole range. Web lines in the fact table are about 2.7k EUR higher than the report over the six periods across all categories. I did not trace the cause, so the Garden web figure could differ slightly from a report-based figure.
Returns are assigned by return date, so a Garden refund in a period can relate to a sale from an earlier period.

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2024/25' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(f.vat_rate*100, 1) AS vat_rate_percent, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-26' AND DATE '2024-09-22' AND s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2024/25 P05 = fiscal weeks 18-21, 26 Aug 2024 to 22 Sep 2024
VAT from the line values: gross_amount minus net_amount, summed per line, with each line keeping its own vat_rate
Stores only: store_id below 900, so web shop (900) is excluded
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Store lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Staff purchases included
Control total: net amount before returns for the same scope equals rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns (938,729.24)
General VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, so both appear in this period
assumptions: Period 5 of FY24/25 means fiscal year FY2024/25, period 5 (26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024), as the request names the year
'In the stores' means the physical stores only, not the web shop
'VAT charged' means VAT on sales lines, before any refunds, since the dictionary does not define how returns enter a VAT figure
'Split by VAT rate' means one row per rate actually applied on the lines (10%, 14%, 24%, 25.5%)
Rates are shown in percent units
caveats: The period spans the 1 September 2024 VAT change: 24% applies to sales on 26-31 Aug 2024 and 25.5% to sales from 1 Sep 2024. Both are separate rows, as the lines carry their own rate.

Figures are VAT charged on sales and are not reduced for returns. Refunds booked in the stores in the same period carried VAT of about 11,136 EUR (10%: 1.20; 14%: 10.48; 24%: 5,094.72; 25.5%: 6,029.57), taken on the original line's rate and the return date. Net VAT after refunds would be lower by those amounts.
Excluded as the standing rule requires: store 999 and ZZ Test category lines (2,732.93 EUR net in the period) and the web shop (4,075 web lines in the date range).
Total VAT across the four rates is 235,090.72 EUR; this total row is not in the table because it was not requested.
Checks passed: no duplicate receipt lines, every line's gross matches net times (1 + its rate), and the net total matches the control table exactly.

answer.sql: SELECT cs.format AS store_format, COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id) AS receipts, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales_before_returns, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts
ATV is a store measure: physical stores only (store_id below 900), so web orders and the web shop are out
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) excluded from ATV
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Sales dated by sale_date, the Helsinki business date
Fiscal period from dim_date: FY2026/27 P4 is fiscal weeks 14-17, 3 to 30 August 2026
Format taken from the current store version (as-is), which is the same in every version of a store
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales_before_returns and receipts)
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, so period 4 is 3 to 30 August 2026 (28 days, fiscal weeks 14-17, fully loaded).

'Store format' means dim_store.format. The schema comment lists Hyper, Standard and Express, but the warehouse holds Large, Medium and Small for the physical stores. The Web and Training formats are left out because the ATV definition excludes web and store 999.
The request asks for ATV only, so the table shows ATV per format. Receipts and net sales are not shown.
caveats: Corrections: web lines (store 900), store 999 and ZZ Test articles were excluded. The staff-purchase receipts were also removed (666 lines across the three store formats). All of this follows the ATV definition and changes the receipt counts and net sales used.

Control check: before removing staff purchases, the stores total for the period was 18,027 receipts and EUR 1,062,266.72 net before returns, identical to rpt_daily_store_sales. The staff receipts removed were 18,027 - 17,747 = 280.
The source rows had no duplicate lines (sales_line_id and receipt_id + line_no are unique) and no store changed format between versions, so no deduplication was needed.
The figures are net of VAT and before returns, per the ATV definition.
Basis of the figures: Large 394,865.46 EUR over 6,508 receipts, Medium 520,763.45 EUR over 8,641, Small 131,841.05 EUR over 2,598.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS gold_members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key
Tier read from the current member version (is_current, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Versioned dimension handling: one row per member, so old versions are not counted
Warehouse tables only: stg_member_updates and bak_ tables not used
assumptions: 'Gold-tier loyalty members we have at the moment' is read as all enrolled members whose current tier is Gold, whether or not they have bought recently
'At the moment' is read as the latest version of each member. The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026 and the count is the same for 4 and 7 October 2026 (5,791)
The metric dictionary has no definition of total members, only of active members, so I applied the plain reading of enrolled members and did not invent a new company metric
caveats: This counts every enrolled Gold member. On the company definition of active members (at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks to Sunday 4 October 2026, any channel), 4,827 of them are active. If the request meant active Gold members, the figure is 4,827
The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so changes after that date are not included
stg_member_updates holds 433 of these Gold members in staging. I did not use it because staging tables are not for reporting. It is not part of the figure
Tiers are counted at the member level (60,000 current members, one current version each), so the version history of members who changed tier does not inflate the count

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 3 of FY2026/27 is weeks 9 to 13, Monday 29 June to Sunday 2 August 2026, 35 days
Units sold is the quantity on sales lines, by sale_date (the Helsinki business date)
Store scope: physical store 108 Lahti only; the web shop (900) is not included
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither changes the figure)
Staff purchases included (4 units, as in net sales)
As-is product hierarchy: Interior Paint is the current subcategory of each article (it sits in the Paint & Decorating category)
Control total: all-product units for Lahti in the period, checked against rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27. The request arrived on 5 October 2026, so period 3 was complete (loaded through 4 October 2026).

'Units sold' means units on sales lines (the company's units-sold basis, which is also what rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold holds), not units net of returns. No metric-dictionary entry defines unit sales after returns.
'The Lahti store' means store_id 108, Lahti. Tampere Lielahti (116) is a different store with a similar name.
'Interior Paint' means the subcategory of that name, 9 to 16 articles per version across the Paint & Decorating category; Exterior Paint is excluded.
caveats: Returns are not netted off. 5 units of Interior Paint were returned at Lahti with return dates in the same period, so net of returns the figure would be about 189. This is a return-date count and some of those returns may relate to sales made before the period.

No corrections to the data were needed. The 142 sales lines have no duplicate sales_line_id or receipt_id and line_no, the Helsinki date matches sale_date on every row, and the sales lines are not dated across the UTC midnight edge.

Control check: Lahti's all-product units for the period are 3,927 from fact_sales_line, and rpt_daily_store_sales gives 3,927 for the same 35 days, so the base data reconciles. The control table has no product dimension, so the Interior Paint figure itself is not directly controlled.
Lahti traded on all 35 days of the period. No refit closure or other dated event affects store 108 in this range.

No deprecated tables or views were used. The query_check.py script was not run. I made the equivalent checks (duplicate keys, date coverage, UTC against Helsinki dates, control total) with my own SQL.

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT f.week_ending_date, sum(f.closing_value) AS chain_stock_value FROM fact_stock_week f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.week_ending_date WHERE p.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND s.store_id < 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY f.week_ending_date) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, round(avg(chain_stock_value), 2) AS avg_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 runs 2026-06-29 to 2026-08-02 (5 fiscal weeks, weeks 9 to 13), fully loaded
Stock value at cost: closing_value in fact_stock_week, which is closing units at standard cost
Average stock: mean of the five weekly closing-stock totals (week-ending Sundays 5, 12, 19, 26 July and 2 August 2026)
Product category 'Paint & Decorating' taken from dim_product through the product_key on each stock row
Whole chain: all 38 trading stores; the web shop (900) and training store (999) are excluded by the store_id < 900 filter, and neither has stock rows in this category and period anyway
assumptions: 'This year' is read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, since the request is dated 8 October 2026 and fiscal year labels run across calendar years
'Average stock' is the average of the weekly closing stock values over the period's weeks, not an opening/closing average
'Value at cost' is standard cost, which is the only cost basis the warehouse holds for stock
Stores with no stock row for a SKU in a week contribute nothing for that week (about 25 delisted-SKU rows in the first week carry zero units, so they do not affect the value)
caveats: No corrections were needed. I checked the period's stock rows and found no duplicate store/SKU rows, no negative stock, no store or product versions outside their validity dates, and no rows where closing_value differed from units times standard unit cost.
The first week (ending 5 July) has 25 more rows than the other weeks. They are zero-unit rows for SKUs delisted before that date, so they add no value and the result is unchanged.
Closed store 129 Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026) has no stock rows in the period, so it is not in the figure.
Standard unit costs are revalued each April, so this figure is on the FY2026/27 cost basis and is not strictly comparable at cost with earlier years' periods.

answer.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT fiscal_year, period_start_date s, period_end_date e FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_period=8 AND fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25','FY2025/26')), cur AS (SELECT sku, category cur_cat FROM dim_product WHERE is_current), sales AS (SELECT per.fiscal_year fy, c.cur_cat cat, f.net_amount amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN cur c ON c.sku=p.sku JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key=f.store_key JOIN per ON f.sale_date BETWEEN per.s AND per.e WHERE st.store_id<>999), rets AS (SELECT per.fiscal_year fy, c.cur_cat cat, -f.refund_net amt FROM fact_return_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN cur c ON c.sku=p.sku JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key=f.store_key JOIN per ON f.return_date BETWEEN per.s AND per.e WHERE st.store_id<>999), u AS (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rets) SELECT cat AS category, 8 AS fiscal_period, 'FY2024/25' AS prior_fiscal_year, round(sum(CASE WHEN fy='FY2024/25' THEN amt END),2) AS prior_net_sales, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, round(sum(CASE WHEN fy='FY2025/26' THEN amt END),2) AS net_sales, round(100.0*(sum(CASE WHEN fy='FY2025/26' THEN amt END)/sum(CASE WHEN fy='FY2024/25' THEN amt END)-1),2) AS growth_pct FROM u WHERE cat IN ('Garden','Electrical') GROUP BY cat ORDER BY cat
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 8 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2024/25 P08 = 2024-11-25 to 2024-12-22; FY2025/26 P08 = 2025-11-24 to 2025-12-21), both 4 weeks and fully loaded
Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns, with returns counted in the period of the return date, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Channels: stores and web (home delivery and click and collect) both included. The FY2025/26 lines have a NULL channel_code and use channel_id instead, so no filter on channel_code was used
Product category taken from the current version of each SKU (dim_product.is_current), applied to both years, so the two periods use the same product hierarchy
Training store (store_id 999, head office) excluded
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) kept in, as they are real sales at the real stores
assumptions: 'Last year' and 'the year before' are read as fiscal years relative to the request date of 2026-10-05, which falls in FY2026/27. Last year is FY2025/26 and the year before is FY2024/25. Period 8 of the current year (December 2026) has not happened yet.
Growth is FY2025/26 P08 against FY2024/25 P08, in percent
'Net sales' means after returns, as in the company's daily net sales report, rather than sales before returns
Web sales are included in the category figures, since the request names no channel
Garden and Electrical are reported on the current category hierarchy (including the Outdoor Lighting move). The as-recorded figures are in the caveats.
caveats: Correction 1, category reclassification: the Outdoor Lighting subcategory (about 70 SKUs) moved from Garden to Electrical on 2025-10-27. Read as recorded, FY2024/25 P08 has it in Garden and FY2025/26 P08 has it in Electrical. That gives Electrical +19.65% (143,159.94 to 171,286.19) and Garden -35.06% (56,462.85 to 36,665.72), which is mostly the move and not trading. I restated FY2024/25 to the current hierarchy, which moves about 19,340 of net sales (after returns) from Garden to Electrical. On the same basis, Electrical is +5.41% and Garden -1.23%. The two categories combined are 199,622.79 in FY2024/25 and 207,951.91 in FY2025/26 (+4.17%), the same on either basis. If Commercial wants the old Garden grouping instead, Outdoor Lighting would be counted in Garden in both years.

Correction 2, channel coding: FY2025/26 sales lines carry a NULL channel_code and use channel_id (1 store, 2 web home delivery, 3 click and collect) after the web-platform migration, while FY2024/25 uses channel_code ST/WB with a NULL channel_id. A filter on channel_code would silently drop all of FY2025/26. No channel filter was used. Web is about 14% of the period's sales in both years.

Correction 3, training store and test articles: store 999 (Training store, head office) holds test sales in both periods, including ZZ Test articles and flagged staff purchases. These lines were excluded. They total about 2.3k EUR in FY2024/25 P08 and 2.6k in FY2025/26 P08, and would otherwise have inflated Electrical and Garden slightly.
Garden and Electrical net sales include returns booked in the period, matched by return date and not by the date of the original sale.
The 'rpt.v_daily_sales' view and other reporting objects were not used as the source, because they depend on channel_code and on the as-recorded category. The figures were built from the fact tables.

Checked and not affecting this result: the duplicate sales lines (418 receipt/line pairs loaded twice, 836 rows, about 20.8k EUR) all fall in FY2025/26 P05 (2025-09-15 to 2025-09-21), not in period 8. Planned store refits (stores 104, 119, 125) do not overlap either period 8. Independence Day closure falls in both periods (Friday 2024-12-06, Saturday 2025-12-06) and is already reflected in the sales.
The growth rates cover one 4-week period each and are on net sales in EUR excluding VAT, with no adjustment for price changes, store openings or closures, or like-for-like store sets.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount), 2) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period IN (5, 6, 7, 8) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web channel identified by channel_code = 'WB' in fact_sales_line
Net sales as sum of net_amount (EUR, excluding VAT, after line discounts)
Fiscal periods from ref_fiscal_calendar joined via dim_date
assumptions: Last year interpreted as prior full fiscal year (FY2024/25, ended April 2025)
Net sales metric refers to net_amount field from fact_sales_line table
caveats: All four requested periods (5-8) are fully loaded in the warehouse
No NULL channel codes present in these periods
Values are in EUR excluding VAT; this is the net sales after line discounts per warehouse design

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 107 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY ALL
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2026/27 is 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (fiscal weeks 18 to 21), fully loaded
Units sold: sum of quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (the Helsinki business date)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded from sales work (no effect on this figure)
As-is product hierarchy: the current dim_product version supplies the subcategory
Versioned dimensions: store_id and sku are the stable keys, and the current product version is joined on is_current
Store scope: physical store 107 only, no web shop (store 900)
Control total: the store's all-category units and receipts for the period match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 5' means fiscal period 5, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026
Hyvinkää is store 107, the only store with that name or city, and it has a single version in dim_store
'Cleaning Products' is a subcategory under the category 'Cleaning & Household', not a category of its own, so I used the subcategory
'Units sold' is the quantity on sales lines in the store, with staff purchases included as in net sales (4 of the 136 units were staff purchases)

Units are counted before returns, as the metric dictionary counts units sold from sales lines. There were no returns of these articles processed at Hyvinkää in the period, so the figure is the same after returns
Web orders collected at Hyvinkää are not included, because they are booked to the web shop (store 900)
caveats: The request wording 'Cleaning Products' matches no category. I read it as the subcategory under Cleaning & Household. If Mika meant the whole Cleaning & Household category, the figure will be higher
No data problem needed correcting. There were no duplicate sales lines (63 lines, 63 distinct keys), no store 999 or test-article rows, and all 28 days of the period are loaded
The same articles had the same subcategory when sold as they have now, so as-is and as-was give the same answer

answer.sql: SELECT tier, count(DISTINCT member_id) AS member_count FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Current member = the latest version of each loyalty number (dim_member.is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Members counted by member_id (the stable loyalty number), not by member_key, because dim_member keeps one row per version
Tier as recorded in the current version (Gold)
assumptions: 'Right now' means the current version of each member as held in the warehouse, which carries changes up to 2026-10-04 (the latest valid_from), not 2026-10-08 when the request arrived
'Members on the Gold tier' counts every loyalty member whose current tier is Gold, whatever their marketing consent or home store
Online sign-ups (home store 900) and staff or other special members are included, since the request did not exclude them
caveats: No data problems found. Each of the 60,000 member_ids has exactly one current version, there are no overlapping versions, no future-dated joins or versions, and no missing join dates or tiers.

Counting all dim_member rows with tier = 'Gold' would give 8,203, because 2,412 historical (superseded) Gold versions are also stored. They are excluded here. Only 5,791 distinct members are Gold now.
The staging table stg_member_updates (2,462 recent changes, 433 of them Gold) is already fully reflected in dim_member, so nothing is pending.
The warehouse's latest member change is dated 2026-10-04, so any tier change made between 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-08 is not in this figure.
Of the 5,791 Gold members, 3,861 have marketing consent. If this count is for a campaign mailing list, that is the reachable number, and I did not apply it.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns deducted on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only; cancelled and processing orders excluded)
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal weeks run Monday to Sunday; P2 of each year lined up by fiscal week number, not calendar date
Growth % = this year / last year - 1
Control total: weekly figures match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (gap 0.00 in all 8 year-weeks)
assumptions: 'This year' is FY2026/27 and 'last year' is FY2025/26, the current and previous fiscal years on the request date of 5 October 2026
Period 2 is FY2026/27 P2 (weeks 5 to 8, 1 to 28 June 2026), compared with FY2025/26 P2 (weeks 5 to 8, 26 May to 22 June 2025)
Each week is compared with the same fiscal week number last year
'Total company sales' means net sales on the company definition (excluding VAT, after returns), including the web shop
Values are in EUR
caveats: Weeks 7 and 8 are not comparable like for like. Midsummer fell in fiscal week 7 this year (Eve Fri 19 June, Day Sat 20 June 2026) but in week 8 last year (Fri 20 June 2025). The stores are shut on both days, so this year's week 7 has 5 trading days against 7 last year, and week 8 has 7 against 5. That explains most of the -32.2% in week 7 and the +76.4% in week 8. Read the two weeks together: weeks 7 and 8 combined are 591,343.83 this year against 535,679.88 last year, +10.4%.

Store closures lower this year's weeks against last year's. Kuopio (store 125) has been in a refit closure since 15 June 2026 and has no sales in weeks 7 and 8. It sold about 11.6k in week 7 and 6.7k in week 8 last year. Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales this year. It sold about 2.1k to 2.9k a week in P2 last year. These are real changes to the business and were left in, because the request is for total company sales, not like-for-like.
Total company includes the web shop. Web net sales were 52.1k, 60.7k, 44.9k and 73.0k in weeks 5 to 8 this year, against 40.7k, 35.4k, 44.4k and 30.5k last year.

No data correction was needed for this range. The sales lines contain 418 duplicated receipt/line keys, but all are in FY2025/26 week 21 (outside P2) and do not affect these figures. The weekly totals match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total exactly.
The deprecated views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used, because they leave out web sales from November 2025. channel_code was not used.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2025-08-25' AS start_date, DATE '2025-09-21' AS end_date
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: DEF-STORE-LEAGUE: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
DEF-NET-SALES: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, on return date
DEF-NET-SALES-SCOPE: excludes store 999 and category ZZ Test; includes staff purchases
CAL-CLOSED-DAYS: trading days = open days minus closed holidays and refits
REG-STORE-EVENTS: store openings, closures, and refit windows from dim_store and ref_store_closure
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: physical stores only (store_id < 900); web shop excluded
assumptions: Period 5 last year: interpreted as P5 FY2025/26 (25 August to 21 September 2025), the most recent completed P5 relative to the request date of 8 October 2026
Trading days: calendar days the store was open, excluding Finnish public holidays and days the store was shut by company rule (dim_date.is_trading_day = true)
Store format: taken from the current store version (dim_store.is_current = true)
caveats: Control total discrepancy: query sum of net_sales (950,787.15) exceeds rpt_daily_store_sales control total (940,396.62) by 10,390.53 (1.1%). The discrepancy is concentrated in store 116 (Tampere Lielahti), where the query calculates 47,679.15 but the control table shows 37,288.62. Root cause not identified within query limit; potential causes include data timing differences (UTC vs Helsinki day boundary for web orders or returns), or differences in how rpt_daily_store_sales is maintained. The league table uses the standard pattern from accepted requests REQ-D37 to REQ-D40.
Store 119 (Pori): 14 trading days instead of 28, due to a refit closure from 8 September to 12 October 2025 (5 whole weeks); the store is ranked on the days it traded during this period

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28' AND status <> 'cancelled'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order (not sales lines), one row per order
Cancelled orders excluded; processing orders would be included (none on this day)
Test orders (category ZZ Test) excluded (none found)
Day boundary taken in UTC as the request asks, instead of the company default of Helsinki time
assumptions: Black Friday 2025 is 28 November 2025, as the request states
'Placed' is read as order_ts_utc, the time the order was placed
Cancelled orders are not counted as placed web orders, following the company web-orders definition
Click-and-collect and home-delivery orders are both included, as both are web orders
caveats: The request asks for the UTC day, which differs from the company default of the Helsinki day. On the Helsinki day the same count is 402 (finland is UTC+2 in November), so the two figures should not be compared directly.
20 orders with a UTC order date of 28 November have status cancelled and are excluded. Including them the UTC-day figure would be 377.
Checks found no duplicate web_order_id values, no test-article orders and no logged-in orders missing a member key, so no corrections to the data were needed.

answer.sql:
SELECT
  d.fiscal_year,
  d.fiscal_period,
  ROUND(SUM(net_sales_contribution), 2) as net_sales
FROM (
  SELECT 
    CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', wo.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) as transaction_date,
    SUM(sl.net_amount) as net_sales_contribution
  FROM fact_sales_line sl
  JOIN fact_web_order wo ON sl.receipt_id = wo.web_order_id
  JOIN dim_store ds ON sl.store_key = ds.store_key
  JOIN dim_product dp ON sl.product_key = dp.product_key
  WHERE ds.store_id = 900 AND dp.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  GROUP BY transaction_date
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT
    rl.return_date as transaction_date,
    -SUM(rl.refund_net) as net_sales_contribution
  FROM fact_return_line rl
  JOIN dim_store ds ON rl.store_key = ds.store_key
  JOIN dim_product dp ON rl.product_key = dp.product_key
  WHERE ds.store_id = 900 AND dp.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  GROUP BY rl.return_date
) combined
JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = combined.transaction_date
WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8
GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
ORDER BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web shop: store 900 (pseudo-store for web orders)
Web sales recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time, not order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Test articles excluded (category ZZ Test)
assumptions: Last year in context of request date 2026-10-06 (FY2026/27) means FY2025/26
Periods 5 to 8 means fiscal periods (not calendar months); fiscal periods are numbered 1-12 within each fiscal year
caveats: Returns booked during periods 5-8 may relate to sales from earlier periods, since returns can arrive up to 30 days after purchase
Data is complete through 2025-12-21 (end of fiscal period 8 of FY2025/26)
Figures in EUR, net of VAT

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(f.vat_rate * 100, 2) AS vat_rate_pct, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2024/25 = 2024-08-26 to 2024-09-22 (4 weeks, fiscal weeks 18-21), from ref_fiscal_calendar; marked fully loaded
Stores = channel_code ST, excluding pseudo-locations (store_id 900 web shop, 999 training store)
VAT charged = gross_amount minus net_amount on the sales lines, grouped by the vat_rate on the line
Store identified through dim_store.store_key (the store version on the sale date), not store_id directly
assumptions: VAT charged is read as VAT on sales as rung up, before returns; refunds are not netted off
Staff purchases are included, since VAT is charged on them like any other sale
Web orders, including click-and-collect orders collected in stores, are excluded because the request asks for stores
Sales are placed in the period by sale_date, which matches the local (Helsinki) date of the sale timestamp on every line
Rates are shown as percentages (25.5 means 25.5%)
caveats: The standard VAT rate changed during the period: 24% applied on sales dated 26-31 Aug 2024 and 25.5% from 1 Sep 2024. Both rates are in the split, as the lines carry them. Reduced rates of 10% and 14% are unchanged.
The training store (store_id 999) has 238 sales lines in the period, with about 885 EUR of VAT. They are excluded. It is not a trading store.
Web shop (store_id 900) lines in the period carry about 30,846 EUR of VAT (19.84 at 10%, 88.65 at 14%, 6,780.38 at 24%, 23,957.29 at 25.5%). They are excluded.
Staff purchases are included in the figures: 3.59 EUR at 10%, 11.77 at 14%, 691.63 at 24% and 2,666.70 at 25.5%, about 3,374 EUR in total.

Refunds in stores booked in the period carry VAT of about 11,136 EUR (1.20 at 10%, 10.48 at 14%, 5,094.72 at 24%, 6,029.57 at 25.5%). These are not deducted. If Finance wants VAT net of returns, subtract these figures.

Data checks on the in-scope lines found no duplicate receipt/line numbers, no VAT amounts out of line with the stated rate, no zero or negative quantities, no sales on non-trading days, and data for all 28 days and 38 stores. No correction was needed beyond excluding the pseudo-locations.

answer.sql: SELECT o.region, SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM f.sale_date) = 8 THEN f.gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024, SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM f.sale_date) = 9 THEN f.gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024 FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON f.store_key = ds.store_key INNER JOIN dim_store_old o ON ds.store_id = o.store_id WHERE f.sale_date >= '2024-08-01' AND f.sale_date <= '2024-09-30' AND ds.store_id < 900 GROUP BY o.region ORDER BY o.region;
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT: gross_amount from fact_sales_line
Before returns: only fact_sales_line rows, no deduction for returns
Regional structure: dim_store_old regions (East, North, South, West) as they existed in 2024
Physical stores only: store_id < 900 excludes web shop and training store pseudo-locations
assumptions: Date range: full calendar months August and September 2024 (2024-08-01 to 2024-09-30)
Regions as they were at the time: interpreted as the dim_store_old structure rather than current regions
Physical stores: assumed request for store channel sales, excluding web and head office
caveats: The current dim_store has additional regions (Capital Region, Online, Head office) not in the old structure; this query returns only the four historical regions
Web channel sales (store_id 900) are excluded as they have no region in the old structure
All store locations in August–September 2024 successfully mapped to old regions with no mismatches

answer.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders
FROM fact_web_order o
WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
  AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    WHERE f.receipt_id = o.web_order_id AND (p.category = 'ZZ Test' OR s.store_id = 999)
  );
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order on the Helsinki order date
Cancelled orders excluded, processing orders would be included
Day boundary at Helsinki midnight, converted from order_ts_utc
Click-and-collect counted as web
Test orders (store 999 / category ZZ Test) filtered out
Did not use channel_code, because the web platform migration on 3 November 2025 left it empty
assumptions: Cyber Monday is Monday 1 December 2025, as the request states.
'Web shop orders' means all non-cancelled orders in fact_web_order, home delivery and click-and-collect together.
Orders are dated by the day they were placed, not the day they were dispatched, as the company definition for order counts says.
caveats: Dating by UTC date would have given 267 orders. The Helsinki date (UTC+2 in December) is what gives 326.
19 orders placed on 1 December 2025 were cancelled and are not counted (345 orders in total on the day, including those cancelled).
No orders placed that day were still in processing status, and none were test orders, so the test-order filter did not change the total.
The figure includes both delivered (239) and collected click-and-collect (87) orders.
fact_web_order has one row per order ID (94,876 rows, all distinct), so the count has no duplicates.

answer.sql:
WITH sales_lines AS (
  SELECT 
    f.sales_line_id,
    cp.sku,
    cp.product_name,
    f.net_amount,
    f.standard_cost
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current
  INNER JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' 
    AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 40 AND 52
    AND cs.region = 'South'
    AND cs.store_id < 900
    AND cp.category != 'ZZ Test'
),
return_lines AS (
  SELECT 
    fr.sales_line_id,
    fr.refund_net,
    fr.standard_cost_returned
  FROM fact_return_line fr
),
product_margins AS (
  SELECT 
    sl.sku,
    sl.product_name,
    SUM(sl.net_amount) as net_sales_before_returns,
    SUM(sl.standard_cost) as cost_before_returns,
    COALESCE(SUM(rl.refund_net), 0) as total_refunds,
    COALESCE(SUM(rl.standard_cost_returned), 0) as cost_of_returns
  FROM sales_lines sl
  LEFT JOIN return_lines rl ON sl.sales_line_id = rl.sales_line_id
  GROUP BY sl.sku, sl.product_name
)
SELECT 
  sku,
  product_name,
  ROUND(net_sales_before_returns - total_refunds - (cost_before_returns - cost_of_returns), 2) as gross_margin
FROM product_margins
ORDER BY gross_margin DESC
LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin (metric-dictionary): net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns
Net sales (metric-dictionary): net amount excluding VAT, after returns; store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
South region as-is (store-and-product-history): current region hierarchy applied to all history
assumptions: Q4 resolved as the most recently completed fiscal quarter: FY2024/25 Q4 (fiscal weeks 40-52, 27 January to 27 April 2025)
South region uses as-is reporting with current store-region mappings (includes stores that moved to South after the period)
Top 10 means the 10 products with the highest absolute gross margin value in EUR
caveats: Gross margin values are in EUR; no margin percentage calculated
Returns are credited back at standard cost per the company definition
Standard cost is revalued each April and applied to all sales in the period
The result spans multiple product categories within the South region

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_category AS (SELECT cp.category, d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM by_category ty JOIN by_category ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.category

Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included

As-is category hierarchy: current product version via sku and is_current, so outdoor lighting counts in Electrical in both years
Fiscal calendar via dim_date: period 8 is fiscal weeks 31 to 34 (24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025; 25 Nov to 22 Dec 2024)
Growth is the percentage change in net sales from FY2024/25 P8 to FY2025/26 P8
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: The request was received on 5 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27. I read 'last year' as FY2025/26, following the past requests from May 2026 onward, and 'the year before' as FY2024/25.
Period 8 means fiscal period 8 of each year, with the same period number lined up and not the same calendar dates.
Garden and Electrical are the product categories in dim_product. Net sales cover all channels, stores and web, since the request does not limit them.
History is as-is, the management default. The request does not ask for as-was.

Garden's growth would then look weaker and Electrical's stronger.
Web sales are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date. They are included: Electrical web was 24,977.12 in FY2025/26 and 20,657.82 in FY2024/25, Garden web 5,443.12 and 6,356.90.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, channel_code or any stg_, bak_ or tmp_ table. The views leave out web sales after 3 Nov 2025, which would have understated FY2025/26 P8.
I checked the data and found no duplicate sales or return lines, no unmatched product or store keys and no web lines without a dispatched order. Every SKU has exactly one current version.

The store-level net sales behind this query (all categories, stores only) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for P8 in both years (1,210,431.52 and 1,196,370.96). The control table has no category dimension, so the Garden and Electrical figures themselves cannot be tied to it directly.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after the sale. Because returns are booked on their own date, the periods are net of returns actually booked in them. They are not a sale-week cohort.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 22 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales in LFL stores against the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
LFL base: store open at least 364 days before the start of the range
A store-week counts only if the store traded in that week in both years; refit weeks from ref_store_closure drop out in both years
Closed store (Savonlinna) drops out
Week 53 excluded (there are none in this range)
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, less returns on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 and Online region excluded
Regions as-is (current dim_store version, five regions including Capital Region)
Fiscal year to date through the last completed fiscal week, aligned on fiscal week number
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Read 'how they are doing' as year-on-year sales growth, and used LFL growth as the company growth measure. Ranked from highest to lowest. Raw net sales would give a different order of size, since West is the largest region.

'This year so far' means FY2026/27 year to date: fiscal weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026), the last completed week in the warehouse. The comparator is FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22 (28 April to 28 September 2025).
Regions as-is: the current region of each store, so the Capital Region covers its six stores in both years, and Kouvola counts in South.
The request was received on 6 October 2026 and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so week 22 is complete and included.
Rank 1 is the highest LFL growth.
caveats: Data correction: fact_sales_line holds every line of store 116 (West) for 15 to 21 September 2025 twice. There are 418 receipt lines (receipt_id plus line_no) with an identical duplicate row and a new sales_line_id. That is last year's comparator, FY2025/26 week 21. I kept one row per receipt line. After this, store 116 agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales. Without the correction, West last year was overstated by about 10,000 EUR (1,768,594 instead of 1,758,204) and its LFL growth showed 1.33% instead of 1.93%. The order of regions does not change either way. Returns point to the first copy of each line, so they are not affected. The duplicates should be reported to whoever owns the ETL load.
Apart from store 116 in that week, every physical store's net sales agree with rpt_daily_store_sales for weeks 1 to 22 in both years.

LFL leaves out store-weeks that did not trade in both years: Pori's refit weeks, Kuopio's refit weeks (15 June to 26 July 2026) and Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026). The base is 38 stores: North 6, Capital Region 5, South 10, West 10, East 7. Regional growth therefore does not cover total regional sales.

East is the only region below last year's level (-0.19%). North and Capital Region are well ahead. The gap between South and West is small (2.11% against 1.93%), so their order is sensitive to small changes in the base.
No VAT-inclusive, margin or web figures are included. Web orders are not in any region.
The schema comment on dim_store.region still says four regions; the data has five.

answer.sql: SELECT sale_date, SUM(net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line WHERE channel_code = 'WB' AND sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY sale_date ORDER BY sale_date
definitions_applied: Web sales channel: channel_code = 'WB'
Net sales: sum of net_amount from fact_sales_line (excludes VAT)
assumptions: Daily grain requested; one row per calendar day
Net sales (excluding VAT) is the correct interpretation of 'net sales'
caveats: No data available for the requested period. Web sales in the warehouse cover 2024-04-29 to 2025-11-02. The requested dates (2025-12-15 to 2025-12-23) are beyond the current data load; ask Data & Analytics whether a future data load is scheduled or if a different date range is available.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key WHERE f.store_key = 4 AND f.sale_date >= '2026-08-31' AND f.sale_date <= '2026-09-27' GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold: quantity from fact_sales_line, all channels and store types included
Store identified by current store master record (is_current = TRUE)
Fiscal period 5 date range from ref_fiscal_calendar
assumptions: This year interpreted as FY2026/27 (fiscal year running Apr 2026–Mar 2027), with period 5 from 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27
Products ranked by total quantity, including all channels (in-store and web)
Staff purchases included in the count

answer.sql: WITH movements AS (SELECT p.sku, f.net_amount AS sales_net, f.standard_cost AS sales_cost, 0::DECIMAL(14,2) AS refund_net, 0::DECIMAL(14,2) AS cost_returned FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-27' AND DATE '2025-04-27' AND s.region = 'South' UNION ALL SELECT p.sku, 0, 0, r.refund_net, r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-27' AND DATE '2025-04-27' AND s.region = 'South'), margin_by_sku AS (SELECT sku, sum(sales_net - sales_cost) - sum(refund_net - cost_returned) AS gross_margin FROM movements GROUP BY sku), names AS (SELECT sku, arg_max(product_name, valid_from) AS product_name FROM dim_product GROUP BY sku) SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY m.gross_margin DESC) AS rank, m.sku, n.product_name, round(m.gross_margin, 2) AS gross_margin_eur FROM margin_by_sku m JOIN names n USING (sku) ORDER BY m.gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Fiscal quarter: Q4 of FY2024/25 is fiscal periods 10 to 12, 2025-01-27 to 2025-04-27 (ref_fiscal_calendar, fully loaded)
Gross margin = net sales excluding VAT minus standard cost of the units sold, in EUR
Returns deducted as in the company's daily net sales report: refund_net less standard_cost_returned, booked on the return date at the store where the return was made
Staff purchases kept in, because rpt_daily_store_sales includes them in net sales
Region taken from the store version in force on the sale or return date, through store_key
Products grouped by sku (stable across versions), not product_key, with the latest product name
Store-channel sales only: the web shop (store 900) and the training store (999) are not in South
assumptions: South region means the stores that were in South during the quarter. 14 stores: 101 to 113 and 137 Lohja. Stores 101 to 105 (Helsinki Vuosaari, Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, Espoo Lommila, Vantaa Tammisto, Kerava) moved to Capital Region on 2025-04-28, the day after the quarter ended. Kouvola (114) moved from East to South on the same date.
Top 10 means ranked by gross margin in EUR, not by margin percentage.

Gross margin is net of returns, as the company reports net sales. Before returns the order is nearly the same: Power Tools Koivuranta 416 would rank 9th at 1687.37 and Plumbing Parts Ahvenisto 279 would rank 11th at 1486.44, behind Bathroom Furniture Mäntylä 246 at 1509.11.
No overhead, freight or supplier rebates are included, as the warehouse holds only standard cost.
caveats: The region basis changes the answer. Using today's region mapping (Capital Region stores out, Kouvola in), 8 of the 10 products stay in the top 10 but the order and values change: rank 1 Cushions & Throws Tuulikki 338 falls to 2927.42, and Power Tools Koivuranta 416 drops out. Indoor Lighting Havu 419 (Electrical, margin 978.84 on that basis) and Smart Home Tuulikki 855 (935.46) are in the top 12 on that basis only. I used the regions as they stood in the quarter. If Commercial wants the current South, the query needs re-running.
dim_store holds two region versions for stores 101 to 105 and 114. Joining on store_id, or on the current version only, would put sales in the wrong region.

No duplicate sales or return lines, null values, cost mismatches or sales outside a product's listing dates were found in the quarter's South data. Line standard cost matches quantity times unit cost on all 41,850 South lines. Store sales and returns reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales.

108 of the 1,528 South returns in the quarter were made at a different store than the original sale (store_key differs). They are counted at the returning store, which is how the company report books them.
Staff purchases (about 2,000 lines company-wide in the quarter) are included. Excluding them would lower some products' margins slightly.
Each SKU has a single product version in the quarter, so there is no cost revaluation within the period. The April standard-cost revaluation does not affect these figures.

answer.sql: SELECT 131 AS store_id, 'Oulu Kaakkuri' AS store_name, 101624 AS sku, 'Fixings & Fasteners Raudikko 251' AS product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 131 AND p.sku = 101624 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-28' AND DATE '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Units sold: the quantity on sales lines, by sale date
Fiscal calendar: last completed fiscal week, Monday to Sunday
Helsinki business date (sale_date) for the day boundaries
Versioned dimensions: counted by the stable keys store_id and sku, joined on the version keys carried by the fact lines
Store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out
Staff purchases included, as in net sales and units sold
Query checked with query_check.py: no deprecated objects, no lint warnings, one result row
assumptions: 'Oulu Kaakkuri' is the store (store_id 131, store_key 37, North region, Large format) and SKU 101624 is the article (Fixings & Fasteners Raudikko 251, Tools & Hardware).

'Last week' means the last completed fiscal week, FY2026/27 week 22, Monday 28 September to Sunday 4 October 2026. The request was received on Thursday 8 October, and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October, so the week is complete.
Units sold means units on sales lines in the store. Returns are not netted off.
The figure covers store sales only. SKU 101624 also sold through the web shop (store 900) that week, 7 units, but web orders are not Oulu Kaakkuri store sales.
caveats: No data problems found for this store, article and week. There were 8 sales lines, with no duplicate line ids, and none carried a staff-purchase flag.
No returns are booked against these 8 lines. Returns made later would not change units sold on this definition.

The metric dictionary has no standalone 'units sold' definition. I used the quantity on sales lines by sale date, as in the weeks-of-cover definition. Net-of-returns units would be the same number here.
The store filter on 999 and ZZ Test did not change the result.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.subcategory AS product_group, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND p.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, p.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 runs 2026-06-29 to 2026-08-02 (5 weeks, fiscal weeks 9 to 13), taken from ref_fiscal_calendar and dim_date
Interior Paint = dim_product.subcategory 'Interior Paint' (category Paint & Decorating), matched through the product_key stored on each sales line (the product version at the sale date)
Lahti = store_id 108 (store_name 'Lahti'), matched through the store_key stored on each sales line
Units sold = sum of fact_sales_line.quantity by sale_date, before returns (the same basis as units_sold in rpt_daily_store_sales)
assumptions: 'Period 3 of FY26/27' means fiscal year FY2026/27, fiscal period 3, not calendar month 3
'Lahti store' means the store named Lahti (store_id 108). I left out 'Tampere Lielahti' (store_id 116), which a text search on 'Lahti' also returns
'Units sold' is gross units sold. Returns are not deducted (see caveats for the net figure)
Staff purchases are included, because the request does not exclude them
Only Interior Paint is counted. Exterior Paint, Brushes & Rollers and Wallpaper & Decor Film are separate subcategories and are left out
No relative or ambiguous date term needed reading, because the request names the fiscal year and period explicitly
caveats: No correction to the data was needed. Checked and clean: FY2026/27 P03 is marked fully loaded; Lahti has a single store version; no refit closures recorded for Lahti; no duplicate receipt/line rows; no lines outside the period; sale_date agrees with the UTC timestamp, with sales between 06:00 and 17:59 UTC, so no time-zone shift across period boundaries; every Lahti line in the period is on the Store channel; the fact table's Lahti total for the period (3,927 units, all products) reconciles exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales
Lahti has 142 Interior Paint sales lines in the period, covering 33 SKUs
194 units is before returns. Lahti had 5 Interior Paint units returned in the period (5 return lines), so net of returns it would be 189 units
The 194 includes 4 units bought by staff on 2026-08-01. Excluding staff purchases it would be 190 units
Two Interior Paint SKUs (100963 and 101047) have two product versions in dim_product, both classed as Interior Paint, so the count is unaffected
Searching for 'Lahti' also matches 'Tampere Lielahti'. Filtering on store_id 108 avoids it

answer.sql: SELECT cp.subcategory, cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on fact_sales_line, dated by sale_date (store sales, so the Helsinki sale date)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded from sales work (neither changes the Nokia total)
As-is hierarchy: subcategory and category taken from the current product version (dim_product is_current)
Store identified by stable store_id 118, not by store_key version
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2026/27 period 5 = 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (28 days, 4 weeks)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same store and days
Did not use channel_code, rpt.v_daily_sales, or any stg_/bak_/tmp_/old tables
assumptions: 'Nokia' is store 118, the store named Nokia in the city of Nokia (West region, Medium format). It is the only store matching the name.
'Period 5 this year' is read as FY2026/27 P05, which is also the last completed period (the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026).
'Units sold' is the gross quantity on sales lines, before returns. The company has no units-net-of-returns definition, and the control table's units_sold is also before returns.
Subcategories are on the as-is (current) hierarchy, the company default. The as-was and as-is rankings are identical here.
Only the physical store is counted, because Nokia has no web component (web is the separate store 900).
caveats: Control total: Nokia units sold for P5 from fact_sales_line (2,245 units, 564 receipts, EUR 29,540.71 net before returns) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly over the same 28 days.
No grain problems found: 1,250 lines for Nokia in P5, all with unique sales_line_id and unique receipt_id + line_no. No test-article or non-positive-quantity lines.

Fixings & Fasteners is far ahead (570 units against 152 for second place). Its sales run at a similar level in every period of FY2026/27 (about 550 to 790 units per period), so this is genuine volume and not a data error.
No tie affects the top 3. Fourth place is a tie between Cleaning Products and Plants & Flowers at 136 units each, but both are below third place (139).
No corrections to the data were needed.

answer.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT min(calendar_date) AS period_start, max(calendar_date) AS period_end FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period = 2), sold AS (SELECT st.format, sum(f.net_amount) AS sold_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key, p WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN p.period_start AND p.period_end AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1), ret AS (SELECT st.format, sum(r.refund_net) AS refunded_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key, p WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN p.period_start AND p.period_end AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, sold.format AS store_format, round(ret.refunded_net / sold.sold_net * 100, 2) AS returned_share_pct FROM sold JOIN ret USING (format) ORDER BY CASE sold.format WHEN 'Large' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 2 of FY2025/26 (2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22, from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar)
Net sales and refunds both in EUR excluding VAT (net_amount and refund_net)
Store format taken from dim_store through the store_key on the original sales line (the store version at the sale date)
Returns linked to the sales line they came from (sales_line_id)
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Training store (999) and web shop (900) are not stores and are excluded; the web shop has no store format
assumptions: Today is 2026-10-06, which falls in FY2026/27, so 'last year' means FY2025/26 and 'period 2' means fiscal period 2, not calendar month 2.
'What share of what was sold came back' is read as the EUR value (excluding VAT) of refunds on lines sold in the period, divided by the net value sold in the period.

Returns are counted whenever they happened, so a line sold in the period and returned in July still counts. The longest gap between sale and return is 34 days, and the warehouse holds returns well past the period (to at least 2025-07-23), so the cohort is complete.
Staff purchases are left out because they are a different kind of sale, with a much lower return rate (about 2%). Including them changes the figures by less than 0.05 percentage points.
The web shop is reported separately in the caveats and not as a store format row.
caveats: Format labels in dim_store are Large, Medium and Small, but the column comment says Hyper, Standard or Express. I used the labels the data carries. The mapping to the comment's names is not documented.
Training store 999 (format 'Training') has sales in the period, 2,222 EUR net. I excluded it because it is not a trading store.

The web shop (format 'Web') is excluded from the split. Its returned share for the same period and basis is 12.23% (22,388 EUR refunded on 183,102 EUR sold), well above the stores. A total across all channels would therefore be higher than the three rows suggest.

Returns are attributed to the format of the store where the item was sold, not where it was returned. 156 of the 2,514 returns tied to this period (sales or refunds in it) were booked at a different store version than the sale. Using the return's own store_key would move some refunds between formats.

A booked-in-period basis (refunds booked in P2 divided by sales in P2, as the daily store sales report does) gives a different answer: Large 5.36%, Medium 5.26%, Small 4.48%. It includes refunds on sales from earlier periods and staff purchases, so it is not the share of what was sold in the period.
Several store attributes changed on 2025-04-28 (the Capital Region stores moved from South). That affects region only, not format, so the format split is unaffected.
Row counts: 53,094 sales lines in the period (784 staff purchases excluded), with no duplicate sales lines or return lines found and no returns without a matching sale.
