answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open, outside refit closures (ref_store_closure) and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day = false)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) left out
Test articles (category ZZ Test) left out; staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P2 = weeks 5-8, Monday 1 June to Sunday 28 June 2026
Store names and format taken from the current dim_store version
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Store ranking' read as the company store league table, ranked by net sales per trading day (the only store ranking the metric dictionary defines), not by total net sales
'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2 (1 to 28 June 2026), since the request was received on 7 October 2026 and FY2026/27 is the current fiscal year; the period is fully loaded
Rank 1 is the highest net sales per trading day; per-day figures are rounded to whole euros and ranks are on the unrounded figures
Net sales per trading day is in EUR excluding VAT
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it is ranked on its 14 trading days (1 to 14 June) against 26 for every other store; its rank (7th) rests on a shorter and different stretch of the period
The period has 26 trading days for a full-period store: Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed days and are not counted
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and had no trading in the period, so it is not listed; the list has 38 stores
Mikkeli and Espoo Lommila both show 947 after rounding; Mikkeli ranks 23rd and Espoo Lommila 24th on the unrounded figures

Store-level net sales agree to the cent with rpt_daily_store_sales for all 38 stores over 1 to 28 June 2026, and there were no duplicate sales lines, no sales on closed days and no sales in Kuopio's closure
No corrections to the data were needed. The deprecated rpt.v_daily_sales view and the bak_/stg_/tmp_ tables were not used

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, p.subcategory, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE p.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, p.subcategory
definitions_applied: Garden Furniture = dim_product.subcategory 'Garden Furniture' (category Garden), joined through the product_key on the return line
Returned units = SUM(quantity_returned) from fact_return_line, one row per returned line
Fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 = 3 Aug 2026 to 30 Aug 2026 (ref_fiscal_calendar, fully loaded)
Return date = fact_return_line.return_date, mapped to the fiscal period through dim_date
assumptions: 'This year' is the current fiscal year FY2026/27, because the request was received on 5 Oct 2026 and period language is fiscal. Period 4 of the previous fiscal year (28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025) was not used.
'Handed back and booked as returned' is read as units booked on return lines (quantity_returned) in the period, as a gross count of returned units, not net of resales and not a refund value.
All return reasons, store returns and web returns (home delivery and click-and-collect) are included, because each is a booked return of the goods.
The period is assigned by the date the return was booked (return_date), not the date of the original sale. Several of the returns relate to sales made in July 2026.
caveats: No correction was needed. I found no duplicate return lines or return lines without a matching sale. I found no returns dated before their sale, and no gaps in the daily return load for the period. The staging table stg_return_line_load only repeats rows that are already in fact_return_line, so it adds nothing.

Garden Furniture was not affected by the October 2025 reclassification of Outdoor Lighting from Garden to Electrical. Outdoor Lighting is excluded from this figure, and it would not have been counted under either classification.

The 92 units come from 92 return lines of 1 unit each: 37 changed mind, 20 defective, 14 not as described, 14 wrong size or fit and 7 damaged in transit. 41 of the 92 units were booked at the web shop (store_key 46), the rest in physical stores. These splits are not requested and are not shown in the result. One return was on a staff purchase and it is included.

The warehouse has no field showing whether goods were physically handed back, so 'damaged_in_transit' returns are included on the basis that they are booked as returns (7 units). Excluding them would give 85.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Prior-year comparator lined up by fiscal week number, not by calendar date
Whole fiscal weeks, Monday to Sunday
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'This year' is read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27. The request arrived on 7 October 2026.
'Period 2' is FY2026/27 P2, fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (1 to 28 June 2026). The period is fully loaded; the warehouse runs through 4 October 2026.
'Same weeks last year' is FY2025/26 fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (26 May to 22 June 2025), the same fiscal week numbers. This follows the company's week-aligned comparison rule.
Neither period contains week 53, so no week was dropped.
Growth percentage is this year over last year minus 1, rounded to 1 decimal.
Net sales are in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: Midsummer falls in different fiscal weeks in the two years. In 2025 Midsummer Eve and Day (20 and 21 June) fell in FY2025/26 week 8. In 2026 (19 and 20 June) they fell in FY2026/27 week 7. The stores are shut on those days, so week 7 this year (-32.2%) and week 8 (+76.4%) are distorted. They compare a Midsummer week with a normal week. Week 7 this year is a Midsummer week against a normal last-year week 7. Week 8 this year is a normal week against last year's Midsummer week. I kept the fiscal-week alignment because it is the company rule, so these two growth figures are not underlying trends.

Over the whole period, net sales were 1,294,647.64 this year against 1,195,882.70 last year, which is +8.3%. The Midsummer effect cancels out in this total. I did not add it as a row because the request asked for weekly figures.

Duplicate sales lines exist in the warehouse: 418 receipt_id and line_no keys appear twice, with identical values and a second load on 23 September 2025. They all fall on 15 to 21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 week 21), outside the weeks used here, so no correction was needed.
Daily totals match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total exactly for all 56 days in both years, with store 999 excluded on both sides.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales. They leave out web sales from 3 November 2025. They would not affect June 2025 or June 2026 here, but I avoided them anyway.

answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
by_category AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d     ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current
    WHERE cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
      AND ((d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 8) 
           OR (d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period = 8))
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)
SELECT fiscal_year, category, net_sales
FROM by_category
ORDER BY fiscal_year DESC, category
definitions_applied: Net sales (net amount excluding VAT, after returns)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Returns reduce net sales on return date
Current product version (as-is reporting)
assumptions: 'Period 8 last year' interpreted as FY2025/26 P8 (2025-11-24 to 2025-12-21)
'Period 8 the year before' interpreted as FY2024/25 P8 (2024-11-25 to 2024-12-22)
Growth calculated as (FY2025/26 - FY2024/25) / FY2024/25 * 100
Reported as-is (current product hierarchy); Electrical now includes outdoor lighting (moved April 2025)
caveats: Both periods are fully loaded and complete in the warehouse
Period 8 is a standard 4-week period in both years, not affected by week 53

),
returns_of_q1_sales AS (

assumptions: Last year refers to fiscal year FY2025/26 (the previous completed fiscal year from the request date of 2026-10-06)
Q1 runs from 2025-04-28 to 2025-07-27 (the three fiscal periods that comprise Q1 of FY2025/26)
Return rate is calculated using unit quantities (not refund amounts)
Returns are counted regardless of when they were returned, so long as the original sale was in Q1

answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
  SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key,
         CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
  FROM fact_web_order
  WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')
)
SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN w.order_member_key IS NOT NULL THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(f.net_amount), 2) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct
FROM fact_sales_line f
JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date
WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales, guest web orders counted as non-member
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (fact_web_order dispatch_ts_utc converted from UTC), not on sale_date
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders have sales lines)
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Net amounts excluding VAT, before returns
Fiscal calendar periods taken from dim_date (P9 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, P10 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026, P11 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026)
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_ or bak_ tables
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the previous fiscal year (current year is FY2026/27), consistent with how requests in May 2026 and later were read. P9 to P11 are therefore FY2025/26 P9 to P11.
'Share of web sales from loyalty members' read as member net sales before returns divided by all web net sales, per the member-share definition (not net of returns).
Whole periods P9, P10 and P11 are all complete in the warehouse, so no part-period issue.
A web order counts as a member order when fact_web_order carries a member_key (login_state logged_in); this was used in place of the member_key on the sales lines for the reason given in the caveats.
No control total against rpt_daily_store_sales was run, because that check does not apply to a member subset.
caveats: Data problem corrected: 655 logged-in web orders (all their lines) have a NULL member_key on fact_sales_line, although fact_web_order carries a valid member_key for them. They were placed between 9 Feb and 1 Mar 2026, so they fall in P10 and P11. Taking the member from the line would count them as non-members and understate the share. I took the member from fact_web_order.member_key instead; all those member keys exist in dim_member.

Size of the correction: using line member_key alone would give 51.77% for P10 (instead of 67.52%) and 55.81% for P11 (instead of 66.70%). P9 is unaffected (67.99% either way). The source of the missing keys is an ETL issue on the sales lines (loaded 10 Feb to 2 Mar 2026) and should be fixed upstream.

Web net sales (EUR excl. VAT, before returns, ZZ Test excluded) were 219,929.50 in P9, 137,569.07 in P10 and 149,798.62 in P11. P9 is a 5-week period and P10 and P11 are 4 weeks each, so P9 is larger.
Figures are before returns, so they are not directly comparable with net sales after returns.
Result is store 900 only; no store 999 or test-article lines were included.

answer.sql:
SELECT 
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY fy25.fiscal_week) AS week_number,
  ROUND(fy25.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26,
  ROUND(fy24.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25,
  ROUND((fy25.net_sales - fy24.net_sales) / fy24.net_sales * 100, 1) AS growth_pct
FROM (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_week,
    SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_week
) fy25
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_week,
    SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_week
) fy24 ON fy25.fiscal_week = fy24.fiscal_week
ORDER BY fy25.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net_amount from fact_sales_line (sales net of line discounts, excluding VAT)
Fiscal period 2: May 26 – June 22, 2025 (FY2025/26); May 27 – June 23, 2024 (FY2024/25)
Weekly aggregation: One row per fiscal week within period 2 (weeks 5–8 per fiscal calendar)
Growth: Year-over-year percentage change, calculated as (2025/26 sales – 2024/25 sales) / 2024/25 sales × 100
assumptions: Total company sales includes all sales channels (store and web) and all customer types (members and non-members)
Staff purchases are included in the totals
Growth percentage rounded to one decimal place
All sales line data in fact_sales_line is included; no filtering by business units or store types
caveats: Week 4 (week ending June 22) includes Midsummer Eve (June 20–21, 2025) and Midsummer Day (June 21–22, 2024), both marked as non-trading days. Physical stores are closed on these dates; the lower sales in week 4 reflect holiday closure. Online and residual sales continue on these dates.
Growth percentages are calculated on net sales before any return deductions. Refunds in fact_return_line are not netted against sales revenue in this query.

answer.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT web_order_id) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', timezone('UTC', order_ts_utc)) AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01' AND status <> 'cancelled'
definitions_applied: Web shop order = one row in fact_web_order (home delivery and click-and-collect both count)
Order date taken in Finnish local time (Europe/Helsinki), the same day boundary the sales lines use for sale_date
Cancelled orders excluded, as they have no sales lines
Orders counted by distinct web_order_id
assumptions: Cyber Monday is read as Monday 1 December 2025, as the request states
'Web shop orders' means orders that went through, so cancelled orders are not counted; processing orders would be included but there were none that day
Both fulfilment types are included: 239 home delivery and 87 click-and-collect
Guest and logged-in orders are both included
caveats: Order timestamps in fact_web_order are in UTC. Counting by the UTC calendar date gives 291 non-cancelled orders (310 including cancelled), which is wrong for a Finnish business day. The local-time day runs from 22:00 UTC on 30 November to 22:00 UTC on 1 December, and 326 is the figure on that basis. This corrects a shortfall of 35 orders.
If cancelled orders should also count as orders placed, the figure is 345 (19 cancelled orders on the day).

Click-and-collect lines in fact_sales_line have a null channel_code (only channel_id = 3 identifies them), so a filter on channel_code = 'WB', as used in the rpt.v_daily_sales view, would miss them. I counted from fact_web_order and did not use that view or filter.

The 326 orders match the web order lines in fact_sales_line for 1 December 2025 (239 home delivery and 87 click-and-collect), so the two tables agree. 1 December 2025 is a normal trading day with no holiday flag.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, params.fiscal_period AS fiscal_period, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS lfl_net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS lfl_net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM params JOIN lfl_sales ty ON ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores for the period against the same fiscal weeks last year, aligned on fiscal week number (weeks 14 to 17 in both years)
LFL store base: physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop is excluded
Opening rule: a store counts only if it opened at least 364 days before the first day of the period (3 August 2026)
Store-week rule: a store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open, not closed, no refit closure in ref_store_closure)
Week 53 never counts as LFL (not in range here)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded; staff purchases included
As-is store hierarchy (current dim_store version)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: period 4 is fiscal weeks 14 to 17
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' read as FY2026/27 P4 (3 to 30 August 2026, fiscal weeks 14 to 17), the P4 of the current fiscal year as of the request date of 5 October 2026. It is complete and fully loaded.
'Last year' read as the same fiscal weeks 14 to 17 of FY2025/26 (28 July to 24 August 2025), aligned on fiscal week number, not calendar dates.
'The stores' read as the whole LFL store base, so one total row with no breakdown by region or store.
Growth is reported in percent units and sales in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: LFL net sales are essentially flat: EUR 1,010,478.52 this year against EUR 1,010,743.32 last year, a change of -0.03%, about EUR 265 lower.

38 stores are in the LFL base (152 store-weeks). Savonlinna (129) is excluded because it closed on 25 January 2026 and did not trade in P4 this year, so it is out of the base. This is why the LFL base has 38 of the 39 stores that traded in P4 last year.

Kuopio (125) is in the base: its refit ran 15 June to 26 July 2026 and ended before P4 began. Pori's (119) refit ran 8 September to 12 October 2025, after P4 last year, so it does not affect this comparison.

Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in September and November 2024. They count as LFL because they were open more than 364 days before P4, although last year's P4 was still within their first year of trading.
The result matches rpt_daily_store_sales for all physical stores on all 28 days of both periods, with a gap of 0.00 on every week and no store-day differing.

I found 418 duplicated sales lines (same receipt_id and line_no, different sales_line_id, identical content, loaded again in September 2025). They all fall in FY2025/26 week 21, so none is in P4 or in this comparison, and no correction was needed.
The web shop (store 900) is not included, because LFL covers physical stores only, so this figure says nothing about web sales.
Regional LFL (not requested) varied a lot: North +6.53%, Capital Region +2.79%, South -0.71%, West -1.65%, East -3.13%. Weekly sales for individual small stores swing widely from year to year.

answer.sql: SELECT s.format, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(r.quantity_returned, 0)) / SUM(f.quantity), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 GROUP BY s.format ORDER BY s.format

Returns matched to sales by sales_line_id

Period 2 is fiscal period 2, not calendar month 2

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS new_members FROM dim_member WHERE join_date = DATE '2026-10-03'
