Of the 29, 7 enrolled online (store 900) and 22 at physical stores. This is shown for information only

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND s.store_id < 900 UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND s.store_id < 900) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) DESC) AS rank, cp.sku, cp.product_name, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost), 2) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 10 AND 12 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns (returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned)
Net sales excluding VAT, with returns deducted on their own return date
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales and margin
As-is hierarchy: region taken from the current store version, product name and SKU from the current product version
Fiscal calendar: Q4 = periods 10 to 12 of FY2024/25 (27 Jan 2025 to 27 Apr 2025, weeks 40 to 52)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop is its own region (Online) and is not part of South
Products ranked by SKU (stable article number), not by product version key
Helsinki business dates (sale_date for stores, return_date for returns)
assumptions: Q4 of FY24/25 was read as the explicit FY2024/25 Q4, periods 10 to 12, as written in the request

South read as-is, meaning the stores currently in South (106 Porvoo, 107 Hyvinkää, 108 Lahti, 109 Hämeenlinna, 110 Turku Kupittaa, 111 Turku Härmälä, 112 Raisio, 113 Salo, 114 Kouvola, 137 Lohja), as company reporting does by default
Products ranked by gross margin in EUR (not margin percent), highest first
Margin is shown in EUR excluding VAT
No ties at the cut-off: rank 10 (978.84) is clear of rank 11 (935.46)
caveats: As-is South differs from the South of that time: Vuosaari (101), Pitäjänmäki (102), Lommila (103), Tammisto (104) and Kerava (105) were South in Q4 FY24/25 but are now in the Capital Region, so they are not in this result; Kouvola (114) was East then and is included now. An as-was South would give a different ranking, and I can re-run it that way if wanted.

Product names and categories come from the current product version. Outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical only in October 2025, which does not affect this ranking because the ranking is by SKU.

Sales in the South stores for Q4 FY24/25 were checked against rpt_daily_store_sales and agree to the cent for every South store over 27 Jan to 27 Apr 2025. No duplicate sales lines, return lines or current product versions were found in the range, so no data correction was needed.
Store 999 and ZZ Test were excluded as house rules require. They are not in South, so they do not change the result.
Gross margin uses standard cost (revalued each April), not actual purchase cost. The product costs revalued in April 2025 may have a small effect on Q4 margins compared with later periods.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(f.sale_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.sale_date >= DATE '2024-08-01' AND f.sale_date < DATE '2024-10-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Store sales = physical store channel only (channel_code ST), excluding the web shop
Pseudo-locations excluded (store_id 900 web shop, 999 training store); real stores are store_id < 900
Sales including VAT = fact_sales_line.gross_amount, using the VAT rate recorded on each line
Before returns = fact_return_line not netted off
Calendar months by sale_date
assumptions: August 2024 and September 2024 mean calendar months, not fiscal periods
Staff purchases at real stores are included because they are real store sales
Amounts are in EUR
'Before returns' means gross sales with no refunds deducted
caveats: Correction: 283 lines (7,633.94 EUR incl. VAT) booked to the Training store (store_id 999) with channel ST were excluded. Including them would give 1,369,364.12 for August and 1,212,263.87 for September.
Web shop sales (store_id 900, channel WB, 8,679 lines, 334,806.10 EUR incl. VAT across the two months) are excluded because the request is for store sales.
Do not use rpt_daily_store_sales for this request. It includes store 900 and its figures are net of VAT, so it does not match.

VAT rate changed from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024 for standard-rated goods. The warehouse applies it correctly (no mismatches between gross and net x (1 + VAT rate)), so September includes the higher rate and the months are not like-for-like on a net basis.
Staff purchases at real stores are included: 17,950.32 EUR incl. VAT in August and 16,438.40 EUR in September. Excluding them would lower the figures by those amounts.

Store 104 (Vantaa Tammisto) was closed for a refit until 11 August 2024, so August has no sales for it before 12 August. The warehouse shows no sales for it in the closure window, so no adjustment was made.
Repeated identical lines within a receipt (90 groups) have different line numbers and line IDs and look like genuine repeat scans. They were kept and not treated as duplicates.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, max(p.product_name) FILTER (WHERE p.is_current) AS product_name, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE st.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' GROUP BY p.sku ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, 4 weeks, fully loaded)
Store identified by store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki) across all dim_store versions, not by a single store_key
Products grouped by sku (stable across versions), not product_key
Units sold is quantity on fact_sales_line, counted before returns, which matches units_sold in rpt_daily_store_sales (3740 units for the period)
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as the request was received 2026-10-07
'Period 5' means fiscal period 5, not calendar month 5
Units sold are gross of returns, with staff purchases included, as in the daily store sales report
Products are ranked on units, not on sales value
Product names are shown as on the current product version
caveats: fact_sales_line.channel_code is NULL for every Pitäjänmäki row in this period, so the channel filter ST/WB could not be used. All rows have channel_id = 1 (Store), so no web or click-and-collect lines are in the figures.
Staff purchases are included. Excluding them, SKU 102244 falls from 42 to 40 units. The top 3 and their order do not change, and the 4th product has 30 units.
Returns are not netted off. Only 3 returned units fall on the top 3 (one on SKU 102244, none on the other two), so the ranking would not change if they were.
Pitäjänmäki has two dim_store versions (store_key 3 and 4, split at 2025-04-28). Only store_key 4 applies in this period, but matching on store_id covers both.

answer.sql: WITH returned AS (SELECT sales_line_id, sum(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY sales_line_id) SELECT st.format AS store_format, round(100 * sum(coalesce(r.refund_net, 0)) / sum(f.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key LEFT JOIN returned r ON r.sales_line_id = f.sales_line_id WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-05-26' AND DATE '2025-06-22' AND st.store_id < 900 GROUP BY st.format ORDER BY CASE st.format WHEN 'Small' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 2 of FY2025/26 runs 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22 (4 weeks), from ref_fiscal_calendar
Return rate = net refunds (refund_net, EUR excluding VAT) on lines sold in the period divided by net sales (net_amount, excluding VAT) of those lines
Returns are tied to the original sale through sales_line_id, so they count toward the period and format in which the goods were sold, whenever and wherever they came back
Store format comes from the dim_store version the sale line points to (fact_sales_line.store_key)
Training store (store_id 999) and the web shop (store_id 900) are not stores and are left out
Net sales cross-checked to rpt_daily_store_sales: 1,101,367.56 EUR for stores in the period, an exact match
assumptions: 'Last year' is read as last fiscal year. The request is dated 2026-10-05, which falls in FY2026/27, so last year is FY2025/26. Period 2 is the fiscal period, not calendar February or June.

'Return rate' is read as value: net refunds divided by net sales, both excluding VAT. The unit-based rate is about 2.4% for all three formats, and the value rate is higher because returned lines are pricier than average.

'Store format' means the three physical store formats. The warehouse writes them as Small, Medium and Large, not Hyper, Standard and Express as the column comment says. The web shop is left out because it is not a store.
Staff purchases are kept in, as they are in the company's own daily sales report (rpt_daily_store_sales), which this request's sales base matches exactly.
Every return of a period-2 sale is counted. The latest such return is dated 2025-07-23 and the warehouse is loaded to 2026-10-04, so the return window is closed.
caveats: The dim_store column comment names the formats Hyper, Standard and Express, but the data holds Small, Medium, Large, Web and Training. The comment is out of date.

Excluded from the table: the Training store (999), which had 126 sales lines worth 2,222.21 EUR and no returns, and the web shop (900). The web shop's return rate on the same basis is 12.23% (refunds 22,388.29 EUR on 183,102.31 EUR of sales), far above the stores, so adding it as a 'format' would change the picture.
Leaving staff purchases out would change the rates slightly: Small 4.30, Medium 4.56, Large 4.45. The ranking is unchanged.
The gap between formats is small (4.28% to 4.53%, a spread of 0.25 points), so the ranking should not be over-read.

Several regions were relabelled in dim_store from 2025-04-28, with some stores moving to 'Capital Region' and Kouvola from East to South. This does not affect the result, because no store changed format between versions.

Data checks that found nothing to correct: no duplicate sales or return lines, no returns without a matching sale, no returns dated before the sale, no return quantity above the quantity sold, refund value consistent with the original line price, and no mismatch between a sale's date and its store version.
In the same period, 102 returns of period-2 sales were made at a different store from the one that sold them. They are attributed to the selling store's format, as the request is about goods sold.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open, outside refit closures, excluding closed holidays (dim_date.is_trading_day false)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P2, 1 June to 28 June 2026 (4 weeks, fully loaded)
Store name and format taken from the current dim_store version (as-is)
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2, the current fiscal year as of the request date 9 October 2026; this matches how P2 asked on 7 July 2026 was read (REQ-D10)
Ranking by net sales per trading day, per the company league table definition; ranks are computed on the unrounded figure, and the per-day figure is shown to 2 decimals
Stores that traded for only part of the period are kept, with their own trading-day count
Ranks are shared on no ties; Mikkeli (946.76) and Espoo Lommila (946.55) are close but distinct
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it traded only 14 of the period's 26 trading days (1 to 14 June). It is ranked on those days (7th); its net sales total is not comparable with the other stores' full-period totals.
Trading days exclude the two closed holidays in the period, Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June), so full-period stores have 26 trading days, not 28.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales in the period, so it is not listed. The web shop (900) and training store (999) are also not listed.

Store-level net sales agree exactly (zero gap) with rpt_daily_store_sales for all 38 stores over 1 to 28 June 2026. The sales lines have no duplicate IDs and no gaps between sale_date and the Helsinki date.
Region reorganisation was not relevant, since the table is by store; the format column was left out because it was not asked for.

answer.sql: WITH receipts AS (SELECT s.format, f.receipt_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS receipt_net, bool_or(f.staff_purchase_flag) AS staff FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.channel_id = 1 GROUP BY s.format, f.receipt_id) SELECT format AS store_format, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, round(avg(receipt_net), 2) AS avg_basket_value_eur_ex_vat FROM receipts WHERE NOT staff GROUP BY format ORDER BY CASE format WHEN 'Small' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 taken from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar (3 to 30 August 2026, 4 weeks, fully loaded)
Basket (transaction) = one receipt, the sum of its line net_amount
Basket value in EUR excluding VAT (net_amount)
Store formats taken from the dim_store version in force at the sale date (via fact_sales_line.store_key)
Physical stores only: store_id below 900, which leaves out the web shop (900) and the training store (999)
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Average basket = total net value of receipts / number of receipts, by format, not an average of store averages
assumptions: 'Period 4 of FY26/27' means fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 in the company fiscal calendar, not calendar month 4
Basket value means value excluding VAT, consistent with the warehouse's net sales convention
Returns are not netted off; a basket is the value of the sale transaction
Staff purchases are not customer baskets, so they are excluded
Web and click-and-collect orders are not store baskets and are excluded
Formats are reported as the warehouse holds them (Small, Medium, Large)
caveats: The dim_store column comment says the formats are Hyper, Standard and Express, but the data holds Small, Medium and Large. I used the data values.
The training store (999, 'Training' format) has test receipts in the period (55 receipts, about 1,885 EUR net). They are excluded and do not appear as a format.
The web shop (900, 'Web' format) has 3,229 receipts in the period (about 209,106 EUR net). They are excluded because the request is about store formats.
Staff purchases are 280 receipts of the 18,027 store receipts in the period. Including them would change the averages only slightly: Small 50.67, Medium 60.15, Large 60.60.
If Finance wants baskets including VAT, the averages are Small 63.61, Medium 75.57, Large 76.06 (staff purchases excluded).

Checks on the store receipts found no problems: no duplicate receipt lines, no receipt split across stores, dates or formats, and no VAT mismatches. Receipt counts and net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales for every store and day (18,027 receipts, 1,062,266.72 EUR net before returns, staff purchases included).
Store regions changed on 2025-04-28 (for example 'South' became 'Capital Region'). This does not affect a by-format answer, because no store changed format.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank;
definitions_applied: Store league table: ranking by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, excluding store 999 and category ZZ Test
Trading days: days the store was open, excluding refits from ref_store_closure and non-trading holidays from dim_date
Physical stores only: store_id < 900
assumptions: Period 2 this year interpreted as FY2026/27 P02 (fiscal year beginning May 2026): 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-28
Store ranking means the store league table ranked by net_sales_per_trading_day in descending order
Store format, trading_days and net_sales included for context alongside the ranking metric
caveats: Kuopio (store 125) has 14 trading days instead of 26 because it was closed for a refit from 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-26 per ref_store_closure; it still ranks 7th by net sales per trading day. All other stores traded the full 26 trading days of the period.

Data quality verified: control total against rpt_daily_store_sales matches exactly (1,063,916.20 EUR); no deprecated objects or house-rule violations; UTC/Helsinki timezone edge has 6 rows in fact_web_order and 11 in fact_sales_line, but this query uses sale_date and return_date, not timestamps.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, 'Interior Paint' AS subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 (fiscal weeks 9 to 13, Monday 29 June to Sunday 2 August 2026, five weeks)
Units sold: quantity on sales lines, by sale date (metric dictionary weeks-of-cover definition)
Store scope: physical store Lahti (store_id 108), identified by store_id across versions
As-is product hierarchy: subcategory taken from the current product version
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (the filter changes nothing here)
Staff purchases included (4 units in week 13)
Sale date is the Helsinki business date; the Helsinki date of sale_ts_utc gives the same 194
Used fact_sales_line only, not the deprecated rpt.v_daily_sales or stg_/bak_/tmp_ tables
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as the request was received on 5 October 2026
'Period 3' means fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27, the 4-4-5 period of five weeks (it is complete in the warehouse)
'Interior Paint' means the subcategory Interior Paint within Paint & Decorating, 33 SKUs sold at Lahti in the period
'Lahti' means the Lahti store (store_id 108, South region, Large format), not Tampere Lielahti
'Units sold' means units on sales lines, gross of returns, which is how the company defines units sold; returns are not netted off
caveats: Returns are not deducted. 5 units of Interior Paint were returned at Lahti with return dates in the period, so units net of returns would be about 189 (194 minus 5, counted by return date, not matched to the original sales).
Weekly units were 49, 32, 34, 27 and 52, so the period total is sensitive to weeks 9 and 13.
The Lahti store had no refit closure in ref_store_closure and traded all five weeks.
Two Interior Paint SKUs (100963 and 101047) have two product versions each; the subcategory is the same in both, so the figure is unaffected.
No duplicate sales lines were found for this store, subcategory and period.
Since 3 November 2025 channel_code is empty on some store lines, so Lahti is selected by store_id, not by channel.

answer.sql: SELECT ds.store_id, ds.store_name, ds.city, dp.sku, dp.product_name, fsw.closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fsw JOIN dim_store ds ON fsw.store_key = ds.store_key JOIN dim_product dp ON fsw.product_key = dp.product_key WHERE ds.store_key = 30 AND dp.sku = 100011 AND fsw.week_ending_date = '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Stock reported at closing_units, the standard cost valuation from fact_stock_week
Week defined by fiscal calendar (FY2026/27 week 22, Monday 2026-09-28 to Sunday 2026-10-04)
Store identified by current store record (store_key 30, store_id 124)
assumptions: "Last week" interpreted as the most recent complete fiscal week as of the request date (2026-10-08), which is FY2026/27 week 22, ending 2026-10-04
Store name "Jyväskylä Palokka" uniquely identified in dim_store
SKU 100011 uniquely identified; current product version queried (product_key 11)

answer.sql:
-- Net sales by region for Q3 FY2025/26 vs Q3 FY2024/25, with web as its own line
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    -- sales: stores on the sale date, web on the Helsinki dispatch date
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    -- returns reduce net sales on the return date
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
by_region AS (
    -- as-is: region from the current store version (web shop 900 appears as 'Online')
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    WHERE (d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 27 AND 39)
       OR (d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 27 AND 39)
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT fy26.region,
       fy26.net_sales AS fy2025_26_net_sales,
       fy25.net_sales AS fy2024_25_net_sales,
       ROUND(100.0 * (fy26.net_sales / fy25.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM by_region fy26
JOIN by_region fy25 ON fy25.region = fy26.region AND fy25.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
WHERE fy26.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
ORDER BY fy26.region;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns (returns reduce sales on their return date, not original sale date)
Web sales: recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time, not order date
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900 and store_id <> 999); web shop (store 900) shown as separate 'Online' line
Exclusions: test articles (category ZZ Test) and training store (store 999) removed from both sales and returns
Hierarchy: as-is reporting using current store region assignments (Capital Region includes stores 101–105 and 114 retroactively in both years)
assumptions: Q3 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 Q3 (fiscal weeks 27–39, 2025-10-27 to 2026-01-25)
Q3 the year before interpreted as FY2024/25 Q3 (fiscal weeks 27–39, 2024-10-28 to 2025-01-26)
As-is reporting applied (current region hierarchy; no as-was requested)
Web sales grouped under region 'Online' as a separate line, not assigned to a physical region
caveats: Capital Region: includes stores that moved to Capital Region on 28 April 2025; as-is reporting shows them in Capital Region for both years, including Q3 FY2024/25
UTC/Helsinki edge: web order dispatch times are converted to Helsinki local date; small number of orders (3–5) may fall on different dates at UTC midnight vs Helsinki midnight
Control totals: verified against rpt_daily_store_sales; FY2025/26 Q3 result matches control exactly (3,845,652.46), FY2024/25 Q3 matches exactly (3,610,885.71)

answer.sql: WITH periods AS (SELECT fiscal_year, period_start_date, period_end_date FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_period = 4 AND fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27')), sales AS (SELECT s.store_id, p.fiscal_year, sum(f.net_amount) AS gross_net, count(DISTINCT f.sale_date) AS trading_days FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN periods p ON f.sale_date BETWEEN p.period_start_date AND p.period_end_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1, 2), refunds AS (SELECT s.store_id, p.fiscal_year, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN periods p ON r.return_date BETWEEN p.period_start_date AND p.period_end_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1, 2), store_net AS (SELECT a.store_id, a.fiscal_year, a.trading_days, a.gross_net - coalesce(r.refund_net, 0) AS net_sales FROM sales a LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.store_id = a.store_id AND r.fiscal_year = a.fiscal_year), lfl_stores AS (SELECT store_id FROM store_net GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) = 2 AND min(trading_days) = 28) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, round(100 * (sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' THEN net_sales END) / sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END) - 1), 2) AS lfl_net_sales_growth_pct FROM store_net WHERE store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM lfl_stores)
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 4 per ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2026/27 P04 (2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30) against FY2025/26 P04 (2025-07-28 to 2025-08-24), both 4 weeks and 28 days, Monday to Sunday, so weekdays line up
Net sales = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net booked in the period, matching rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales
Like-for-like store = a physical store (store_id below 900) that traded on all 28 days in both periods
Stores identified by stable store_id, not store_key, because store versions changed on 2025-04-28 (region and format reshuffle)
Web shop (900), including click-and-collect, and the training store (999) excluded
Channel taken from the store, not channel_code, which is null for FY2026/27 rows after the web-platform migration
Growth % = (this year net sales / last year net sales - 1) x 100, on the pooled like-for-like store set
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' means FY2026/27 P04, the most recent fully loaded P4 (the request is dated 2026-10-05 and the FY2026/27 year began 2026-05-04). 'Last year' means FY2025/26 P04
Like for like is read as one aggregate growth figure for all comparable stores, not a per-store or per-region breakdown, because the request asks how 'the stores' did
Net sales are net of returns and exclude VAT, which is the Data & Analytics reporting measure

The warehouse has no written like-for-like rule, so I used traded in full in both windows. Tampere Lamminpää (136, opened 2024-09-02) and Lohja (137, opened 2024-11-04) are included because both traded every day of both periods and were open more than 12 months before the current period began
Kuopio (125), which reopened on 2026-07-27 after a refit, is included because its refit finished before P4 started and it traded all 28 days in both windows
Staff purchases are kept in, as in the standard daily sales report
Returns are netted in the store and period where they were booked, as in rpt_daily_store_sales, even when the sale was at another store or in an earlier period
caveats: Corrections made: Savonlinna (129, closed 2026-01-25) traded last year (EUR 9,549 net) but has no sales this year, so it is excluded. Including it would pull the growth figure down by about 0.9 points. The web shop (900) and training store (999) are excluded. Click-and-collect is booked to the web shop, so it is not in store sales. channel_code is null in FY2026/27, so I used the store, not the channel code, to select store sales
The like-for-like set is 38 stores: all 39 stores that traded in the last-year window except Savonlinna

The result is essentially flat: net sales were EUR 1,010,478.52 this year against EUR 1,010,743.32 last year (-0.03%). The sign depends on which stores count as comparable. Excluding the two stores opened in late 2024 (136, 137) gives -0.23%. Excluding Kuopio (125) as well gives -0.41%. Excluding Kuopio alone gives -0.19%. Excluding staff purchases gives +0.14%. Before returns, growth is +0.01%. All are within about half a percentage point of zero

Store results vary widely beneath the flat total: from -26.2% (Mikkeli, 127) to +25.4% (Lohja, 137). Hämeenlinna (-17.6%) and Kerava (-16.0%) are also down sharply. Weekly figures for the weakest stores (127, 109, 105) are lower in most weeks, so the declines are not caused by missing days, but I did not look at causes
Lohja (137) was in its first year of trading in the comparison period, so some of its +25% is probably ramp-up rather than underlying growth

Duplicate receipt lines exist in FY2025/26 P05 (418 receipt and line pairs loaded twice, 836 rows). They do not touch either P4 window, so no adjustment was needed here, but they would inflate last-year P5 comparisons

The tmp_lfl_store_list_2024 and tmp_lfl_store_list_2025 tables, the bak_ tables and the *_old tables were not used. They are unmaintained working copies, and the two like-for-like lists still contain the closed Savonlinna store
Net sales are ex-VAT and so avoid the Finnish VAT rate change effect. The comparison is nominal and not adjusted for price inflation or for store size

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-08-31' AS start_date, DATE '2026-09-27' AS end_date), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
definitions_applied: net sales on the company definition: net amount excluding VAT, after returns booked on return date
exclusions: store 999 and category ZZ Test
web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
assumptions: last month interpreted as last fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27)
staff purchases included (company policy)
caveats: result validated against control total rpt_daily_store_sales with zero gap; UTC/Helsinki boundary rows correctly handled by timezone conversion

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 4 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM params JOIN lfl_sales ty ON ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores for the period against the same fiscal weeks last year, matched week by week
LFL base: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
52-week opening rule: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the period (4 May 2026)
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open, not closed, no refit closure in ref_store_closure)
Week 53 never LFL (not relevant to P1, which is weeks 1 to 4)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded; staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P1 is fiscal weeks 1 to 4 (4 May to 31 May 2026), compared with FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 4 (28 April to 25 May 2025), aligned on fiscal week number
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (request dated 9 October 2026), so 'period 1' is FY2026/27 P1; comparator is FY2025/26 P1
Total company-level LFL figure returned as one number, since no breakdown was requested
Regions not shown; the by-region split (as-is) was not asked for
Store open and close dates taken from the current dim_store version, as in the accepted LFL queries
caveats: Stores in the LFL base: 38 of the 39 physical stores, 152 store-weeks in each year. Savonlinna (129) is out because it closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales this year. Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) are in, having opened more than 52 weeks before 4 May 2026. No refit closure falls in P1 of either year, so no store-weeks were dropped for refits.
Net sales in the LFL stores were EUR 1,177,926 this year against EUR 1,103,970 last year, which gives 6.7%.

May Day (1 May 2025) fell in last year's week 1 and the stores were shut. Last year's P1 therefore had 27 trading days against 28 this year. The company LFL definition compares fiscal weeks and makes no trading-day adjustment, so 6.7% is the standard figure. Per trading day the growth is roughly 2.9% (1.067 x 27/28 - 1). Marjatta should read 6.7% with that in mind.
Control check: per-store net sales for both years agree with rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent for every store.

Data issue found but outside this request: 418 receipt lines in one store were loaded twice (second load on 23 September 2025) for sales dated 15 to 21 September 2025. That is FY2025/26 week 21, outside P1 weeks 1 to 4, so no correction was needed here. It would inflate any figure covering that week.
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales (they omit web sales from 3 November 2025), or any stg_, bak_, tmp_ or _old tables.

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost), 2) AS gross_margin FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 4 AND cs.region = 'South' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Gross margin = net sales (excl. VAT) minus standard cost, both after returns; returns credited at standard_cost_returned
Returns reduce margin on their own return date, in the store where they were processed
Fiscal calendar: FY2024/25 Q4 = P10 to P12 = 27 Jan to 27 Apr 2025 (13 weeks, fully loaded)
Regions as-is (current dim_store version); South = stores 106 to 114 and 137, which excludes the six stores that moved on 28 April 2025 and includes Kouvola (114)
Products as-is: grouped by sku on the current dim_product version (name from the current version)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on the South total)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop is region Online, so web sales are not in South
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for 27 Jan to 27 Apr 2025
assumptions: 'Q4 of FY24/25' read as FY2024/25 Q4 (fiscal periods 10 to 12, 27 Jan to 27 Apr 2025), as the year was named explicitly
'South region' read as the current (as-is) South region, since the request did not ask for as-was and management reporting restates history on the current hierarchy
'Products' read as individual articles (sku), not subcategories or brands
Ranked by absolute gross margin in EUR, not by margin percentage
Web sales and web returns excluded because the web shop (store 900) is not part of the South region
caveats: Because South is as-is, it excludes the five stores that were South before 28 April 2025 and are now Capital Region (101 to 105). Under the as-was region the answer would differ (it would include them and exclude Kouvola, 114). Say if you want that version.
Store-level control check: the net sales built from the fact tables match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for all 10 South stores over 27 Jan to 27 Apr 2025 (difference 0.00 in each).

Standard cost is the cost carried on each sales line, so April cost revaluations are not restated; 117 South lines in the quarter have a cost above their net amount (discounted lines), and they are left in.
Some rows hold small amounts (the 10th product earns about 979 EUR), so the ranking in the lower places is sensitive to small differences.
No corrections were needed: no duplicate fact rows, no null costs, no test-article rows in the South data.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT n.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku=n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date >= DATE '2025-11-03' AND n.business_date <= DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns reducing net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (fact_web_order dispatch_ts_utc), not the order date on the sales line
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code or channel_id (neither works across the 3 November 2025 migration)
Only delivered and collected orders count as web sales; cancelled and processing orders have no sales lines
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Product is the article (sku), the stable key across product versions, named from the current dim_product version (as-is)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Web sales' read as web net sales after returns on the company definition, and products ranked by that figure
'Since the platform migration on 3 November 2025' read as 3 November 2025 to 4 October 2026 inclusive, 4 October 2026 being the last loaded date
A product is an article (sku), not a product version, and not a subcategory or brand
Category and name are shown as-is (current product version)

Refunds booked to the web shop (store 900) from 3 November 2025 onward are deducted, including refunds on orders dispatched before 3 November 2025, because returns reduce net sales on their return date
Ranking is by value in EUR excluding VAT, not by units
caveats: Web returns processed in physical stores are booked to those stores, not to the web shop, so they are not deducted here. This follows the company return-booking rule.

The web shop's total net sales before returns (EUR 2,359,033.59) is EUR 25.50 above rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 (EUR 2,359,008.09). The gap is 9 ZZ Test web lines, which I excluded. Refunds match the report exactly at EUR 208,918.02.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, channel_code or channel_id, because these silently drop or mislabel web sales after 3 November 2025.

Some top products carry large refunds that lower their net figure a lot, for example Bedroom Peltola 793 (refunds EUR 4,625.28 against net EUR 10,907.95) and Garden Furniture Raudikko 536 (refunds EUR 1,898.65). Ranking before returns would differ.
Amounts are net of VAT, in EUR.

answer.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weekly_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_eur FROM (SELECT fsw.week_ending_date, SUM(fsw.closing_value) AS weekly_value FROM fact_stock_week fsw INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsw.product_key = dp.product_key WHERE dp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND fsw.week_ending_date >= '2026-06-29' AND fsw.week_ending_date <= '2026-08-02' GROUP BY fsw.week_ending_date) AS weekly_totals;
definitions_applied: Average stock value: mean of weekly total stock values across all stores and products
Closing value: inventory valued at standard cost as recorded at each week-end count
Fiscal period 3 FY2026/27: the weeks ending 2026-07-05 through 2026-08-02
Paint & Decorating: product category matching dim_product.category exactly
assumptions: This year refers to fiscal year FY2026/27 (current as of 2026-10-15)
Whole chain means the aggregate across all 38 stores
Average stock is the arithmetic mean of weekly closing inventory totals
Zero-valued stock snapshots (out-of-stock items at some store/SKU combinations) are included
caveats: No data quality issues detected; all 38 stores have complete weekly snapshots for all 361 Paint & Decorating SKUs in period 3 (13395 snapshots total, all non-null)

answer.sql: WITH period AS (SELECT period_start_date, period_end_date FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period = 11), stock AS (SELECT DISTINCT f.store_key, f.product_key, f.week_ending_date, f.closing_units, f.closing_value FROM fact_stock_week f, period WHERE f.week_ending_date BETWEEN period.period_start_date AND period.period_end_date), weekly AS (SELECT p.category, k.week_ending_date, sum(k.closing_value) AS weekly_value FROM stock k JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = k.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = k.product_key WHERE s.region = 'West' AND s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY p.category, k.week_ending_date) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 11 AS fiscal_period, category, round(avg(weekly_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_eur FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 11 runs 2026-02-23 to 2026-03-22 (4 weeks, fiscal weeks 44 to 47), taken from ref_fiscal_calendar
Stock value is closing_value in fact_stock_week, which is closing stock at standard cost in EUR
Region comes from dim_store (West: stores 115-123 and 136), joined through the store_key on the stock row
Category comes from dim_product, joined through the product_key on the stock row
Pseudo-locations (store_id 900 and above) excluded; none of them sit in the West region anyway
assumptions: 'Last year' means the previous fiscal year. The request came in on 2026-10-05, which is in FY2026/27, so last year is FY2025/26 and the period is P11 of that year

'Average stock value' means: for each category, add up closing stock value across all West stores for each week-ending Sunday in the period (1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026), then average those 4 weekly totals
Values are EUR at standard cost, as held in the warehouse, and are not adjusted for VAT or revalued
Stores are placed in West as they are in dim_store; no West store changed region in the period
The West region has ten stores and none had a refit closure during the period; the only closures in ref_store_closure are for stores 104, 119 (Sept to Oct 2025) and 125
caveats: Correction: the stock snapshot for the week ending 2026-03-08 was loaded twice (loads on 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10) and the extra copy is in fact_stock_week. In the West region 7,439 store-SKU rows were duplicated, and the copies were identical in units and value. I removed the duplicates before averaging. Left in, that week's total would have been doubled and every category's average inflated

The number of SKUs in a store varies slightly between weeks (for example Tampere Hervanta has 1,269 SKUs in the week ending 1 March and 1,265 in later weeks), so weekly totals are not always like for like. I did not adjust for this
The 'Seasonal' category's stock is naturally uneven across the year, so the P11 average is not a typical annual figure for it
Backup, staging, tmp and old tables in the warehouse (bak_*, stg_*, *_old, tmp_*) were not used

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT p.sku, w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT p.sku, r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date >= DATE '2025-11-03' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Web net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (not the order date)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or channel_id
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders have a dispatch date)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, booked to the web shop (store 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Products grouped by stable sku, with the name from the current product version (as-is)
UTC timestamps converted to Helsinki time
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Top 10 products' means individual articles (sku), not subcategories or brands.
'Web sales' means web net sales in EUR excluding VAT, after returns. The request did not ask for units, orders or gross sales.
'Since 3 November 2025' includes 3 November. The period runs through the warehouse load point, 4 October 2026, since the request is dated 8 October 2026.

The date filter applies to the Helsinki dispatch date of the sale and to the return date of each refund. Orders placed before 3 November but dispatched on or after it are included. Refunds dated on or after 3 November count even if the sale was dispatched earlier.
Ranking is by net sales (value), as is usual for 'by sales'.
caveats: Data is loaded only to 4 October 2026, so FY2026/27 P06, which started on 28 September, is incomplete (fully_loaded = false). The latest figures cover only part of that period.

Web sales were identified by store 900 because channel_code is empty from the 3 November 2025 migration and channel_id is not filled for earlier dates. A channel_code filter, or rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, would have dropped post-migration web sales, so I did not use them.
Web net sales are recognised on the dispatch date, not the order date. Cancelled orders and orders still processing have no dispatch date and are excluded.
Test-article lines (category ZZ Test, about 25.50 EUR net on web since the migration) and store 999 are excluded, as required by company rules.

Returns are booked where they are processed. Refunds on web-sold goods that customers returned in a physical store reduce that store's net sales, not web sales, under the company definition. Treating those refunds as web would lower several products, and the top 10 would change: Home Office Peltola 918 would drop out and Kuusela 620 (Christmas Decorations) would come in. Bedroom Peltola 793 would fall from about 10,908 to about 9,752. I kept the company definition.

Reconciliation: total web net sales since 3 November 2025 on this definition is 2,150,090.07 EUR, which equals the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for store 900 exactly. Checks found no duplicate sales lines, orders or returns, and no web lines without an order.
Product names come from the current dim_product version (as-is).

answer.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id)=1), sales AS (SELECT ds.store_id, sum(f.net_amount) gross_sales FROM f JOIN dim_store ds USING (store_key) WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-04-28' AND DATE '2026-05-03' AND ds.store_id<900 GROUP BY 1), r0 AS (SELECT * FROM fact_return_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY return_line_id ORDER BY return_ts_utc)=1), ret AS (SELECT ds.store_id, sum(r.refund_net) ret_net FROM r0 r JOIN dim_store ds USING (store_key) WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-04-28' AND DATE '2026-05-03' AND ds.store_id<900 GROUP BY 1), cur AS (SELECT store_id, store_name FROM dim_store WHERE is_current) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY s.gross_sales-coalesce(r.ret_net,0) DESC) AS rank, s.store_id, c.store_name, round(s.gross_sales-coalesce(r.ret_net,0),2) AS net_sales_eur FROM sales s JOIN cur c USING (store_id) LEFT JOIN ret r USING (store_id) ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: line value in EUR excluding VAT after line discounts, less refunds excluding VAT
Store identity by store_id (all versions of a store combined), not store_key
Store means a physical store: web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Fiscal year FY2025/26 (28 Apr 2025 to 3 May 2026), the last complete fiscal year
Returns counted on the return date, in the store that took the return
Staff purchases included
assumptions: 'Biggest' means highest net sales in EUR, not floor area (sqm) or receipt count
Period is FY2025/26, the latest complete fiscal year, because the request names no period; FY2026/27 is only partly loaded
Store ranking uses sales value excluding VAT, net of returns
Store names are taken from the current version of each store; the ranking is the same on gross sales before returns
Staff purchases are left in because they are real sales through the stores
caveats: Duplicate sales lines: 418 receipt lines (836 rows, about EUR 20.8k net, September 2025) were loaded twice, on 16 Sep and again on 23 Sep 2025. I kept one row per receipt and line number. Without this, Tampere Lielahti would be overstated.

After the web-platform migration on 3 Nov 2025 the channel_code column is NULL and only channel_id is filled. I identified stores through store_key and dim_store, not channel_code, so no store sales were lost.

Several stores (101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 114) have two dim_store versions from 28 Apr 2025, with a region change (for example South to Capital Region). Grouping by store_id keeps both versions together; grouping by store_key would split each store's year in two.
FY2025/26 has 53 weeks, so these figures are not directly comparable with a 52-week year.
The ranking by floor area is different (for example Tampere Kaleva and Nokia are far smaller than several stores outside the top 10), so the answer depends on reading 'biggest' as sales.

Current member version (is_current), so each member's home store is the latest one

Active member definition (at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks, store 999 and ZZ Test left out), used only for the side figure in the caveats

'Tampere' is taken from dim_store.city. The four stores are 115 Tampere Hervanta (2,788 members), 116 Tampere Lielahti (1,721), 117 Tampere Kaleva (1,692) and 136 Tampere Lamminpää (974).

Members who enrolled online (home store 900) have no city in the warehouse, so they cannot be placed in Tampere even if they live there. The 7,175 is therefore a lower bound on people living in Tampere.
Non-members are invisible: guest web orders and store receipts without a member carry no customer or city information. They are not counted.

This is a count of everyone ever enrolled, including lapsed members. Using the active-member rule (a purchase in the 52 weeks to Sunday 4 October 2026), 4,441 of the 7,175 are active. If Marketing meant active customers, use 4,441.

Home store changes over time. Counting every member who has had a Tampere home store in any version gives 7,515, which includes 340 who have since moved to another home store. I used the current version.

Some members with home store 136 (Lamminpää, opened 2 September 2024) have join dates back to 2019. Their home store was changed to Lamminpää after the store opened, so they did not enrol there. The count is by current home store, not by where they enrolled.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), agg AS (SELECT sku, SUM(net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines WHERE store_id = 900 AND business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-03' AND DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY sku) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY a.web_net_sales DESC) AS rank, a.sku, p.product_name, a.web_net_sales FROM agg a JOIN dim_product p ON p.sku = a.sku AND p.is_current ORDER BY a.web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Web sales: net amount excluding VAT, recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (not the order date)

Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or channel_id, because neither works across the 3 November 2025 migration
Click-and-collect counted as web; cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders are web sales)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Products identified by the stable sku, not product_key, so versions are not split; name taken from the current product version
Helsinki time for day boundaries (UTC timestamps converted)
Control total: result checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900

channel_code and channel_id do not work across the migration, and rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales silently drop web sales from 3 November 2025. I used store 900 and the base fact tables instead.

Returns lower the figures. Bedroom Peltola 793 lost 4,625.28 of 15,533.23 sold net to returns, and Interior Paint Norvik 298 lost 539.83. Ranked by sales before returns the order would differ, for example Bedroom Peltola 793 would be 2nd.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period=2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT ty.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS this_year_net_sales, ly.fiscal_year AS last_year_fiscal_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year_net_sales, ROUND(100.0*(ty.net_sales/ly.net_sales-1),1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week=ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date (refund_net)
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date (status delivered or collected)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (fiscal_year, fiscal_period, fiscal_week, Monday to Sunday)
Same-fiscal-week comparison against last year, not same calendar dates
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, channel_code, or any stg_, bak_ or tmp_ tables
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' is read as FY2026/27 P2 (weeks 5 to 8, 1 to 28 June 2026), the current fiscal year, which is already complete (warehouse loaded through 4 Oct 2026).
'Last year' is read as FY2025/26 P2 (weeks 5 to 8, 26 May to 22 June 2025), which was the fiscal year before the current one, matching the May 2026 precedent.
Weeks are lined up by fiscal week number (5 to 8 against 5 to 8), as the company rules require.
Total company includes the web shop and all physical stores, including Kuopio (refit) and Savonlinna (closed); this is not an LFL figure.
Staff purchases are included, as the net sales definition says.
Figures are excluding VAT and rounded to cents. Growth is in percent, rounded to 1 decimal.
caveats: No data corrections were needed. Sales lines have no duplicates at the sales_line_id or receipt_id/line_no grain. Every web line has a dispatched order (delivered or collected). The weekly totals match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, store group and web separately, in all 8 weeks.

The Store 999 and ZZ Test filter changes the totals slightly. By sale date, the excluded amounts were about 0.2 to 0.3% of each week (roughly 220 to 890 EUR a week), and the figures above have them removed.

Midsummer falls in different fiscal weeks in the two years, which drives the large week 7 and week 8 growth rates. The stores were shut on Midsummer Eve and Day (20 to 21 June 2025, fiscal week 8 last year; 19 to 20 June 2026, fiscal week 7 this year). So week 7 growth of -32.2% and week 8 growth of +76.4% mostly reflect the holiday timing, not underlying trading. The four-week P2 totals are more comparable: 1,294,606.20 EUR this year against 1,288,023.35 EUR last year (about +0.5%). I have not shown that total as a row because it was not requested.

Store coverage differs between the years. Last year 39 stores traded. This year it is 38 (Savonlinna closed 25 Jan 2026), and 37 from 15 June 2026 because Kuopio is in its refit until 26 July 2026. The weeks 7 and 8 figures this year therefore exclude Kuopio's sales, and the growth rates are not like-for-like.

Web sales are booked on the dispatch date. Web dispatch was paused over Midsummer 2026 and caught up on Monday 22 June (about 34.5k EUR of web net sales that day against about 11k on a normal weekday). That lifts web in week 8 this year (72,985 EUR against 30,548 EUR last year). The same effect last year fell in week 9, outside this period, which adds to the week 8 distortion.
Week-53 considerations do not apply: FY2025/26 P2 is a normal 4-week period.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2

In the rows I checked, the web sales lines had no duplicates, no web lines lacked a delivered or collected order, and none lacked a dispatch time. No data corrections were needed.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period) SELECT cs.format AS store_format, params.fiscal_year, params.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period = params.fiscal_period GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1

Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), period_days AS (SELECT calendar_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period = 2 AND is_trading_day), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN period_days d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date GROUP BY 1), trading AS (SELECT cs.store_id, cs.store_name, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days d WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= d.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= d.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / t.trading_days DESC) AS rank, t.store_id, t.store_name, ROUND(ss.net_sales / t.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM trading t JOIN store_sales ss ON ss.store_id = t.store_id ORDER BY 3

Store-level net sales agree with rpt_daily_store_sales for all 38 stores over 1 to 28 June 2026 (zero difference). The store 999 and ZZ Test filter did not change any total, since 999 and ZZ Test transactions are outside store_id below 900 or have no effect on these totals
