answer.sql:
-- Like-for-like (LFL) net sales growth for Q3 FY2025/26 by region (as-is).
-- Physical stores only (store_id below 900); week 53 is never LFL.
-- Q3 = weeks 27-39
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week
),
range_start AS (
    SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week
),
weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN weeks w
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    CROSS JOIN params
    CROSS JOIN range_start
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
    GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))
)
SELECT ty.region, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM lfl_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: week-by-week net sales comparison in LFL stores between the same fiscal weeks in two years

Refit closures: ref_store_closure weeks excluded for affected stores in both years
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns; store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded; web shop (store 900) excluded from LFL

assumptions: Q3 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 Q3 (weeks 27-39) compared to FY2024/25 Q3 (same week numbers); request received 2026-10-05 during FY2026/27

answer.sql: WITH campaign_info AS (SELECT mailing_list_size - holdout_size as targeted_member_count, holdout_size as holdout_member_count FROM dim_campaign WHERE campaign_id = 15), holdout_ids AS (SELECT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), holdout_keys AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_key FROM dim_member m WHERE m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM holdout_ids) AND m.is_current = TRUE), exposed_ids AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_key FROM fact_campaign_exposure WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted_spend AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(net_amount), 0) as total FROM fact_sales_line WHERE sale_date BETWEEN '2025-11-24' AND '2025-11-30' AND member_key IN (SELECT member_key FROM exposed_ids)), holdout_spend AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(net_amount), 0) as total FROM fact_sales_line WHERE sale_date BETWEEN '2025-11-24' AND '2025-11-30' AND member_key IN (SELECT member_key FROM holdout_keys)), calculations AS (SELECT ci.targeted_member_count, ci.holdout_member_count, ts.total as targeted_total, hs.total as holdout_total, ROUND(ts.total / ci.targeted_member_count, 2) as avg_spend_targeted, ROUND(hs.total / ci.holdout_member_count, 2) as avg_spend_holdout FROM campaign_info ci, targeted_spend ts, holdout_spend hs) SELECT 'Targeted Members' as group_name, avg_spend_targeted as avg_spend_per_member UNION ALL SELECT 'Held-out Members', avg_spend_holdout UNION ALL SELECT 'Uplift', ROUND(targeted_total - (targeted_member_count * avg_spend_holdout), 2) FROM calculations

Held-out members = control group explicitly excluded from campaign exposure

All amounts are net of VAT (using net_amount column from fact_sales_line)

answer.sql:
WITH sales_grouped AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    CASE 
      WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN 'Web'
      WHEN s.region IN ('Capital Region', 'South') THEN 
        CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN 'South/Capital Region (merged)' 
             ELSE 'South' END
      ELSE s.region
    END AS region_display,
    ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount), 2) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25')
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year,
    CASE 
      WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN 'Web'
      WHEN s.region IN ('Capital Region', 'South') THEN 
        CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN 'South/Capital Region (merged)' 
             ELSE 'South' END
      ELSE s.region
    END
)
SELECT 
  COALESCE(fy26.region_display, fy25.region_display) as region,
  COALESCE(fy26.net_sales, 0) as sales_fy2025_26,
  COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0) as sales_fy2024_25,
  CASE 
    WHEN COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND((COALESCE(fy26.net_sales, 0) - COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0)) / COALESCE(fy25.net_sales, 0) * 100, 2)
  END as growth_percent
FROM sales_grouped fy26
FULL OUTER JOIN sales_grouped fy25 
  ON (fy26.region_display = 'South/Capital Region (merged)' AND fy25.region_display = 'South')
    OR (fy26.region_display = fy25.region_display AND fy26.region_display NOT IN ('South/Capital Region (merged)'))
  AND fy25.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
WHERE fy26.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
ORDER BY CASE WHEN COALESCE(fy26.region_display, fy25.region_display) = 'Web' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
         COALESCE(fy26.region_display, fy25.region_display)
definitions_applied: Net sales: fact_sales_line.net_amount (excluding VAT)
Fiscal quarter: calendar-aligned quarters per ref_fiscal_calendar
Regional sales: grouped by dim_store.region
Web shop: all sales through store_id 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop)
assumptions: Web shop sales reported separately as requested, including both channel_code WB and NULL entries for store 900
Fiscal year basis: FY2025/26 (Oct 2025 - Sep 2026) is 'last year' and FY2024/25 (Oct 2024 - Sep 2025) is 'the year before'
Q3 defined as fiscal_quarter = 3 per the fiscal calendar
Growth percentage: (FY2025/26 - FY2024/25) / FY2024/25 × 100
caveats: Regional restructuring: Five stores (101, 102, 103, 104, 105: Helsinki Vuosaari, Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, Espoo Lommila, Vantaa Tammisto, Kerava) were reassigned from region 'South' to region 'Capital Region' effective 2025-04-28. FY2025/26 Q3 sales are reported under the new region. To enable year-over-year comparison, South and Capital Region figures are merged for FY2025/26.

Data quality issue in FY2025/26: Web shop sales (store 900) show 21,898 lines with NULL channel_code (EUR 588,457.57) and 1,426 lines with channel_code WB (EUR 38,287.09). Both are included in the Web total. The NULL channel_code appears to be a data loading anomaly.
Head office (store 999) and Training store sales are included in the results as received from fact_sales_line.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 22 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY rank;
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
LFL store base: open at least 364 days before the start of the range, and trading in that week in both years
Refit and closure weeks dropped for the store concerned in both years (ref_store_closure, Savonlinna closure)
Week 53 never counts in LFL
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns dated on their return date
Staff purchases included
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Physical stores only (store_id below 900), so the web shop is excluded
Fiscal year to date (YTD): FY2026/27 weeks 1 to 22 against FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22, aligned on fiscal week number
Regions as-is: current dim_store version, five regions including Capital Region
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'How they are doing' is read as growth, so the ranking is LFL net sales growth for the year to date against the same weeks last year. Absolute sales would mostly rank region size.

'This year so far' is read as FY2026/27 YTD, weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026), which are the weeks loaded as of the request date. Week 22 is the last complete fiscal week and P6 is only partly through.
Regions are shown as-is (today's five-region structure, applied to last year as well), which is the management-reporting default. The Capital Region therefore includes last year's South stores.
LFL is used because it is the company growth measure and it neutralises the Kuopio refit, the Savonlinna closure, last year's Pori refit and the 2024 openings.
Rank 1 is the highest LFL growth.
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line holds 418 receipt lines loaded twice in 15 to 21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 week 21). The duplicates have identical amounts and different sales_line_id values, and they overstate last year's net sales by EUR 10,390.53 against rpt_daily_store_sales. I kept one row per (receipt_id, line_no). After that, net sales match the control total with a gap of 0.00 for every week of both years. The duplicates affected West: its LFL growth is 1.93% after the correction, against 1.33% before. The ranking does not change.
East is the only region with negative LFL growth (-0.19%), and it is close to flat. East has only 7 stores in the LFL base, since Savonlinna closed on 25 January 2026.

Raw net sales growth, which is not LFL, gives a different picture. After the duplicate correction, YTD net sales growth for all physical stores in each region is North +3.80%, West +3.24%, Capital Region +2.71%, South +2.11% and East -11.61%. East falls mainly because Savonlinna closed, and West rises partly because of Lohja entering and Kuopio's refit. If Finance wants unadjusted growth, West would rank second and Capital Region third.
LFL is calculated on stores and weeks that traded in both years, so each region's base is smaller than its full store list: North 6, Capital Region 5, South 10, West 10, East 7 stores.
The stores are shut on closed holidays (Midsummer and so on). These fall in the same fiscal weeks in both years, so they are not adjusted for.
The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so the YTD stops there.

Several dashboard views (rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, rpt_weekly_sales_by_region) were avoided. They either omit web sales from 3 November 2025 or use the old four-region structure. This request is stores only, so web was not needed.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS this_year_net_sales, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS last_year_net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM params JOIN lfl_sales ty ON ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales in LFL stores for the same fiscal weeks, compared week by week with last year
LFL base: physical stores only (store_id below 900), open at least 364 days before the first day of the period
A store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years; refit weeks from ref_store_closure and closed or not-yet-open weeks drop out
Week 53 is never LFL (not relevant to P4 weeks 14-17)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns booked on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded; staff purchases included
Web shop (store 900) is not part of LFL
Fiscal calendar: P4 is fiscal weeks 14-17, lined up by week number with last year, not by calendar date
As-is store hierarchy; current dim_store version used for open and close dates
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'This year' is read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (request received 5 October 2026), and 'last year' as FY2025/26.
'Period 4' is FY2026/27 P4, 3 to 30 August 2026 (weeks 14-17). It is compared with FY2025/26 P4, 28 July to 24 August 2025 (weeks 14-17).
FY2026/27 P4 is fully loaded in the warehouse (the warehouse runs through 4 October 2026).
The request asks for the stores overall, so I gave one total LFL row with no breakdown by region or store.
Values are EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026. It traded in P4 last year (net sales about 9,913 EUR) but not this year, so it is excluded from the LFL base for all four weeks.

The LFL base is 38 physical stores for all 4 weeks (152 store-weeks). No store-weeks were removed for refits. The Pori (Sep 2025), Kuopio (Jun-Jul 2026) and Tammisto (2024) refits all fall outside P4 in both years, and both new stores (Tampere Lamminpää, Lohja) were open more than 364 days before the period.

The result is flat: -0.03 percent, a difference of about 265 EUR on roughly 1.01 million EUR. Underneath, the regions moved in different directions: North +6.53%, Capital Region +2.79%, South -0.71%, West -1.65%, East -3.13%. These regional figures are from a check run, not part of the table above.
Store-level net sales (physical stores, FY2026/27 and FY2025/26 P4) reconcile with rpt_daily_store_sales for every store, with no gaps.

-- Weekly total company net sales, P2 this year vs last year
-- Weeks 5-8 FY2026/27 vs FY2025/26
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year,
           5 AS first_week, 8 AS last_week
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    -- sales: stores on the sale date, web on the Helsinki dispatch date
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    -- returns reduce net sales on the return date
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
weekly AS (
    -- total company: sum across all stores
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS this_year_sales, ly.net_sales AS last_year_sales,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM weekly ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year
ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Company scope: all stores except training store 999, all products except ZZ Test category
Web sales: recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Returns: reduce net sales on their return date, not on the original sale date
As-is reporting: current store and product versions
assumptions: Period 2 this year = FY2026/27 P2 (fiscal weeks 5-8, 1 June to 28 June 2026)
Comparison year = FY2025/26 P2 (fiscal weeks 5-8, 26 May to 22 June 2025), using same fiscal week numbers for alignment
Total company = sum of all store locations including Online (web shop 900)
caveats: Kuopio refit closure (store 125) from 15 June to 26 July 2026 affects this comparison: week 7 (15-21 June) is a full week of closure, and week 8 (22-28 June) is partially closed for the first part of the week. Web sales recognized on dispatch date; store sales on sale date

answer.sql: WITH web_orders AS (SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN w.order_member_key IS NOT NULL THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(f.net_amount), 1) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_orders w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2

Guest web orders count as non-member

Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 P9 = 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026 (5 weeks), P10 = 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026, P11 = 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026

Share taken on net sales before returns, as in the company member-share definition, giving one percentage per period. On net sales after returns (returns on their return date, tied to the original order's member status) the shares would be 68.6, 67.4 and 68.0 for P9, P10 and P11.
Percentages rounded to one decimal place.
caveats: Data defect corrected: between about 5 Feb and 7 Mar 2026 (fiscal weeks 42 to 45, which falls in P10 and P11), 1,309 sales lines on logged-in web orders lost their member_key (706 lines worth 21,669.74 EUR net in P10, 603 lines worth 16,311.55 EUR in P11), although fact_web_order still carries the member key for those orders. The figure uses web sales before returns. Web returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so the after-returns shares above are slightly different and the last weeks of P11 may not have all their returns booked.

answer.sql:
WITH sales_by_period AS (
  SELECT 
    dd.fiscal_year,
    dd.fiscal_period,
    SUM(fsl.net_amount) as period_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON dd.calendar_date = fsl.sale_date
  INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON dp.product_key = fsl.product_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product_old dpo ON dpo.sku = dp.sku
  WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
    AND dd.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12
    AND dpo.category = 'Garden'
  GROUP BY dd.fiscal_year, dd.fiscal_period
),
returns_by_period AS (
  SELECT 
    dd.fiscal_year,
    dd.fiscal_period,
    SUM(frl.refund_net) as period_returns
  FROM fact_return_line frl
  INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON dd.calendar_date = frl.return_date
  INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON dp.product_key = frl.product_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product_old dpo ON dpo.sku = dp.sku
  WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
    AND dd.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12
    AND dpo.category = 'Garden'
  GROUP BY dd.fiscal_year, dd.fiscal_period
)
SELECT 
  s.fiscal_year,
  s.fiscal_period,
  s.period_sales - COALESCE(r.period_returns, 0) as net_sales
FROM sales_by_period s
LEFT JOIN returns_by_period r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period)
ORDER BY s.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales at product line level, excluding VAT, after line discounts, minus refunds booked in the same period
Old category setup = dim_product_old table, which defines the legacy Garden category
Garden category = all SKUs assigned to category 'Garden' in dim_product_old, matched to current sales via SKU
Period = fiscal period as defined in ref_fiscal_calendar (P7–P12 of fiscal year FY2024/25, spanning 28 Oct 2024 – 27 Apr 2025)
assumptions: Returned items are attributed to the period in which they were returned (return_date), not the original sale period, consistent with how Tuomimetsä reports in rpt_daily_store_sales
The dim_product_old table represents the historical category structure the requester described as 'the old way'
Products are identified by SKU and matched across dim_product_old and dim_product to handle category changes
caveats: P12 (12 March – 27 April) contains significantly higher sales (€310.9k net) than other periods, driven by spring seasonal demand
Returns are recorded in the period when they are processed, which may differ from the original sale period; 975 returned lines across P7–P12 are accounted for
Garden category exists in both old and current dimension structures with the same SKU set; no reclassification was required

answer.sql: WITH contacted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 19), sales AS (SELECT sum(f.net_amount) AS v FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-05-24' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM contacted)), refunds AS (SELECT sum(r.refund_net) AS v FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-05-24' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM contacted)) SELECT 'Spring Garden Launch 2026' AS campaign_name, 19 AS campaign_id, (SELECT count(*) FROM contacted) AS members_contacted, round((SELECT v FROM sales) - (SELECT v FROM refunds), 2) AS net_spend_eur
definitions_applied: Contacted member: a distinct loyalty number (member_id) with at least one row in fact_campaign_exposure for campaign 19
Members identified by member_id, not member_key, because dim_member keeps one row per version and the contact and purchase rows can carry different keys
Spend is net sales: EUR excluding VAT (net_amount, after line discounts), less refunds (refund_net)
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag = true) excluded, along with refunds on those lines
Window 2026-05-04 to 2026-05-24 inclusive, on sale_date for sales and return_date for refunds (refunds count on the day booked)
All channels counted: stores, web home delivery and click-and-collect
The 2026 campaign is campaign_id 19; the 2024 and 2025 editions have the same name stem and were not used
assumptions: 'Contacted' means a contact was made (a row in fact_campaign_exposure), whatever the channel and whether or not it was delivered. 14,814 of the 15,001 had at least one contact delivered.
'Spend' means net sales excluding VAT, after refunds. Marketing may prefer a different basis; see the caveats for the alternatives.
Spend covers every purchase made by the contacted members in the window, not only purchases of garden products or purchases attributed to the mailing.
The window 4 to 24 May 2026 matches the campaign window in dim_campaign. Both dates are included.
sale_date is taken as the local (Finnish) business date. It differs from the UTC date on some lines.
caveats: fact_sales_line.channel_code is null for 2026 sales rows, although the column comment says ST/WB. I used channel_id and the store version (store 900 = web shop) instead. Filtering on channel_code would have dropped all of the 2026 spend.
dim_member has one row per member version (89,314 rows for 60,000 members). Joining on member_key would have missed purchases made under a different version, so I matched on member_id.

The mailing list size in dim_campaign is 16,624 including a holdout of 1,597, which implies about 15,027 contacted. The exposure table has 15,001 distinct members, which is 26 fewer. I reported the count actually contacted. I did not find the reason for the 26.
None of the 1,597 held-out members (campaign_holdout) appears in the contact data, so no holdout members are in the count or the spend.
Staff purchases excluded: they would add 2,540.79 of gross-of-refund net sales (191,576.08 with them, 189,035.29 without) from contacted members.

Refunds: 8,228.60 net, booked in the window against contacted members' non-staff purchases, was deducted. Net sales before refunds is 189,035.29. If Marketing wants sales before returns, that is the figure. Including VAT, sales before refunds are 236,735.14.

Only 2,626 of the 15,001 contacted members bought anything in the window. The spend is not attributed to the mailing: there is no comparison with the holdout group here, so it says nothing about the campaign's effect.

Checked and found clean for the window: no duplicate sales or return lines, no cancelled web orders, no sales on non-trading days, no orphan member keys, and gross amounts consistent with net plus VAT. Staging tables for the campaign contacts and sales lines hold no rows for these data.

WITH params AS (

),

           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost

    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),

    SELECT cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin

)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 2) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 6 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect web net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns, with returns taken off on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (UTC dispatch timestamp converted to Europe/Helsinki)
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded from web sales (only delivered and collected orders are included)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is broken from the 3 November 2025 migration)
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, which works on both sides of the migration
Store 999 and category ZZ Test left out
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: periods 6 to 8 of FY2025/26 are fiscal weeks 22 to 34, 22 Sep to 21 Dec 2025
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current one (FY2026/27) on the request date of 9 October 2026. This follows the accepted reading of earlier 'last year' requests made in FY2026/27.
'Periods 6 to 8' read as fiscal periods 6, 7 and 8 of that year, all complete and loaded.
'Sales' read as net sales excluding VAT on the company definition, not gross sales or order counts.
Shares are shown to two decimals in percent units.
caveats: No correction to the data was needed. Web net sales per period (175,588.62, 154,977.27 and 225,265.08 EUR) match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in all three periods.
Click-and-collect net sales were 48,901.47, 39,403.04 and 60,899.16 EUR in periods 6, 7 and 8.

Refunds on web orders processed in physical stores (for example items returned at a shop) are booked to that store, not to the web shop. They stay in the stores' net sales, not in the web figures, as in the company control total. They are small, roughly a few hundred EUR per store per period, and I did not move them to web.

The legacy views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used because they omit web sales after 3 November 2025. That date falls inside period 7, so using them would have understated the web totals.
Period 7 straddles the 3 November 2025 web-platform migration. The figures are unaffected because the fulfilment type comes from fact_web_order, not channel_code or channel_id.

answer.sql: WITH first_version AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS rn FROM dim_member) SELECT cs.store_id, cs.store_name, COUNT(DISTINCT fv.member_id) AS new_members FROM first_version fv JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = fv.home_store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE fv.rn = 1 AND fv.join_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-04-28' AND DATE '2026-05-03' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: New member: counted on the join date, at the home store in the member's first dim_member version (the store where they enrolled)
Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key
Online sign-ups sit under store 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop), shown as its own row
Store names taken from the current dim_store version (as-is)
Fiscal year FY2025/26 as defined in the fiscal calendar: 28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026, including week 53 (no comparison requested, so week 53 stays in)
Store 999 (training store) excluded from reporting; no new members were enrolled there in the period
assumptions: 'Last year' asked on 7 October 2026 (FY2026/27) read as FY2025/26, following the accepted readings for requests made in May 2026 or later in FY2026/27 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35)
Because FY2025/26 has 53 weeks, the count covers 28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026 inclusive, with week 53 included
Attribution is to the enrolling store (first version home store), not the member's current home store
Stores are shown as a flat list without regional grouping, as the request asked for each store only
caveats: 817 of the 14,854 members who joined in the period have since changed home store; they are counted at the store where they enrolled, not their current one. Counting by current home store would give different per-store figures

Counting every dim_member version instead of the first version only (or by member_key) would inflate the totals, because members have up to 4 versions. I counted distinct member_id on the first version
The 40 rows total 14,854 new members: 11,922 across the 39 physical stores and 2,932 online
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026, so its 113 sign-ups cover only the part of the year it was open
Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in autumn 2024, so they were open for the full year

Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026, which falls after the period; Pori (119) was shut for a refit from 8 September to 12 October 2025, inside the period, and its sign-ups cover only the weeks it was open
If 'last year' was meant as calendar year 2025, the figures would differ; I used the fiscal year as the company does
No control total in rpt_daily_store_sales applies to member counts, so there is no cross-check against it

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, round(f.vat_rate*100, 1) AS vat_rate_pct, sum(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2024/25 = 26 Aug 2024 to 22 Sep 2024 (4 weeks, fiscal weeks 18 to 21), taken from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar; the period is fully loaded
Stores only: channel_code ST and store_id below 900, which leaves out the web shop (store 900) and the training store (store 999)
VAT charged = gross_amount minus net_amount on the sales line; this matches net_amount times vat_rate to the cent on every line
Split by the vat_rate stored on each sales line, not by the product's current VAT class
sale_date as the business date (it is the Finnish local date; sale_ts_utc is UTC)
assumptions: 'Charged' means VAT on sales made in the period, before any refunds. Returns are not netted off.
Period 5 read as the company fiscal period (4-week retail period starting 26 Aug 2024), not calendar month 5 (May).
'FY24/25' read as the warehouse label FY2024/25.
Staff purchases are included because VAT is charged on them. The 104 staff-flagged lines in the training store are excluded with that store.
The 24% and 25.5% rows are kept as separate rows, as the request asks for a split by VAT rate.
caveats: The standard VAT rate changed on 1 Sep 2024 from 24% to 25.5%, in the middle of this period. Sales from 26 to 31 Aug are at 24% (VAT 54105.20) and sales from 1 to 22 Sep are at 25.5% (VAT 180017.23). Anyone expecting a single standard-rate row should add the two.

Excluded as non-store: web shop lines (4,075 lines, VAT 30846.16) and training-store lines (140 lines, VAT 685.00), which are recorded with channel code ST but store 999. The training store is not a real shop.
Total store VAT charged is 235090.72 (sum of the four rows). No total row is given because none was requested.

Refunds are not deducted. Store returns booked in the period carried 11135.97 of VAT (24%: 5094.72, 25.5%: 6029.57, 14%: 10.48, 10%: 1.20). Net of refunds, store VAT would be about 223954.75, with 24% and 25.5% returns also relating partly to earlier sales.

Checks run: no duplicate sales lines, no unmatched store or product keys, every line sits inside its store version's validity dates, and the rate and VAT amount agree on all lines. No other data problems were found in this period.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web shop = store_id 900 (not channel_code, which is empty after the 3 Nov 2025 migration)
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected orders; cancelled and processing orders have no sales
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, booked to the store where they were processed
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26 P5 to P8), whole periods
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year that ended 3 May 2026. This follows how the 12 to 27 May 2026 requests (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35) read it, in the same fiscal year as today (FY2026/27). FY2024/25 would give different numbers.

'Periods 5 to 8' read as FY2025/26 P5 (25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025), P6 (22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, 5 weeks), P7 (27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025) and P8 (24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025). Periods are not equal in length, so P6 includes an extra week.
Figures are net of returns and excluding VAT, since 'net' was read as the company net sales definition.
One row per period, no total row, since none was asked for.
caveats: Test-article correction: one ZZ Test web line (5.50 EUR) was removed from P6. Without that filter P6 would be 175,594.12 instead of 175,588.62.

Returns on web orders that were handed in at a physical store (about 501 lines, 19.7k EUR refunded across P5 to P8) are booked to that store under the company rule, so they are not deducted here. If they were deducted from the web shop, web net sales would fall by 5,495.34 (P5), 4,783.52 (P6), 4,901.43 (P7) and 4,545.10 (P8). Those amounts exclude ZZ Test.
Web net sales by order date instead of dispatch date would differ (e.g. P8 249,084 before returns versus 243,086 on dispatch date), so the dispatch-date rule moves sales between periods.

The control total in rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 matches exactly in P5, P7 and P8. In P6 its net_sales matches exactly (175,588.62), but its net_sales_before_returns includes the 5.50 test line (193,190.55 against 193,190.55 plus nothing further; the report table lacks the test filter on the before-returns column only). No unexplained gaps remain.

Data is loaded through 4 Oct 2026, so all four periods are complete. Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, but they are counted on the return date, so late returns for P8 sales in January 2026 do not affect these figures.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS gold_members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold'
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not by version row
Current tier read from the latest dim_member version (is_current, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
dim_member is slowly changing, one row per version, so only the current version of each member is used
assumptions: 'At the moment' means the latest data in the warehouse, loaded through Sunday 4 October 2026, which is the current version of every member
'Gold-tier loyalty members' means every member whose current tier is Gold, whatever their channel, home store or marketing consent
Members who are no longer active (no purchase in the last 52 weeks) are still counted, because the request asks about tier membership and not about active members
caveats: The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, three days before the request date of 7 October 2026. Any tier change on 5 to 7 October is not in the figure.

I checked the data for problems and found none that changed the count. Each of the 60000 members has exactly one current version, no member has overlapping versions, and no member_key is duplicated. Reading Gold by validity date gives the same 5791 on 4 and 7 October 2026 as the is_current flag does.

Counting version rows or filtering tier = 'Gold' without is_current would overstate the figure (8203 Gold version rows in all, 2412 of them superseded), because members who moved tier over time have several versions.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-08-25' AS start_date, DATE '2025-09-21' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ROUND(ss.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date
Trading days: days the store was open (after opening, before closure, outside refit closures) and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Part-period stores stay in the table with their own trading days
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 left out
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Store identity and name taken from the current dim_store version (store_id as the stable key)
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P05 = 25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025 (fiscal weeks 18 to 21)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same stores and days
assumptions: Request received 8 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27. 'Last year' is read as the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26, as past requests asked in FY2026/27 were read. 'Period 5 last year' is therefore FY2025/26 P05, 25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025. FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026) was not used.
'Store league table' follows the company definition: ranking by net sales per trading day, not by total net sales. Total net sales are shown alongside.
Rank 1 is the highest net sales per trading day, and ranking uses the unrounded figure. There are no ties.
All 39 physical stores traded in the period and are listed, including Pori with part of the period closed.
The period has no closed holidays, so trading days equal calendar days (28) for every store that was open throughout.
Store names and format come from the current dim_store version. Vantaa Tammisto moved region in April 2025, but this table shows no region, so as-is versus as-was does not affect it.
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line holds duplicate lines for Tampere Lielahti (store 116) from 15 to 21 Sep 2025. The same receipt_id and line_no appear twice with different sales_line_id values, identical amounts, and a second ETL load on 23 Sep 2025 03:12. There are 836 rows (418 duplicated lines), worth about 10,390.53 EUR of overstated net sales. I kept one row per receipt_id + line_no, the earlier load. Without this fix Lielahti would show 47,679.15 EUR (1,702.83 per day) and rank 3. Corrected, it shows 37,288.62 EUR (1,331.74 per day) and ranks 7, which matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly.

Control check: after the correction, net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales for all 39 stores over the period with no gap. This reconciliation was done store by store; a check on Lielahti by day showed the other 21 days already agreed.
No other store has duplicated sales lines in the period, and return lines have no duplicates.

Pori (store 119) was closed for a refit from 8 Sep 2025 (ref_store_closure runs 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025), so it has only 14 trading days (25 Aug to 7 Sep) and no sales in the closure. Its per-day figure is on those 14 days only and its total net sales are not comparable with the other stores' 28-day totals.
Stores that opened recently (Tampere Lamminpää, Lohja) traded the full period, so they are not marked as new.
Savonlinna (closed 25 Jan 2026) was open and trading throughout this period, so it is ranked normally.
The reporting view rpt.v_weekly_store_sales and rpt.v_daily_sales were not used because they omit web sales from Nov 2025 on; this table covers physical stores only, so web is not part of it.
Returns are deducted on their own return date, so some refunds in the period relate to sales made before 25 Aug 2025 and some sales in the period will be refunded after 21 Sep 2025.

answer.sql: SELECT count(*) AS web_orders_placed FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST((order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki' AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web order = one row in fact_web_order (web_order_id is unique, no duplicates)
Order date = calendar date of order_ts_utc converted from UTC to Europe/Helsinki local time, the same convention the warehouse uses for sale_date on sales lines
Orders placed = all statuses counted, including cancelled
Cyber Monday 2025 = Monday 1 December 2025 (dim_date confirms it is a normal trading day)
assumptions: 'Placed' means every order that was submitted on the day, whatever its later status: 239 delivered, 87 collected and 19 cancelled.
Orders from guest and logged-in customers, home delivery and click-and-collect, are all included.
'1 December' means the Helsinki calendar day, 00:00 to 24:00 local time (UTC+2 in December). That is 30 Nov 22:00 UTC to 1 Dec 22:00 UTC.
caveats: Timestamps are stored in UTC. Cutting at the UTC date gives only 291 orders, which would miss 54 orders placed between 00:00 and 02:00 Helsinki time and add 0 wrong ones. I corrected for this by converting to Helsinki time.

The 345 includes 19 cancelled orders. Excluding them gives 326, which matches the orders that have sales lines in fact_sales_line (cancelled orders have none). Use 326 if you want orders that actually went through.

The 345 orders come only from fact_web_order, so the sales-line channel migration on 3 Nov 2025 (channel_code ST/WB replaced by channel_id 1/2/3) does not affect the count. The 326 non-cancelled orders all have sales lines dated 2025-12-01, and their line counts match line_count.
stg_web_order_load holds no orders in this window and nothing there that is not already in fact_web_order, so staging had no effect.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order o WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01' AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted on order date in Helsinki time
Processing orders included, cancelled orders excluded
UTC timestamp converted to Helsinki timezone (Europe/Helsinki)
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is 1 December 2025
Web orders are counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines, to include processing orders
caveats: The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so December 2025 data is complete
7 rows in the fact_web_order table for the period cross the UTC/Helsinki day boundary (rows that exist only in Helsinki time when the day boundary is taken at midnight)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND NOT (s.store_id = 900 AND w.web_order_id IS NULL) UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_cat AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') AND cp.category IN ('Garden','Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM by_cat ty JOIN by_cat ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.category
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected orders count
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
As-is hierarchy: current product version for category, so outdoor lighting is in Electrical in both years
Fiscal calendar: period 8 is fiscal weeks 31-34, compared period against period (same week numbers)
Growth is net sales in FY2025/26 P8 divided by net sales in FY2024/25 P8, minus 1, in percent
Control total: all-category net sales for the period match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly in both years (1,435,696.60 and 1,373,188.97)
assumptions: Today is 5 Oct 2026, which is in FY2026/27, so 'last year' is read as FY2025/26 (25 Nov-21 Dec 2025 region: P8 runs 24 Nov-21 Dec 2025) and 'the year before' as FY2024/25 (P8 runs 25 Nov-22 Dec 2024). This follows how past requests were accepted (REQ-D04 and others).
Reported as-is (current category hierarchy), the company default, since the request did not ask for as-was.
Net sales cover the whole company including the web shop (store 900), because the request names no channel or store scope.
Growth is FY2025/26 P8 against FY2024/25 P8, i.e. last year over the year before.
Garden and Electrical are shown as two rows, one per category, with no combined total, since the request did not ask for one.
caveats: The outdoor lighting subcategory moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025 (FY2025/26 P7). On the as-is basis used here it sits in Electrical in both years, so the comparison is consistent. On an as-was basis (categories as they stood at the time), FY2024/25 P8 would be Electrical 142,914.41 and Garden 56,270.57. Growth would then be Electrical +19.8% and Garden -34.6%. The as-is growth of +5.4% and +0.1% is the like-for-like picture; the as-was figures would mostly reflect the reclassification.

Duplicate loads: 836 sales lines (418 pairs, 178 receipts) dated 15-21 Sep 2025 are loaded twice with different sales_line_ids. That falls in FY2025/26 P5, outside both P8 windows, so no correction was needed here. Anyone reusing these tables for P5 FY2025/26 should de-duplicate on receipt_id + line_no.

The channel_code column breaks after the web platform migration on 3 Nov 2025, and rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales drop web sales from that date. Neither was used. Web was identified by store 900 and dated on the Helsinki dispatch date.
Web lines for orders that are cancelled or still processing (no dispatch) are excluded, per the company web definition. They did not change either P8 total.
FY2025/26 P8 compares with FY2024/25 P8 by fiscal week number (31-34 in both years), not calendar dates. Week 53 is not in either period.

answer.sql: WITH stock AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_value FROM fact_stock_week WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN (SELECT period_start_date FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period=11) AND (SELECT period_end_date FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period=11)), weekly AS (SELECT p.category, k.week_ending_date, sum(k.closing_value) AS week_value FROM stock k JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = k.store_key AND s.region = 'West' JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = k.product_key GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT category, round(avg(week_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_eur FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 11 of FY2025/26 (23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026, 4 weeks), taken from ref_fiscal_calendar
Stock value = closing stock at standard cost (fact_stock_week.closing_value), counted on the Sunday ending each fiscal week
West region from dim_store.region, joined on the store key carried by the stock row
Category from dim_product.category, joined on the product key carried by the stock row
Average stock value = mean of the four week-end category totals (sum over all West stores and SKUs per week, then averaged over the weeks)
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, since the request came in October 2026 (FY2026/27 period 6). Period 11 is therefore 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026. A calendar-year reading (2025) would give a different period.
'Average stock value' is the average of the four weekly closing totals, not an average per store or per SKU.
All ten West stores are included (store ids 115 to 123 and 136). No West store was closed for a refit in the period.
Values are in EUR at standard cost, as held in the warehouse (no VAT is involved).
The weekly category totals are averaged over all four weeks, including the zero-value rows for delisted articles in the week ending 1 Mar.
caveats: Correction: the stock snapshot for the week ending 8 Mar 2026 was loaded twice (9 Mar 01:00 and 10 Mar 02:45). It holds 7,439 duplicate key pairs in 10 stores (7,439 extra rows in the West data). The copies are identical in every column. I counted each store/SKU once. Without this the week total would be overstated, and the all-store total for that week was about 3.69m against about 2.87m in neighbouring weeks.
The 12 'ZZ Test' articles (TEST ARTICLE 3989 to 4000) are in dim_product but have no stock rows in West in this period, so they do not affect the answer and no 'ZZ Test' row appears.

The week ending 1 Mar 2026 has 38 more West rows than the following weeks. All 38 are zero-unit, zero-value rows for articles delisted on 1 Mar 2026, so they change no totals but are counted in the four-week average as zero.
Categories are the current warehouse categories; I did not check them against any older category structure.

answer.sql: WITH signups AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, arg_min(home_store_id, valid_from) AS signup_store_id FROM dim_member WHERE join_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31' GROUP BY member_id, join_date), names AS (SELECT store_id, arg_max(store_name, valid_from) AS store_name FROM dim_store GROUP BY store_id) SELECT s.signup_store_id AS store_id, n.store_name, count(*) AS new_members FROM signups s LEFT JOIN names n ON n.store_id = s.signup_store_id GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: New member = a distinct loyalty member_id, counted once however many dim_member versions it has (not a count of version rows, which would be 21805 instead of 14629)
Sign-up date = join_date (the same on every version of a member)
Sign-up store = home_store_id on the member's earliest version (the one valid from the join date)
Home store 900 = online sign-ups, shown as Tuomimetsä web shop
Store names taken from the latest dim_store version per store_id
assumptions: 'Last year' means calendar year 2025 (1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025), read against the request date of 7 Oct 2026. If Marketing meant the last fiscal year (FY2025/26, 28 Apr 2025 to 3 May 2026), the figures will differ.
Each member is credited to the store they signed up at, which is their home store on the date they joined, not the store they are assigned to today.
Online sign-ups appear as one row, store_id 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop), as the warehouse records them.
No staging or backup tables were used; the member data comes from dim_member only.
caveats: Correction: counting rows in dim_member would overstate sign-ups (21805 rows against 14629 distinct members) because members have a new row each time their tier, home store or consent changes.
Correction: 832 of the 2025 joiners later changed home store. Using the current home store would give different store totals, so the sign-up store is taken from the first version.

Correction: Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 Jan 2026 and all 152 of its 2025 joiners have since been reassigned to other home stores. Using the current store would show Savonlinna with zero sign-ups; it is shown here with its 152.
The 40 rows add up to 14629 distinct new members for 2025, of which 2877 (about 20%) signed up online.

The member table has no field recording where a member physically signed up. The first-version home store is the best available proxy, and a member who joined online and was later given a home store would not be visible as such (online members show store 900 only on their first version).
I did not check whether the same person holds more than one loyalty number.

answer.sql:
WITH q1_fy2026_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    p.subcategory,
    SUM(s.quantity) as total_quantity_sold
  FROM fact_sales_line s
  JOIN dim_product p ON s.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_date d ON s.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE p.category = 'Garden'
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1
  GROUP BY p.subcategory
),
q1_fy2026_returns AS (
  SELECT 
    p.subcategory,
    SUM(r.quantity_returned) as total_quantity_returned
  FROM fact_return_line r
  JOIN dim_product p ON r.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_date d ON r.return_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE p.category = 'Garden'
    AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1
  GROUP BY p.subcategory
)
SELECT 
  s.subcategory,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.total_quantity_returned, 0) * 100.0 / s.total_quantity_sold, 2) as return_rate
FROM q1_fy2026_sales s
LEFT JOIN q1_fy2026_returns r ON s.subcategory = r.subcategory
ORDER BY s.subcategory
definitions_applied: Return rate: ratio of units returned to units sold, expressed as percentage
Fiscal year FY2025/26: the company's fiscal year running from 2025-04-28 to 2026-05-03
Fiscal quarter 1: the first quarter of the fiscal year (2025-04-28 to 2025-07-27)
Sale date: calendar_date from fact_sales_line; return date: return_date from fact_return_line
assumptions: Last year: FY2025/26 (the most recent completed fiscal year as of 2026-10-15)
Q1: fiscal quarter 1 of FY2025/26
Garden: products with category = 'Garden'
Return rate calculated per subcategory by summing all quantities without weighting by value
caveats: Return rate calculation includes only items with a matching sale and return in the database
Returns are matched to sales by product_key; returns of items sold outside Q1 are excluded
One subcategory (Garden Furniture) has an unusually high return rate (12.08%); recommend further investigation into return reasons

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-02-23' AS start_date, DATE '2026-03-22' AS end_date), stock AS (SELECT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_units, closing_value FROM fact_stock_week, params WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY store_key, product_key, week_ending_date ORDER BY etl_loaded_at DESC) = 1), weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM stock fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE cs.region = 'West' AND cs.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 11 AS fiscal_period, category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_value FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: sum across stores and products within each week first, then average across the weeks of the period (never sum across weeks)
Stock value is closing_value, at standard cost in EUR
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 11 is 23 Feb 2026 to 22 Mar 2026, fiscal weeks 44 to 47, four week-ending Sundays (1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026)
As-is reporting: West region and product category taken from the current dim_store and dim_product versions (is_current)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); store 999 and the web shop excluded; category ZZ Test excluded
Fact stock rows were deduplicated at the grain store_key, product_key, week_ending_date
assumptions: 'Last year' was read as FY2025/26. The request is dated 5 October 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests in the new fiscal year read 'last year' as the previous fiscal year. FY2025/26 P11 is fully loaded.

'Average stock value' was read as the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost (closing_value), summed across all West stores within each week. It is not the last week's closing, and not an average per store.

The request gave no as-is or as-was instruction, so the company default (as-is) was used. For this period the answer is the same either way: West did not change in the April 2025 reorganisation, and the outdoor lighting move to Electrical took effect on 27 October 2025, before the period.
The West region has 10 physical stores. Online (store 900) is its own region and is not part of West.
caveats: Correction: the week ending 8 March 2026 was loaded twice for all 10 West stores in fact_stock_week. The 7,439 rows reloaded on 10 March 2026 duplicate the 9 March load exactly, with identical units and values. Summing them as they stand double-counts that week. I kept one row per store, article and week. This also made the 8 March figure about EUR 813,600 lower, which would have overstated the 4-week average by about EUR 203,400 across the West categories.

The set of ranged articles differs slightly between weeks: 102 store-article rows present in the week ending 1 March are absent from 8 March onward (articles dropped from the range). This is normal ranging change, so I left it as is.
No negative or null stock, and no test-article rows, were found for the West stores in this period. closing_value agrees with closing_units times the standard unit cost on every row.
Values are at standard cost, not retail. Standard costs were revalued in April 2026, which is before this period, so the period uses a single cost basis.
The control table rpt_daily_store_sales covers sales only, not stock, so no control total was available. The duplicate check was done against the grain of the stock snapshot.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END AS category, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0*SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost)/SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS gross_margin_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 6 AND (cp.category IN ('Garden','Electrical') OR cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns, with returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned
Gross margin %: gross margin divided by net sales
As-is reporting: category taken from the current product version
Outdoor lighting counted in Electrical for all history
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 6 runs from 22 September to 26 October 2025 (weeks 22 to 26, 5 weeks)
Web shop (store 900) included in the company total; it is not a physical store
assumptions: 'Period 6 last year' read as FY2025/26 P6, because the request was made on 8 October 2026 in FY2026/27 and past requests in this situation (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35) took the previous fiscal year. FY2026/27 P6 has only its first week loaded (28 September to 4 October 2026), so a same-period comparison would not be possible.
Reported as-is (current category hierarchy), the company default, because the request did not ask for as-was.
Both categories include web sales, which are not split out, since the request did not ask for a channel breakdown.
Net sales and margin are after returns, the company definition, and are not on a sale-week cohort basis.
Result is two rows, one per category, with no combined total, since none was asked for.
caveats: Correction applied: five delisted outdoor lighting articles (SKUs 100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) were never given the new Electrical product version from 27 October 2025. Their current dim_product row still says Garden, which contradicts the rule that outdoor lighting is Electrical for all history. I treated subcategory 'Outdoor Lighting' as Electrical. They had no sales or returns in FY2025/26 P6, so the figures above are the same with or without this correction, but a plain join on category would give wrong history for other periods.

Period 6 of FY2025/26 ends on 26 October 2025, the day before the outdoor lighting subcategory moved from Garden to Electrical. An as-was view would put outdoor lighting (about 36.5k EUR of sales before returns) under Garden for this period. This answer is as-is, so it sits in Electrical. If Commercial wants the category as it stood at the time, say so and I will rerun it.

Control total: all-category net sales for the same days (22 September to 26 October 2025), built with the same method, equal rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (1,293,219.69 EUR across 40 locations, no store-level differences). This check does not apply to a category subset, so the Garden and Electrical figures are not themselves reconciled to it.
Period 6 sits entirely before the 3 November 2025 web-platform migration, so the channel_code problem does not affect it. I did not use channel_code, the deprecated tables or the rpt.v_ views.
Returns booked in P6 reduce P6 sales, including returns of goods sold in earlier periods. The margin therefore includes a small mix of earlier-period sales.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN f.member_key IS NOT NULL THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(f.net_amount), 2) AS member_share_pct FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10, 11) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales: fact_sales_line records with channel_code = 'WB'
Loyalty member: member_key is not null (excludes guest orders)
Sales value: net_amount (excluding VAT)
Fiscal period: Tuomimetsä's 4-4-5 week calendar periods
assumptions: Last year relative to request date 2026-10-09 = FY2024/25
Share calculated as percentage of net sales value (EUR), not order count
Periods requested are fiscal periods, not calendar months

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND fs.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
definitions_applied: Closing stock is the fact_stock_week snapshot at the end of a fiscal week (Sunday)
Last week means the last completed fiscal week, FY2026/27 week 22 (Monday 28 September to Sunday 4 October 2026), as at the request date of 8 October 2026
Stock for one store and one SKU is read straight from the snapshot, with no summing across weeks
Store and product are joined through their version keys (store_key, product_key) and identified by stable store_id and sku
Physical store scope (store_id below 900), and store 999 and category ZZ Test are excluded (neither applies here)
Query-check run: one row, unique at store and SKU, no deprecated objects used
assumptions: SKU 100011 is the article 'Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570' (Garden, Plants & Flowers), and 'Jyväskylä Palokka' is store 124, a Medium-format store
'The end of last week' means closing stock at the end of fiscal week 22 (Sunday 4 October 2026), the last complete week loaded in the warehouse
'Stock' means the units the store holds, as recorded in the weekly stock snapshot (closing_units)
caveats: Each of the store and the SKU has only one dimension version, so no as-is versus as-was difference applies
The snapshot has one row for this store and SKU in week 22, with no duplicate loads

Stock is unchanged from the previous week (11 units at 27 September). There were no sales or receipts for this SKU in the store during week 22, and the earlier fall from 13 to 11 units matches two sales on 21 and 24 September
The snapshot holds only articles the store ranges. Web stock is held centrally and is not included

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day -
