364)), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))) SELECT ty.region, ty.store_weeks, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY ty.region NULLS FIRST
definitions_applied: DEF-LFL-BASIS: Like-for-like base comprises physical stores open for at least 52 weeks before the period
DEF-LFL-BOTH-YEARS: Store-weeks counted in LFL only if trading in both the comparison year and prior year
DEF-LFL-REFIT: Refit closure weeks excluded from both years using ref_store_closure
DEF-LFL-WEEK53: Week 53 never included in LFL as it has no comparator week
DEF-NET-SALES: Net sales excluding VAT, after returns (returns recorded on return date)
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: Physical stores only (store_id < 900); web shop excluded from LFL
CAL-COMPARE: Fiscal week alignment across years (weeks 14-17 in both FY2026/27 and FY2025/26)
assumptions: Period 4 this year interpreted as FY2026/27 P4 (fiscal weeks 14-17, 3 August to 30 August 2026)
Period 4 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 P4 (fiscal weeks 14-17, 28 July to 24 August 2025)
Request asking for aggregate company performance; no regional breakdown requested
Comparison uses same fiscal week numbers across years, not aligned calendar dates
caveats: Query passed all validation checks with no failures
Result represents flat growth: like-for-like net sales declined 0.03% comparing 152 store-weeks that traded in both periods
The store_weeks figure shows the LFL base size (number of store-week combinations included in the comparison)

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, f.net_amount AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND s.store_id <> 999), refunds AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, -r.refund_net AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND s.store_id <> 999), weekly AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, sum(amt) AS net_sales FROM (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM refunds) GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT t.fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, t.fiscal_week, round(t.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_this_year, round(l.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, round((t.net_sales / l.net_sales - 1) * 100, 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly t JOIN weekly l ON l.fiscal_week = t.fiscal_week AND l.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE t.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY t.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar: this year is FY2026/27 (period 2 runs 1 to 28 June 2026, fiscal weeks 5 to 8) and last year is FY2025/26 (period 2 runs 26 May to 22 June 2025, fiscal weeks 5 to 8)
Net sales = line value excluding VAT after line discounts (fact_sales_line.net_amount), less refunds excluding VAT (fact_return_line.refund_net) booked on the return date, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Total company sales = all physical stores plus the web shop (store 900), covering web home delivery and click-and-collect
Weeks compared by fiscal week number (week 5 against week 5, and so on)
Growth % = this year / last year - 1, in percent
Sale date taken as sale_date (local date), not the UTC timestamp
Amounts in EUR excluding VAT
assumptions: 'This year' is FY2026/27 and 'last year' is FY2025/26, based on the request date of 5 October 2026. 'Period 2' means fiscal period 2, not calendar month 2.

'Sales' is read as net sales after returns, the company's net sales measure in rpt_daily_store_sales. Sales before returns would be 365,073 / 382,301 / 258,294 / 364,723 this year and 345,894 / 349,608 / 346,618 / 242,351 last year for weeks 5 to 8.
Returns are deducted in the week they are booked (return date), not the week of the original sale.
Staff purchases are kept in sales. They are about 1% of the total and the request did not ask to exclude them.
Total company sales is taken as reported, not like-for-like. Stores that closed or were shut for a refit are left in the comparison.
Growth is calculated on the unrounded sales figures.
caveats: Correction: the Training store (store_id 999) is excluded from both years. It has small test-style sales, mostly staff-flagged, of about 300 to 900 EUR a week, and it is not company trading.

Correction: web sales are taken from fact_sales_line using the web shop location (store 900), not from channel_code. Since the web-platform migration, web and click-and-collect lines have channel_code NULL and channel_id 2 or 3. rpt.v_daily_sales picks web lines by channel_code = 'WB', so it would drop all of this year's web sales.

Correction: I did not use rpt_daily_store_sales for the answer. Its web rows do not match the fact tables. For example, 7 June 2026 shows 13 receipts and 784 EUR against about 9,949 EUR of web lines in fact_sales_line, and its weekly web totals differ from the fact tables in every week. The answer is built from fact_sales_line and fact_return_line.

Midsummer is in different fiscal weeks. Last year it fell in week 8 (20 and 21 June 2025, stores shut by law), this year in week 7 (19 and 20 June 2026). Week 7 growth of -26.5% and week 8 growth of +54.4% mostly reflect that shift and say little about trading. Weeks 5 and 6 are clean, with no store-shut days either year (the Ascension Day and Whit Sunday holidays in last year's weeks 5 and 6 did not close stores). Comparing this year's week 7 with last year's Midsummer week 8 gives +6.8%.
Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a planned refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, so it has no sales in weeks 7 and 8 this year. Last year it sold about 11.6k in week 7 and 6.7k in week 8.
Savonlinna (store 129) closed permanently on 25 January 2026, so it has no sales this year. The store count was 39 physical stores last year, 38 in weeks 5 and 6 this year and 37 in weeks 7 and 8.
Excluding the closed stores (125 and 129), like-for-like growth is 6.3%, 9.9%, -23.2% and 60.7% for weeks 5 to 8. The Midsummer shift is the main distortion in weeks 7 and 8.

Click-and-collect is a separate web channel (channel_id 3) from this year. Last year's web lines have no channel_id, but last year's web orders were already split between home delivery and click-and-collect in fact_web_order. Both are included in both years, so the comparison is consistent.
No duplicate sales or return lines, cancelled web orders or failed VAT checks were found in the period. All of period 2 is loaded in both years.

answer.sql: SELECT d.calendar_year, d.calendar_month, ROUND(SUM(f.gross_amount), 2) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' AND s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Store sales: physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop (store 900) is not included
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test left out of all sales reporting
Including VAT: sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, so each line keeps its own VAT rate (no flat rate applied to a net total)
Before returns: fact_return_line not used
Staff purchases included (they count in sales, only ATV excludes them)
Dated by sale_date, the Helsinki business date

Control total: net amounts for the same stores and days agree with rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales_before_returns, store by store and day by day (net 1,101,807.91 for August and 964,016.09 for September)
Only canonical tables used (fact_sales_line, dim_store, dim_product, dim_date); no deprecated, staging, backup or tmp objects and no channel_code
assumptions: August 2024 and September 2024 are read as calendar months (1 to 31 August and 1 to 30 September 2024), because the request names months and not fiscal periods. Fiscal periods would give different figures.

'Store sales' is read as the physical stores only, excluding the web shop. If web is wanted too, store 900 would add 178,692.70 for August and 163,747.34 for September (gross, on the order date, not the dispatch date).
Both months are sales as they stand in the current warehouse; store sales are not restated for any hierarchy, so as-is or as-was does not matter for a company-wide figure.
caveats: No data problems were found for these months, so no correction was made. The checks were: no duplicate sales lines (line IDs and receipt+line keys are unique), no null or inconsistent gross amounts (gross equals net times (1 + VAT rate) to the cent on every line), and no non-positive amounts.

The VAT rate change on 1 September 2024 (general rate 24% to 25.5%) is already in the line data: the last line of 31 August carries 24% and the first of 1 September carries 25.5%. Part of the fall from August to September is therefore mix of days and rates, not a like-for-like trend. August has 31 days and September 30, and gross sales for the two months should not be compared as growth.

Filters that changed the total: the stores group contained no store 999 or ZZ Test lines in these months, so excluding them does not change the store figures. The excluded store 999 lines were 4,068.06 (gross, incl. 186.93 test articles) in August and 3,250.61 (plus 98.04) in September, and are all outside the 'stores' group anyway.
Returns are not deducted, as requested. The figures are therefore not net sales and will not match a net-sales report that includes returns.
The control against rpt_daily_store_sales can only be made on net amounts (the report has no gross column and no VAT split). The gross figures rest on the line-level check above.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(date_trunc('month', f.sale_date), '%Y-%m') AS calendar_month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' AND s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900)
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test left out
Including VAT: sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, each line at its own VAT rate
Before returns: no refunds deducted
Store lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Staff purchases included
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales_before_returns)
assumptions: 'August 2024' and 'September 2024' read as calendar months (1-31 August, 1-30 September 2024), not fiscal periods, because the request names calendar months
'Store sales' read as the physical stores only; the web shop (store 900) is not included
Figures are in EUR including VAT
Staff purchases are included, as in the company sales definition
History is as-is; no region or category breakdown was requested, so the hierarchy does not affect the totals
caveats: Corrections made: store 999 and ZZ Test lines were left out. No ZZ Test lines appeared in the physical stores; store 999 was already outside the store_id < 900 scope, so no total changed.

The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. Each line carries its own rate: August standard-rate lines are at 24% and September at 25.5%. Gross/net is therefore about 1.239 in August and 1.254 in September, so the month-to-month change mixes a sales change with a rate change. Gross was not computed by applying one flat rate to net sales.

Checks: gross_amount equals net_amount x (1 + vat_rate) on every line. No duplicate lines were found (receipt_id plus line_no, and sales_line_id, are unique). Every trading day in both months has sales. The sale_date matches the Helsinki date of the UTC timestamp on every line.

The same lines excluding VAT total 1,101,807.91 for August and 964,016.09 for September. These agree to the cent with rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns for the physical stores, so the line set is the same as the control table's.

Returns are not deducted, as requested. Refunds booked in these months were 51,492.65 (August) and 45,299.75 (September) excluding VAT. The company dictionary does not say how returns enter a figure including VAT, and none were applied.
Web sales are excluded. If Finance wants stores plus web, that is a separate request, and web sales are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date rather than the order date.

answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
sales_by_month AS (
    SELECT 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date)) AS sales_year,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date)) AS sales_month,
        SUM(f.gross_amount) AS gross_sales_incl_vat
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date)) = 2024
      AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date)) IN (8, 9)
    GROUP BY 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date)),
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date))
)
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN sales_month = 8 THEN 'August 2024'
        WHEN sales_month = 9 THEN 'September 2024'
    END AS month,
    gross_sales_incl_vat
FROM sales_by_month
ORDER BY sales_month
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT (sum of gross_amount from sales lines)
Net sales scope (excluded store 999 and category ZZ Test)
Web sales recognition on Helsinki dispatch date
VAT rate change on 1 September 2024 (24% to 25.5% general rate)
assumptions: Total company sales (all stores combined, not per-store breakdown)
Before returns means sales lines from specified months, unadjusted for returns
Calendar dates: August 2024 (1-31 Aug) and September 2024 (1-30 Sep)
Web orders included using their dispatch dates in Helsinki time
caveats: Gross sales (including VAT) differ from rpt_daily_store_sales control totals, which report net sales excluding VAT
Exclusions: store 999 (web shop) and category ZZ Test per company definition; no data quality issues detected
Requested calendar months do not align with fiscal period boundaries (request spans FY2024/25 P04-P06)
VAT rates correctly summed per individual line; the 24%-to-25.5% change on 1 September 2024 is reflected in line-level gross amounts

answer.sql: WITH dedup AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_units, closing_value FROM fact_stock_week WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22'), weekly AS (SELECT d.week_ending_date, cp.category, SUM(d.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM dedup d JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = d.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = d.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE cs.region = 'West' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 11 AS fiscal_period, category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value FROM weekly GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a week-end snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week first, then averaged across the weeks of the period, never summed across weeks
Stock value is closing_value, at standard cost, excluding web stock (the web is picked from the central warehouse and is not in fact_stock_week)
Fiscal period 11 = fiscal weeks 44 to 47, week-ending Sundays 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026 (23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026), from dim_date via fiscal.py
As-is hierarchy: region and category taken from the current version of dim_store and dim_product
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900); store 999 and the web shop 900 excluded
Category ZZ Test excluded
Snapshot rows are only for articles the store ranges
assumptions: 'Last year' on 5 October 2026 (inside FY2026/27) is read as the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26. This follows the readings accepted for requests made in May 2026. Period 11 of FY2025/26 is 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026. FY2025/26 is the 53-week year, but week 53 falls in period 12, so period 11 is a normal four weeks.
'Average stock value' is the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost. It is not a sum over the weeks and not the last week's closing.

'West region' and 'category' are as-is, the current hierarchy. For this period as-was gives the same answer: all nine West stores (115 to 123 and 136) were West in the snapshot and today, and no article changed category between the snapshot and its current version. The outdoor lighting move to Electrical was in October 2025, before this period.

West covers the nine stores 115 Tampere Hervanta, 116 Tampere Lielahti, 117 Tampere Kaleva, 118 Nokia, 119 Pori, 120 Rauma, 121 Vaasa, 122 Seinäjoki and 123 Kokkola, plus 136 Tampere Lamminpää (ten stores in all). Values are EUR at standard cost.
caveats: Correction: the stock snapshot for the week ending 8 March 2026 was loaded twice. 7,439 of the West store-article rows are exact duplicates (same keys and same units and values), reloaded on 10 March at 02:45 after the original load on 9 March. Across the whole warehouse the week has 34,600 rows against 27,161 distinct store-article keys. Left in, the duplicates would add about 0.81 million EUR to that week's West total and inflate the period average by about 0.2 million EUR (roughly 25%). I kept one row per store, article and week with SELECT DISTINCT.
After the de-duplication every store-article-week is unique and closing_value equals closing_units x standard unit cost on every row, so there are no other problems in the snapshot for these weeks.

The category figures add up to 813,525.02 EUR, the average weekly West stock value across the four weeks. The weekly totals were 816,086.49, 813,641.20, 812,053.77 and 812,318.58. I did not add the weekly values together.

The week ending 1 March 2026 has 38 more West store-article rows than the other three weeks (7,477 against 7,439), because it carries a few more ranged articles. Nothing is repeated there, and I left them in.
Stock is valued at standard cost, not retail value. It covers ranged articles in the physical West stores only, with no web stock and no stock held in the central warehouse.
The control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales applies to sales, not to stock, so it was not run for this request.

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND s.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY 1, 2), returns AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, sum(r.refund_net) AS returns_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND s.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY 1, 2), weekly AS (SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_week, s.sales_net - coalesce(r.returns_net, 0) AS net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN returns r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_week)) SELECT t.fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, t.fiscal_week, t.net_sales AS net_sales, l.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, round(100.0 * (t.net_sales / l.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly t JOIN weekly l ON l.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND l.fiscal_week = t.fiscal_week WHERE t.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY t.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales lines net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns
Returns are deducted in the week of the return date, not the week of the original sale, matching rpt_daily_store_sales
Total company = all physical stores plus the web shop (store_id 900)
Training store (store_id 999) excluded as a non-trading pseudo-location
Fiscal calendar: period 2 = fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (FY2026/27: 1 to 28 June 2026; FY2025/26: 26 May to 22 June 2025), Monday to Sunday weeks from dim_date
Prior-year comparison by same fiscal year, period and week number (FY2025/26 weeks 5 to 8)
growth_pct = (this year / last year - 1) x 100, rounded to 1 decimal
assumptions: 'This year' is read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (request dated 7 Oct 2026). P02 of FY2026/27 is fully loaded in the warehouse.
'Same weeks last year' is read as the same fiscal week numbers in FY2025/26, not the same calendar dates.
'Net sales' is read as after returns, ex VAT, following the warehouse's own net sales definition in rpt_daily_store_sales.
Staff purchases are kept in net sales (no rule excludes them, and the existing daily report includes them). They are about 1% of store sales.
Web click-and-collect and home-delivery orders are both counted, dated by order date (sale_date). Cancelled orders have no sales lines, so they do not count.
caveats: Correction 1: web sales are identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code. After the web-platform migration (November 2025) channel_code is NULL on all lines and channel_id is used instead, with both coding styles in November 2025. The view rpt.v_daily_sales filters web on channel_code = 'WB', so it would miss all web sales from November 2025 on, including all of this year's P02. I did not use it.

Correction 2: the web row in rpt_daily_store_sales (store 900) is dated by dispatch date rather than sale date. Its daily and weekly figures differ from the sales facts: web sales before returns for the four weeks of FY2026/27 P02 are about 231k in the report against 254k in the fact table. I took web sales from fact_sales_line by sale date. The store rows in the report do reconcile to the fact table.
Correction 3: the training store (store_id 999) has small sales (about 0.2 to 0.9k a week) that do not belong in company net sales, so I excluded them.

Weeks 7 and 8 are distorted by Midsummer. Midsummer Eve and Day (stores shut by law) fall on 19 to 20 June 2026 in FY2026/27 week 7, but on 20 to 21 June 2025 in FY2025/26 week 8. Week 7 is therefore -26.5% and week 8 +54.4% on a fiscal-week basis. Neither is a real trend. Over all of P02 net sales are 1,296k against 1,211k last year, +7.0%.

Store 125 is closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 (weeks 7 and 8 of this year), which lowers this year's figures slightly in those weeks. Total company net sales are as requested and not adjusted for it.

Net sales here include web returns, which are booked against the web shop. The store-only figures in rpt_daily_store_sales do not tie to the totals above, because that report's web figures use the dispatch-date basis.

Checks that came out clean: no duplicate sales or return lines, no orphan store keys or return links, VAT arithmetic consistent, no zero or negative sales lines, no refund above the original line value.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), sales AS (SELECT CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN w.dispatch_date ELSE f.sale_date END AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT region, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount END), 2) AS august_2024_gross_sales_incl_vat, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount END), 2) AS september_2024_gross_sales_incl_vat FROM sales WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines (each line carries its own VAT rate)
Before returns: fact_return_line not netted off
As-was regions: region of the store version on the transaction (fact store_key joined to dim_store)
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered and collected orders only, so cancelled orders are excluded
Web shop (store 900) reported as its own region, Online
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Calendar months: August is 1-31 Aug 2024 and September is 1-30 Sep 2024
Helsinki time for web dispatch dates
assumptions: August and September 2024 read as calendar months, not fiscal periods, because the figures are for a VAT filing
Regions as they were at the time read as as-was, so the four regions (East, North, South, West) in use in 2024, before the Capital Region was created on 28 April 2025
Online (web shop) is shown as a fifth row because web sales belong to no physical region

Web sales are dated on the dispatch date, as in the company definition, not the order date. Orders placed in late September but dispatched in October are therefore not in September, and August orders dispatched in early September are in September
Gross sales are sales lines only, with no returns deducted, as the request says before returns
caveats: The VAT rate for the general rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. August standard-rate lines carry 24% and September lines 25.5%; the figures use each line's own gross_amount, so no flat rate was applied. Reduced rates (14% and 10%) did not change.
Excluded 283 store-999 lines and 68 ZZ Test lines in the period (by sale date) as non-reporting transactions.
Cancelled web orders are excluded. Without this filter they would be dated on their order date and wrongly included in gross sales.
Basis check: the same query on net_amount before returns matches rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales_before_returns) exactly, 2,333,805.81 EUR for 1 Aug to 30 Sep 2024, with no store-level gaps.
Web gross sales follow the company's dispatch-date recognition. If the VAT filing needs web sales on the order date or invoice date instead, the Online row would change.
Region labels are as-was and differ from the current five-region management reporting: Capital Region stores sit in South here, and Kouvola sits in East.
Tampere Lamminpää opened 2 September 2024 and is included under its region as it traded; there were no data errors, duplicates or missing dimension keys in the range.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN wo.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(DISTINCT wo.web_order_id), 2) as click_collect_share_pct FROM fact_web_order wo INNER JOIN dim_date d ON DATE(wo.order_ts_utc) = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10) GROUP BY d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales defined as orders in fact_web_order table
Click-and-collect share calculated as count of orders with fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' divided by total distinct web orders
Orders identified by web_order_id
Fiscal period assignment based on order timestamp (order_ts_utc) mapped to dim_date
assumptions: Last year interpreted as fiscal year FY2025/26 (the immediately preceding fiscal year from current fiscal year FY2026/27)
Click-and-collect share expressed as a percentage
One row per fiscal period as requested
caveats: Warehouse data is current as of 2026-10-04; request received 2026-10-06 is within the data window
Click-and-collect orders identified by fulfilment_type column value 'click_and_collect'
Orders counted by distinct web_order_id; orders with multiple lines are counted once

answer.sql: SELECT cs.store_id, cs.store_name, 'Cleaning Products' AS subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE cs.store_name = 'Hyvinkää' AND cs.store_id <> 999 AND cp.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2026/27 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), filtered on dim_date fiscal_year and fiscal_period
Units sold is the quantity on sales lines, by sale_date
Physical store scope: store_id 107, with store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
As-is product hierarchy: subcategory taken from the current dim_product version, joined on sku and is_current
Control total against rpt_daily_store_sales (store-level check)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
assumptions: 'This year' is the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 5' is fiscal period 5 of that year. It is the last complete period.
'Cleaning Products' is a subcategory of the category Cleaning & Household. There is no category with that name.
'Units sold' means gross units sold on sales lines. Returns are not netted off.
Hyvinkää is store 107, the only store with that name, with a single version in dim_store.
Staff purchases are included. Of the store's 1,626 units sold in P5 across all categories, 31 were staff purchases.
caveats: No data problems found and no corrections made. There were no duplicate sales lines, no non-positive quantities, no test articles and no store 999 lines in the selection.
Control total: Hyvinkää's P5 units sold across all categories were 1,626, with 410 receipts and EUR 27,297.68 net sales before returns. This matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly.
The 136 units come from 63 sales lines. The subcategory is the same in the product version on the sale date and in the current version, so as-is and as-was give the same figure.
No Cleaning Products returns were booked at Hyvinkää in P5, so net-of-returns units would also be 136.
Store 107 has no web lines, because web sales sit under pseudo-store 900. This is a store figure only.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY p.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2026/27 is 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (weeks 18 to 21 of the 4-4-5 pattern, four weeks)
Units sold is the quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date), as in the weeks-of-cover definition
Store scope: store_id 102 Helsinki Pitäjänmäki (all store versions, joined through the store_key on each line)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither changed the result)
Products counted by stable sku, named from the current product version
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Deprecated objects, rpt.v_daily_sales and the stg_, bak_ and tmp_ tables not used
Control total: units from fact_sales_line (3,740) equal rpt_daily_store_sales units_sold for store 102 over the same 28 days
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 5' as its last completed period, which ended on 27 September 2026 (request received 7 October 2026)
'Units sold' read as gross units on sales lines, not netted for returns, because no company definition of units nets them
'Top 3' ranked by units, with ties broken by sku (no tie occurred among the top 3)
Store sales only: the web shop (store 900) is a separate pseudo-store and click-and-collect orders do not appear on store 102's lines
caveats: No data problems found for this store and period: no duplicate sales lines, no non-positive quantities, each top-3 sku has a single product version and name, and the units reconcile exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales (3,740)
Returns were not deducted. Only one returned unit appears among the top 3 (one unit of sku 102244 in the period), which does not change the ranking
Store 102 moved from region South to Capital Region on 28 April 2025. This does not affect a store-level answer

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, p.sku FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_quarter, cp.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(r.refund_net, 0)) / SUM(sold.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = sold.sku AND cp.is_current LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.sales_line_id = sold.sales_line_id WHERE cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory <> 'Outdoor Lighting' GROUP BY cp.subcategory ORDER BY cp.subcategory
definitions_applied: Return rate: refund_net divided by sold net_amount, both excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: sold lines selected by the fiscal quarter of fact_sales_line.sale_date, with refunds matched through sales_line_id whenever and wherever they were booked, web included
As-is hierarchy: category and subcategory taken from the current product version (dim_product.is_current, joined on sku)
Outdoor lighting treated as Electrical for all history (moved from Garden on 27 October 2025)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (FY2025/26 Q1 = fiscal weeks 1 to 13, 28 April to 27 July 2025)
Deprecated objects not used (no stg_, bak_, tmp_, old dim tables, rpt.v_ views, channel_code)
assumptions: 'Q1 of last year' on 6 October 2026 (current year FY2026/27) is read as FY2025/26 Q1, 28 April to 27 July 2025. This follows past readings of 'last year' made in FY2026/27 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).
Hierarchy is as-is, since the request did not ask for as-was. Category management reporting restates history on the current hierarchy.
All channels are included (stores and the web shop, store 900), as in the accepted return-rate queries REQ-D14 to D16. Web is not shown separately because the request did not ask for it.
Staff purchases are kept in, as in the sales definitions.
caveats: Correction 1: five outdoor-lighting articles (SKUs 100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) were delisted before the 27 October 2025 move. They never got an Electrical version, so the current dim_product row still says Garden / Outdoor Lighting. Read literally, this gives a spurious 'Outdoor Lighting' row under Garden (19 lines, EUR 375 sold, no returns, rate 0.0%). I treated them as Electrical, as the as-is rule requires, and removed that row. The remaining outdoor lighting (68 articles) is Electrical as-is, so Garden has seven subcategories. Electrical Outdoor Lighting would have shown 7.22% for the same quarter.
Correction 2: store 999 (390 sales lines in the quarter) and ZZ Test articles were excluded.

Returns on the quarter's sales that arrived later are all included. The warehouse is loaded to 4 October 2026, past the 30-day return window, so the cohort is complete. 439 return lines in the data arrived more than 30 days after the sale and are counted.

Checks passed. No duplicate sales or return lines. No returns without a sales line, none dated before the sale, and none refunding more than the line value. No sales lines are lost in the store or product joins.

Sold values (EUR net) behind the rates: Barbecue & Grills 176074.46, Edible Plants & Seeds 74584.72, Garden Furniture 406939.18, Garden Tools 276601.44, Plants & Flowers 441427.45, Pots & Planters 144538.28, Soil & Fertiliser 147290.55.
The rpt_daily_store_sales control total was not run. It applies to store-level figures and not to a category subset, so it does not apply to this request.

Return rate is the value share (refund net divided by sold net), not a unit share. It is dated by the sale quarter, not the return date, so it differs by design from net sales, which are dated by return date.

Gross amount (net_amount + VAT) used for sales including VAT

INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key
INNER JOIN dim_member dm ON fsl.member_key = dm.member_key

Tampere location = stores with city='Tampere' (physical stores only)
Excluded store 900 (web shop) and 999 (training store) per house rules
Excluded test articles (category ZZ Test) per house rules
assumptions: 'Customers in Tampere' interpreted as distinct members who have made purchases in Tampere stores
Counting only member purchases (excluding non-member cash sales)
Including all historical purchases (no date filter)
Reporting as-is (current store assignments)

Member versions (dim_member) can change over time; counted by stable member_id
Does not include members with home_store_id in Tampere who have not made purchases

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (the 3 November 2025 migration broke channel_code)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Cancelled and processing orders are not web sales
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern)
UTC timestamps converted to Helsinki time before taking the date
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (1 May 2025 to 3 May 2026 fiscal year, 28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026), because the request was received on 6 October 2026 in FY2026/27. Earlier accepted requests made in FY2026/27 used FY2025/26 for 'last year'.

'Periods 5 to 8' read as fiscal periods P05 to P08 of FY2025/26: P05 25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025, P06 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, P07 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025, P08 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025. All four are fully loaded, so week 53 is not involved.
'The web shop' read as web store 900, including click-and-collect orders. 'Net' read as the company net sales definition: excluding VAT, after returns.
One row per period, since the request asks for each period. No total row was given because none was asked for.
caveats: The 3 November 2025 web-platform migration falls inside P07. channel_code stops being filled from that date, so web was identified by store 900. rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales leave out web sales from that date and were not used.
Correction: one web test line in ZZ Test (5.50 EUR net, in P06) is excluded, as is all store 999. No other web lines were excluded.

Correction: cancelled and processing web orders have no sales lines, so they add nothing. Web revenue is dated by the Helsinki dispatch date, not by the order date, so some orders placed in an earlier period count in the period they were dispatched, and the reverse.

Returns are dated on the day the refund was booked and are booked to the web shop. A web return handled over a store counter would sit in that store's figures, not here. This follows the company definition.
The result agrees to the cent with rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 in each of the four periods.

Separate from this request: fact_sales_line has duplicate (receipt_id, line_no) pairs for store 116 in September 2025 (836 rows on 178 receipts, about 20,781 EUR net). No web lines are affected, so this answer is not. The store 116 duplicates should be looked at for any store-level request covering that month.
Figures exclude VAT. All dates are Helsinki business dates, and the warehouse is loaded to 4 October 2026, so the four periods are complete.

answer.sql: WITH targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 19), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, m.member_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM targeted) AS members_contacted, ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS net_sales_before_returns_eur FROM targeted t JOIN lines l ON l.member_id = t.member_id WHERE l.business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-05-24'
definitions_applied: Targeted member: at least one exposure row in the campaign, counted as distinct member_id through dim_member
Net sales before returns, EUR excluding VAT, on lines linked to the member, as in the campaign uplift definition
Web lines dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered or collected orders only)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included, since they count in net sales
Member lines matched to people through member_id, not member_key, so every member version is picked up
Holdout members checked against the contacted group, by member_id
assumptions: The campaign is Spring Garden Launch 2026 (campaign_id 19), window 4 to 24 May 2026. That is the same range Sanna asked for, so no extra days were added. The uplift definition adds 7 days, but I followed the stated dates.
'Contacted' means at least one row in fact_campaign_exposure, whether or not it was delivered or opened. Counting only delivered contacts would give 14,814 members.
'Spend' means net sales before returns, excluding VAT, matching the campaign convention. Returns are not deducted and VAT is not included.
Spend covers only the contacted members, all channels (stores and web). It is not an uplift figure against the holdout.
Members with no purchases in the window add nothing to the spend. The count of members contacted is not limited to buyers.
caveats: Counting rows or member_key would overstate the contacted members. The exposure table has 31,685 rows and 15,063 member_keys for this campaign, but only 15,001 distinct members, because contacts are one row each and some members have several versions in dim_member. I reduced to distinct member_id.

Of the 15,001 contacted members, 2,605 made at least one purchase in the window (8,080 lines). Of the 190,687.59 EUR, 155,518.67 is from stores and 35,168.92 from the web shop. These two figures are not in the result table.

Web purchases are counted on their dispatch date, not the order date. Web orders placed before 4 May but dispatched in the window are included. Orders placed in the window but dispatched after 24 May are excluded.

I checked that no contacted member is also in the campaign_holdout list (0 overlap, 1,597 holdout members). No contact was made to a member without marketing consent, or outside the campaign window, or before the member's join date.

The campaign record says the mailing list had 16,624 members including 1,597 held out. The contacted count (15,001) is lower than the roughly 15,027 you would get by subtracting. I could not trace the difference of about 26 from the warehouse alone, because the stated mailing list cannot be rebuilt from the current consent flags. The 15,001 comes from the actual contact records.
The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply here, since this is a member subset.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT p.sku, w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT p.sku, r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales) DESC) AS rank, n.sku, cp.product_name, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-03' AND DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY n.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is empty from 3 November 2025)
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (status delivered or collected only)
Click-and-collect counted as web, dated on the ready-for-collection date in Helsinki time
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Product identified by stable sku, named from the current dim_product version (as-is)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Since the platform migration on 3 November 2025' means web sales dispatched from 3 November 2025 (Helsinki date) up to the end of the warehouse load, Sunday 4 October 2026, inclusive.
'Web sales' means net sales excluding VAT, ranked by value rather than units.
Returns are counted where the company definition books them: refunds processed at the web shop (store 900), on the return date.
Products are ranked by sku, so product versions are merged and the current product name is shown.
caveats: Corrections: I did not use channel_code or the deprecated rpt.v_daily_sales view, which lose web sales after 3 November 2025. I used store_id 900 and dispatch dates from fact_web_order.

Corrections: 1,296 orders were left out as not yet web sales: 1,062 cancelled click-and-collect orders and 78 processing click-and-collect orders, plus 2,766 cancelled and 218 processing home-delivery orders. Cancelled orders have no lines, and processing orders have none until dispatch.
Corrections: test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 were filtered out. Neither affected the top 10.

Control total: web sales of 2,359,008.09 less refunds of 208,918.02 give 2,150,090.07 for store 900 over 3 Nov 2025 to 4 Oct 2026. This matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly. It is a total for all products, so it does not check individual product figures.

Web purchases returned in a physical store are refunded in that store's books and are not deducted here, following the company definition. Deducting them would change the order. Bedroom Peltola 793 would drop from 3rd to 4th and Garden Furniture Raudikko 536 would rise from 4th to 3rd. Garden Furniture Norvik 499 would fall from 8th to 10th and Home Office Peltola 918 from 10th to 14th. Sauna & Winter Havu 699 would rise from 9th to 8th and Christmas Decorations Kuusela 620 from 11th to 9th.

Ranking before returns would differ more. Bedroom Peltola 793 would be 1st (15,533.23 before returns), and Interior Paint Norvik 298 and Christmas Decorations Poutaranta Home 601 would be 2nd and 3rd.
Several of the top 10 are seasonal (Christmas decorations, garden furniture, sauna and winter), so the ranking depends on the 11-month window.
The data runs to 4 October 2026 only.
Dates use the Helsinki time zone for web dispatch.

answer.sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sale_date) AS calendar_year, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sale_date) AS calendar_month, SUM(gross_amount) AS sales_including_vat_eur FROM fact_sales_line WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sale_date) = 2024 AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sale_date) IN (8, 9) GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sale_date), EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sale_date) ORDER BY calendar_month
definitions_applied: Gross sales amount from fact_sales_line, which includes VAT
Before returns: original transaction amounts, not adjusted for refunds
All sales channels combined (physical store and web)
assumptions: 'Store sales' interpreted as all sales channels operated by Tuomimetsä stores (ST = physical store, WB = web), not physical stores only
Calendar months: August = 8, September = 9
Included all sale types: regular purchases, staff purchases, and all customer segments
caveats: Web sales (WB channel) represent approximately 11-12% of these totals (August: EUR 174,410; September: EUR 160,396). If reporting requires physical store locations only (ST channel), the figures would be August: EUR 1,369,364 and September: EUR 1,212,264.
Staff purchase flag is present in the data but not applied as a filter; verify with the requester whether staff purchases should be excluded

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount, f.staff_purchase_flag, COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS first_period, 3 AS last_period, ROUND(SUM(l.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT l.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date WHERE NOT l.staff_purchase_flag AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 1 AND 3
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR excluding VAT) divided by the number of sales receipts
Staff purchases excluded from ATV (staff_purchase_flag)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store_id 900) identified by store, not channel_code; click-and-collect counted as web
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected orders count (cancelled and processing orders have no sales lines)
Store sales dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Fiscal calendar: this year = FY2026/27; P1 to P3 = fiscal weeks 1 to 13 = 4 May to 2 August 2026 (complete, loaded)
Returns not netted off (ATV is before returns)
Control total: net sales before returns across stores and web (including staff purchases) matches rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days exactly (4,539,452.02 and 81,025 receipts)
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27, and 'periods 1 to 3' as FY2026/27 P1 to P3 (Q1, 4 May to 2 August 2026)

ATV is the company-wide average over all receipts in the three periods (total net sales divided by total receipts), not an average of period or store ATVs; one figure for the whole company as requested, no breakdown

Each web order is counted as one transaction (equal to one receipt, since receipt_id equals web_order_id) and its net sales are taken on the dispatch date, the same date basis as the numerator, so numerator and denominator cover the same orders
Staff purchases left out of the web part as well, as in the store definition (there are none on the web in this range anyway)
caveats: Correction to the company ATV definition: the dictionary defines ATV as a store measure with web orders not included. You asked for web orders in, so I followed the request and included them. This is a departure from the company default.

For reference, stores only on the standard definition: 55.52 (3,719,186.33 EUR over 66,984 receipts). Web only: 59.33 (771,530.75 EUR over 13,004 orders). Combined: 4,490,717.08 EUR over 79,988 receipts = 56.14.
Correction: staff purchases excluded (1,037 store receipts, 48,734.94 EUR), as the ATV definition requires.
Correction: store 999 excluded (132 staff-training receipts and 54 test-article receipts) and three web test orders containing only ZZ Test articles (6.00 EUR) excluded.

Web orders are dated by dispatch date, not order date. On an order-date basis the order count would differ slightly (roughly 12,962 orders against 13,004), so the web ATV and the combined figure would move marginally. Cancelled orders are excluded from the web side; no orders in the range were still processing.
Click-and-collect orders are included as web, dated on the ready-for-collection date.
The deprecated views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used; they omit web sales from 3 November 2025.
The result is in EUR excluding VAT.

answer.sql: WITH ytd AS (SELECT DATE '2026-05-04' AS start_date, DATE '2026-10-04' AS end_date), sales AS (SELECT s.region, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key CROSS JOIN ytd WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN ytd.start_date AND ytd.end_date AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.channel_id = 1 GROUP BY s.region), refunds AS (SELECT s.region, sum(r.refund_net) AS refunds_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key CROSS JOIN ytd WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN ytd.start_date AND ytd.end_date AND s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY s.region) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY sales.sales_net - coalesce(refunds.refunds_net, 0) DESC) AS rank, sales.region, round(sales.sales_net - coalesce(refunds.refunds_net, 0), 2) AS net_sales_eur FROM sales LEFT JOIN refunds USING (region) ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net amount excluding VAT, less refunds (refund_net) booked on the return date, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Fiscal year FY2026/27, starting 2026-05-04 per ref_fiscal_calendar
Stores only: web shop (store_id 900, channel_ids 2 and 3) excluded
Training store (store_id 999) excluded as a pseudo-location
Regions from dim_store at the sale date: since 2025-04-28 the Helsinki-area stores sit in 'Capital Region', which is the fifth region alongside North, South, East and West
Refunds are attributed to the store where the return was booked, not the store of the original sale
assumptions: 'How they are doing' is read as total net sales (EUR, excluding VAT) for the fiscal year to date, highest first. Region size therefore drives the order. This is not a growth or per-store measure.

'This year so far' is the fiscal year FY2026/27 from 2026-05-04 to 2026-10-04, the end of fiscal week 22, the last full week loaded. Period P06 is flagged not fully loaded because it is still running.
Staff purchases are included in net sales. I found no rule to exclude them, and they are about 1.3% of store sales.
The five regions are the current ones in dim_store: North, South, East, West and Capital Region.
Ties and near-ties are ranked on the exact figure. East and Capital Region are about 1.1% apart.
caveats: Correction: web shop sales (store 900, channel_ids 2 and 3) are excluded. rpt_daily_store_sales includes store 900, so summing that table over all stores would overstate store sales by about 1.2m EUR before returns. I computed from the fact tables instead. For stores 101-139 the report matches the fact table.
Correction: the training store (999, about 13k EUR, 94% staff purchases) is excluded.

Correction: from this year channel_code is NULL on sales lines (only channel_id is filled), and before the web migration (up to FY2025/26 P06) channel_id is NULL. I identified stores by store_id < 900 and channel_id = 1 and did not rely on channel_code.

Correction: the Capital Region split from South (and Kouvola moved from East to South) on 2025-04-28. Using the old or temporary region lists, or old region labels, would show four regions and misstate the comparison with last year.
Net sales deducts refunds of 292k EUR across the stores. A rank on sales before returns gives the same order.
The same order holds if the period is cut at the end of P05 (2026-09-27): West, South, East, Capital Region, North.

East's total is lowered by the Kuopio refit closure (store 125, 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-26, 6 weeks). Without that closure East would probably rank higher against Capital Region, which is only 1.1% behind it.
Savonlinna (store 129, East) closed on 2026-01-25 and has no sales this year. It is not in the East figure. East's year-on-year comparison is affected by this closure.

Ranking by size is not the same as ranking by trend. In a rough comparison with the same fiscal weeks last year (week 1 to week 22 of FY2025/26), excluding closed stores and refit stores, growth in store net sales was North +3.8%, Capital Region +2.7%, South +2.1%, West +1.6% and East -1.2%. If Finance wants performance against last year, the order would be different. I can produce that on request.
Store Kemi (133) has no sales on one trading day, 2026-08-31. Neighbouring days are about 300-500 EUR, so the effect is negligible. I did not adjust for it.
stg_sales_line_load duplicates the last two days already in fact_sales_line (same line ids, 3,118 lines). I did not add them, so nothing is double counted.
The warehouse comments describe formats as Hyper, Standard and Express, but the data holds Large, Medium and Small. This does not affect the regional result.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order o WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines
Counted on the order date in Helsinki time (UTC timestamp converted to Europe/Helsinki)
Cancelled orders excluded; processing orders would be included (none on this day)
Click-and-collect orders counted as web orders
Guest and logged-in orders both counted
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is taken as Monday 1 December 2025, as stated in the request
'Placed' is read as the order date (order_ts_utc in Helsinki time), not the dispatch date
Cancelled orders are not counted as orders placed, following the company web-order definition
Home delivery and click-and-collect are both included
caveats: order_ts_utc is stored in UTC. Filtering on the UTC date instead of the Helsinki date would give 274 orders, 52 too few, because the Helsinki day runs from 22:00 UTC on 30 November to 22:00 UTC on 1 December. I used the Helsinki date.
18 orders placed that day are cancelled and are excluded: 2 click-and-collect guest, 3 home delivery guest, 4 click-and-collect logged-in, 10 home delivery logged-in. Counting them would give 344.
Of the 326 orders, 87 are click-and-collect (collected), 239 are home delivery (delivered). All 326 are guest or logged-in orders with no test articles (category ZZ Test) among them.

I did not use channel_code or the sales-line table to count orders. channel_code is not filled after the 3 November 2025 platform migration, and no sales line carries channel_code WB on 1 December 2025.
No duplicate web_order_id values were found in fact_web_order.

answer.sql: WITH days AS (SELECT calendar_date AS sale_date FROM dim_date WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23'), sales AS (SELECT sale_date, sum(net_amount) AS sales_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line WHERE channel_id IN (2,3) AND sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1), refunds AS (SELECT r.return_date AS sale_date, sum(r.refund_net) AS returns_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1) SELECT d.sale_date, COALESCE(s.sales_before_returns,0) - COALESCE(r.returns_net,0) AS net_sales FROM days d LEFT JOIN sales s USING (sale_date) LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sale_date) ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Net sales = line value in EUR excluding VAT (net_amount), less refunds (refund_net) booked on the day, the same split rpt_daily_store_sales uses
Web channel = channel_id 2 (web home delivery) plus 3 (click and collect), channel_group 'web', not the legacy channel_code
Web returns = refunds booked on the day at the web shop pseudo-location (store_id 900), by return_date
sale_date is the Helsinki local business date; it already lines up with the UTC timestamps (local midnight = 22:00 UTC in December)
Web orders sit under store_id 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop), not any physical store
assumptions: I read '(net)' as the company's net sales: EUR excluding VAT, after returns. Before returns, the same days are 13007.30, 16359.14, 10686.17, 11354.33, 11627.57, 7425.77, 7762.68, 12878.11 and 13459.24 for 15 to 23 December in order. Say if you want that version.
Dates 15 to 23 December 2025 are inclusive, calendar days in Finnish local time
Click and collect counts as web sales, since dim_channel puts it in channel_group 'web'
Staff purchases are included. None of the web lines in the window carry the flag, so this has no effect
Orders are counted on the sale date of their lines. All web orders in the window are delivered or collected, none cancelled or still processing
caveats: Correction: from the web-platform migration, web lines carry channel_code NULL and are identified only by channel_id (2 or 3). Filtering on channel_code = 'WB', as the view rpt.v_daily_sales does, would drop every web line in the window and return nothing for web.

364)), sales_dedup AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (receipt_id, line_no) * FROM fact_sales_line WHERE sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-10-28' AND DATE '2026-01-25' ORDER BY receipt_id, line_no, etl_loaded_at DESC), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-10-28' AND DATE '2026-01-25'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT cs.region, d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 27 AND 39 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.region, ROUND(ty.net_sales,2) AS this_year_net_sales, ROUND(ly.net_sales,2) AS last_year_net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS web_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 2 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period

"Before returns" is read as no refund deduction at all, so the figures are gross sales including VAT with refund_gross not subtracted.
The dictionary does not define a figure including VAT beyond summing gross_amount from the lines. I used that sum and did not apply any flat VAT rate to a net total.

The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, which falls in P5. P5 therefore mixes lines at 24% (orders placed before the change but dispatched after it) and 25.5%. I used the rate each line carries and did not restate anything to one rate. P4 is all 24% and P6 all 25.5% on standard-rate goods.

VAT). So the line selection is complete and has no duplicates, but the control table is net only, so it does not check the including-VAT figures directly.
I found no duplicate lines or missing lines. For every order in the range, the line count and the gross total agree with fact_web_order.
Because the figures are before returns, they are not net sales. Returns on web sales would lower them.

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key WHERE s.store_id<900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id<900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'), sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period=2 GROUP BY 1), trading AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs JOIN dim_date d ON d.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period=2 WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id<900 AND d.is_trading_day AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date<=d.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date>=d.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id=cs.store_id AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.net_sales/t.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ROUND(s.net_sales,2) AS net_sales, t.trading_days, ROUND(s.net_sales/t.trading_days,2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM sales s JOIN trading t ON t.store_id=s.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id=s.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank, cs.store_id
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day, physical stores only (store_id below 900)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT after returns, with returns reducing net sales on their own return date
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded (neither changed the totals in this period)
Web shop (store 900) excluded, as store-level analyses cover physical stores only
Trading days: days the store was open (after opening, before closure), outside ref_store_closure refit closures, and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2026/27 P02 = 1 June to 28 June 2026 (weeks 5 to 8, 4 weeks)
Store attributes (name) from the current dim_store version, via store_id
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days, store by store
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old tables) not used
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2 (1 to 28 June 2026), the fiscal year current on the request date of 7 October 2026. P2 is fully loaded and complete.
'Store ranking' read as the standard store league table: rank by net sales per trading day, highest first. Net sales and trading days are shown alongside.
Ties would share a rank (RANK); there are none in the result.
Net sales are shown as-is for the store attributes (store names from the current version). No region or format breakdown was requested, so none is shown.
The web shop is not ranked (stores only), and Savonlinna (129) is not listed because it had closed on 25 January 2026 and had no trading days in P2.
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026 (closure 15 June to 26 July), so it traded only 14 days in P2 (1 to 14 June) against 26 for every other store. It is ranked on its own trading days, per the rule, and ranks 7th at 1713.84 per day, with net sales of 23993.71 that are not comparable with the full-period stores.
Both Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed holidays, so every full-period store has 26 trading days, not 28.

Store-by-store net sales agree exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales for all 38 stores over 1 to 28 June 2026 (zero difference), and I found no duplicate sales lines (unique on sales_line_id and receipt/line) in the period. No corrections to the data were needed.

Returns are booked on their return date at the store that processed them, so a store's figure includes refunds for goods sold in earlier periods and excludes refunds for P2 sales that arrive after the period ends (the warehouse is loaded to 4 October 2026).
Staff purchases are included in net sales, as in the company definition. Amounts are in EUR excluding VAT.

answer.sql:
WITH net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date
                FROM dim_date
                WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27') AND fiscal_period = 4) d
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-08-03' - 364)
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_period = 4
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS this_year_net_sales, ly.net_sales AS last_year_net_sales,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM lfl_sales ty, lfl_sales ly
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL): same fiscal weeks last year, week by week, physical stores only, web shop excluded
LFL base rule: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the period (3 Aug 2026)
LFL store-week rule: a store-week counts only if the store traded in that week in both years (open and close dates, ref_store_closure)
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar: P4 = fiscal weeks 14 to 17 (FY2026/27: 3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026; FY2025/26: 28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025)
Single LFL total, no breakdown
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, channel_code, stg_/bak_/tmp_ tables) not used
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' read as FY2026/27 P4 (3 to 30 August 2026, weeks 14 to 17). P4 is a completed period, and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026.

One total (this year, last year, growth) because no breakdown was asked for.
LFL means the company LFL definition: physical stores only, web shop not included.
caveats: LFL net sales are essentially flat: 1,010,478.52 EUR this year against 1,010,743.32 EUR last year, a change of -0.03% (about -265 EUR).

Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 25 January 2026. It traded in P4 last year (about 9,913 EUR net sales) but not this year, so it is excluded from both years. Including it would have understated growth.

38 of the 39 physical stores are in the LFL base, giving 152 store-weeks (38 stores x 4 weeks). Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in 2024 and have been in the base since before this period.
No refit closures overlap P4 in either year. Kuopio's refit ended on 26 July 2026, the day before P4 started.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were filtered out. They sit only in store 999 and the web shop, so the physical-store total is unchanged by the filter.
Store-level net sales for P4, both years, matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for every store (no differences above 0.01 EUR).
Source rows were unique (no duplicate lines or returns) for the period in both years. I found no data problem that needed a correction.

Individual store-weeks vary widely year on year (for example store 105 weeks 16 and 17 are about 40% down, store 137 week 17 is about 87% up). These are real transactions that reconcile to the control table, so they were left in.
Returns arriving after P4 for goods sold in P4 are not relevant here, because LFL net sales put returns on their own return date.

definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: 'last period' is the last completed fiscal period
As-is product hierarchy (current product version by sku)
Web shop (store 900) included as part of the total company
Products identified by stable sku, not product_key version
assumptions: 'Last period' read as FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), the last completed fiscal period as of the request date 8 Oct 2026; P06 has only one week loaded
'Best-selling' read as ranked by net sales value in EUR excluding VAT, since the metric dictionary has no unit-based definition

Products are ranked by sku with name, category and brand from the current product version (as-is)
caveats: Ranking is by value. A ranking by units would differ, because some high-volume low-price articles (for example Fixings & Fasteners Nordhem 594 at 474 net units, Cushions & Throws Tuulikki 338 at 384) sell more units but less value. Ask if a unit ranking is wanted.

No duplicate sales lines were found in the period, and the query-check passed the deprecated-object, lint, row count and grain checks. Store keying and slowly-changing dimension valid_from/valid_to logic
assumptions: Interior Paint refers to the subcategory 'Interior Paint' in the Paint & Decorating category

Period 3 of FY2026/27 uses the official fiscal calendar date range

Returned units from fact_return_line (booked returns)
assumptions: 'This year' interpreted as current fiscal year FY2026/27
