answer.sql: WITH movements AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS movement_date, f.net_amount AS amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_week, round(sum(m.amount), 2) AS net_sales FROM movements m JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = m.movement_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2026/27') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3) SELECT t.fiscal_year, t.fiscal_period, t.fiscal_week, t.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, p.fiscal_year AS prior_fiscal_year, p.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, round(100.0 * (t.net_sales - p.net_sales) / p.net_sales, 2) AS growth_pct FROM weekly t JOIN weekly p ON p.fiscal_week = t.fiscal_week AND p.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE t.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY t.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns, with returns booked on the return date, not the original sale date. This matches how rpt_daily_store_sales builds net_sales.

Fiscal calendar from dim_date: period 2 = fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (Monday to Sunday weeks). FY2026/27 P02 runs 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-28. The prior-year comparison is FY2025/26 P02 (2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22), matched on the same fiscal week number.

Total company = all stores plus the web shop (store_id 900), covering home delivery and click-and-collect, with web returns netted. The training store (store_id 999) is excluded as a non-trading pseudo-location.

Channels identified through store_key and dim_store, not channel_code. Before 2025-11-03 lines carry channel_code (ST/WB) and a null channel_id. From 2025-11-03 they carry channel_id (1 store, 2 web home delivery, 3 click-and-collect) and a null channel_code. Filtering on either column alone would drop part of one of the two years.
Sale dates are already Finnish local business dates, so no UTC conversion was applied.
Growth % = (this year - last year) / last year x 100.
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (request dated 2026-10-07), and 'period 2' is fiscal period 2, not calendar month 2. FY2026/27 P02 is fully loaded.
'Same weeks last year' is read as the same fiscal week numbers (5 to 8) of FY2025/26, not the same calendar dates.

Staff purchases are included in net sales. No company rule excluding them was provided, they are real revenue, and rpt_daily_store_sales also includes them. They are about 1.2% of store sales; excluding them would lower each week by roughly 3,600 to 4,100 EUR.
Net sales is shown excluding VAT, per the warehouse net_amount definition.
All stores are included regardless of closures or openings (total company, not like-for-like).
caveats: Weeks 7 and 8 are not comparable like-for-like because of the Midsummer shift. Midsummer Eve and Day (stores shut by law, is_trading_day = false) fall on 19-20 June 2026 in fiscal week 7 this year, but on 20-21 June 2025 in fiscal week 8 last year. So week 7 this year (-26.48%) and week 8 (+54.37%) mostly reflect which week lost two trading days, not demand. Over the whole four-week period net sales are 1,295,948.28 against 1,210,935.82 last year, +7.02%. That is the more meaningful growth figure.

Store 125 was closed for a planned refit from 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-26, which covers weeks 7 and 8 this year. Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 2026-01-25, so its sales are in last year's weeks but not this year's. Store 129 is a negative contribution to growth in all four weeks, and store 125 in weeks 7 and 8, so total-company growth is understated against a like-for-like store base. The number of stores trading was 39 last year, 38 in weeks 5 and 6 this year and 37 in weeks 7 and 8.
Web is growing quickly (web net sales roughly 40% above last year in the weeks compared, for example 62.2k against 42.8k in week 5), so part of the growth is a channel shift, not store growth.
Excluded the training store (store_id 999): 509.55 EUR of sales in week 5 last year, with small amounts in every week. Its returns are zero in these weeks.

Duplicate sales lines exist in the warehouse: 418 (receipt_id, line_no) pairs appear twice, reloaded on 2025-09-23. They are all in September 2025, so they do not touch period 2 of either year and no de-duplication was needed for this answer. Anyone summing September 2025 would double count about 20.8k EUR.

rpt_daily_store_sales matches the fact tables for every store but not for the web shop (store 900). Its daily web figures differ from fact_sales_line (for example 45,197 against 42,782 for week 5 last year). I did not use that table. The result comes from fact_sales_line and fact_return_line, which reproduce the report's store sales and returns exactly.
Cancelled web orders have no sales lines, so they are not in the figures. The rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales views were not used.
Data runs to 2026-10-04, so all four weeks in both years are complete.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE p.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period

Product category taken from the product version in force at the return (via product_key)

'Handed back and booked as returned' means rows in fact_return_line, counted in units returned. I did not use refund value or sales lines.
All channels are included: stores, web home delivery and click-and-collect. The request did not limit the channel.
Returns of staff purchases are included. One of the 92 units is a staff purchase.

I checked for these problems and found none: duplicate return lines (92 distinct return lines for 92 distinct sales lines); overlap with the staging load (stg_return_line_load only holds 3 to 4 Oct 2026 rows); returns dated before the sale; returned units above units sold; and zero-value refunds.
The Garden Furniture product versions were stable. Only Outdoor Lighting SKUs were re-categorised between Garden and Electrical, and they do not affect this figure.

WITH first_version AS (

WHERE version_no = 1
  AND join_date = '2026-10-03'
definitions_applied: DEF-NEW-MEMBER: A new member is counted on their join_date, at the home_store in their first version in dim_member (the store where they enrolled)
REG-MEMBER-VERSIONS: dim_member holds multiple versions per member; use the first version to capture the enrollment details
assumptions: The request asked for a simple total count, not a breakdown by store or member tier
The date 3 October 2026 is treated as a calendar date (2026-10-03) to match against join_date in dim_member
Used first version of each member via ROW_NUMBER to ensure join_date and enrolling store are from the original enrollment
caveats: None: query-check validation passed all checks (no deprecated objects, no lint warnings, correct grain)

definitions_applied: Current member version: dim_member.is_current = true, one row per member_id, so each member is counted once at the tier they hold now
Member counted by loyalty number (member_id), not by surrogate member_key
Tier taken from dim_member.tier = 'Gold'

'Members on the Gold tier' means all members currently on the Gold tier, whatever their marketing consent, home store or activity. No filter was applied for recent purchases or consent.
Online sign-ups (home_store_id 900) are included. 1161 of the 5791 Gold members are online sign-ups.
caveats: No correction was needed. Each of the 60000 members has exactly one current row and no member has overlapping versions. No tier values are null or outside Basic, Silver and Gold. No Gold member has a join date after the request date.

Counting every dim_member row with tier = 'Gold' would give 8203 rows. That figure includes 2412 superseded versions from 2233 members, many of whom are on Gold today, so it overstates the answer. The result uses current versions only.
The staging table stg_member_updates (Sept to early Oct 2026 changes) is already reflected in dim_member: its current rows match dim_member's current tiers. Nothing was added from it.
The latest member change and latest sale in the warehouse are both dated 2026-10-04, so any tier changes after that date are not in this figure.

answer.sql:
WITH sales_data AS (
  SELECT 
    CASE 
      WHEN s.region = 'Online' THEN 'Web'
      ELSE s.region 
    END as region,
    d.fiscal_year,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as gross_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
    AND s.region != 'Head office'
  GROUP BY region, d.fiscal_year
),
returns_data AS (
  SELECT 
    CASE 
      WHEN s.region = 'Online' THEN 'Web'
      ELSE s.region 
    END as region,
    d.fiscal_year,
    SUM(f.refund_net) as returns
  FROM fact_return_line f
  JOIN dim_date d ON f.return_date = d.calendar_date
  JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_quarter = 3 
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
    AND s.region != 'Head office'
  GROUP BY region, d.fiscal_year
),
combined_data AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(s.region, r.region) as region,
    COALESCE(s.fiscal_year, r.fiscal_year) as fiscal_year,
    COALESCE(s.gross_sales, 0) - COALESCE(r.returns, 0) as net_sales
  FROM sales_data s
  FULL OUTER JOIN returns_data r 
    ON s.region = r.region AND s.fiscal_year = r.fiscal_year
)
SELECT 
  region,
  MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END) as fy2025_26_q3,
  MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales END) as fy2024_25_q3,
  ROUND(
    (MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END) - 
     MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales END)) /
    NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales END), 0) * 100, 
    2
  ) as growth_percentage
FROM combined_data
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Net sales: sum of fact_sales_line.net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus fact_return_line.refund_net, matching rpt_daily_store_sales definition
Fiscal quarters: Q3 defined by dim_date fiscal_quarter = 3 (FY2024/25 Oct 28–Jan 26, FY2025/26 Oct 27–Jan 25)
Regional classification: store region from dim_store, with Online region (store 900) relabeled as Web
Regional scope: excludes Head office (training store, pseudo-location)
assumptions: Last year = Q3 FY2025/26 (Oct 27, 2025 – Jan 25, 2026); earlier year = Q3 FY2024/25 (Oct 28, 2024 – Jan 26, 2025)
Web shop defined as the Online region (store 900), aggregated across click-and-collect and web home delivery channels
Returns linked to sales by matching return_date to the fiscal quarter; a return in Q3 applies to Q3 net sales regardless of original sale date
Growth percentage calculated as (FY2025/26 – FY2024/25) / FY2024/25 × 100, expressed as a percentage point
caveats: Capital Region: opened April 28, 2025, so no comparable Q3 FY2024/25 data. The FY2025/26 figure is Q3 sales only, not a year-over-year comparison.
South region shows a significant 37.4% decline (EUR 434,900 decrease), the largest regional movement in either direction. This warrants further investigation.
Web sales grew 28.1%, the strongest regional performance. This includes click-and-collect and home delivery fulfillment routed through store 900.
Total Q3 net sales across all regions: FY2025/26 EUR 3,842,260; FY2024/25 EUR 3,613,628 (6.3% overall growth)

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS period
),
sold_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.sale_date, s.format, f.net_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s     ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p   ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_date d      ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
      AND d.fiscal_period = params.period
),
refunds AS (
    SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT l.format,
       SUM(l.net_amount) AS sold_net,
       COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) AS returned_net,
       ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct
FROM sold_lines l
LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC
definitions_applied: Return rate: returned net divided by sold net, attributed to the fiscal week of the original sale
Net sales scope: excludes store 999 and category ZZ Test
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900), web shop not included
assumptions: Period 2 last year = FY2025/26 P2 (fiscal period 2 of 2025/26, dated 26 May - 22 June 2025)
Store format dimension is the format of the store on the sale date
caveats: Return cohort is complete: maximum sale date plus 30 days is before the warehouse load point (4 October 2026), so all expected returns have been recorded
Web sales and online purchases are excluded; only physical store formats are reported

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (which breaks after the 3 Nov 2025 platform migration)
Click-and-collect counted as web (delivered and collected orders)
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Timestamps converted from UTC to Helsinki time
Fiscal calendar: periods from dim_date (4-4-5 weeks), Monday to Sunday weeks
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_ tables) not used
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (the fiscal year just ended; the request came on 2026-10-09, in FY2026/27). Past requests made in FY2026/27 read it the same way.
Periods 5 to 8 of FY2025/26 run 25 Aug 2025 to 21 Dec 2025 (P5 25 Aug-21 Sep, P6 22 Sep-26 Oct, P7 27 Oct-23 Nov, P8 24 Nov-21 Dec).
'Web net sales' means the company definition of web net sales, net of web returns booked to the web shop, with the web shop (store 900) as one block including click-and-collect.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT, one row per fiscal period, with no total row because none was asked for.
caveats: The result matches the net_sales control total in rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in all four periods.

Source-data duplicate found, no effect on this answer: fact_sales_line has 418 repeated (receipt_id, line_no) rows in the Aug-Dec 2025 window. They are double-loaded lines in store 116 (loaded on 16 Sep and again on 23 Sep 2025, week of 15-21 Sep 2025, roughly 20.8k EUR net extra on 836 lines). None are web lines, so the web figures are not affected. Store 116's P5 sales (and anything built from the store tables) would be overstated if not de-duplicated.
Web returns processed in physical stores would be booked to those stores rather than the web shop, so they are not netted from web sales. This follows the company definition.

Period 5 to 8 return dates and dispatch dates are all within the loaded range, and the periods are fully loaded. Returns on web sales dispatched late in P8 may still arrive after 21 Dec 2025, but returns are booked on their own date, so these figures are final for the period.
No corrections to the web figures were needed. Cancelled orders (627 in the Aug-Dec window) were left out as they have no sales lines.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 22 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) net sales growth, FY2026/27 vs FY2025/26, same fiscal weeks, week by week
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, returns on their own return date
Staff purchases included in net sales
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (store 900) excluded
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
LFL base: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the range
LFL store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years; refit weeks from ref_store_closure and the closed store's weeks dropped
Week 53 never LFL (not in range)
Regions as-is (current dim_store version, five regions including Capital Region)
Fiscal year to date through the last completed fiscal week (YTD)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'How they are doing' was read as growth, not size, and ranked on LFL growth, the company's growth measure. LFL puts the regions on a like basis despite refits, an opening and a closure.
'This year so far' is the current fiscal year FY2026/27 to date. That is fiscal weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026), the last completed week, compared with weeks 1 to 22 of FY2025/26.
Regions are as-is (today's region of each store), so Capital Region and the South/East membership of Kouvola are restated for last year as well. This is the company default; no as-was was requested.
Ranked 1 = best, by LFL growth percent.
Only the ranking and the growth figure are given, since the request asked only for a ranking.
caveats: Correction: 418 sales lines in store 116 Tampere Lielahti (West), 15 to 21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 week 21), were loaded twice by the ETL, with identical content and different sales_line_id. They overstated last year's West sales by about 10,390 EUR (roughly double that store's sales that week). I kept one row per receipt_id and line_no. After the fix the sales match rpt_daily_store_sales for all stores in all 22 weeks of both years. The duplicate only affects West's last-year base: unfixed, West would show 1.33% instead of 1.93%. The ranking does not change.

East is the only region with negative LFL growth. Its LFL base excludes Savonlinna (closed 25 January 2026) and Kuopio's refit weeks (15 June to 26 July 2026). Raw year-on-year net sales for East, without LFL adjustment, are -11.6%, mostly from Savonlinna's loss. This is not a like-for-like figure.

The LFL base leaves out some store-weeks. West loses Pori's weeks 20 to 22 (Pori's refit last year, 8 September to 12 October 2025), East loses Kuopio's refit weeks and Savonlinna, and the regional LFL totals are therefore on slightly different weeks from the full-year sales.

A different reading of 'doing' gives a different order. Ranked on raw net sales YTD against last year with no LFL adjustment, West would be first (+3.24%, helped by Pori's closed weeks last year), then North (+3.80%) in a tie-like position by growth. Ranked on the size of net sales, the order is West, South, East, Capital Region, North. If Finance wanted size, or unadjusted growth, say so and I will rerun.

LFL regional percentages come from slightly different store counts per region (North 6 stores, Capital Region 5, South 10, West 10, East 7 in the base), so the East and North figures sit on smaller bases. The gaps between South (2.11) and West (1.93) are small and I have not tested them for significance.
Not used: rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales and rpt_weekly_sales_by_region (known gaps or stale), and no deprecated or staging tables.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS fiscal_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END AS category, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) / SUM(n.net_sales), 1) AS gross_margin_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN params ON d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period = params.fiscal_period WHERE CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost, both after returns (returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned)
Gross margin % = gross margin / net sales
As-is reporting: current product hierarchy, so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical for the whole period
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 6 (22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, 5 weeks, fully loaded)
Control total: the net sales query's daily store figures for the period match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27, so 'period 6 last year' is FY2025/26 P6, which ran from 22 September to 26 October 2025. Past requests from May 2026 onward (FY2026/27) read 'last year' this way. FY2026/27 P6 is not complete (only week 1 is loaded).
Categories are reported as-is (current hierarchy), the company default, because the request did not ask for as-was.
Web sales are included in both categories (web shop store 900 is part of company net sales).
Net sales and margin are shown as one row per category, with no total row.
caveats: As-is vs as-was: outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 October 2025, the day after this period ended. As-is, its sales are in Electrical. As-was (the hierarchy on the day), they would sit in Garden. Outdoor lighting accounts for 33,781.91 of net sales (gross margin 12,586.84) in P6. As-was, Electrical would be 185,711.09 at 41.6% and Garden 148,587.85 at about 39.6%.

Correction: five delisted outdoor lighting SKUs (100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) are still flagged Garden in the current product version. Their move to Electrical was not recorded. I mapped every Outdoor Lighting subcategory article to Electrical so the whole subcategory is treated consistently. These five articles have no sales or returns in P6, so the figures are unaffected.

Data issue found, outside this period: 418 sales lines in one store dated 15 to 21 September 2025 were loaded twice (second load 23 September 2025, 03:12), about 10,390 net too much. This is the week before P6 and does not touch these figures. It also inflates rpt_daily_store_sales for that week, so a control-total match does not prove the source is clean. It would matter for any P5 or weekly figure.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale. Net sales here are by return date as per the company definition, so returns of goods sold in P6 that arrive in later periods are not in these figures.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT.

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND p.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3
definitions_applied: Units sold from fact_sales_line.quantity
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900)
Fiscal period: FY2026/27 P3 (29 June to 2 August 2026)
Product category: Interior Paint subcategory only
assumptions: "This year" interpreted as current fiscal year FY2026/27
"Interior Paint" interpreted as all products in the Interior Paint subcategory (123 products)
"Lahti store" resolved to store_id 108 from dim_store
Quantity includes all sales (staff purchases included, returns not deducted from quantity)
caveats: Interior Paint is a broad subcategory with 123 current products; the request did not specify a single product
142 sales lines were counted across the period; all had non-null quantities

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-08-25' AS start_date, DATE '2025-09-21' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open (after opening, before closure), outside refit closures in ref_store_closure, excluding closed holidays (dim_date.is_trading_day = false)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 5 = fiscal weeks 18 to 21, Monday 25 August 2025 to Sunday 21 September 2025 (28 days, all trading days)
Store name, format and open/close dates taken from the current dim_store version (as-is)
Control total: store-level net sales reconciled to rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 (request received 8 October 2026), so period 5 means FY2025/26 P05. This follows the past requests that read 'last year' as the previous fiscal year once the new fiscal year had started.

'Store league table' read as the company definition: ranking by net sales per trading day (not by total net sales), so a store that traded for part of the period is still listed with its own trading days.
Rank is on unrounded net sales per trading day; Kerava, Kemi and Raisio show the same rounded value (384) but are ranked on the unrounded figures.
Net sales is shown in EUR excluding VAT; net sales per trading day is rounded to whole euros.
caveats: Correction: store 116 Tampere Lielahti had duplicated sales lines for 15 to 21 September 2025. 418 receipt lines (836 rows) were loaded twice, the second copy on 23 September 2025 (etl_loaded_at 2025-09-23) under new sales_line_ids. I kept one copy per receipt_id and line_no (the earliest load). Without this fix, Tampere Lielahti would show 47,679.15 net sales (1,703 per day) and rank 3 instead of 37,288.62 (1,332 per day) at rank 7, and the total across stores would be overstated by 10,390.53. After the fix every store agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent (total 940,396.62). The duplicates only affect store 116 in this period, and the source table should be repaired.

Pori (119) was closed for a refit from 8 September 2025, so it traded only 14 of the 28 days (25 August to 7 September). It is ranked on its per-day figure, so its total net sales (16,057.86) are not comparable with the full-period stores.

Savonlinna (129) is still in the table with a full 28 trading days because it closed only on 25 January 2026. Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) had been open since September and November 2024 and traded all 28 days.
Store format values are Large, Medium and Small, not Hyper, Standard or Express as the column comment says; format is not shown in the answer table.
Regions are not in the table. Stores are shown as-is on the current dim_store version.
Web shop (900) and training store (999) are not part of the league table.

answer.sql: WITH web_line AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.sale_date, f.net_amount, o.fulfilment_type FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)), sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, w.fulfilment_type, w.net_amount AS amt FROM web_line w JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.sale_date), refunds AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, w.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN web_line w ON w.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date), net AS (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM refunds) SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, round(100 * sum(CASE WHEN fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN amt ELSE 0 END) / sum(amt), 1) AS click_and_collect_share_pct FROM net WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period BETWEEN 6 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: EUR excluding VAT (net_amount), after returns
Web shop sales: all web order lines, home delivery plus click-and-collect
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, which matches channel_id 3 (Click and collect) in dim_channel
Returns deducted in the period in which the refund was booked (return_date), as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Fiscal periods taken from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar (period 7 is 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025, period 8 is 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025)
Cancelled web orders excluded (they have no sales lines)
assumptions: Last year means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26. Today is in FY2026/27, and periods 6 to 8 of FY2025/26 run from 22 Sep to 21 Dec 2025.
Share of the web shop's sales is click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (home delivery plus click-and-collect), by value in EUR excluding VAT.
Sales are net of returns. Refunds are attributed to the channel of the original sales line and to the period of the return date.
No staff purchases appear among the web lines, so none were excluded.
caveats: Channel coding changed at the web-platform migration. Web lines up to 2 Nov 2025 carry channel_code 'WB' with channel_id NULL. Lines from 3 Nov 2025 carry channel_code NULL with channel_id 2 (home delivery) or 3 (click and collect). Filtering on channel_code = 'WB' alone would miss most of period 7 and all of period 8. I used both codes and took click-and-collect from fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, so the period 7 figure covers both coding regimes.

Returns of web orders are booked at many physical stores as well as at the web shop pseudo-store (store 900). I linked every refund to its original web sales line through sales_line_id instead of filtering on the return store, so none are lost.

Before returns, the click-and-collect shares are 27.65% (P6), 26.63% (P7) and 26.56% (P8). Returns lower each share by 0.2 to 0.6 percentage points because click-and-collect is returned less than home delivery. If the requester wants gross sales rather than net, use those figures.

Cancelled web orders (483 over the three periods) have no sales lines and are not counted. Order and line counts reconcile (line_count and order_total_gross match the lines for every delivered or collected order). I found no duplicate sales, return or order IDs, and no orphan returns.
The stg_* load tables hold only 3 to 4 Oct 2026 data, so they do not affect these periods. The bak_, old and tmp tables were not used.

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE fs.week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-06-29' AND DATE '2026-08-02' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' GROUP BY 1) SELECT ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot, summed across stores and products within each week, then averaged across weeks (never summed across weeks)
Stock value at standard cost (closing_value in fact_stock_week)
Fiscal calendar: period 3 of FY2026/27 is fiscal weeks 9 to 13, 29 June to 2 August 2026, with five week-ending Sundays
Physical stores only (store_id below 900), so the web shop (900) and the training store (999) are excluded; web stock is not in this table
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product category: the current dim_product version of each SKU, joined on sku and is_current
Only articles each store ranges, as held in fact_stock_week
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (request received 8 October 2026), so period 3 is 29 June to 2 August 2026, a complete period.
'Average stock' means the average of the five weekly closing stock values in the period, rather than the last week's closing.
'Whole chain' means all physical stores combined, as one figure and not a store breakdown.
'Value at cost' is read as standard cost, which is the basis of closing_value in the warehouse.
Paint & Decorating is the category named in dim_product. It does not include Home Textiles & Decor.
caveats: No corrections were needed. The stock snapshot rows had no duplicate keys, and every week had exactly one load.
Closing value equals closing units times standard unit cost on every row, so the figure is at standard cost, not purchase or market cost.
The product category is the same under as-is and as-was for every Paint & Decorating article in this period, so the choice does not change the figure.
The first week had 2,699 article-store rows against 2,674 in the other four weeks, because 3 more articles were ranged in that week. The average includes them as recorded.
Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, but it still holds stock rows in the snapshot, so it is included in the chain figure.
Savonlinna (129), closed 25 January 2026, has no stock rows in the period.
The control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply, because it covers net sales and not stock.

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, s.format AS store_format, round(sum(f.net_amount) / count(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS average_basket_value_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-03' AND DATE '2026-08-30' AND f.channel_id = 1 AND s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag GROUP BY s.format ORDER BY CASE s.format WHEN 'Large' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 4 of FY2026/27 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar: 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30, 4 weeks, fully loaded
Basket (transaction) = one distinct receipt_id
Basket value = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts), summed per receipt
Average basket value = total net sales of the receipts divided by the number of distinct receipts, in each format
Store format taken from the dim_store version linked by store_key, i.e. the version valid on the sale date
Store channel only (channel_id 1, Store); web home delivery and click-and-collect excluded
Training store (999) and the web shop (900) excluded
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag = true) excluded, so the figure measures customer baskets
assumptions: Read 'period 4 of FY26/27' as fiscal year FY2026/27, fiscal period 4 (the 4-week period 3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026), not a calendar month
Read 'basket value' as value excluding VAT, matching the company's net sales reporting; the VAT-inclusive figures would be higher
Basket value is measured before returns. Refunds are separate rows in fact_return_line and are not netted off the original basket
Staff purchases are not customer baskets, so they are left out. The warehouse has no written definition for this, so it is my choice
Grouped by the three formats the warehouse actually holds (Large, Medium, Small), with no total row because none was requested
caveats: The dim_store column comment says format is Hyper, Standard or Express, but the data holds Large, Medium and Small (plus Web and Training for the pseudo-locations). I used the values in the data.

No duplicate lines, no duplicate receipt and line combinations, no receipts split across stores, dates or staff flags, and no store-version mismatches were found for the period. No correction was needed beyond the exclusions listed.

Excluded: the training store (999), with 55 receipts and 127 lines in the period; web orders (store_key for the web shop), which are not a store format; and 99 Large, 138 Medium and 43 Small staff-purchase receipts.
Including staff purchases, which is how rpt_daily_store_sales counts receipts, the averages would be about Large 60.60, Medium 60.15 and Small 50.67. The difference is under 0.15 EUR per format.

Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 2026-01-25 and has no sales in the period. Refit closures in ref_store_closure do not overlap with the period. Store 125 Kuopio finished its refit on 2026-07-26, before period 4 began.
The channel_code column is empty in this period. I used channel_id, which is populated. Nothing in the column comments mentions this.

answer.sql:
WITH period2_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_week,
    d.fiscal_week_start_date,
    d.fiscal_week_end_date,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE (d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 2)
     OR (d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2)
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
)
SELECT 
  this_year.fiscal_week,
  this_year.fiscal_week_start_date,
  this_year.fiscal_week_end_date,
  this_year.net_sales as net_sales_this_year,
  last_year.net_sales as net_sales_last_year,
  ROUND((this_year.net_sales - last_year.net_sales) / last_year.net_sales * 100, 2) as growth_pct
FROM period2_sales this_year
LEFT JOIN period2_sales last_year 
  ON this_year.fiscal_week = last_year.fiscal_week 
  AND this_year.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
  AND last_year.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
WHERE this_year.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
ORDER BY this_year.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Total company net sales: sum of net_amount from fact_sales_line
Net sales basis: transaction value excluding VAT, after line discounts
Period 2 definition: weeks 5-8 of the fiscal calendar
Growth percentage: ((current_year - prior_year) / prior_year) * 100

Units sold means sum of fact_sales_line.quantity, which is gross of returns and includes staff purchases, matching how rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold is built (checked: the two agree at 3,927 units for all of Lahti in the period)

answer.sql: SELECT store_id, store_name, city, region, format, sqm FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900 ORDER BY sqm DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900), so the web shop (900) and the training store (999) are excluded
Current store version only (dim_store.is_current), so each store appears once, not once per version
Region and format shown as-is (current hierarchy, including the Capital Region created on 28 April 2025)
Store size is the sales area in square metres (dim_store.sqm)
assumptions: The metric dictionary does not define 'biggest'. I read it as store size, meaning sales area in square metres, because store operations asked and sqm is the stored size attribute. I did not invent a new sales-based definition.
Ranking is by sqm, largest first. There are no ties around the cut-off (10th is 4738 sqm, 11th is 4676 sqm).
Only current stores are ranked. Savonlinna (129), closed on 25 January 2026, is not in the top 10 on size either way.
caveats: If 'biggest' meant sales, the ranking is different. On FY2025/26 net sales from rpt_daily_store_sales, the top 10 are Tampere Hervanta, Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, Oulu Kaakkuri, Lahti, Turku Kupittaa, Vantaa Tammisto, Kuopio, Tampere Lielahti, Tampere Kaleva and Nokia. Tampere Hervanta is first on sales but eighth on size. Espoo Lommila and Lappeenranta are in the size top 10 but not the sales top 10. Say if you want the sales version.
Sales area does not change across store versions (one sqm value per store), so using the current version gives the same size as any historical version.
dim_store.format values include 'Large' and 'Medium'. The column comment (Hyper, Standard or Express) is out of date, and the region comment still lists four regions.
No store-level sales figures are in the answer, so the rpt_daily_store_sales control-total check does not apply. The size ranking comes from dim_store alone.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT ty.region, ty.fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales of LFL stores in the same fiscal weeks, this year versus last year, aligned on fiscal week number
LFL store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
LFL opening rule: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the period (open_date on or before 2024-10-28)
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open, not closed, no ref_store_closure refit overlap)
Week 53 never counts in LFL (not relevant to Q3, weeks 27-39)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: Q3 = P7-P9 = fiscal weeks 27-39; FY2025/26 Q3 = 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026; comparator FY2024/25 weeks 27-39 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025)
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT after line discounts, less refunds (refund_net) on the return date; store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded; staff purchases included
As-is regions: current dim_store version (is_current) for every year, five regions including Capital Region
Control check: store-level net sales over the Q3 weeks in both years reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales with no gap
assumptions: "Q3 last year" read as FY2025/26 Q3 (fiscal weeks 27-39, 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026), the most recently completed Q3 for a request received 5 Oct 2026 in FY2026/27. This follows how past requests read "last year"
The comparator is FY2024/25 weeks 27-39, lined up by fiscal week number
Regions are as-is (current hierarchy, including the Capital Region), since no as-was reading was requested
"By region" is read as one growth figure per region and no company total row, because only a breakdown was asked for
Growth is shown as a percentage in percent units, rounded to two decimals
caveats: Lohja (137) is excluded from the LFL base: it opened 4 Nov 2024, less than 52 weeks before the start of the period (27 Oct 2025), and only part of the comparator Q3 was open. 38 physical stores are in the base, with 13 store-weeks each in both years (494 per year)
Tampere Lamminpää (136) opened 2 Sep 2024 and meets the 52-week rule, so it is in the West figure. Its sales are up 39% as it ramps up, which lifts West. Without it West would be lower

Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026, the last day of week 39, so it traded all 13 weeks and is in the East figure. No refit closure (Tammisto, Pori, Kuopio) overlaps Q3 in either year, so no store-weeks dropped out for refits

Region is as-is: Vantaa Tammisto, Kerava and the other Capital Region stores count under the Capital Region for both years, and Kouvola counts in South, not East. As-was regions would give different regional figures and the Capital Region would not exist in the comparator year

Duplicate sales lines (same receipt_id and line_no loaded twice, 418 pairs, about 20.8k EUR net) exist for 15-21 Sep 2025. They fall outside both Q3 windows, so they do not affect this answer. They would inflate any figure covering that week

The regional growth rates are on LFL net sales excluding VAT. Company-wide LFL for the same basis is +2.65% (3,223,127 EUR vs 3,140,011 EUR), not shown in the table because only the regional breakdown was asked for

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending),
closing AS (
  SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units
  FROM fact_stock_week fs
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key
  JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
  CROSS JOIN params
  WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  GROUP BY 1),
sold AS (
  SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
  CROSS JOIN params
  WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7
    AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  GROUP BY 1)
SELECT c.category, ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover
FROM closing c LEFT JOIN sold s USING (category) ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Last period = last completed fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, weeks 18-21)
Weeks of cover = closing stock units at the end of the fiscal week / average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Closing stock is a snapshot, summed across stores and products for the single week-ending Sunday 27 Sep 2026, never summed across weeks
Units sold = quantity on sales lines by sale_date, summed over the four weeks 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026 and divided by 4
Physical stores only (store_id < 900): web shop (900) excluded, since web is picked from the central warehouse and not in the stock table; store 999 excluded
Category ZZ Test excluded from stock and sales
As-is product hierarchy (current dim_product version per sku, so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical)
Ranged articles only, as held in fact_stock_week
Staff purchases included in units sold, returns not netted off units sold
assumptions: Request received 7 Oct 2026, so 'end of last period' is Sunday 27 Sep 2026, the end of FY2026/27 P05. P06 is only partly loaded and was not used.

'Prior four fiscal weeks' is read literally as the four whole fiscal weeks before the snapshot week (weeks 17-20, 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026), not the four weeks ending on the snapshot date (weeks 18-21, which are the period itself).
Weeks of cover is computed per category over all physical stores combined (category total stock / category total average weekly sales), not as an average of per-store ratios.
Category as-is (current hierarchy); as-was was not requested.
caveats: No data corrections were needed. The stock snapshot for 27 Sep 2026 has 27,143 rows with no duplicate store/product keys, no negative stock, and only physical stores (101-139) and the ten real categories; sales lines are unique and loaded through 4 Oct 2026.

Seasonal (48.8 weeks) and Furniture (29.5 weeks) have very high cover because their current sales rates are low (about 524 and 168 units a week across all stores). Seasonal stock is probably being built ahead of its peak, so its cover based on the last four weeks' sales will overstate the real cover.
Cover uses the trailing four-week sales rate, so it ignores seasonality and any upcoming promotions.
Web sales are not included in units sold and web stock is not in the table, so the figures are for the store network only.

The week 21 snapshot is a different set of weeks from the sales window by design (stock at the end of week 21, sales in weeks 17-20); if Supply chain wants sales from the period itself (weeks 18-21), the cover figures would change.

answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date,
           p.category,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND p.category = 'Garden'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date,
           p.category,
           -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND p.category = 'Garden'
),
with_period AS (
    SELECT n.business_date,
           d.fiscal_period, 
           d.fiscal_period_label,
           n.net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 27 AND 52
)
SELECT 
  fiscal_period_label,
  fiscal_period,
  ROUND(SUM(net_sales), 2) AS net_sales
FROM with_period
GROUP BY fiscal_period_label, fiscal_period
ORDER BY fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Store 999 and ZZ Test category excluded
Web sales recognised on Helsinki dispatch date
Returns reduce net sales on the return date
assumptions: Reporting basis: as-was (Garden category as it stood at the transaction date)
Fiscal periods resolved to FY2024/25 weeks 27-52 (2024-10-28 to 2025-04-27)
caveats: Control total check shows a gap of 5,969,697.02 EUR between Garden category and total company net sales; this is expected because the control total (rpt_daily_store_sales) covers all products while this query reports only the Garden category

answer.sql: WITH web_lines AS (SELECT CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date, f.net_amount, o.member_key AS order_member_key FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id AND o.status IN ('delivered','collected') JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(net_amount) FILTER (WHERE order_member_key IS NOT NULL) / SUM(net_amount), 3) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM web_lines w JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Web = store_id 900 (not channel_code)
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date from fact_web_order (delivered and collected orders only)
Guest web orders count as non-member
Test articles (category ZZ Test) left out
Net amounts excluding VAT, before returns
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26 P9 to P11)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales_before_returns for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request came on 9 October 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests from May 2026 onward took 'last year' as FY2025/26.
'Periods 9 to 11' read as FY2025/26 P09 (22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026), P10 (26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026) and P11 (23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026), one row per period.
'Web sales' includes click-and-collect, per company definition.
'Loyalty member' means the order is linked to a member key. Logged-in orders always carry one and guest orders never do.
No returns are netted, because member share is defined before returns.
caveats: Data defect corrected: in February and March 2026, 655 logged-in web orders (618 in February, 37 in March; 1,309 lines) have a null member_key on their sales lines, although fact_web_order carries the member key. They fall in P10 and P11. Taking membership from the lines would show P10 at 51.77% and P11 at 55.81%, which understates the true shares. I took membership from fact_web_order.member_key (logged-in = member). P9 is unaffected.
Where both keys are present on an order they agree, with no mismatches.
Three web lines in P11 (one) and P12 (two) are in category ZZ Test and were excluded. This changes P11 web net sales by a negligible amount. The P12 lines are outside the requested range.
My web net sales (excluding ZZ Test) match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 (net_sales_before_returns) exactly in P9 (219,929.50), P10 (137,569.07) and P11 (149,798.62).
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or any channel_code logic, so the 3 November 2025 migration gap does not affect these figures.
Percentages are shown to three decimals. P10 is 67.525%, which rounds to 67.53% at two decimals.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, fs.week_ending_date, fs.closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND fs.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Closing stock: weekly snapshot counted on the week-ending Sunday (fact_stock_week.closing_units)
Fiscal calendar: fiscal weeks run Monday to Sunday
Last completed fiscal week: FY2026/27 week 22, 28 Sep to 4 Oct 2026
Store scope: physical store, store_id 124, not the web shop (900) or training store (999)
Versioned dimensions: stock rows joined through the store_key and product_key versions to the stable store_id and sku
Ranged articles only; web stock is not in the table
assumptions: 'End of last week' means the closing snapshot of the last completed fiscal week, Sunday 4 October 2026. The request arrived Thursday 8 October, in fiscal week 23, which is still running and has no snapshot yet.
'SKU 100011 Jyväskylä Palokka' means article 100011 (Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570, Garden) in store 124 Jyväskylä Palokka.
The answer is in units, as asked.
caveats: I found no problem in the data for this store, article and week.
The warehouse is loaded through Sunday 4 October 2026, so the 4 October count is the latest available.
The Sunday 4 October snapshot has exactly one row for this store and article, and the week has no duplicate store-article rows. The snapshot was loaded on 5 October.

The stock movement for the article reconciles with sales: 20 units on 30 Aug, then 16, 13, 13, 11 and 11 on the following Sundays. Weekly sales match the drops (4, 3, 0, 2, 0) and there were no receipts or adjustments.
This is the stock in the store only. Web orders are picked from the central warehouse, which is not in this table.

answer.sql: SELECT p.subcategory AS product_group, SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE p.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-03' AND DATE '2026-08-30' GROUP BY p.subcategory
definitions_applied: Garden Furniture = dim_product.subcategory 'Garden Furniture', which sits under the Garden category
Fiscal period 4 of the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 P04, from ref_fiscal_calendar: 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30 (4 weeks, fully loaded)
Returned units = fact_return_line.quantity_returned, counted by return_date (when the item was handed back and booked), not by the original sale date
Product versions taken from dim_product via the product_key on the return line
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, because the request was received on 2026-10-05 and period 4 is a fiscal period
'Period 4' means fiscal period 4 (3 to 30 August 2026), not calendar April
Garden Furniture means the 'Garden Furniture' subcategory only. No other category, such as the separate 'Furniture' category, was included

All sales channels and all return reasons are included: stores, web home delivery and click-and-collect, and all five reason codes (changed_mind, damaged_in_transit, defective, not_as_described, wrong_size_or_fit)
The staging table stg_return_line_load was not added. It holds only 141 lines, dated 3 to 4 October 2026, all of which are already in fact_return_line, so it has no effect on period 4
caveats: No corrections were needed. I checked the figure for duplicate return lines, orphan return lines, returns dated before the sale, returns above the quantity sold, and return product keys that did not match the sales line product. I found none
Two Garden Furniture articles (SKU 100527 and SKU 100583) have two product versions each. Both versions are in the Garden Furniture subcategory, so the count is the same whichever version is used

34 of the 92 units were booked to the web shop (store 900). Another 10 came from click-and-collect orders, which were booked at physical stores, so they are included in the store figures. Excluding web orders would give a lower number than 92

fact_sales_line.channel_code is NULL on these lines. The channel can only be read from channel_id (1 store, 2 web home delivery, 3 click and collect). The rpt.v_daily_sales view filters on channel_code, so it would miss these sales lines. I did not use it
No fiscal-period filter is needed beyond the date range. P04 2026 is marked fully loaded

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 is 29 June to 2 August 2026 (fiscal weeks 9 to 13, 5 weeks), fully loaded
Units sold are the quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (the metric dictionary's definition of units sold)
Store scope: physical store Lahti, store_id 108, as a single store version; the web shop (900) is not part of a store figure
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (the filter changes nothing here)
Staff purchases included (4 of the 194 units)
As-is product hierarchy: the Interior Paint subcategory on the current product version (is_current)
Versioned dimensions joined on version keys and then on sku with is_current, so no rows are multiplied
Control total: all Lahti units for the period (3,927 units, 1,048 receipts, 35 days) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly
assumptions: Read 'period 3 of FY26/27' as fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 (29 June to 2 August 2026), not calendar month 3
Read 'Interior Paint' as the dim_product subcategory 'Interior Paint' (category Paint & Decorating), which covers 125 articles. The name is not a category in its own right.
Read 'sold' as units on sales lines, before returns. The company metric dictionary defines units sold as the quantity on sales lines, and returns are not netted off units.
Counted units sold in the Lahti store only. Web orders are booked to the web shop (store 900) and are not attributed to Lahti, including any click-and-collect pickups there.
Used the article hierarchy as-is. The two Interior Paint articles that have older versions kept the same subcategory, so as-was gives the same figure.
caveats: The 194 units are before returns. 6 of those units were later returned. Net of returns the figure would be 188, if Olli wants units kept by customers rather than units sold.

Only one store matches 'Lahti' as a city or name: store 108 Lahti (South, format Large). Tampere Lielahti was not a match. No data problem needed correcting: there were no duplicate sales lines, no negative quantities, and Lahti traded on all 35 days of the period.
The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so the period is complete. Returns can still arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so the 6 returned units are final only for sales up to early July.

answer.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date AS d0, period_end_date AS d1 FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period = 6), lines AS (SELECT p.category, f.net_amount AS net, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN per ON f.sale_date BETWEEN per.d0 AND per.d1 WHERE p.category IN ('Garden','Electrical') AND s.store_id <> 999 UNION ALL SELECT p.category, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN per ON r.return_date BETWEEN per.d0 AND per.d1 WHERE p.category IN ('Garden','Electrical') AND s.store_id <> 999) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS fiscal_period, category, round(sum(net), 2) AS net_sales_eur, round(100 * (sum(net) - sum(cost)) / sum(net), 2) AS gross_margin_pct FROM lines GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 6 of FY2025/26 is 22 Sep 2025 to 26 Oct 2025 (5 weeks), from ref_fiscal_calendar
Net sales = line net amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refunds (refund_net) booked in the period, as the company's daily store sales report does
Gross margin % = (net sales minus standard cost of units sold, with the standard cost of returned units taken off) divided by net sales, as a percentage
Cost = the standard cost on each sales and return line, which matches the product's standard unit cost times quantity
Category taken from the product version in force on the sale date (product_key on the fact line)
Both channels included: stores and web (home delivery and click-and-collect)
Staff purchases included, as in the company's daily store sales report
Training store 999 excluded; it is not a trading store and the company's daily sales report excludes it
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; they lie outside the two categories asked for, so they do not touch the figures
assumptions: Today is 8 Oct 2026, so the current fiscal year is FY2026/27 and 'last year' is FY2025/26. Period 6 of FY2025/26 is the same period as the current, still open FY2026/27 P06.
'Period 6' means fiscal period 6 of the company's 4-4-5 style calendar, not calendar month 6 (June).
'Garden' and 'Electrical' mean the categories as they stood at the time of sale. Outdoor Lighting was in Garden then and moved to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, the day after this period ended.
Returns are counted in the period in which the refund was booked, whenever the original sale was made, and in the category of the returned product.
Web sales are counted by sale date, with the web shop (store 900) as the location. All web orders in the period are delivered or collected, with none cancelled.
Staff purchases are kept in, since the company's report keeps them. Taking them out would change the figures slightly.
caveats: Excluded the training store (store 999): 21 Garden and 21 Electrical staff-flagged lines, about EUR 615 and EUR 511 of net sales. These are not real trading.
Excluded 67 test-article lines (category ZZ Test, brand TEST). They fall outside both categories, so the effect on these figures is nil.

Outdoor Lighting was reclassified from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, so current dim_product shows these 65 articles under Electrical. I used the category as at sale date, as the fact tables do. On that basis Outdoor Lighting is EUR 34,119.26 net sales (37.26% margin) inside the Garden figure. If Hanna wants today's category structure, Garden would be about EUR 113,813 net sales at 40.20% margin, and Electrical about EUR 219,696 at roughly 40.95% (the Electrical margin is my own back-calculation, not a query result). The comparison with the current year and any later period should use the same basis.

rpt_daily_store_sales does not tie to the fact table for the web shop. Daily web figures are off by up to several thousand euros, with Sundays far too low, so I did not use it. Store-level net sales before returns match the fact table exactly.
Garden and Electrical returns in the period are 295 and 420 lines, with net refunds of EUR 9,990.37 and EUR 9,040.69. They are already netted off the net sales above.
52 groups of identical lines (same receipt, product, quantity, amount and timestamp) exist in the period. I read them as repeat scans of the same item and did not remove them.
Margin is at standard cost (revalued each April), not actual purchase cost, so it is a standard margin.
Net sales are in EUR excluding VAT.
Period 6 of FY2025/26 is fully loaded. I found no missing days and no duplicate sales lines, and the staging tables hold no rows for the period.

answer.sql: WITH stock AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(w.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week w JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = w.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = w.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE w.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-09-27' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_4w FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-24' AND DATE '2026-09-20' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, st.category, st.closing_units, ROUND(so.units_4w / 4.0, 1) AS avg_weekly_units_sold, ROUND(st.closing_units / (so.units_4w / 4.0), 2) AS weeks_of_cover FROM stock st JOIN sold so ON so.category = st.category ORDER BY st.category
definitions_applied: Weeks of cover: closing stock units at the end of the fiscal week divided by the average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Last period: last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P5 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), so the snapshot is the closing stock at the end of fiscal week 21, Sunday 27 Sep 2026
Prior four weeks read literally as the four weeks before the snapshot week: fiscal weeks 17 to 20, 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026
Units sold: quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date
Stock summed across stores and products within the single snapshot week; never summed across weeks
Stock by store covers physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (store 900) and store 999 excluded on stock and units sold alike
Category ZZ Test excluded on stock and units sold
As-is reporting: category taken from the current product version (sku joined to dim_product on is_current), so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical
Control total: units and net sales before returns over 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026 checked against rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store
assumptions: 'Last period' read as FY2026/27 P5, the last complete period as of the request date of 7 Oct 2026 and the warehouse load through 4 Oct 2026 (P6 has only its first week)
'Category' read as the top-level product category in dim_product, with no subcategory breakdown
The prior four weeks are weeks 17 to 20, ending the Sunday before the snapshot week, not the four weeks ending with the snapshot week (weeks 18 to 21)
Units sold are gross sales-line quantities and are not reduced for returns, because the definition says quantity on sales lines
Staff purchases are included in units sold, as in net sales
Weeks of cover is computed per category from category totals, not as an average of store-level or SKU-level ratios
caveats: No corrections were needed. fact_stock_week for the snapshot week had one row per store_key and product_key, 27,143 rows, matching the distinct store_id and sku count, so the join to current product versions did not multiply rows
The snapshot week has no rows for store 999, store 900 or ZZ Test, so those filters did not change the stock total (211,157 units). Savonlinna (129, closed) has no stock rows
Units sold over weeks 17 to 20 agree with rpt_daily_store_sales for all 38 stores: 69,438 units and 1,006,345.09 EUR net before returns, no differences
Cover is on the four weeks immediately before the snapshot week. Using weeks 18 to 21 instead would give slightly different figures
Seasonal (48.8 weeks) and Furniture (29.5 weeks) are far above the other categories because their weekly sales are very low relative to stock. This is the data as it stands, not a data error
Cover is based on 4-week average sales only, with no adjustment for seasonality or promotions
Web demand is not in the figures: web orders are picked from the central warehouse, which is not in fact_stock_week, so this is store-network cover only
Kuopio (125) was back from its refit (15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026) well before the window, so no closure adjustment was needed for the four weeks

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period
),
sold_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.sale_date, s.format, f.net_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s     ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p   ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_date d      ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
      AND d.fiscal_period = params.fiscal_period
),
refunds AS (
    SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net 
    FROM fact_return_line 
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT l.format,
       ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct
FROM sold_lines l
LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY l.format;
definitions_applied: Return rate: refund net divided by sold net, sale-week cohort (return attributed to the fiscal week of original sale)
Net sales: excluding VAT, after returns, store 999 and ZZ Test category excluded, staff purchases included
assumptions: Period 2 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 P02 (22 May–22 June 2025)
Store format includes all physical store formats (Large, Medium, Small) plus Web
Return rate reported as percentage of sales in P2 (all returns, whenever received, attributed to the sale period)
caveats: Cohort complete: P2 FY2025/26 ended 22 June 2025, more than 30 days before warehouse load date (4 October 2026), so all returns have been received
Web returns sent by post are booked to store 900, the web shop

Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Products grouped by stable sku, with the current product name
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales (units_sold) for store 102 over the same days
assumptions: 'Period 5 of FY26/27' read as fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, the last complete period
