answer.sql: WITH this_year AS (SELECT d.fiscal_week, SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 GROUP BY d.fiscal_week), last_year AS (SELECT d.fiscal_week, SUM(f.net_amount) as net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 GROUP BY d.fiscal_week) SELECT ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales as net_sales_fy2026_27, ly.net_sales as net_sales_fy2025_26, ROUND(((ty.net_sales - ly.net_sales) / ly.net_sales * 100), 2) as growth_pct FROM this_year ty JOIN last_year ly ON ty.fiscal_week = ly.fiscal_week ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 = this year, FY2025/26 = last year
Period 2 defined by ref_fiscal_calendar
Net sales: sum of net_amount from fact_sales_line (EUR, excluding VAT, after line discounts)
Company total: all stores and all channels combined (no filtering)
Growth percentage: ((this_year - last_year) / last_year) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals
assumptions: Request received 2026-10-07; 'this year' interpreted as fiscal year FY2026/27 and 'last year' as FY2025/26
Period 2 refers to fiscal period 2, not calendar period 2
Fiscal week used as the natural grain of comparison (same week 5, 6, 7, 8 across fiscal years)
All sales transactions included (store and web channels, including staff purchases)
caveats: No data quality issues detected; all weeks in both fiscal years have complete sales data
Week 7 (FY2026/27) shows significant decline (-25.33%) compared to same week prior year; this may warrant investigation but no data anomalies found
Fiscal week numbers are the same (5-8) across both periods; this is consistent with a standard 52/53-week fiscal calendar

Ranking by total cumulative net sales across the period from 3 November 2025 to 3 October 2026

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN wo.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN wo.order_total_gross ELSE 0 END) / SUM(wo.order_total_gross), 2) as click_and_collect_share_pct FROM fact_web_order wo INNER JOIN dim_date d ON CAST(wo.order_ts_utc AS DATE) = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period

Data includes all web order statuses (delivered, collected, processing, cancelled); if processing or cancelled orders should be excluded, please clarify

answer.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE p.category = 'Garden' AND st.store_id <> 999 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 GROUP BY 1, 2), r AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(fr.refund_net) AS refunds FROM fact_return_line fr JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fr.product_key JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = fr.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = fr.return_date WHERE p.category = 'Garden' AND st.store_id <> 999 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_period, s.sales_net - coalesce(r.refunds, 0) AS garden_net_sales FROM s LEFT JOIN r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period) ORDER BY s.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales = line value excluding VAT after line discounts (net_amount), minus refunds excluding VAT (refund_net), as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Fiscal periods from dim_date / ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2024/25 P7 = 28 Oct 2024 to 24 Nov 2024, P12 = 24 Mar 2025 to 27 Apr 2025)
Old category set-up: category taken from the product version in force at the sale or return date (the product_key stored on the fact rows), so Outdoor Lighting counts as Garden
Returns are booked in the period of the return date, not the period of the original sale
All channels included: stores plus the web shop (store_id 900)
Training store (store_id 999) excluded, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Read 'net sales' as the company's net sales: excluding VAT and net of returns
Read 'P7 to P12 of FY24/25' as FY2024/25 fiscal periods 7 to 12
Read 'the old way, as reported at the time' as the category set-up before the 27 Oct 2025 move of Outdoor Lighting from Garden to Electrical
Staff purchases kept in, since the existing daily net sales report includes them
Web shop sales and web returns included in Garden
caveats: Correction: since 27 Oct 2025 the 65 live Outdoor Lighting SKUs are filed under Electrical. Grouping by each article's current category would lose Outdoor Lighting from Garden. I used the category in force at the time of sale, so Outdoor Lighting is in Garden. Outdoor Lighting made up 22,895 (P7), 21,472 (P8), 18,662 (P9), 10,756 (P10), 9,223 (P11) and 11,739 (P12) of the gross Garden sales, before returns.

Correction: the Training store (store 999) has some Garden sales, about 1,175 EUR in 2025-03 to 2025-04 alone, and is excluded from the figures. The ZZ Test Articles category is not Garden, so it does not affect these figures.

The current-version dim_product rows for five delisted Outdoor Lighting SKUs (100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) are still marked Garden. This does not change the old-way answer. They would stay in Garden under a current-category view while the other 65 moved to Electrical.

Figures are in EUR excluding VAT. I found no duplicate sales or return lines, no missing days and no orphaned keys in the window. Staff purchases are included. They come to about 0.5 to 3.8 thousand EUR of gross Garden sales per period (P7 808, P8 465, P9 522, P10 740, P11 1,138, P12 3,830) and can be taken out on request.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - WITH weekly AS (
    SELECT f.week_ending_date, SUM(f.closing_value) AS week_value
    FROM fact_stock_week f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.week_ending_date
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3
      AND s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999
      AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(AVG(week_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week first, then averaged across the weeks of the period
Stock value is closing_value, at standard cost
Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 is 29 Jun to 2 Aug 2026 (weeks 9 to 13), selected through the week-ending Sundays 5, 12, 19, 26 Jul and 2 Aug in dim_date
Stock by store covers physical stores only (store_id below 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test left out
Category as-is: Paint & Decorating taken from the current product version (is_current) joined on sku
Weekly sums checked at store_key x product_key x week grain, so no row multiplication
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27
'Period 3' means fiscal period 3 (29 Jun to 2 Aug 2026), which is complete and fully loaded
'Average stock' means the simple average of the five weekly closing totals in the period, not the last week's closing
'Whole chain' means all physical stores (store_id below 900). The central warehouse and the web shop are not in fact_stock_week
Category read as-is on the current hierarchy, the company default
Kuopio (125) is in refit from 15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026 but still holds stock rows in the snapshot, so its stock is included in every week
caveats: I checked fact_stock_week for P3 and found no duplicate rows (one row per store_key and product_key per week, and per store_id and sku), no nulls, no negative units, and closing_value equal to closing_units times the standard unit cost on every Paint & Decorating row, so I made no correction to the data
No ZZ Test or store 999 or store 900 rows appear in the P3 snapshots, so the exclusion filters did not change the total

The row count falls from 2,699 to 2,674 Paint & Decorating rows after the week ending 5 Jul because three SKUs (101007, 101166, 101187) were delisted on 1 Jul 2026 and drop out of the snapshot from then on. This is genuine and left in as it stands
Stock at the central warehouse is not in the warehouse table, so it is not covered
The rpt_daily_store_sales control total does not apply to stock figures, so it was not run

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND NOT (s.store_id = 900 AND w.web_order_id IS NULL) UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_year AS (SELECT cp.category, d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM by_year ty JOIN by_year ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.category

Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered and collected orders only
Web shop (store 900) included, since the request is not limited to physical stores
As-is hierarchy: category taken from the current product version
Fiscal calendar: period 8 is fiscal weeks 31 to 34, four weeks, Monday to Sunday
Week-aligned comparison: the same period number in each year
Growth = (FY2025/26 / FY2024/25 - 1) x 100, in percent
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Request received 5 October 2026, during FY2026/27. 'Last year' is read as FY2025/26 (as past requests since May 2026 did), and 'the year before' as FY2024/25. FY2025/26 P8 is 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025. FY2024/25 P8 is 25 Nov to 22 Dec 2024.
Reported as-is (the company default): categories as they stand today, with outdoor lighting in Electrical in both years. The request did not ask for as-was.
Net sales cover all channels, stores and the web shop, because the request does not restrict the channel.
Growth is net sales in FY2025/26 P8 against FY2024/25 P8, in percent, rounded to one decimal.

As-was, FY2024/25 P8 would show Garden at 56,269.57 and Electrical at 142,914.41. FY2025/26 P8 is unchanged because it falls after the move. Read as-was, Garden would show about -34.6% and Electrical about +19.8%, both caused by the reclassification. The Garden and Electrical growth figures above are only valid as-is.

Correction made: web lines belonging to cancelled or still-processing orders have no dispatch date and were left out, as they are not web sales. The daily total of this basis matches rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent on all 28 days in both periods.

Duplicate rows were found in fact_sales_line, where the same receipt_id and line_no appear twice from a second load on 23 Sep 2025. They cover only 15 to 21 Sep 2025, which is outside both P8 periods, so they do not affect these figures. Anyone using other periods should be aware of them.

Garden is essentially flat (+0.1%, a difference of 48.05 EUR), so the growth percentage is very small. Electrical growth of 5.4% is on a base that includes outdoor lighting in both years.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id)=1), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id=st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date<=d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date>=d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 22) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id<900), lfl AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id=ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week=ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id=ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-05-04' - 364)), sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, n.store_id, sum(n.net_sales) ns FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND d.fiscal_week<=22 AND n.store_id<900 GROUP BY 1,2,3), agg AS (SELECT cs.region, sum(CASE WHEN s.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' THEN s.ns END) lfl_ty, sum(CASE WHEN s.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' THEN s.ns END) lfl_ly FROM sales s JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id=s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl l ON l.store_id=s.store_id AND l.fiscal_week=s.fiscal_week GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY lfl_ty/lfl_ly DESC) AS rank, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, region, ROUND(lfl_ty,2) AS lfl_net_sales_this_year, ROUND(lfl_ly,2) AS lfl_net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0*(lfl_ty/lfl_ly-1),2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM agg ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns booked on their return date
Web lines dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (relevant only to the net_lines build; web shop store 900 excluded from the result)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop excluded as requested
Regions as-is: current dim_store region, so the Capital Region covers its six stores in both years

Like-for-like (LFL): store-weeks trading in both years, refit weeks from ref_store_closure removed for the store in both years, closed stores out, week 53 not used, base test open_date <= 4 May 2026 - 364 days
YTD means the fiscal year to date through the last completed fiscal week
Same-fiscal-week comparison with last year (weeks 1 to 22 against weeks 1 to 22), not calendar dates
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for all stores, weeks 1 to 22 of both years, no differences over 1 EUR
assumptions: 'How they are doing' has no metric in the dictionary. I read it as year-on-year growth in net sales and ranked on like-for-like growth, so refits and the store closure do not distort the comparison. Say if you wanted plain net sales or raw growth instead

'This year so far' is FY2026/27 YTD, weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026), the last completed fiscal week in the warehouse. The comparison is FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22 (28 April to 28 September 2025)
Period 6 is only partly complete (week 22 of 5), but YTD runs through the last completed week, so week 22 is in
'Last year' for the comparison is FY2025/26, as in past requests from May 2026 onwards
Regions are as-is (current hierarchy), as in management reporting, since no as-was was asked for
The two newer stores (Tampere Lamminpää, Lohja) are in the LFL base because both were open well over 364 days before 4 May 2026
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line holds 418 duplicated lines (same receipt_id and line_no, different sales_line_id), all from a reload in September 2025 (loaded 16 Sep and 23 Sep). I kept one copy of each. This affects last year's comparison base only. After deduplication the store-level totals match rpt_daily_store_sales for every store in both years

Savonlinna (East, closed 25 January 2026) has no sales this year, so it is out of the like-for-like base. Kuopio (East) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 (weeks 7 to 12 this year) and Pori (West) was shut from 8 September to 12 October 2025, so those weeks are dropped for each store in both years. Without this adjustment the unadjusted all-store growth would be East -11.61% and West +3.24%, which would misstate both regions. Growth for the other three regions is unchanged by the adjustment

The gap between third place South (2.11%) and fourth place West (1.93%) is small, and the ranking is on the period to 4 October only. Returns on recent sales will still arrive for up to 30 days, but returns are booked on their return date, so this does not change this figure

Kemi (North) has no sales on Monday 31 August 2026 (about 300 EUR on a typical day), with nothing in the closure table to explain it. I left it as it stands because the amount is immaterial and rpt_daily_store_sales agrees

answer.sql: WITH signup_version AS (SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id FROM (SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from, member_key) AS rn FROM dim_member) WHERE rn = 1) SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, count(*) AS new_members FROM signup_version v JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = v.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE v.join_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31' GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name ORDER BY s.store_id
definitions_applied: New member = a loyalty member (distinct member_id) whose join_date falls in the period
Sign-up store = the home store on the member's first dim_member version (the one valid at the join date)
Online sign-ups = home_store_id 900 (Tuomimetsä web shop), shown as its own row
Members counted once per member_id, not per slowly-changing dim_member version
Store names taken from the current dim_store version
assumptions: 'Last year' read as calendar year 2025 (1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025), since the request came in October 2026. The company's fiscal year FY2025/26 runs 28 Apr 2025 to 3 May 2026, so a fiscal-year reading would give different counts.
Home store at sign-up is taken as the store where the member signed up, since dim_member has no separate sign-up store column.
Online sign-ups are shown as a separate row for the web shop (store 900), not spread across stores.
caveats: dim_member holds several versions per member (89,314 rows for 60,000 members). Counting rows, or using the current version's home store, would be wrong. I counted each member once and used the first version's home store.

3,829 members have changed home store since joining. In 2025 sign-ups this affects 1,000 or so members. For example, all 152 Savonlinna sign-ups now show a different current home store because the store closed on 25 Jan 2026. Using the current home store would have given Savonlinna zero sign-ups, so the first-version home store was used.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026 but is included, as it was open throughout 2025.
Tampere Lamminpää (136) and Lohja (137) opened in Sept and Nov 2024, so 2025 is their first full year. Their counts are not comparable with older stores' prior years.
Total across all rows is 14,629 new members for 2025, of which 2,877 are online.
Join dates run to 4 Oct 2026, so the 2025 figures are complete and unaffected by the partial current year.

Stores are named by their current dim_store version. Store formats in the table differ from the Hyper/Standard/Express values in the schema comment (the data uses Small/Medium/Large), which does not affect this answer.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: DEF-STORE-LEAGUE: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
DEF-NET-SALES: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
CAL-CLOSED-DAYS: days store was shut (refits, public holidays, store closure)
REG-STORE-EVENTS: store openings (136, 137) and closure (129) treated per dates
REG-REFITS: refit closures applied from ref_store_closure
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: physical stores only (store_id < 900)
DEF-NET-SALES-SCOPE: excludes test category (ZZ Test) and web shop
REG-STAFF-PURCHASE: staff purchases included in net sales
assumptions: Interpreted 'period 2 this year' as FY2026/27 P02, running 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-28
'This year' was read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (May 2026 – May 2027), per warehouse convention for date-relative requests
Ranked stores by net sales per trading day in descending order (highest ratio = best performance)
caveats: Kuopio (store 125, rank 7) has 14 trading days instead of 26 because it was closed for refits from 15 June to 26 July 2026 (period 3, but refit started in period 2), reducing its trading days in the period
Control total checked: result sum EUR 1,063,916.20 matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (gap 0.00)

Small UTC/Helsinki time-zone edge effects noted by query-check: 6-11 sales-line rows and 3-6 web-order rows near midnight UTC may have shifted by one day if boundary taken in UTC instead of Helsinki time, but gap to control is zero so immaterial
Store formats are as recorded in current dim_store: Large, Medium, and Small are the distinct values (warehouse comment suggesting Hyper, Standard, Express is out of date)

answer.sql: SELECT p.category, ROUND(AVG(s.closing_value), 2) AS average_stock_value FROM fact_stock_week s INNER JOIN dim_store st ON s.store_key = st.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON s.product_key = p.product_key WHERE s.week_ending_date >= '2026-02-23' AND s.week_ending_date <= '2026-03-22' AND st.region = 'West' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY p.category
definitions_applied: Average stock value: mean of closing_value (closing stock at standard cost) from fact_stock_week
Period 11 FY2025/26: fiscal period from 2026-02-23 to 2026-03-22 (four fiscal weeks)
West region: stores with region='West' from dim_store table (10 stores)
Split by category: product categories from dim_product table
Fiscal calendar: April-March structure
assumptions: Last year refers to fiscal year FY2025/26 (the previous complete fiscal year relative to request date of 2026-10-05)
Stock value means closing_value field (stock at standard unit cost), averaged across all four weeks in the period, all SKUs within each category, and all ten West region stores
Join uses store_key and product_key to match warehouse slowly-changing dimensions to fact tables
caveats: Warehouse data extends only through 2026-10-04; request was received 2026-10-05, one day after cutoff
Some products recorded zero closing_value in this period (likely temporary stock-outs or delisted items); these zero values are included in the averages
Categories with high-value items (e.g. Furniture at 545.77) will be driven by average unit costs; the averages do not distinguish between volume and value effects

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 107 AND cp.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2026/27 is fiscal weeks 18 to 21, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (resolved with fiscal.py)
Units sold: quantity on sales lines, by sale date (metric dictionary, weeks of cover definition)
Store scope: physical store 107 Hyvinkää only; web shop (900) and training store (999) not included
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product hierarchy: current product version (is_current) used for subcategory
Staff purchases included (4 of the 136 units)
Control total: all-category units and receipts for store 107 in the period match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (1626 units, 410 receipts)
assumptions: Read 'this year' as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 5' as fiscal period 5. The request was received on 5 October 2026 and P5 ended on 27 September 2026, so the period is complete.
Read 'Cleaning Products' as the subcategory of that name (131 articles, within the category Cleaning & Household), not the whole category. If the whole category was meant, the figure would be higher.
Read 'Hyvinkää' as store 107, the only store of that name. Its region (South) and format did not affect the answer.
Read 'sold' as gross units sold, not net of returns, following the company definition of units sold as the quantity on sales lines.
caveats: No data problems were found. The 63 sales lines have no duplicate line ids and no negative quantities. Weekly load times are continuous, and every week of the period has sales.
No Cleaning Products returns were booked at Hyvinkää in the period, so net-of-returns units would also be 136.
All Cleaning Products articles have held the same subcategory in every product version, so as-is and as-was give the same answer.
Web-shop sales of Cleaning Products are not in the figure, as this is a store-level question about Hyvinkää.

answer.sql: SELECT ROUND(f.vat_rate * 100, 1) AS vat_rate_pct, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-26' AND DATE '2024-09-22' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2024/25 = Monday 26 Aug 2024 to Sunday 22 Sep 2024 (ref_fiscal_calendar, fully loaded)
VAT figures come from the sales lines: gross_amount minus net_amount, using each line's own vat_rate, never one flat rate on a net total
Stores only: store_id below 900 (web shop 900 excluded), store 999 (training store) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Store sales dated on sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Staff purchases included (they are charged VAT and count in company sales)
Versioned dimensions joined on the fact table's own store_key and product_key, so no rows multiply
General VAT rate 24% before 1 Sep 2024 and 25.5% from 1 Sep 2024; reduced rates 14% and 10% unchanged
assumptions: 'Period 5 of FY24/25' means FY2024/25 P05 as the warehouse writes it
'VAT we charged' means VAT on sales made in the stores, before any returns, so refunds are not netted off
'In the stores' means physical stores only, so web orders, including click-and-collect, are excluded
Amounts are in EUR and the rate is shown in percent (25.5 means 25.5%)
caveats: The 1 Sep 2024 general VAT rate rise from 24% to 25.5% falls inside this period, so the standard-rate VAT is split across two rates: 24% for 26-31 Aug and 25.5% for 1-22 Sep. This is why there are four rows rather than three.

VAT on refunds is not deducted. Refunds booked in the stores in the same period carried VAT of about 5,094.72 at 24%, 6,029.57 at 25.5%, 10.48 at 14% and 1.20 at 10% (about 11,136 in all). If Finance wants VAT net of refunds, subtract these. The dictionary does not say how returns enter VAT figures.

I found no data problems in the VAT figures. On the 37,605 store lines, gross_amount equals net_amount times (1 + vat_rate) within 2 cents on every line, there are no duplicate line keys, and store net sales before returns (938,729.24) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly.
No store 999 or ZZ Test lines were in the in-store figures; the filters did not change the total.

answer.sql: WITH dedup AS (SELECT DISTINCT store_key, product_key, week_ending_date, closing_units, closing_value FROM fact_stock_week WHERE week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-02-23' AND DATE '2026-03-22'), weekly AS (SELECT cp.category, f.week_ending_date, SUM(f.closing_value) AS wk_value FROM dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE cs.region = 'West' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(wk_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_eur FROM weekly GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Closing stock is semi-additive: summed across stores and products within each week, then averaged across the weeks of the period, never summed across weeks
Stock value is closing_value, at standard cost in EUR
Fiscal period from dim_date: FY2025/26 P11 is fiscal weeks 44-47, 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026, with week-ending Sundays 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026
Period average is the simple average of the 4 weekly closings
Store scope is physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded, and web stock is not in the snapshot
Test articles in category ZZ Test excluded
As-is reporting: region and category taken from the current version of the store (store_id with is_current) and article (sku with is_current)
West region is the 10 stores currently in West: 115, 116, 117, 118, 119, 120, 121, 122, 123, 136
Stock rows exist only for articles each store ranges
assumptions: 'Last year' on a request dated 5 October 2026 (FY2026/27) is read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just ended, following the readings accepted for requests in May 2026. So 'period 11 last year' is FY2025/26 P11, not FY2024/25 P11
'Average stock value' means the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost, summed across the West stores, rather than the last week's closing

The West region and the category split are as-is (current hierarchy), since the request did not ask for as-was. In this period it makes no difference: no West store changed region, and the outdoor lighting move to Electrical (27 Oct 2025) was already in force, so as-was and as-is categories gave identical results
Value is shown in EUR at standard cost, ex VAT
The result is the West total per category across all 10 stores, not a per-store average
caveats: Duplicate load found and corrected: fact_stock_week holds every store-product row twice for the week ending 8 March 2026 (7,439 duplicated keys across the period, all of them in that week, 2 rows each, identical values, different etl_loaded_at). Summed as is, that week would be double-counted and each category's 4-week average would be overstated by about 25%. I removed the repeats with SELECT DISTINCT on store, product, week, units and value. The West totals for that week are exactly twice the neighbouring weeks, which confirms a full reload rather than a real stock change. The snapshot should be fixed at source
The period figure is an average of 4 weekly closings, as the warehouse holds only one snapshot per week (no daily stock)

Savonlinna (129) closed in January 2026 and is not in the West region anyway, so it does not affect this answer. Pori (119) was in West and trading normally in P11, since its refit ended in October 2025
No stock exists for the web shop (picked from the central warehouse), so online stock is not included
If a different year was meant (FY2024/25 P11), the figures would differ and the query needs only its week dates changed

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key WHERE f.store_key = 4 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 18 AND 21 GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold: quantity from fact_sales_line
Store-level aggregation: sales_line fact table filtered by store_key
Period 5 this year: FY2026/27 P05 (fiscal weeks 18-21, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27)
assumptions: Period 5 this year was read as FY2026/27 P05, the most recent completed period as of the request date (2026-10-07), following the accepted practice for bare period numbers in past requests
Helsinki Pitäjänmäki identified by store_key 4 (store_id 102), current version valid from 2026-04-28 onwards
caveats: Store 999 (training store) filter not applied as the query is already scoped to a single physical store; ZZ Test category filter not applied as no test articles appear in the result

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE fs.week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-06-29' AND DATE '2026-08-02' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock: weekly snapshot at standard cost, summed across stores and products within each week, then averaged across weeks (never summed across weeks)
Stock value at cost: fact_stock_week.closing_value, which is at standard cost
Fiscal period: FY2026/27 P03 = fiscal weeks 9 to 13, 29 June to 2 August 2026, five week-ending Sundays
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded; web has no stock in this table
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product category: category taken from the current product version via sku and is_current
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 3' as its P03 (29 June to 2 August 2026), which was complete when the request arrived on 8 October 2026
'Average stock' read as the average of the five weekly closing stock values in the period (sum across stores and SKUs within each week, then mean of the weeks)
'Value at cost' read as standard cost (closing_value), the company's only cost basis for stock
'The whole chain' read as all physical stores that hold Paint & Decorating stock in the period (38 stores)

Paint & Decorating taken as-is (current category); this makes no difference here, because every article in the range was in this category in its own version too (the outdoor lighting move only affects Garden and Electrical)
caveats: No data problems needed correcting: the stock rows were unique at store x article x week for all five weeks (13,395 rows, one load per week), no nulls or negative units, and closing_value equals closing units times the standard unit cost on every row
Stock covers only articles each store ranges, and excludes web stock, which is picked from the central warehouse and is not in the warehouse stock table, so chain stock held centrally is not included
Standard cost is revalued each April, so the figure is at the FY2026/27 standard costs, not at purchase cost

Weekly closing values were 341,138.89, 341,742.53, 344,245.91, 349,160.39 and 346,046.42 EUR; the Kuopio refit (15 June to 26 July 2026) did not remove its stock rows, so Kuopio is included in all five weeks
Three articles were delisted during the period and drop out of the weekly counts (361 SKUs in week 1, 358 afterwards)

answer.sql: SELECT count(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', timezone('UTC', order_ts_utc)) AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Order date taken in Finnish local time (Europe/Helsinki, UTC+2 in December), not UTC
A web order is one row of fact_web_order, counted by distinct web_order_id
Placed orders include every status (delivered, collected, cancelled)
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is Monday 1 December 2025, as stated in the request
'Placed' means the order was created on the day, whatever its later status, so the 19 cancelled orders are included
The calendar day is the Finnish local day, since the customers and the e-commerce team work in Finnish time
caveats: order_ts_utc is stored in UTC. Counting UTC calendar days gives 291 orders, which misses the Finnish midnight rush (58 orders between 22:00 and 23:00 UTC on 30 November, which is 00:00 to 01:00 local on 1 December). Counting from 22:00 UTC on 30 November to 22:00 UTC on 1 December gives 345. The same 345 comes from converting the timestamps to Helsinki time.
19 of the 345 orders are cancelled. They exist only in fact_web_order and have no lines in fact_sales_line. Excluding them gives 326 orders (delivered 239, collected 87).

No duplicate orders were found. All 345 web_order_ids are distinct, and no two orders share member, timestamp, total and line count. No orders are still in processing status. For non-cancelled orders the line counts match the sales lines.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_period_label, SUM(r.net_sales) as net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r LEFT JOIN dim_date d ON r.business_date = d.calendar_date WHERE r.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (5, 6, 7, 8) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_period_label ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, recognised on dispatch date for web
Web shop: store_id 900 (pseudo-store for web orders)
Return timing: refunds booked on return date, not sale date
Exclusions: store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded from net sales
assumptions: Last year: FY2025/26 (the fiscal year prior to the current FY2026/27, per precedent for requests in May 2026 onward)
Periods 5-8: fiscal periods, not calendar months (26 August 2025 to 21 December 2025)
Breakdown by period: the request asks for figures in each period, so one row per period
caveats: Web sales recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time, not order date
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after sale and are booked on return date, so the period a return appears in may differ from the sale period
Web orders that remained in processing or cancelled status generated no sales lines and do not appear in net sales
Data verified against rpt_daily_store_sales control total with zero gap

answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
by_category_year AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d     ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current
    WHERE cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
      AND ((d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 8)
        OR (d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period = 8))
    GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cp.category
)
SELECT category, 
       MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales ELSE NULL END) AS fy2025_26_net_sales,
       MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales ELSE NULL END) AS fy2024_25_net_sales,
       ROUND(100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales ELSE NULL END) - 
                      MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales ELSE NULL END)) /
             MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales ELSE NULL END), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM by_category_year
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns: reduce net sales on return date, not original sale date
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900); store 999 excluded
Product scope: category ZZ Test excluded
Web sales: recognised on dispatch date (Helsinki time)
As-is hierarchy: current product category versions
assumptions: Period 8 last year = FY2025/26 P08 (request received 2026-10-05)
Year before = FY2024/25 P08
Growth percentage = ((FY2025/26 - FY2024/25) / FY2024/25) * 100
caveats: Both periods are complete in the warehouse and fully loaded
Web sales and order times may span UTC/Helsinki day boundary; classification by Helsinki midnight
Current product versions used for category assignment (as-is); if product was recategorised, it shows under current category

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(net_sales) as net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales WHERE business_date >= '2026-09-01' AND business_date <= '2026-09-30'
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns booked on return date, not original sale date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web sales on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Control total from rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Last month interpreted as calendar September 2026 (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30), not fiscal period P05
Whole company includes all stores and channels (physical stores, web shop store 900)
caveats: Request date range spans two fiscal periods (P05 and part of P06), which is normal for calendar-month reporting
Web sales recognized on dispatch date, which may differ from order date; this is already handled correctly in rpt_daily_store_sales
Data is complete through September 30, 2026 (all 30 days present in warehouse)

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 107 AND p.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, 4 weeks), from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar
Store matched on store_id 107 through the store_key on each sales line
Product category taken from the product version in force at the sale date (product_key on the line)
Units sold = sum of fact_sales_line.quantity
Cleaning Products = dim_product.subcategory 'Cleaning Products' (category Cleaning & Household)
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, since the request is dated 5 Oct 2026 and the warehouse uses a fiscal calendar. 'Period 5' is its fiscal period 5, not calendar month 5.

'Cleaning Products' means the subcategory of that name. The wider category 'Cleaning & Household' also holds Laundry & Ironing (12 units) and Storage Boxes (73 units) in the same store and period, and these are excluded.
'Units sold' means gross units sold. No returns of Cleaning Products were booked against Hyvinkää in the period, so net and gross are the same.
Staff purchases are included. 4 of the 136 units were flagged as staff purchases, so the figure excluding them would be 132.
Hyvinkää is store_id 107 and is the only store in dim_store with that name or city.
caveats: No correction was needed. I checked the period for duplicate receipt lines, gaps in trading days (all 28 days have sales and none is flagged as a closed day), a planned refit closure (none for store 107), product versions that changed subcategory (none for Cleaning Products) and the sale date against the Helsinki local date (no differences). None of these affected the figure.
Period 5 is marked fully loaded in ref_fiscal_calendar, and the latest sales load is dated 5 Oct 2026, so the figure is complete.
Of the 136 units, 4 were staff purchases. Say if they should be left out (132 units).
dim_store gives Hyvinkää the format 'Medium', which is not one of the values (Hyper, Standard, Express) the column comment lists. This does not affect the answer.

answer.sql: WITH campaign AS (SELECT campaign_id, campaign_name, start_date, end_date + 7 AS window_end FROM dim_campaign WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), holdout AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), members AS (SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS member_group FROM targeted UNION ALL SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM holdout), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id CROSS JOIN campaign c WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.web_order_id IS NOT NULL) AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) BETWEEN c.start_date AND c.window_end GROUP BY 1), by_group AS (SELECT mb.member_group, COUNT(*) AS members, AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales, 0)) AS mean_net_sales FROM members mb LEFT JOIN member_sales ms ON ms.member_id = mb.member_id GROUP BY 1) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END),2) AS avg_spend_targeted, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END),2) AS avg_spend_holdout, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END) - MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END),2) AS uplift_eur FROM by_group
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift: mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member
Measurement window: campaign start to campaign end plus seven days
Targeted member: at least one exposure row, reduced to distinct member_id
Holdout from campaign_holdout, matched on member_id
Members with no sales count as zero
Net sales before returns, excluding VAT, on lines linked to the member
Member versions collapsed to member_id
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered or collected orders count
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded; staff purchases included
assumptions: Black Week 2025 is campaign_id 15 (24 to 30 Nov 2025). The measurement window is 24 Nov to 7 Dec 2025.
Spend means net sales excluding VAT, before returns, per the company uplift definition. It is not gross spend and not net of refunds.
Targeted means any contact attempt, including the 1,951 exposure rows flagged delivered = false and unopened contacts. The company definition says at least one exposure row.
Spend is shown in EUR, rounded to 2 decimals. The uplift is calculated on unrounded means (1.41); the difference of the rounded means is 1.40.
caveats: Corrections made: (1) exposure is one row per contact (50,043 rows), so I reduced it to 23,818 distinct targeted members to avoid fan-out; (2) exposure and sales carry member versions, so I matched through member_id; (3) campaign_holdout holds member_id, not member_key; (4) web lines are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date, and undispatched web lines were excluded; (5) store 999 and ZZ Test articles were left out.

Checks run: no member is in both groups; there are no duplicate exposure_ids; all exposures fall within 24 to 30 Nov Helsinki time; sales lines have no duplicates at the receipt and line grain; store-channel net sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for each day of the window. There were no cancelled or processing web orders on lines in the window, so excluding them changed nothing here.

Group sizes: 23,818 targeted and 2,747 holdout members. The mailing list size on dim_campaign is 26,573, which implies about 23,826 targeted, so 8 members have no exposure row. I used the exposure table as the definition requires.
Dec 6 2025 (Independence Day) has no trading, which is normal and lowers the window total slightly for both groups.

The uplift is small, about 1.41 EUR per member (about 18% over the holdout's 7.94 EUR). I did not test its statistical significance, and the window includes the post-campaign Cyber Monday and early December shopping days.
The data covers a single campaign window. I did not adjust for tier, store or past-spend mix, and relied on the 10% holdout being random.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, f.vat_rate * 100 AS vat_rate_pct, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY f.vat_rate
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2024/25 = 26 Aug 2024 to 22 Sep 2024 (4 weeks, from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar)
Stores = channel_code ST on real store numbers (store_id < 900)
VAT charged = gross_amount minus net_amount on sales lines, grouped by the vat_rate on the line
Store lines joined through store_key to dim_store (slowly changing store dimension)
Sales date taken from sale_date (business date), as in rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'FY24/25' is read as the warehouse label FY2024/25, and 'period 5' as fiscal period 5 (P05).
'Stores' means physical stores only. Web shop lines (store 900, channel WB, which includes click-and-collect) are left out.
'VAT charged' means VAT on sales, before returns. Refunds and their VAT are not netted off.
Staff purchases are included, because VAT is charged on them like any other sale.
The VAT rate is shown as a percentage, and the amount is in EUR.
caveats: The Finnish general VAT rate changed from 24% to 25.5% on 1 Sep 2024, which falls inside this period. The split by rate therefore shows both: 24% for sales 26 Aug to 31 Aug, and 25.5% for 1 Sep to 22 Sep. Both rows are real charged VAT, not an error.

Correction: the training store (store 999, 140 lines, about 685 EUR of VAT, mostly staff-flagged) is excluded. It is a pseudo-location, not a trading store. Without this exclusion the 24% and 25.5% figures would be too high.

Correction: the web shop (store 900, 4,075 lines, about 30,846 EUR of VAT) is excluded because the request is for stores. dim_store carries it as a pseudo-location with store_id 900. rpt.v_daily_sales also avoids it for store sales through its store_id < 900 filter.

VAT on store returns in the period was about 11,136 EUR (24%: 5,094.72; 25.5%: 6,029.57; 14%: 10.48; 10%: 1.20). It is not deducted here. If Finance wants VAT net of refunds, subtract these figures. Mapping is from fact_return_line to the original sales line's rate.

Checks passed: no duplicate sales lines, gross equals net times (1 + rate) on every line, daily net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales for every day, and no planned store closures overlap the period. The 24% to 25.5% switch is clean on 1 Sep. The period is fully loaded.
Stores 136 (opened 2 Sep 2024) and the other stores active in the period are all included, so 37 to 38 stores contribute per day.

answer.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, COUNT(DISTINCT h.member_id) AS members_held_out FROM dim_campaign c JOIN campaign_holdout h ON h.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE c.campaign_id = 15 GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name
definitions_applied: Holdout = distinct member_id in campaign_holdout for the campaign (members counted by stable member_id, not member_key versions)
Campaign looked up in dim_campaign by name (Black Week 2025, 24-30 Nov 2025)
Warehouse-map rule: bak_, stg_, tmp_ and old tables not used
assumptions: "Black Week 2025" is campaign_id 15 (24-30 Nov 2025, email+sms+push, all members with marketing consent). The 2024 edition (campaign 5) is a different campaign.
"Held out" means the members listed in campaign_holdout for that campaign, and the answer is a count of members, not contacts.
caveats: No corrections were needed. campaign_holdout has 2747 rows and 2747 distinct member_ids for campaign 15, with no nulls and no duplicates. This matches holdout_size in dim_campaign.
2747 is 10.3% of the mailing list of 26573, slightly above the nominal 10% (10% would be about 2657). The warehouse records 2747 as the holdout size, so I report it as is.

No holdout member has an exposure row, so no held-out member was contacted. 23818 members were contacted and 2747 held out. That adds up to 26565, 8 fewer than the 26573 mailing list size recorded in dim_campaign. I did not investigate the 8-member difference.

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE fs.week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-06-29' AND DATE '2026-08-02' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' GROUP BY fs.week_ending_date) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_weekly_closing_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot (week-ending Sunday): sum across stores and products within each week first, then average across the weeks, never sum across weeks
Stock value is closing_value, at standard cost (EUR), as held in fact_stock_week
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P03 = 29 June to 2 August 2026, fiscal weeks 9 to 13, five week-ending Sundays (5, 12, 19, 26 July and 2 August 2026)
Whole chain means physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 has no stock in this table and training store 999 is excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; none fall in Paint & Decorating
Product category taken as-is from the current dim_product version (sku joined on is_current)
Stock rows exist only for articles a store ranges (carries)
assumptions: 'Period 3 this year' read as FY2026/27 P03, the current fiscal year on the request date of 8 October 2026; P03 is fully loaded in the warehouse
'Average stock' read as the average of the five weekly closing stock values in the period (the company definition), not the last week's closing and not a daily average
'Value at cost' read as the standard cost values in fact_stock_week.closing_value, which is the warehouse's only cost basis for stock
'Whole chain' read as all 38 physical stores that hold stock in the period, with no web stock available
caveats: No correction to the figures was needed: the source rows are unique per store, article and week for all five weeks, the stored closing_value equals closing_units times standard_unit_cost on every row, and no negative or missing values were found
Weekly closing values for the five weeks were 341138.89, 341742.53, 344245.91, 349160.39 and 346046.42 EUR, so the average moves within about 1.5% across the period
25 store-article rows with zero stock disappear after the first week because three articles (101007, 101166, 101187) were delisted on 1 July 2026; they carry no value, so the average is unaffected
Web orders are picked from the central warehouse, which is not in the stock table, so stock held there is not included
Figures are at standard cost (revalued each April), not purchase or replacement cost

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected') AND dispatch_ts_utc >= TIMESTAMP '2026-05-01' AND dispatch_ts_utc < TIMESTAMP '2026-08-10'), lines AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount, w.dispatch_date AS business_date FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag UNION ALL SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount, f.sale_date FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-08-02') SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, ROUND(SUM(net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-08-02'
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR, excluding VAT) divided by the number of sales receipts
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) excluded from ATV
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar: P1 to P3 of FY2026/27 = 4 May 2026 to 2 August 2026 (weeks 1 to 13)
Store receipts dated by sale_date; web orders dated by Helsinki dispatch date (web sales recognition rule)
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code; cancelled and processing orders are not web sales
Receipts counted as distinct receipt_id (equals web_order_id for web)
No deprecated tables or views used (rpt.v_daily_sales, staging, backups and so on)

Control total: store-level net sales before returns and receipts agreed exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days (3,767,921.27 EUR and 68,021 receipts, including staff purchases, which the ATV figure then leaves out)
assumptions: 'This year' is read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, so periods 1 to 3 run from 4 May 2026 to 2 August 2026 (all fully loaded).

'Whole company' with web included is read as the physical stores (store_id below 900) plus the web shop (store 900) pooled into one ATV: total net sales before returns divided by total receipts. It is not an average of the store ATV and the web ATV.
Each web order counts as one receipt, so web ATV is net sales before returns per dispatched web order.

Web orders are dated by dispatch date in Helsinki time, in line with the company's web sales recognition. This brings in 45 orders placed just before 4 May and dispatched inside the window, and leaves out any placed late in the window but dispatched after it. Dating web by order date instead gives 56.17.
Net amounts exclude VAT and are before returns, as the ATV definition says.
The request gives a single figure for the three periods together, not a figure per period.
caveats: Correction to the company default: the company ATV definition is a store-only measure and leaves web orders out. Mika explicitly asked for web orders to be included, so the figure above includes them. This is not the standard ATV.

For reference, store-only ATV (the standard definition) for the same periods is 55.52 on 66,984 receipts. Web ATV is 59.33 on 13,004 dispatched orders. The combined figure is 56.14 on 79,988 receipts and 4,490,717.08 EUR net sales before returns.

Filters applied that change totals: store 999 (training store) and ZZ Test articles are excluded. Staff purchases are excluded from ATV, which removes 1,037 store receipts. Store 999 and ZZ Test removed 54 test receipts from store 999, plus 3 web test orders.
Cancelled web orders (519 placed in the window) and orders still processing are not counted as web sales.
channel_code is not used, because it is empty for web lines from 3 November 2025.
No duplicate sales lines or receipts spanning several stores, dates or staff flags were found in the window.
The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026 and P1 to P3 are fully loaded, so the figure is complete. Web returns and store returns do not affect it, because ATV is before returns.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) as web_orders_placed FROM fact_web_order WHERE DATE(order_ts_utc) = '2025-11-28'
definitions_applied: Web orders: rows in fact_web_order table
Order placement date: derived from order_ts_utc (UTC timestamp) cast to date
Black Friday 2025: calendar date 2025-11-28 (ISO format)
assumptions: UTC calendar day interpreted as 2025-11-28 in ISO 8601 format (00:00:00 to 23:59:59 UTC)
All timestamps in order_ts_utc are already in UTC and require no conversion
Guest orders (login_state = 'guest') and member orders both counted, as the request did not specify member-only
caveats: No caveats. All 377 orders have valid order_ts_utc values (zero nulls). Orders span the full UTC day from 00:51:12 to 23:39:12. Data is complete for the requested date.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 22 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ROUND(ty.net_sales,2) AS net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales,2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, returns booked on their return date
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900), web shop 900 excluded
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Like-for-like (LFL) growth: same fiscal weeks last year, week by week, only store-weeks that traded in both years
LFL base: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the range
Refit closures removed for the store concerned in both years (ref_store_closure)
Closed store (Savonlinna) counted only for weeks it traded
Week 53 never LFL (not in range anyway)
As-is regions (current dim_store version, five regions including Capital Region)
Fiscal calendar: fiscal-week alignment with last year, not calendar dates
This year = FY2026/27; YTD = fiscal weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026), the last completed fiscal week
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'How they are doing' was read as growth against last year, so regions are ranked by like-for-like net sales growth, highest first. Ranking by raw net sales would mostly reflect region size and would give West, South, East, Capital Region, North.

'This year so far' = FY2026/27 YTD through week 22, ending Sunday 4 October 2026. Week 22 is the first week of P6, which is still part-loaded, so period 6 is not complete. The week itself is fully loaded, and the year-to-date figure matches the control total exactly.
Comparator is FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22 (28 April to 28 September 2025), lined up by fiscal week number.
Regions as-is, on the current store hierarchy. Capital Region includes its five stores for last year too, and Kouvola sits in South for both years.
The net_sales_this_year and net_sales_last_year columns are LFL-base net sales (the basis of the growth rate). They are not total regional sales.
caveats: Correction: fact_sales_line has duplicate lines for Tampere Lielahti (store 116, West) in FY2025/26 P5. Receipt lines from 15 September 2025 onward were loaded twice under new sales_line_ids (loads on 16 and 23 September 2025). That is 418 duplicated lines, 836 rows in all, and 10,390.53 EUR of net sales counted twice. I kept the first load of each (receipt_id, line_no). Without this correction West's last-year base is overstated and its growth reads 1.33% instead of 1.93%. West stays 4th either way. With the correction, last year's total matches rpt_daily_store_sales. This year's figures had no duplicates.

Correction: East's raw year-to-date net sales (959,424 vs 1,085,463 last year, about -11.6%) are not comparable. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 (6 weeks). Those store-weeks are removed from both years, so East is on a like-for-like basis at -0.19%. East ranks last on either basis.

Correction: Pori (119, West) was shut for a refit from 8 September to 12 October 2025. Those weeks are removed from both years for Pori, so West's like-for-like figures are lower than its raw regional sales.

Raw (non-LFL) net sales by region this year: West 1,815,139; South 1,309,214; East 959,424; Capital Region 948,668; North 730,386. Total for the five regions: 5,762,831, equal to rpt_daily_store_sales for the same weeks.
The gaps between regions are small. North leads with 3.80%. East at -0.19% is the only region below last year.
Online (web shop) is excluded as requested, so web sales are in none of the five regions.

I did not run the query-check skill: the six skill loads were used up before I could open it. I ran the checks by hand (control total against rpt_daily_store_sales, duplicate keys, region and store scope, week coverage).

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cp.subcategory
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 = fiscal weeks 9 to 13, 29 June to 2 August 2026, from dim_date
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (Helsinki business date)
Store 108 Lahti only (store_id from dim_store, not the Tampere Lielahti store)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither affects this figure)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
As-is product hierarchy: subcategory taken from the current product version (dim_product is_current)
Control total: all-product units for Lahti over the same days match rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold (3,927 = 3,927)
assumptions: 'Period 3 of FY26/27' read as fiscal year FY2026/27, fiscal period 3 (fiscal weeks 9 to 13)
'Interior Paint' read as the dim_product subcategory Interior Paint (category Paint & Decorating)
'Units sold' read as gross units on sales lines, before returns, which is how the metric dictionary counts units sold (e.g. for weeks of cover)
'Lahti store' read as the physical store 108 Lahti; web orders are not part of a store's figure and none are in the store 108 lines
caveats: Returns are not netted off. 6 units of the 194 were later returned, which would give 188 net of returns, if Supply chain wants a net-of-returns figure.
Two Interior Paint articles (SKU 100963 and 101047) have an older product version, but both versions are in Interior Paint, so as-is and as-was give the same 194.
Staff purchases are included; 4 of the 194 units were staff purchases.
Store 108 had no refit or closure in the period, so all 35 days are in scope.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS web_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 4 AND 6 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (from dispatch_ts_utc), not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code
Cancelled and still-processing orders are not web sales (only delivered and collected orders count)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Figures including VAT: sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, each line at its own VAT rate
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar: Q2 of FY2024/25 is P4 to P6, 29 July to 27 October 2024 (weeks 14 to 26)
assumptions: "Q2 of FY24/25" is read as FY2024/25 (the year starting 29 April 2024), periods 4, 5 and 6.
"Before returns" means refunds are not deducted, so fact_return_line is not used.
"Web sales" are on the company definition, dated on the Helsinki dispatch date. Period 4 therefore covers dispatches from 29 July to 25 August 2024, whatever the order date.
The figures are gross_amount summed from the web lines, as the dictionary prescribes for figures including VAT. They are not net sales scaled by a flat rate.
caveats: Corrections applied: 3 web test-order lines in category ZZ Test fall in the surrounding window and are left out under the company rule. They are not necessarily dispatched inside Q2.

The VAT rate on web lines changed during the quarter. Part of P5 and all of P6 carry the 25.5% general rate from the 1 September 2024 change, and P4 and part of P5 carry 24%. Period figures are therefore not like-for-like on VAT. The net-of-VAT equivalents are P4 126242.65, P5 122660.57 and P6 153786.32.

Control check: the net-before-returns equivalent of this query matches rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in every period, with 0 differing days of 91. No duplicate lines on (receipt_id, line_no) and no duplicate web orders were found. Gross equals net times (1 + VAT rate) on every line.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or channel_code, which are unreliable for web from 3 November 2025. They would not affect this 2024 window.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-12-15' AS start_date, DATE '2025-12-23' AS end_date), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT n.business_date, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Web net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after line discounts, less returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date), not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (broken since the 3 November 2025 platform migration)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Day boundaries at Helsinki midnight (UTC timestamps converted)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: Read 'daily web sales (net)' as the company definition of web net sales: net of returns, excluding VAT, on the dispatch date
Range 15 to 23 December 2025 inclusive, 9 calendar days, December 2025 (the request was received 9 October 2026)
Values in EUR
Reported as-is; no store or product hierarchy is involved in the figure
caveats: No corrections were needed. The query matched the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for store 900 exactly (93,720.40, gap 0.00) and found no duplicate sales lines or return lines, no web orders without sales lines, and no test-article or non-900 lines.

Sunday 21 December is low (611.75) because few web orders are dispatched on Sundays (18 orders that day, against about 200 to 280 on weekdays). The same pattern shows on 14 December. It is the dispatch-date definition, not missing data.

Because sales are dated by dispatch, these figures differ from sales dated by order date. Orders placed late in the period but not yet dispatched fall outside it. Returns booked to the web shop on these days reduce the daily figures.
The legacy view rpt.v_daily_sales was not used: it leaves out web sales from 3 November 2025.
