answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.web_order_id IS NOT NULL) UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 18 AND 21 GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY net_sales DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns (returns deducted on their own return date)
Last period = last completed fiscal period: FY2026/27 P05, fiscal weeks 18 to 21, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected web orders counted
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Products identified by stable sku, using the current product version for the name (as-is)
Company-wide scope: all physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days
assumptions: 'Best-selling' is read as highest net sales value in EUR excluding VAT, the company's sales measure, rather than units sold
'Last period' read as FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), the last completed period as of the request date 8 Oct 2026; P06 is only one week loaded
Scope is the whole company (stores and web), as the request names no region or channel
Products are ranked individually at article (sku) level
caveats: If 'best-selling' was meant as units sold, the ranking is very different. For example, Fixings & Fasteners Nordhem 594 is second by net units, Cushions & Throws Tuulikki 338 is eighth, and Interior Paint Norvik 298 is only 24th. Net sales is used here as the company definition. A units ranking can be run on request.
The web orders filter removes web lines from cancelled and still-processing orders, because only delivered and collected orders count as web sales. This follows the company definition.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were excluded. This did not change the total, because the company-wide control total (EUR 1,109,546.52 for the period) matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly.
No duplicate sales or return lines were found in the period. Returns are netted on their own return date, so a product's figure can include refunds for goods sold before the period.
Rankings 1 to 10 are clear with no ties at the cut-off: rank 10 is EUR 4,477.73 and rank 11 is EUR 4,262.06.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or any deprecated, staging, backup or tmp tables.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(date_trunc('month', f.sale_date), '%Y-%m') AS month, sum(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.sale_date >= DATE '2024-08-01' AND f.sale_date < DATE '2024-10-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Store sales means physical store channel only (channel_code ST), with web shop sales excluded
Pseudo-locations excluded (store_id 900 web shop, 999 Training store); real stores are store_id below 900
Sales including VAT is gross_amount on fact_sales_line, which is net_amount plus VAT at the line's own VAT rate
Before returns: fact_return_line is not used and nothing is netted off
Calendar months by sale_date (1 to 31 August 2024, 1 to 30 September 2024)
Store identity via fact_sales_line.store_key joined to dim_store, the store version valid at the sale date
assumptions: August 2024 and September 2024 are read as calendar months, not fiscal periods
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag = true) are kept in, because they are real till sales. Excluding them would give 1,348,131.97 for August and 1,192,473.76 for September
Store sales means all real stores trading in the period, not only like-for-like stores
gross_amount is taken as stored. I checked that it equals net_amount x (1 + vat_rate) on every store line in the window, and that the rates are valid for the dates
The Training store (999) is test data, not a trading location, so it is excluded
Click-and-collect and home-delivery web orders are all web sales, not store sales, so they are excluded even when collected in a store
caveats: Correction: 283 ST-channel lines (7,633.94 EUR including VAT across the two months) are booked to the Training store (store_id 999). They are removed from the figures. The existing view rpt.v_daily_sales would include them, since it filters ST by store_id below 900 only for the store branch of its union and so is not a safe source for this request.
Correction: the web channel (WB, booked to the web shop, store_id 900) is excluded. rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns includes web, which is why it does not match the store-only figures.

The VAT rate changed on 1 September 2024, with the standard rate going from 24% to 25.5%. The September gross figure uses the higher rate on standard-rated goods. This is correct for the period, but the VAT share of the month-on-month change is not a volume change.

Vantaa Tammisto (104) was closed for a refit until 11 August 2024, so August is missing its first 11 days for that store. Tampere Lamminpää (136) opened on 2 September 2024, so September includes a new store with no August comparison. Both are real and not data errors, but they distort any month-on-month comparison.
Porvoo (106) has no sales on 22 September 2024, which is a trading day. It is a small store and I could not confirm whether this is a real zero or a missing day.
No duplicate lines were found in the window (receipt_id and line_no are unique in fact_sales_line for these months). The staging tables hold no rows for this period.
The figures are in EUR including VAT and are not net of returns, as requested. Net of returns they would be lower.

answer.sql:
-- Like-for-like (LFL) net sales growth for P1 FY2026/27 vs P1 FY2025/26
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 4 AS last_week
),
range_start AS (
    SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week
),
weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN weeks w
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    CROSS JOIN params
    CROSS JOIN range_start
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
    GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))
)
SELECT ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM lfl_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NULL;
definitions_applied: DEF-LFL-BASIS: LFL covers physical stores only (store_id < 900); web shop excluded
DEF-LFL-OPEN: Store must be open at least 52 weeks (364 days) before the first day of the period
DEF-LFL-BOTH-YEARS: Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years
DEF-LFL-REFIT: Refit weeks excluded using ref_store_closure for both years
DEF-LFL-WEEK53: Week 53 never counts as LFL (has no comparator week)
DEF-NET-SALES: Net amount excluding VAT, after returns; store 999 and ZZ Test category excluded
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: Physical stores only; store 999 never included
DEF-HIERARCHY-ASIS: Current store region as-is reporting
CAL-COMPARE: Fiscal weeks aligned by week number for year-over-year comparison
assumptions: Interpreted 'period 1 this year' as P1 FY2026/27 (fiscal weeks 1-4, May 4-31, 2026)
Compared against the same fiscal weeks in the prior year: P1 FY2025/26 (fiscal weeks 1-4, April 28-May 25, 2025)
Request asks for total company LFL growth only (no regional breakdown requested)
Warehouse loaded through 2026-10-04; P1 FY2026/27 is fully complete as of that date
caveats: LFL sales are 152 store-weeks in total across both periods (some stores excluded due to opening rule or closure/refit events)
Web shop and store 999 are not part of LFL base per company definition
Timezone note: UTC/Helsinki day boundary differences noted in query check but do not affect this aggregate result

answer.sql: WITH store_receipts AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-08-02'), web_receipts AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-08-02'), all_receipts AS (SELECT * FROM store_receipts UNION ALL SELECT * FROM web_receipts) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS first_period, 3 AS last_period, ROUND(SUM(net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM all_receipts
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR excluding VAT) divided by the number of sales receipts
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 periods 1 to 3, 4 May 2026 to 2 August 2026 (13 weeks, whole fiscal weeks)
Staff purchases excluded from ATV (staff_purchase_flag)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop = store_id 900, identified by store_id and not by channel_code
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (UTC converted with timezone('Europe/Helsinki', ...)); store sales dated by sale_date
Each web order counts as one receipt (receipt_id equals web_order_id); cancelled and processing orders have no sales lines, so they are not counted
Returns not deducted (ATV is before returns)
Control total: store figures checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, so 'periods 1 to 3' is P01 to P03 (4 May to 2 August 2026). The warehouse is loaded to 4 October 2026 and all three periods are fully loaded.
'The whole company' read as the physical stores plus the web shop (store 900).
The company definition of ATV leaves web orders out. You asked for them in, so I followed the request and added them, treating each dispatched web order as one transaction.

Web orders are dated by dispatch date, as for web sales, so the revenue and the order count in the ATV come from the same set of orders. The metric dictionary counts web orders by order date, but that would pair the revenue and the count on different order sets. The effect is small: 12,959 orders by order date against 13,004 by dispatch date, with similar net sales.
Staff purchases excluded from the combined ATV as in the standard ATV definition. There are no staff purchases on web lines, so this only affects the stores.
The answer is one company-wide figure for the three periods together (net sales divided by receipts over the whole range). It is not an average of three period ATVs.
caveats: Correction 1: the standard ATV excludes web. I added web at your request, so this figure is not comparable with ATV figures reported on the store-only definition. Stores only, the same periods give 55.52, and web alone gives 59.33 (13,004 dispatched web orders). The combined figure is 56.14 on 79,988 receipts and EUR 4,490,717.08 of net sales before returns.
Correction 2: web revenue is dated by dispatch date in Helsinki time, not by the sale_date on the web lines, which is the order date.

Correction 3: store 999 and the ZZ Test articles are excluded. Store 999 has 186 receipts in the range. Three web orders dispatched in the range carry ZZ Test lines (EUR 6.00 in total) and were removed, which gives 13,004 web receipts and EUR 771,530.75. The same figures appear in rpt_daily_store_sales.

Control check: for the same days, physical stores reconcile exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales (68,021 receipts and EUR 3,767,921.27 including staff purchases, before the staff exclusion used for ATV). Web reconciles on 13,004 receipts and EUR 771,530.75.

I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, because they leave web sales out from 3 November 2025 (channel_code is no longer filled). I did not use channel_code at all, and the period starts after the migration anyway.
Cancelled web orders (519 placed in the range) and orders still processing (none placed in the range) are not in the figure, since they have no sales lines.
No duplicate sales lines or receipt keys were found in the range, and no sale_date disagreed with the Helsinki date of sale_ts_utc.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, w.order_member_key, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_member_key IS NOT NULL THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_amount), 1) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Guest web orders count as non-member
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only; cancelled and processing excluded)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26 P9 = 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, P10 = 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026, P11 = 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026)
Control total checked: web sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 in all three periods
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the last completed fiscal year, as in past requests made in FY2026/27. The request arrived on 9 October 2026, in FY2026/27. Periods 9 to 11 are therefore FY2025/26 P9 to P11.

'Share of web sales' read as the company member-share definition applied to web, which is before returns. It is not the net-of-returns web sales figure. A share computed after returns would differ slightly.
'Loyalty members' means web orders placed while logged in with a member key. Guest checkouts count as non-members.
One row per period, as the request says 'by period'. No total across P9 to P11 was given.
Percentages are rounded to one decimal place.
caveats: Data fault corrected: 655 logged-in web orders (order times 8 Feb to 1 Mar 2026 UTC) have member_key null on their sales lines, though fact_web_order carries the member key for every logged-in order. Using the line member_key would treat them as non-member sales and understate the share. I took the member key from fact_web_order instead (it never conflicts with the line key where both exist).

Size of that correction: P10 is 67.5% rather than 51.8% and P11 is 66.7% rather than 55.8%. P9 is unaffected at 68.0%. Anyone computing this from the line-level member_key in the sales table will get the lower, wrong figures for P10 and P11.
The sales-line member_key should be fixed at source for 8 Feb to 1 Mar 2026. Other member-share or member-based web reports for that window are probably understated too.
Four euros of ZZ Test web sales in P11 were excluded as test articles.
Figures are before returns. Web returns are small (about 9 to 10% of web sales) but they would lower both the member and the total figure if netted.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, s.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT l.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net, on the sale-week cohort: refunds follow the original sales line (sales_line_id) whenever they were booked
Sold lines selected by the fiscal period of sale_date
Net amounts excluding VAT
Store 999 (training store) excluded
Category ZZ Test (test articles) excluded
Web shop is store 900, format Web, identified by store_id rather than channel_code
Format taken from dim_store through the fact's store_key (format is identical in every store version)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 period 2 = fiscal weeks 5-8, 26 May 2025 to 22 June 2025, no week 53
Staff purchases included, as in the net sales definition
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (the most recent completed fiscal year at 5 Oct 2026, current year being FY2026/27), following the accepted readings of 'last year' in requests from May 2026 onwards. 'Period 2' is therefore 26 May to 22 June 2025.

'Store format' read as the dim_store format values. These are Large, Medium, Small and Web (the web shop, store 900, has its own format), so Web is shown as its own row, as in the accepted by-format request for sales. If only physical stores are wanted, drop the Web row. The Large, Medium and Small figures are unaffected.

'Goods sold in period 2' read as lines sold in that period, with the return rate counted on the sale cohort. Returns are attributed to the period the goods were sold in, not the period they came back in.
Web lines are dated by sale_date (the order date), as the accepted web-vs-stores return rate request did. All web lines in the period are delivered or collected orders; none are cancelled.
caveats: Training store 999 (126 lines, EUR 2,222 net) and one test-article web line (EUR 3.82) were excluded. None of them had returns, and the effect on the rates is negligible.
The cohort is complete. The last sale was 22 June 2025, the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, and the latest matching return is 23 July 2025, within the 30-day return window.
Checks run on the data found no problems: no duplicate sales or return lines, no returns without a matching sale, no refund larger than the line sold, and no line with more than one return row.
The web rate (12.23%) is about three times the store rates (4.28 to 4.53%), so a blended company figure would be dominated by the web shop mix. No total row is given because none was requested.
No control-total comparison with rpt_daily_store_sales was made. That table is net sales after returns by return date, so it does not apply to a sale-cohort return rate.

answer.sql: WITH web_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2), web_refunds AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(r.refund_net) AS refunds_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_period, w.sales_net - COALESCE(r.refunds_net, 0) AS net_sales FROM web_sales w LEFT JOIN web_refunds r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period) ORDER BY w.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales = line value excluding VAT after line discounts, less refunds excluding VAT (same construction as rpt_daily_store_sales: net_sales_before_returns minus returns_net)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date / ref_fiscal_calendar (4-4-5 periods; FY2025/26 runs 2025-04-28 to 2026-05-03)
Web shop = lines booked to the web shop pseudo-store (store_id 900), which covers home delivery and click-and-collect
Sales assigned to a period by sale_date; refunds assigned to a period by return_date (refunds booked on the day)
Staff purchases kept in (none exist on web lines)
Training store (store_id 999) excluded
assumptions: 'Last year' means the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26, because the request date (6 Oct 2026) falls in FY2026/27 P06; periods 5 to 8 are 2025-08-25 to 2025-12-21
'Sold, net' means net sales: excluding VAT and after returns, in EUR
The web shop includes both web channels, home delivery and click and collect
Refunds on web-sold lines count against the web shop even when the customer returned the item in a physical store; the refund is matched to the original sales line
Cancelled web orders have no sales lines, so they add nothing
sale_date is taken as the local business date and used as is
caveats: Correction: the channel coding changed on 2025-11-03 (web-platform migration). Before then web lines carry channel_code 'WB' and a null channel_id; from then on channel_code is null and channel_id is 2 (home delivery) or 3 (click and collect). Filtering on either field alone drops part of the period. I identified web lines through the web shop store (store_id 900) instead, which is consistent across the whole window and matches WB / channel_id 2,3 line for line (27,829 lines, no gaps).

Correction: refunds for web purchases returned in physical stores are booked to those stores (about 4,000 to 5,700 EUR net a month across periods 5 to 8, 18,586 / 22,385 / 17,045 / 22,366 EUR net per period in total). I deducted them from web sales. Taking only refunds booked at the web shop would give net sales of 144,. 034 / 176,574 / 154,366 / 231,263 EUR, about 3% to 4% higher. If Finance books store-side refunds to the stores, the web figure should be read on that basis.
Net sales before returns, for reference: 158,124.35 / 194,176.17 / 166,510.02 / 249,084.84 EUR for periods 5 to 8. Returns reduce the figure by about 11% in each period.
Period 6 has 5 weeks and periods 5, 7 and 8 have 4, so the periods are not directly comparable without adjusting for length.
Period 8 (24 Nov to 21 Dec) includes the pre-Christmas peak, which accounts for its higher figure.

Checks run: no duplicate sales lines (all 27,829 lines unique), gross equals net times (1 + VAT) on every line, no non-positive quantities or amounts, and every line ties to a web order that was delivered or collected.

answer.sql: WITH period AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date, period_end_date FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period = 2), sales AS (SELECT s.store_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN period p ON f.sale_date BETWEEN p.period_start_date AND p.period_end_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1), refunds AS (SELECT s.store_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN period p ON r.return_date BETWEEN p.period_start_date AND p.period_end_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1), cur AS (SELECT store_id, store_name FROM dim_store WHERE is_current) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, rank() OVER (ORDER BY sales_net - coalesce(refund_net, 0) DESC) AS net_sales_rank, sales.store_id, cur.store_name, round(sales_net - coalesce(refund_net, 0), 2) AS net_sales_eur FROM sales JOIN cur USING (store_id) LEFT JOIN refunds USING (store_id) ORDER BY net_sales_rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 2 = 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-28 (4 weeks, fiscal weeks 5 to 8), taken from ref_fiscal_calendar
Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns booked in the period, matching the rpt_daily_store_sales definition
Returns are deducted in the period and store where the refund is booked (return_date and the return's store), not against the original sale
Store identity by store_id, joined through the dated store_key on each fact row (slowly changing dimension), with the current store name
Stores only: pseudo-locations 900 (web shop) and 999 (training store) are excluded
Ranking: 1 = highest net sales
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (request dated 2026-10-07), so 'period 2' is fiscal period 2 (June 2026), not calendar February
'Store ranking' read as ranking stores by net sales for the period, with returns deducted and VAT excluded

Staff purchases are kept in net sales: no definition in the warehouse excludes them, and the existing daily store sales report includes them. Excluding them (EUR 0 to 955 per store) would only swap a few adjacent ranks (Vantaa Tammisto and Oulu Kaakkuri at 4 and 5, Joensuu and Vaasa/Lappeenranta at 14 to 16)
Web sales and web returns are online, not store sales, so they are not attributed to any store (including click-and-collect pickup stores)
Savonlinna (129) is left out because it closed on 2026-01-25 and has no sales in the period; showing it would be a padding row
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 2026-06-15 (closure runs to 2026-07-26), so it traded only 14 of the 26 trading days in the period. It ranks 24th on actual net sales, but would rank 7th on net sales per trading day (about EUR 1,714 per day). Read its rank as a closure effect, not weak trading

Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (2026-06-19 and 2026-06-20) are non-trading days, so physical stores show 26 trading days in the period; the only sales on those two days are web orders, which are excluded here
Web lines on those days carry a NULL channel_code, so channel_code cannot be used to identify web sales. I identified stores through store_key and store_id instead

Store region changed on 2025-04-28 (for example South to Capital Region, Kouvola East to South), and dim_store uses format names (Medium, Large, Small) and a 'Capital Region' that do not match the column comments. Neither affects this ranking, because it is by store, but a regional roll-up of this period needs the version of the store valid on the sale date

Checks that passed, so no correction was needed: no duplicate receipt lines or return lines, no overlap with the staging load tables, fact figures match rpt_daily_store_sales and the sum of fact_return_line refunds for every store, no dimension keys outside their validity dates, VAT arithmetic consistent, the period is fully loaded (fully_loaded not flagged false for P02) and the last load ran on 2026-06-29

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-11-03' AS start_date, DATE '2026-10-04' AS end_date), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC LIMIT 10

answer.sql: WITH campaign AS (SELECT campaign_id, campaign_name, start_date, end_date + 7 AS window_end FROM dim_campaign WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), holdout AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id CROSS JOIN campaign WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) BETWEEN campaign.start_date AND campaign.window_end GROUP BY 1), t AS (SELECT AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales,0)) AS mean_t FROM targeted x LEFT JOIN member_sales ms USING (member_id)), h AS (SELECT AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales,0)) AS mean_h FROM holdout x LEFT JOIN member_sales ms USING (member_id)) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, ROUND(t.mean_t,2) AS avg_spend_targeted_eur, ROUND(h.mean_h,2) AS avg_spend_holdout_eur, ROUND(t.mean_t - h.mean_h,2) AS uplift_eur FROM t, h

Checks passed: no member is in both groups, no holdout member was contacted, and every targeted and holdout member had marketing consent on 24 Nov 2025. The two groups look alike on tier mix and tenure.

Spend is before returns. Web orders placed in the window but dispatched after 7 Dec 2025 are not counted, and orders placed earlier but dispatched inside the window are.

364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - Part of the 6.7% is this extra trading day. Per trading day the growth would be roughly 2.9%, an indicative figure from simple arithmetic that was not run through the warehouse.

Checks run: the two years' P1 physical-store net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (0 mismatched store-days of 1,053 and 1,064). There were no duplicate sales lines, and no deprecated tables or views were used. The store-by-store spread is wide, from -17.6% (Porvoo) to +25.8% (Lohja), and the total masks that.
The channel_code and web-dispatch logic is not relevant because web is outside LFL.

answer.sql: WITH web_order_periods AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, o.fulfilment_type, SUM(o.order_total_gross) as total_value FROM fact_web_order o INNER JOIN dim_date d ON DATE(o.order_ts_utc) = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (6, 7, 8) AND o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, o.fulfilment_type), period_totals AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, SUM(total_value) as period_total_value, SUM(CASE WHEN fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN total_value ELSE 0 END) as cac_value FROM web_order_periods GROUP BY fiscal_year, fiscal_period) SELECT fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * cac_value / period_total_value, 2) as click_and_collect_share_pct FROM period_totals ORDER BY fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web shop sales: orders with completed status (delivered or collected), excluding cancelled orders
Click-and-collect share: click_and_collect order value as percentage of total web order value
Fiscal periods: from ref_fiscal_calendar table, periods 6-8 of FY2025/26
assumptions: Interpreted 'last year' as FY2025/26, the previous fiscal year relative to current date 2026-10-15
Sales measured by order_total_gross value from fact_web_order
Excluded cancelled orders as they do not represent completed sales
Order timestamp converted from UTC to calendar date for joining with dim_date fiscal periods
caveats: Cancelled orders (476 total across the three periods with value EUR 34,697.92) were excluded from the calculation as they do not represent completed web shop sales
The share percentages are calculated from order values (EUR gross including VAT), not from order counts or units
Click-and-collect orders include both 'collected' and 'processing' status orders; 'processing' orders are counted as part of click-and-collect volume

answer.sql: SELECT dp.category, ROUND(SUM(fsl.net_amount) - COALESCE(SUM(frl.refund_net), 0), 2) as net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * ((SUM(fsl.net_amount) - COALESCE(SUM(frl.refund_net), 0)) - (SUM(fsl.standard_cost) - COALESCE(SUM(frl.standard_cost_returned), 0))) / (SUM(fsl.net_amount) - COALESCE(SUM(frl.refund_net), 0)), 2) as gross_margin_pct FROM fact_sales_line fsl INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date LEFT JOIN fact_return_line frl ON fsl.sales_line_id = frl.sales_line_id WHERE dp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') AND dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND dd.fiscal_period = 6 GROUP BY dp.category ORDER BY dp.category
definitions_applied: Net sales: gross sales (net_amount) less refunds (refund_net)
Gross margin: (net sales - cost of goods sold) / net sales × 100
Cost of goods sold: standard_cost less standard_cost_returned for returned items
Fiscal period: fiscal_period = 6 of fiscal_year FY2024/25
Category: product_name matched to current product dimension (is_current = TRUE)
assumptions: Period 6 last year interpreted as FY2024/25 P06 (2024-09-23 to 2024-10-27)
Gross margin calculated on net_amount (EUR excluding VAT) as revenue base
Returns linked to sales via sales_line_id with return dates in the same period
Standard cost used as COGS basis; cost revaluation (each April) already applied in the warehouse
caveats: No data quality issues detected: all net_amount and standard_cost values are present and non-negative
Return records (382 for Electrical, 298 for Garden) successfully matched to sales lines
Period spans 35 calendar days with sales activity across both categories on all selling days

answer.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date, period_end_date FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_period = 8 AND fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25','FY2025/26')), prod AS (SELECT product_key, CASE WHEN subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE category END AS category FROM dim_product), sales AS (SELECT per.fiscal_year, per.fiscal_period, prod.category, f.net_amount AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN per ON f.sale_date BETWEEN per.period_start_date AND per.period_end_date JOIN prod ON prod.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND prod.category IN ('Garden','Electrical')), rets AS (SELECT per.fiscal_year, per.fiscal_period, prod.category, -r.refund_net AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN per ON r.return_date BETWEEN per.period_start_date AND per.period_end_date JOIN prod ON prod.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND prod.category IN ('Garden','Electrical')), agg AS (SELECT category, round(sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN amt END), 2) AS ns_prior, round(sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN amt END), 2) AS ns_last FROM (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rets) GROUP BY category) SELECT category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ns_prior AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ns_last AS net_sales_fy2025_26, round(100.0 * (ns_last - ns_prior) / ns_prior, 1) AS growth_pct FROM agg ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 8 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2025/26 P08 = 2025-11-24 to 2025-12-21; FY2024/25 P08 = 2024-11-25 to 2024-12-22; both 4 weeks, 28 days)

Net sales = line net_amount (EUR, excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns, with returns counted on the return date and in the category of the returned product (same logic as rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales)
Stores and web shop both included (web is store_id 900; web sales identified through the store key because channel_code is NULL in FY2025/26 and only channel_id is populated)
Training store (store_id 999) and the ZZ Test articles excluded as non-trading test data
Staff purchases kept in net sales, matching the daily store sales report, which includes them
Store and product joins made on the surrogate keys in the fact tables (the version valid at the sale date)
assumptions: 'Last year' means FY2025/26 and 'the year before' means FY2024/25, because the request is dated 2026-10-05, which falls in FY2026/27
'Period 8' means fiscal period 8, not calendar month 8
'Garden and Electrical' is read as two categories reported side by side, each with its own growth, not as one combined figure
Growth is FY2025/26 P08 against FY2024/25 P08, in percent

Outdoor Lighting is placed in Electrical for both years, which is where the product hierarchy has it since 2025-10-27. The five delisted Outdoor Lighting articles that still carry the Garden label are treated the same way
The 5 staff-purchase and 3 training-store sales are small, and the staff-purchase treatment is the only judgement call on definition
Net sales are in EUR excluding VAT, with no currency symbols
caveats: Correction: Outdoor Lighting (73 SKUs) moved from Garden to Electrical from 2025-10-27, and the sales lines carry the category the product had on the sale date. Left as booked, FY2024/25 P08 has 20,168.86 of Outdoor Lighting in Garden while FY2025/26 P08 has 20,320.36 of it in Electrical. That would show Garden down about 35% and Electrical up about 19.6%, and both figures would be wrong. I restated FY2024/25 on the current hierarchy so both years use the same category definition. After restating, Garden is +1.0% and Electrical is +4.9%. Outdoor Lighting alone is roughly flat year on year (20,168.86 to 20,320.36, +0.7%)

Correction: sales lines from FY2025/26 have a NULL channel_code, with only channel_id filled in, so any filter on channel_code = 'ST' or 'WB' would drop the whole of the latest year. I did not filter on channel_code

Correction: the training store (999) and ZZ Test articles carry small amounts of test data in the two periods (about 145 and 12 EUR in FY2024/25; about 340 EUR in FY2025/26 for these two categories). I excluded them
The warehouse holds a duplicated set of 418 receipt lines (same receipt and line number, different line id) in mid-September 2025. They fall outside both periods, so they do not affect this answer
Web sales are a large share of both categories, so the figures are total company sales and not stores only

Not like-for-like: the store base changed between the two periods (Tampere Lamminpää and Lohja opened in September and November 2024, and Savonlinna closes on 2026-01-25), so the growth is for the whole business and is not a same-store figure
Fiscal 2025/26 is a 53-week year, but period 8 has the same four weeks in both years, so the comparison is not affected
If staff purchases were left out, the figures would change by a little over 1,300 EUR in FY2024/25 and about 2,400 EUR in FY2025/26 across the two categories, with no change to the picture

The rpt_daily_store_sales table does not match the sales facts on 28 of 1,081 store-days in FY2025/26 P08 (about 6,000 EUR in total), so I built the answer from the fact tables rather than from the report

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27','FY2025/26') AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS this_year_net_sales, ly.net_sales AS last_year_net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Prior-year comparison lined up by fiscal week number (week 5 against week 5, and so on)
Fiscal calendar: period 2 is fiscal weeks 5 to 8, Monday to Sunday, whole weeks
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales: gap 0.00 over the period
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' is FY2026/27 P2 (1 to 28 June 2026), the latest completed period 2, compared with FY2025/26 P2 (26 May to 22 June 2025)
'Sales' means net sales excluding VAT, the company default, including web and the total company scope
Growth is the percentage change in net sales against the same fiscal week last year
No like-for-like adjustment was applied, since the request asks for total company sales
caveats: No correction to the data was needed: no duplicate sales or return lines were found, and the weekly totals match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (period total 1,294,647.64).

Weeks 7 and 8 are not like for like because Midsummer falls in a different fiscal week each year. This year Midsummer Eve and Day (19 to 20 June 2026) fall in week 7, and the stores were shut. Last year they (20 to 21 June 2025) fell in week 8. So week 7 growth (-32.2%) and week 8 growth (+76.4%) mostly reflect that shift of two shut days, not underlying trading.
Week 8 this year is also boosted by web orders dispatched after the Midsummer break (web net sales were about 34,500 on Monday 22 June, against about 11,000 to 16,000 on a normal Monday).

Kuopio (store 125) is closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, so weeks 7 and 8 this year are missing one store's sales. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026, so it traded last year but not this year. Stores trading were 39 in weeks 5 and 6 and 38 in weeks 7 and 8 this year, against 40 last year.

Over the whole of period 2 the combined figure is 1,294,647.64 against 1,195,882.70 last year, which is +8.3%. This is the fairer single comparison, because the Midsummer shift cancels out across the four weeks.
Last year is read as FY2025/26 (the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27). The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so period 2 is complete.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 5 (fiscal weeks 18 to 21, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), taken from dim_date and the fiscal-calendar skill
Units sold: sum of quantity on fact_sales_line, dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date), as in the weeks-of-cover definition
Store scope: store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), joined through the store_key version on each line
Products counted by stable sku, with the current product version's name (is_current)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither changed the result)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 102
assumptions: 'Period 5 this year' means FY2026/27 P05. The request arrived 7 Oct 2026, and P05 is the latest completed period of the current fiscal year, in a warehouse loaded through 4 Oct 2026.
'Products' means individual articles (sku), not subcategories or brands.

'Units sold' means units on sales lines in the period, before returns. This is the company's own use of 'units sold'. Net of returns the ranking is unchanged: only 1 unit of the third-ranked article came back, and none of the first two.

'Helsinki Pitäjänmäki' is store_id 102, the only store of that name. Its dim_store row has two versions (South until 27 Apr 2025, Capital Region since 28 Apr 2025). The region change has no effect on this request.
Only the store's own sales are counted. Web orders are not included, even if they were collected at this store.
caveats: No data problems were found, so no corrections were made. Store 102's daily units and net sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales on every one of the 28 days. There are no duplicate sales lines, no test-article or store 999 lines, and no negative quantities.
The margin over fourth place is clear: the third article sold 42 units and the fourth 30. The first three (52, 44 and 42 units) are not tied.
The top 3 are each a single article version, so no product-version splitting arose.
The ranking was run on the Helsinki sale_date and the full 28 days of P05 are loaded.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders_placed FROM fact_web_order WHERE DATE(order_ts_utc) = '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web order: transaction recorded in fact_web_order table
Order placed: timestamp in order_ts_utc column falls on the calendar date
Cyber Monday 2025: December 1, 2025 (confirmed as Monday)
assumptions: The request counts all orders by placement time (order_ts_utc), regardless of final status
Timestamps are interpreted in UTC per the warehouse schema
All records in fact_web_order represent valid placed orders
caveats: No data quality issues detected for this date; 291 orders distributed across all three final statuses (delivered 193, collected 81, cancelled 17)

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, cp.subcategory, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1 AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory <> 'Outdoor Lighting'), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_quarter, l.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY l.subcategory ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net (net_amount), excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: lines selected by the fiscal period of the original sale date, with refunds matched through sales_line_id whenever and wherever they were booked (web and store lines both included)
Fiscal calendar: Q1 = P1 to P3 = fiscal weeks 1 to 13 (28 Apr 2025 to 27 Jul 2025)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
As-is product hierarchy: current product version (dim_product.is_current) for category and subcategory
Staff purchases included (as in net sales)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just ended (the request was received on 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27), as in earlier accepted requests such as REQ-D14 and REQ-D16
'Q1' read as fiscal Q1 of FY2025/26, which is P1 to P3
'Goods sold' includes both store and web sales (store 900), with web refunds following the line
Category and subcategory are as-is (current hierarchy), because the request did not ask for as-was
One row per Garden subcategory, with no total row, as the request asked for a breakdown by subcategory
caveats: Correction, Outdoor Lighting: the outdoor lighting subcategory moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025. Five articles (SKUs 100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) were delisted before the move and never got a new product version, so dim_product still shows them in Garden / Outdoor Lighting. I treated outdoor lighting as Electrical in full, as the company's as-is rule says, and left these five out of Garden. They had 19 lines and EUR 375.00 net sold in Q1 and no returns, so including them would add an Outdoor Lighting row at 0.00% and would barely move any other figure. The 65 articles that did move (1,445 lines, EUR 50,442.94 sold, 7.22% returned) are also in Electrical, not Garden.

As-was would differ: on the hierarchy of the time, Outdoor Lighting was still part of Garden in Q1 FY2025/26 and would appear as a Garden subcategory with a 7.22% return rate for the moved articles. Pekka should say if he wants that view.
The Q1 cohort is complete. The last sale was 27 Jul 2025 and the data is loaded through 4 Oct 2026. The last return booked against these sales is 22 Aug 2025, inside the 30-day return window.
Store 999 (training store) lines were excluded. No ZZ Test articles appear in Garden.

Checks run: no duplicate sales line ids and no duplicate current product versions. No returns without a matching sale. No refund above the sold value or returned quantity above the quantity sold. No cancelled web orders among the Garden lines. The rpt_daily_store_sales control total does not apply to a category-level return rate, so it was not used.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-05-04' AS start_date, DATE '2026-08-02' AS end_date), store_lines AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key CROSS JOIN params WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date), web_lines AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id CROSS JOIN params WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN params.start_date - 60 AND params.end_date AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date), all_lines AS (SELECT receipt_id, net_amount FROM store_lines UNION ALL SELECT receipt_id, net_amount FROM web_lines) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_quarter, ROUND(SUM(net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM all_lines
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (excluding VAT) divided by the number of sales receipts
Staff purchases excluded from ATV
Store 999 (training store) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Web shop (store 900) counted as web orders, as the request asked
Web orders recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (web sales convention)
Store receipts dated by Helsinki sale_date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 periods 1 to 3 (Q1), whole weeks, 4 May to 2 August 2026
Cancelled orders have no sales lines and are not counted
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'periods 1 to 3' means fiscal periods P1 to P3 (Q1), 4 May to 2 August 2026, all fully loaded

The metric dictionary defines ATV as a store measure with web orders excluded. The request explicitly asks for web orders, so they are included and the figure differs from the standard store-only ATV.

Web orders are dated by dispatch date, so revenue and order count fall in the same period. Dating by order date gives 12,959 orders and 771,025.31 EUR instead of 13,004 and 771,530.75 EUR, a difference of about 0.1 cent on the ATV.
Web staff purchases do not occur (no web line carries the staff flag), so the staff exclusion only affects stores
A single company-wide figure was given as the request did not ask for a breakdown by period, store or channel
caveats: Correction: web orders are included in ATV, which departs from the company definition (store measure, web not included). Without web, the store-only ATV for the same periods is 55.52 EUR; web alone is 59.33 EUR.
Correction: staff purchases excluded from stores (2,650 staff lines in the range), store 999 excluded (training store), and ZZ Test articles excluded, including 3 test lines on web orders
Correction: web is dated by Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date stored in sale_date; processing and cancelled orders are not counted and none fall in the range as sales

Checks passed: no duplicate sales lines or receipts in the range; store receipts (68,021) and net sales before returns (3,767,921.27 EUR) reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales store by store and day by day, including staff purchases; web receipts (13,004) and net sales (771,530.75 EUR) reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900. The ATV figure itself excludes staff purchases so it is not compared to the control directly.
The result is based on 79,988 receipts and 4,490,717.08 EUR net sales before returns excluding VAT
Returns are not deducted, per the ATV definition
rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used, as they omit web sales since 3 November 2025

answer.sql: WITH web AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, f.net_amount, (o.member_key IS NOT NULL) AS is_member FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND o.status IN ('delivered','collected') AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11) SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_member THEN net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(net_amount), 1) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM web GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (dispatch_ts_utc converted to Europe/Helsinki), not the order date in sale_date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines); only delivered and collected orders counted
Guest web orders counted as non-member
Click-and-collect counted as web, dated on ready-for-collection time
Net sales excluding VAT, before returns
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; store 999 is not in the data used
Fiscal periods taken from dim_date (fiscal_year and fiscal_period), not calendar months
Control total: web net sales before returns compared with rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, channel_code, stg_, bak_, tmp_ tables) not used
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just ended. The request came on 9 October 2026 (FY2026/27), and past requests asked in May 2026 or later took FY2025/26 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).
'Periods 9 to 11' read as FY2025/26 P09 to P11: 22 December 2025 to 22 March 2026. All three periods are fully loaded, and week 53 sits in P12, so it does not affect these periods.
'Loyalty member' means a web order placed while logged in to a member account. Members are identified from fact_web_order.member_key, not from the member_key on the sales lines (see caveats).
'Web sales' covers all web orders including click-and-collect, in line with company practice.
Period shares are reported one decimal place; no total across the three periods was requested, so none is given.
caveats: Data defect corrected: for logged-in web orders dispatched between 10 February and 4 March 2026 (655 orders, 1,309 lines, loaded 10 Feb to 2 Mar 2026), member_key is null on the sales lines although fact_web_order carries the member. Using the line member_key as-is would understate the member share. As-is it would give P10 51.8% and P11 55.8%, against 67.5% and 66.7% corrected. P09 is unaffected at 68.0%. The correction uses the member_key on fact_web_order, which has no gaps for logged-in orders. The warehouse team may want to fix the load of fact_sales_line.member_key.
Filter effect: one test-article line (ZZ Test, EUR 4.00 net) in P11 web sales was excluded. The effect on the share is negligible.

Control total: web net sales before returns (store 900) matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for all three periods: P09 219,929.50; P10 137,569.07; P11 149,798.62 EUR. The reference table is for the total only, so it cannot confirm the member split.
Shares are on net sales before returns and exclude VAT; returns are not netted off.
The member flag is a yes/no on the order, so member-share figures do not depend on which version of the member record applied.
Share fell slightly across the three periods (68.0 to 66.7 percent) once corrected, which is a small drift, not a break.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, cs.region) SELECT ty.region, ty.fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: Like-for-like growth: net sales of LFL stores for the same fiscal weeks, compared week by week with the prior year
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT after line discounts, less returns booked on their own return date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 never LFL
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
LFL base: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the range
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open, not closed, outside ref_store_closure refit weeks)
Week 53 never LFL (not in Q3 anyway)
Regions as-is (current dim_store version, five regions including Capital Region)
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = P7 to P9 = fiscal weeks 27 to 39, Monday to Sunday, compared by fiscal week number
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' read as FY2025/26 Q3 (27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, weeks 27 to 39), since the request was made on 5 Oct 2026 in FY2026/27; past requests in FY2026/27 read 'last year' as FY2025/26. The comparator is FY2024/25 weeks 27 to 39 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025).
Regions as-is on the current hierarchy (Capital Region applied to its stores in both years), since as-was was not requested.

The fiscal year is named FY2025/26; if 'last year' meant the calendar year 2025 or the latest completed quarter (FY2026/27 Q1), the answer would differ.
Web sales are excluded (not part of LFL). The rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales views were not used because they drop web sales after 3 November 2025.

Control check: net sales by store for Q3 in both years agree with rpt_daily_store_sales with no differences over 1 EUR, and no duplicate sales or return line ids were found, so no data corrections were needed.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_product AS (SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) AS gross_margin, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) / SUM(n.net_sales), 1) AS gross_margin_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = n.store_id AND s.is_current JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 40 AND 52 AND s.region = 'South' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name) SELECT sku, product_name, net_sales, gross_margin, gross_margin_pct FROM by_product ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 10;
definitions_applied: DEF-GROSS-MARGIN: net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, after returns (returned units credited at standard_cost_returned)
DEF-NET-SALES: net amount excluding VAT after line discounts and returns; web sales recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time
DEF-NET-SALES-SCOPE: excludes store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test (test articles)

Q4 of FY2024/25 interpreted as fiscal weeks 40-52 (2025-01-27 to 2025-04-27) based on fiscal calendar. This period predates the April 2025 region reorganisation.

Store 137 (Lohja) opened 4 November 2024 and has sales only from that date within Q4 FY24/25.
Web sales (store 900, region Online) are excluded from the South region filter as intended; web is reported separately as its own channel.

definitions_applied: League table: stores ranked by net sales performance

Physical stores only: excluded web and pseudo-locations (store_id < 900)

definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (net_amount, excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts

Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Receipts dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 4 = fiscal weeks 14 to 17, Monday 3 August to Sunday 30 August 2026
Store format taken from the store version on the sale date (format is identical across all versions of a store)
assumptions: Read 'average basket value' as the company's ATV (average transaction value), as the request says
Period 4 of FY26/27 read as FY2026/27 P04, which is complete in the warehouse (loaded through 4 October 2026)
Formats are the values in dim_store: Large, Medium and Small. The web shop's format is Web and the training store's is Training; both are left out
Averages are per receipt (sum per receipt first, then average across receipts), shown to 2 decimals, in EUR excluding VAT
caveats: Figures are excluding VAT, since ATV is defined on net sales
Staff-purchase receipts are excluded per the ATV definition, so these averages are lower than a figure that includes them
The dim_store column comment says formats are Hyper, Standard or Express, but the data holds Large, Medium and Small. I used the data values
In stores, channel_code is not filled after the 3 November 2025 web-platform migration, so I identified store sales by store_id below 900 and not by channel_code

No data defects found in the period. The sales lines have no duplicate keys, no store 999 or ZZ Test lines appear in physical stores, and before the staff exclusion my receipt and net sales totals matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly over all 1,064 store-days (18,027 receipts, EUR 1,062,266.72)

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar: 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, four weeks (fiscal weeks 18 to 21), fully loaded

Store identified by store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), so both store versions (store_key 3 and 4, before and after the 28 April 2025 region change) would count; only version 4 has sales in this period
Products grouped by sku (stable article number) rather than product_key, so product versions do not split a product's units
Units sold means the sum of quantity on fact_sales_line, by sale_date
Store sales only: this store has no web lines, and web orders are not attributed to a store
assumptions: 'This year' is read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (the request is dated 2026-10-07), so 'period 5' is FY2026/27 P05, not calendar-year May and not the previous fiscal year's P05
'Top products' is read at SKU level (article), not subcategory or brand

Units sold is gross of returns. Returned units are not deducted, because 'units sold' is a sales measure; the top-3 returns in the period were 0, 0 and 1 units, so netting would not change the ranking

Staff purchases are included, because the request does not exclude them. This matters only for the third place: SKU 102244 has 2 of its 42 units flagged as staff purchases. Excluding staff purchases gives 40 units, and the top 3 and their order stay the same
A product's name is the name on its current dim_product row. Each SKU has a single version in the period
caveats: No data problem needed correcting. Checks run: no duplicate sales_line_id or (receipt_id, line_no) among the 2,121 lines for the store in the period; sales on all 28 days with every day a trading day; no refit closure recorded for store 102; the 3,740 units total matches rpt_daily_store_sales for the same store and dates; all lines carry one store version (store_key 4)
The staging table stg_sales_line_load holds only 3 to 4 October 2026 lines, outside this period and already in the fact table, so it has no effect
The store's region changed from South to Capital Region on 2025-04-28. This does not affect a single-store answer but would matter for region roll-ups across that date

The margin between 3rd place (42 units) and 4th (SKU 102233, 30 units) is 12 units, so the top 3 is not close. The gap between 2nd (44) and 3rd (42) is only 2 units, so their order is sensitive to treatment of staff purchases and returns in principle. In practice staff purchases (-2) leave it at 44 vs 40 and a 1-unit return leaves it at 44 vs 41, so the order holds either way
Period 6 of FY2026/27 is not fully loaded in the warehouse, but period 5 is, so the answer is final

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, w.week_ending_date, w.closing_units AS units_in_stock FROM fact_stock_week w JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = w.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = w.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND w.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-10-04'
definitions_applied: Closing stock is the end-of-fiscal-week snapshot in fact_stock_week (week-ending Sunday)
Fiscal weeks run Monday to Sunday
Stock by store covers physical stores (store_id below 900); store 124 qualifies
Test articles (ZZ Test) excluded; SKU 100011 is in Garden, so it is not affected
Natural keys store_id and sku used, with the store and product version keys joined on the fact row; each has a single version, so no row multiplication
Grain check: one row per store_key, product_key and week_ending_date (81,429 rows, 81,429 distinct keys in the weeks from 20 Sep 2026 on)
assumptions: 'Last week' is read relative to the request date of Thursday 8 October 2026 as the last completed fiscal week, FY2026/27 week 22 (Monday 28 September to Sunday 4 October 2026), so the snapshot is the one for Sunday 4 October 2026. The warehouse is loaded exactly through that date.
'Jyväskylä Palokka' is store 124 (store_key 30, the only version). 'SKU 100011' is Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570 (product_key 11, the only version).
The request asks for units, so I report closing_units. Stock value at standard cost was EUR 46.64 and is not part of the answer.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, cs.format FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), ret AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, s.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold s LEFT JOIN ret r ON r.sales_line_id = s.sales_line_id GROUP BY s.format ORDER BY CASE s.format WHEN 'Large' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Small' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END
definitions_applied: Return rate: returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net, sale-week cohort
Sold lines selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date, refunds matched through sales_line_id wherever and whenever they were booked
Net amounts excluding VAT
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Format taken from the current dim_store version, which is as-is and identical to the version on the sale date for every store
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own format, Web
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (FY2025/26 P2 = 26 May to 22 June 2025)
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or any deprecated, staging, backup or tmp table
assumptions: 'Period 2 last year' is read as FY2025/26 P2 (26 May to 22 June 2025), because the request was received on 6 October 2026 in FY2026/27 and past requests in that situation took 'last year' to mean FY2025/26
'What share of what was sold came back' is read as the value-based return rate (returned net EUR divided by sold net EUR), the company definition, not a share of units
'Store format' includes the web shop as its own row (Web), as in past format requests, because its sales are in the warehouse under format Web
Web lines are dated by sale_date (the order date) for the sold cohort, following the accepted return-rate queries for web against stores
The Training format (store 999) is left out as a test location
caveats: Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test removed 127 sold lines (about EUR 2,226 net, all of it in store 999 apart from 1 web test line of EUR 3.82), none of which had returns. The filter shifts the stores' totals by less than 0.1% and the web total by EUR 3.82
Return rate is by sale-week cohort and includes returns booked up to 23 July 2025, so the cohort is complete (returns arrive within 30 days of the sale)
Web returns are booked to the web shop but follow the original line here, so they count against the Web format, as intended

Control total: sold net by store format matches rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns exactly for Large (400,763.11), Medium (552,936.25) and Small (147,668.20). Web does not tie (183,098.49 here against 168,049.19 in the report) because the report dates web sales on the dispatch date while this return-rate cohort dates them on the order date, per the accepted convention
The web return rate (12.23%) is about three times the store rate (4.28% to 4.53%). Large, Medium and Small stores are close to each other
20 and 21 June 2025 (Midsummer Eve and Day) had only web sales because the stores were shut
No duplicate sales lines, duplicate return lines, orphan returns, or returns above sold quantity or value were found in the cohort

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members_joined
FROM dim_member

definitions_applied: Members counted as distinct member_id values from dim_member
Join date from dim_member.join_date column
assumptions: Counted distinct loyalty members (by member_id) who joined on the specified date
