answer.sql: WITH sl AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY sales_line_id) = 1), nl AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sl f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), sw AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id=st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date<=d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date>=d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 22) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM sw ty JOIN sw ly ON ly.store_id=ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week=ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id=ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-05-04' - 364)), agg AS (SELECT cs.region, d.fiscal_year, sum(n.net_sales) lfl_sales FROM nl n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id=n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl l ON l.store_id=n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week=d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_week<=22 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27','FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY ty.lfl_sales/ly.lfl_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, round(ty.lfl_sales,2) AS lfl_net_sales_this_year, round(ly.lfl_sales,2) AS lfl_net_sales_last_year, round(100*(ty.lfl_sales/ly.lfl_sales-1),2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM agg ty JOIN agg ly ON ly.region=ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: physical stores only, store-weeks that traded in both years, refit and closure weeks removed for the store concerned in both years (ref_store_closure and close_date), 52-week (364-day) opening rule
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce sales on their own return date

Fiscal calendar: weeks run Monday to Sunday and this year is FY2026/27; YTD runs from week 1 (4 May 2026) to the last completed fiscal week (week 22, ending 4 October 2026), compared with weeks 1 to 22 of FY2025/26
Regions as-is: the current dim_store version, so the Capital Region covers stores 101 to 105 in both years and Kouvola (114) is in South in both years
Stores only (store_id below 900): the web shop is excluded, so no Online row
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded from sales and returns
Control total: store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for weeks 1 to 22 of both years, store by store
Deprecated objects not used: rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, rpt_weekly_sales_by_region, stg_, bak_, tmp_ and _old tables
assumptions: The request does not name a measure. I read 'how they are doing this year so far' as performance against last year, so I ranked the regions by YTD like-for-like growth in net sales. That is the company's like-for-like growth measure, and it is not distorted by refits and closures.

'This year so far' is read as FY2026/27 year to date, weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026). Week 22 ended on 4 October, so it is complete, and the warehouse is loaded through that date. Period 6 is only partly loaded, but whole weeks are used, so that does not matter here.
The comparison is with FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22, lined up by fiscal week and not by calendar date. Week 53 of FY2025/26 is outside the range.
Regions are as-is, meaning the current hierarchy applied to all history. As-was regions would change the Capital Region, South and East comparisons for last year.

LFL base: all 39 physical stores that traded in the range were old enough, because every store opened more than 364 days before 4 May 2026, including Lohja (137) and Tampere Lamminpää (136). Open and close dates come from the current store version.
The ranking is by growth, not by size. Absolute net sales in the table are the like-for-like store-weeks only, not the regions' full totals.
caveats: Data correction: fact_sales_line holds duplicate loads for store 116 (Tampere Lielahti, West) on 15 to 21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 weeks 21 to 22). 836 lines were reloaded on 23 September 2025 with new sales_line_ids. They are identical on receipt_id, line_no, store, product, quantity and amount, and they double-count 20,781.06 EUR of net sales in last year's comparison base. I kept the first load of each receipt_id and line_no pair and dropped the reload. After this correction every store matches rpt_daily_store_sales for weeks 1 to 22 of both years, within 0.50 EUR. Without it, West's last-year base would be overstated and its growth understated.

Excluded from the LFL base: Kuopio (125, refit 15 June to 26 July 2026, weeks 7 to 12 dropped in both years), Pori (119, refit from 8 September 2025, weeks 20 to 22 dropped in both years), and Savonlinna (129, closed 25 January 2026, so no like-for-like weeks this year). The two refit stores stay in for their other weeks. The refit and closure exclusions mainly affect East (Kuopio and Savonlinna) and West (Pori).

Ranking depends on the measure. On unadjusted YTD net sales growth the order would be North 3.8%, West 3.24%, Capital Region 2.71%, South 2.11%, East -11.61%. That order is misleading because the Savonlinna closure and the Kuopio refit remove East's sales, and West's growth includes Pori's refit. On absolute YTD net sales the order is West 1.82M, South 1.31M, East 0.96M, Capital Region 0.95M, North 0.73M. If Finance wants a size ranking, say so and I will resend.

East is the only region with a decline (-0.19%, essentially flat). The gap between East's like-for-like growth and its unadjusted growth of -11.61% comes almost entirely from the Savonlinna closure and the Kuopio refit.

Kemi (133, North) has no sales rows on Monday 31 August 2026, a trading day. The sales table, the control table and the staging table all show nothing. The other 38 stores traded that day and Kemi's average day is about 430 EUR, so the effect on North is about 0.1%. I could not verify whether the store was shut or the data is missing, and I made no correction.
Regions rank closely at the bottom: West (1.93%) and South (2.11%) are 0.18 points apart.
No store 999 or ZZ Test lines sit in the 39 stores' figures. The training store's 45,322.82 EUR of net sales since April 2025 is excluded, and it does not change any regional total.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), lines AS (SELECT CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN w.dispatch_date ELSE f.sale_date END AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT region, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024_gross_incl_vat, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024_gross_incl_vat FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales = sum of gross_amount on sales lines (each line carries its own VAT rate), before returns
As-was regions: region taken from the dim_store version on the fact line's store_key
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (fact_web_order joined on receipt_id = web_order_id), delivered and collected orders only; web shown as its own Online region (store 900)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Calendar months used, as the request names months for a VAT filing, not fiscal periods
Did not use channel_code, rpt.v_daily_sales or any deprecated, staging, backup or tmp table
Control total: net sales before returns for the same lines and days (stores and web store 900) agree with rpt_daily_store_sales for every store
assumptions: August and September 2024 read as calendar months (1 to 31 August and 1 to 30 September 2024), not fiscal periods
Regions as they were means as-was: the four regions of the time (South, West, East, North) plus Online. Capital Region did not exist until 28 April 2025, so it has no row

Web gross sales are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date rather than the order date, per the company definition of web sales. Orders placed in July and dispatched in August are in; orders placed in late September and dispatched in October are out
Returns excluded as the request asks for gross sales before returns, so no refund column is shown
Online is kept as its own row since web sales have no physical region
caveats: Store 999 (training store, 283 lines) and ZZ Test articles (68 lines) were excluded from the Aug to Sep 2024 lines; this lowers the totals relative to an unfiltered sum

Gross amounts use the VAT rate in force on each line: 24% for standard goods in August 2024 and 25.5% from 1 September 2024. Reduced classes (14% and 10%) are unchanged. I checked that gross_amount equals net_amount times (1 + vat_rate) on every line in the range and that vat_rate matches each article's vat_class, with no mismatches
I found no duplicate sales lines (sales_line_id and receipt_id + line_no both unique) and no unmatched web lines, so no data corrections were needed
Stores 101 to 105 report under South and 114 Kouvola under East, as they were in 2024. As-is reporting would move them to Capital Region and South respectively and give different regional figures
Cancelled and not-yet-dispatched web orders have no sales lines and so are not in the figures
The VAT filing basis may differ: if VAT is due on the order or payment date rather than the dispatch date, the Online row would change. This figure follows the company sales definition

answer.sql: WITH stock AS (SELECT p.category, sum(f.closing_units) AS stock_units FROM fact_stock_week f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-09-27' AND s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT p.category, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag GROUP BY 1), returned AS (SELECT p.category, sum(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag GROUP BY 1) SELECT st.category, round(st.stock_units / ((sd.units_sold - coalesce(rt.units_returned, 0)) / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM stock st JOIN sold sd USING (category) LEFT JOIN returned rt USING (category) ORDER BY st.category
definitions_applied: Last period = last fully loaded fiscal period: FY2026/27 P05 (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, 4 weeks); P06 is in progress and not fully loaded
Weeks of cover = closing units in stock at the end of the period divided by average weekly units sold
Stock counted at the week ending 2026-09-27 (last Sunday of P05) from fact_stock_week
Real stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
Staff purchases excluded from the sales rate (staff_purchase_flag)
Units sold net of units returned in stores (returns tied to staff-purchase lines also excluded)
Category taken from the product version valid at the sale or stock date (dim_product via product_key)
Average weekly sales = the 4 weeks of P05 divided by 4
assumptions: Read 'last period' as FY2026/27 P05, since the request is dated 2026-10-07 and P06 (from 2026-09-28) is still running
Measured cover in units, not value, so category price levels do not distort it
Used the most recent 4 weeks of sales as the sales rate, so cover reflects the current seasonal run rate (autumn ramp in Seasonal and Electrical, Garden easing) rather than a longer average
Stock exists only for physical stores, so the sales rate is store sales only; web sales excluded because the web shop holds no stock in the warehouse
Returned units are counted as back in sellable stock, so they reduce the net sales rate
Rows are categories as in dim_product; the 'ZZ Test' category is excluded as it has no stock and sales only in the training store
caveats: Web shop sales are not in the sales rate, so cover is overstated if web orders are picked from store stock; the warehouse does not say where web orders are fulfilled from

Cover is very sensitive to the chosen sales window for seasonal categories: Seasonal (43.5 weeks) and Garden (19.4) rest on a 4-week rate that is moving fast (Seasonal units rose from about 250 to about 620 a week; Garden fell from about 6,000 to about 2,500 over 3 months)
Netting returns changes the result most for Furniture (about 29 weeks gross vs 33 net); returns of defective or damaged goods may not be resellable, so net may overstate sales slightly
The existing view rpt.v_daily_sales filters on channel_code = 'WB', which is null for recent lines, so it misses web sales; I did not use it

Outdoor Lighting SKUs moved from Garden to Electrical on 2025-10-27; the product version valid on each date was used, so P05 figures all sit in Electrical, but any comparison with earlier periods needs the same treatment
Savonlinna (store 129, closed 2026-01-25) holds no stock and was not part of the result
No stock rows were found for delisted products or for the test category at 2026-09-27, so no adjustment was needed
Staff purchases are about 1.5% of store units; including them would lower cover by about 1.5% in each category

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date, w.order_member_key, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_member_key IS NOT NULL THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_amount), 1) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.dispatch_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (UTC converted to Europe/Helsinki)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders have dispatched sales lines)
Guest web orders count as non-member
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26 P9 to P11), whole periods only
Net sales excluding VAT
Staff purchases included
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just ended (the request was received 2026-10-09, in FY2026/27), following the accepted past readings for requests made in FY2026/27
'Periods 9 to 11' read as fiscal periods P09 (22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026), P10 (26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026) and P11 (23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026), one row per period
'Share of web sales' read as the company's member share of sales definition applied to web: before returns, so returns are not deducted from numerator or denominator
Member status taken from fact_web_order (logged-in orders carry a member_key)
Result is a share in percent, rounded to one decimal
caveats: Correction: on 655 logged-in web orders (lines dated 9 Feb to 1 Mar 2026, falling in P10 and P11) fact_sales_line.member_key is null even though fact_web_order has the member_key and login_state is logged_in. Using the line member_key would understate the member share: P10 would be 51.8% instead of 67.5%, and P11 55.8% instead of 66.7%. I took member status from fact_web_order.member_key instead. P9 is unaffected (68.0% either way). Worth reporting to the data engineers.
One test line (ZZ Test, 4.00 EUR net, P11) was excluded; it does not change the rounded figures.

Shares are before returns, in line with the member share definition. Web net sales after returns would give a slightly different base. My web net sales after returns reconcile exactly to rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 in each period (P9 200,208.58; P10 123,131.15; P11 135,257.73).

The legacy views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, which drop web sales from 3 Nov 2025, were not used. channel_code was not used because it is not filled across the 3 Nov 2025 migration.
Orders placed in the period but dispatched later (or still processing) fall in the period of their dispatch date, as the web sales definition requires.

answer.sql: WITH web_orders AS (SELECT web_order_id, fulfilment_type, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_net AS (SELECT o.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_orders o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN web_orders o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN w.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN w.net_sales END) / SUM(w.net_sales), 1) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_net w JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counted as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (converted from dispatch_ts_utc), not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is empty from 3 Nov 2025)
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date: FY2025/26 P9 is 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026 (5 weeks), P10 is 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026 (4 weeks)
Control total: web net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 over the same periods
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_ and old tables) not used
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request is dated 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests made in May 2026 in FY2026/27 took last year as FY2025/26. It is the last complete fiscal year.
'Periods 9 and 10' read as fiscal periods P9 and P10 of FY2025/26, reported as one row per period. The request did not ask for a combined figure. For reference, P9 and P10 combined come to 29.8%.
'Web sales' read as company net sales (after returns, ex VAT) on the dispatch date, not gross or order-date figures.
Returns are assigned to click-and-collect or home delivery through the original sales line's web order, and dated on the return date.
caveats: Web sales do not use channel_code or the order date (sale_date). channel_code is unreliable after the 3 Nov 2025 platform migration, and sale_date on web lines is the order date. I used store 900, the dispatch date in Helsinki time, and fulfilment_type from fact_web_order instead.

Web net sales include only returns booked to the web shop (store 900), which matches the company definition and rpt_daily_store_sales. Some web-line returns were processed in physical stores (P9: 35 click-and-collect and 113 home-delivery return lines, about 5.8k EUR net; P10: 31 and 101 lines, about 5.0k EUR net). They are booked to those stores' net sales, not to web, so they are excluded here. Including them would lower the share slightly.

Control total agrees: web net sales after returns are 200,208.58 EUR for P9 and 123,131.15 EUR for P10, equal to rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900. The pre-return figures also agree: 219,929.50 and 137,569.07 EUR.

Before returns the shares are 28.95% (P9) and 30.62% (P10). After returns they are 29.24% (P9) and 30.75% (P10, shown as 30.7 after rounding). The returns-inclusive net sales definition was used, as it is the company default.
The filter that excludes ZZ Test removes test items from web sales (one test web sales line seen in the wider date window). Its effect on these two periods was not isolated.
No duplicates were found in fact_sales_line or fact_return_line for these periods, and all web lines matched a delivered or collected order. No corrections to the data were needed.

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), sales AS (SELECT store_id, SUM(net_sales) net_sales FROM net_lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-28' GROUP BY 1), days AS (SELECT st.store_id, COUNT(*) trading_days FROM dim_store st JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-28' AND d.is_trading_day WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900 AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.calendar_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id=st.store_id AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.net_sales / d.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ROUND(s.net_sales,2) AS net_sales, d.trading_days, ROUND(s.net_sales/d.trading_days,2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM sales s JOIN days d USING (store_id) JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id=s.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Trading days: days open, after opening and before closure, outside ref_store_closure refit closures, and not a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (900) not listed
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P2 = weeks 5 to 8, 1 June to 28 June 2026
Store-level net sales checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days
Current store names (dim_store is_current); no deprecated tables, no channel_code
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2 (1 to 28 June 2026), the current fiscal year as of the request date 9 October 2026; P2 is a complete period and is fully loaded
Ties on the ranking key use RANK(); none occurred
Stores with no trading in the period (Savonlinna, closed 25 January 2026) are not listed
Net sales and trading days are shown beside the ranking measure so the ranking can be checked; the table is ordered by net sales per trading day, descending
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it is ranked on its 14 trading days (1 to 14 June) rather than 26; its net sales per trading day is therefore on a shorter base and its raw net sales (23,993.71) is not comparable to the full-period stores
Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed holidays, so the other 37 stores have 26 trading days, not 28
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles are excluded; the store-level figures agree with rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent for every store, so the filters did not change any listed total
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and is not in the table; the web shop (900) is not a store and is not ranked

The ranking is by net sales per trading day, so smaller stores can rank above larger ones on raw sales only where trading days differ (Kuopio at 7 sits above Turku Kupittaa at 8 although its period net sales are lower)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (fact_web_order dispatch_ts_utc converted from UTC to Helsinki time), not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is not filled from the 3 Nov 2025 platform migration)
Cancelled and processing orders are not web sales (only delivered and collected orders with a dispatch date count)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods taken from dim_date (fiscal_year, fiscal_period)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year that has just finished (the request was received 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27). Accepted past requests made in FY2026/27 read 'last year' as FY2025/26.

Periods 5 to 8 are FY2025/26 P5 (25 Aug-21 Sep 2025), P6 (22 Sep-26 Oct 2025), P7 (27 Oct-23 Nov 2025) and P8 (24 Nov-21 Dec 2025). All four are fully loaded. Week 53 of FY2025/26 falls in P12, so it does not affect these periods.
'Web shop' read as the whole web channel (store 900), including click-and-collect orders.
Shown as one row per period, as the request says 'in each of periods 5 to 8', with no total.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: Returns are counted only where they are booked to the web shop (store 900), as in the company's web net sales template. In the same four periods, 501 return lines on web-sold items, worth 19,725.39 EUR net in total, were booked to physical stores (returned in-store). They reduce those stores' net sales, not web net sales. If you want web sales net of every return on web orders, wherever it was processed, the four periods would be lower by their share of that amount.
Corrections applied: one test-article line (category ZZ Test, 5.50 EUR net) on a web order in the range was excluded.

No problem found in the web data: no duplicate sales lines on store 900, and no sales lines on cancelled or processing orders. I found 418 duplicate receipt-line pairs (re-loaded on 23 Sep 2025), but all are in store 116 in the week of 15-21 Sep 2025. They do not touch web sales, but would affect any store-level figure for that week.
The figures match the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for store 900 exactly in all four periods.
The legacy views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales were not used. They omit web sales from 3 Nov 2025, which falls in P7.

answer.sql: SELECT strftime(f.sale_date, '%B %Y') AS month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY date_trunc('month', f.sale_date), 1 ORDER BY date_trunc('month', f.sale_date)
definitions_applied: Sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines (each line carries its own VAT rate)
Before returns: fact_return_line not used, no refunds deducted
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Store lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns
assumptions: 'Store sales' read as physical-store sales only, so web sales (store 900) are left out
'August 2024' and 'September 2024' read as calendar months (1-31 August, 1-30 September), not fiscal periods, because the request names calendar months
Sales are shown as originally recorded, including VAT at the rate in force when sold
Store set is as sold on each date (the sales lines' store_key), with no regional grouping needed for a company-wide figure
caveats: The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. August lines carry 24% and September lines 25.5% (reduced rates of 14% and 10% unchanged), so the month-on-month change in VAT-inclusive sales is partly a tax effect. Net sales before returns excluding VAT, for reference, were 1,101,807.91 for August and 964,016.09 for September.

No data correction was needed. Line gross_amount agreed with net_amount x (1 + vat_rate) on every line; there were no duplicate sales lines and no test-article lines in physical stores; net sales before returns on the same filter matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly in both months (difference 0.00).

Store 999 (training store) lines were excluded, but they carried no physical-store sales, so this did not change the totals. Web sales (store 900) are excluded: web gross for the two months would be additional (about 178.7k in August and 163.7k in September combined with a small amount of store 999, figures not used here).
Figures are before returns as requested; refunds are not deducted and would reduce the figures if wanted.

answer.sql:
SELECT 
  p.subcategory,
  SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold
FROM fact_sales_line f
INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
WHERE s.store_id = 118
  AND f.sale_date BETWEEN '2026-08-31' AND '2026-09-27'
  AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
GROUP BY p.subcategory
ORDER BY units_sold DESC
LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Top N by units sold: summed quantity across all transactions in the period
Period 5 FY2026/27: fiscal period ending 2026-09-27
Store filter: store_id = 118 (Nokia), westregion, all transactions by channel
Exclusion: category ZZ Test (training data)
assumptions: Period 5 this year: FY2026/27 P05 (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27), the most recent completed period at request date 2026-10-09
Nokia: store_id 118 (the unique store with exact name match)
Units sold: quantity from fact_sales_line, all channels (store and web)
caveats: Period FY2026/27 P05 is fully loaded as of warehouse load date 2026-10-04
Query spans both fiscal weeks 19 and 20, aligned to the full fiscal period
Result excludes training-store (999) and test-category (ZZ Test) transactions

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending
),
closing AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units
    FROM fact_stock_week fs
    JOIN dim_store s    ON s.store_key = fs.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p  ON p.product_key = fs.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending
      AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    GROUP BY cp.category
),
sold AS (
    SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s    ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p  ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7
      AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    GROUP BY cp.category
)
SELECT c.category,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(s.units_sold_4w, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) END AS weeks_of_cover
FROM closing c
LEFT JOIN sold s ON s.category = c.category
ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Weeks of cover: closing stock units at the end of the fiscal week divided by average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks
Physical stores only (store_id < 900)
Test articles excluded (category ZZ Test)
Last period: FY2026/27 P05, week ending 2026-09-27
Prior four fiscal weeks: fiscal weeks 17-20 (2026-08-24 to 2026-09-20)
assumptions: Interpreted 'weeks of cover by category' as aggregated across all physical stores, not broken down by store
Interpreted 'at the end of last period' as the week-ending Sunday of the final fiscal week in the period (2026-09-27)
caveats: No data issues found. Query validated: unique grain by category, all filters correctly applied, no deprecated objects.

answer.sql: SELECT cs.store_id, cs.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, fs.week_ending_date AS week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 124 AND p.sku = 100011 AND fs.week_ending_date = DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY ALL
definitions_applied: Closing stock is the weekly snapshot in fact_stock_week, counted on the week-ending Sunday
Last week means the last completed fiscal week (Monday 28 September to Sunday 4 October 2026, FY2026/27 week 22)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Versioned dimensions joined on store_key and product_key, current store name via is_current
Control checks on the stock table: one row per store, article and week
assumptions: Request received Thursday 8 October 2026, so last week is the completed fiscal week ending Sunday 4 October 2026. This is also the last week loaded in the warehouse.
Closing stock for that week is the snapshot at the end of Sunday 4 October, not an average over the week.
SKU 100011 is Plants & Flowers Kuusela 570 (Garden). Store 124 is Jyväskylä Palokka (East region, open and current).
The answer is in units, as asked. Stock value is not given.
caveats: No data problems found for this store, article and week. The stock table has exactly one row per store and article in each of the last three weeks (27,143 rows, no duplicates). Both dimensions have a single version.

The count is unchanged from the previous Sunday (11 units). That is consistent with the sales lines: 2 units sold in the week ending 27 September and none in the week ending 4 October, with no receipts or adjustments.
Stock is only held for articles the store ranges, and web stock is not included, which does not affect this store-level figure.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, cs.format FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, l.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY l.format ORDER BY l.format
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net (net_amount), excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: goods are selected by the fiscal period of the sale date, and refunds are matched to the original line through sales_line_id, whenever and wherever they were booked
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900, format Web) counted as its own format, with web refunds following the line
Format taken from the current store version (format is the same in every store version)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 period 2 is 26 May to 22 June 2025, fiscal weeks 5 to 8
assumptions: 'Last year' asked on 5 October 2026 (FY2026/27) is read as FY2025/26, the same reading past requests used, so 'period 2 last year' is FY2025/26 P2
Web is shown as a fourth row because it is a store format in the warehouse (Web), as in past requests that split by format
Percentages are rounded to two decimals
Web lines are dated by sale_date (the order date), as for the return-rate cohort. All web orders in the period are delivered or collected, so no cancelled or processing orders affect the figures
caveats: Store 999 (126 lines, 2,222.21 EUR net) and category ZZ Test (1 web line) were excluded. This changes no format's figure materially, but it is a correction to the raw data
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale; the latest return on this cohort is dated 23 July 2025 and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026, so the cohort is complete
No duplicate sales or return lines were found, no refund exceeds the sold value, and every return links to a sales line
The warehouse comments list the formats as Hyper, Standard or Express, but the data holds Large, Medium, Small and Web (plus Training for store 999). The labels shown are the actual values
The web return rate (12.23%) is much higher than the store formats (4.28% to 4.53%), so it should not be compared directly with them without allowing for the different channel
The control total in rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to a return-rate cohort measure, so it was not used
Query-check passed with no failures

answer.sql: WITH web_sales AS (SELECT sale_date AS business_date, sum(net_amount) AS net_sales_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line WHERE channel_id IN (2, 3) AND sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1), web_returns AS (SELECT r.return_date AS business_date, sum(r.refund_net) AS returns_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id WHERE f.channel_id IN (2, 3) AND r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' GROUP BY 1) SELECT d.calendar_date AS business_date, s.net_sales_before_returns - coalesce(r.returns_net, 0) AS net_sales FROM dim_date d LEFT JOIN web_sales s ON s.business_date = d.calendar_date LEFT JOIN web_returns r ON r.business_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-15' AND DATE '2025-12-23' ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns
Web channel = channel_id 2 (web home delivery) and 3 (click and collect), i.e. dim_channel.channel_group = 'web'
Sales dated by sale_date (Finnish local business date)
Returns dated by return_date (refunds booked on the day they are made), as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Cancelled web orders excluded (they have no sales lines)
assumptions: 'Net' is read as net sales in the company sense: excluding VAT and after returns. Without returns the daily figures (EUR excl. VAT) are 13007.30, 16359.14, 10686.17, 11354.33, 11627.57, 7425.77, 7762.68, 12878.11 and 13459.24 for 15 to 23 December.
Click-and-collect orders count as web sales, because dim_channel puts them in the web group.
Returns of web-order lines are counted against web wherever they were handed in, including those taken at physical stores.

15 to 23 December 2025 is read as inclusive on both ends, in Finnish local dates; sale_date already follows local time, since UTC timestamps from 22:00 UTC the evening before fall on the next local date.
Staff purchases are not flagged on any web line in this period, so no staff exclusion was needed.
caveats: Web sales lines have a NULL channel_code. The documented 'WB' code does not appear on any row from the web-platform migration onward, and only channel_id identifies web. Filtering on channel_code = 'WB' returns no rows, and the view rpt.v_daily_sales (which filters on 'WB') therefore shows no web sales for these dates, so it was not used.

The Data & Analytics report table rpt_daily_store_sales (store 900) does not match the warehouse facts for web. For example, 15 December net_sales_before_returns shows 11714.52 against 13007.30 in the facts, and 21 December shows 1445.65 against 7762.68. Its returns count only refunds booked at the web shop (store 900) and miss web-order refunds made in physical stores. I computed everything from fact_sales_line and fact_return_line instead.

Web-order refunds taken in physical stores (store ids 101 to 137) are subtracted from web sales. Counting only refunds booked at the web shop (store 900) would give higher figures. These in-store refunds total about 100 to 450 EUR a day in the period.
Net sales for a day can include refunds for items sold on earlier days, as the company report does, so a day's net figure is not strictly that day's orders less their own returns.
All web orders in the period are delivered, collected or cancelled. None are still processing, and the cancelled ones have no sales lines, so there is nothing to correct for open or cancelled orders.
Order totals and sales lines tie out for every non-cancelled order. I found no duplicate lines, no negative amounts and no VAT mismatches in the period.

answer.sql:
SELECT s.region,
  sum(CASE WHEN f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN f.gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024_gross_sales,
  sum(CASE WHEN f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN f.gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024_gross_sales
FROM fact_sales_line f
JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30'
  AND s.store_id <> 999
GROUP BY s.region
ORDER BY CASE s.region WHEN 'North' THEN 1 WHEN 'South' THEN 2 WHEN 'East' THEN 3 WHEN 'West' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END
definitions_applied: Gross sales = fact_sales_line.gross_amount (EUR including VAT), before returns (fact_return_line not used)

Region as at the time of sale: fact_sales_line.store_key points to the store version valid on the sale date, so dim_store.region is the historical region (the April 2025 regrouping of the five Helsinki-area stores into Capital Region and of Kouvola from East to South is not applied)
Calendar months by sale_date (August 1-31, September 1-30, 2024), not fiscal periods
Staff purchases included, since they are real sales liable to VAT
Web lines (channel WB) included under the web shop pseudo-location, region Online
assumptions: 'August and September 2024' means calendar months, because this is for a VAT filing; fiscal periods P05 and P06 of FY2024/25 run on different dates (26 Aug to 22 Sep and 23 Sep to 27 Oct)
'Regions as in the old reports' means the pre-April-2025 North/South/East/West structure, with Helsinki-area stores and Kouvola in their 2024 regions

Web sales are shown as a separate 'Online' row, because they are VAT-liable sales and belong in a VAT filing; the old regional report (rpt_weekly_sales_by_region) covers the four store regions only, so Finance can drop that row to match it
sale_date is the Helsinki local date and is used as is; it matches the local date of sale_ts_utc on every line checked
caveats: Correction: the Training store (store_id 999, region 'Head office') has 283 sales lines over the two months worth 7,633.94 EUR gross (284.97 in non-staff lines and 7,348.97 in staff-flagged lines). I excluded it as non-trading test activity, so the figures above leave it out. If Finance wants it included it would be a separate row.

Do not compute the month split from sale_ts_utc: 428 lines in the period (checked over 30 July to 2 October) fall on a different UTC date than the local sale_date, which would move sales across the month boundary.
VAT rates are as expected: standard rate 24% in August and 25.5% from 1 September 2024; reduced rates 14% and 10% unchanged. Gross amounts are consistent with net times (1 + VAT rate) on all lines.

No duplicate lines found: receipt_id and line_no are unique, and no lines in the period appear in stg_sales_line_load. All web order lines belong to delivered or collected orders; none are cancelled or still processing.
The figures are gross of VAT at the line level and do not net off returns, as requested. Returns were not queried, so the VAT liability after returns is not shown here.
Staff purchases are included: 1,446 lines (about 33.4k EUR gross, excluding the Training store) across the store regions. Remove them if Finance treats them differently.
Regions are historical: the same stores would be in a different region grouping (Capital Region for five Helsinki-area stores, Kouvola in South) if the current dim_store regions were used.

answer.sql: WITH campaign AS (SELECT campaign_id, campaign_name, start_date, end_date + 7 AS window_end FROM dim_campaign WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), holdout AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), members AS (SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS member_group FROM targeted UNION ALL SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM holdout), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id CROSS JOIN campaign WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) BETWEEN campaign.start_date AND campaign.window_end GROUP BY 1), by_group AS (SELECT mb.member_group, AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales, 0)) AS mean_net_sales FROM members mb LEFT JOIN member_sales ms ON ms.member_id = mb.member_id GROUP BY 1) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_targeted_member, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_holdout_member, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END) - MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS uplift_eur FROM by_group
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift = mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member
Measurement window = campaign window plus seven days (24 Nov to 7 Dec 2025)
Targeted member = at least one exposure row in the campaign, reduced to distinct member_id
Holdout = campaign_holdout (member_id based)
Members with no sales count as zero
Net sales before returns, excluding VAT, on lines linked to the member
Web sales dated on Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded; staff purchases included
Member versions collapsed to member_id
assumptions: The Black Week 2025 campaign is campaign_id 15 (24 to 30 Nov 2025, email+sms+push, all members with marketing consent); Black Week 2024 (id 5) is a different campaign.
Spend is read as net sales before returns excluding VAT, as the company uplift definition says.
Returns made later are not deducted from either group.
The seven-day extension after the campaign end applies to both groups.
Uplift is the difference of the unrounded means (1.4055), shown as 1.41; the difference of the two rounded means would be 1.40.
caveats: No data corrections were needed. I checked the following and found nothing to correct: no duplicate sales lines or exposure ids, no overlap between the targeted and holdout groups, no holdout member contacted, no contacted member without marketing consent, and no orphan member keys.
Exposure has one row per contact (50,043 rows, 23,844 member versions) and was reduced to 23,818 distinct members, so contacts were not counted as members.

dim_campaign says the mailing list was 26,573 members including the 2,747 held out, which implies 23,826 targeted. The warehouse has exposure rows for 23,818 members, so 8 listed members have no exposure row and are not in the targeted group.

Only about 14% of targeted members (3,279 of 23,818) and 12% of holdout members (323 of 2,747) bought in the window. The uplift is a small difference between two low means and comes from a small number of buyers. Treat it as an average per member, not a per-buyer effect.
The uplift is gross of any margin or discount cost of the campaign.
The holdout is about 10% of the list, so the holdout mean is the noisier of the two. No significance test was run.
rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it omits web sales from 3 Nov 2025. channel_code was not used because it stops being filled from the November 2025 migration.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS new_members FROM dim_member WHERE join_date = DATE '2026-09-25'
definitions_applied: New member = a distinct loyalty number (member_id) whose join_date is the given day
dim_member is slowly changing, so members are counted on member_id and not on member_key or row count
join_date is a calendar date, so no UTC conversion was needed
assumptions: 'Signed up on 25 September 2026' means join_date = 2026-09-25
Online sign-ups (home_store_id 900) count as new members, together with in-store sign-ups. Of the 39, 7 are online sign-ups.
Marketing consent and tier were not used to filter the count, because the request does not ask for it
'New members' means members who joined that day. It does not mean members who made a first purchase that day.
caveats: I found no data problem that needed a correction. Each of the 39 members has exactly one row in dim_member, and each row's valid_from equals the join date. No member_id has more than one join_date.
stg_member_updates also holds the same 39 members for that day. They match dim_member on both key and id, so they were not counted twice.
dim_member has join dates up to 2026-10-04 and daily counts look steady (about 25 to 49 a day), so 25 September does not look partially loaded.
The count cannot detect the same person signing up twice under two different loyalty numbers.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND p.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY ALL
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 = 29 Jun 2026 to 2 Aug 2026 (5 weeks), from ref_fiscal_calendar and dim_date
Interior Paint = dim_product.subcategory 'Interior Paint' (category Paint & Decorating)
Lahti store = store_id 108, matched through store_key on the sales line
Units sold = gross units on in-store sales lines (fact_sales_line.quantity), before returns
Sales date = fact_sales_line.sale_date
assumptions: 'FY26/27' is read as the warehouse label FY2026/27
'Period 3' is read as fiscal period 3, not calendar month 3
'Sold in the Lahti store' means sales rung up at the Lahti store (channel Store). Web orders collected at Lahti are not counted.
Units sold are gross of returns, which is how the warehouse reports units_sold
Staff purchases are included. The daily store sales report includes them in its units_sold, so I did the same.
caveats: No data problems found that needed a correction. Period 3 is fully loaded, with sales on all 35 days. There were no duplicate sales lines, no non-positive quantities and no refit closures at Lahti.
Five units of Interior Paint ordered on the web shop and collected at Lahti are booked to the web shop (store 900, click-and-collect) and are not in the 194.
Five units of Interior Paint were returned at Lahti in the same period and are not netted off. Net of returns the figure would be 189.
Four of the 194 units were staff purchases (all on 1 Aug 2026). Excluding them would give 190.
Two Interior Paint SKUs (100963 and 101047) have two product versions. Both are Interior Paint in each version, so the result is unaffected.
channel_code is NULL on the Lahti lines, and the channel_id 1 (Store) column was used to confirm they are store sales.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS web_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period IN (4, 5, 6) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect counted as web
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders have dispatch dates and sales lines)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 excluded
Figures including VAT: sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, using each line's own VAT rate
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25 Q2 = periods 4 to 6
Helsinki time zone conversion of UTC timestamps
assumptions: Q2 of FY24/25 is read as fiscal year FY2024/25, periods 4, 5 and 6 (29 July to 27 October 2024), as the request states
Before returns means no refunds are deducted, so the figure is gross_amount on the sales lines only
Web sales are dated on the dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date) in Helsinki time, following the company definition
Staff purchases are left in, as in company net sales
VAT is taken as recorded on each line (24% standard rate before 1 September 2024, 25.5% from then on, 14% and 10% reduced rates)
caveats: Test-article lines were removed from the web figures: 8.06 EUR in P4 and 3.77 EUR in P5 (none in P6)
Cancelled orders and orders still processing are not in the figures, as they have no dispatch date or sales lines. All orders dispatched in the range are delivered or collected
Orders placed before 1 September 2024 and dispatched after it keep the VAT rate recorded on the line (24%), as the warehouse holds it
As a cross-check, the same selection on net amounts before returns matches rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in all three periods (126,242.65, 122,660.57 and 153,786.32 EUR excluding VAT)
Do not use rpt.v_daily_sales for this: it leaves out web sales from 3 November 2025, though that is after this range

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web = store_id 900 (not channel_code)
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Click-and-collect counted as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date (4-4-5 calendar, FY2025/26)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26. The request is dated 9 October 2026, in FY2026/27. Earlier accepted requests from May 2026 onward read 'last year' this way.
Periods 5 to 8 are FY2025/26 P5 (25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025), P6 (22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025), P7 (27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025) and P8 (24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025). All four are fully loaded.
'Web net sales' follows the company definition: excluding VAT, after returns, as shown for the web shop (store 900).
One row per fiscal period, because the request says 'by period'. No total row.
caveats: Figures are for FY2025/26, not FY2026/27. Say if the current year was meant.
Cancelled and still-processing orders have no sales lines and no dispatch date, so they are not in web sales. Nothing needed correcting.

The P7 and P8 figures cover the 3 November 2025 platform migration, when channel_code stopped being filled. I used store 900, so web sales are complete across it. rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales would understate them from that date, and I did not use them.
Excluded 19 web test-article lines (ZZ Test, total 61.27 EUR net across all periods). Their effect on P5 to P8 is negligible.

Returns are booked where they are processed. About 20k EUR net of refunds on web-order lines in P5 to P8 were processed in physical stores and reduce those stores' net sales, not web. Web net sales therefore only deducts returns booked to the web shop (60.7k EUR over the four periods). Counting store-processed web returns against web would lower these figures.

In store 116 during 15 to 21 September 2025, sales lines were loaded twice: 418 receipt lines, loaded again on 23 September 2025. This does not touch web, so the web figures needed no correction, but the store 116 figures are overstated.
Web net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 to the cent in all four periods.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_key) as customers FROM fact_sales_line WHERE member_key IS NOT NULL AND store_key IN (SELECT store_key FROM dim_store WHERE city = 'Tampere' AND is_current = TRUE AND store_id < 900)

Current store versions (is_current = TRUE)
Unique customers = distinct loyalty members (member_key not null) who made at least one purchase

Included all historical sales data (2024-04-29 to 2026-10-04) with no specific time window requested
Counted unique customer identities (member_key), so customers shopping at multiple Tampere locations are counted once

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key, because dim_member keeps one row per version
Current tier read from the current member version (is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Tier values are Basic, Silver and Gold; Gold is matched exactly
dim_member only, with no staging, backup or old tables
assumptions: 'Members on the Gold tier right now' means every loyalty member whose current version has tier Gold. I did not limit it to active members, because the request says 'members' and the active-member definition (a purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks) was not asked for.

'Right now' means the current state of the warehouse. The request is dated 8 October 2026 and no member version has a valid_from after 4 October 2026, so the current versions are the same as the versions valid on 8 October 2026 (also 5791).
The count includes all Gold members, whether or not they have marketing consent and whichever home store or online sign-up store they have.
caveats: Data is loaded only to 4 October 2026: the latest sale date is 4 October, the latest ETL load is 5 October at 01:00, and the latest member version starts on 4 October. Any tier change made on 5 to 8 October is not in the figure.

Checks on dim_member found no data problem to correct. Every member has exactly one current version, there are no overlapping validity ranges, and is_current agrees with valid_to = 9999-12-31 for every row. Counting version rows instead of distinct members would overstate Gold: 8,203 Gold versions against 5,791 current Gold members, because 2,233 members had a Gold version that has since been replaced.

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 AND cp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P4 (3 Aug to 30 Aug 2026, fully loaded)
Returns dated by return_date (the date the return was booked), not the sale date and not the sale-week cohort
Units = quantity_returned from fact_return_line
As-is product hierarchy (current dim_product version: subcategory Garden Furniture, category Garden)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900) returns included as part of company returns
Helsinki business dates for return_date
No deprecated, staging, backup or tmp tables used
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27; 'period 4' is FY2026/27 P4, 3 to 30 August 2026. P4 is complete and fully loaded.
'Garden Furniture' is the subcategory in the Garden category (dim_product.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture'), not the whole Garden category.
'Handed back and booked as returned' means units on return lines booked with a return date in P4, whenever the original sale happened. This is a count of units, not a refund value.
Returns from all channels are included (stores and the web shop), since the request did not limit the channel. Of the 92 units, 58 were booked in physical stores and 34 to the web shop.
No breakdown was asked for, so the answer is one total.
caveats: No data problems needing correction were found. Checks run on the P4 Garden Furniture return lines: no duplicate return lines or sales lines returned twice, no return larger than the quantity sold, no return dated before its sale, no return line without a matching sales line, and no difference between the stored return_date and the Helsinki date of the UTC timestamp.
As-is and as-was give the same answer here: every P4 return line was already in Garden Furniture, so the outdoor lighting move out of Garden in October 2025 does not affect it.
The filters for store 999 and category ZZ Test did not change the total; no such returns exist in the range.
Each return line is 1 unit, so units equal return lines (92).
A returns control total is not available: rpt_daily_store_sales holds returns_net by store-day but has no product or category split, so the figure could not be reconciled to it.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year,
           31 AS first_week, 34 AS last_week
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    -- sales: stores on the sale date, web on the Helsinki dispatch date
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.category,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    -- returns reduce net sales on the return date
    SELECT r.return_date, p.category, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
by_period AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, n.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    CROSS JOIN params par
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (par.ty_year, par.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN par.first_week AND par.last_week
      AND n.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, n.category
)
SELECT ty.category, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM (SELECT * FROM by_period WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26') ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN (SELECT * FROM by_period WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25') ly ON ly.category = ty.category
ORDER BY ty.category;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognized on Helsinki dispatch date
Returns reduce net sales on return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
As-is reporting: current product category hierarchy
Growth: percentage change from prior-year period
assumptions: Period 8 last year = FY2025/26 P8 (fiscal weeks 31-34, 24 Nov 2025 to 21 Dec 2025)
Period 8 the year before = FY2024/25 P8 (fiscal weeks 31-34, 25 Nov 2024 to 22 Dec 2024)
Year-over-year comparison aligned by fiscal week number
Categories reported as-is (current product version at sale date)
Both physical stores and web (store 900) included
caveats: Growth calculated as (FY2025/26 / FY2024/25 - 1) * 100
Electrical grew 19.8% year-over-year while Garden declined 34.6%
Web sales included on dispatch date per company convention

WITH params AS (

),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, 
           f.product_key, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key

    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, r.product_key, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
period_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cp.category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = n.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week
      AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT ty.category, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25,

FROM period_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN period_sales ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year

definitions_applied: DEF-NET-SALES: net amount excluding VAT, after returns; return reduces net sales on return date, not sale date

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27'
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the date of the original sale
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected orders count, cancelled and processing orders are left out
Whole company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900) in the total
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Last period means the last completed fiscal period (fiscal-calendar skill)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales passed with a gap of 0.00 at store x day level
Deprecated objects not used (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_ tables)
assumptions: Read 'last month' as the last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, 4 weeks), because the company reports on fiscal periods and not calendar months, and the metric dictionary has no definition of 'last month'. Past requests read 'last four weeks' as the last completed period in the same way.
Read 'whole company' as all stores plus the web shop, as the store-scope rule says for the total company.
Figure is in EUR excluding VAT, shown as a single total with no breakdown, since none was asked for.
caveats: If Mika meant calendar September 2026 (1 to 30 Sep), the figure is different: about 1179035.98 EUR from rpt_daily_store_sales (the same control table that matched my P05 figure exactly). It spans 30 days, two days more than the 28-day period, and includes days from fiscal periods P05 and P06. I did not rebuild it from the fact tables.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were excluded as the house rule requires. In P05 they amount to 140 sales lines worth 2696.92 EUR net by sale date, so the exclusion changes the total slightly.
Web orders still in 'processing' status have no dispatch date and so are not in this total; they are recognised once dispatched. Cancelled orders are also left out.
Stores and web are on different day boundaries to the UTC timestamps: dates are Helsinki local dates, not UTC. About 14 sales lines in the period move days if UTC midnight were used instead.

No duplicate sales, return or control-table keys were found in the period. The warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026, so P05 is fully loaded. Returns of P05 sales that arrive later will reduce future periods, not this one.

answer.sql: WITH web AS (SELECT f.sale_date, f.net_amount, o.fulfilment_type FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)) SELECT r.fiscal_year, r.fiscal_period, round(100.0 * sum(CASE WHEN web.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN web.net_amount END) / sum(web.net_amount), 2) AS click_and_collect_share_pct FROM web JOIN ref_fiscal_calendar r ON web.sale_date BETWEEN r.period_start_date AND r.period_end_date WHERE r.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND r.fiscal_period BETWEEN 6 AND 8 GROUP BY r.fiscal_year, r.fiscal_period ORDER BY r.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: periods taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2025/26 P06 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, P07 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025, P08 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025)
Web shop sales = fact_sales_line lines on the web channel (channel_code WB, or channel_id 2 or 3 after the migration)
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' (joined on receipt_id = web_order_id)
Sales value = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts)
Period assignment by sale_date, which is the local (Helsinki) date, not the UTC date
Training store (store 999) lines are not web sales and are excluded
assumptions: 'Last year' means FY2025/26, because the request is dated 2026-10-09 and falls in FY2026/27. Periods 6 to 8 are therefore 22 Sep to 21 Dec 2025.
'Sales' means net sales value excluding VAT (net_amount), before returns. Veikko did not say whether returns should be netted off.

'Share of the web shop's sales' means click-and-collect value divided by total web value (home delivery plus click-and-collect). Cancelled orders have no sales lines, so they are not in either figure.
Shares are rounded to two decimals, in percent.
caveats: Correction: before the web-platform migration (sales lines up to 2 Nov 2025) channel_id is NULL and the web channel is just 'WB', so click-and-collect cannot be told apart in fact_sales_line. Periods 6 and 7 and the start of period 8 fall in that range. From 3 Nov 2025, channel_id 3 is click-and-collect. I classified every web line by joining to fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, which is populated throughout. Filtering on channel_id = 3 would have understated the share for periods 6 and 7 and part of period 8.
The join to fact_web_order matches every web line in the periods checked. There are no duplicate sales lines or orders, and line counts and VAT arithmetic reconcile.

Returns are not netted off. Netting web refunds by return date (refund_net on web lines, any original sale date) gives slightly lower shares of 27.26 (P6), 26.03 (P7) and 26.39 (P8) percent. If net-of-returns is the reporting basis, use those figures.
Web value for the three periods (EUR excluding VAT) is 194176.17 (P6), 166510.02 (P7) and 249084.84 (P8). Click-and-collect value is 53697.28, 44335.88 and 66151.51.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.category, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY units_sold DESC, cp.subcategory LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold = sum of quantity on sales lines, dated by Helsinki sale_date
Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 = fiscal weeks 18 to 21, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (whole period, fully loaded)
Store scope: physical store only (store_id 118 Nokia); web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this store and period: zero test units)
As-is product hierarchy (current dim_product version via sku and is_current)
Staff purchases included (as in net sales)
Control total: line quantity of 2,245 units for Nokia in the period matches rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold exactly
assumptions: 'Nokia' read as the Nokia store, store_id 118 (the only store of that name; region West, format Medium)
'Period 5 this year' read as FY2026/27 P5, the current fiscal year, which ended 27 Sep 2026 and is complete in the warehouse (loaded through 4 Oct 2026)
'Units sold' read as gross units on sales lines, not net of returns
Subcategories ranked on the current (as-is) product hierarchy; no Nokia units were restated by a category change in this period
Ranking by units only; no ties among the top 3
caveats: No data problems found: no duplicate sales lines at Nokia in the period (1,250 lines, 1,250 distinct line ids and receipt/line pairs) and the unit total reconciles to the control table. No corrections were needed.

Units are before returns. Returned units at Nokia in the period (booked on their return date) were 9 for Storage Boxes, 7 for Fixings & Fasteners and 5 for Indoor Lighting. Cleaning Products sold 136 units, only 3 behind Storage Boxes at 139, so if units were counted net of returns, Storage Boxes could fall behind Cleaning Products for third place. Fixings & Fasteners and Indoor Lighting keep first and second place either way.
Fixings & Fasteners sold 570 units, nearly four times the second place, so the ranking is dominated by small-ticket fasteners.
