answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, f.net_amount, COALESCE(f.member_key, w.order_member_key) AS member_key_fixed FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.member_key_fixed IS NOT NULL THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_amount), 1) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Guest web orders count as non-member
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Only delivered and collected orders count (cancelled and processing orders have no sales and are excluded)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar periods from dim_date (FY2025/26 P9 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, P10 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026, P11 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026)
Net amounts exclude VAT
Control total: web net sales before returns agree exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 over 22 Dec 2025 to 22 Mar 2026 (gap 0.00)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year that ended on 3 May 2026, as in past requests made in the same fiscal year
'Periods 9 to 11' read as fiscal periods P09, P10 and P11 of FY2025/26, one row per period
'Web sales' read as web net sales excluding VAT, before returns, which is the basis of the company's member-share definition
'Loyalty members' read as web lines or orders carrying a member key; logged-in orders count as member, guest orders as non-member
Click-and-collect orders are included as web, as in the company definition
caveats: Data defect corrected: for orders dispatched between about 10 February and 4 March 2026 (655 logged-in orders, 1,309 lines, inside P10 and P11), the member_key is missing on the sales lines, although fact_web_order carries the member for those same orders. I took the member from fact_web_order when the line had none. Without this correction the shares would have been 51.8% in P10 and 55.8% in P11, understated by about 15.7 and 10.9 points.
P9 was not affected: every logged-in order in P9 has a member key on its lines.
Returns are not deducted, in line with the member-share definition. A share of web net sales after returns would differ slightly.
The 19 web test lines in category ZZ Test were excluded. Cancelled orders and orders still processing have no sales lines and do not affect the figures.
Percentages are rounded to one decimal place.

definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2026/27 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, whole period loaded)

As-is reporting: subcategory taken from the current product version (sku and is_current)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded

Store identified by stable store_id 118 through the store_key on the line

'Period 5 this year' read as FY2026/27 P05, the current fiscal year and the last complete period (asked 9 October 2026)

Fixings & Fasteners (570) sells almost four times as many units as the second subcategory, because it is a low-priced, multi-unit item with many lines of 4 to 8 units. Ranking by net sales would probably give a different order.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.receipt_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id AND s.store_id = 900 WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-04-01' AND DATE '2026-08-31' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS first_fiscal_period, 3 AS last_fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT receipt_id), 2) AS atv_eur FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-08-02'
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (net_amount, excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) left out of ATV
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test left out
Web shop (store_id 900) identified by store_id, not channel_code or channel_id
Web orders dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (status delivered or collected); cancelled and processing orders have no sales lines and are not counted
Stores dated by sale_date
Fiscal calendar: P1 to P3 of FY2026/27 = Monday 4 May 2026 to Sunday 2 August 2026 (4+4+5 weeks)
Control total: store-level receipts and net sales before returns checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: "This year" is read as the current fiscal year, FY2026/27. "Periods 1 to 3" are fiscal periods, which is the first quarter. All three periods are complete.
"The whole company" is read as all physical stores plus the web shop, giving one figure.

Web orders are dated on the Helsinki dispatch date, which is the company's date for web sales. For click-and-collect this is the date the order was ready for collection. Dating web orders by order date instead would move a few hundred web lines across the period boundaries.
Each web order counts as one receipt, the same way a store receipt does.
caveats: Correction: the company ATV definition covers stores only and leaves web orders out. Mika asked for web orders to be included, so I followed the request and added web orders (store 900) as receipts. For comparison, the stores-only ATV is 55.52 EUR on 66,984 receipts. The web-only ATV is 59.33 EUR on 13,004 orders. This figure is therefore not comparable with ATV figures that exclude web.
Correction: three web test orders with ZZ Test articles, dispatched in the period, were removed. This does not change the figure at the rounding shown.
Staff purchases are excluded, as in the standard ATV. No web lines carry the staff flag.

The stores part reconciles exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales. Across all stores and days in the period, receipts (68,021) and net sales before returns (3,767,921.27 EUR) match to the cent. That comparison included staff receipts, because the control table does not exclude them. It does not cover web.
The result is net sales before returns, excluding VAT: 4,490,717.08 EUR over 79,988 receipts (staff, store 999 and test articles excluded).
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or any stg_, bak_, tmp_ or _old table, and I did not use channel_code.
Kuopio (store 125) is shut for refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026. Its receipts only cover the weeks it traded, so no adjustment was needed for ATV.

answer.sql: WITH campaign AS (SELECT campaign_id, campaign_name, start_date, end_date + 7 AS window_end FROM dim_campaign WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), holdout AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), members AS (SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS grp FROM targeted UNION ALL SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM holdout), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN fact_web_order w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id CROSS JOIN campaign c WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.status IN ('delivered','collected')) AND CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', w.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) ELSE f.sale_date END BETWEEN c.start_date AND c.window_end GROUP BY 1), by_group AS (SELECT mb.grp, AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales, 0)) AS mean_net FROM members mb LEFT JOIN member_sales ms USING (member_id) GROUP BY 1) SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN grp='targeted' THEN mean_net END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_targeted_member, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN grp='holdout' THEN mean_net END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_held_out_member, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN grp='targeted' THEN mean_net END) - MAX(CASE WHEN grp='holdout' THEN mean_net END), 2) AS uplift_eur FROM by_group CROSS JOIN campaign c GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift = mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member
Measurement window = campaign window plus seven days (24 Nov to 7 Dec 2025)
Targeted member = at least one exposure row in the campaign, reduced to distinct member_id via dim_member
Holdout from campaign_holdout joined on member_id, not member_key
Net sales before returns, excluding VAT, on lines linked to the member; members with no sales count as zero
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; web lines identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Cancelled web orders excluded
Members counted by distinct member_id across member versions
assumptions: The request names 'Black Week 2025', which is campaign_id 15 (24 to 30 Nov 2025). Black Week 2024 (campaign_id 5) is a different campaign and was not used.
Spend is net sales before returns, excluding VAT, as the company uplift definition says. Returns are not deducted and VAT is not included.
Spend is measured over the campaign window plus seven days, as the company definition says, not the campaign window alone.
Averages are per member in each group, over everyone in the group including members who bought nothing. Only 3,279 of 23,818 targeted and 323 of 2,747 held-out members bought anything in the window.
Uplift is the difference of the unrounded group means (1.4055), rounded to 1.41 euros per member.
caveats: Corrections made: exposure has one row per contact (50,043 rows for 23,818 distinct members), so it was reduced to one row per member to avoid counting members several times. Web sales were dated on dispatch date rather than order date. Cancelled web orders were excluded. Web lines were identified by store 900 because channel_code is not populated after the November 2025 platform migration.

Group sizes are 23,818 targeted and 2,747 held-out members. The two groups do not overlap. The holdout size matches dim_campaign.holdout_size (2,747). The targeted count is 8 below the mailing list size minus the holdout (26,573 - 2,747 = 23,826), so 8 listed members have no exposure row and are not counted as targeted.

The uplift is small relative to the average spend (about 18 percent of the holdout mean). Only about 12 percent of targeted members and about 12 percent of holdout members made a purchase in the window, so the difference rests on a small number of buyers. No significance test was run, so the figure may not be distinguishable from chance.

About 6,500 members who had marketing consent on 24 Nov 2025 are in neither the targeted group nor the holdout, even though the target group is described as all consenting members. They were left out of the comparison because they are neither contacted nor held out. This is not explained by the data and may be worth checking with CRM.
Tier mix of the two groups is similar (Gold about 9 percent in each), which supports the holdout being a fair comparison group.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS first_period, 8 AS last_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 2) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date), not the order date
Cancelled and still-processing orders are not web sales (only delivered and collected orders are included)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, because neither channel_code nor channel_id works across the 3 November 2025 platform migration
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern, Monday to Sunday weeks)
UTC timestamps converted to Helsinki time before taking the date
Template pattern from accepted request REQ-D22 (click-and-collect share of web sales by period)
assumptions: 'Last year' asked on 9 October 2026 (in FY2026/27) is read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, following how accepted requests from May 2026 read it. Periods 6, 7 and 8 are therefore FY2025/26 P6 (22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025), P7 (27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025) and P8 (24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025).
'Share of the web shop's sales' is read as the company-standard measure: share of web net sales in EUR excluding VAT, not share of order counts.
Web returns are tied back to the original order's fulfilment type, so each period's share is net of its own refunds.
Figures are as-is, with no regional or product hierarchy involved.
caveats: The period boundaries straddle the 3 November 2025 platform migration (inside P7), and channel_code is not filled after that date. I identified web by store 900 and click-and-collect by fulfilment_type, so the migration does not distort the shares. rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it drops web sales after the migration.
Control check: the web net sales behind each share (P6 175,588.62; P7 154,977.27; P8 225,265.08 EUR) match store 900 in rpt_daily_store_sales exactly in all three periods.

Duplicate sales lines were found (same receipt_id and line_no loaded twice), but only for store 116 in 15 to 21 September 2025. That is outside the web shop and outside P6 to P8, so no correction was needed. No duplicates exist among web lines in the range.

Web returns processed at physical stores (about 4,800 / 4,900 / 4,500 EUR net in P6 / P7 / P8, of which click-and-collect about 1,900 / 1,400 / 1,300 EUR) are booked to those stores under the company definition and are not in web net sales. Counting them against web would lower the shares by roughly 0.3 percentage points. I kept the company definition.
Cancelled orders (about 750 in September 2025 to January 2026, including click-and-collect) are excluded from web sales, as they have no sales lines.
Shares are rounded to two decimals; net amounts are before any rounding of the underlying lines.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS web_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 4 AND 6 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (not the order date in sale_date)
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code
Sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, each line at its own VAT rate
Before returns: refunds in fact_return_line left out
Cancelled orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders with a dispatch time)
Click-and-collect counted as web
Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25 Q2 = periods 4 to 6, weeks 14 to 26, 29 Jul to 27 Oct 2024
Dispatch timestamp converted from UTC to Helsinki time before assigning the date
assumptions: Q2 of FY24/25 read as FY2024/25 Q2, periods 4 to 6 as the request states, 29 July to 27 October 2024
The figures are gross sales including VAT with no refunds deducted, as asked. Refunds are not shown
Web sales dated on the dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date), the company default, so an order placed in one period can fall in the next
Amounts are in EUR
caveats: The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, inside P5. The figures sum gross_amount line by line, so each line carries the rate in force, and no flat rate was applied to a net total.
Two web lines for test articles (category ZZ Test, EUR 11.83 gross in total) were left out of the figures.

Data checks found no duplicate lines, no web lines without an order, no orders without dispatch time, and no order-total differences. Web net sales before returns for the same lines match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in all three periods (126242.65, 122660.57, 153786.32 excl. VAT).
Figures are not net sales. Net sales would be excl. VAT and after returns, so these figures are higher than the company's net sales metric.

answer.sql:
WITH period_8_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    dp.category,
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    SUM(f.net_amount) AS total_net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON f.product_key = dp.product_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25')
    AND dp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
  GROUP BY dp.category, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
)
SELECT 
  category,
  8 AS period,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN total_net_sales END), 2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN total_net_sales END), 2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25,
  ROUND(
    (MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN total_net_sales END) - 
     MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN total_net_sales END)) / 
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN total_net_sales END) * 100,
    2
  ) AS growth_pct
FROM period_8_sales
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Net sales from fact_sales_line.net_amount (value excluding VAT, after line discounts)
Fiscal period from dim_date.fiscal_period
Product categories from dim_product.category (current products)
assumptions: Last year interpreted as fiscal year FY2025/26
Year before interpreted as fiscal year FY2024/25
Growth calculated as year-on-year percentage change: ((FY2025/26 - FY2024/25) / FY2024/25) × 100
All sales included regardless of channel, member status, or staff flag
Only current product records (is_current = TRUE) used for category matching
caveats: Net sales exclude VAT, consistent with fact_sales_line definition
Sales line amounts only; returns are tracked in fact_return_line and are not netted
Garden category shows decline of 34.21% year-on-year despite Electrical growing 21.22%

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, s.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, l.format AS store_format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY l.format ORDER BY l.format
definitions_applied: Return rate: returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net (net_amount), both excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: refunds are matched to the sold line through sales_line_id, so a return counts in the period of the original sale, whenever and wherever it was booked
Goods sold selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date (Helsinki date, the order date on web lines)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Store format taken from dim_store on the version key of the sales line (format is the same in every store version)
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own format, Web, as in past requests
Staff purchases included
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request is dated 5 Oct 2026, which is in FY2026/27, and requests made after the new fiscal year began took the previous fiscal year.
'Period 2' read as fiscal period 2 of FY2025/26, 26 May to 22 June 2025 (weeks 5 to 8).
The Web shop is included as a fourth format row, because it is a format in dim_store and past format breakdowns included it. Drop that row if Commercial only wants physical store formats.
Return rate is measured on value (net EUR), not on units or number of lines.
Formats are Large, Medium and Small (plus Web), not the Hyper, Standard and Express named in the dim_store column comment.
caveats: Excluded training store 999 (126 lines, EUR 2,222 net, none returned) and ZZ Test articles (20 lines in store 999 and 1 web line, EUR 3.82). The effect on the rates is negligible.
The dim_store.format column comment ('Hyper, Standard or Express') is out of date. The actual values are Large, Medium, Small and Web.
The cohort is complete. The last sale in the period was 22 June 2025 and returns arrive up to 30 days later. Refunds were counted through the loaded data (latest return date seen 23 July 2025).

Web (12.23%) is much higher than the physical formats (4.28% to 4.53%), so any combined figure across formats would be driven by the web mix. Web returns are booked to the web shop, but they are attributed back to the original sale.
Sold net by format: Large EUR 400,763, Medium EUR 552,936, Small EUR 147,668, Web EUR 183,098. Returned net: Large EUR 17,708, Medium EUR 25,030, Small EUR 6,319, Web EUR 22,388.

No cancelled or processing web orders in the period's sold lines (only delivered and collected), so no web adjustment was needed. Source checks found no duplicate sales lines or return lines and no orphan returns.
The rpt_daily_store_sales control total was not run. It covers net sales after returns on return date, not a sale-cohort return rate, so it does not apply to this figure.

answer.sql:
WITH first_version AS (
    SELECT member_id, join_date, home_store_id,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS version_no
    FROM dim_member
)
SELECT fv.home_store_id, COALESCE(cs.store_name, 'Online') AS store_name, COUNT(*) AS new_members
FROM first_version fv
JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = fv.join_date
LEFT JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = fv.home_store_id AND cs.is_current
WHERE fv.version_no = 1
  AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
GROUP BY fv.home_store_id, cs.store_name
ORDER BY fv.home_store_id;
definitions_applied: DEF-NEW-MEMBER: counted on join_date at home_store_id in first version of dim_member
Member versioning: each member's first dim_member version defines their enrollment location
Store-as-is: store_name shown as current (is_current = true)
assumptions: Last year = FY2025/26 (28 Apr 2025 - 3 May 2026), based on request date 2026-10-07 being in FY2026/27
Online sign-ups are members with home_store_id = 900
Store names shown in current form, not as they were on enrollment date
Includes week 53 of FY2025/26 (27 Apr - 3 May 2026)
caveats: No issues detected. Query validated: unique at grain home_store_id, no deprecated objects, date coverage complete for FY2025/26.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS first_period, 4 AS last_period
)
SELECT cs.format,
       ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv
FROM fact_sales_line f
JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
JOIN dim_store cs  ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current
JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
JOIN dim_date d    ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE s.store_id < 900                         -- stores only: no web, no training store
  AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag                -- staff purchases are out of ATV
  AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
  AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY atv DESC;
definitions_applied: ATV (average transaction value): net sales before returns divided by the number of sales receipts
Store scope: physical stores only, excluding store 999 (training) and web shop (store 900)
Staff purchase exclusion: staff_purchase_flag = false
Test article exclusion: category <> 'ZZ Test'
assumptions: Period 4 this year read as FY2026/27 P04, the most recent completed period with that label as of the request date (following documented practice for relative period names without a year)
Store format breakdown includes all physical store formats in the warehouse: Large, Medium, Small

answer.sql: SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(year FROM f.sale_date) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year, CAST(EXTRACT(month FROM f.sale_date) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_month, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS store_sales_incl_vat_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Store sales = physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (store 900) left out
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Including VAT = sum of gross_amount from the lines; each line carries its own VAT rate, no flat rate applied to a net total
Before returns: fact_return_line not used and no refunds deducted
Staff purchases included (net sales definition; only ATV excludes them)
Store sales dated on fact_sales_line.sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Calendar months read literally as 1-31 August 2024 and 1-30 September 2024
Control total against rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales_before_returns on the net amounts
assumptions: August 2024 and September 2024 were read as calendar months, as the request names months rather than fiscal periods
Store sales means physical stores only, with the web shop not included
Staff purchases are kept in, since the request does not exclude them
Figures are in EUR including VAT, one figure per month
caveats: The general VAT rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. The gross_amount on each line already carries the right rate (24% standard-rate lines in August, 25.5% in September; 14% and 10% unchanged), so no correction was needed. I checked that no line used the wrong rate for its date and that gross_amount equals net times (1 + vat_rate) within rounding.
The September figure includes the higher 25.5% rate on standard-rate goods, so the August to September change in gross sales is not a like-for-like volume comparison.

The gross figures cannot be reconciled with rpt_daily_store_sales, which holds net sales only. I checked the net amounts for the same stores and days instead (August 1,101,807.91 and September 964,016.09 EUR excluding VAT). They matched the control table exactly, store by store and day by day.
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were filtered out. The result is for stores below 900 only, so these filters did not change the store totals shown here.

Returns are not deducted, as requested. If a figure after refunds is needed later, refund_gross from fact_return_line would be shown as its own column, since the dictionary does not define how returns enter a VAT-inclusive figure.
I found no duplicate sales lines, no mismatch between sale_date and the Helsinki date of sale_ts_utc, and no null amounts in the range.

answer.sql: WITH w AS (SELECT min(period_start_date) AS s, max(period_end_date) AS e FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period IN (9,10)) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, '9 and 10' AS fiscal_periods, round(100.0*sum(CASE WHEN o.fulfilment_type='click_and_collect' THEN f.net_amount END)/sum(f.net_amount), 2) AS click_and_collect_share_of_web_net_sales_pct FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id=f.receipt_id, w WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN w.s AND w.e
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: periods 9 and 10 of FY2025/26 run 2025-12-22 to 2026-02-22 (ref_fiscal_calendar, 9 weeks, fully loaded)
Web sales = lines of web orders in fact_sales_line, linked to fact_web_order via receipt_id = web_order_id
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, not by channel_id
Sales value = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts)
sale_date used as the date of sale (it is the Helsinki local date)
Cancelled and processing orders have no sales lines, so they are excluded
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, since the request was received on 2026-10-06 and the current fiscal year is FY2026/27. 'Periods 9 and 10' are fiscal periods, not calendar months.

'Web sales' means net sales value in EUR excluding VAT, the company's standard sales measure, before returns. The share is click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (home delivery plus click-and-collect).
Returns are not deducted. Netting off returns booked in the window (the refunds are booked against the original line, whichever period it was sold in) would give 30.47%.
caveats: Correction: dim_channel separates 'Click and collect' (channel_id 3) from 'Web home delivery' (channel_id 2), but 758 click-and-collect orders (1,473 lines, 43,819.29 EUR net, sale dates 2026-01-12 to 2026-02-08) are coded channel_id 2. Taking click-and-collect from channel_id would give 17.41% (60,496.25 of 347,431.30 EUR net) instead of 30.02%. The corrected figure classifies by fulfilment_type on the web order: 104,315.54 EUR click-and-collect net out of 347,431.30 EUR web net.
Channel coding is also unreliable for other dates. Lines before Nov 2025 have no channel_id, and channel_code is null in the periods checked, so fulfilment_type is the only reliable key.
On an order-count basis the share is 29.62% (1,830 of 6,178 orders). On a gross (VAT-inclusive) basis it is 30.03%.

No other defects were found in the window. There were no duplicate receipt lines, net and gross amounts agreed with VAT, order totals and line counts matched fact_web_order, and every delivered or collected order has sales lines.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P5 is 31 August to 27 September 2026 (ref_fiscal_calendar, fully loaded)
Units sold are the quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki) identified by natural key store_id, covering both store versions
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither affected the result)
Products grouped by stable sku, with the name taken from the current product version
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 102 over the same days
Web (store 900) not included, since the question is about a physical store
assumptions: Pitäjänmäki read as store 102, Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, the only store with that name
'Period 5 of FY26/27' read as FY2026/27 P5, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026; P5 is the latest complete period
'Sold the most units' read as gross units sold, before returns; staff purchases are included, as in the net sales definition
A product means a sku, not a product version
caveats: No data problems affected the answer. Sales lines for store 102 over the period (2,121 lines, 3,740 units, 57,200.59 EUR net before returns) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, and there are no duplicate lines.
Staff purchases are included. Only 2 of the 42 units for sku 102244 were staff purchases, and the top three are unchanged if they are excluded.
Returns are not deducted. In the period, sku 102244 had 1 unit returned at the store and the other two had none, so the order does not change on a net-units basis.
The margin to the fourth place is clear: the fourth product (sku 102233 Batteries & Bulbs Havu Pro 384) sold 30 units, against 42 for third.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, cs.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT s.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net),0) / SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold s LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.sales_line_id = s.sales_line_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Return rate = refund_net divided by sold net_amount, both excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: sold lines selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date, refunds matched through sales_line_id whenever and wherever they were booked
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop is store 900 with format Web, shown as its own format row
Format taken from the current dim_store version (format is the same in every version of each store)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (FY2025/26 P2 = 26 May 2025 to 22 June 2025, 4 weeks)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
No deprecated tables or views used and no channel_code used
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 because the request is dated 5 Oct 2026 (FY2026/27). This matches how earlier requests were read (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).
'Period 2' means fiscal period 2 of FY2025/26, not calendar February.
'Goods sold in period 2' means a sale-week cohort, so returns count against the period of the original sale. This follows the return-rate definition and REQ-D14 to D16.
Web lines are dated by sale_date (the order date) when selecting the cohort, as in the accepted return-rate queries. Web order dispatch dates are not used here.
Format groups are the values in the warehouse (Large, Medium, Small, Web). The schema comment (Hyper, Standard, Express) is out of date and was not used.
Result shows the four rows the request implies and no company total, because none was asked for.
caveats: Store 999 and ZZ Test lines were removed from the sold base: 127 lines, EUR 2,226.03 net in the period. They are excluded from every format row.
The out-of-date format comment in the schema was corrected by checking the distinct values. Real formats are Large, Medium, Small and Web. Store 999 has format Training and is excluded.

Web is the outlier at 12.23%, against 4.28% to 4.53% for the physical formats, so Web should be read separately from the store formats. Web returns booked to store 900 included reasons such as damaged_in_transit.

The cohort is complete. Returns arrive up to about 30 days after sale (a few lag 31 to 56 days) and the warehouse is loaded to 4 Oct 2026. Every return matched an existing sales line and no refund exceeded its sold line.

Underlying figures (EUR, net excluding VAT): Large sold 400,763.11 and returned 17,707.57; Medium sold 552,936.25 and returned 25,030.11; Small sold 147,668.20 and returned 6,319.09; Web sold 183,098.49 and returned 22,388.29.
The store-level control total against rpt_daily_store_sales was not run, because it does not apply to a return-rate cohort or a category-filtered subset.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop 900 excluded
Trading days: days after opening and before closure, outside refit closures (ref_store_closure), excluding closed holidays (dim_date.is_trading_day false)
A store that traded only part of the period stays in the table, ranked on its own trading days
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2026/27 P02 = weeks 5-8, 1 to 28 June 2026
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
Store attributes (name, closure and opening dates) from the current dim_store version
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P2, the current fiscal year as of the 7 Oct 2026 request. This matches how P2 was read in past request D10.
'Store ranking' read as the store league table: net sales per trading day, highest first, not total net sales.
Ties are ranked with RANK(); there were no ties.
net_sales is the period total excluding VAT, in EUR. net_sales_per_trading_day is that total divided by the store's trading days, rounded to 2 decimals.
Store names are taken from the current store version (as-is). Stores have no region column in the answer, so the April 2025 regional reorganisation does not affect the ranking.
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it traded only 14 of the 26 trading days in the period. It is ranked on its own 14 days and ranks 7th. Its period total (23,993.71) is much lower than its per-day figure implies for a full period, so do not compare its net sales total with other stores.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales or trading days in the period, so it is not in the table (38 stores listed).
Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (19 and 20 June 2026) are closed holidays and do not count as trading days, so the full-period stores have 26 trading days, not 28.
The sum of store net sales (1,063,916.20) matches the rpt_daily_store_sales control total for the same stores and days exactly, by store and by day, with no gap and no duplicate store-day rows.
The web shop (900) and store 999 are not in the ranking.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.sale_date, cp.subcategory, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory <> 'Outdoor Lighting' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 13), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_quarter, l.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY l.subcategory ORDER BY l.subcategory
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net (net_amount), both excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: returns are attributed back to the original sale line via sales_line_id, whenever and wherever they were booked
Goods selected by fiscal period of the sale date (sale_date, Helsinki business date)
Q1 = P1 to P3 = fiscal weeks 1 to 13 (28 April 2025 to 27 July 2025)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900) included as sales; web lines selected by order date as in accepted REQ-D16; none of the web orders in scope were cancelled
Staff purchases included
As-is hierarchy: current category and subcategory of each SKU (is_current product version)
Outdoor lighting treated as Electrical for all history (moved from Garden on 27 October 2025)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just completed when the request was received on 6 October 2026 (FY2026/27 is the current year), consistent with past accepted readings.
'Q1' read as fiscal Q1 (P1 to P3), not calendar Q1.
'Garden' read on the current (as-is) product hierarchy, as management reporting does by default, so subcategories are those of the current Garden category.
Web and store sales both included, since the request does not limit the channel.
Rate is value-based (refund net / sold net), the company definition, not a units-based rate.
caveats: Outdoor lighting is excluded from Garden as-is, because it moved to Electrical from 27 October 2025. Five delisted outdoor lighting SKUs never got a new product version and still show category Garden in the current dimension. I excluded their 19 Q1 sales lines (375.00 EUR net sales, no returns) to keep outdoor lighting in Electrical for all history. Including them would add an 'Outdoor Lighting' row at 0.00%, with no effect on the other subcategories. On an as-was basis Garden in Q1 would also include all outdoor lighting.
The cohort is complete: the last Q1 sale was 27 July 2025, well over the 30-day return window before the last loaded date (4 October 2026).
Store 999 sales (133 Garden lines, 2,444.50 EUR net sales, no returns) were excluded.

I found duplicated sales lines in fact_sales_line (418 pairs sharing receipt_id and line_no, loaded twice on 16 and 23 September 2025). They sit entirely in FY2025/26 P5, outside Q1, so they do not affect this result. Q1 sales_line_ids are unique.
I checked fact_return_line for duplicates, orphan returns, returns exceeding the quantity or value sold, and returns dated before the sale. I found none.
Garden Furniture has by far the highest rate (12.87%). Outdoor Lighting is the only Garden subcategory with no returns, and I have not shown it.
A few lines each side of the Q1 boundaries sit on a different day in UTC than in Helsinki. I used the Helsinki sale_date, as the company does.

answer.sql:
WITH as_of AS (SELECT DATE '2025-12-21' AS d),
members_at_date AS (
  SELECT m.member_id, m.tier
  FROM dim_member m, as_of
  WHERE m.valid_from <= as_of.d AND m.valid_to >= as_of.d AND m.join_date <= as_of.d
),
purchasers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key
  , as_of
  WHERE f.sale_date > as_of.d - INTERVAL 12 MONTH AND f.sale_date <= as_of.d
)
SELECT a.tier, count(*) AS active_members
FROM members_at_date a JOIN purchasers p USING (member_id)
GROUP BY a.tier
ORDER BY CASE a.tier WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1 WHEN 'Silver' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: end of FY2025/26 period 8 is 2025-12-21, from ref_fiscal_calendar
Slowly changing member dimension: tier taken from the dim_member version valid on 2025-12-21, not the current tier
Members counted by member_id (loyalty number), not member_key, so each member is counted once
Member must have joined on or before 2025-12-21
Active member: at least one purchase line in the 12 months up to and including 2025-12-21
assumptions: 'Last year' means FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 (request dated 2026-10-07). Period 8 of FY2026/27 has not happened yet, so no other reading is possible.
'End of period 8' means the last day of the period, 2025-12-21.

The warehouse documents no definition of 'active member'. I took it to mean at least one purchase in the trailing 12 months, which is the usual loyalty-programme meaning. Purchases are identified through member_id, so a member who bought under an earlier or later version of their record still counts.
All purchase lines count, including staff purchases and web orders by logged-in members. Returns are not netted off, so a member whose only purchase was later returned still counts as active.
Tiers are listed as Basic, Silver, Gold, in loyalty-programme order, not alphabetically.
caveats: Without the 12-month purchase test, 48,675 members were on file at 2025-12-21 (Basic 29,304, Silver 15,035, Gold 4,336). Only about 60% of them (29,557) had bought anything in the prior 12 months. If Marketing counts 'active' as simply enrolled, those are the figures to use.
Using the current tier (is_current = true) instead of the tier on 2025-12-21 would misstate the counts, because members change tier over time. I used the version valid on the date.
The sales data starts on 2024-04-29, so the full 12-month look-back window is covered.
Checks on dim_member found no gaps or overlaps between member versions, no duplicate member_id on the as-of date, and no members with a join date after 2025-12-21.
Any definition of 'active' other than the 12-month purchase rule would change the numbers. Please confirm the intended definition with Marketing and CRM.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - As-is store hierarchy (current dim_store version)

WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, 
           p.sku, p.product_name, p.product_key,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, 
           p.sku, p.product_name, p.product_key,
           -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT n.sku, n.product_name, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales
FROM net_lines n
WHERE n.business_date >= DATE '2025-11-03'
GROUP BY n.product_key, n.sku, n.product_name
ORDER BY web_net_sales DESC
LIMIT 10;
definitions_applied: Web sales: net amount excluding VAT, recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time (not order date)
Returns: reduce net sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Net sales: calculated as sum of sales lines minus refunds, excluding store 999 and category ZZ Test
Web identification: by store_id 900 (not by channel_code or channel_id, which changed at migration)
Dispatch date: converted from UTC timestamp to Helsinki time
assumptions: Platform migration date 3 November 2025 is the start date; no explicit end date was specified, so the query includes all available data through the warehouse load point (4 October 2026)
Request asks for 'top 10 products', so the result is ordered by net sales descending and limited to 10 rows
Web sales include click-and-collect orders (fulfilment_type is not filtered, as both home_delivery and click_and_collect are web)
caveats: The results show the sum of net sales per product across the entire period (11 months); if a product appears multiple times in the list due to versioning changes, sales are combined into the current product version
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so recent sales weeks may have incomplete return data
The top 10 products represent EUR 96,223.06 of total web net sales of EUR 2,150,090.07 in the period (4.5% of total web revenue)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(n.net_sales) DESC) AS rank, n.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, cp.brand, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS web_net_sales_eur FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-03' AND DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY n.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, cp.brand ORDER BY web_net_sales_eur DESC LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (fact_web_order dispatch_ts_utc converted with timezone('Europe/Helsinki', ... AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')), not the order date
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded (only delivered and collected orders count as web sales)
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date (refund_net, booked to the web shop store 900)
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code or channel_id (neither works across the 3 November 2025 migration)
Click-and-collect counted as web (collected orders are included)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Product identified by stable sku, with name, category, subcategory and brand from the current product version (as-is)
Deprecated objects (rpt.v_daily_sales, stg_, bak_, tmp_ and old tables) not used

assumptions: Measure: the request does not say what 'web sales' is ranked by, so I ranked by web net sales in EUR excluding VAT, after returns, per the company definition (not units, not gross including VAT)

Period: 3 November 2025 to 4 October 2026 inclusive, the last day loaded in the warehouse, using the dispatch date. Orders placed shortly before 3 November but dispatched on or after it are included, because sales are recognised on dispatch

Returns in the window are netted against the sku regardless of when the original sale took place, including returns of web sales dispatched before 3 November 2025 (per the 'returns on their return date' rule)
'Product' read as article (sku), not subcategory or brand

Web returns processed in physical stores are not netted here: following the company definition they belong to the store that processed them, so web sales only carry refunds booked to the web shop (store 900)
caveats: No data correction was needed. The only duplicate rows found in fact_sales_line (418 duplicated receipt_id + line_no pairs, loaded 23 Sep 2025) are in store sales for 15 to 21 September 2025, not in web lines or in the requested window, so they do not affect this result.

The data run through 4 October 2026 only, so the period is 11 months, not a full year; the Christmas decoration and garden furniture lines are seasonal, so the ranking reflects one winter and one summer season.

Refunds change the order materially: ranked on sales before returns, 'Bedroom Peltola 793' (sku 103390) would be first at 15,533.23 EUR, but returns of 4,625.28 EUR booked to the web shop bring it to third place at 10,907.95. Ranking on gross sales gives a different order, though the same top-10 set under the other return treatment I tested below.

Sensitivity: if refunds on web lines processed in physical stores were also netted against the web lines (rather than against those stores), the ten products would be the same, with Garden Furniture Raudikko 536 moving ahead of Bedroom Peltola 793 for third; values would be lower by 0.2 to 0.8 thousand EUR for several products. The 10 listed use the company definition (store 900 returns only).
Test articles (ZZ Test) in web orders were excluded; this removed 25.50 EUR of web net sales in the window and has no effect on the ranking.
