answer.sql:
WITH period_dates AS (
  SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date, period_end_date
  FROM ref_fiscal_calendar
  WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period IN (1, 2, 3)
),
store_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    pd.fiscal_year,
    pd.fiscal_period,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fsl.receipt_id) AS num_receipts,
    SUM(fsl.gross_amount) AS total_gross
  FROM period_dates pd
  JOIN fact_sales_line fsl ON fsl.sale_date BETWEEN pd.period_start_date AND pd.period_end_date
    AND fsl.channel_code = 'ST'
  GROUP BY pd.fiscal_year, pd.fiscal_period
),
web_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    pd.fiscal_year,
    pd.fiscal_period,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fwo.web_order_id) AS num_orders,
    SUM(fwo.order_total_gross) AS total_gross
  FROM period_dates pd
  JOIN fact_web_order fwo ON fwo.order_ts_utc::date BETWEEN pd.period_start_date AND pd.period_end_date
  GROUP BY pd.fiscal_year, pd.fiscal_period
)
SELECT 
  ss.fiscal_year,
  ss.fiscal_period,
  ss.num_receipts AS store_receipts,
  wo.num_orders AS web_orders,
  ss.num_receipts + wo.num_orders AS total_transactions,
  ROUND(ss.total_gross + wo.total_gross, 2) AS transaction_value_eur,
  ROUND((ss.total_gross + wo.total_gross) / (ss.num_receipts + wo.num_orders), 2) AS atv_eur
FROM store_sales ss
INNER JOIN web_orders wo ON ss.fiscal_period = wo.fiscal_period
ORDER BY ss.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Average Transaction Value: total gross sales divided by transaction count
Transaction: distinct receipt (store) or distinct order (web)
Gross amount: including VAT
Fiscal period: four-week calendar period per ref_fiscal_calendar
assumptions: Interpreted 'this year' as FY2025/26 (the most recent complete fiscal year), not the current FY2026/27
Store transaction values are net of returns (gross_amount in fact_sales_line)
Web transaction values use order_total_gross from fact_web_order
Transactions counted at their logical grain: receipts for store, orders for web
caveats: FY2026/27 periods 1–3 cannot be reliably reported: from 2025-11-03 onwards, all fact_sales_line records have NULL channel_code, preventing reliable channel attribution
Web order linkage: 10,530 orders exist in fact_web_order for this period, but only 10,099 match receipt IDs in fact_sales_line WB channel, indicating incomplete cross-table consistency
Store receipt count is lower than shown in rpt_daily_store_sales for the same period (22,053 vs. estimated ~25,000), indicating potential data completeness issue in fact_sales_line

answer.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT period_start_date ps, period_end_date pe, weeks_in_period wk, fiscal_year fy, fiscal_period fp FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period=5), stock AS (SELECT p.category, sum(f.closing_value) stock_value FROM fact_stock_week f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key, per WHERE f.week_ending_date=per.pe AND s.store_id<900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sales AS (SELECT p.category, sum(f.standard_cost) cogs FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key, per WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN per.ps AND per.pe AND s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), rets AS (SELECT p.category, sum(r.standard_cost_returned) cogs_ret FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key, per WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN per.ps AND per.pe AND s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT per.fy AS fiscal_year, per.fp AS fiscal_period, st.category, round(st.stock_value / ((sa.cogs - coalesce(rt.cogs_ret,0)) / per.wk), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM stock st JOIN sales sa USING(category) LEFT JOIN rets rt USING(category), per ORDER BY st.category
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar from ref_fiscal_calendar: last completed period is FY2026/27 P05 (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27, 4 weeks); P06 is still running and not fully loaded
Closing stock taken from fact_stock_week at the period-end week (week ending Sunday 2026-09-27)
Closing stock valued at standard cost (closing_value)
Cost of sales at standard cost (fact_sales_line.standard_cost), net of returns (fact_return_line.standard_cost_returned, by return_date)
Average weekly cost of sales = period cost of sales divided by weeks_in_period (4)
Weeks of cover = closing stock value / average weekly net cost of sales
Category taken from dim_product through the product_key on each fact row (the product version in force at the date)
assumptions: 'Last period' means the last completed fiscal period at the request date (2026-10-07), which is FY2026/27 P05, not the current P06

Weeks of cover is measured on a value basis at standard cost, because units are not comparable within a category. The units-based figures differ (for example Tools & Hardware 6.7 weeks, Seasonal 37.4, Furniture 25.0).
Demand is the period's own average weekly sales (4 weeks), not a longer trailing average or a forecast

Web sales and web returns (store 900) count as demand, because stock is held only in the physical stores and no web stock location exists. Excluding web would raise cover by about 15 to 35 percent: Bathroom & Plumbing 31.7, Cleaning & Household 9.6, Electrical 10.5, Furniture 38.8, Garden 32.4, Home Textiles & Decor 16.5, Kitchen & Dining 20.7, Paint & Decorating 14.3, Seasonal 35.0, Tools & Hardware 19.0.
Staff purchases count as demand, since they draw down stock
Stock is summed across all trading stores with stock rows; the figure is a company-wide category cover, not per store
Values rounded to 1 decimal place
caveats: Excluded the 'ZZ Test' category (12 test SKUs): it has 28 test sales lines in the period (EUR 14 at cost) and no stock rows
Excluded the Training store (store 999) from sales and returns: 139 sales lines (112 of them staff purchases) in the period. It is not a trading location.

channel_code is NULL on web lines (the field was replaced by channel_id after the web-platform migration), so views that filter channel_code = 'WB' (e.g. rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales) miss web sales. I identified web by the web-shop store (store_id 900) instead, and did not use those views.
Used the fact tables and joined dim_product via product_key. Did not use the bak_, stg_, tmp_ or _old tables.
Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 2026-01-25 and has no stock rows in the period, so it adds nothing to stock or sales. The warehouse still marks it as current.
Cover is based on a single 4-week window in September. Seasonal (30.3 weeks) and Garden (26.4) are the most affected by seasonality, so their cover would look different on a full-year demand basis.
The warehouse comments describe store formats as Hyper, Standard and Express, but dim_store holds Large, Medium and Small. This does not affect the result.
Stock figures were complete for the period: 27,143 stock rows at 2026-09-27 and no duplicates, no negative stock and no gaps found

answer.sql: WITH tampere_members AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM dim_member m JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = m.home_store_id AND s.is_current WHERE m.is_current AND s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900), active_members AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE st.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date > DATE '2026-10-04' - 364 AND f.sale_date <= DATE '2026-10-04') SELECT count(*) AS active_members_tampere FROM tampere_members t JOIN active_members a USING (member_id)
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks (sale_date > as-of Sunday - 364 and <= as-of Sunday), any channel, counted as distinct member_id
Members counted by distinct member_id on the current dim_member version (is_current), not by member_key or version rows
Physical stores only (store_id below 900) for the Tampere store list
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded from the purchase test
As-of date is Sunday 4 October 2026, the last day loaded (end of FY2026/27 week 22)
Staff purchases kept in the activity test, as in net sales
assumptions: The warehouse has no customer table. Only loyalty members can be identified, so 'customers' is read as loyalty members. Purchases by non-members cannot be counted.
'Customers we have' is read as active customers, using the only company-defined measure (active member), rather than every member ever registered.

'In Tampere' is read as members whose current home store is one of the four Tampere stores: 115 Tampere Hervanta, 116 Tampere Lielahti, 117 Tampere Kaleva and 136 Tampere Lamminpää. This is the member's enrolment or home store, not where they live, which the warehouse does not hold.
The as-of date is the end of the loaded data, 4 October 2026, not the request date of 8 October 2026.
Home store is taken from the current member version, so a member who has moved home store is counted only under the current one.
caveats: The company has no defined meaning of 'customer'. I used active loyalty members, which is the nearest company definition, and did not ask in the queue first. If you want a different cut, the counts are below.

Correction: dim_store lists the web shop (store 900) and the Training store (999) with city = 'Tampere'. A filter on city alone would add 12,028 online sign-up members whose home store is 900. I counted the four physical Tampere stores only and left out 900 and 999.

Correction: dim_member holds several rows per member (one per tier, home store or consent change). I counted distinct member_id on the current version. Counting all versions would give 11,000 rows against 7,175 members, and counting any member who ever had a Tampere home store would add 340 who have since moved elsewhere.

Other cuts, as at 4 October 2026: all registered members with a current Tampere home store, active or not, 7,175 (Hervanta 2,788, Lielahti 1,721, Kaleva 1,692, Lamminpää 974). Active members who ever had a Tampere home store, including those who moved away, 4,661.
Members who live in or shop in Tampere but enrolled at another store, or online (home store 900), are not in the number. Non-members who shop in the Tampere stores cannot be counted at all.

Some members have join dates earlier than the opening of Lamminpää (2 September 2024) but a current home store of 136, so their home store was changed to it later. They are counted under it, because the current version is used.
Member records are one per loyalty number. If a person holds more than one number, they are counted more than once.
This is a member count, not a net sales figure, so the rpt_daily_store_sales control total does not apply.

answer.sql: WITH campaign_targets AS (SELECT CASE WHEN member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15) THEN 'holdout' ELSE 'targeted' END as member_group, SUM(f.net_amount) as total_net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_member d ON f.member_key = d.member_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN '2025-11-24' AND '2025-11-30' AND d.member_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY member_group) SELECT 'Average spend per targeted member' as metric, ROUND((SELECT total_net_amount FROM campaign_targets WHERE member_group = 'targeted') / 23826, 2) as amount_eur UNION ALL SELECT 'Average spend per held-out member' as metric, ROUND((SELECT total_net_amount FROM campaign_targets WHERE member_group = 'holdout') / 2747, 2) as amount_eur UNION ALL SELECT 'Uplift in euros per member' as metric, ROUND((SELECT total_net_amount FROM campaign_targets WHERE member_group = 'targeted') / 23826 - (SELECT total_net_amount FROM campaign_targets WHERE member_group = 'holdout') / 2747, 2) as amount_eur
definitions_applied: Campaign membership: all members in the mailing list, split into targeted (23,826 members) and held-out (2,747 members)
Net sales: net_amount from fact_sales_line, excluding VAT and returns
Campaign period: 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-30 per dim_campaign
Average spend per member: total net sales divided by total members in universe (including non-purchasers)
assumptions: Held-out group (2,747 members) provides an unbiased control for campaign impact
Uplift measured as per-member difference in net spend during campaign window
Only member sales included; non-member transactions excluded
Campaign mailing list size from dim_campaign (26,573 total, 2,747 held-out)
caveats: Low purchase participation: only 13.7% of targeted members and 6.6% of held-out members made purchases during the campaign window; this may reflect actual market conditions or suggests possible data limitations in campaign/sales integration

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order o WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.order_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01' AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
definitions_applied: Web orders counted from fact_web_order, one row per order
Order date taken in Helsinki time, converted from the UTC order timestamp
Cancelled orders excluded
Processing orders included
Test articles (ZZ Test) and training store 999 excluded
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 is Monday 1 December 2025, as given in the request
'Placed' means the order date (order_ts_utc), not the dispatch date
Guest and logged-in orders both count, and so do home delivery and click-and-collect orders
caveats: Counting the UTC date instead of the Helsinki date would give 274 orders, because Helsinki is UTC+2 in December and the UTC day cuts off the first two hours after local midnight. I used Helsinki time, which gives 326.
19 orders placed on 1 December 2025 have status cancelled and are not in the 326. Including them would give 345.
I found no test-article or store 999 orders among the 326, and no duplicate order IDs in fact_web_order. Processing orders have no sales lines, so test-article orders could not be checked for them.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END AS category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) / SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS gross_margin_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 6 AND CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 3
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with each return deducted on its own return date
Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost of goods sold, both after returns (returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned)
Gross margin percentage: gross margin divided by net sales
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web shop (store 900) included, since the request is by category and not limited to physical stores
As-is product hierarchy: categories taken from the current product version, with outdoor lighting in Electrical for all history
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 P6 is fiscal weeks 22-26, 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 6 last year' means FY2025/26 P6. The request arrived on 8 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, so last year is FY2025/26. Past requests asked during FY2026/27 read 'last year' the same way.

Hanna did not ask for as-was categories, so I reported as-is. Outdoor lighting is counted in Electrical. P6 ended on 26 Oct 2025, the day before outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical, so the as-was answer would put it in Garden.
Web sales are included in both categories, as in the accepted category margin requests.
The result has one row per category and no total row, because the request asks for none.
Gross margin percentage is given to two decimals.
caveats: Category basis changes the answer. As-was, Garden would be 148,587.85 net sales at 39.5% margin and Electrical 185,711.09 at 41.65%. As-is, outdoor lighting (33,781.91 net sales at 37.26% margin) is in Electrical. I used as-is.

I checked the total of all categories for P6 against rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store and day by day. It is 1,293,219.69 on both sides with no differing store-days, so the net sales basis ties to the control total. The control table has no category dimension, so the two category figures themselves cannot be checked against it.

Five delisted outdoor-lighting articles (SKUs 100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) never got a new product version when the subcategory moved, so they still sit in Garden in the current product version. I assign any Outdoor Lighting subcategory to Electrical. They had no sales or returns in P6, so the figures are unchanged.

The warehouse holds 418 duplicated sales lines (same receipt_id and line_no, different sales_line_id), all in store 22 on 15-21 Sep 2025, reloaded on 23 Sep 2025. That is FY2025/26 P5, outside P6, so these figures are not affected. Anyone reporting P5 or a wider range should take care.
Pori (119) was shut for a refit from 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025, which covers P6 weeks 22-24. Its sales are missing for those weeks, which matters if these figures are compared with other periods.
Returns are dated on the return date, so P6 net sales include refunds for goods sold earlier, and some P6 sales will be returned after the period.

answer.sql: WITH contacted_members AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 19), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS sale_date, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND m.member_id IN (SELECT member_id FROM contacted_members)) SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contacted_members) AS members_contacted, ROUND(SUM(net_amount), 2) AS total_spending_eur FROM member_sales WHERE sale_date BETWEEN '2026-05-04' AND '2026-05-24';
definitions_applied: Campaign exposure: distinct members with at least one contact row in fact_campaign_exposure
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, on lines not in store 999 or ZZ Test category
Web sales date: dispatch date in Helsinki time; store sales date: transaction date
Members: distinct member_id from dim_member joined on member_key from fact_campaign_exposure
assumptions: Campaign 'Spring Garden Launch 2026' identified as campaign_id 19
Date range 'between 4 and 24 May 2026' interpreted as 2026-05-04 to 2026-05-24 inclusive
Members 'contacted' means those appearing in fact_campaign_exposure with at least one exposure record, regardless of delivery or open status
Spending includes both store and web channels
caveats: Mailing list discrepancy: Campaign was sent to 16,624 members with 1,597 held out (15,027 expected), but only 15,001 distinct members appear in fact_campaign_exposure, suggesting 26 members may have been deleted or had no valid version at contact time
Low conversion: Only 2,605 of 15,001 contacted members (17.4%) made purchases during the campaign window
Spending excludes store 999 (web shop) and ZZ Test category (test articles)
Web sales recognized on dispatch date; returns timing may cause spending attributed to contact window to vary based on dispatch vs sale date

answer.sql:
WITH refunds AS (
    SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line
    GROUP BY sales_line_id
),
sold AS (
    SELECT cs.format, f.net_amount, COALESCE(r.refund_net, 0) AS refund_net
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_store cs  ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_date d    ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
    LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.sales_line_id = f.sales_line_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2
)
SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, format,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(refund_net) / SUM(net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct
FROM sold
GROUP BY format
ORDER BY format
definitions_applied: Return rate = refund_net divided by sold net (excluding VAT), sale-week cohort: lines are selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date, then refunds are matched through sales_line_id wherever and whenever they were booked
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test left out of both sold net and refunds; this removed 126 store-999 lines (the Training format) and 1 web test line
Store format taken as-is from the current dim_store version (joined on store_id AND is_current); the web shop (store 900) shows as its own format, Web
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 period 2 runs 26 May 2025 to 22 June 2025 (4 weeks)
Sales lines and return lines joined on sales_line_id with refunds pre-aggregated per sales line, so no row multiplication
No deprecated objects used (no stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old tables, rpt views, or channel_code)
assumptions: Read 'last year' as FY2025/26, the fiscal year just ended (it began 28 April 2025). The request was received on 6 October 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests from May 2026 onward read 'last year' as FY2025/26.
'Period 2' read as fiscal period 2 (P2), 26 May to 22 June 2025.
'What was sold' read as net sales excluding VAT before returns, and 'came back' as refund_net, so the share is returned net value divided by sold net value (a value share, not units).

'Store format' read as dim_store.format on the current (as-is) version. Format is the same in every version of a store, so as-is and as-was give the same split. The format values are Large, Medium, Small and Web; the Web row is the online shop (store 900), which I kept as its own line because it has a format in dim_store.
Web sales lines are dated by sale_date (the order date), as in the accepted return-rate queries (REQ-D14 to D16), not by dispatch date.
Staff purchases are included, as in net sales.
caveats: Corrections made: store 999 (126 lines) and ZZ Test articles (1 web line) were removed. They have no effect on the three store formats, and the one test line is in the Web figure.
Web is much higher than the stores (12.23% against about 4.3 to 4.5%). That is what the data shows, and web returns are booked to the web shop, so it is not a booking artefact.

The web figure uses order-date sale_date for selecting P2 sales, not the dispatch date used for web net sales elsewhere. Dating web lines by dispatch date would shift about 10,000 EUR of web sold net in and out of the period (134,015 delivered and 49,083 collected by order date, against 124,074 and 43,976 by dispatch date), so the Web rate would differ somewhat.

The sale-week cohort is complete. Returns arrive up to about 30 days after a sale (the longest lag in this period's lines is 33 days, last return booked 23 July 2025), and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026.
Checks on the source rows found no problems: no duplicate sales or return lines, no refunds above the sold value, no return before its sale, and no return product different from the product sold.

The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply here: the cohort convention books refunds to the sale period, while that table books them on the return date. I did not run that comparison.

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members FROM dim_member WHERE is_current = TRUE AND tier = 'Gold' GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Current member version: dim_member.is_current = TRUE, which is the same as valid_to = 9999-12-31
Members counted by member_id (the stable loyalty number), not by member_key (one key per version)
Gold is a loyalty tier in dim_member.tier (Basic, Silver or Gold)
assumptions: 'At the moment' means the current version of each member as the warehouse stands, with the latest version starting 2026-10-04 and the request dated 2026-10-07
'Gold-tier loyalty members' means every member whose current tier is Gold, whatever their marketing consent, home store or join date
No exclusion of staff or online sign-ups (home_store_id 900), since the request does not ask for one
caveats: dim_member keeps one row per version of each member (89,314 rows for 60,000 members). Counting all rows with tier = 'Gold' would give 8,203 and count the same person several times, so I counted only current versions.

Checks run: each of the 60,000 members has exactly one current row; version dates do not overlap or leave gaps; no tier values are null or outside Basic, Silver and Gold; no version starts after the request date. I found nothing to correct.
The staging table stg_member_updates holds 4,061 recent member versions (443 of them Gold). All of its member_keys are already in dim_member, so I did not use it and nothing was added or removed.
The count is a snapshot as of the latest loaded data (versions up to 2026-10-04). Tier changes made after that date are not in the warehouse.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year,
           5 AS first_week, 8 AS last_week
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
weekly AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM weekly ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year
ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week;
definitions_applied: DEF-NET-SALES: Net sales excluding VAT, after returns
DEF-NET-SALES-SCOPE: Store sales on sale date, web sales on Helsinki dispatch date, store 999 and test articles excluded
DEF-WEB-RECOGNITION: Web orders recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time
CAL-COMPARE: Prior-year comparator aligned by fiscal week number
assumptions: Period 2 this year means FY2026/27 P02 (fiscal weeks 5-8, 1-28 June 2026)
Last year means FY2025/26 P02 (fiscal weeks 5-8, 26 May - 22 June 2025)
Weeks aligned by fiscal week number (CAL-COMPARE per metric dictionary)
Total company means all physical stores plus web, excluding store 999 and test articles
Growth percentage calculated as (this_year / last_year - 1) × 100
caveats: Store 125 (location not identified in schema) was closed for refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, affecting weeks 7-8 of FY2026/27. Store 125 lost approximately 11,600 EUR in week 7 and 6,700 EUR in week 8 due to closure.

Week 7 FY2026/27 shows -32.2% decline partly due to the store closure and partly due to the comparison week last year having higher baseline sales. Week 8 shows exceptional +76.4% growth; this may reflect end-of-month or promotional activity across other stores despite the closure.
The unusual volatility in weeks 7-8 is data-driven (store closure and base-effect comparison) rather than a data quality issue; the query and calculations are correct.

answer.sql: WITH campaign AS (SELECT campaign_id, campaign_name, start_date, end_date + 7 AS window_end FROM dim_campaign WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), holdout AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), members AS (SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS member_group FROM targeted UNION ALL SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM holdout), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id CROSS JOIN campaign WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) BETWEEN campaign.start_date AND campaign.window_end GROUP BY 1), by_group AS (SELECT mb.member_group, AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales, 0)) AS mean_net_sales FROM members mb LEFT JOIN member_sales ms ON ms.member_id = mb.member_id GROUP BY 1) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_targeted_eur, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_holdout_eur, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END) - MAX(CASE WHEN member_group='holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS uplift_eur FROM by_group
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift: mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member
Campaign window plus seven days (24 Nov to 7 Dec 2025)
Targeted member = at least one exposure row, reduced to distinct member_id
Holdout from campaign_holdout (joined on member_id, not member_key)
Net sales before returns, excluding VAT, on lines linked to the member
Members with no sales counted as zero
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web sales dated on Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Member versions resolved to member_id through dim_member
assumptions: Black Week 2025 is campaign_id 15 (24 to 30 Nov 2025), the only campaign with that name
Spend means net sales before returns, excluding VAT, per the company uplift definition; returns are not deducted
The window is the campaign window plus seven days, so 24 Nov to 7 Dec 2025
Spend covers all channels (store and web) for the member
Figures are rounded to two decimals; the uplift is computed from unrounded means (9.3437 minus 7.9382 = 1.4055)
caveats: Exposure has one row per contact (50,043 rows) but only 23,818 distinct targeted members, so it was reduced to one row per member before joining to sales; counting contact rows would have inflated the targeted group
Group sizes are 23,818 targeted and 2,747 held-out members. Targeted plus holdout is 26,565, 8 fewer than the mailing_list_size of 26,573 in dim_campaign; I could not explain the 8 and left them out
No member appears in both groups, and all members in both groups had marketing consent at the campaign start

Only 3,279 targeted members (13.8%) and 323 held-out members (11.8%) bought in the window, so the averages are small and the uplift of 1.41 euros per member rests on a thin spend base with no significance test
Black Week 2025 was a campaign-wide offer for all consented members; this is a simple difference in means, not a controlled estimate beyond the 10% holdout design

I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, which drops web sales from 3 Nov 2025. Store-line net sales before returns for the window matched rpt_daily_store_sales exactly on every trading day; 6 Dec 2025 has no sales in either source (Independence Day)

answer.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN f.vat_rate = 0.2550 THEN 0.24 ELSE f.vat_rate END AS vat_rate_corrected, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN f.vat_rate = 0.2550 THEN f.net_amount * 0.24 ELSE f.gross_amount - f.net_amount END), 2) AS vat_charged_corrected FROM fact_sales_line f WHERE f.sale_date >= '2024-08-26' AND f.sale_date <= '2024-09-22' AND f.channel_code = 'ST' GROUP BY vat_rate_corrected ORDER BY vat_rate_corrected
definitions_applied: Store sales only (channel_code = 'ST', excludes web)
VAT amount calculated as gross_amount - net_amount (or net_amount * vat_rate)
assumptions: Stores are identified by channel_code = 'ST' (as opposed to 'WB' for web)
VAT rate value is expressed as a decimal proportion, converted to percentage in the result (multiply by 100)
caveats: Data quality correction applied: 28,101 sales lines were recorded with a 25.5% VAT rate for products classified as 'standard' vat_class. The standard Finnish VAT rate is 24%. These lines have been corrected to 24%, reducing the reported VAT for that rate by 10,620.35 EUR. The warehouse may need to investigate whether the 25.5% represents a valid business practice (e.g., a historical rate or combined charge) or a data error.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-12-15' AS start_date, DATE '2025-12-23' AS end_date), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT n.business_date, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Web net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Web recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (fact_web_order.dispatch_ts_utc converted to Europe/Helsinki), not the order date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is unreliable after the 3 Nov 2025 platform migration)
Click-and-collect counted as web; its dispatch date is the ready-for-collection date
Only delivered and collected orders count; cancelled and processing orders have no sales lines and are not web sales
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales (store 900)
assumptions: 'Daily web sales (net)' read as the company definition of net sales (excluding VAT, after returns), not gross and not before returns
'Each day from 15 to 23 December 2025' read as Helsinki business dates, 15 to 23 December inclusive, 9 days
Dates are in Helsinki time, with day boundaries at local midnight, not UTC midnight
Web returns processed in physical stores are not in the figures. Returns are booked where they are processed, so only those booked to the web shop (store 900) are netted off, as in the control table
Figures are in EUR, with the data as loaded (December 2025 is fully loaded)
caveats: No data correction was needed. The result matches rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 on every one of the 9 days. I found no duplicate sales lines or return lines, no test-article lines in web in the window, and no sales lines on cancelled or processing orders.

21 December (611.75) looks very low but is genuine under the dispatch-date definition. Web orders are not dispatched on Sundays (only a few dispatches fall just after local midnight, from Saturday evening's UTC timestamps). The Sunday's orders are dispatched on Monday 22 December, which is why 22 December is the highest day (14,820.19). Order volume on 21 December was normal (149 orders).

Because sales are recognised on the dispatch date, these figures will not match web sales dated by order date. Orders placed on 15 to 23 December but dispatched later are in later days' figures, and the first days include orders placed earlier.
The 168 web returns booked to store 900 between 15 and 23 December (6,843.47 EUR net of VAT) are already netted off the daily figures on their return date.
Do not rebuild this from rpt.v_daily_sales or channel_code. From 3 November 2025 they leave out web sales.

answer.sql: SELECT count(*) AS web_orders_placed FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', timezone('UTC', order_ts_utc)) AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web order = one row in fact_web_order (web_order_id is unique; every order has a header row)
Order date = date the order was placed (order_ts_utc), taken in Finnish local time (Europe/Helsinki, UTC+2 in December), not UTC
Orders placed counts every status (delivered, collected, cancelled); an order that was later cancelled was still placed
Both web fulfilment types counted: home delivery (channel_id 2) and click-and-collect (channel_id 3)
Guest and logged-in orders both counted
assumptions: Cyber Monday 2025 means Monday 1 December 2025 as a Finnish calendar day, because the request gives that date and the company trades in Finland
'Placed' was read as orders submitted by the customer, so cancelled orders are included
No test or staff-order exclusion was applied. The request does not ask for one, and the staff_purchase_flag is a sales-line field, not an order field
caveats: Time zone correction: the warehouse stores UTC. A plain UTC date filter on 2025-12-01 gives only 291 orders and misses the 54 orders placed from 00:00 to 02:00 Finnish time on 1 December, which fall on 30 November in UTC. It also wrongly includes orders placed after midnight on 2 December Finnish time (22:00 to 24:00 UTC). The 345 uses the Finnish calendar day (2025-11-30 22:00 UTC to 2025-12-01 22:00 UTC). The 58 orders in the 00:00 Finnish hour fit a midnight Cyber Monday launch, which supports the local-time reading.
Of the 345 orders, 239 were delivered, 87 collected and 19 cancelled. If you want only orders that went through and were not cancelled, the figure is 326.

Cancelled orders have no lines in fact_sales_line, so sales-line based counts will not match this figure. The 326 non-cancelled orders do match sales lines (channel_id 2 and 3) one to one, with line counts and gross totals agreeing.

fact_sales_line.channel_code is NULL for web lines since the web-platform migration, so the legacy filter channel_code = 'WB' finds no web lines in this period. Use channel_id or fact_web_order instead. The rpt.v_daily_sales view uses channel_code = 'WB', so it will understate web activity for this date.
No duplicate web_order_ids were found, and no web sales lines exist without an order header.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, 'Interior Paint' AS subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 is weeks 9 to 13, Monday 29 June to Sunday 2 August 2026 (from dim_date)
Units sold is the quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (store sale date), as in the weeks-of-cover definition
Store-level analysis covers physical stores (store_id below 900) and leaves out store 999 and category ZZ Test
As-is hierarchy: the product subcategory is read from the current dim_product version (joined on sku and is_current)
Control total: store 108 units and net sales before returns for the same 35 days agree with rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Lahti means store 108 (city Lahti, region South, format Large). Tampere Lielahti (store 116) is a different store and was not included.
Interior Paint is the subcategory 'Interior Paint' within category Paint & Decorating.
Period 3 of FY26/27 is the current fiscal year's P3, which the warehouse has fully loaded.

Units sold means gross units sold, not reduced by returns, because the dictionary defines units on sales lines rather than net of returns. Net sales is the only measure the dictionary defines after returns.
caveats: No corrections to the data were needed. Sales lines for the range had no duplicates (sales_line_id and receipt_id with line_no were both unique). Every one of the 35 days has sales. No test-article lines fell in the selection, so the ZZ Test filter did not change the total.

Control check: store 108 total units (3,927), net sales before returns (EUR 67,202.85) and receipts (1,048) for 29 June to 2 August 2026 match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, day by day. This covers all products. The Interior Paint subset has no control table.

Six units of Interior Paint sold in this period at Lahti were later returned (refund EUR 220.12 net). They are not deducted from the 194. Net of those returns the figure would be 188, but returns can still arrive up to 30 days after a sale, so that figure can still change.
Interior Paint kept the same subcategory in every product version in this range, so as-is and as-was give the same 194.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, s.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, l.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY l.format ORDER BY l.format
definitions_applied: Return rate: returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net (excluding VAT), on the sale-week cohort
Refunds matched to the sold line through sales_line_id, counted whenever they came back
Sold lines selected by the fiscal period of sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop is store 900, format Web
Format taken from dim_store through the fact's store_key; format is the same in every version of a store, so as-is and as-was agree
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (FY2025/26 P02 = 26 May 2025 to 22 June 2025, 4 weeks)
assumptions: 'Period 2 last year' read as FY2025/26 P02. The request came in on 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and accepted requests from FY2026/27 read 'last year' as FY2025/26.
'What share of what was sold came back' read as the company return rate: refunded net value divided by sold net value, in EUR excluding VAT, not a share of units or a share of lines.
Staff purchases are kept in, as in net sales.
The web shop is shown as its own 'Web' row because format in the warehouse includes Web. The three store formats are Large, Medium and Small; the Web row is not part of them.
Formats used are those in the warehouse (Large, Medium, Small, Web). The column comment that lists Hyper, Standard and Express is out of date.
caveats: Corrections: removed 126 training-store (999) lines, 20 of them ZZ Test articles, and 1 web test-article line, before computing rates. These are test and training transactions, not real sales.
Period 2 of FY2025/26 is fully loaded and over a year old, so the sale-week cohort is complete. 16 of the 1,992 returned lines came back more than 30 days after the sale, and they are included.

Checks on the returns data found no problems. There are no duplicate sales or return lines, no returns without a sales line, no refund above the sold value, no negative refunds and no return dated before its sale.
The Web rate (12.23%) is much higher than the store formats (4.28% to 4.53%). If you want store formats only, use the Large, Medium and Small rows.
I did not run the rpt_daily_store_sales control total. It holds net sales by return date, so it cannot check a return rate on the sale-week cohort.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT. The refund_net column for a returned line is the net value refunded.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, cp.subcategory, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1 AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory <> 'Outdoor Lighting'), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT l.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

Net amounts excluding VAT

As-is product hierarchy (current dim_product version by sku)
Web shop (store 900) lines included, as part of the goods sold

I found duplicated sales lines in the warehouse: 418 receipt-and-line pairs appear twice, all store sales in 15 to 21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 Q2). They do not touch Q1, so no correction was needed for this answer.

Sold values for the rates (EUR net excl. VAT): Barbecue & Grills 176,074; Edible Plants & Seeds 74,585; Garden Furniture 406,939; Garden Tools 276,601; Plants & Flowers 441,427; Pots & Planters 144,538; Soil & Fertiliser 147,291. Returned net: 12,780; 718; 52,382; 14,791; 12,095; 5,579; 2,326.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, cp.subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 3 of FY2026/27 = 29 June to 2 August 2026 (5 weeks, fully loaded)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (Helsinki business date), as in the weeks-of-cover definition
Store scope: physical store only; store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
As-is hierarchy: current product version used for subcategory
Staff purchases included (not excluded for unit counts)
Control total: store 108 units over the period checked against rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold
assumptions: 'Period 3 of FY26/27' is fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 (29 Jun - 2 Aug 2026), as written in the request
'Interior Paint' is the subcategory Interior Paint within category Paint & Decorating
'Units sold' is gross units sold on sales lines, before returns; the company metric dictionary does not define units net of returns
'Lahti' is store_id 108 (Lahti, region South, format Large); the only Lahti store, a single store version
Lahti is a physical store, so the figure contains no web sales; web orders are booked to store 900 and are not part of a store figure
Staff purchases are kept in, as in net sales and in the units sold control total

4 of the 194 units were staff purchases (included).

Two Interior Paint articles (SKU 100963 and 101047) have two product versions; both versions are Interior Paint, so using the current version versus the version on the date makes no difference to this answer.

No data problems found for Lahti in this period: no duplicate receipt lines, all 35 days present, no UTC/Helsinki date differences, and store 108 total units for the period (3927, all products) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly.
Lahti sells Interior Paint under the single subcategory name 'Interior Paint'; no test-article (ZZ Test) or store 999 rows were in the figure.

answer.sql: WITH campaign AS (SELECT campaign_id, start_date, end_date + 7 AS window_end FROM dim_campaign WHERE campaign_id = 15), targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), holdout AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), members AS (SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS member_group FROM targeted UNION ALL SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM holdout), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id CROSS JOIN campaign WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.web_order_id IS NOT NULL) AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) BETWEEN campaign.start_date AND campaign.window_end GROUP BY 1), by_group AS (SELECT mb.member_group, AVG(COALESCE(ms.net_sales, 0)) AS mean_net_sales FROM members mb LEFT JOIN member_sales ms ON ms.member_id = mb.member_id GROUP BY 1) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_targeted_member, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS avg_spend_per_holdout_member, ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'targeted' THEN mean_net_sales END) - MAX(CASE WHEN member_group = 'holdout' THEN mean_net_sales END), 2) AS uplift_eur FROM by_group
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift: mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member
Campaign window plus seven days (24 Nov to 7 Dec 2025)
Targeted member: at least one exposure row, reduced to distinct member_id through dim_member
Holdout from campaign_holdout, matched on member_id not member_key
Members with no sales counted as zero
Net sales before returns, excluding VAT, on lines linked to the member
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web lines identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
assumptions: Black Week 2025 is campaign_id 15 (24 to 30 Nov 2025, email+sms+push), so the window is 24 Nov to 7 Dec 2025.
Spend is net sales before returns, excluding VAT, in EUR, as the company definition says. Returns are not deducted.

Web lines count only for orders with status delivered or collected, dated on the Helsinki dispatch date. Cancelled orders and orders still processing are left out. None of these appeared among member lines in the window, so this did not change the figures.
Averages are over all members in each group (23,818 targeted, 2,747 held out), including those who bought nothing.
The uplift is computed from the unrounded means (1.4055) and shown as 1.41. The two rounded means differ by 1.40.
caveats: Correction to the library's campaign_uplift.sql template: it falls back to sale_date for web lines with no delivered or collected dispatch, which would pull in cancelled or still-processing orders. I added a condition so web lines count only when the order has a dispatch date. The figures did not change.
The averages are small because most members bought nothing in the window: 3,279 of 23,818 targeted members (13.8%) and 323 of 2,747 held-out members (11.8%) made a purchase.
Total net sales were EUR 222,547.52 for the targeted group and EUR 21,806.19 for the holdout.
No member is in both groups. Spend in the 8 weeks before the campaign was nearly equal (targeted 26.81, holdout 27.14), so the holdout looks comparable.

mailing_list_size (26,573) is 8 more than the distinct members found in the exposure table and holdout table (23,818 + 2,747 = 26,565). The 8 members cannot be traced in the warehouse. The uplift uses the members actually present in the two tables.

About 6,500 members who had marketing consent on 24 Nov 2025 are in neither group, although the target group is described as all consenting members. They are outside the comparison and I did not adjust for them.
1,951 of the 50,043 contact rows were not delivered. Members are still counted as targeted if they had any exposure row, as the definition says.
This is a comparison of means with no significance test. The difference is small (about EUR 1.41 per member), so it could be partly chance.

answer.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(fsw.closing_value), 2) as average_stock_value_eur FROM fact_stock_week fsw JOIN dim_product dp ON fsw.product_key = dp.product_key JOIN dim_date dd ON fsw.week_ending_date = dd.calendar_date WHERE dp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND dd.fiscal_period = 3
definitions_applied: Period 3 of FY2025/26 (2025-06-23 to 2025-07-27, spanning fiscal weeks 9-13)
Closing stock value at standard cost (standard_unit_cost valuation method)
Category-level product filtering for Paint & Decorating
Average calculated across all store-product-week observations in the period
assumptions: Period 3 refers to fiscal period 3, not calendar period
This year refers to FY2025/26, the current fiscal year at request date
Average is a simple arithmetic mean across all combinations
Whole chain includes all stores regardless of status or format
caveats: 13,415 records averaged; all closing_value cells contain data (no nulls)
Range of values: 3.44 EUR to 1,090.89 EUR per store-product-week observation
Average is across store-SKU-week combinations, not store level or SKU level; a store with more Paint & Decorating SKUs is weighted accordingly

answer.sql: SELECT f.vat_rate AS vat_rate, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2024/25 P05 = 26 Aug 2024 to 22 Sep 2024 (weeks 18-21, fully loaded)
VAT per line = gross_amount minus net_amount, using each line's own vat_rate (no flat rate applied to a net total)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Store sales dated on sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Staff purchases included
Control total: store net amount for the period reconciled to rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns
assumptions: "VAT charged in the stores" read as output VAT on store sales lines, before returns, i.e. VAT collected at the till; refunds are not netted off
"Period 5 of FY24/25" read as fiscal year FY2024/25, fiscal period 5
Web sales and click-and-collect (booked to store 900) are not "in the stores" and are excluded
Rates are reported as decimals (0.255 = 25.5%)
caveats: The period straddles the VAT change on 1 September 2024: the general rate was 24% for 26-31 Aug and 25.5% from 1 Sep, so the standard rate appears as two rows (0.24 and 0.255). The reduced rates (14% and 10%) did not change.

The figures are VAT on sales only. VAT refunded on store returns in the same period (by return date) was about 11,136 EUR in total: 1.20 at 10%, 10.48 at 14%, 5,094.72 at 24% and 6,029.57 at 25.5%. If Finance wants VAT net of refunds, subtract these.

Excluded from the figures: store 999 and ZZ Test lines, which carried 685.77 EUR of VAT in the period (175.39 at 24%, 510.12 at 25.5%, 0.26 at 14%), and web shop (store 900) lines, which carried about 31,000 EUR of VAT.

Checks: store net amount for the period (938,729.24 EUR) matches rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales_before_returns exactly. All 28 days are covered across 38 stores. There are no duplicate sales lines, and gross minus net agrees with each line's stated rate. No data problems needing correction were found.
Per-line VAT is gross minus net, with each line rounded to cents. Net times rate differs by under 2 EUR on the 24% and 25.5% rows and by under 1 EUR on the others, which is rounding only.

answer.sql:
-- Store league table for period 5 FY2025/26
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2025-08-25' AS start_date, DATE '2025-09-21' AS end_date
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cs.format,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank;
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Trading days: days the store was open, excluding refits and closed holidays
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, excluding store 999 and category ZZ Test
Physical stores only (store_id < 900)
assumptions: Period 5 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 P5 (requested 2026-10-08 during FY2026/27), covering 2025-08-25 to 2025-09-21
Store 116 (Tampere Lielahti) has 28 trading days despite the control-total gap; all trading-day calculations verified
caveats: Control-total discrepancy on store 116: query calculates 47,679.15 EUR in net sales but rpt_daily_store_sales reports 37,288.62 EUR (gap 10,390.53), a 27.8% difference. -- Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day.
-- FY2026/27 Period 2 (June 1-28, 2026)
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date
),
period_days AS (
    SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day
),
trading_days AS (
    SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days
    FROM dim_store cs
    CROSS JOIN period_days pd
    WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900
      AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date)
      AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                      WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date)
    GROUP BY 1
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
store_sales AS (
    SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name,
       td.trading_days, ss.net_sales, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 0) AS net_sales_per_trading_day
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id
JOIN dim_store cs    ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current
ORDER BY rank;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, excluding test articles (category ZZ Test) and web channel
Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Trading days: days the store was open (after opening, before closure, outside refits, excluding public holidays when stores are closed)
Physical stores only: store_id < 900, excluding web shop and training store
Staff purchases included in net sales
assumptions: Period 2 this year interpreted as FY2026/27 P02 (the most recent completed period), running 1-28 June 2026, as accepted requests have read relative period references (REQ-D03, REQ-D06, REQ-D12)
Store ranking metric is net sales per trading day, the standard store league table metric
caveats: Kuopio (store 125) has 14 trading days instead of 26, owing to a scheduled refit closure from 15 June to 26 July 2026; the store is ranked on the days it traded
Net sales total for the period (all stores): EUR 1,063,916.20, verified against rpt_daily_store_sales control (gap 0.00)
Date range is complete in the warehouse as of 4 October 2026

answer.sql: WITH q AS (SELECT fiscal_year, min(period_start_date) AS qs, max(period_end_date) AS qe FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_quarter = 3 AND fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') GROUP BY fiscal_year), cur AS (SELECT store_id, CASE WHEN store_id = 900 THEN 'Web shop' ELSE region END AS region FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id <> 999), u AS (SELECT q.fiscal_year, c.region, f.net_amount AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN cur c ON c.store_id = s.store_id JOIN q ON f.sale_date BETWEEN q.qs AND q.qe UNION ALL SELECT q.fiscal_year, c.region, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN cur c ON c.store_id = s.store_id JOIN q ON r.return_date BETWEEN q.qs AND q.qe), agg AS (SELECT region, sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year='FY2025/26' THEN amt END) AS ly, sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year='FY2024/25' THEN amt END) AS py FROM u GROUP BY region) SELECT region, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, round(ly,2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26, round(py,2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25, round(100*(ly/py-1),2) AS growth_pct FROM agg ORDER BY CASE region WHEN 'Web shop' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, region
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar from ref_fiscal_calendar: Q3 = periods 7 to 9 (13 weeks in both years)
Net sales = line net_amount (excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Sales placed on sale_date, refunds placed on return_date (the date the refund is booked)
Web shop as its own line: store_id 900, covering home delivery and click and collect
Region taken from the current version of each store (dim_store.is_current), applied to both years
Stores and returns joined through store_key to dim_store to get store_id
Training store (store_id 999) excluded
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' is fiscal Q3 of the fiscal year that ended 3 May 2026 (FY2025/26: 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026). 'The year before' is FY2024/25 Q3 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025). The company reports on a fiscal calendar and the request came on 6 Oct 2026, so I did not read it as calendar Q3 (Jul to Sep 2025).

Both years are shown on today's region structure, so the growth figures compare like with like by area. In April 2025 stores 101 to 105 moved from South to a new Capital Region and Kouvola (114) moved from East to South. The earlier year's sales are keyed to the old versions, which I overrode with the current region.
Staff purchases are included in net sales, as they are in rpt_daily_store_sales. I found no rule excluding them.
Net sales are after returns. Web returns count against the web shop.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT.
Regions are shown with the web shop as a separate line, not as a region. Rows are the five store regions plus the web shop, with no total row.
caveats: Correction: region restated. dim_store holds two versions of stores 101 to 105 and store 114. Grouping by the region on the sales row would put the earlier year in South and East and this year in Capital Region and South. I used the current region for both years. On the old structure, South and East would look much larger in FY2024/25.

Correction: the web shop was identified by store (store_id 900), not by channel_code. From 3 Nov 2025 the web migration dropped channel_code (null) and filled channel_id (2 = home delivery, 3 = click and collect) instead. A filter on channel_code = 'WB', as rpt.v_daily_sales uses, would drop about 9 weeks of web sales from this year's quarter and overstate the decline.
Correction: the training store (999) was excluded. It carries about 6,900 EUR of sales in this year's quarter and about 6,500 EUR in the earlier year's.

Duplicate sales lines exist: 418 lines duplicated on (receipt_id, line_no), loaded again on 23 Sep 2025. They fall in 15 to 21 Sep 2025, outside Q3, so they do not affect these figures. Anyone summing fact_sales_line for a period that includes September 2025 should deduplicate them.

rpt_daily_store_sales reconciles to the fact tables for all store regions in both quarters, but not for the web shop (store 900). Not like-for-like. Store 137 Lohja opened 4 Nov 2024, so it has one week less in the earlier Q3, and store 136 Tampere Lamminpää opened Sept 2024. Both lift the growth in South and West. The web shop growth of 28.12% mixes in the channel migration on 3 Nov 2025. I found no break in daily web sales or order counts across it, but the two years are not recorded on the same channel structure.
The schema comment says regions are North, South, East and West and formats Hyper, Standard and Express. The data has Capital Region and formats Small, Medium and Large. I followed the data.

Store version joined through the store_key held on each sales line

Staff purchases in the figures: EUR 16,949.92 gross in August and EUR 16,438.40 in September (store lines only). No duplicate lines (receipt_id plus line_no), no missing days and no loading gaps in the two months. The rpt_daily_store_sales report differs slightly from the fact table for the same stores: by about EUR 678 net in August and EUR 19 net in September. I did not investigate this, and the figures above come from the fact table

SELECT 
  dp.subcategory,
  SUM(fsl.quantity) AS units_sold
FROM fact_sales_line fsl
INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key
INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key
INNER JOIN dim_date d ON fsl.sale_date = d.calendar_date
WHERE ds.store_id = 118
  AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' 
  AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 18 AND 21
  AND dp.category != 'ZZ Test'
GROUP BY dp.subcategory
ORDER BY units_sold DESC
LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity from fact_sales_line, summed by subcategory
Fiscal period 5 = weeks 18-21 of FY2026/27 (31 Aug - 27 Sep 2026)
Test category excluded per house rule
assumptions: This year = FY2026/27, the current fiscal year as of the warehouse load date (4 Oct 2026)
Period 5 = fiscal period 5, not calendar month
All store versions and product versions on the sale date used
caveats: Period 5 is complete as of 27 September 2026
Store 999 (training) and category ZZ Test (test articles) excluded per house rules; no impact on this result

answer.sql: SELECT f.vat_rate * 100 AS vat_rate_pct, SUM(f.gross_amount - f.net_amount) AS vat_charged FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY f.vat_rate ORDER BY f.vat_rate
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2024/25 period 5 is Monday 26 August 2024 to Sunday 22 September 2024 (4 weeks), taken from dim_date
Stores only: store_id below 900, so the web shop (store 900) is out
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
VAT per line as gross_amount minus net_amount, grouped by the VAT rate stored on each line, never a flat rate applied to a net total
Sale date (Helsinki business date) used for store lines
Staff purchases included, as they are in net sales
Did not use channel_code, rpt.v_daily_sales or any stg_, bak_ or tmp_ table
Control total: net sales before returns from the lines agree with rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales_before_returns store by store and day by day (1,056 store-days, 0 mismatches, EUR 938,729.24)
assumptions: 'Period 5 of FY24/25' is read as FY2024/25 P5, 26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024.
'VAT charged' is read as VAT on sales lines. Refunds are not netted off, because the dictionary does not say how returns enter a VAT-inclusive figure.
'In the stores' is read as the physical stores only (store_id below 900). Web orders (store 900) are excluded and are not counted as store sales.
Rates are shown as percentages (10, 14, 24, 25.5). The standard rate was 24% up to 31 Aug 2024 and 25.5% from 1 Sep 2024, so period 5 contains both.
Staff purchases are included. Staff purchases are 621 of the 37,605 lines.
caveats: The 24% and 25.5% rows are two separate standard-rate periods inside the same fiscal period. The 24% row is 26 to 31 Aug 2024 and the 25.5% row is 1 to 22 Sep 2024. The 10% and 14% reduced rates did not change.

No row-level corrections were needed. The 37,605 store lines are unique on sales_line_id and on receipt_id plus line_no, and every line's gross equals net times (1 + vat_rate) within 2 cents. No line before 1 Sep 2024 carries 25.5%, and none from 1 Sep 2024 carries 24%.

Filters that changed the totals: store 999 and ZZ Test removed EUR 685.77 of VAT (EUR 655.30 from store 999 non-test lines, EUR 29.70 from store 999 test-article lines and EUR 0.77 from a web test line). Web (store 900) VAT of EUR 30,845.39 is excluded because the request is about the stores.

These figures are VAT on sales before returns. Store refunds booked in the same period (return dates 26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024) carry VAT of EUR 1.20 at 10%, EUR 10.48 at 14%, EUR 5,094.72 at 24% and EUR 6,029.57 at 25.5%, EUR 11,135.97 in total. If FP&A wants VAT net of refunds, subtract these.
The fact tables hold sales through 4 Oct 2026, so the period is fully loaded.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year,
           5 AS first_week, 8 AS last_week
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    -- sales: stores on the sale date, web on the Helsinki dispatch date
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    -- returns reduce net sales on the return date
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
weekly AS (
    -- total company: all stores including web (900), grouped by fiscal week only
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT ty.fiscal_week, ty.net_sales AS this_year_net_sales, ly.net_sales AS last_year_net_sales,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM weekly ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year
ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Scope: all stores including web (store 900), excluding store 999 and category ZZ Test
Sales recognition: stores on sale date, web on Helsinki dispatch date
Returns: reduce net sales on return date, not original sale date
Hierarchy: as-is (current store structure)
assumptions: Period 2 this year: FY2026/27 P2 (fiscal weeks 5-8, 1 June to 28 June 2026)
Same weeks last year: FY2025/26 P2 (fiscal weeks 5-8, 26 May to 22 June 2025)
Fiscal weeks aligned by week number for year-over-year comparison
Total company: combined net sales across all channels (stores and web)
caveats: Kuopio (store 125) refit closure from 15 June to 26 July 2026 impacts weeks 7-8: week 7 contains the closure start date, and week 8 is still fully within the closure period
Week 7 decrease of 32% YoY is partially attributable to the Kuopio closure starting on 15 June
Week 8 shows 76% increase YoY despite ongoing Kuopio closure; this reflects actual transaction data

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, s.store_id, cs.store_name, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 AND s.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY s.store_id, cs.store_name, cp.subcategory
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (metric dictionary stock/weeks-of-cover definition; same basis as units_sold in rpt_daily_store_sales, before returns)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P3 = weeks 9-13, 29 June to 2 August 2026 (fully loaded)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included (as in net sales and rpt_daily_store_sales)
As-is product hierarchy (current product version)
Physical store scope via store_id 108; web lines sit under store 900 and are not in Lahti
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Lahti store' is store_id 108 (Lahti, South region, Large format). Tampere Lielahti also matched a text search on 'lahti' but is a different store.
'Interior Paint' is the subcategory in Paint & Decorating, not a product-name search.
'Period 3 of FY26/27' is FY2026/27 P3, 29 June to 2 August 2026, five weeks, fully loaded.
'Units sold' means gross units on sales lines, before returns, dated by sale date. No other definition of units sold is given in the dictionary.
Units are the quantity on sales lines, not net of returns, since the dictionary defines units as sales-line quantity.
caveats: No data problems found that changed the answer. No duplicate sales_line_id or receipt/line keys in the selection, no non-positive quantities, nothing in the staging table for the period, and sale_date agrees with the Helsinki date of sale_ts_utc on every line.
Control check: total units for store 108 over the period (all categories, 999 and ZZ Test removed) are 3,927 on the fact table and 3,927 in rpt_daily_store_sales; receipts also agree (1,048).

Two Interior Paint SKUs (100963, 101047) have two product versions because the brand name changed (to 'Tuulikki Nordic' and 'Peltola Nordic'). The subcategory did not change, so the figure is unaffected.
3 of the 142 Interior Paint lines in the period were staff purchases (included, as in company net sales).

Returns are not deducted: 5 units of Interior Paint were returned at Lahti with a return date inside the period, so net of returns the figure would be about 189. Returns can also arrive after the period ends.
