answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = fs.week_ending_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS average_closing_stock_value_at_cost FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot (week-ending Sunday), valued at standard cost (closing_value)
Semi-additive stock: sum across stores and products within each week first, then average across weeks, never sum across weeks
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 is weeks 9 to 13 (29 June to 2 August 2026), five week-ending Sundays (5, 12, 19, 26 July and 2 August 2026)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop (900) and training store (999) are excluded, and web has no stock in this table anyway
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded; none fall in Paint & Decorating
As-is product category: the current version of each article (dim_product on sku and is_current) decides whether it is Paint & Decorating
Only ranged articles are in fact_stock_week, so the figure covers the stock the stores actually carry
assumptions: 'Average stock' is read as the average of the five weekly closing stock values in the period, not the last week's closing
'Period 3 this year' is read as FY2026/27 P3, the current fiscal year as of the request date of 8 October 2026. It is complete and fully loaded
'Value at cost' is read as the warehouse's closing_value, which is stock at standard cost
'Whole chain' is read as all 38 physical stores that carry stock, with the web shop excluded because it holds no stock here
Paint & Decorating is read as the category of that name, not the separate category Home Textiles & Decor
caveats: No corrections were needed. The five weeks of Paint & Decorating stock had no duplicate store, article and week rows, no negative or null values, and closing_value matched units times standard unit cost exactly
The category was the same on the sale-date version and the current version of every article, so as-is and as-was give the same answer
The weekly chain totals were 341,138.89; 341,742.53; 344,245.91; 349,160.39; and 346,046.42 EUR. The average is a mean of these five

The range is 358 to 361 articles across 38 stores. Article count dropped from 361 to 358 after the first week of the period (2,699 store-article rows to 2,674) as ranging changed, so the figure covers whatever was ranged each week
The figure is stock at standard cost, which is revalued each April, so it is not a retail value and not a purchase-price value, and it excludes VAT

WITH web_dispatch AS (

net_lines AS (

    FROM fact_sales_line f

Returns dated on their own return date, not the original sale date

answer.sql: SELECT cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' GROUP BY cp.subcategory ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 P05, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (fiscal weeks 18 to 21, all four weeks loaded)
Units sold: sum of quantity on sales lines by Helsinki sale_date, before returns (the same basis as units_sold in rpt_daily_store_sales)
Store scope: Nokia is store_id 118 (a single store version, West region, Medium format); store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded, and neither changed the figures
As-is hierarchy: subcategory taken from the current product version
Staff purchases included (34 units at Nokia in the period)
Control total: Nokia units for the period, 2245 from the sales lines, equal 2245 in rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Nokia' means the store named Nokia (store_id 118); it is the only store or city of that name
'Period 5 this year' means FY2026/27 P05, the current fiscal year and a completed period, not calendar May
'Units sold' means units on sales lines before returns. The metric dictionary does not define 'units sold', so I used the quantity-on-sales-lines basis its stock section and rpt_daily_store_sales use
Ranking is by units, not by sales value
Web orders collected at Nokia are not included, because web sales belong to the web shop (store 900)
caveats: Only first place is clear: Fixings & Fasteners sold 570 units, almost four times the next subcategory. Places 3 to 5 are close: Storage Boxes 139, Cleaning Products 136, Plants & Flowers 136.

If returns were netted off, by return date, Storage Boxes would fall to 130 and Cleaning Products (134) would take third place. The company definition for units sold does not net returns, so I did not.

No subcategory in the top 3 was affected by the October 2025 outdoor lighting move to Electrical or by the April 2025 region reorganisation.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount, cp.subcategory FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND cp.category = 'Garden' AND cp.subcategory <> 'Outdoor Lighting') SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_quarter, sold.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(sold.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON r.sales_line_id = sold.sales_line_id GROUP BY sold.subcategory ORDER BY sold.subcategory
definitions_applied: Return rate = refund_net divided by sold net_amount (both excluding VAT), as a sale-week cohort: sold lines selected by the fiscal quarter of fact_sales_line.sale_date, refunds matched through sales_line_id whenever and wherever they were booked
Net amounts excluding VAT; staff purchases included
As-is reporting: subcategory and category taken from the current product version (dim_product joined on sku and is_current)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 Q1 = fiscal weeks 1 to 13, 28 April 2025 to 27 July 2025
Stores and web shop (store 900) both included, as the request does not limit the channel
Outdoor lighting treated as Electrical for all history, per the 27 October 2025 reclassification rule
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 (the request is dated 6 October 2026), in line with the past requests from May 2026 onward
'Q1' read as fiscal Q1 (P1 to P3, weeks 1 to 13), not calendar Q1
'Garden' means the Garden category on the current (as-is) hierarchy, with no region or channel restriction
Web lines are dated by sale_date (the order date), as in the accepted return-rate queries D14 to D16; the dispatch-date rule applies to net sales, not to this sale-week cohort measure
Q1 sales were made more than 12 months ago, so the 30-day return window is complete and the cohort is final
caveats: Data correction: five outdoor lighting SKUs (100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) were delisted before the 27 October 2025 reclassification and never received an Electrical product version. Their current version still says Garden / Outdoor Lighting, which would put an 'Outdoor Lighting' row in the Garden breakdown. I excluded the whole Outdoor Lighting subcategory from Garden, as the as-is rule requires. This removes 19 FY2025/26 Q1 sales lines worth EUR 375.00 net with no returns; they have no effect on the other subcategories' rates.

Because of the as-is rule, outdoor lighting (about EUR 50,443 sold net in Q1, all 68 SKUs that were reclassified plus those 5) is not in Garden here. Counted as it was classified at the time (as-was), it would have been a Garden subcategory; the request did not ask for as-was.
Returns are matched to the original sale whenever they came back, so the rates are for the goods sold in Q1, not refunds booked in Q1.
Garden Furniture has by far the highest return rate (12.87%, EUR 52,382 refunded on EUR 406,939 sold); Edible Plants & Seeds is the lowest (0.96%).

The sold and refunded amounts behind each rate were checked at the line level (no duplicate sales lines or return lines, every return matches a sales line), but I did not run the rpt_daily_store_sales control total because this is a category subset, to which that check does not apply.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT web_order_id) AS web_orders_placed FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28'

Placed orders include every status (delivered, collected, cancelled), since a cancelled order was still placed
assumptions: 'Web orders placed' counts every order placed that day, including the 20 later cancelled
Both web channels are counted, home delivery and click-and-collect, because both are web orders in fact_web_order
Black Friday 2025 is 28 November 2025, as the request states
caveats: fact_sales_line.channel_code is NULL on the 2025 lines, so a filter on channel_code = 'WB' returns no web lines for this date. I counted from fact_web_order, which does not use that column. Where I used sales lines to cross-check, I filtered on channel_id (2 = home delivery, 3 = click and collect).

Of the 377 orders, 20 were cancelled, so 357 were not cancelled. Cancelled orders have no sales lines, so a count from sales lines would give 357 on the UTC day. If the carrier's report only covers orders that shipped, 357 is the comparable figure.

A count from sales lines by sale_date (the local date) gives 402 receipts, not 377. The sale_date column is the local Finnish date, so the late-evening UTC orders fall on a different local day. I used the UTC timestamp, as requested.
Order timestamps match the sales-line timestamps for every order checked (0 minutes difference), and there are no duplicate order ids, so I found no loading or duplication problem for this date.

answer.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_start_date, period_end_date FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period = 2) SELECT p.fiscal_year, p.fiscal_period, s.format AS store_format, ROUND(100 * SUM(r.refund_net) / SUM(f.net_amount), 2) AS returned_share_pct FROM p JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sale_date BETWEEN p.period_start_date AND p.period_end_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON r.sales_line_id = f.sales_line_id WHERE s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY p.fiscal_year, p.fiscal_period, s.format ORDER BY CASE s.format WHEN 'Small' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Large' THEN 3 END
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period dates taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2025/26 P02 = 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22)
Net sales: net_amount, EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts
Refunds: refund_net, EUR excluding VAT, linked to the original sales line through sales_line_id
Store format taken from dim_store through the sale's store_key, which carries the store version valid on the sale date
Stores are store_id below 900; the web shop (900) and the Training store (999) are pseudo-locations and are left out of the store formats
assumptions: 'Last year' is read against the request date of 2026-10-06. The current fiscal year is FY2026/27, so last year is FY2025/26 and period 2 is 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22.

'Share of what was sold that came back' is read as a cohort measure. The numerator is the value of refunds on lines sold in P2, whenever they were refunded. The denominator is the value of those P2 sales. All refunds are loaded: 411 of the 1,992 returned lines were refunded after 22 June 2025, and the latest return date is 2026-10-04.
The measure is value, net of VAT, matching how net sales are reported. A share by units would be slightly lower (about 2.4% in every store format).

Staff purchases are kept in both sold and returned amounts, as in rpt_daily_store_sales and rpt.v_daily_sales. Excluding them would change the shares by 0.01 to 0.03 points (Small 4.30, Medium 4.55, Large 4.45).
'Store format' means the physical store formats. The web shop's own format, Web, is not shown as a row; its figure is given in the caveats.
caveats: Correction: the Training store (store_id 999, 126 lines, EUR 2,222 net) is excluded. It is a test location and has no returns, so including it would only dilute the Large/Medium/Small figures.

Correction: the web shop (store_id 900) is excluded from the store formats because it is not a store. Web sales in P2 were EUR 183,102 net with EUR 22,388 refunded, a returned share of 12.23%. That is nearly three times the store rate and should be reported separately.
The schema comment for dim_store.format says 'Hyper, Standard or Express', but the data holds Small, Medium and Large (plus Web and Training). The labels in the data are used.
Regions were redrawn on 2025-04-28. I split by format, which did not change, so this did not affect the result.

Returns booked in the period against earlier sales are not counted, and returns on P2 sales booked after the period are. A report on returns booked in P2 (rpt_daily_store_sales.returns_net) would give different figures.
A refund made at a different store from the sale is attributed to the format of the store where the item was sold (102 of the 1,992 lines).

No duplicates, orphan returns, refunds above the sale value or VAT inconsistencies were found in the P2 sales and returns. The stg_* tables hold only loads dated 3-4 October 2026 and do not touch P2 2025, and the bak_*, *_old and tmp_* tables were not used.
The sales and returns data contain no formats other than Small, Medium and Large for the stores. The three store rates are within 0.25 points of each other, so the format differences are small.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders_placed FROM fact_web_order WHERE DATE(order_ts_utc) = '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Cyber Monday 2025 = 1 December 2025
Web orders = all rows in fact_web_order with order timestamp on that date
assumptions: Order timestamp is in UTC; the date filter uses the calendar date of the UTC timestamp
All statuses included: delivered, collected, processing, cancelled

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(f.gross_amount) AS web_sales_gross_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 4 AND 6 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales = sales lines with channel_code WB (web shop, store 900), including click-and-collect orders
Sales including VAT = gross_amount on fact_sales_line
Before returns = fact_return_line not deducted
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25 periods 4 to 6 (29 Jul 2024 to 27 Oct 2024)
Periods assigned by sale_date, which matches the Helsinki-local date of sale_ts_utc on every web line
Staff purchases excluded from web: none present on web lines, so no adjustment was needed
assumptions: Q2 of FY24/25 read as FY2024/25 fiscal periods 4, 5 and 6, as the request states
Web sales read as the web channel (channel_code WB), which covers both home delivery and click-and-collect orders
Cancelled web orders carry no sales lines, so they are not in the figures
Period 6 has five weeks (23 Sep to 27 Oct 2024), so it is higher than periods 4 and 5, which have four weeks each
caveats: No corrections were needed. Checked and found clean: no duplicate sales lines, no web rows missing from the fact table (staging has no extra rows), line gross equals net times (1 + VAT rate) on every line, and per-order line totals equal fact_web_order.order_total_gross for delivered and collected orders
VAT rates in the data change as they should: standard rate 24% up to 31 Aug 2024 and 25.5% from 1 Sep 2024, so period 4 and part of period 5 are at 24% and the rest at 25.5%
255 cancelled web orders (about EUR 18,047 order value) in the quarter have no sales lines and are not counted
Store 999 (Training store) has 472 store-channel lines in the quarter. They are not web sales and are excluded; they would matter only in a store sales figure
All three periods are marked fully_loaded in ref_fiscal_calendar

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 1) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 10 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect web net sales / all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (for click-and-collect, the ready-for-collection date), not the order date
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Cancelled and still-processing orders excluded from web sales (only delivered and collected orders with dispatch time)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, not channel_code or channel_id (neither works across the 3 Nov 2025 migration)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 P9 and P10
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, because the request was received 6 October 2026 in FY2026/27 and earlier accepted requests in FY2026/27 read 'last year' as FY2025/26
'Periods 9 and 10' read as fiscal periods P9 and P10 of FY2025/26 (22 Dec 2025 to 22 Feb 2026, fiscal weeks 35 to 43)
The request names two periods, so the answer gives one share per period, not a single combined figure
Refunds on web returns are attributed to the fulfilment type of the original order
Shares rounded to one decimal place
caveats: Both periods fall after the 3 Nov 2025 web platform migration, so channel_code and channel_id were not used to find web or click-and-collect; fulfilment_type was used instead. rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it omits web sales after the migration.
No data corrections were needed. The web lines are unique at (receipt_id, line_no), all sit in store 900, and every order has a fulfilment type.
The query's web net sales for P9 and P10 together (323,339.73 EUR: P9 200,208.58 and P10 123,131.15) match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 over the same 63 days, with a gap of 0.00.
Click-and-collect net was 58,536.07 EUR in P9 and 37,861.39 EUR in P10.
Net sales are ex-VAT. A share of web orders (counted on the order date) would be a different figure.

answer.sql: SELECT p.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY p.subcategory ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity from fact_sales_line (excludes returns)
Store identification by store_id (118 for Nokia)
Fiscal period calendar per ref_fiscal_calendar
assumptions: Nokia store = store_id 118, the only store with name/location Nokia in the warehouse
This year = current fiscal year FY2026/27 (today is in this fiscal year)
Period 5 = fiscal period 5 per the fiscal calendar
Units sold = transaction quantity from fact_sales_line, before any returns are applied
caveats: Warehouse data current to 2026-10-04 only; today is 2026-10-15
Period 5 (FY2026/27 P05) data is complete and period-ended (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27)
Result excludes returned units; uses gross sales lines only

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.web_order_id IS NOT NULL)) SELECT region, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024_gross_sales_incl_vat, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024_gross_sales_incl_vat FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines, so each line carries its own VAT rate
Before returns: fact_return_line is not netted off
As-was regions: the region of the store version on the transaction date, taken via fact_sales_line.store_key
Web sales on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered or collected orders count
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own region, Online
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Helsinki-time days; the UTC dispatch timestamp is converted to a Helsinki date
No deprecated tables or views used
assumptions: August and September 2024 are read as calendar months (1-31 August, 1-30 September 2024), not fiscal periods, because the figures are for a VAT filing.

'As they were at the time, as in the old reports' is read as as-was. The old reports had four regions (North, South, East, West); the Capital Region does not exist before 28 April 2025, so South still contains Helsinki Vuosaari, Pitäjänmäki, Espoo Lommila, Vantaa Tammisto and Kerava, and East still contains Kouvola.
Online (the web shop, store 900) is its own row because it belongs to no physical region. The request did not say whether to include it. Excluding it gives the physical-store figures only.

Web orders are placed in the month they are dispatched, following the company rule that web sales are recognised on dispatch. Click-and-collect orders count on the date they were ready for collection.
Figures are in EUR including VAT, rounded to cents as stored.
caveats: Correction: the library's gross_sales_incl_vat template falls back to the order date for web lines that have no delivered or collected order. I excluded those lines. None existed in Aug-Sep 2024 (no cancelled or processing web orders), so the totals are not affected, but the template needs fixing before it is used for later periods.
Correction: store 999 (training store) sales of 4,282.23 in August and 3,351.71 in September, and two test-article web lines (8.06 and 3.77), are excluded.

The VAT rate changed on 1 September 2024: the general rate went from 24% to 25.5%, while the 14% and 10% rates were unchanged. I summed each line's own gross_amount rather than applying a flat rate. I checked that every line's gross equals net x (1 + vat_rate), with no mismatches, in the two months.

Online uses the dispatch date, so it differs from an order-date basis. By order date, Online would be 174,402.41 for August and 160,391.86 for September. Physical regions are the same either way. If the filing follows the date of sale rather than dispatch, use these figures for Online.
The figures are before returns, as asked. Refunds booked in these months are not deducted, so they are not a net VAT base.
Control check: net sales before returns on the same basis matched rpt_daily_store_sales for every store and both months, including the web shop, with no differences above 0.50 EUR.
I found no duplicate sales lines in the period (sales_line_id and receipt_id with line_no are both unique).
dim_store.region's column comment still lists only four regions. That matches the as-was view for 2024, but it is out of date for current data.

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(r.quantity_returned) AS units_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE cp.subcategory = 'Garden Furniture' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 4 of FY2026/27 is fiscal weeks 14 to 17, Monday 3 August to Sunday 30 August 2026
Returns counted on their own return date (fact_return_line.return_date), not the date of the original sale
Units returned = quantity_returned summed over fact_return_line
Product hierarchy as-is: current product version (is_current) for subcategory
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no Garden Furniture return lines were affected)
Web returns are booked to the web shop (store 900) and are included, so the figure covers stores and web
assumptions: "This year" means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and "period 4" means fiscal period 4, which is fully loaded (the warehouse runs to 4 October 2026).
"Garden Furniture" means the subcategory Garden Furniture (category Garden, 87 articles). I did not read it as the Furniture category or as all of Garden.

"Handed back and booked as returned" is read as units on return lines dated in the period (the booking date), not as a return rate against that period's sales and not as units sold in P4 that later came back.
All channels are included: 58 units returned in 24 physical stores and 34 through the web shop.
The figure is gross units returned, with no netting off of exchanges or resales.
caveats: No data problems needed correcting. The 92 return lines have distinct return_line_id and sales_line_id values, every one matches an original sales line and a product, no return exceeds the quantity sold, none is dated before its sale, and the stored return_date matches the Helsinki date of the UTC timestamp on every row.
Two Garden Furniture articles (SKUs 100527 and 100583) have an older product version, but both versions are Garden Furniture, so the as-is and as-was readings give the same answer.
Some of the 92 units come from sales made before 3 August, as early as 17 July 2026, because a return counts on the date it was booked.
The query-check script only warned about the store 999 filter on sales lines. This query uses return lines only, and none of the returns were booked to store 999.

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT sum(f.net_amount) AS v FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30' AND s.store_id <> 999), rets AS (SELECT sum(r.refund_net) AS v FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30' AND s.store_id <> 999) SELECT round(sales.v - rets.v, 2) AS net_sales_eur FROM sales, rets
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns
Returns counted in the month they were booked (return_date), not the month of the original sale
Company-wide = all physical stores plus the web shop (store_id 900), home delivery and click-and-collect both included
Sale date taken from sale_date, which is the local Finnish date and matches the business date
Fact tables used directly, joined to dim_store through store_key
Calculation follows the rpt_daily_store_sales logic: net sales = net sales before returns minus returns, excluding VAT
assumptions: 'Last month' read as calendar September 2026, 1 to 30 September, since the request is dated 9 October 2026 and September is fully loaded (latest sale loaded 4 October)
Staff purchases are included, as in the Data & Analytics daily store sales report. They are real sales, EUR 13,499.45 net in September excluding the training store
'Whole company' includes the online channel
Net means excluding VAT, as net_amount and refund_net are defined in the warehouse
caveats: Training store (store_id 999) removed: EUR 3,084.66 of September sales lines (63 receipts, of which EUR 2,957.51 flagged as staff purchases) are training or test transactions, not trading. It has no returns.

Do not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales for a company figure. They identify web sales through channel_code = 'WB', but channel_code is NULL on current rows (the web platform migration moved to channel_id), so web sales drop out of those views, and the store half of the views would also pick up the training store.

rpt_daily_store_sales gives EUR 1,179,035.98 for September, EUR 4,422.88 more than this figure. The whole difference is the web shop: the report shows EUR 209,990.40 of web sales before returns against EUR 205,567.52 in the sales fact table (3,544 receipts against 3,475), so I used the fact tables for it. Store figures in the report match the fact tables exactly.
If 'last month' means the company's fiscal period instead, FY2026/27 period 5 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026) net sales are EUR 1,107,414.30. Period 6 (from 28 Sep) is not fully loaded.
Returns of EUR 74,262.24 (2,051 lines, 428 of them web, EUR 19,546.58) are deducted. Some will relate to sales made in August or earlier.
Excluding staff purchases would lower the figure by EUR 13,499.45 sales net of EUR 768.22 of staff-purchase refunds, if the team prefers that definition.

Other checks found no problems for September: no duplicate sales or return lines, no store or day missing sales, no orphan store keys, no cancelled or processing web orders with sales lines, and net and gross amounts agree with VAT on every line.

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT s.format, f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-05-26' AND DATE '2025-06-22' AND f.channel_code = 'ST' AND s.store_id < 900) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, sold.format AS store_format, round(100 * coalesce(sum(r.refund_net), 0) / sum(sold.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON r.sales_line_id = sold.sales_line_id GROUP BY sold.format ORDER BY CASE sold.format WHEN 'Large' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 2 of FY2025/26 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar: 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22 (4 weeks, fully loaded)

Goods sold in the period: sales lines with sale_date in the period, so returns are attributed to the period of the original sale whatever their own return date (returns on these lines run to 2025-07-23)
Return rate = refund_net divided by net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, value basis), linking each return to its sales line through sales_line_id
Store format taken from dim_store through the sales line's store_key (the store version valid at the sale date), as fact_sales_line defines it
Store sales only: channel_code ST and store_id below 900, the same store filter as rpt.v_daily_sales
Returns counted on fact_return_line only (no duplicates found: one return row per sales line)
Staff purchases kept in, as in rpt_daily_store_sales, whose gross sales for P2 match the store totals including staff purchases
assumptions: Last year means the last completed fiscal year before the request date of 2026-10-05, so FY2025/26. The current year is FY2026/27, and period 2 is the fiscal period (2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22), not calendar month 2.

Return rate is read as the value of refunds against the value of net sales, both excluding VAT. A unit-based rate would be lower, about 2.4% in each format (Large 2.37, Medium 2.44, Small 2.39), because returned lines are worth more per unit than the average sold line.

By store format means physical stores only, so the web shop (format Web, store 900) and the Training store (999) are left out. The web shop is a channel, not a store format, and would be a fourth row at roughly 12.2% on the same basis if Commercial wants it.
Each return is attributed to the format of the store that made the original sale, not the store where the return was made.
caveats: Correction: the Training pseudo-location (store 999) has 126 sales lines in P2 (about 2,222 EUR net, mostly flagged staff purchases). It is excluded because it is not a trading store.
Correction: the web shop (store 900, 6,351 lines, 183,102 EUR net) is excluded from the store-format split. The rpt.v_daily_sales view treats store_id below 900 as stores and WB lines as web.

The format values in dim_store are Large, Medium and Small (plus Web and Training), but the column comment says Hyper, Standard or Express. I used the values as stored, and the labels in the answer are the stored ones. The mapping to the comment's names is not documented, so please check it before using them elsewhere.
Staff purchases are included. Leaving them out moves the rates by under 0.03 points (Large 4.45, Medium 4.56, Small 4.30), which does not change the ranking.
The three formats are within 0.25 points of each other (4.28 to 4.53). That gap is small, and I did not test whether it is meaningful.
Return rates are complete for this period, since the latest return on any P2 sale is 2025-07-23 and returns are loaded to 2026-10-04. Some other fiscal years' P2 figures would not be as mature.

dim_store carries a region change on 2025-04-28 for six stores, but none changed format, so the format split is unaffected. Two stores were open in the period but are not flagged as closed: Savonlinna has a close_date of 2026-01-25, after the period.
The warehouse also holds bak_*, *_old, tmp_* and stg_* tables. None of them were used.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 5 (31 August to 27 September 2026, filtered on sale_date)
Store-level analysis on store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), all store versions via store_id
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date
Products counted by stable sku, named from the current product version (as-is)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included (as in net sales and units sold)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 5 this year' read as FY2026/27 P5, the last completed period (request dated 7 October 2026; the period ended 27 September 2026).
'Products' read as individual articles (sku), not subcategories or brands.
'Units sold' is gross units on sales lines. Returns are not netted off, because the company definition of units sold is the quantity on sales lines.
Product names and categories are as-is (current product version). Each of the top products has only one version in the period, so as-was gives the same result.
Staff purchases are left in, since they count as sales.
caveats: No data problems found. Receipt lines were unique at the grain (receipt_id, line_no), with no duplicates in the period for store 102.
Daily units and net sales before returns for store 102 in P5 match rpt_daily_store_sales on every day, so no correction was needed.
The ZZ Test filter did not change the store total.
Web orders are not part of this figure. They sit under store 900, not Pitäjänmäki.
The top 3 are clear, with no ties at the cut-off (4th place has 30 units).

answer.sql: WITH movements AS (SELECT p.category, f.net_amount AS net, f.standard_cost AS cst FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-22' AND DATE '2025-10-26' AND s.store_id <> 999 UNION ALL SELECT p.category, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-22' AND DATE '2025-10-26' AND s.store_id <> 999) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS fiscal_period, category, round(sum(net), 2) AS net_sales, round(100 * (sum(net) - sum(cst)) / sum(net), 2) AS gross_margin_pct FROM movements WHERE category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY category ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 6 of FY2025/26 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar (22 Sep 2025 to 26 Oct 2025, 5 weeks, fully loaded)
Net sales: line value in EUR excluding VAT after line discounts (net_amount), less refunds excluding VAT (refund_net) booked in the period, the same way rpt_daily_store_sales builds net sales
Gross margin %: (net sales minus standard cost of units sold, plus standard cost of units returned) divided by net sales, times 100
Standard cost as carried on the fact rows (standard_cost, standard_cost_returned), which tie exactly to quantity times the standard unit cost of the product version
Category taken from the product version in force at the sale date (fact product_key), not the current version
Channels: all stores plus the web shop (store and web channels both counted, as in rpt.v_daily_sales)
Staff purchases kept in, as rpt_daily_store_sales keeps them
Store 999 (Training store) excluded
assumptions: 'Last year' means the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26, because the request is dated 8 Oct 2026, which falls in FY2026/27; 'period 6' means fiscal period 6, not calendar month 6
Both channels (stores and web) are included because the request does not limit it to stores
Net sales is after returns, and gross margin % is on that net-of-returns basis
Garden and Electrical are shown as the category hierarchy stood at the time of sale in period 6, not the hierarchy as it stands now
Gross margin uses standard cost, the only cost in the warehouse, so it is a standard-cost margin and not an actual-cost margin
caveats: Correction: Outdoor Lighting was reclassified from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, the day after period 6 ended. I kept it in Garden for this period, as it was then. On today's hierarchy (Outdoor Lighting in Electrical) the figures would be: Electrical net sales 219695.83 at 40.95% gross margin; Garden net sales 113813.42 at 40.20% gross margin. Joining on the current product version would give these figures instead. Tell me if you want them as the headline.

Correction: Training store (store 999) sales were excluded. Across all categories, period 6 had 204 lines worth about 4,173.72 net, including a 'ZZ Test' category of test articles. Within Garden and Electrical the exclusion removes the training-store lines.
Staff purchases are included, following the existing daily sales report. They are about 14k net across all stores and categories, so you can ask for a version without them.
Refunds are counted by the date they were booked, so some of the refunds deducted relate to sales made before 22 Sep 2025.
Gross margin is at standard cost. Some individual lines sell below standard cost (about 89 lines across the two categories), and these are included.

rpt_daily_store_sales does not match the fact table day by day for the web shop. Web sales on Sundays are much lower there and the other days higher, but the period total is close (193,191 against 194,176). I used the fact table with sale_date and did not use the report table.

answer.sql: WITH grp AS (SELECT member_id, 'holdout' AS grp FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15 UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id, 'targeted' FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), spend AS (SELECT m.member_id, sum(f.net_amount - coalesce(r.refund_net, 0)) AS net_spend FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key LEFT JOIN (SELECT sales_line_id, sum(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) r ON r.sales_line_id = f.sales_line_id WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-24' AND DATE '2025-11-30' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag GROUP BY 1), per_group AS (SELECT g.grp, count(*) AS members, sum(coalesce(s.net_spend, 0)) / count(*) AS avg_spend FROM grp g LEFT JOIN spend s USING (member_id) GROUP BY g.grp) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, round(max(avg_spend) FILTER (WHERE grp = 'targeted'), 2) AS avg_spend_targeted_eur, round(max(avg_spend) FILTER (WHERE grp = 'holdout'), 2) AS avg_spend_holdout_eur, round(max(avg_spend) FILTER (WHERE grp = 'targeted') - max(avg_spend) FILTER (WHERE grp = 'holdout'), 2) AS uplift_eur FROM per_group
definitions_applied: Campaign window: dim_campaign start and end dates, 24-30 Nov 2025
Holdout group: members in campaign_holdout, matched on member_id rather than member_key
Targeted group: distinct members with a contact in fact_campaign_exposure, mapped from member_key to member_id
Spend measured in EUR excluding VAT (net_amount, after line discounts)
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Refunds on those purchase lines deducted (fact_return_line.refund_net via sales_line_id)
Averages taken over all group members, zero spenders included
Sale date is the local sale_date, not the UTC timestamp
Spend counted on all channels (store, web home delivery, click and collect), because sales lines carry channel_id rather than channel_code from November 2025
assumptions: Spend means net sales excluding VAT, after returns, over the 24-30 Nov 2025 campaign window only. Purchases after 30 Nov are not counted.
Targeted means members who were actually contacted, whether or not the contact was delivered or opened (intention to treat). Delivered-only would be a different, smaller group.

Returns are attached to the original purchase line. Refunds booked in the window for earlier purchases are not counted. Refunds booked later for window purchases are deducted, since returns data runs to 4 Oct 2026.
Guest web orders cannot be tied to a member, so they are in neither group. Cancelled orders have no sales lines.
Uplift is the difference in average spend per member (targeted minus holdout), in EUR per member, not a total campaign effect.
caveats: The uplift of 0.74 EUR per member is small against an average of about 4 EUR. Only 8 percent of targeted members (1,880 of 23,818) and 6.5 percent of holdout members (179 of 2,747) bought anything. Holdout is only 2,747 members, so the result is noisy and no significance test was run.

Correction: dim_campaign.holdout_pct says 0.100, but the actual holdout is 2,747 of 26,573 on the mailing list (10.3 percent). Also, targeted (23,818) plus holdout (2,747) is 26,565, 8 short of the stated mailing list size. I used the actual contacted and held-out members, not the stated size.

Correction: campaign_holdout holds member_id but the fact tables hold member_key, which is one row per member version. Joining the two directly would miss members. I mapped everything to member_id through dim_member.

Correction: staff purchases are excluded. They are 52 lines for targeted members and 2 for holdout members. Without the exclusion the averages would be 4.74 EUR (targeted) and 4.06 EUR (holdout) before returns.

Correction: refunds are deducted. Before returns, with staff purchases excluded, the averages are 4.70 EUR (targeted) and 4.04 EUR (holdout), an uplift of 0.66 EUR. After returns, they are 4.47 and 3.73, an uplift of 0.74 EUR. If Marketing wants spend before returns, use the first set.
From November 2025 the channel_code column on sales lines is null and channel_id is used instead. A filter on channel_code (ST/WB) would drop all of that data. I did not filter on channel.

The two groups look comparable before the campaign: average spend in the prior six months was 93.65 EUR (holdout) and 91.51 EUR (targeted), and tier mix, tenure and online share were similar. This supports reading the difference as campaign-driven, though it is not proof.

Holdout and targeted members were all marketing-consenting at the campaign start, and no holdout member was contacted. 1,951 of the 50,043 contacts were not delivered, and they are still counted as targeted.
Only members can be measured. Non-member and guest sales, and members outside both groups (for example those without consent), are excluded, so this is not the campaign's effect on total sales.

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week
),
range_start AS (
    SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week
),
weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN weeks w
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    CROSS JOIN params
    CROSS JOIN range_start
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
    GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))
)
SELECT ty.store_weeks, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM lfl_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NULL
ORDER BY ty.region NULLS FIRST;
definitions_applied: DEF-LFL-BASIS: Like-for-like compares net sales in stores present in both years
DEF-LFL-OPEN: Store must have been open at least 52 weeks (364 days) before the period starts
DEF-LFL-BOTH-YEARS: Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years
DEF-LFL-REFIT: Refit weeks from ref_store_closure are excluded for the store, in both years
DEF-LFL-WEEK53: Week 53 is never part of like-for-like comparison
DEF-NET-SALES: Net sales exclude VAT and include returns (reducing sales on the return date)
DEF-STORE-SCOPE: Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop and store 999 excluded
CAL-COMPARE: Comparison aligned by fiscal week number, not calendar dates
DEF-HIERARCHY-ASIS: Store regions are reported as-is (current versions)
assumptions: Period 4 this year read as FY2026/27 P04 (weeks 14-17), the most recent completed period as of the request date 2026-10-07
Prior-year comparator is FY2025/26 P04 (weeks 14-17), aligned by fiscal week number
Request for overall LFL growth (not broken down by region); returned total row only
Web dispatch date used for web orders (Helsinki time); store sales use sale_date
caveats: Timezone edge: 8-9 rows in fact_web_order and 14-20 rows in fact_sales_line fall on the UTC/Helsinki day boundary in the requested period; their fiscal assignment depends on whether the day boundary is taken at UTC midnight or Helsinki midnight. The query uses Helsinki midnight (the warehouse standard).
Data is complete through 2026-08-30 (the end of FY2026/27 P04), as of the warehouse load point 2026-10-04

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= d.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date, fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_period = 1) d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= DATE '2026-05-04' - 364)), sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week WHERE d.fiscal_period = 1 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_period, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0*(ty.net_sales/ly.net_sales-1),2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM sales ty, sales ly WHERE ty.fiscal_year='FY2026/27' AND ly.fiscal_year='FY2025/26'
definitions_applied: LFL: this year vs the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week, one total
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop store 900 excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns (returns on their return date)
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that week in both years (open_date, close_date, ref_store_closure)
Opening rule: open_date <= first day of range minus 364 days (4 May 2026 - 364 = 5 May 2025)
Open and close dates from the current dim_store version
Fiscal calendar from dim_date (P1 = weeks 1 to 4)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 1 this year' read as FY2026/27 P1 (4 May to 31 May 2026, weeks 1 to 4). The request is dated 9 October 2026, so the current fiscal year is FY2026/27 and P1 is complete and fully loaded.
Compared with FY2025/26 P1, weeks 1 to 4 (28 April to 25 May 2025), by fiscal week and not by calendar date.
Returned a single total row (this year, last year, growth), since no breakdown was requested.
Staff purchases are included, as in the net sales definition.
caveats: Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026, so it has no sales in FY2026/27 P1 and drops out of the LFL base for all four weeks. 38 stores (152 store-weeks) are in the base, out of 39 physical stores last year.
No store was dropped for a refit. The Tammisto, Pori and Kuopio refit closures fall outside P1 in both years.
Lohja (137, opened 4 November 2024) and Tampere Lamminpää (136, opened 2 September 2024) pass the 364-day opening rule for this range and are in the base.

Last year's week 1 (28 April to 4 May 2025) contains May Day (1 May 2025), when all stores were shut. This year's week 1 has no closed day. The LFL definition works on whole store-weeks, so the day was not adjusted for. It lifts the growth figure somewhat compared with a trading-day-matched comparison.

Control totals: daily store-level net sales (sales less returns, stores only, excluding 999 and ZZ Test) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly on every day of both periods, with no gaps. I found no duplicate sales or return lines.
Online sales are not in this LFL figure, per the LFL definition.

answer.sql:
WITH sales_data AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_week,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as sales_amount
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
    AND d.fiscal_week IN (5, 6, 7, 8)
    AND f.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week
),
returns_data AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_week,
    SUM(r.refund_net) as refund_amount
  FROM fact_return_line r
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
    AND d.fiscal_week IN (5, 6, 7, 8)
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week
),
combined AS (
  SELECT 
    s.fiscal_year,
    s.fiscal_week,
    COALESCE(s.sales_amount, 0) - COALESCE(r.refund_amount, 0) as net_sales
  FROM sales_data s
  LEFT JOIN returns_data r ON s.fiscal_year = r.fiscal_year AND s.fiscal_week = r.fiscal_week
),
pivot_data AS (
  SELECT 
    fiscal_week,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales END) as sales_fy2024_25,
    MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END) as sales_fy2025_26
  FROM combined
  GROUP BY fiscal_week
)
SELECT 
  fiscal_week as week,
  sales_fy2024_25 as sales_last_year,
  sales_fy2025_26 as sales_this_year,
  ROUND(((sales_fy2025_26 - sales_fy2024_25) / sales_fy2024_25 * 100), 2) as growth_percent
FROM pivot_data
ORDER BY fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: fact_sales_line net amounts minus fact_return_line refunds
Staff purchases excluded from sales totals
All channels combined (store and web)
Period 2 equals fiscal weeks 5-8
Growth percentage calculated as year-on-year change
assumptions: Total company sales includes all channels without segmentation
Staff purchases excluded as non-commercial transactions
Returns matched to return date rather than original sale date
This year is FY2025/26, last year is FY2024/25

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members_joined FROM dim_member WHERE join_date = DATE '2026-10-03'
definitions_applied: A member is counted once by member_id (the stable loyalty number), not by member_key, because dim_member keeps one row per version of each member
Join date is dim_member.join_date, the date the member joined
All members are counted whatever their sign-up route, including online sign-ups (home_store_id 900), because the request asks for all members who joined
assumptions: 'Joined' means the loyalty programme join date in dim_member.join_date
3 October 2026 is a calendar date, so no fiscal calendar or time zone conversion is involved
Staff and non-consenting members are included, because the request does not exclude them
caveats: No correction was needed. Each member_id has a single join_date, and the 29 members who joined on 3 October 2026 each have one row, so counting by version rows or by distinct member_id gives the same 29.
The staging table stg_member_updates and the backup tables were not used. The 29 members are all in dim_member already, and stg_member_updates holds the same 29 for that date.
dim_member currently runs up to 4 October 2026, so 3 October is a complete day. The count is in line with the neighbouring days (29 to 40 per day in the last week).

answer.sql: WITH treated AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure x JOIN dim_member m USING (member_key) WHERE x.campaign_id = 15), held AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15), grp AS (SELECT member_id, 'targeted' AS grp FROM treated UNION ALL SELECT member_id, 'holdout' FROM held), sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, f.net_amount AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m USING (member_key) WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-24' AND DATE '2025-11-30' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag), refunds AS (SELECT m.member_id, -r.refund_net AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_member m USING (member_key) JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-24' AND DATE '2025-11-30' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag), spend AS (SELECT member_id, sum(amt) AS spend FROM (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM refunds) GROUP BY 1), per_group AS (SELECT g.grp, avg(coalesce(s.spend, 0)) AS avg_spend FROM grp g LEFT JOIN spend s USING (member_id) GROUP BY 1) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, round((SELECT avg_spend FROM per_group WHERE grp = 'targeted'), 2) AS avg_spend_per_targeted_member_eur, round((SELECT avg_spend FROM per_group WHERE grp = 'holdout'), 2) AS avg_spend_per_held_out_member_eur, round((SELECT avg_spend FROM per_group WHERE grp = 'targeted') - (SELECT avg_spend FROM per_group WHERE grp = 'holdout'), 2) AS uplift_eur
definitions_applied: Campaign window: 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-30 (dim_campaign, campaign 15 Black Week 2025)
Holdout group: members listed in campaign_holdout for campaign 15 (matched by member_id, not member_key)
Targeted group: members who received at least one contact in fact_campaign_exposure for campaign 15 (mailing list less holdout)
Members identified by stable member_id, so slowly changing member versions are not counted twice
Spend: net sales in EUR excluding VAT (net_amount), across store, web home delivery and click-and-collect lines
Net of returns: refund_net deducted by return date within the campaign window, the same basis as net_sales in rpt_daily_store_sales
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) excluded, together with returns of those lines
Average per member over all members in the group, including those who bought nothing
Uplift in euros: targeted average minus holdout average
assumptions: Uplift is the absolute difference in average spend per member over the campaign week, not a percentage and not a total incremental revenue figure.
Spend is counted in the campaign week only (24-30 Nov 2025), with no post-campaign attribution window.
Spend is net of VAT and net of returns, because the request did not say otherwise and this matches the company's net sales definition.
All sales channels (store and web) count, since members could respond to the email, SMS and push contacts in any channel.
Targeted members are those with a recorded exposure row, including contacts that were not delivered or opened (intention to treat), so the figure is not limited to delivered or opened contacts.
Only identified members are included. Guest web orders and non-member receipts have no member_key and cannot be assigned to either group.
caveats: The uplift is small, about 0.68 EUR per member, and is a point estimate with no significance test. Mean weekly spend per member is low and varies widely, so the true uplift could be materially different or close to zero.

The two groups were not perfectly balanced beforehand. In the four weeks before the campaign (2025-10-27 to 2025-11-23), average net spend was 14.02 EUR for the targeted group and 14.85 EUR for the holdout group. The holdout spent slightly more beforehand, so if anything the uplift is not flattered by this.
Correction: before deducting returns the figures were 4.70 (targeted) and 4.04 (holdout), an uplift of 0.66. I deducted returns, and I excluded staff purchases (about 2 percent of member lines).

Correction: I matched holdout and exposure rows by member_id, not member_key. The fact tables carry the key of the member version at the time, so joining on member_key against campaign_holdout (which stores member_id) would give wrong counts.

Gap in the targeted group: dim_campaign gives mailing_list_size minus holdout_size as 23,826 targeted members, but only 23,818 have a contact row in fact_campaign_exposure. I used the 23,818 who were actually contacted, and could not identify the 8 missing members. The effect on the averages is negligible.
Holdout integrity checked: 2,747 distinct held-out members, matching holdout_size, and none of them received a contact in this campaign.
About 6,500 members who had marketing consent on 2025-11-24 are in neither the mailing list nor the holdout. They are excluded from both groups because they were not part of the campaign design.

Not used: bak_, stg_, tmp_ and old tables, which are unlabelled backups or staging copies. The staging load tables hold no rows for this period and nothing overlaps the fact tables. Web orders in the window show no cancelled status, so no cancelled-order adjustment was needed.
In the Nov 2025 sales data, channel_code is NULL on every line. Channel was read from channel_id (1 store, 2 web home delivery, 3 click and collect).

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 6 AS first_period, 8 AS last_period), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), web_lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN l.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_sales), 2) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counts as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (dispatch_ts_utc converted to Europe/Helsinki), not sale_date
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code breaks at the 3 November 2025 migration)
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type
Cancelled and processing orders excluded from web sales (only delivered/collected orders with dispatch time)
Test articles (category ZZ Test) and store 999 excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 periods 6 to 8
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales store 900
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 (request dated 9 October 2026), as past requests read it
'Periods 6 to 8' read as fiscal periods P6, P7 and P8 of FY2025/26: 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025, 27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025, and 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025; all three are fully loaded
Share is of web net sales (money) rather than of web order counts, because the request says 'share of the web shop's sales'
Staff purchases are kept in, as the company definition says
Shares are given in percent, rounded to two decimals
caveats: The net sales behind the shares reconcile exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 in each period: P6 175,588.62, P7 154,977.27 and P8 225,265.08 EUR. Click-and-collect net is 48,901.47, 39,403.04 and 60,899.16 EUR.

Do not use channel_code or rpt.v_daily_sales / rpt.v_weekly_store_sales for web: from 3 November 2025 (inside P7) they leave out web sales. I used store 900 and fulfilment_type instead, so no correction was needed to the numbers.

Some refunds on web orders were booked to physical stores rather than the web shop. They total about 4.8k EUR in P6, 4.9k in P7 and 4.5k in P8, of which click-and-collect is about 1.9k, 1.4k and 1.3k. Under the company definition they count against those stores, not web, so I left them out of web sales. Including them would lower each share by under about 0.3 percentage points.

fact_sales_line has duplicated lines (same receipt_id and line_no, loaded twice) for store 116 in the week of 15 to 21 September 2025. That is before P6 and not in the web shop, so it does not affect these figures. Anyone running store-level sales for that week should de-duplicate.
One ZZ Test line (5.50 EUR) on the web shop in the wider period was excluded as a test article.
P7 is the lowest share (25.43%) and spans the 3 November 2025 platform migration. The result does not depend on channel_code, so the migration does not distort it.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.subcategory, cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.subcategory, cp.category ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (returns not netted)
Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2026/27 (31 Aug 2026 to 27 Sep 2026, weeks 18 to 21)
Store scope: Nokia is store_id 118 only; web shop 900 not included
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
As-is product hierarchy (current product version)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Nokia means the Nokia store (store_id 118, West region, Medium format), not a brand
This year means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27; period 5 is the last complete period (ended 27 September 2026)
Units sold is gross units on sales lines, not net of returns, following the weeks-of-cover wording in the metric dictionary, since the dictionary has no separate units-sold definition
Subcategories are on the current product hierarchy (as-is); as-was gives the same figures for these rows
caveats: Store 118's period 5 units (2245) and 28 trading days match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, so no gap to the control total
No duplicate sales lines found at the sales_line_id or receipt and line level, and no test-article lines at Nokia in the period
Netting returns booked in the period (7, 5 and 9 units for the three) would leave 563, 147 and 130, with the same ranking
Fixings & Fasteners is far ahead of the rest, about 3.7 times the second place
The 4th and 5th subcategories (Plants & Flowers and Cleaning Products) are tied at 136 units, which does not affect the top 3

answer.sql: WITH sold AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, cs.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT l.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Return rate = returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net, both excluding VAT
Sale-week cohort: returns are matched to the original sales line via sales_line_id and counted against the period of the original sale, whenever and wherever they were booked
Sold lines selected by the fiscal period of fact_sales_line.sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Format as-is: each line's store is mapped to the current store version (format does not change between store versions)
Web shop (store 900, format Web) shown as its own format line
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 P02 = fiscal weeks 5 to 8, 26 May to 22 June 2025
No deprecated objects used (no rpt.v_daily_sales, no stg_, bak_ or tmp_ tables, no channel_code)
assumptions: 'Period 2 last year' read as FY2025/26 P02, since the request was made on 6 October 2026 (FY2026/27) and recent requests read 'last year' as the previous fiscal year
'What was sold' read as net sales value excluding VAT, not units, in line with the company return-rate definition
'Came back' read as all returns booked against those sales lines, however late they arrived (up to 30 days after the sale; the last ones landed 23 July 2025)
Web is included as its own line because the format column includes Web; Leena may only want physical stores, in which case the three store formats (Large, Medium, Small) are the answer
Web lines are placed in the period by their order date (sale_date), as the accepted return-rate requests do, not by dispatch date
caveats: Format labels in the warehouse are Large, Medium, Small and Web (plus Training for store 999). The schema column comment (Hyper, Standard, Express) is out of date.
Excluded as per house rules: store 999 (126 lines) and ZZ Test articles (21 lines) in the period. These do not appear in the figures.
The web return rate (12.23%) is about three times the store formats (4.3 to 4.5%). That is a real feature of the data (all web returns matched through sales_line_id), not a join artefact.

Web is dated by order date here, whereas web net sales elsewhere are recognised on dispatch date. Using dispatch date would change which web orders fall into P2 (net 183,098 EUR by order date; about 152,557 EUR of those dispatched within P2). The accepted return-rate method uses sale_date, so I followed it.

The cohort is complete: the warehouse is loaded to 4 October 2026, more than 30 days after the period ended on 22 June 2025. 16 of 1,992 returned lines came back slightly more than 30 days after sale, and are included.

Checks passed: no duplicate sales lines or return lines at the stated grain, no refund larger than its sold line, no return before its sale, no cancelled web orders in the cohort, and no store changed format between versions. Sold net by format: Large 400,763.11, Medium 552,936.25, Small 147,668.20, Web 183,098.49 EUR; returned net: 17,707.57, 25,030.11, 6,319.09, 22,388.29 EUR.

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' as fiscal_year, 3 as fiscal_period, ds.store_id, ds.store_name, 'Interior Paint' as product_subcategory, SUM(fsl.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line fsl INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date WHERE ds.store_id = 108 AND dp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND dd.fiscal_week BETWEEN 9 AND 13 GROUP BY ds.store_id, ds.store_name
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: Period 3 of FY2026/27 spans fiscal weeks 9–13 (29 June to 2 August 2026)
Units sold: Sum of quantity from sales lines (fact_sales_line), sales channel inclusive
Store identification: City/store name 'Lahti' resolved to store_id 108
Product category: Interior Paint refers to the Interior Paint subcategory
assumptions: Interior Paint refers to all products in the Interior Paint subcategory, not a single product variant
Store 'Lahti' is uniquely identified by store_id 108
Units sold includes all sales channels (store and web)
Returns are not subtracted from the units count
caveats: Twenty distinct Interior Paint product variants exist; all are summed in the total
This count represents sales lines only and does not deduct units subsequently returned

answer.sql:
WITH sales_with_dates AS (
  -- Store sales with sale_date
  SELECT 
    s.region,
    f.sale_date as transaction_date,
    f.gross_amount
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  WHERE s.store_id <> 999
    AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    AND f.channel_code = 'ST'
    AND f.sale_date >= '2024-08-01'
    AND f.sale_date <= '2024-09-30'
  
  UNION ALL
  
  -- Web sales with dispatch_date in Helsinki time
  SELECT 
    s.region,
    CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', wo.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) as transaction_date,
    f.gross_amount
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN fact_web_order wo ON wo.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
  JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
  WHERE s.store_id <> 999
    AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    AND f.channel_code = 'WB'
    AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', wo.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) >= '2024-08-01'
    AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', wo.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) <= '2024-09-30'
)
SELECT 
  region,
  SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM transaction_date) = 8 THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS august_2024,
  SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM transaction_date) = 9 THEN gross_amount ELSE 0 END) AS september_2024
FROM sales_with_dates
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales: sum of gross_amount (including VAT) from fact_sales_line
Before returns: sales lines only, excluding return lines
Region: as-was (the region hierarchy as it stood at each transaction date)
Store sales: recognized on sale_date
Web sales: recognized on dispatch_ts_utc converted to Helsinki time (tax point at delivery)
Exclusions: store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test filtered out
assumptions: Calendar months 'August and September 2024' interpreted as 1–31 August and 1–30 September
Web sales tax point is dispatch date in Helsinki time, not order date
Regions as specified in the as-was store dimension at each transaction date
Online region represents the web shop (store_id 900)
caveats: Net sales total verified against rpt_daily_store_sales control total (2,333,805.81 EUR net, before VAT)
In August–September 2024, the warehouse held four physical regions (North, South, East, West) plus Online; the Capital Region did not exist until 28 April 2025
VAT rate changed on 1 September 2024 from 24% to 25.5%; each line carries its own vat_rate (standard, reduced14, reduced10)
Web sales include only dispatched orders; cancelled and processing orders excluded

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE p.sku = 101624 AND s.store_id = 131 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-28' AND DATE '2026-10-04' GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name
definitions_applied: Fiscal week: Monday to Sunday (dim_date), FY2026/27 week 22 = 28 Sep to 4 Oct 2026
Units sold = sum of fact_sales_line.quantity, before returns
Store identified by store_id (131), product by sku (101624), joined through the surrogate keys store_key 37 and product_key 1702
Staff purchases would be included (none in the week)
assumptions: 'Oulu Kaakkuri' is the store (store_id 131, Oulu, North region), not part of the product name. The SKU's article description in dim_product is 'Fixings & Fasteners Raudikko 251'.
'Last week' means the last complete fiscal week before the request date of 8 Oct 2026 (a Thursday): week 22 of FY2026/27, 28 Sep to 4 Oct 2026. The warehouse has no sales after 4 Oct 2026.
'Units sold' means units sold gross, with returns not netted off.
The question is about this store's own sales. The SKU sold in no other channel at this store, and web sales were not part of the question.
caveats: One return of this SKU at this store was booked in the week: 4 units on 30 Sep 2026 (return_line 56829, reason 'changed_mind'). It belongs to a sale on 19 Sep 2026, in the previous week. If you want units net of returns booked in the week, the figure is 13 (17 minus 4).
The product name does not contain 'Oulu Kaakkuri'; I treated that as the store name.
Sales were recorded on 8 of the 9 days with sales in the surrounding period, with none on 30 Sep, 3 Oct or other days shown as zero. I did not add rows for days without sales.

No data problems found for this SKU and store in the week: no duplicate sales lines, no unloaded staging rows (the 3 lines in the staging table were already in the fact table with the same quantities), one product version and one store version, no store closure, and the period is loaded to 4 Oct 2026. The channel_code column is null on these lines, so I identified store sales by channel_id 1 (Store) and by the store key.
