One order is one web_order_id in fact_web_order, so each order is counted once however many lines it has.
assumptions: Cyber Monday means Monday 1 December 2025, as the request states.
'Orders' means orders placed and not cancelled, the same basis as sales reporting. Counting cancelled orders as well gives 345.
Click-and-collect orders count as web shop orders. The split is 239 home delivery and 87 click-and-collect.
caveats: Timezone correction: 59 of the 326 orders were placed on the evening of 30 November UTC. In Helsinki time they fall on 1 December, which is the business date the sales lines use. A UTC date filter would give 267 and miss them.
Cancelled orders: 19 orders placed on 1 December (Helsinki time) were cancelled and are excluded. Including them gives 345.
Consistency checks: all 326 orders have sales lines. Line counts and order totals match the lines, and I found no duplicate orders, staff purchases or zero or negative quantities.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS customers FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_member m ON f.member_key = m.member_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key WHERE s.city = 'Tampere' AND s.store_id < 900 AND f.member_key IS NOT NULL AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
definitions_applied: Customer: unique loyalty member (distinct member_id)
Tampere stores: physical stores only (store_id < 900, excludes web shop and training store)
Test articles excluded: category != 'ZZ Test'
assumptions: Interpreted 'customers in Tampere' as unique members who made at least one purchase at physical Tampere stores
Included all historical purchases (not limited to active members in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks)
Physical store purchases only; web orders excluded
caveats: Loyalty members only; non-members cannot be counted uniquely by individual customer (43,920 non-member transactions recorded at Tampere stores but individual purchasers unidentifiable)
Web shop (store_id 900) excluded as per warehouse house rules; true 'in Tampere' population limited to physical-store shoppers
Figure represents all members who have purchased in Tampere at any point in the warehouse history; does not filter for active members (those with purchases in trailing 52 fiscal weeks)

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS period
),
sold_lines AS (
    SELECT 
        f.sales_line_id, 
        f.sale_date,
        s.format,
        f.net_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s     ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p   ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_date d      ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
      AND d.fiscal_period = params.period
),
refunds AS (
    SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 
    l.format,
    ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct
FROM sold_lines l
LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY l.format;
definitions_applied: Return rate: returned net divided by sold net, on the sale-week cohort
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Store format: Large, Medium, Small, and Web from dim_store
assumptions: Period 2 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 P02 (29 April 2025 - 3 May 2026 fiscal year, period 2 runs 26 May to 22 June 2025)
Store format includes all physical stores and the web channel, excluding the training store (store 999)
Return rate is calculated on the fiscal week of the original sale (sale-week cohort), with returns matched back to the original sale line regardless of when they are processed
caveats: The sale-week cohort is complete (all returns have been processed; last sale date is more than 30 days before warehouse load date of 4 October 2026)
Store 999 (Training store) excluded per company rules
Category ZZ Test excluded per company rules
Web sales are recognized on the dispatch date; refunds for web items sent by post are booked to store 900

answer.sql: SELECT p.subcategory, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY p.subcategory ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period: FY2026/27 P05 runs 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27 (4 weeks, fiscal weeks 18-21, fully loaded)
Store identified by store_id 118 (Nokia), joined through store_key
Units sold means the quantity on sales lines, before returns, as in rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold
Subcategory taken from the product version in force at the sale date via product_key
Channel: Nokia has only in-store lines (channel_id 1). The channel_code column is NULL in current data, so I did not filter on it
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, as the request date (2026-10-09) falls in it. Period 5 is the fiscal period, not a calendar month
'Nokia' means the store named Nokia (store_id 118, West region). There is only one store version and one match
'Units sold' is gross units sold, not net of returns, and includes staff purchases (19 lines, 34 units), as the team's daily sales report does
Ranking is by units across all channels for that store, which is in-store only
Top 3 is by the 'subcategory' field as it stands, without grouping into categories
caveats: I found no data problems that needed a correction. Nokia has no refit closure in ref_store_closure. All 28 days of the period have sales and the period is fully loaded. There are no duplicate lines and every line matches a product version. The total of 2,245 units agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales

Sensitivity to returns: Nokia had 9 units of Storage Boxes returned in the period. If units were counted net of returns, third place would change. Cleaning Products would then lead Storage Boxes (134 against 130) and Plants & Flowers would be on 129. The first two places stay the same

Sensitivity to staff purchases: excluding staff purchases gives Fixings & Fasteners 560, Indoor Lighting 150, Storage Boxes 136, with Cleaning Products tied with Storage Boxes at 136. I counted staff purchases because they are units sold
Third place is close: Storage Boxes 139, Cleaning Products 136, Plants & Flowers 136
Outdoor Lighting products moved category in October 2025 (Electrical to a different category). The subcategory name did not change, so the answer is not affected

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS web_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = w.dispatch_date WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 4 AND 6 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (not the order date)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Figures including VAT: sum of gross_amount on the lines, each at its own VAT rate
Cancelled and still-processing orders are not web sales (only delivered and collected orders, which are the ones with dispatch times and sales lines)
Click-and-collect counted as web, dated on the ready-for-collection time
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25 P4 is 29 Jul to 25 Aug 2024, P5 is 26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024, P6 is 23 Sep to 27 Oct 2024
Helsinki time: UTC timestamps converted with timezone('Europe/Helsinki', ...) before dating
assumptions: Q2 of FY24/25 read as fiscal year FY2024/25, periods 4 to 6, as the request says
Before returns means sales lines only: no refunds (refund_gross) are deducted, and the VAT-inclusive figure is gross_amount, not net multiplied by a VAT rate
One figure per period, with no total row, as asked
Dispatch-date dating is the company default for web sales and the request did not ask for order-date dating, so I used dispatch date
Staff purchases are included, as in the company net sales definition
caveats: Test articles (category ZZ Test) in a few web test orders were removed: 8.06 EUR from P4 and 3.77 EUR from P5, nothing from P6. Without this correction P4 would be 156435.28 and P5 153250.01
Web orders dispatched in the three periods are all included, even if the order was placed before the period start. Orders placed but not yet dispatched at the period end fall in the next period

I checked the data and found no further problems: no duplicate order lines, every dispatched order has lines, line totals match order_total_gross, gross_amount agrees with net multiplied by the line VAT rate (which changed from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024, inside this quarter), and all 91 days have web sales
The control total in rpt_daily_store_sales is net of returns and excluding VAT, so it cannot be compared directly with this figure and I did not run that check

answer.sql: SELECT p.category, AVG(fsw.closing_value) as avg_stock_value FROM fact_stock_week fsw INNER JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = fsw.week_ending_date INNER JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fsw.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fsw.product_key WHERE s.region = 'West' AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 44 AND 47 GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY p.category
definitions_applied: Closing stock value at standard cost from fact_stock_week
Average of weekly closing values for the period, not last week only
Physical stores only, excluding web shop (store 900) and training store (999)
Fiscal period P11 FY2025/26 defined as fiscal weeks 44–47 (23 February to 22 March 2026)
Semi-additive aggregation: summed across stores within each week, then averaged across weeks
Excluded ZZ Test category per stock reporting scope
assumptions: Period 11 last year means fiscal period 11 of FY2025/26 (the prior fiscal year from the current FY2026/27)
Average stock value means the arithmetic mean of weekly closing values, not the final week's closing
West region refers to stores with dim_store.region = 'West'
Only ranged articles included (fact_stock_week contains only articles in stock at each store)
caveats: Stock snapshot taken on week-ending Sundays only; closing_value reflects standard cost, revalued each April
No web shop stock; web orders fulfilled from central warehouse outside fact_stock_week

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND p.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND f.channel_id = 1 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY ALL
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 taken from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar (29 June to 2 August 2026, 5 weeks, fully loaded)
Interior Paint taken as dim_product.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' (category Paint & Decorating), joined on the product_key in force at the sale date
Lahti store taken as store_id 108 (dim_store.store_key 13, the only version of that store)
In-store sales only: channel_id = 1 (Store). The channel_code column is empty on these lines, so the channel key was used
Units sold taken as fact_sales_line.quantity
assumptions: 'FY26/27' read as FY2026/27, the warehouse's fiscal year label
Units sold means gross units sold in the store, so returns are not netted off
Staff purchases are included (4 units on 3 lines on 2 August 2026), as they are sales that take stock out of the store
Web and click-and-collect sales are excluded. They are booked to the web pseudo-store 900, not to Lahti, even where the pick-up is at Lahti
Store 999 (a separate pseudo-location) is not part of Lahti and is excluded
caveats: channel_code is NULL on all the Interior Paint lines checked, although the column comment says ST/WB. The query uses channel_id instead, with no effect on the figure.
Returns not netted: 5 units of Interior Paint were returned at Lahti in the period (2 not_as_described, 1 wrong_size_or_fit, 2 changed_mind), so net of returns the figure would be 189 units.
Excluding the 4 staff-purchase units would give 190 units.

Checks that found nothing to correct: no duplicate sales lines, Lahti has no store closure in the period and a sales line on every day of it, no Interior Paint SKU changed category or subcategory, and every fact row points to the product version valid on its sale date. The October 2025 move of Outdoor Lighting from Garden to Electrical does not touch Interior Paint.

answer.sql: SELECT store_id, store_name, format, sqm FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900 AND close_date IS NULL ORDER BY sqm DESC, store_id LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Store counts and store-level analyses cover physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop (900) and training store (999) excluded
dim_store keeps one row per version: used the current version only (is_current) so each store appears once
Natural key store_id used to identify stores, not store_key
Sales area (sqm) taken from dim_store as the measure of size
Closed stores excluded (Savonlinna 129, closed 25 January 2026)
assumptions: The wiki does not define 'biggest'. I read it as largest sales area in square metres (dim_store.sqm), the usual meaning for store operations. The request was not clarified in the queue, so this is my reading
Ranking reflects the current store version; sqm is identical across all versions of the stores that changed region in April 2025
Ties are broken by store_id (no ties arose in the top 10)
caveats: Without the is_current filter the table would list stores 102 and 104 twice, because dim_store holds a South and a Capital Region version of each. I counted each store once, so the ranking is by distinct store_id

If 'biggest' means sales rather than size, the answer is different. By net sales in FY2025/26 (after returns, web excluded, store 999 and ZZ Test excluded, EUR excl. VAT) the top 10 are: Tampere Hervanta 804,121; Helsinki Pitäjänmäki 679,652; Oulu Kaakkuri 555,975; Lahti 543,957; Turku Kupittaa 539,966; Vantaa Tammisto 531,925; Tampere Lielahti 517,285; Kuopio 512,758; Tampere Kaleva 474,881; Nokia 415,259. This list was not checked against rpt_daily_store_sales and is for comparison only. Tell me if you want that version delivered
Kuopio (125) was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 but is a trading store and is included on size
Sqm is the value held in the warehouse and I could not verify it against another source

answer.sql: WITH lines AS (SELECT f.receipt_id, f.net_amount, s.store_id, CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', w.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) ELSE f.sale_date END AS business_date FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN fact_web_order w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag), per_receipt AS (SELECT receipt_id, store_id, SUM(net_amount) AS receipt_net FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-08-02' GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, ROUND(SUM(receipt_net) / COUNT(*), 2) AS atv FROM per_receipt
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns / number of sales receipts
Net amount excluding VAT (net_amount), before returns
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 periods 1 to 3 = 4 May to 2 August 2026 (13 whole weeks)
Store 999 (training store) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded, including 3 web test orders
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Web shop identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (UTC timestamp converted to Europe/Helsinki)
Cancelled web orders excluded (they have no sales lines)
Web order counted as one receipt (receipt_id = web_order_id)
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'This year' is the current fiscal year, FY2026/27 (the request is dated 5 October 2026). 'Periods 1 to 3' is P1 to P3, which are fully loaded.

The company ATV definition says web orders are not included. Mika asked for web orders to be in it, so I followed the request and included web. For reference, the stores-only ATV on the standard definition is 55.52 (66,984 receipts, 3,719,186.33 EUR). Web alone is 59.33 (13,004 orders, 771,530.75 EUR).
Staff purchases are left out, as in the standard ATV definition. All staff receipts are in stores; none are web.

Web orders are dated on their Helsinki dispatch date, both for sales and for the order count, so the numerator and denominator cover the same orders. Counting orders on their order date instead moves the combined ATV by only a few cents.
ATV is before returns, per the definition. It is a single company-wide figure with no breakdown by store or channel because none was asked for.
The figure is based on net amounts excluding VAT.
caveats: Correction: web orders are included although the standard ATV definition excludes them, because the request asked for it. The standard stores-only ATV for the same periods is 55.52.
Correction: web sales use the Helsinki dispatch date, not sale_date. On a web line sale_date is the order date, and 26,344 of 27,398 web lines in the surrounding range have a different dispatch date.
Correction: store 999 (training store) and test articles were removed. This takes out 3 web test orders and store 999 test and staff-training receipts.
Correction: staff purchases were removed from the receipt count and from net sales (2,473 store lines, 1,087 receipts in the wider date range).
Web is identified by store 900. channel_code is not used because it is not filled from the 3 November 2025 platform migration, and rpt.v_daily_sales was not used because it omits web sales.

Checks: no duplicate sales lines at (receipt_id, line_no), no receipt spans several stores or dates, and web lines match fact_web_order line counts. Receipt counts and net sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for the period (stores 3,767,921.27 EUR / 68,021 receipts and web 771,530.75 EUR / 13,004 orders, both including staff purchases). The ATV figure itself excludes staff purchases, so it is not directly comparable with that control.
No web orders in this period are still processing, so the choice of order date versus dispatch date does not change which orders are counted, only the period edges.
Week 7 of the year (Midsummer) is much lower in volume because stores were shut on public holidays; it is included as it is.

answer.sql: SELECT cp.sku, cp.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cp.sku, cp.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, cp.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 5 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), from ref_fiscal_calendar
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by Helsinki sale_date
Store scope: store_id 102 (Helsinki Pitäjänmäki), physical store only
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither changed the figures here)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales
Products identified by stable sku, named from the current product version
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales units_sold
assumptions: 'Period 5 this year' means FY2026/27 P5, the current fiscal year. It is the last complete period; the warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026.
'Units sold' means gross units on sales lines, not net of returns. Returns are not netted, because the company's definition of units sold is the quantity on sales lines.
'Product' means an article (sku), not a subcategory or brand.
Helsinki Pitäjänmäki is store_id 102, with stable sku grouping across store versions.
caveats: No data problems found that needed correcting. There were no duplicate lines and no ZZ Test or store 999 rows in this store and period.
The store's units total for the period (3,740) matches rpt_daily_store_sales units_sold for store 102 over the same days exactly.
Store 102 moved from South to Capital Region on 28 April 2025. This does not affect the answer, because it is a single-store request.
The top three are clear, with no ties at the cut-off: 52, 44 and 42 units, and the fourth place has 30.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT cp.category, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(n.net_sales - n.cost) / SUM(n.net_sales), 1) AS gross_margin_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 6 AND cp.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns dated on their return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost, both after returns, with returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned
Gross margin percentage: gross margin divided by net sales
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web shop (store 900) included, since the request is company-wide by category
As-is reporting: categories from the current product version (is_current)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 period 6, weeks 22 to 26, 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025
assumptions: 'Last year' is read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 (the request was received on 8 Oct 2026). Earlier requests asked in FY2026/27 read 'last year' the same way.
'Period 6' is fiscal period 6 of FY2025/26, which ran 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025 (5 weeks) and is fully loaded.
Reported as-is, the company default, since the request did not ask for as-was. Outdoor lighting is therefore in Electrical for the whole period.
Web sales are included, as the request does not limit it to stores.
The request asked for net sales and gross margin percentage only, so gross margin in EUR is left out of the table.
caveats: As-is versus as-was: outdoor lighting moved from Garden to Electrical on 27 Oct 2025, the day after P6 ended. As-is, 33,781.91 EUR of P6 net sales that was booked as Garden at the time sits in Electrical. As-was (categories as they were at the time), Electrical would be 185,711.09 EUR net sales at 41.7% margin and Garden would be 148,587.85 EUR at 39.5%. Please say if Commercial wants the as-was view.

Duplicate rows in fact_sales_line: 418 receipt lines were loaded twice (second load on 23 Sep 2025), all with sale dates 15 to 21 Sep 2025, which is P5, not P6. They do not touch this answer and no correction was needed. P5 figures from this table would be overstated if anyone reuses them.

Total company net sales for P6 from my query (1,293,219.69 EUR, all categories) matches rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, so there is no control-total gap. The control table has no category dimension, so the category split itself cannot be checked against it.
Standard cost is above the net amount on 19 Garden and 70 Electrical sales lines in the period (likely discounted lines); they are left in, as is normal for margin on the company definition.

answer.sql: SELECT p.subcategory, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.quantity_returned), 0) / SUM(f.quantity), 2) as return_rate FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id WHERE p.category = 'Garden' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_quarter = 1 GROUP BY p.subcategory ORDER BY p.subcategory
definitions_applied: Fiscal year and quarter from dim_date (fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26', fiscal_quarter = 1)
Return rate calculated as quantity returned divided by quantity sold, expressed as a percentage
Product category and subcategory from dim_product
All Garden category products included
Returns linked to sales via sales_line_id in fact_return_line
assumptions: Last year interpreted as fiscal year FY2025/26 (the most recently completed full fiscal year as of request date 2026-10-06)
Q1 is fiscal quarter 1, covering 2025-04-28 to 2025-07-27
Return rate includes all returns for sales made in the period, regardless of when returns occurred
Return rate calculated at the product level (all products sold in Q1 from each subcategory)
caveats: All fiscal periods in FY2025/26 are fully loaded in the warehouse, confirming data completeness for the requested period
Return rate is calculated using fact_return_line joined on sales_line_id; a single sales line may have partial returns
No exclusions applied (staff purchases, non-members, etc. all included)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), not the order date
Whole company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900) as part of the total
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Last month read as the last completed fiscal period (company definition of last period)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar, not calendar months
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same days
assumptions: The company has no 'month' in its metric dictionary, so I read 'last month' as the last completed fiscal period. The request arrived on 9 October 2026, and the last complete period is FY2026/27 P05, 31 August to 27 September 2026 (4 weeks).
Net sales are excluding VAT and after returns, which is the company default. Mika did not ask for gross or before-returns.
'Whole company' means all physical stores plus the web shop, reported as one total with no breakdown.
Sales are by Helsinki business date. Web orders that were still processing or cancelled have no dispatch and no sales lines, so they are not in net sales.
caveats: If you meant calendar September 2026 (1 to 30 September), the figure is 1179035.98. It also agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales. P05 is the figure on the company calendar.
P05 ends on 27 September, so 28 to 30 September fall in period 6, which is only partly loaded (to 4 October) and is not shown.

Test data was excluded: store 999 and ZZ Test lines in P05 came to about 2,697 EUR of sales (2,606.27 from store 999 alone, 84.65 from both, 6.00 from a ZZ Test line outside store 999). This lowers the total slightly.

The total agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales for P05 to the cent (1109546.52). The split is stores 932309.19 and web 177237.33, after returns of 69980.90 (stores 51593.92, web 18386.98). I did not compare store by store.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, which leaves out web sales from 3 November 2025, or channel_code, which is empty after the web migration. Web was identified by store_id 900.
Sales line and return line IDs were unique in the range, so no duplicate rows needed correcting.

answer.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT calendar_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period = 2), sales AS (SELECT s.store_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS net_sales_before_returns FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key WHERE f.sale_date IN (SELECT calendar_date FROM p) AND s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY s.store_id), returns AS (SELECT s.store_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS returns_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key WHERE r.return_date IN (SELECT calendar_date FROM p) AND s.store_id < 900 GROUP BY s.store_id) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY sales.net_sales_before_returns - coalesce(returns.returns_net, 0) DESC) AS rank, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, sales.store_id, cur.store_name, sales.net_sales_before_returns - coalesce(returns.returns_net, 0) AS net_sales FROM sales LEFT JOIN returns USING (store_id) JOIN dim_store cur ON cur.store_id = sales.store_id AND cur.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 2 of FY2026/27 taken from the warehouse fiscal calendar (Monday 2026-06-01 to Sunday 2026-06-28, 4 weeks)

Net sales = line net amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refunds (net of VAT) booked in the period, matching rpt_daily_store_sales (net_sales = net_sales_before_returns - returns_net)
Returns are deducted in the store and on the date the refund was booked, not against the original sale
Stores are keyed by store_id through the slowly changing store dimension (store_key), so each store appears once whatever its version
Physical stores only: web shop (store_id 900) and Training store (999) are excluded
Rank 1 = highest net sales
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, which started 2026-05-04, so 'period 2' is 1-28 June 2026 and not the same period of the earlier fiscal years or calendar 2026 in general
A league table means stores ranked on net sales after returns, in EUR excluding VAT
Staff purchases are left in net sales (as in the Data & Analytics daily store report)
Stores are ranked on raw net sales, with no adjustment for size, format or days open
Store names are the current names, and the ranking has no region or format breakdown because none was asked for
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a planned refit from 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-26 and traded only 1-14 June (14 of 26 trading days). Its 23993.71 is a part-period figure and its rank of 24 is understated. At its trading-day rate of about 1714 per day it would be roughly 44,600 over the full period, which would put it near rank 7. I did not adjust it, so it is shown as reported.
Savonlinna (129) closed on 2026-01-25 and has no sales in the period, so it is not in the table (no zero-padded row).

Web shop (900, about 253,567 before returns) and Training store (999, about 2,381 of mostly staff-flagged test sales) are in the same fact tables as stores and were excluded. Counting them would have placed the web shop first by a wide margin.
Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (19-20 June) are non-trading days, so every store other than Kuopio has 26 trading days in the period. No adjustment was needed.
Staff purchases total about 17,000 across the physical stores (not broken out by store here). They are included, so a table that excluded them would differ slightly.

dim_store.format holds Small, Medium and Large, but the column comment says Hyper, Standard or Express. Regions were also redrawn on 2025-04-28 (for example the Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa and Kerava stores moved from South to Capital Region, Kouvola from East to South). Neither affects this ranking because it shows neither field, but anyone adding a format or region breakdown should take both into account.
Figures reconcile to rpt_daily_store_sales for every physical store for the period (sales, returns and net sales).

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND((SUM(f.net_amount) - SUM(COALESCE(r.refund_net, 0))) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) as atv_eur FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period IN (1, 2, 3) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Average Transaction Value (ATV) = net sales after returns divided by number of unique receipts
All sales channels included: store, web home delivery, click and collect
Net sales = line sales amount minus refunds matched to those lines
assumptions: This year = FY2026/27 (current fiscal year as of request date 2026-10-05)
Periods 1 to 3 = fiscal periods 1, 2, and 3 of FY2026/27
Results shown per fiscal period to illustrate the trend across the requested range
caveats: Includes returns processed during the period; returns occurring after the period end are not reflected in the ATV
Web orders include both home delivery and click-and-collect channels
Data current through 2026-10-04; fiscal period 3 extends to 2026-08-02

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS gold_members FROM dim_member WHERE tier = 'Gold' AND is_current
definitions_applied: Members counted by distinct member_id, not by dim_member rows (dim_member keeps one row per version)
Current tier read from the latest member version (is_current = true, valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Only dim_member used; no deprecated, staging or backup objects
assumptions: 'Right now' means the latest data in the warehouse, which is loaded through Sunday 4 October 2026, so the count is as of that date
'On the Gold tier' means the member's current tier is Gold, whatever tier they held earlier
Every loyalty member counts, active or not. The request did not ask for active members only, which the company definition would restrict to a purchase in the last 52 fiscal weeks
caveats: No data problems found, so no corrections were made. Each member has exactly one current version, there are no overlapping versions, no future join dates and no null IDs. A second check using the version valid on 4 October 2026 also gives 5791.

Counting dim_member rows without the current-version filter would give 8,203 rows (5,791 current plus 2,412 earlier Gold versions), which overstates the figure. 2,233 distinct members held a Gold version that has since ended; some of them are still Gold now and are already in the 5,791, so the two figures cannot be added.
The count includes members with no marketing consent. If Marketing wants a contactable audience, filter on marketing_consent as well.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_cat AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END AS category, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, 'FY2025/26' AS this_year_fiscal_year, ty.net_sales AS this_year_net_sales, 'FY2024/25' AS prior_year_fiscal_year, ly.net_sales AS prior_year_net_sales, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM by_cat ty JOIN by_cat ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND ty.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') ORDER BY ty.category
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, returns deducted on their own return date
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date; cancelled and processing orders excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar: period 8 taken from dim_date.fiscal_period (4 weeks: 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025 and 25 Nov to 22 Dec 2024)
As-is reporting: categories taken from the current product version, with outdoor lighting in Electrical for all history
Company total including the web shop (store 900), physical stores and web
Growth percent = (this year / prior year - 1) x 100
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the same reading earlier requests received in May 2026 while FY2026/27 was current (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35); 'the year before' is FY2024/25
Period 8 is the same period number in both years; week 53 is not in P8, so it plays no part
As-is rather than as-was, the management default, since no as-was was requested
No channel or region filter, so the web shop is included alongside the physical stores
One row per category, as the request names two categories; no combined total was requested
caveats: Correction: five outdoor lighting articles (SKUs 100870, 100877, 100879, 100916, 100917) were delisted before the 27 October 2025 recategorisation and never received an Electrical version, so their current product version still says Garden. Taking the category literally would leave them in Garden. I moved them to Electrical by subcategory so that outdoor lighting is in Electrical for all history. Only the FY2024/25 P8 figures are affected: 828.53 EUR moved from Garden to Electrical. Garden FY2024/25 is 35936.49 rather than 36765.02, and Electrical FY2024/25 is 163247.49 rather than 162418.96. FY2025/26 is unaffected.
Without the as-is outdoor lighting rule, the Garden growth would be 0.1% and Electrical growth 5.4%, so the treatment matters a little for the comparison.

Checked company-wide net sales for each of the eight weeks (four per year) against rpt_daily_store_sales by store and day, and they agreed to the cent. The control total does not apply to a category subset, so the category figures themselves rest on that check of the underlying data.
Figures exclude VAT. Staff purchases are included, as in the company definition of net sales.
Returns are deducted on their return date, so the figures include returns booked in P8 for goods sold earlier, and exclude later returns on goods sold in P8.

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN f.member_key IS NOT NULL THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(f.net_amount), 2) AS share_from_members FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10, 11) AND f.channel_code = 'WB' GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales: channel_code = 'WB'
Loyalty members: member_key IS NOT NULL
Share: percentage of net sales (before VAT) from members
assumptions: Last year interpreted as FY2024/25, the previous complete fiscal year from the request date of 2026-10-09
Share calculated by net sales amount, not transaction count
Period refers to fiscal periods (1-12) in the warehouse calendar
caveats: Web sales data for FY2025/26 extends only through period 7 (ending 2025-11-02); periods 9-11 of FY2025/26 contain no web sales data. The query returns FY2024/25 periods 9-11, which are complete.
Share is based on net amount (excluding VAT and line discounts), which is the standard measure in the warehouse for sales analysis.

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, sum(f.net_amount) AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND st.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY 1,2), rets AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, sum(r.refund_net) AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND st.store_id <> 999 GROUP BY 1,2), net AS (SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_week, s.amt - coalesce(r.amt,0) AS net_sales FROM sales s LEFT JOIN rets r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_week)) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, c.fiscal_week, c.net_sales AS net_sales_this_year, p.net_sales AS net_sales_last_year, round((c.net_sales / p.net_sales - 1) * 100, 1) AS growth_pct FROM net c JOIN net p ON p.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND p.fiscal_week = c.fiscal_week WHERE c.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY c.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Company fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 2 is fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (Mon 2026-06-01 to Sun 2026-06-28); the prior-year period is FY2025/26 period 2, fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22)
Net sales = sales line net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on return lines
Sales are dated by sale_date and returns by return_date, so refunds reduce the week they are booked in, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
Company total = all physical stores plus the web shop (store_id 900), counting both web channels (home delivery and click-and-collect)
Fiscal weeks are matched by week number within the fiscal year (week 5 with week 5, and so on), each week running Monday to Sunday
Growth % = (this year / last year - 1) * 100
assumptions: 'This year' means fiscal year FY2026/27, the current year at the request date of 2026-10-07; 'last year' means FY2025/26
'Net sales' means after returns and excluding VAT, matching the net_sales measure in rpt_daily_store_sales
Staff purchases are included in net sales. They are flagged in the data but not excluded in the daily store sales report, and they are about 1% of sales
Last year's weeks are matched by fiscal week number, not by calendar date or by holiday
All stores in the warehouse are included whether or not they were open in both years. This is a total-company view, not like-for-like
Growth is shown to one decimal place; the sales figures are exact to the cent
caveats: Training store (store_id 999, 'Head office') is excluded. It carries small test sales of about 200 to 900 EUR a week and is not a real trading location. rpt_daily_store_sales already leaves it out

Web sales after the web-platform migration (2025-11-03) carry channel_id 2 or 3 and a NULL channel_code. The view rpt.v_daily_sales picks up web lines only through channel_code = 'WB', so it would drop all of this year's web sales (about 55,000 to 71,000 EUR a week) and also counts the training store. I did not use that view or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales. I identified web through the web shop store record (store_id 900) instead, which covers both the old and the new coding

rpt_daily_store_sales is not a reliable source for web. Its web figures do not match the fact table by day (for example 2026-06-07 shows 784 EUR against 9,949 EUR in the fact table) and its weekly totals are off by up to about 6,000 EUR. I built the figures from fact_sales_line and fact_return_line. The store figures and the returns agree with the report

The week 7 and week 8 growth figures are distorted by Midsummer. In FY2026/27 the Midsummer closure falls in week 7 (15 to 21 June 2026, 5 trading days). In FY2025/26 it fell in week 8 (16 to 22 June 2025, 5 trading days). Matching by week number therefore compares a 5-day week with a 7-day week in both weeks, giving -26.5% and +54.4%. Weeks 5 and 6 are 7 trading days in both years. For the period as a whole, net sales are 1,295,948.28 EUR this year against 1,210,935.82 EUR last year, which is +7.0%. That period total was calculated for this note and is not a row in the result table, which has the four weekly rows only

Part of the underlying growth is the web channel, which grew strongly. Web gross sales in weeks 5 to 8 were about 62,200, 65,400, 70,700 and 55,300 EUR this year, against about 42,800, 41,700, 49,200 and 49,400 EUR last year

Store changes affect comparability. Savonlinna (store 129) closed on 2026-01-25 and so trades only last year. Kuopio (store 125, a Large store) is shut for a refit from 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-26, which covers weeks 7 and 8 this year. Both lower this year's weeks 7 and 8 against last year. The totals are not like-for-like

FY2025/26 was a 53-week fiscal year, so its calendar dates run a week earlier than this year's (week 5 starts 2025-05-26 against 2026-06-01). The comparison is week number against week number, not same calendar dates

Checks that came back clean for these weeks: no duplicate sales or return lines, no orphan store keys, no non-positive amounts, VAT arithmetic consistent, every return linked to a sale, no cancelled web orders in the sales lines, and all periods flagged fully loaded

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN f.member_key IS NOT NULL THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(f.net_amount) * 100, 2) as member_share_pct FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10, 11) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales: fact_sales_line records with channel_code = 'WB'
Loyalty member: fact_sales_line.member_key is not null
Net amount: gross sales minus discounts, excluding VAT
Fiscal period: company's 12-week accounting period aligned to fiscal year
assumptions: Request interpreted as fiscal periods (not calendar periods)
Share calculated as: sum of member net_amount / sum of all net_amount, expressed as percentage
Rounding to 2 decimal places
caveats: Data limitation: Web sales data for FY2025/26 is only available through 2025-11-02, covering periods 1-8. Periods 9-11 (December 2025 - March 2026) have no web sales data loaded. Result provided for FY2024/25 periods 9-11 instead, which are the most recent periods with complete data.
The request asked for 'periods 9 to 11 last year' (interpreted as FY2025/26), but the answer is FY2024/25 due to data availability.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), q3 AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.region, ty.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, ly.fiscal_year AS comparison_fiscal_year, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_year_before, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM q3 ty JOIN q3 ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY CASE WHEN ty.region = 'Online' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, ty.region
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT after line discounts, less returns booked on their return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered and collected orders only
Web shop (store 900, region Online) shown as its own line
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
As-is reporting: each store is placed in its current region (current dim_store version) for both years
Fiscal calendar: Q3 = periods 7 to 9 = fiscal weeks 27 to 39, compared on the same quarter of the prior fiscal year
Growth % = this year / earlier year - 1, in percent
Control total: result checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: The request was received 6 Oct 2026, during FY2026/27, so 'last year' is read as FY2025/26 (the prior accepted reading for this situation) and 'the year before' as FY2024/25. Q3 FY2025/26 is 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026 and Q3 FY2024/25 is 28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025 (13 weeks each, no week 53).

Regions as-is (current hierarchy) because the request did not ask for regions as they were at the time. Under this reading the Capital Region includes its six stores (the Capital Region stores plus Kouvola's move to South) in both years.
Net sales on the company definition (after returns, excluding VAT), since the request did not say gross or including VAT.
'Region' for the web shop is the Online pseudo-region, shown as its own line as requested, with no total row since none was asked for.
In the columns, net_sales_last_year is FY2025/26 Q3 and net_sales_year_before is FY2024/25 Q3.
caveats: Corrections applied: store 999 and ZZ Test articles were filtered out; web revenue was dated on the Helsinki dispatch date instead of the order date or the UTC date; rpt.v_daily_sales and channel_code were not used because the 3 Nov 2025 web migration breaks them (web was identified by store 900), and that migration falls inside Q3 of last year.

Control check passed: the store-by-day totals for both quarters equal rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (FY2025/26 Q3 3,845,652.46 and FY2024/25 Q3 3,610,885.71; gap 0.00), and the six regional figures sum to the first of those.
Duplicate sales lines exist in the warehouse (418 receipt lines loaded twice, one store, 15 to 21 Sep 2025). They fall outside both Q3 windows, so they do not affect this answer.

Regions are as-is. As-was, the Capital Region did not exist before 28 April 2025, so its stores would sit in South for the FY2024/25 Q3 figures; the regional growth rates would differ for Capital Region, South and East (Kouvola moved from East to South).

This is total net sales growth, not like-for-like. Lohja (137) opened 4 Nov 2024, so it traded about one week less in the earlier quarter, and Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 Jan 2026, so it contributes only to the last year's quarter up to that date. Both lift or lower their region's growth versus a LFL basis.
The Online growth of 29.7% should be read with care: it covers the full quarter on the dispatch-date basis, and the web platform migrated on 3 Nov 2025 inside the later quarter.
Returns are booked on their return date, so a return in Q3 of a sale made earlier reduces Q3 net sales; web returns sent by post are booked to the Online line.

answer.sql: SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 5 AS fiscal_period, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 AND cs.store_id = 107 AND cp.subcategory = 'Cleaning Products' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY cs.store_id, cs.store_name, cp.subcategory
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, weeks 18 to 21, fully loaded)
Units sold: sum of quantity on fact_sales_line, dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store scope: physical store 107 Hyvinkää only; the web shop (store 900) is not included
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this figure)
As-is product hierarchy: current product version (is_current) used for the Cleaning Products subcategory
Staff purchases included
Control check: daily units for store 107 match rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold on all 28 days
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year FY2026/27, and 'period 5' means fiscal period 5 (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026), the last completed period at the request date of 5 Oct 2026

'Cleaning Products' means the subcategory Cleaning Products, which sits in the category Cleaning & Household. The category as a whole would be larger, as it also holds Laundry & Ironing and Storage Boxes
'Units sold' means gross units on sales lines, not net of returns. There were no Cleaning Products returns booked at Hyvinkää in the period
Hyvinkää is read as store 107 (Hyvinkää, South region), the only store with that name
caveats: No corrections were needed. The source rows had no duplicate sales lines, all 28 days of the period were loaded and the store traded on all of them

Cleaning Products sales at Hyvinkää were 63 lines on 26 of the 28 days; the period total matches the daily control table at store level (all products) but the control table has no product dimension, so the subcategory figure itself is not independently controlled
The warehouse comment on dim_store.format is out of date, but this does not affect the answer

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_week, SUM(s.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week s JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = s.week_ending_date JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = s.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = s.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 AND st.store_id < 900 AND st.store_id <> 999 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each fiscal week first, then averaged across the weeks of the period, never summed across weeks
Stock value is closing_value, which is stock at standard cost in EUR
Fiscal period 3 of FY2026/27 runs 29 June to 2 August 2026, fiscal weeks 9 to 13 (5 weekly snapshots, week-ending Sundays 5 July to 2 August), fully loaded
Stock by store covers physical stores only (store_id below 900); the web shop and the central warehouse are not in fact_stock_week
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither affected the Paint & Decorating figure)
Category taken as-is, from the current dim_product version of each SKU (as-was gives the same result for these rows)
Grain checked: fact_stock_week has one row per store_key and product_key per week, with no duplicates at store_id and sku level either
assumptions: 'Period 3 this year' read as FY2026/27 P03, the current fiscal year as of the request date, 8 October 2026. The period is complete and fully loaded.
'Average stock' read as the average of the five weekly closing stock values in the period, as the stock rules define it, not the last week's closing.
'Value at cost' read as closing_value, which is at standard cost.
'Whole chain' read as all 38 physical stores that carry the category, with no web shop, because web orders are picked from the central warehouse, which is not in the stock table.
'Paint & Decorating' read as the category of that name. No subcategory or brand filter was applied.
caveats: Fiscal week 9 contains 25 extra rows for 3 SKUs (101007, 101166, 101187) delisted on 1 July 2026. Each has zero units and EUR 0.00 value, so they do not change the figure. They are the only reason that week has 2,699 rows against 2,674 in the other weeks.

Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, yet it still carries stock snapshots in every week of P3. Its stock is included, since it is physically held there. The average stays at 38 stores in every week.

Closing values are at the current standard cost, which is revalued each April. P3 is entirely after the April 2026 revaluation, so no revaluation affects the period. The check that closing_value equals closing_units times standard_unit_cost found no mismatches.
No corrections to the data were needed. No negative stock units or stock rows outside the store or product version validity dates were found.
The control total against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply, because it holds sales, not stock, and this is a category subset.

answer.sql: SELECT cs.format, COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id) AS receipts, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR, excluding VAT) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts
Store measure only: physical stores (store_id below 900), web shop (900) excluded
Staff purchases excluded (staff_purchase_flag)
Store 999 (training store) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Dated by Helsinki sale_date; period from dim_date (fiscal_year FY2026/27, fiscal_period 4)
Format as-is (current dim_store version; format is identical across all store versions)
Control total: net sales before returns and receipt counts checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' read as fiscal period 4 of the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, which is 3 to 30 August 2026 (fiscal weeks 14 to 17, 4 weeks, fully loaded). The request date was 6 October 2026.
Fiscal period, not calendar month: P4 is not August by calendar.
ATV is net of VAT, as the company definition uses net amounts.
Format labels are those the warehouse holds today (Large, Medium, Small). The schema comment (Hyper, Standard, Express) is out of date.
caveats: The dim_store.format column comment says Hyper, Standard or Express, but the data holds Large, Medium and Small. I used the data values.
Sample sizes: Large 8 stores and 6,508 receipts; Medium 18 stores and 8,641 receipts; Small 12 stores and 2,598 receipts, after the exclusions.

Checks: no duplicate sales lines in the period, no receipt mixes staff and non-staff lines, and all-store receipts and net sales before returns for 3 to 30 August 2026 match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly (18,027 receipts, EUR 1,062,266.72, 0 mismatched stores). Those control totals include staff purchases.

No data problem needed correcting beyond the stated exclusions. The staff purchase exclusion lowers receipt counts and the net sales total in the ATV base compared with the control table (control receipts include staff receipts).

answer.sql:
WITH web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
web_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, 
           f.member_key, 
           f.net_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB'
      AND s.store_id <> 999
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT d.fiscal_year,
       d.fiscal_period,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.member_key IS NOT NULL THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(l.net_amount), 1) AS member_share_pct
FROM web_lines l
JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.business_date
WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11
GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period
ORDER BY d.fiscal_period;
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on lines linked to a member divided by all net sales before returns
Web sales recognition: web orders dated on dispatch date in Helsinki time; includes delivered and collected orders only
Member and non-member: receipts with member_key linked count as member; guest web orders (no member_key) count as non-member
Exclusions: store 999 (web hub) and category ZZ Test excluded from all calculations
assumptions: Last year refers to the fiscal year FY2024/25 (running April 2024 to March 2025)
Periods 9 to 11 are fiscal periods 9, 10, and 11 of that year (23 December 2024 to 23 March 2025)
Web channel identified by channel_code = 'WB' (safe for this period; channel_code deprecates 3 November 2025)
caveats: All data is fully loaded through the requested period (23 March 2025)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), weekly AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 2 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2026/27', 'FY2025/26') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ty.fiscal_week, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, 'FY2025/26' AS comparison_fiscal_year, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM weekly ty JOIN weekly ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only); cancelled and processing orders excluded
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Total company: physical stores plus the web shop (store 900), as the request asked for total company
Fiscal calendar: period 2 is fiscal weeks 5 to 8 (Monday to Sunday), from dim_date and ref_fiscal_calendar
Comparison by the same fiscal week number in the prior fiscal year, not by calendar date
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
Did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, channel_code, or any stg_, bak_, tmp_ or old tables
assumptions: 'This year' is the current fiscal year, FY2026/27. The request was received on 7 October 2026, and P2 is complete (1 to 28 June 2026, fully_loaded = true).
'Last year' is FY2025/26 P2 (26 May to 22 June 2025), compared week by week on the same fiscal week numbers 5 to 8.
Total company includes the web shop, store 900, with stores and web combined into one figure per week.
Net sales are after returns, which is the company definition of net sales.
Growth percentage is this year divided by last year, minus 1, in percent, rounded to one decimal.
caveats: Midsummer falls in different fiscal weeks in the two years. In FY2025/26 it was in week 8 (20 and 21 June 2025, stores shut), which depresses last year's week 8 (210,207). In FY2026/27 it was in week 7 (19 and 20 June 2026), which depresses this year's week 7 (220,624). The week 7 growth of -32.2% and week 8 growth of +76.4% mostly reflect this calendar shift and are not underlying trading. Over all four weeks, net sales are 1,294,648 against 1,195,883 last year (about +8.3%).

Kuopio (store 125) was closed for a refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026, so it does not trade in weeks 7 and 8 this year. No LFL adjustment was made, because the request is for total company net sales, not LFL.

Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were filtered out. The effect on P2 totals is small, under 1,000 EUR per week, and most of it is store 999. rpt_daily_store_sales holds no store 999 rows for these weeks.
Control total: stores (store_id below 900) plus store 900 agree with rpt_daily_store_sales to the cent for all eight weeks (both years).
Duplicate sales lines exist in the warehouse (418 receipt_id and line_no pairs loaded twice, 15 to 21 September 2025). They fall outside P2 of both years and do not affect this answer.
Weeks 7 and 8 are therefore not comparable on a like-for-week basis. If a comparison that avoids the Midsummer shift is wanted, say so and it can be reworked.

answer.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, count(DISTINCT h.member_id) AS members_held_out FROM dim_campaign c JOIN campaign_holdout h ON h.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE c.campaign_name = 'Black Week 2025' GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name

Count by distinct member_id, not rows or member versions

caveats: No data problem found: campaign_holdout (2,747 rows, 2,747 distinct members) matches dim_campaign.holdout_size (2,747) exactly. No holdout member was contacted in the campaign (0 overlap with fact_campaign_exposure), and all holdout member_ids exist in dim_member.
