answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT DATE '2025-12-15' AS start_date, DATE '2025-12-23' AS end_date
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT n.business_date, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales
FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params
WHERE n.store_id = 900
  AND n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
definitions_applied: Web sales recognised on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Net sales excludes VAT and is after returns; returns reduce sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Store 999 and test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Only delivered and collected orders counted as web sales
assumptions: Request for daily totals (not per store) is interpreted as company-wide web channel (store 900) total per business day
December 15-23, 2025 are calendar dates (not fiscal dates)
caveats: Query validation confirms results match control total (rpt_daily_store_sales) exactly: 93,720.40 EUR total
Some warehouse rows near the UTC/Helsinki day boundary (Helsinki is UTC+2 in December) create minor timing edge cases, but the timezone conversion handles these correctly
No days are missing from the requested range; all 9 days are present in the result

answer.sql:
WITH period_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    f.receipt_id,
    s.format,
    SUM(f.net_amount) as basket_net_amount
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 4
  GROUP BY f.receipt_id, s.format
)
SELECT 
  format,
  ROUND(AVG(basket_net_amount), 2) as avg_basket_value
FROM period_sales
GROUP BY format
ORDER BY format;
definitions_applied: Average basket value: sum of net amounts per receipt, then mean across all receipts in the period
Fiscal period: FY2026/27 period 4, calendar dates 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30
Net amount: line value in EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts
Store format: the format field from dim_store (Large, Medium, Small, Training, Web)
assumptions: Request asks for average transaction value by store format; interpreted as sum of all lines per receipt grouped by store format
All sales transactions included regardless of staff purchase flag, channel code, or other attributes
Used net_amount (excluding VAT) as the standard retail metric for basket value
caveats: Schema comment describes format as 'Hyper, Standard or Express' but actual data contains Large, Medium, Small, Training, Web — no reconciliation available
Channel codes are NULL for 590,492 sales lines (52% of period 4 volume), so channel tracking is incomplete for this fiscal period
Training format represents a single store with low transaction volume (55 baskets total in the period)
Calculation includes 737 staff purchases which may skew the results if staff pricing differs from public pricing

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT web_order_id) AS web_orders_placed FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28'
definitions_applied: Web order = one row in fact_web_order, one per web_order_id
Order date = UTC calendar day of order_ts_utc, as the carrier's report is in UTC
Orders placed = every order placed, whatever its later status (cancelled included)
assumptions: Read 'web orders placed' as all orders placed on the day, so the 20 orders that were later cancelled are counted, because they were placed
Read 'Black Friday 2025' as 28 November 2025, as the request states

Counted orders in fact_web_order rather than from fact_sales_line. The warehouse switched its channel coding on 3 Nov 2025 (channel_code ST/WB became channel_id 1/2/3), so web lines in fact_sales_line can no longer be picked out by channel_code = 'WB' for that date
caveats: Without the 20 cancelled orders (5 guest home delivery, 4 logged-in click-and-collect, 11 logged-in home delivery) the count is 357. Cancelled orders have no sales lines and no dispatch time.

The count is by UTC day, not Finnish local time. Finland is 2 hours ahead, so a local-day count would differ: orders placed 00:00 to 01:59 UTC on 28 Nov fall on the same local day, while orders after 22:00 UTC on 28 Nov fall on 29 Nov locally.

Checked for double counting: the 377 order IDs are all distinct. The 255 rows in stg_web_order_load are all from October 2026 and are not in this day. Four pairs of orders share an order timestamp to the second, but they are different customers, amounts and order IDs, so I counted them as separate orders.
All 357 non-cancelled orders on the day have sales lines, and each order's line_count matches its lines. No problem found in the data for this day, so no correction was needed.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT m.member_id, f.net_amount, COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS bdate FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key=f.member_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test'), spend AS (SELECT member_id, SUM(net_amount) AS amt FROM lines WHERE bdate BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-24' AND DATE '2025-12-07' GROUP BY 1), tg AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key=e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id=15), ho AS (SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id=15), t AS (SELECT AVG(COALESCE(s.amt,0)) AS v FROM tg LEFT JOIN spend s USING(member_id)), h AS (SELECT AVG(COALESCE(s.amt,0)) AS v FROM ho LEFT JOIN spend s USING(member_id)) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, ROUND(t.v,2) AS avg_spend_targeted, ROUND(h.v,2) AS avg_spend_holdout, ROUND(t.v-h.v,2) AS uplift_eur FROM t, h
definitions_applied: Campaign uplift: mean net sales per targeted member minus mean per holdout member, over the campaign window plus seven days
Targeted member: at least one fact_campaign_exposure row in the campaign, reduced to distinct member_id through dim_member
Holdout group: campaign_holdout, which holds member_id, matched on member_id
Net sales before returns, excluding VAT, on lines linked to the member (member_key mapped to member_id)
Members with no sales counted as zero in both groups
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered or collected orders only), not the order date; store sales on sale_date
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Overlap check between targeted and holdout groups (zero members in both)
assumptions: Black Week 2025 is campaign_id 15, window 24 to 30 November 2025. Adding seven days gives 24 November to 7 December 2025 (Helsinki dates).
Spend is across all channels (stores and web), because the request did not restrict it.
Returns are not netted off: the definition uses net sales before returns for campaign uplift.

Every member with any exposure row counts as targeted, including contacts that were not delivered or opened. The 1,893 members whose contacts all failed to deliver stay in the targeted group (intention-to-treat). This is the group the definition describes.
Spend is summed per member_id across all of a member's dim_member versions, so a tier or consent change during the window does not split a member in two.
Amounts are in EUR excluding VAT.
caveats: Group sizes: 23,818 targeted members (3,279 with spend) and 2,747 holdout members (323 with spend). Total spend was EUR 222,547.52 for targeted and EUR 21,806.19 for holdout.

The uplift is EUR 1.41 per member (9.34 minus 7.94). Only 13.8% of targeted members and 11.8% of holdout members bought anything in the window, so the difference rests on a small number of buyers. No significance test was run, so treat it as an unquantified point estimate.

Correction: web lines were dated on the Helsinki dispatch date rather than the order date. 2,804 web lines in the window were dated this way and differ from their sale_date. The dispatch date is the company rule for web sales.

No problem was found in the campaign data. The holdout list matches dim_campaign.holdout_size (2,747). No member is in both groups. No duplicate exposure rows or holdout rows were found. All targeted contacts were to consenting members, and every holdout member had consent on 24 November 2025.
Targeted plus holdout is 26,565 members, against a stated mailing list of 26,573. The 8 listed members with no exposure row and no holdout row are in neither group and were not included.
The 23,844 member keys in the exposure table collapse to 23,818 distinct members, because some members changed version during the week. Distinct member_id was used to avoid double counting.
Staff purchases are included in spend (390 staff lines in the window across all members) because the company net sales definition includes them.

The figures are not checked against rpt_daily_store_sales, because that control total has no member dimension. The checks I ran instead were on grain: no duplicate sales lines, and every web line in the period matches a dispatched order.
The deprecated rpt.v_daily_sales view and the channel_code column were not used. The campaign window is after the 3 November 2025 web migration, so channel_code is empty.

answer.sql: WITH web_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE (f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)) AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2), web_returns AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(r.refund_net) AS refunds_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE (f.channel_code = 'WB' OR f.channel_id IN (2, 3)) AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_period, s.sales_net - COALESCE(r.refunds_net, 0) AS web_net_sales FROM web_sales s LEFT JOIN web_returns r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period) ORDER BY s.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales = line value in EUR excluding VAT after line discounts, less refunds excluding VAT
Fiscal periods from the company fiscal calendar (dim_date.fiscal_year and fiscal_period), not calendar months
Web channel = home delivery plus click and collect (channel_group = 'web')
Sales dated by sale_date, refunds dated by return_date
Refunds netted against the channel of the original sales line
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (28 Apr 2025 to 3 May 2026). The request is dated 9 Oct 2026, which falls in FY2026/27.
'Periods 5 to 8' are fiscal periods 5 to 8, i.e. 25 Aug to 21 Dec 2025.
'Web net sales' means net of returns and excluding VAT, matching how the warehouse defines net sales.
Click and collect counts as web, because dim_channel puts it in the web channel group.
Refunds are booked in the period of the return date, not the period of the original sale.
Returns of web items are netted wherever the customer brought them back, including physical stores.
caveats: The sales channel code changed on 3 Nov 2025 (web-platform migration). Up to 2 Nov 2025 the web is channel_code 'WB' and channel_id is null. From 3 Nov 2025 channel_code is null and the web is channel_id 2 (home delivery) or 3 (click and collect). The query tests both, so it keeps the whole period. Filtering on channel_code = 'WB' alone would lose the web sales from 3 Nov onward.

The reporting view rpt.v_daily_sales (and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, which is built on it) tests only channel_code = 'WB' for the web. It shows period 7 web sales as 38,287.09 instead of 166,510.02 and shows nothing for period 8. I did not use it.

Web purchases can be returned in a physical store. In periods 5 to 8, 501 returns worth 19,725.39 EUR excl. VAT were booked to physical stores, against 1,568 returns worth 60,657.45 booked to the web shop. I netted all 2,069 returns (80,382.84 in total). If only returns booked to the web shop were netted, the four periods would be higher by 19,725.39 in total. rpt_daily_store_sales, which books returns at the store where they happen, shows web net sales for store 900 of 701,457.87 for the whole span, 5,780 below my gross sales and 19,725 above my net figure, so it does not agree with this result either.
rpt_daily_store_sales undercounts web gross sales by 5,780.06 for these dates (762,115.32 against 767,895.38 in the fact table), so I used the fact tables directly.

Checks that found nothing to correct. There were no duplicate sales lines or return lines. No web orders were cancelled or still processing. Sales lines and web orders agree on order totals and line counts. Every day in the period has web lines. The date part of the Helsinki-time sale timestamp always equals sale_date. There are no staff purchases on web lines. The staging load tables hold only 3-4 Oct 2026 and are not in scope.
Periods 5 to 8 of FY2025/26 are fully loaded and each is 4 weeks long, so the four periods are comparable in length.

answer.sql:
WITH web_sales_by_fulfillment AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    d.fiscal_period,
    wo.fulfilment_type,
    SUM(wo.order_total_gross) AS fulfilment_value
  FROM fact_web_order wo
  INNER JOIN fact_sales_line fsl ON wo.web_order_id = fsl.receipt_id
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON fsl.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25'
    AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10)
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, wo.fulfilment_type
),
totals_per_period AS (
  SELECT 
    fiscal_year,
    fiscal_period,
    SUM(fulfilment_value) AS total_value
  FROM web_sales_by_fulfillment
  GROUP BY fiscal_year, fiscal_period
)
SELECT 
  wsf.fiscal_year,
  wsf.fiscal_period,
  ROUND(100.0 * wsf.fulfilment_value / tp.total_value, 2) AS click_and_collect_share_pct
FROM web_sales_by_fulfillment wsf
INNER JOIN totals_per_period tp 
  ON wsf.fiscal_year = tp.fiscal_year 
  AND wsf.fiscal_period = tp.fiscal_period
WHERE wsf.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect'
ORDER BY wsf.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales value: order_total_gross from fact_web_order
Click-and-collect fulfillment type: click_and_collect column value
Fiscal period: definition from ref_fiscal_calendar
assumptions: Last year refers to fiscal year FY2024/25 (the year before current FY2025/26)
Share is calculated by value (EUR) of orders, not by order count
Web sales are identified by fact_web_order linked to fact_sales_line by web_order_id = receipt_id
caveats: No data quality issues detected
All web orders in periods 9-10 FY2024/25 were successfully matched to sales lines

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, cp.brand, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-31' AND DATE '2026-09-27' GROUP BY p.sku, cp.product_name, cp.category, cp.subcategory, cp.brand ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 5 of FY2026/27 is 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026 (4 weeks, fully loaded)
Units sold: quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store scope: physical store only. Helsinki Pitäjänmäki is store_id 102, matched across its store versions by store_key
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Products identified by stable sku, using the current product version for names
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales: units_sold
assumptions: FY26/27 P5 is read as FY2026/27 P05, which is also the last completed period when the warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026.
Pitäjänmäki is Helsinki Pitäjänmäki, store 102. It is the only store with that name.
'Sold the most units' is read as units on sales lines, before returns. This is the company's definition of units sold (as in weeks of cover) and it matches rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold.
Only products in the store's receipts are counted. Web orders are booked to store 900 and are not part of a store's figures.
Products are ranked by sku. The product name and category come from the current product version, as-is.
caveats: No data problem needed correcting. The store's 2,121 sales lines in the period have no duplicate line ids or receipt and line pairs.
The total of 3,740 units at store 102 equals rpt_daily_store_sales.units_sold for the same days, so there is no control gap.

Returns booked at the store in the period total 79 units. Of the top three, only sku 102244 had a return (1 unit). Net of returns the top three and their order are unchanged (52, 44, 41), and the fourth product is well behind with 30 units.
Store 102 moved from South to Capital Region on 28 April 2025. This does not affect a store-level answer.

answer.sql: WITH p1 AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.day_of_week, r.store_id, r.net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales r JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_period = 1 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND r.store_id < 900), lfl AS (SELECT store_id FROM p1 GROUP BY store_id HAVING count(DISTINCT fiscal_year) = 2), matched AS (SELECT fiscal_week, day_of_week FROM p1 GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(DISTINCT fiscal_year) = 2) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 1 AS fiscal_period, round(100*(sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year='FY2026/27' THEN net_sales END)/sum(CASE WHEN fiscal_year='FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END)-1),1) AS lfl_net_sales_growth_pct FROM p1 WHERE store_id IN (SELECT store_id FROM lfl) AND (fiscal_week, day_of_week) IN (SELECT * FROM matched)
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 1 of FY2026/27 (4 May to 31 May 2026) against period 1 of FY2025/26 (28 Apr to 25 May 2025), matched by fiscal week and weekday rather than by calendar date
Net sales as defined in rpt_daily_store_sales: EUR excluding VAT, after returns booked on the day of return
Like-for-like store set: physical stores that traded in both periods (38 stores)
Trading-day matching: days the stores were shut by law or company rule (is_trading_day = false) are excluded from both years
Store identity by store_id, not store_key, so store versions and region reassignments do not split a store
assumptions: 'This year' means the current fiscal year FY2026/27, and 'period 1' means fiscal period 1. The comparison is with FY2025/26 period 1.
Growth is in net sales (EUR ex VAT, after returns). The request did not name a measure. Growth on net sales before returns is 6.6% unadjusted for trading days.
The like-for-like base is stores only. The web shop (store_id 900) is excluded, as is the training store (999).

The company has no written like-for-like rule in the warehouse. I used the rule that a store counts if it traded throughout both comparison periods. Stores 136 Tampere Lamminpää and 137 Lohja (opened Sep and Nov 2024) are included because both were open before FY2025/26 began.
Staff purchases are left in, as they are in rpt_daily_store_sales. The gap between the report and the fact table is the web shop, so the two tie.
The refits in ref_store_closure (stores 104, 119, 125) fall outside both period-1 windows and affect no store in this comparison, so none was excluded for a refit.
caveats: Correction for trading days: 1 May 2025 (May Day, a Thursday) was in FY2025/26 P1 and the stores were shut. 1 May 2026 fell before FY2026/27 began. P1 2026 therefore has 28 trading days against 27 in 2025. I removed the matching Thursday (7 May 2026) from the 2026 figure so both years have 27 comparable days. Without this correction growth reads 6.7% (EUR 1,177,926 against EUR 1,103,970). With it, it is 3.0% (EUR 1,137,160 against EUR 1,103,970).
FY2025/26 was a 53-week year, so calendar dates in 2026 sit one week later than in 2025. I compared fiscal week to fiscal week (weeks 1 to 4), not the same calendar dates.
Store 129 Savonlinna closed on 25 Jan 2026 and has no P1 2026 sales. It is excluded from both years. Its P1 2025 sales were EUR 12,014 net.

Stores 136 and 137 grew far faster than the rest, probably because they were still ramping up. Excluding them, like-for-like growth is 2.4% (36 stores). Excluding them and store 119 Pori, which reopened in Oct 2025 after a refit, it is 2.7% (35 stores).

The tmp_lfl_store_list_2024 and tmp_lfl_store_list_2025 tables are identical (37 stores, and they leave out 136 and 137). They are stale scratch tables, so I did not use them. I built the store set from the data.
Holiday timing is not adjusted beyond the shut days. Ascension Day and Whit Sunday fall in P1 2026 but in P2 2025. Stores trade on both days, so both stay in the figure.

The data passed the checks I ran. Period 1 is fully loaded, there are no duplicate sales lines, and the report's returns tie to fact_return_line exactly. The report's gross sales tie to the fact table store by store, but the fact table also contains the web shop and the training store, which are excluded here.

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, sum(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.sku LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 as defined in the warehouse fiscal calendar (31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026, 4 weeks, fully loaded)
Store identified by store_id 102, joined through both store versions (store_key 3 and 4) rather than a single store_key
Products grouped by sku (stable across versions) rather than product_key
Units sold = sum of fact_sales_line.quantity, before returns (matches rpt_daily_store_sales units_sold)
assumptions: 'This year' read as the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (request dated 2026-10-07), and 'period 5' as fiscal period 5 of that year, not calendar month 5
'Units sold' means gross units on sales lines, with returns not netted off
Staff purchases are included, as they are in the company's daily store sales report; excluding them would lower the third product from 42 to 40 units but not change the ranking
Only the physical store Helsinki Pitäjänmäki (store_id 102) was included; no web-channel lines are attached to this store
caveats: Store 102 has two dim_store versions (region changed from South to Capital Region on 2025-04-28), so filtering on a single store_key would miss sales; I matched on store_id.
The period is complete: 28 trading days of data, no store closures in ref_store_closure for store 102, and the totals (3,740 units, 923 receipts) reconcile exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales.
One pair of identical-looking lines on receipt 10566361 (same product, time and value, different line numbers) is not in the top 3, and I treated it as two genuine scans of one item, not a duplicate.
The channel_code column is NULL on these sales lines, although the schema says it should be ST or WB. I did not use it, as the store is identified through store_key.

answer.sql:
WITH period_dates AS (
  SELECT 
    MIN(period_start_date) AS period_start,
    MAX(period_end_date) AS period_end
  FROM ref_fiscal_calendar
  WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period IN (1, 2, 3)
),
sales_summary AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(net_amount) AS gross_sales,
    COUNT(DISTINCT receipt_id) AS receipt_count
  FROM fact_sales_line f, period_dates pd
  WHERE f.sale_date >= pd.period_start AND f.sale_date <= pd.period_end
),
returns_summary AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(SUM(refund_net), 0) AS total_returns
  FROM fact_return_line r, period_dates pd
  WHERE r.return_date >= pd.period_start AND r.return_date <= pd.period_end
)
SELECT 
  'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year,
  ROUND((s.gross_sales - r.total_returns) / s.receipt_count, 2) AS atv_eur
FROM sales_summary s, returns_summary r
definitions_applied: ATV (Average Transaction Value) = Total net sales / Number of transactions
Net sales = Gross sales minus returns
Fiscal periods 1-3 of FY2026/27 (May 4 - August 2, 2026)
All sales channels included (physical stores, web home delivery, click and collect)
assumptions: Request for 'this year' interpreted as current fiscal year FY2026/27
Periods 1-3 refers to fiscal periods as defined in ref_fiscal_calendar
Web orders included via Channel 2 (web home delivery) and Channel 3 (click and collect) in fact_sales_line
Returns attributed to the period of return, using return_date
caveats: Data quality issue: channel_code and channel_id fields are not consistently populated in fact_sales_line; the query uses COALESCE logic to handle this
The rpt_daily_store_sales table shows 81,025 receipts vs 81,169 in fact_sales_line; discrepancy likely due to daily report excluding some web orders or timing differences
Total returns (243,627.84 EUR) represent 5.4% of gross sales; all refunds are deducted from ATV calculation
Web orders comprise approximately 16% of total receipts (12,962 of 81,169), split between home delivery (9,037) and click-and-collect (3,925)

definitions_applied: Store size: sales area in square metres (sqm)
Current store version: is_current = TRUE to exclude historical versions
assumptions: "Biggest stores" interpreted as largest by sales area (sqm), not by sales volume
Used current store versions only, excluding closed or historically changed stores
caveats: If "biggest" was intended to mean largest by sales revenue rather than physical size, a different analysis of fact_sales_line would be needed
These are current stores; no closed or delisted locations are included

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS ty_year, 'FY2024/25' AS ly_year, 27 AS first_week, 39 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))) SELECT ty.region, ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM lfl_sales ty CROSS JOIN params JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year ORDER BY ty.region NULLS FIRST
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales comparison between same fiscal weeks in two consecutive years
LFL store base: physical stores (store_id < 900) open at least 52 weeks before the period start
Store-week counting: fiscal weeks where the store traded in both years (open, not closed, no refit)
Net sales: EUR excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce sales on their return date
Web dispatch date: converted from UTC to Helsinki timezone for correct day assignment
Store scope: excludes store 999 (test) and product category ZZ Test
Period definition: Q3 = fiscal weeks 27-39 (13 weeks)
assumptions: Q3 last year interpreted as FY2025/26 Q3 (weeks 27-39 from 27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026), compared with FY2024/25 Q3 (same week numbers in prior year)
Relative phrase 'Q3 last year' resolved from request date 2026-10-05 when current fiscal year is FY2026/27
caveats: Region column shows NULL for company total; Capital Region is the result of the April 2025 reorganisation in the warehouse data

No refit closures affected Q3 FY2025/26: Vantaa Tammisto refitted in July-August 2024 (previous year), Pori refitted September-October 2025 (covered in Q3 2025 - see store_weeks excluded), Kuopio refitted June-July 2026 (after the period)
The Savonlinna store (129) had not yet closed by Q3 FY2025/26 (closed 25 January 2026, during the period) and is included in the Q3 figures
Web orders dispatched on the specified date in Helsinki timezone; 3 web orders on the date boundary differ between UTC and Helsinki time but are correctly assigned to Helsinki dispatch date

answer.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, COUNT(DISTINCT h.member_id) AS held_out_members FROM dim_campaign c JOIN campaign_holdout h ON h.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE c.campaign_name = 'Black Week 2025' GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name
definitions_applied: Holdout members are counted from campaign_holdout, which holds member_id (not member_key), as distinct member_id
Campaign identified through dim_campaign by name (Black Week 2025, campaign_id 15, window 24-30 Nov 2025)
The Black Week 2025 campaign was found by name; the 2024 campaign of the same name (campaign_id 5) was not used
assumptions: 'Black Week 2025 mailing' is read as campaign_id 15, Black Week 2025 (email+sms+push, 24-30 Nov 2025), the only campaign with that name and year
'Held out' means the members in campaign_holdout for that campaign, i.e. the members deliberately not contacted
caveats: No corrections were needed. campaign_holdout has 2747 rows and 2747 distinct member_id for campaign 15, with no duplicates. This matches dim_campaign.holdout_size (2747), and every held-out member exists in dim_member.
None of the 2747 held-out members appears among the 23818 members who were contacted in the campaign, so the holdout is clean.

The holdout is 10.34% of the mailing list (26573, which includes the holdout), not exactly 10%. Other campaigns also range from about 9.4% to 11%, so this looks like normal rounding or sampling in how the lists were drawn. I did not adjust for it.
Held-out plus contacted members total 26565, which is 8 fewer than the recorded mailing_list_size of 26573. I did not investigate this gap, and it does not change the holdout count.

Loyalty tier classification as stored in the dim_member.tier column (Basic, Silver, or Gold)

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT CASE WHEN s.store_id=900 THEN w.dispatch_date ELSE f.sale_date END AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=r.product_key WHERE s.store_id<>999 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cp.category, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS net_sales, ROUND(100.0*SUM(n.net_sales-n.cost)/SUM(n.net_sales),1) AS gross_margin_pct FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku=n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period=6 AND cp.category IN ('Garden','Electrical') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns dated on their return date
Gross margin: net sales minus standard cost, both after returns, with returned units credited back at standard_cost_returned
Gross margin %: gross margin divided by net sales
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date, delivered and collected orders only (cancelled and processing excluded)
As-is category hierarchy: current product version, so outdoor lighting counts in Electrical
Fiscal period 6 taken from dim_date (FY2025/26 weeks 22-26, 22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025)

Control total checked: all-category P6 net sales (1,293,219.69) match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly
assumptions: 'Period 6 last year' is read as FY2025/26 P6. The request came in on 8 Oct 2026, which is in FY2026/27, so last year is FY2025/26. Accepted past requests read 'last year' the same way.
No basis (as-is or as-was) was specified, so the company default, as-is, was used, as in past category-margin requests.
Web sales are included, since net sales are a company figure and the request did not limit it to stores.
Margin is the company definition, after returns.

Duplicate loads found in fact_sales_line: 418 receipt lines for 15-21 Sep 2025 appear twice, with identical content and a reload stamp of 23 Sep 2025. They fall in fiscal week 21 (P5), so they do not change P6 figures. The query removes them anyway by keeping one row per receipt_id and line_no.

Returns are dated on the return date. P6 net sales therefore include refunds on goods sold earlier, and later returns of P6 sales will fall in later periods.
Net sales are excluding VAT, in EUR.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.sku, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.sku, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), by_category AS (SELECT CASE WHEN cp.subcategory = 'Outdoor Lighting' THEN 'Electrical' ELSE cp.category END AS category, d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = n.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8 AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25') GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.category, 8 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(ty.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ROUND(ly.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM by_category ty JOIN by_category ly ON ly.category = ty.category AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND ty.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical') ORDER BY ty.category

As-is product hierarchy (current product version)
Outdoor lighting counted in Electrical for all history

assumptions: The request was received on 5 October 2026, in FY2026/27. I read 'last year' as FY2025/26 and 'the year before' as FY2024/25, which matches how past requests read 'last year' in FY2026/27.

Period 8 is 24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025 (fiscal weeks 31 to 34) in FY2025/26 and 25 Nov to 22 Dec 2024 (fiscal weeks 31 to 34) in FY2024/25. Both periods are fully loaded and have 28 days. Week 53 sits in period 12, so it does not affect this request.

Products counted by natural key sku, not product_key

Store 999 and category ZZ Test filtered out of sales work (the test-article filter did not change the total)
Staff purchases included, as in net sales

answer.sql: SELECT m.tier, count(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS active_members FROM dim_member AS m WHERE m.valid_from <= DATE '2025-12-21' AND m.valid_to >= DATE '2025-12-21' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fact_sales_line AS f JOIN dim_member AS v ON v.member_key = f.member_key WHERE v.member_id = m.member_id AND f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-12-22' AND DATE '2025-12-21') GROUP BY m.tier ORDER BY CASE m.tier WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1 WHEN 'Silver' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: period 8 of FY2025/26 runs 2025-11-24 to 2025-12-21 (ref_fiscal_calendar), so 'end of period 8' is 2025-12-21
Slowly changing member dimension: tier taken from the dim_member version valid on 2025-12-21 (valid_from <= date <= valid_to), not the current tier
Members counted by member_id (the stable loyalty number), not member_key (which is one per version)
Sales lines linked to members through member_key, then mapped to member_id so purchases made under any version of the member count
Loyalty tiers shown in the order Basic, Silver, Gold
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the previous fiscal year, FY2025/26, because the request date (2026-10-07) falls in FY2026/27 P06. Period 8 of FY2026/27 has not happened yet.

'Active' member read as a member with at least one purchase (a fact_sales_line row linked to the member, store or web) in the 12 months up to and including the as-of date, i.e. 2024-12-22 to 2025-12-21. The warehouse documents no definition of 'active', so this is my choice.
Staff purchases are counted as purchase activity. Excluding them would change the counts only slightly, to Basic 14604, Silver 10967 and Gold 3901.
Returns are not netted off. Every member line in the window has a positive net amount, and a purchase that was later returned still counts as activity.
Only members who had joined on or before 2025-12-21 are included, which follows from the version validity test.
caveats: Because 'active' is not defined in the warehouse, the figures depend on my 12-month purchase rule. A different rule, such as 6 months, 24 months or a consent-based definition, would give different numbers.
Of the 48,675 members on the loyalty list at 2025-12-21 (Basic 29,304, Silver 15,035, Gold 4,336), 29,657 count as active under this rule. The rest had no purchase in the 12 months.
I used the tier valid on 2025-12-21. Using the current tier from dim_member (is_current) would put members in the wrong tier, because 25,526 of the 60,000 members have more than one version.

No data defects affected the result. dim_member has no overlapping versions and no gaps at the as-of date. stg_member_updates matches dim_member exactly. Every sales member_key resolves to a dim_member row valid on the sale date. The period is fully loaded.
fact_sales_line has 418 duplicate (receipt_id, line_no) pairs. They do not affect distinct member counts.
Sales before 2024-04-29 are not in the warehouse. This does not affect the 12-month window used here.

WITH weekly AS (

    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.week_ending_date
    WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999
      AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating'
      AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)
SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period AS period, COUNT(*) AS weeks, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS average_stock_value_at_cost_eur
FROM weekly GROUP BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and articles within each week first, then averaged across the weeks of the period, never summed across weeks
Stock value at standard cost (closing_value in fact_stock_week)
Stock by store covers the physical stores only (store_id below 900): web shop and store 999 left out
Test articles (category ZZ Test) left out; none appeared in Paint & Decorating anyway
Category as-is: the current product version (dim_product is_current) per sku
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P3 is fiscal weeks 9 to 13, week-ending Sundays 5, 12, 19 and 26 July and 2 August 2026
Warehouse grain check: fact_stock_week has one row per store_key, product_key and week-ending date (and per store_id and sku) in these weeks
assumptions: 'This year' is the current fiscal year, FY2026/27, and 'period 3' is its P3 (29 June to 2 August 2026); P3 is complete, and the warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026
'Average stock' is the average of the five weekly closing values in the period, not the last week's closing
'As a value at cost' is closing_value, which is stock at standard cost in EUR
'Whole chain' is all physical stores (store_id below 900); the web shop is not in fact_stock_week because web orders are picked from the central warehouse
Paint & Decorating is taken as-is (current category hierarchy)
caveats: No data problems found for these weeks: no duplicate rows at the store x article x week grain, no null or negative units, no web shop, store 999 or test-article rows, and closing_value equals units times standard unit cost on every row. No corrections were needed.
The result excludes the central warehouse, which is not in fact_stock_week, so it is store stock only.

Kuopio (125) was shut for its refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026 but still holds stock rows, so its stock is included in all five weeks. Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no stock rows.

WITH store_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    s.store_id,
    ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount), 2) as net_sales
  FROM dim_store s
  INNER JOIN fact_sales_line f ON s.store_key = f.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  WHERE s.store_id < 900

  ss.store_id,

INNER JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_id = ss.store_id AND s.is_current = true
ORDER BY ss.net_sales DESC
LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900), training store (999) excluded
Product scope: test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
assumptions: Biggest stores means highest total net sales (standard retail metric)
Request asks for cumulative sales across all available data with no specific period
Store name and attributes are from the current version (is_current = true)
caveats: Six stores (101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 114) have multiple dimension versions due to attribute changes over time; net sales are aggregated across all versions to show total store performance
Store 999 (training store) and test articles excluded per house rules
Data covers 2024-04-29 to 2026-10-04; no specific period was requested

answer.sql:
WITH sales_by_category AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    p.category,
    COALESCE(SUM(f.net_amount), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
  WHERE p.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
    AND d.fiscal_period = 8
    AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25')
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, p.category
)
SELECT 
  category,
  MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END) as net_sales_fy2025_26,
  MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales END) as net_sales_fy2024_25,
  ROUND((MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales END) - 
          MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales END)) / 
         MAX(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales END) * 100, 2) as growth_pct
FROM sales_by_category
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category;
definitions_applied: Net sales: sum of net_amount (line value excluding VAT after discounts) minus refund_net (returns)
Fiscal period: fiscal period numbering 1-12 within each fiscal year (period 8 mid-way through fiscal year)
Category: product category from dim_product, used to group sales
Growth: year-over-year percentage change calculated as (FY2025/26 - FY2024/25) / FY2024/25 × 100
assumptions: Last year interpreted as FY2025/26 (most recent complete fiscal year); year before as FY2024/25
Period 8 means fiscal period 8 in the respective fiscal years
Growth calculated as year-over-year percentage change
Net sales includes both store (ST) and web (WB) channels
Net sales calculation accounts for returns (refunds subtracted from gross sales)
caveats: Staff purchases are included in the sales totals (marked separately in the data but not filtered out)
Returns accounted for: Garden had EUR 2,139.65 returned in FY2025/26 P8 and EUR 3,259.83 in FY2024/25 P8; Electrical had EUR 10,240.51 returned in FY2025/26 P8 and EUR 6,999.52 in FY2024/25 P8
Garden category shows significant decline (-34.2%), driven by lower sales volume in the later fiscal year

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, fs.week_ending_date, fs.closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON fs.store_key = s.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON fs.product_key = p.product_key WHERE s.store_key = 30 AND p.product_key = 11 AND fs.week_ending_date = '2026-10-04'

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cp.subcategory, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id = 118 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cp.subcategory ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period 5 of FY2026/27 (weeks 18 to 21, Monday 31 August to Sunday 27 September 2026), from dim_date
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date), before returns
Store scope: Nokia is store_id 118, a physical store in the West region. It has a single version in dim_store, so no store-version issue arises.
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded. This changed nothing, because Nokia has no test-article lines.
Staff purchases included, as in net sales (about 17 of the units are staff purchases)
Subcategory taken as-is, from the current product version (dim_product.is_current). The as-was subcategory was identical for every Nokia line in the period.
Control total: Nokia units sold for the period, 2245 over 28 days and 564 receipts, equal rpt_daily_store_sales exactly.
assumptions: 'Period 5 this year' is FY2026/27 P05, the current fiscal year and a completed period. The warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026 and the request came in on 9 October 2026.
'Nokia' is the store named Nokia (store_id 118).

'Units sold' is the quantity sold on sales lines. I did not net off returned units because the metric dictionary defines units sold as sales-line quantity. The same basis is used in the weeks-of-cover and rpt_daily_store_sales definitions.
Ranking is by units. The subcategory names are the current hierarchy (as-is).
caveats: No data problems turned up for Nokia in this period. The sales-line keys are unique, all 28 days are present, and the total ties to the control table.

Third place is sensitive to the returns basis. If returns in the period were netted off (5 to 9 returned units in these subcategories), Cleaning Products (134 net) would overtake Storage Boxes (130 net) for third. On the company's sales-line basis Storage Boxes has 139 units against 136 each for Cleaning Products and Plants & Flowers. Fixings & Fasteners and Indoor Lighting hold first and second on either basis.
Fixings & Fasteners is far ahead (570 units, about 3.0 units per line), which fits a small-item, multi-pack article type.

answer.sql: WITH grp AS (SELECT member_id, 'holdout' AS grp FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15 UNION SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id, 'targeted' FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m USING (member_key) WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, sum(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1), spend AS (SELECT m.member_id, sum(f.net_amount - coalesce(r.refund_net, 0)) AS net_spend FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m USING (member_key) LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-24' AND DATE '2025-11-30' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag GROUP BY 1), per_group AS (SELECT g.grp, count(*) AS members, avg(coalesce(s.net_spend, 0)) AS avg_spend FROM grp g LEFT JOIN spend s USING (member_id) GROUP BY 1) SELECT 15 AS campaign_id, 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, round(max(avg_spend) FILTER (WHERE grp = 'targeted'), 2) AS avg_spend_per_targeted_member_eur, round(max(avg_spend) FILTER (WHERE grp = 'holdout'), 2) AS avg_spend_per_held_out_member_eur, round(max(avg_spend) FILTER (WHERE grp = 'targeted') - max(avg_spend) FILTER (WHERE grp = 'holdout'), 2) AS uplift_eur FROM per_group
definitions_applied: Campaign window from dim_campaign: Black Week 2025 (campaign_id 15), 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-30, using sale_date (local business date)
Holdout group = campaign_holdout rows for campaign 15, keyed on member_id (stable loyalty number)
Member versions resolved through dim_member: sales and exposure rows carry member_key, mapped to member_id so every version of a member counts as the same person
Targeted group = distinct members with a contact in fact_campaign_exposure for campaign 15
Spend = net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) less refund_net on returns of those same sales lines
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) excluded
All channels counted: store, web home delivery and click-and-collect
Members with no purchase in the window count as zero spend in the averages
Uplift = average spend per targeted member minus average spend per held-out member
assumptions: Spend is read as net sales excluding VAT and net of returns, matching the company's net sales convention
Returns are netted against the original sales line whatever date they were booked, so refunds up to 2025-12-31 on window sales are deducted
The targeted group is every member contacted at least once, including 1,951 undelivered contacts, so the comparison is as-targeted
The window is the campaign window only, with no post-campaign tail
Staff purchases are not customer spend and are excluded
Purchases made without scanning the loyalty card cannot be attributed to a member in either group
caveats: Correction: the holdout list holds member_id, not member_key, so joining it directly to sales lines would miss members whose record has several versions. All joins go through dim_member to member_id.
Correction: returns are deducted. Without this the figures are 4.70 targeted and 4.04 held out, an uplift of 0.66 EUR.
Correction: staff purchases are excluded. Including them would change the averages by about 0.04 EUR in the targeted group and 0.01 EUR in the held-out group.

Group sizes are 23,818 targeted and 2,747 held out. Together that is 26,565 members against a mailing_list_size of 26,573 in dim_campaign. I could not find the 8 missing members, who may have no exposure rows. Their effect is negligible.
No held-out member appears in the exposure data, so the holdout is clean. Average prior spend and tier mix are similar in the two groups, so the comparison looks fair.

This is a point estimate. The uplift of about 0.74 EUR per member comes from a small average (most members buy nothing in the week), and I did not test it for statistical significance, so it could partly be noise.
Uplift is measured on spend within the campaign week only. It does not count lost sales from pulled-forward purchases, and it is not net of campaign cost.
Table names like bak_*, stg_*, tmp_* and *_old were not used. Only the maintained dim_ and fact_ tables were.

answer.sql: WITH web_lines AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, w.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fact_web_order w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10) AND w.status IN ('delivered', 'collected') AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag) SELECT fiscal_year, fiscal_period, round(100.0 * sum(CASE WHEN fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN net_amount END) / sum(net_amount), 2) AS click_and_collect_share_pct FROM web_lines GROUP BY fiscal_year, fiscal_period ORDER BY fiscal_period

answer.sql: WITH weekly AS (SELECT fs.week_ending_date, SUM(fs.closing_value) AS closing_value FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE fs.week_ending_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-06-29' AND DATE '2026-08-02' AND s.store_id < 900 AND cp.category = 'Paint & Decorating' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_period, 'Paint & Decorating' AS category, ROUND(AVG(closing_value), 2) AS avg_stock_value_at_cost_eur FROM weekly
definitions_applied: Closing stock: weekly snapshot on week-ending Sundays, summed across stores and products within each week, then averaged across weeks (never summed across weeks)
Stock value at standard cost (closing_value in fact_stock_week)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P3 = fiscal weeks 9 to 13, 29 June to 2 August 2026, five weeks, week-ending Sundays 5, 12, 19 and 26 July and 2 August

Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
As-is product hierarchy: category taken from the current product version (is_current)
Ranged articles only, as held in fact_stock_week
assumptions: 'Period 3 this year' read as FY2026/27 P3 (29 June to 2 August 2026), the current fiscal year as of the request date 8 October 2026; the period is fully loaded
