answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year,
           5 AS first_week, 8 AS last_week
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, p.sku,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales, f.standard_cost AS cost
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, p.sku, -r.refund_net, -r.standard_cost_returned
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
weekly_with_dates AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, 
           MIN(d.fiscal_week_start_date) AS week_start_date,
           MAX(d.fiscal_week_end_date) AS week_end_date,
           SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT ty.fiscal_week, ty.week_start_date, ty.week_end_date,
       ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct
FROM weekly_with_dates ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN weekly_with_dates ly ON ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year
ORDER BY ty.fiscal_week;
definitions_applied: Net sales (excluding VAT, after returns, store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded)
Web sales recognized on dispatch date in Helsinki time
Comparison by fiscal week number (CAL-COMPARE)
assumptions: Period 2 read as the most recent completed one, FY2026/27 P2 (weeks 5-8)
Last year read as the same fiscal period in the prior year, FY2025/26 P2
Total company includes all stores except store 999 and all products except category ZZ Test
Web orders included, recognized on dispatch date
Growth calculated as (this_year / last_year - 1) × 100 percent
caveats: No data quality issues detected by validation checks
All four weeks of P2 in both years are complete as of the warehouse load date (2026-10-04)

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week
),
range_start AS (
    SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week
),
weeks AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date
    FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
),
store_weeks AS (
    SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week,
           (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date)
           AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c
                           WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id
                             AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date
                             AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading
    FROM dim_store st
    CROSS JOIN weeks w
    WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900
),
lfl_store_weeks AS (
    SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week
    FROM store_weeks ty
    CROSS JOIN params
    CROSS JOIN range_start
    JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
    JOIN dim_store st   ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current
    WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading
      AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)
),
web_dispatch AS (
    SELECT web_order_id,
           CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date
    FROM fact_web_order
    WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')
),
net_lines AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
lfl_sales AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT n.store_id || '-' || d.fiscal_week) AS store_weeks
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d   ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week
    CROSS JOIN params
    WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year)
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)
    GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d.fiscal_year), (d.fiscal_year, cs.region))
)
SELECT ty.net_sales AS this_year, ly.net_sales AS last_year,
       ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct
FROM lfl_sales ty
CROSS JOIN params
JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.region IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.region IS NULL
ORDER BY ty.region NULLS FIRST;
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales in the same LFL stores week-by-week
LFL stores: physical stores open 364+ days before the period; trading both years
Week 53 never counts in LFL comparisons
Refits excluded: refit weeks in ref_store_closure drop out for the affected store in both years
Net sales: excluding VAT, after returns; return amount reduces net sales on return date
Physical stores only: store_id < 900; store 999 and test category excluded
Fiscal week alignment: same fiscal week numbers compared across years (CAL-COMPARE)
assumptions: Period 4 (P4) without a fiscal year reads as the most recent completed P4: FY2026/27 P4
Last year: FY2025/26 P4 (same fiscal week numbers 14-17 as the comparator)
Web shop (store 900) and training store (999) excluded; web orders reported on dispatch date
caveats: Data loaded through 2026-10-04; P4 FY2026/27 data complete through 2026-08-30
Result is company-wide total LFL; represents 152 store-weeks in the LFL base
Essentially flat performance: -0.03% growth reflects minimal net sales change (265 EUR decrease)

answer.sql: SELECT cs.store_id, cs.store_name, 'Interior Paint' AS subcategory, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE cs.store_id = 108 AND cp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 3 GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
definitions_applied: Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 period 3 = fiscal weeks 9-13, 29 June to 2 August 2026 (5 weeks, fully loaded)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines, by sale date (metric dictionary, weeks-of-cover definition); returns not netted off
Store scope: physical store Lahti (store_id 108) only; web shop (900) not included
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither affects this figure)
Staff purchases included (no exclusion for unit counts)
As-is product hierarchy: sku joined to the current dim_product version (is_current) for subcategory Interior Paint
Versioned dimensions counted by natural key (store_id, sku), with no multiplication of rows
Control check: daily units and receipts for Lahti (all products) match rpt_daily_store_sales on every day of the period
assumptions: 'Interior Paint' read as the subcategory Interior Paint within Paint & Decorating (123 SKUs)
'Lahti store' read as store_id 108, Lahti (the only Lahti store; Tampere Lielahti is a different store)
'Period 3 of FY26/27' read as FY2026/27 P03, i.e. 29 June to 2 August 2026
'Units sold' read as gross units on sales lines before returns, since the metric dictionary defines units sold as the quantity on sales lines and sets no return adjustment
Sale date (Helsinki business date) used for dating the sale
Store sales only; no web or click-and-collect lines are attributed to the Lahti store key
caveats: 6 units of Interior Paint sold in Lahti in this period were returned (returns booked 30 June to 3 August 2026); net of those returns the figure would be 188
Two Interior Paint SKUs (100963, 101047) have two product versions; both versions are Interior Paint, so the as-is join does not change the count
channel_code is NULL on these sales lines (post-migration); the figure relies on store_id, so it is unaffected
No data problems needing correction were found: no duplicate sales lines, no negative quantities, and the daily control against rpt_daily_store_sales agrees
Includes 4 units bought by staff, which the company definition leaves in

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-12-21' AS as_of_end), active AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key CROSS JOIN params p WHERE f.sale_date > p.as_of_end - 364 AND f.sale_date <= p.as_of_end) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 8 AS fiscal_period, cur.tier, COUNT(*) AS active_members FROM active a CROSS JOIN params p JOIN dim_member cur ON cur.member_id = a.member_id AND p.as_of_end BETWEEN cur.valid_from AND cur.valid_to GROUP BY cur.tier ORDER BY CASE cur.tier WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1 WHEN 'Silver' THEN 2 WHEN 'Gold' THEN 3 END
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in any channel in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks, ending with and including the as-of week (sale_date > as-of Sunday - 364 and <= as-of Sunday)
Members counted by distinct member_id, not member_key, so versions do not double count
Tier read from the dim_member version valid on the as-of Sunday
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P08 is fiscal weeks 31 to 34, 24 Nov 2025 to 21 Dec 2025; end of the period is Sunday 21 Dec 2025
Sales lines linked to a member through member_key; guest orders carry no member key and so are not counted
assumptions: "Last year" asked on 7 Oct 2026 (FY2026/27) is read as FY2025/26, the previous fiscal year, as in accepted requests from May 2026. So "period 8 last year" is FY2025/26 P08.
"End of period 8" means the Sunday ending the period, 21 Dec 2025, which is the last day of fiscal week 34. The 52-week window runs 23 Dec 2024 to 21 Dec 2025.
Tier is the tier on 21 Dec 2025, not the current tier.
No total row was given because the request asked for a breakdown by tier only. The three tiers sum to 29,526 distinct active members.
caveats: No data problems were found that needed correcting. All 328,182 member-linked sale lines in the window are unique. None are in training store 999 or the ZZ Test category, so the usual exclusions change nothing. Every active member had exactly one dim_member version valid on 21 Dec 2025, so none were dropped by the tier lookup.
If "last year" was meant as the 12 months before the request date, or as FY2024/25, the answer would differ. FY2025/26 was used.

answer.sql: WITH web_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(s.net_amount) AS sales_net FROM fact_sales_line s JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = s.sale_date WHERE (s.channel_code = 'WB' OR s.channel_id IN (2,3)) AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1,2), web_returns AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, sum(r.refund_net) AS refunds_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fact_sales_line s ON s.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = r.return_date WHERE (s.channel_code = 'WB' OR s.channel_id IN (2,3)) AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_period, w.sales_net - coalesce(r.refunds_net, 0) AS web_net_sales FROM web_sales w LEFT JOIN web_returns r USING (fiscal_year, fiscal_period) ORDER BY w.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales excluding VAT, after line discounts, minus refunds excluding VAT (the net_sales convention used in rpt_daily_store_sales)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: 4-4-5 periods, Monday to Sunday weeks
Web channel = channel_code 'WB' before the migration, channel_id 2 (web home delivery) and 3 (click and collect) from 3 November 2025
Sales dated by sale_date; refunds dated by return_date (refunds booked in the period)
Returns linked to web sales lines through sales_line_id
Cancelled web orders have no sales lines, so they add nothing
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (28 April 2025 to 3 May 2026). The request came in on 9 October 2026, which falls in FY2026/27.
'Periods 5 to 8' are fiscal periods 5 to 8 of FY2025/26: 25 August to 21 December 2025.
'Web net sales' means net of returns, excluding VAT, in EUR. This follows the company's net sales definition.
Click and collect counts as web, as dim_channel puts it in channel_group = 'web'.
Refunds on web orders count as web returns wherever they were booked. About 21,000 EUR of the 80,383 EUR in refunds over the four periods were booked at physical stores.
A refund falls in the period of its return date, not the period of the original sale.
caveats: Correction: from 3 November 2025 (the web-platform migration) web lines carry channel_code NULL and channel_id 2 or 3, so a filter on channel_code = 'WB' would drop them. I used both codes. The rpt.v_daily_sales view has the same gap for web from that date, so it understates web sales from the migration onward. The number of lines affected is 14,330 (10,480 + 3,850), worth 377,308 EUR before returns. Period 8 and the last 3 weeks of period 7 are most affected.

Correction: refunds on web lines are netted off. They come to 80,382.84 EUR over the four periods (period 5: 18,585.85; period 6: 22,385.45; period 7: 17,045.14; period 8: 22,366.40). Gross of returns, web sales are 158,124.35, 194,176.17, 166,510.02 and 249,084.84 EUR for periods 5 to 8.

The web returns are split across several store keys: the web shop (store 900) and physical stores. I took them by the channel of the original sale. Counting only refunds booked at store 900 would raise the figures by 5,495.34, 4,783.52, 4,901.43 and 4,545.10 EUR (periods 5 to 8, about 19,725 EUR in total). If the e-commerce team wants refunds limited to the web shop location, that would change the net figures.
Period 6 has 5 weeks, so it is not like for like with periods 5, 7 and 8, which have 4. Period 8 includes the pre-Christmas peak.

The checks I ran found no duplicate lines, no web sales lines without an order, no returns without a sales line, no over-returns, and no gaps in daily web sales. The VAT arithmetic on the web lines checks out. Dates match Helsinki local dates.
The training store (999) and staff purchases have no web lines in the window, so they did not affect these figures.

answer.sql:
WITH sold_lines AS (
    SELECT f.sales_line_id, cp.subcategory, f.net_amount
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 
      AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
      AND cp.category = 'Garden'
      AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
      AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 13
),
refunds AS (
    SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net 
    FROM fact_return_line 
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT l.subcategory,
       ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / NULLIF(SUM(l.net_amount), 0), 2) AS return_rate
FROM sold_lines l
LEFT JOIN refunds r ON l.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
definitions_applied: Return rate: sum of refund_net divided by sum of net_amount, on the sale-week cohort (returns attributed to the fiscal week of original sale, whenever the return occurred)
As-is reporting: current product category and subcategory applied to historical sales
Exclusions: store 999 (training store) and ZZ Test category excluded; staff purchases included in base; store-level figures reconcilable with rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: Q1 of last year interpreted as Q1 of FY2025/26 (fiscal weeks 1-13, 28 April 2025 to 27 July 2025), the most recent completed Q1 as of the request date
Return rate expressed in percent units (7.26 = 7.26%)
All sales channels included (physical stores and web)
caveats: Outdoor Lighting (0.0% return rate, 375.00 EUR net sales): 2 SKUs (100916 Outdoor Lighting Lumiko 455, 100917 Outdoor Lighting Ahvenisto 492) retain Garden category in current product versions. The majority of outdoor lighting SKUs (59 with Q1 sales) have current versions in Electrical category following the 27 October 2025 category move. The mixed categorisation of a minority of outdoor lighting products may warrant data review.
Return cohort is complete: Q1 sales ended 27 July 2025, returns arrive within 30 days, warehouse loaded through 4 October 2026.

answer.sql: WITH sales AS (SELECT CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', o.dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id AND o.status IN ('delivered','collected') WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), rets AS (SELECT r.return_date AS business_date, o.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net AS net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id LEFT JOIN fact_web_order o ON o.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), u AS (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rets) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN u.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN u.net ELSE 0 END) / SUM(u.net), 2) AS click_and_collect_share_pct FROM u JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = u.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counted as web)
Net sales excluding VAT and after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (fact_web_order.dispatch_ts_utc converted to Europe/Helsinki), not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code or channel_id
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type, joined on receipt_id = web_order_id; returns classified through sales_line_id to the original order
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines); only delivered and collected orders count
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2025/26 P9 = 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026 (5 weeks), P10 = 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026 (4 weeks)
Control total checked: web net sales for store 900 equals rpt_daily_store_sales net_sales for both periods (P9 200,208.58; P10 123,131.15)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27, as in past requests made in May 2026 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35)
'Periods 9 and 10' read as fiscal periods 9 and 10, reported as one row per period rather than combined
'Web sales' read as web net sales on the company definition (excluding VAT, after returns)
Returns counted are those booked to the web shop (store 900), in line with the company net-sales definition and the control total
caveats: Correction: channel_id cannot identify click-and-collect. In the sample checked, 758 click-and-collect orders from 12 January to 11 February 2026 carry channel_id 2, the home-delivery key, instead of 3. I used fulfilment_type from fact_web_order.
Correction: one ZZ Test line on a web home-delivery order was excluded as a test article. This does not change the figures at the precision shown.

Some returns of web orders were processed in physical stores (for example 38 returns of click-and-collect lines and about 190 of home-delivery lines across stores 101 to 139 in P9 and P10). Under the company definition these reduce store net sales, not web net sales, so they are excluded here. Including them would give 29.54% for P9 and 30.65% for P10.
Before returns the shares are 28.95% (P9) and 30.62% (P10). The figures sent are after returns, per the company net sales definition.
P9 is a five-week period that includes Christmas and New Year, and P10 has four weeks, so the two periods are not like for like in length.

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_name, s.store_id, rfc.fiscal_year, rfc.fiscal_period, SUM(f.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key INNER JOIN ref_fiscal_calendar rfc ON f.sale_date BETWEEN rfc.period_start_date AND rfc.period_end_date WHERE s.store_id = 108 AND p.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND rfc.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND rfc.fiscal_period = 3 AND f.staff_purchase_flag = FALSE GROUP BY s.store_name, s.store_id, rfc.fiscal_year, rfc.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Fiscal period as defined in ref_fiscal_calendar (FY2026/27 P03 spans 2026-06-29 to 2026-08-02)
Interior Paint defined as products with subcategory = 'Interior Paint'
Units sold measured by fact_sales_line.quantity excluding staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag = FALSE)
assumptions: Request phrase 'period 3 this year' interpreted as fiscal period 3 of the current fiscal year FY2026/27 (request date 2026-10-05 falls in FY2026/27)
Units sold refers to customer sales; staff purchases are excluded as non-revenue transactions
All Interior Paint SKUs (123 products in subcategory) are included in the aggregation
caveats: Data includes only transactions at the Lahti store (store_id 108); regional or corporate sales are not included
Four additional units of Interior Paint were purchased as staff purchases during this period and are excluded from the reported figure
The Lahti store is a Large format store in the South region; other locations may have different sales patterns

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), q AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2024/25') AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 27 AND 39 GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT ty.region, ty.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2025_26, ly.net_sales AS net_sales_fy2024_25, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 1) AS growth_pct FROM q ty JOIN q ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' ORDER BY ty.region
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT after line discounts, minus returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered and collected orders count (cancelled and processing orders excluded)
Web shop is store 900, region Online, shown as its own line (identified by store_id, not channel_code)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Regions as-is: current store version (is_current), restated on today's five-region structure
Fiscal Q3 = periods 7-9 = fiscal weeks 27-39, compared with the same fiscal week numbers in the prior year (aligned on week number, not calendar date)
Helsinki time for all dates (UTC timestamps converted)
Control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Q3 last year' read as FY2025/26 Q3 (27 Oct 2025 to 25 Jan 2026), because the request was received on 6 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27. This is the same reading accepted in past requests that asked in FY2026/27 for 'last year' (REQ-D04 and others).
'Q3 the year before' read as FY2024/25 Q3 (28 Oct 2024 to 26 Jan 2025), weeks 27-39.

Regions reported as-is (current hierarchy), the company default, since as-was was not requested. Capital Region therefore also covers the five stores that were South before 28 April 2025, in both years, and Kouvola is in South in both years.
Net sales is the company definition (after returns, web on dispatch date). No gross or VAT-inclusive figure was requested.
No like-for-like adjustment was applied. All stores trading in each quarter are included.
caveats: No correction to the numbers was needed. Both years' region totals reconcile exactly with rpt_daily_store_sales, store by store and day by day (FY2025/26 Q3 total 3,845,652.46; FY2024/25 Q3 total 3,610,885.71; gap 0.00).
Store 999 and ZZ Test lines were removed. In sold lines that is about 6,888 EUR in FY2025/26 Q3 and 6,486 EUR in FY2024/25 Q3 (the removal of their returns is not included in those two figures).

Duplicate sales lines (same receipt_id and line_no loaded twice, 418 receipt lines) exist in the warehouse for 15-21 September 2025. That is outside this quarter's range, so the figures here are not affected. They would overstate any figure for that week.
The Online line (+29.7%) is not like-for-like with the stores. It is the web shop (store 900) on dispatch date, and it grew far faster than any physical region.

Growth for physical regions is not like-for-like. Lohja (opened 4 Nov 2024, South) and Tampere Lamminpää (opened 2 Sep 2024, West) were not in the full prior-year quarter, which lifts South and West growth. Savonlinna (East) closed on 25 Jan 2026, the last day of the quarter, so it trades in nearly all of it.

The deprecated views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales and rpt_weekly_sales_by_region were not used. The views drop web sales after 3 Nov 2025, and the table uses the old four-region structure.

Net sales are net of returns booked in the quarter, including returns of goods sold earlier. Web orders placed late in the quarter but dispatched after 25 Jan 2026 fall in Q4, and orders placed before the quarter but dispatched in it fall in Q3.

answer.sql: WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT fiscal_year, fiscal_week, fiscal_week_start_date AS ws, fiscal_week_end_date AS we FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26','FY2026/27') AND fiscal_week <= 22), st AS (SELECT store_id, region FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id < 900), g AS (SELECT st.store_id, st.region, wk.fiscal_year, wk.fiscal_week, coalesce(sum(r.net_sales),0) AS net, coalesce(sum(r.receipts),0) AS rc FROM st CROSS JOIN wk LEFT JOIN rpt_daily_store_sales r ON r.store_id = st.store_id AND r.business_date BETWEEN wk.ws AND wk.we GROUP BY ALL), p AS (SELECT a.region, a.net AS cy, b.net AS py FROM g a JOIN g b ON a.store_id = b.store_id AND a.fiscal_week = b.fiscal_week AND a.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND b.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE a.rc > 0 AND b.rc > 0), r AS (SELECT region, round((sum(cy)/sum(py) - 1)*100, 2) AS lfl_net_sales_growth_pct FROM p GROUP BY region) SELECT rank() OVER (ORDER BY lfl_net_sales_growth_pct DESC) AS rank, region, lfl_net_sales_growth_pct FROM r ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Net sales = sales excluding VAT minus refunds excluding VAT (rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales), refunds booked on the day of the return
Stores only: store_id below 900 (web shop 900 and the training store 999 left out; click-and-collect belongs to the web shop)
Fiscal year FY2026/27 (starts Monday 4 May 2026), year to date = fiscal weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 Oct 2026, the last complete loaded week)
Prior-year comparison = fiscal weeks 1 to 22 of FY2025/26 (28 Apr to 28 Sep 2025), matched week for week on Monday-to-Sunday fiscal weeks
Like-for-like: a store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years, so planned refit closures and closed stores drop out of both years
Current five-region structure (Capital Region split out of South, Kouvola moved from East to South on 28 Apr 2025) applied to both years, using each store's current region by store_id
Duplicate sales lines removed (one row per receipt_id and line_no)
assumptions: 'How they are doing this year so far' is read as like-for-like net sales growth against the same fiscal weeks last year, so a small region can rank above a large one. Ranked by absolute net sales YTD instead, the order would be West, South, Capital Region, East, North (all stores, after returns: about 1.82m, 1.31m, 0.95m, 0.96m, 0.73m EUR; East and Capital Region are close and I did not rank them precisely on that basis)

Year to date runs to Sunday 4 Oct 2026, the last complete week loaded, even though period 6 is flagged as not fully loaded. The 4 Oct figures are a normal short Sunday with all 38 trading stores present
Staff purchases and loyalty sales are kept in net sales, as in the D&A daily store report; staff purchases are about 1.3% of sales
Stores 136 Tampere Lamminpää (West, opened 2 Sep 2024) and 137 Lohja (South, opened 4 Nov 2024) are in the like-for-like base because they traded in every week of both years
Growth is on net sales as reported, not adjusted for the extra trading day this year
caveats: Regional restatement: dim_store moved 5 stores (101 to 105) from South to a new Capital Region and Kouvola (114) from East to South on 28 Apr 2025. The comment on dim_store.region still lists only four regions. I used current regions for both years; using the region held at each sale date would have mixed old and new regions in the prior-year comparison

Double-loaded data: Tampere Lielahti (116, West) has every sales line for 15 to 21 Sep 2025 loaded twice (reload on 23 Sep 2025, 418 duplicated lines). I kept one copy of each; the daily store report already agrees with the de-duplicated data. Without this the prior year for West would be overstated

Channel field change: from 3 Nov 2025 channel_code is empty and channel_id is used (1 store, 2 web home delivery, 3 click and collect). Filtering on channel_code = 'ST' would silently drop every store sale since then; I selected stores by store (store_id below 900) instead

East is distorted in headline figures: its YTD net sales are down 11.6% (959k against 1,085k EUR) because Savonlinna (129) closed in January 2026 (no sales this year, 57.5k EUR in the same weeks last year) and Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 Jun to 26 Jul 2026 (fiscal weeks 7 to 12). Both are removed from the like-for-like figure, which leaves East at -0.19%. The closures themselves cost East real sales and are not shown in the ranked figure
West: Pori (119) was shut for a refit from 8 Sep to 12 Oct 2025, so fiscal weeks 20 to 22 are excluded for Pori in both years. Without that, West would show +3.24% instead of +1.93%

Close calls: South (2.11%) and West (1.93%) are within 0.2 points. Stores 136 and 137 were still ramping up in the prior-year period (growth of +12% and +26% against about 3% for the group). If the two 2024 openings are treated as not yet like-for-like, South falls to +0.97% and West to +0.99% and they swap places; North, Capital Region and East keep their positions
The current year has 152 trading days against 151 in the comparison weeks (1 May 2025 fell inside last year's window), a small tailwind of roughly 0.7% for every region and no effect on the order
Fiscal week 22 of FY2026/27 sits in period 6, which the fiscal calendar marks as not fully loaded; the figures for the weeks completed to 4 Oct are complete
Returns are matched to the day and store of the refund, not of the original sale, so a refund can fall in a different week from its sale. Web returns were excluded

answer.sql: WITH stock AS (SELECT DISTINCT f.store_key, f.product_key, f.week_ending_date, f.closing_units, f.closing_value FROM fact_stock_week f), wk AS (SELECT cp.category, d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, d.fiscal_week, SUM(k.closing_value) AS week_value FROM stock k JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = k.week_ending_date JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = k.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = k.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 11 AND s.store_id < 900 AND s.store_id <> 999 AND cs.region = 'West' AND cp.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY ALL) SELECT category, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, ROUND(AVG(week_value), 2) AS avg_stock_value FROM wk GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY category
definitions_applied: Closing stock is a weekly snapshot: summed across stores and products within each week first, then averaged over the weeks of the period (never summed across weeks)
Stock value is closing_value, which is stock at standard cost in EUR
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 P11 is 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026, fiscal weeks 44 to 47, four weeks, fully loaded
As-is reporting: region taken from the current dim_store version (is_current) and category from the current dim_product version (is_current)
Stock by store covers physical stores only (store_id below 900), so the web shop is out, and the warehouse is not in this table
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Grain of fact_stock_week: one row per store_key, product_key and week_ending_date
Distinct natural keys: joins to versioned dimensions use the version key from the fact, then is_current for as-is
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26. The request was received on 5 Oct 2026, in FY2026/27, and past requests from May 2026 onward (FY2026/27) read 'last year' as FY2025/26 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35)
'Period 11' read as fiscal period 11 of FY2025/26, not a calendar month
'Average stock value' read as the average of the four weekly closing stock values at standard cost, which are the Sunday snapshots on 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026

'West' read as the West region as-is, meaning the current region assignment. This is the ten stores 115 to 123 and 136 (Tampere Hervanta, Tampere Lielahti, Tampere Kaleva, Nokia, Pori, Rauma, Vaasa, Seinäjoki, Kokkola, Tampere Lamminpää). Stores that moved out of South to Capital Region or East to South are not West as-is
Category is the current product category (as-is). This matters for outdoor lighting, which sits in Electrical for all history, and in P11 its product versions are already Electrical either way
The split is by category only, with one row per category and no total row, as the request did not ask for a total
caveats: Correction: the week ending 8 March 2026 (fiscal week 45) was loaded twice. 7,439 store x product rows appear a second time, loaded on 10 March at 02:45 after the original load on 9 March at 01:00, and the duplicates carry identical units and values. I kept one row per store, product and week. Summing the raw table would have overstated that week's stock by about 813,641 EUR company-wide and inflated the West averages
Week 44 has 102 more store x product rows than weeks 45 to 47, which looks like a normal change in ranging between weeks. I left those rows in as genuine snapshot rows

closing_value equals closing_units times the standard unit cost on every row checked for the West stores in P11, and no row has negative stock. Stock is valued at standard cost, not at selling price or purchase cost
Only the articles each store ranges (carries) have rows in fact_stock_week, so zero-stock lines (38 rows in the West in P11) are included at value 0 and absent articles are not
The control-total check against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply, because that table holds sales rather than stock
The warehouse is loaded through 4 Oct 2026, and P11 FY2025/26 is fully loaded, so the period is complete

answer.sql:
SELECT 
  p.category,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26,
  ROUND(
    (SUM(CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END) - 
     SUM(CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END)) /
    NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN f.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 0) * 100, 
    2
  ) AS growth_pct
FROM fact_sales_line f
INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
WHERE d.fiscal_period = 8
  AND p.category IN ('Garden', 'Electrical')
  AND d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25', 'FY2025/26')
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY p.category;
definitions_applied: Net sales: net_amount from fact_sales_line (net of line discounts, excluding VAT)
Fiscal period: period number from dim_date, with period 8 spanning the same calendar weeks in both fiscal years
Category: category from dim_product, matched to current product version
Sales lines: all transactions including both member and non-member sales, excluding staff purchase flag analysis
assumptions: Interpreted 'last year' as FY2025/26 (the most recent complete fiscal year with period 8 data) and 'year before' as FY2024/25 (the prior fiscal year)
Growth is calculated as year-over-year percentage change: (FY2025/26 P08 - FY2024/25 P08) / FY2024/25 P08 * 100
Net sales includes all regular customer sales plus staff purchases (which represent less than 2% of total sales for both categories)
Excluded web returns as these are recorded in fact_return_line; included only gross sales from fact_sales_line
caveats: Data availability: The warehouse contains only FY2026/27, FY2025/26, and FY2024/25 data. FY2023/24 and earlier years are not available.

Garden category shows significant decline (-34.21%), driven by both lower unit volume (2,505 lines in FY2024/25 vs 1,976 in FY2025/26) and lower average transaction value, which may warrant investigation into product assortment, pricing, or promotional activity changes
Both categories processed through 41 stores in both periods, ensuring consistency in store footprint across the comparison
Staff purchases represent 0.99% of Electrical sales in FY2024/25 and 1.15% in FY2025/26; and 0.80% of Garden in FY2024/25 and 1.71% in FY2025/26 — all immaterial to the totals

answer.sql: SELECT store_id, store_name, sqm, city, region, format FROM dim_store WHERE is_current = TRUE ORDER BY sqm DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
definitions_applied: Biggest stores: ranked by sales area (sqm)
Current store versions only: is_current = TRUE
Store classifications by size: sqm values assigned to Large or Medium format
assumptions: Interpreted 'biggest stores' as stores with the largest sales floor area (sqm)
Included only the current version of each store (is_current = TRUE) to avoid duplicates from slowly-changing dimensions
caveats: The request did not specify which dimension of 'size' to use (floor area, revenue, footfall, etc.); sqm (sales area) was chosen as the most straightforward physical measure
This ranking is by physical store size and does not reflect financial performance or sales volume

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS members_joined FROM dim_member WHERE join_date = '2026-10-03'
definitions_applied: Member join date: the join_date field in dim_member, representing when each member joined the loyalty program
Distinct count: members counted by distinct member_id to account for slowly changing dimension structure
assumptions: Date specified as 3 October 2026 is interpreted as 2026-10-03 in ISO date format
The question asks for the count of unique individuals who joined on this date, not the count of member records

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE CAST(order_ts_utc AS DATE) = DATE '2025-11-28' AND status <> 'cancelled'
definitions_applied: Web orders are counted from fact_web_order, not from sales lines
Cancelled orders are not counted as web orders
Orders still processing would count (there were none on this day)
Test orders (ZZ Test articles) and store 999 are excluded (none were found among these orders)
Count by the UTC order date, as the request asks, instead of the company default of the Helsinki order date
assumptions: Black Friday 2025 is Friday 28 November 2025, as the request says
'Placed' is read as order_ts_utc, the time the order was placed
Cancelled orders are left out, following the company definition of a web order
Click-and-collect and home delivery orders are both included, since both are web orders
Guest and logged-in orders are both included
caveats: The request asks for the UTC calendar day. The company default is the Helsinki order date, and I followed the request. On the Helsinki date the count would be 350, so 7 of the 357 orders fall on a different local day.
20 orders placed on 28 November (UTC) were cancelled and are excluded. Including them would give 377.
I checked for duplicate order ids, orders with missing timestamps, test articles and non-web store keys among these orders and found none, so no corrections were needed.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, w.order_member_key, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id=f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id=900 AND p.category<>'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_member_key IS NOT NULL THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END)/SUM(l.net_amount),2) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date=l.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Web sales identified by store 900, not channel_code
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (UTC converted to Europe/Helsinki)
Cancelled and processing web orders excluded (no dispatch, no sales lines)
Store 999 and ZZ Test articles excluded
Guest web orders count as non-member
Fiscal periods from dim_date (fiscal_year and fiscal_period columns)
Staff purchases included
Member status taken from fact_web_order.member_key (correction for line-level nulls)
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26 (the most recently completed fiscal year, as accepted in past requests from May 2026 onward); periods 9 to 11 are 22 Dec 2025 to 22 Mar 2026, 13 whole weeks, fully loaded, no week 53
'Share of web sales' read as the company member-share measure, i.e. before returns, rather than net of returns
A loyalty member means a web order with a member key (logged-in order); guest orders are non-members
Percentages are rounded to 2 decimals
caveats: Correction: in fact_sales_line, web lines of logged-in orders lost their member_key for orders placed between 9 February and 1 March 2026 (1,309 lines, which hit P10 and P11). Counting member_key on the lines would understate the member share: 51.77% in P10 and 55.81% in P11 instead of 67.52% and 66.70%. I took the member status from fact_web_order.member_key, which is filled for every logged-in order and agrees with the line's member where both exist. P9 is unaffected (67.99% either way). The line-level gap should be raised with the ETL owners.
If web sales were taken net of returns instead (refunds on their own return date, tied to the order's member), the shares would be 68.59% (P9), 67.41% (P10) and 67.96% (P11).
Member share is by order-level logged-in status at the time of the order; a member who bought as a guest cannot be identified and counts as non-member.
The requester did not say what 'last year' meant; if FY2024/25 was intended, the answer must be rerun.

answer.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM fact_web_order WHERE DATE(order_ts_utc) = '2025-12-01'
definitions_applied: Web order: one row in fact_web_order, identified by web_order_id
Order timestamp: order_ts_utc, converted to date for comparison
Cyber Monday 2025: 1 December 2025, confirmed as Monday in dim_date
assumptions: Cyber Monday is 1 December 2025 (the first Monday following Thanksgiving in the US calendar, commonly observed globally on that date)
Order timestamp in order_ts_utc is in UTC and represents when the order was placed
All orders in fact_web_order with order_ts_utc on 2025-12-01 are counted, regardless of status or fulfillment type
caveats: All 291 orders have valid timestamps with no null values; data quality is sound
Timestamps span the full day (00:11:43 to 23:33:52 UTC), indicating live order capture throughout the day
No orders excluded for data validation; no corrections applied

answer.sql:
WITH period_sales AS (
  SELECT
    f.sales_line_id,
    f.net_amount,
    s.format
  FROM fact_sales_line f
  INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key
  INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 5 AND 8
    AND s.store_id < 900
    AND p.category != 'ZZ Test'
)
SELECT
  ps.format,
  COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(ps.net_amount) * 100 AS return_rate_pct
FROM period_sales ps
LEFT JOIN fact_return_line r ON ps.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id
GROUP BY ps.format
ORDER BY ps.format
definitions_applied: Return rate: refund_net divided by net_amount, grouped by fiscal week of original sale (sale-week cohort)
Fiscal period: P2 FY2025/26 (fiscal weeks 5–8, 26 May to 22 June 2025)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900), excluding web and training stores
Product scope: excludes test articles (category ZZ Test)
Net sales: excluding VAT, after returns
assumptions: Period 2 last year interpreted as P2 FY2025/26, since request date 2026-10-06 falls in FY2026/27; precedent from requests D04, D08, D28, D35
Share interpreted as return rate: the percentage of sales that came back
Return rate cohort is by sale date (fiscal week of original purchase), not return date
caveats: Store format values are Large, Medium, Small (not Hyper, Standard, Express as per schema documentation)
Staff purchases are included per company definition
Return rate is a snapshot of current warehouse data; additional returns may arrive for P2 sales after the warehouse load date

answer.sql: SELECT tier, COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS member_count FROM dim_member WHERE tier = 'Gold' AND is_current GROUP BY tier
definitions_applied: Current member version: dim_member is slowly changing with one row per version, so only the row with is_current = true is used (valid_to = 9999-12-31)
Members counted once by member_id (the stable loyalty number), not by member_key
Loyalty tier as held on the current member version (Basic, Silver or Gold)
assumptions: 'Right now' means the current version of each member in the warehouse. The latest data is dated 2026-10-04 and the request came in on 2026-10-08, so changes made after 2026-10-04 are not captured.
'Members on the Gold tier' means all current Gold members, whatever their marketing consent or home store (including online sign-ups, store 900). No filter was applied.
caveats: Counting every row in dim_member with tier = 'Gold' would give 8,203, because it includes 2,412 superseded versions (2,233 members who were Gold earlier and have since changed tier or attributes). These were excluded, so the count is current versions only.

Integrity checks found no problems: each of the 60,000 members has exactly one current row, with no duplicates and no open-ended rows that are marked non-current. No Gold member has a future join date or version date.
stg_member_updates (4,061 rows) is a staging table. Every row is already in dim_member with identical values, so it adds nothing and was not used.
Anyone who changed tier after the warehouse's last load (2026-10-04) is not reflected in this figure.

answer.sql:
WITH fy26_p04 AS (
  SELECT 
    ds.store_id,
    SUM(fsl.net_amount) as sales
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key
  JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date
  WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
    AND dd.fiscal_period = 4
    AND ds.store_id < 900
  GROUP BY ds.store_id
),
fy25_p04 AS (
  SELECT 
    ds.store_id,
    SUM(fsl.net_amount) as sales
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key
  JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date
  WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26'
    AND dd.fiscal_period = 4
    AND ds.store_id < 900
  GROUP BY ds.store_id
),
lfl AS (
  SELECT 
    b.sales as fy25_sales,
    a.sales as fy26_sales
  FROM fy26_p04 a
  INNER JOIN fy25_p04 b ON a.store_id = b.store_id
)
SELECT 
  'FY2026/27' as fiscal_year,
  4 as period,
  ROUND(SUM(fy25_sales), 2) as fy25_p04_net_sales_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(fy26_sales), 2) as fy26_p04_net_sales_eur,
  ROUND((SUM(fy26_sales) - SUM(fy25_sales)) / NULLIF(SUM(fy25_sales), 0) * 100, 2) as like_for_like_growth_pct
FROM lfl
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) calculation: stores open and trading in both the same period in consecutive fiscal years
Net sales: gross sales lines after line discounts (net_amount field), excluding VAT
Store channel filter: store_id < 900 (excludes web channel code 900)
Fiscal period: week-aligned fiscal periods aligned to fiscal calendar
assumptions: Period 4 'this year' interpreted as FY2026/27 P04 (2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30)
Like-for-like comparison: same period in prior fiscal year FY2025/26 P04 (2025-07-28 to 2025-08-24)
Only stores with sales in both periods are included (38 of 39 total stores)
Store closure events are identified from dim_store.close_date (date the store closed)
caveats: One store (Savonlinna, store 129) had sales in FY2025/26 P04 but not in FY2026/27 P04; excluded from LFL as it closed 2026-01-25
Like-for-like growth of 0.01% is effectively flat (EUR 61.70 absolute growth on EUR 1,062,205 base)
Regional variation: North region +6.93%, East region -2.97%, West region -2.24%, Capital Region +2.68%, South region +0.03%
All figures are net sales excluding VAT; staff purchases are included in sales data
Web channel is excluded (filter applied: store_id < 900); web order line-item sales are counted separately in fact_sales_line

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 5 AND 8 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
definitions_applied: Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns
Returns reduce net sales on their own return date, not the original sale date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only), not the order date
Cancelled and still-processing orders are not web sales
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code (channel_code is not filled from the 3 Nov 2025 platform migration)
Click-and-collect counts as web
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Fiscal periods from dim_date (4-4-5 pattern, weeks Monday to Sunday)
Helsinki time for the dispatch date, converted from UTC
assumptions: Read 'last year' as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27 at the request date of 6 Oct 2026. Earlier accepted requests read it the same way.

Read 'periods 5 to 8' as FY2025/26 P05 (25 Aug to 21 Sep 2025), P06 (22 Sep to 26 Oct 2025), P07 (27 Oct to 23 Nov 2025) and P08 (24 Nov to 21 Dec 2025). I gave one figure per period because the request says 'in each of'.
Read 'what the web shop sold, net' as the company net sales definition for the web shop (store 900): sales excluding VAT, less web refunds booked to the web shop.
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT. Week 53 is not involved, because it falls in P12.
caveats: No data corrections were needed. Checks found no duplicate sales, return or web-order keys, no web lines outside store 900, no delivered or collected orders without a dispatch time, and no sales lines on cancelled or processing orders.
The result matches rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 exactly in all four periods (145,626.90, 175,588.62, 154,977.27 and 225,265.08).

Period 7 includes the 3 Nov 2025 web-platform migration. channel_code is empty from that date and the legacy views rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales leave out web sales from it. I used store 900 and did not use those views, so the figures are complete.
Test articles (ZZ Test) and store 999 were excluded. The warehouse has 19 ZZ Test lines on the web shop, and they would have slightly inflated web sales if left in.

Web refunds are booked where they are processed. Web orders returned at a physical store (for example stores 115, 131, 108 and 102) reduce that store's net sales and not the web shop's. This is the company definition, so the web figures above are not reduced by those in-store returns.

Web sales sit on the dispatch date, so an order placed late in one period and dispatched in the next counts in the later period. For click-and-collect the date is when the order was ready for collection.
Returns can arrive up to 30 days after a sale. Period 8 (ended 21 Dec 2025) is long past that window, so the figures will not move.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, member_key AS order_member_key, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), lines AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date, w.order_member_key, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN l.order_member_key IS NOT NULL THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END)/SUM(l.net_amount),1) AS member_share_of_web_sales_pct FROM lines l JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = l.dispatch_date WHERE d.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2
definitions_applied: Member share of sales: net sales before returns on member-linked lines divided by all net sales before returns
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (dispatch_ts_utc converted from UTC)
Web identified by store_id 900, not channel_code
Cancelled and processing orders excluded (no dispatch, not web sales)
Guest web orders count as non-member
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal periods from dim_date (FY2025/26 P9 = 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, P10 = 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026, P11 = 23 Feb to 22 Mar 2026)
Control total: web net sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900 in each period (219,929.50; 137,569.07; 149,798.62)
assumptions: 'Last year' on 9 Oct 2026 (in FY2026/27) read as FY2025/26, consistent with past accepted requests; periods 9 to 11 are therefore FY2025/26 P9 to P11
'Share of web sales' read as member net sales divided by total web net sales, before returns, following the company's member-share definition
'Loyalty members' read as logged-in web orders that carry a member key; guest checkouts are non-members
One row per period, as the request says 'by period'; no combined P9-P11 figure was given
caveats: Data defect corrected: in the web sales lines for about 9 Feb to 1 Mar 2026 (affecting P10 and P11), around 55% of logged-in orders lost the member_key on their sales lines. Taken from the lines, the member share would have been wrongly low (P10 51.8%, P11 55.8%). I took membership from fact_web_order.member_key instead, which is filled for every logged-in order and agrees with the line key wherever both exist. P9 is unaffected (68.0% either way).
Figures are before returns, so refunds on web orders are not deducted from either the member or the total figure.
Member share is by order-level member key, so it counts the member of the order as of the order date.
Shares are rounded to one decimal place.

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(net_sales) AS net_sales FROM rpt_daily_store_sales WHERE business_date >= '2026-09-01' AND business_date < '2026-10-01'
definitions_applied: Net sales: the company's revenue net of returns and VAT (from rpt_daily_store_sales.net_sales)
Last month: the previous complete calendar month (September 2026, from October 15, 2026 reference date)
Whole company: all 39 operating stores included in the sales report
assumptions: Last month interpreted as the full calendar month preceding the request (September 2026), not a rolling 30-day period
Net sales sourced from rpt_daily_store_sales table rather than aggregating fact_sales_line, as this report is the official daily summary
caveats: Data current through October 4, 2026 (request dated October 9, 2026 but data nine days behind)

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-06-01' AS start_date, DATE '2026-06-28' AS end_date), period_days AS (SELECT d.calendar_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.calendar_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date AND d.is_trading_day), trading_days AS (SELECT cs.store_id, COUNT(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store cs CROSS JOIN period_days pd WHERE cs.is_current AND cs.store_id < 900 AND (cs.open_date IS NULL OR cs.open_date <= pd.calendar_date) AND (cs.close_date IS NULL OR cs.close_date >= pd.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = cs.store_id AND pd.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), store_sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ss.net_sales / td.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(ss.net_sales / td.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM store_sales ss JOIN trading_days td ON td.store_id = ss.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = ss.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: physical stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Trading days: days the store was open, after opening and before closure, outside refit closures (ref_store_closure) and excluding closed holidays (dim_date.is_trading_day = false)
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) and training store 999 excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P02 = fiscal weeks 5 to 8, Monday 1 June to Sunday 28 June 2026 (28 days)
Store attributes (name) taken from the current dim_store version (as-is)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' read as FY2026/27 P02 (1 to 28 June 2026), the current fiscal year; it is complete and fully loaded (warehouse is loaded through 4 October 2026)
'Store ranking' read as the store league table: ranked by net sales per trading day, the basis of the accepted league-table requests (REQ-D37 to D40), not by total net sales
Rank 1 is the highest net sales per trading day; ties would share a rank, and there were none
Stores that did not trade for the whole period (Kuopio) are kept and ranked on their own trading days
Net sales per trading day is rounded to 2 decimals; ranking is done on the unrounded values
Total net sales and trading days per store are not shown because they were not asked for; they are available on request
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026 (ref_store_closure), so it traded only 14 of the 26 trading days other stores had; its figure is per trading day over those 14 days, not a full-period figure. It would rank lower on total period sales (23,993.71 EUR) than its rank of 7 suggests
Midsummer Eve and Midsummer Day (19 and 20 June 2026) are closed days, so every fully trading store has 26 trading days rather than 28
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no sales in P2, so it is not in the table (38 of the 39 current physical stores are shown)

Period average = mean of the four weekly closings (week endings 1, 8, 15 and 22 March 2026)

The whole period is loaded and the four weekly snapshots are complete; the sum of the category averages (EUR 813,525.02) matches the West total averaged directly.

WITH net_lines AS (
    -- sales: stores on the sale date
    SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id,
           f.net_amount AS net_sales
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
    UNION ALL
    -- returns reduce net sales on the return date
    SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net
    FROM fact_return_line r
    JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = r.store_key
    JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key
    WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
),
by_region AS (
    SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, cs.region, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales
    FROM net_lines n
    JOIN dim_date d  ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date
    JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current
    WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 1 AND 22
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)
SELECT 
  region,
  ROUND(SUM(net_sales), 2) as net_sales,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(net_sales) DESC) as rank
FROM by_region
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Net sales: the net amount excluding VAT after returns, on the return date for refunds
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900), excluding training store (999) and test articles (category ZZ Test)
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 weeks 1-22 (4 May to 4 October 2026), the company's fiscal year to date as of the request
Regions: current (as-is) region assignments from dim_store.is_current
assumptions: Interpreted 'this year so far' as FY2026/27 (the current fiscal year from 4 May 2026), weeks 1-22 as loaded in the warehouse through 4 October 2026
Performance ranking: ordered by net sales descending (primary metric for regional comparison)
As-is reporting: restated history to current region hierarchy; Capital Region includes stores that moved there on 28 April 2025
caveats: Data available through 4 October 2026 only (the warehouse load date); 30 of 52 weeks in FY2026/27 remain unreported
Web shop (store 900) excluded per request; net sales of 1,110,040.88 excluded from this answer
Training store (999) and test articles (ZZ Test) excluded from all figures per company rules
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and is not in the data for this year; Kuopio (125) had a refit closure from 15 June to 26 July 2026 (6 weeks)

Member counted once by member_id, not by member_key
Loyalty tier as stored on the current version of the member

'Gold-tier loyalty members' means every member whose current tier is Gold, whatever their marketing consent or home store
No activity or expiry filter was applied, because the warehouse has no membership status column
caveats: I checked dim_member for duplicate current versions, is_current flags that disagree with valid_to, and tier values outside Basic, Silver and Gold. I found none. Each of the 60,000 members has exactly one current version, and 5,791 of them are Gold.

Counting all rows with tier = 'Gold' gives 8,203 (5,791 current plus 2,412 past versions), which overstates the answer. Past Gold versions belong to members who moved tier or are listed again under a newer version.
stg_member_updates holds 4,061 rows dated from 2026-09-04 to 2026-10-04. All of them are already in dim_member with identical tier and dates, so the count includes them.

answer.sql:
WITH store_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    s.region,
    SUM(rds.net_sales) as net_sales
  FROM rpt_daily_store_sales rds
  LEFT JOIN dim_date d ON rds.business_date = d.calendar_date
  LEFT JOIN dim_store s ON rds.store_id = s.store_id AND d.calendar_date >= s.valid_from AND d.calendar_date <= s.valid_to
  WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25')
    AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3
    AND rds.store_id < 900
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, s.region
),
web_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    d.fiscal_year,
    'Web shop' as region,
    SUM(fsl.net_amount - COALESCE(frl.refund_net, 0)) as net_sales
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  LEFT JOIN fact_return_line frl ON fsl.sales_line_id = frl.sales_line_id
  LEFT JOIN dim_date d ON fsl.sale_date = d.calendar_date
  WHERE d.fiscal_year IN ('FY2025/26', 'FY2024/25')
    AND d.fiscal_quarter = 3
    AND fsl.channel_code = 'WB'
  GROUP BY d.fiscal_year
),
combined_sales AS (
  SELECT fiscal_year, region, net_sales FROM store_sales
  UNION ALL
  SELECT fiscal_year, region, net_sales FROM web_sales
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT 
    region,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) as fy2525_sales,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' THEN net_sales ELSE 0 END) as fy2425_sales
  FROM combined_sales
  GROUP BY region
)
SELECT 
  region,
  ROUND(fy2525_sales, 2) as q3_fy2525_net_sales,
  ROUND(fy2425_sales, 2) as q3_fy2425_net_sales,
  CASE 
    WHEN fy2425_sales != 0 THEN ROUND((fy2525_sales - fy2425_sales) / fy2425_sales * 100, 1)
    ELSE NULL
  END as growth_percentage
FROM pivoted
ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Net sales from rpt_daily_store_sales (store sales, net of returns) for physical stores excluding pseudo-locations (store_id < 900)
Web shop sales from fact_sales_line with channel_code = 'WB', net of returns from fact_return_line
Growth percentage calculated as (current period - prior period) / prior period × 100
assumptions: Last year = FY2025/26 Q3 (most recent completed fiscal year); the year before = FY2024/25 Q3
Web shop treated as a separate line from regional stores, using fact_sales_line channel_code = 'WB' (not store_id = 900)
Store sales sourced from rpt_daily_store_sales rather than fact_sales_line to use the maintained Data & Analytics report
All amounts in EUR excluding VAT (net basis), as defined by the warehouse
caveats: Capital Region is new as of FY2025/26 P01 (2025-04-28); no prior-year data exists for comparison. The 0.00 value indicates the region did not operate in Q3 FY2024/25.
Web shop sales declined 92% year-over-year, from EUR 440,057.54 to EUR 34,335.23. This substantial drop warrants investigation into whether it reflects a genuine business change or a data issue.
Southern region sales declined 37% (EUR 1,163,921.84 to EUR 729,021.20) and Eastern region declined 9% (EUR 659,319.32 to EUR 597,583.01). Only North (+6.7%) and West (+4.8%) regions showed growth.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 14 AS first_week, 17 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52)), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), lfl_sales AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND LEAST(params.last_week, 52) GROUP BY d.fiscal_year) SELECT params.ty_year AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period, ROUND(100.0 * (ty.net_sales / ly.net_sales - 1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM params JOIN lfl_sales ty ON ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year JOIN lfl_sales ly ON ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year
definitions_applied: LFL growth: net sales in LFL stores vs the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) excluded
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Net sales = net amount excluding VAT after returns, with returns booked on their own return date
Opening rule: store open at least 364 days before the first day of the period (3 Aug 2026)
Store-week counts only if the store traded in that fiscal week in both years (open, not closed, no ref_store_closure refit week)
Week 53 never counts (not in P4 anyway)
Fiscal calendar: P4 = fiscal weeks 14 to 17, 4-4-5 pattern, weeks aligned by fiscal week number, not by calendar date
As-is store region and attributes (current dim_store version)
Control total check against rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Period 4 this year' read as FY2026/27 P4 (fiscal weeks 14 to 17, Monday 3 Aug to Sunday 30 Aug 2026), compared with FY2025/26 P4 (weeks 14 to 17, 28 Jul to 24 Aug 2025). It is a complete period, loaded in the warehouse through 4 Oct 2026.
Read as one total LFL growth figure, since no breakdown was requested.
Growth is rounded to two decimals in percent units (-0.03 means -0.03%, practically flat).
Open and close dates are taken from the current dim_store version, as in earlier accepted LFL requests.
caveats: Savonlinna (129) is out of the LFL base for all four weeks because it closed on 25 January 2026 and did not trade in FY2026/27 P4. Its sales of about 9,549 EUR in the comparison weeks last year are not in the base.

The base is 38 physical stores, 152 store-weeks in each year, and every store traded in all four weeks in both years. The two stores opened in 2024 (Tampere Lamminpää 136, Lohja 137) pass the 52-week rule for this period.
No refit closures fall in P4 in either year. Kuopio's refit ended on 26 Jul 2026, before P4 began, so Kuopio is fully in the base.

LFL net sales are 1,010,478.52 EUR this year against 1,010,743.32 EUR last year, a difference of about 265 EUR, so the result is essentially flat. Store results vary widely: Mikkeli is down 26.2% and Lohja up 25.4%.
Control check: for the same 38 stores and weeks, my store-day net sales match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly, with a gap of 0.00 and no store-day differences, in both years.
Not used on purpose: rpt.v_daily_sales and rpt.v_weekly_store_sales (they drop web sales from 3 Nov 2025), the bak_, stg_, tmp_ and _old tables, and channel_code.

WITH member_first_version AS (
  SELECT 
    member_id,
    home_store_id,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY valid_from ASC) as version_num
  FROM dim_member

WHERE m.version_num = 1
GROUP BY m.home_store_id, s.store_name
