answer.sql: WITH active AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE f.sale_date > DATE '2025-12-21' - 364 AND f.sale_date <= DATE '2025-12-21' AND s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT m.tier, COUNT(DISTINCT a.member_id) AS active_members FROM active a JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_id = a.member_id AND DATE '2025-12-21' BETWEEN m.valid_from AND m.valid_to GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CASE m.tier WHEN 'Basic' THEN 1 WHEN 'Silver' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks, ending with and including the as-of week (sale_date > as-of Sunday - 364 and <= as-of Sunday), in any channel
Distinct count by member_id, not member_key
Tier read from the dim_member version valid on the as-of Sunday
End of period 8 taken from ref_fiscal_calendar: FY2025/26 P08 ends Sunday 21 December 2025
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases count as purchases
Web lines counted on sale_date (order date), as in the accepted active-member queries, with no channel_code filter
assumptions: 'Last year' read as FY2025/26, the fiscal year before the current FY2026/27. This follows the readings accepted for requests made in May 2026 and later in FY2026/27 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35).
'End of period 8' read as the last day of FY2025/26 P08, Sunday 21 December 2025. The 52-week window therefore runs from 23 December 2024 to 21 December 2025.
Tier is the tier on 21 December 2025, not a member's current tier.
Sanna gave no breakdown beyond tier, so the table has no total row. The three tiers add up to 29,526 active members.
caveats: fact_sales_line holds 418 duplicated receipt_id and line_no pairs in the window, loaded twice. This does not affect the count, because it is a distinct count of members.
Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test lines changed nothing. Every member with a test or training purchase also had a real purchase in the window.
Every active member had exactly one dim_member version valid on 21 December 2025, so no member was dropped or counted twice.
I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales, channel_code, the stg_, bak_ or tmp_ tables, or the old dimension tables.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), lines AS (SELECT CASE WHEN s.store_id = 900 THEN w.dispatch_date ELSE f.sale_date END AS business_date, s.region, f.gross_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT region, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-08-31' THEN gross_amount END) AS gross_sales_incl_vat_aug_2024, SUM(CASE WHEN business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-09-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' THEN gross_amount END) AS gross_sales_incl_vat_sep_2024 FROM lines WHERE business_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-08-01' AND DATE '2024-09-30' GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
definitions_applied: Gross sales including VAT = sum of gross_amount on the sales lines (each line carries its own VAT rate)
Before returns: no refunds deducted
As-was region: dim_store joined on the fact's store_key, so the region is the one valid on the transaction date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (delivered and collected orders only)
Store lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop (store 900) shown as its own region, Online
Staff purchases included
Calendar months used (1-31 Aug 2024 and 1-30 Sep 2024)
No deprecated tables, staging or backup tables, or rpt views used
assumptions: August and September 2024 are read as calendar months, not fiscal periods, because the figures are for a VAT filing
'Regions as they were at the time' is read as as-was: the region each store had on the date of sale. In 2024 there is no Capital Region, and stores 101-105 are in South and Kouvola (114) is in East
Web sales are placed in the Online region as their own row, because the web shop is not in any physical region
Web sales follow the company recognition rule (dispatch date in Helsinki time) rather than the order date, because the request did not ask for anything different
Refunds are not shown at all, since the request says before returns
caveats: Excluded from the figures: store 999 training-store lines (EUR 4,282.23 gross in August, EUR 3,351.71 in September) and ZZ Test web lines (EUR 8.06 in August, EUR 3.77 in September). If Finance wants every receipt in the warehouse, add these back

Web orders are counted by dispatch date, not order date. Some orders placed in late August were dispatched in September (and late September into October), so the Online figures differ from a count by order date. Web orders are placed in the month they were dispatched, which may not match the month in which Finance's VAT point of supply or invoicing falls; check this before filing

The VAT rate for the general class rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024. The line gross_amount carries the rate applied on each line, so August lines are mostly at 24% and September lines at 25.5%. Reduced rates (14%, 10%) are unchanged. A web order placed before 1 September but dispatched in September carries its order-date rate
Orders with status cancelled or processing have no dispatch date and are not in the Online figures (none were found in Jul-Oct 2024)

Checks run: no duplicate sales lines in the period; every line's store and product version was valid on its sale date; sale_date matches the Helsinki date of sale_ts_utc on all lines; net sales before returns by store and month tie to the rpt_daily_store_sales control with no differences. The control compares net, not gross, so the VAT amounts themselves are not independently checked against another source
The region column comment in the warehouse is out of date (it lists four regions); the as-was result uses the four regions that existed in 2024 plus Online

answer.sql: SELECT p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f INNER JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date INNER JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key AND d.calendar_date >= s.valid_from AND d.calendar_date <= s.valid_to INNER JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key AND d.calendar_date >= p.valid_from AND d.calendar_date <= p.valid_to WHERE s.store_id = 102 AND s.store_id != 999 AND p.category != 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN 18 AND 21 GROUP BY p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period P5 FY2026/27: 28 August to 27 September 2026 (fiscal weeks 18-21)
Units sold: quantity from fact_sales_line, sum across all transactions
Store versions joined by validity dates to match store at transaction date
Product versions joined by validity dates to match product at transaction date
House rules: store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
assumptions: Request phrase 'period 5 this year' interpreted as P5 of the current fiscal year FY2026/27
Store name 'Helsinki Pitäjänmäki' matched to store_id 102
Ranked by total quantity across all transactions at the store during the period
caveats: All three products are physical merchandise (Fixings & Fasteners and Batteries & Bulbs categories), not returns or non-standard sales
The house-rule filters (store 999, ZZ Test) do not change this result

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(fsl.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line fsl INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key WHERE ds.store_id = 108 AND LOWER(dp.subcategory) = 'interior paint' AND fsl.sale_date >= '2026-06-29' AND fsl.sale_date <= '2026-08-02'
definitions_applied: Interior Paint: all products with subcategory = Interior Paint
Lahti store: store_id 108 (dim_store)
Period 3 of FY26/27: fiscal dates 2026-06-29 to 2026-08-02 (ref_fiscal_calendar)
Units sold: sum of quantity column from fact_sales_line
assumptions: Request refers to all Interior Paint products, not a specific variant
Request includes all sales channels (store and web) at the Lahti location
Request asks for gross sales units, not net after returns
caveats: 125 distinct Interior Paint products were active during this period; query aggregates all variants
Data includes 142 sales lines across 137 receipts; no quality issues detected
No deviations or data corrections needed

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, fulfilment_type, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), web_net AS (SELECT w.dispatch_date AS business_date, w.fulfilment_type, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, w.fulfilment_type, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key JOIN fact_sales_line f ON f.sales_line_id = r.sales_line_id JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id = 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN n.fulfilment_type = 'click_and_collect' THEN n.net_sales ELSE 0 END) / SUM(n.net_sales), 2) AS click_collect_share_pct FROM web_net n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period IN (9, 10) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2
definitions_applied: Click-and-collect share = click-and-collect net sales divided by all web net sales (click-and-collect counted as web)
Net sales excluding VAT, after returns; returns reduce net sales on their own return date
Web sales recognised on the Helsinki dispatch date (dispatch_ts_utc converted from UTC), not the order date
Web identified by store_id 900, not by channel_code
Click-and-collect identified by fact_web_order.fulfilment_type; returns assigned to the order type through sales_line_id
Cancelled and still-processing orders are not web sales (only delivered and collected orders with a dispatch time)
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Fiscal periods from dim_date (fiscal_year and fiscal_period), not calendar months
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900
assumptions: Request received 6 Oct 2026 (FY2026/27), so 'last year' is read as FY2025/26, as in past requests made in FY2026/27 (REQ-D04, D08, D28, D35). FY2025/26 P9 is 22 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026 and P10 is 26 Jan to 22 Feb 2026.
'Periods 9 and 10' is read as one share per period, giving two rows, not a single combined share for the two periods.
'Web sales' is read as net sales on the company definition (excluding VAT, after returns), the basis used for the click-and-collect share in REQ-D22.
Returns count as web returns only when they were booked to the web shop (store 900), as the company net sales definition and the control total do.
caveats: Web sales are dated by Helsinki dispatch date. For click-and-collect that is the date the order was ready for collection, not the date the customer collected it. The order date is not used.

Some refunds on web orders were processed in physical stores. In P9 these were 1,100.14 EUR on click-and-collect and 4,657.68 EUR on home delivery. In P10 they were 1,655.62 EUR and 3,356.20 EUR. They are not part of web net sales on the company definition and are not deducted. If every refund were followed back to its web order, the shares would shift slightly.
Before returns, the share is 28.95% for P9 (63,662.80 of 219,929.50 EUR) and 30.62% for P10 (42,118.86 of 137,569.07 EUR).
Figures after returns are: P9 click-and-collect 58,536.07 of 200,208.58 EUR web net sales; P10 37,861.39 of 123,131.15 EUR.

The control total agrees with rpt_daily_store_sales for store 900. Sales before returns were 219,929.50 and 137,569.07 EUR, web returns were 19,720.92 and 14,437.92 EUR, and net sales were 200,208.58 and 123,131.15 EUR for P9 and P10. No unexplained gap.
No ZZ Test or store 999 lines changed the totals for these periods (the control total matches with the filters applied).
Period 10 contains 4 weeks and period 9 contains 5 weeks. The shares are ratios, so period length does not distort them.

I did not use rpt.v_daily_sales or rpt.v_weekly_store_sales, or channel_code for web or click-and-collect. The periods are before the 3 Nov 2025 migration cut-off in the other direction, but fulfilment_type and store 900 are valid across the whole range.

answer.sql:
SELECT 
  dp.sku,
  dp.product_name,
  SUM(fsl.quantity) as units_sold,
  SUM(fsl.net_amount) as net_sales
FROM fact_sales_line fsl
INNER JOIN dim_product dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key
INNER JOIN dim_date dd ON fsl.sale_date = dd.calendar_date
WHERE dd.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27'
  AND dd.fiscal_period = 5
  AND fsl.staff_purchase_flag = false
GROUP BY dp.sku, dp.product_name
ORDER BY units_sold DESC
LIMIT 10
definitions_applied: Best-selling defined as highest units sold (standard retail measure)
Last period = most recently completed fiscal period (FY2026/27 P05, fully loaded)
Excludes staff purchases
assumptions: Best-selling interpreted as volume (units sold) rather than revenue
Period = one complete fiscal period, not calendar month or year
Includes both store and web channel sales
caveats: Net sales shown in EUR excluding VAT. P05 covers 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27
Return rates are low (<4% for these products) and do not change ranking
FY2026/27 P06 is partially loaded (current period); P05 is the latest complete period

answer.sql: SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period AS period, SUM(f.gross_amount) AS web_sales_incl_vat FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE f.channel_code = 'WB' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 4 AND 6 GROUP BY d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period ORDER BY d.fiscal_period
definitions_applied: Web sales = fact_sales_line rows with channel_code 'WB' (all web shop lines, home delivery and click-and-collect)
Sales including VAT = gross_amount as stored on the line, before returns (fact_return_line not used)
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: FY2024/25 P04 29 Jul to 25 Aug 2024 (4 weeks), P05 26 Aug to 22 Sep 2024 (4 weeks), P06 23 Sep to 27 Oct 2024 (5 weeks)
Q2 = fiscal periods 4 to 6, reported as one figure per period
sale_date is Helsinki local date (checked against sale_ts_utc), so used as is for period assignment
VAT rate as applied on each line (standard rate 24% to 31 Aug 2024, 25.5% from 1 Sep 2024)
assumptions: Q2 of FY24/25 read as the warehouse's FY2024/25 (the year starting 29 Apr 2024)
Request says 'web sales', so click-and-collect orders are included along with home delivery, because both are web channel orders
Cancelled web orders are left out, since they have no sales lines. Staff purchase lines are included, though no web lines carry the staff flag
Figures are in EUR including VAT
caveats: No corrections were needed. In the Q2 window the web lines had no duplicate line ids, no duplicate receipt/line pairs, and no gaps in daily coverage. Gross amounts matched net amounts times (1 + VAT rate) on every line, and each web order's lines matched its order total and line count in fact_web_order
The three periods sum to 499,578.73, which agrees with the total of web lines for 29 Jul to 27 Oct 2024
Periods 4 to 6 are marked fully loaded in ref_fiscal_calendar

dim_channel.channel_id is empty on all lines in this window because it only applies from the web-platform migration, so the web channel was identified through channel_code = 'WB' (store key 900, Tuomimetsä web shop)
VAT rate changed on 1 Sep 2024, so P05 and P06 gross figures carry 25.5% on standard-rated lines and P04 carries 24%. The P04 to P06 growth in gross sales is partly a rate effect
P06 has 5 weeks against 4 for P04 and P05, so it is not directly comparable to them without adjusting for length
172 cancelled web orders... 257 cancelled web orders (EUR 18,204.46 gross) exist in the window with no sales lines, and are excluded, as expected for cancelled orders

answer.sql: SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(f.quantity) as units_sold FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON f.store_key = s.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON f.sale_date = d.calendar_date WHERE f.store_key = 4 AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 5 GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, p.sku, p.product_name ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 3
definitions_applied: Fiscal period: FY2026/27 period 5 (fiscal weeks 18-21, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-27)
Units sold: sum of quantity from fact_sales_line
Store: Helsinki Pitäjänmäki (store_id 102, store_key 4, current version)
assumptions: Store version: Used store_key 4 (current version, valid from 2025-04-28), which was active during period 5
Product version: Used current product versions at the time of sale, as stored in product_key
caveats: The Pitäjänmäki store has two recorded versions in the warehouse: store_key 3 (South region, valid until 2025-04-27) and store_key 4 (Capital Region, current). The April 2025 region reorganisation moved Pitäjänmäki from South to Capital Region.
Period 5 data is complete and fully loaded through 2026-09-27

answer.sql: WITH cur AS (SELECT store_id, store_name, CASE WHEN store_id=900 THEN 'Web shop' ELSE region END AS region_line FROM dim_store WHERE is_current AND store_id <> 999), sk AS (SELECT store_key, c.region_line FROM dim_store s JOIN cur c USING(store_id)), fy AS (SELECT calendar_date, fiscal_year FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_quarter=3 AND fiscal_year IN ('FY2024/25','FY2025/26')), sales AS (SELECT fy.fiscal_year, sk.region_line, f.net_amount AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN fy ON fy.calendar_date=f.sale_date JOIN sk USING(store_key)), rets AS (SELECT fy.fiscal_year, sk.region_line, -r.refund_net AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN fy ON fy.calendar_date=r.return_date JOIN sk USING(store_key)), agg AS (SELECT region_line, fiscal_year, sum(amt) net_sales FROM (SELECT * FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT * FROM rets) GROUP BY ALL) SELECT a.region_line AS region, 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 3 AS fiscal_quarter, round(a.net_sales,2) AS net_sales_fy2025_26, round(b.net_sales,2) AS net_sales_fy2024_25, round(100*(a.net_sales/b.net_sales-1),1) AS growth_pct FROM agg a JOIN agg b ON a.region_line=b.region_line AND b.fiscal_year='FY2024/25' WHERE a.fiscal_year='FY2025/26' ORDER BY CASE WHEN a.region_line='Web shop' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, 1
definitions_applied: Net sales = line net_amount (EUR excl. VAT, after line discounts) minus refund_net on returns booked in the period, matching how rpt_daily_store_sales defines net_sales
Fiscal calendar from dim_date: Q3 = fiscal periods 7-9 (FY2025/26 Q3: 2025-10-27 to 2026-01-25; FY2024/25 Q3: 2024-10-28 to 2025-01-26)
Web shop is its own line (store_id 900): home delivery and click-and-collect both count as web
Returns are netted in the period of the return date, against the store/web shop recorded on the return
Training store (999) excluded as a non-trading pseudo-location
Staff purchases are included, as in rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Last year' read as the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26 (request dated 2026-10-06, inside FY2026/27), and 'the year before' as FY2024/25; Q3 means fiscal Q3, not calendar Q3
Both Q3s have 13 weeks, so FY2025/26 being a 53-week year does not distort the comparison
All stores trading in each period are included (not like-for-like), since the request asks for regional net sales and not a like-for-like comparison
Growth % = (FY2025/26 / FY2024/25 - 1) x 100, rounded to one decimal; amounts are in EUR excluding VAT
Staff purchases kept in net sales because the company's daily sales report includes them
caveats: Correction: regions were reorganised from 2025-04-28. Stores 101-105 moved from South to a new Capital Region, and Kouvola (114) moved from East to South. The sales lines carry the region version in force at the sale date, so a plain join would put the FY2024/25 Capital Region stores into South. I restated both years to the current region assignment, so the regional growth rates are like-for-like on region definition.

Correction: from 2025-11-03 the channel_code column is empty and the channel_id column is used instead (1 store, 2 web home delivery, 3 click-and-collect). I identified the web shop by store_id 900 rather than by channel_code, otherwise most FY2025/26 web sales would be lost.
Correction: the training store (999) has sales lines, about EUR 6.5k in FY2024/25 Q3 and EUR 6.9k in FY2025/26 Q3, mostly staff purchases. These are excluded.
Correction: web returns are booked against the web shop, and I netted them in the web line. Web net sales are therefore EUR 626.7k before returns in FY2025/26, against EUR 577.1k as reported here.

The pre-calculated web figures in rpt_daily_store_sales are unreliable. Several days (e.g. 2024-11-03, 2025-11-02) show receipts and sales far below the underlying lines, and one day is negative. I used the fact tables for the web line. The store figures in that table agree with the fact tables.

Growth is not like-for-like on stores. Tampere Lamminpää (136) opened in Sept 2024 and Lohja (137) in Nov 2024. Lohja has no sales for the first 8 days of the FY2024/25 Q3 (it traded 77 of 85 days). The new stores lift West (+4.8%) and South (+2.7%). Savonlinna (129) closed on 2026-01-25, the last day of FY2025/26 Q3, so it is fully in the period.
Capital Region and the other regions cannot be compared with pre-2025-04-28 history on the old regional definitions without the same restatement.
Both quarters are fully loaded and contain no duplicate line IDs. No gaps in trading days were found, and VAT and net amounts reconcile.

answer.sql: SELECT SUM(fsl.quantity) AS units_sold FROM fact_sales_line AS fsl INNER JOIN dim_product AS dp ON fsl.product_key = dp.product_key INNER JOIN dim_store AS ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key WHERE ds.city = 'Lahti' AND dp.subcategory = 'Interior Paint' AND fsl.sale_date >= '2026-06-29' AND fsl.sale_date <= '2026-08-02' AND fsl.staff_purchase_flag = false
definitions_applied: Interior Paint: products with subcategory = 'Interior Paint' in dim_product
Lahti store: store with city = 'Lahti' in dim_store
Period 3 of FY2026/27: fiscal period 3 (2026-06-29 to 2026-08-02) per ref_fiscal_calendar
Units sold: customer sales only (staff_purchase_flag = false)
assumptions: Interior Paint refers to the 'Interior Paint' subcategory in the product dimension
Lahti store is identified by city name, not store ID
Units sold excludes staff purchases, which are internal company transactions not customer sales
caveats: Four additional units of Interior Paint were purchased by staff during this period (2026-08-01) but are excluded per the standard definition of 'units sold'
The Lahti store has a single dimension record valid from 2000-01-01 onwards with no version changes during the query period

definitions_applied: Last week = last completed fiscal week (Monday to Sunday, FY2026/27 week 22, 28 Sep to 4 Oct 2026)
Units sold = quantity on fact_sales_line, by sale_date (Helsinki business date)
Store-level scope: store_id 131, physical store only; store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (no effect on this figure)
Natural keys: store_id 131 and sku 101624 (each has a single version in dim_store and dim_product)
Control total: store 131 daily units and net sales before returns checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for 28 Sep to 4 Oct
No deprecated objects used (no stg_, bak_, tmp_, _old tables, no rpt.v_ views, no channel_code)

No data problems found for this store, SKU and week: no duplicate lines (sales_line_id and receipt_id + line_no are unique), no negative quantities, and the store's daily units and net sales before returns match rpt_daily_store_sales exactly for all seven days. No corrections were needed.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS ty_year, 'FY2025/26' AS ly_year, 1 AS first_week, 22 AS last_week), range_start AS (SELECT MIN(d.calendar_date) AS first_day FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND d.fiscal_week = params.first_week), weeks AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_week, d.fiscal_week_start_date, d.fiscal_week_end_date FROM dim_date d CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week), store_weeks AS (SELECT st.store_id, w.fiscal_year, w.fiscal_week, (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= w.fiscal_week_end_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND c.closure_start_date <= w.fiscal_week_end_date AND c.closure_end_date >= w.fiscal_week_start_date) AS trading FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN weeks w WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900), lfl_store_weeks AS (SELECT ty.store_id, ty.fiscal_week FROM store_weeks ty CROSS JOIN params CROSS JOIN range_start JOIN store_weeks ly ON ly.store_id = ty.store_id AND ly.fiscal_week = ty.fiscal_week AND ly.fiscal_year = params.ly_year JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_id = ty.store_id AND st.is_current WHERE ty.fiscal_year = params.ty_year AND ty.trading AND ly.trading AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= range_start.first_day - 364)), sales_dedup AS (SELECT * FROM fact_sales_line QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY receipt_id, line_no ORDER BY etl_loaded_at, sales_line_id) = 1), net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM sales_dedup f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), agg AS (SELECT d.fiscal_year, cs.region, SUM(CASE WHEN l.store_id IS NOT NULL THEN n.net_sales END) AS lfl_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = n.store_id AND cs.is_current LEFT JOIN lfl_store_weeks l ON l.store_id = n.store_id AND l.fiscal_week = d.fiscal_week CROSS JOIN params WHERE d.fiscal_year IN (params.ty_year, params.ly_year) AND d.fiscal_week BETWEEN params.first_week AND params.last_week GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ty.lfl_sales/ly.lfl_sales DESC) AS rank, ty.region, ROUND(ty.lfl_sales, 2) AS lfl_net_sales_this_year, ROUND(ly.lfl_sales, 2) AS lfl_net_sales_last_year, ROUND(100.0*(ty.lfl_sales/ly.lfl_sales-1), 2) AS lfl_growth_pct FROM agg ty JOIN agg ly ON ly.region = ty.region AND ly.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' WHERE ty.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Like-for-like (LFL) growth: net sales in the LFL stores against the same fiscal weeks last year, week by week

LFL store-week rule: the store must have traded in that fiscal week in both years; store 125 Kuopio's FY2026/27 refit weeks, store 119 Pori's FY2025/26 refit weeks and store 129 Savonlinna's closed weeks drop out
LFL opening rule: open at least 364 days before the first day of the range
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT, after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) excluded; training store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included in net sales
As-is regions: current dim_store version, so the five regions including Capital Region apply to both years
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 weeks 1 to 22 (4 May to 4 October 2026) against FY2025/26 weeks 1 to 22 (28 April to 28 September 2025), lined up by fiscal week number
Control total: region totals checked against rpt_daily_store_sales for the same weeks
assumptions: 'This year so far' is read as the fiscal year to date, FY2026/27 weeks 1 to 22, the last fully loaded week (warehouse loaded through Sunday 4 October 2026). It runs from 4 May 2026, and week 23 is not yet started.

'How they are doing' is read as growth against last year, ranked on like-for-like net sales growth, because the regions differ in size and are affected by refits and a closure. Rank 1 is the highest LFL growth. The request did not say which measure to rank on.
'Stores only' is read as store_id below 900. Click-and-collect and other web orders are excluded, since web is booked to store 900 (region Online).
Regions are as-is, the current five-region hierarchy, restated back over last year. Capital Region exists in last year's comparison only on this basis. No as-was view was asked for.
Week 53 is not involved, because FY2025/26 week 53 falls after week 22.
Rank is shown with RANK(); there are no ties.
caveats: Correction 1, duplicate sales lines: store 116 (West) has its sales for 15 to 21 September 2025 (FY2025/26 week 20) loaded twice in fact_sales_line, 418 receipt lines each duplicated under a new sales_line_id. The duplicates inflated last year's West net sales by 10,390.53 EUR, which is exactly the gap to rpt_daily_store_sales. I kept the first load of each receipt_id and line_no. After the correction every region matches the control table for both years. Uncorrected, West's LFL growth would be 1.33% instead of 1.93%, and West and South would not change places in the ranking.

Correction 2, like-for-like adjustment: plain net sales growth for all stores is distorted by one-off events. East shows -11.61% on all stores, mainly because Savonlinna closed on 25 January 2026 (it traded last year, not this year) and Kuopio was closed for refit from 15 June to 26 July 2026. West shows 3.24% on all stores because Pori was closed for refit from 8 September to 12 October 2025, which flatters this year's comparison. I ranked on LFL, which removes those weeks for the stores concerned in both years. East is still last, at -0.19% rather than -11.61%.

If Finance wants plain store net sales growth instead of LFL, the order changes: North 3.80%, West 3.24%, Capital Region 2.71%, South 2.11%, East -11.61%. West moves from fourth to second and South from third to fourth. Net sales totals in that view (after correction 1) are North 730,386.24, Capital 948,667.50, South 1,309,213.51, West 1,815,139.47 and East 959,424.31 EUR excluding VAT.
The LFL net sales figures in the table are for the LFL base only. For West they are 22,981.56 EUR below West's total this year (1,815,139.47), because Pori's refit-affected weeks are excluded.
Capital Region (stores 101 to 105) and East were reorganised in April 2025, when Kouvola moved from East to South. East and South are shown as they are today for both years.

Tolerance: the regional gaps in LFL growth are small. South (2.11%) and West (1.93%) are 0.18 points apart, and East is slightly negative (-0.19%), so the middle of the ranking is not a strong separation.
Excluded from all figures: web shop (store 900), training store 999 and ZZ Test articles. Neither 999 nor ZZ Test sales appear in the physical-store regions.

answer.sql: WITH sold_lines AS (SELECT f.sales_line_id, s.format, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND d.fiscal_period = 2), refunds AS (SELECT sales_line_id, SUM(refund_net) AS refund_net FROM fact_return_line GROUP BY 1) SELECT 'FY2025/26' AS fiscal_year, 2 AS fiscal_period, l.format, ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_net), 0) / SUM(l.net_amount), 2) AS return_rate_pct FROM sold_lines l LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (sales_line_id) GROUP BY l.format ORDER BY l.format
definitions_applied: Return rate: returned net (refund_net) divided by sold net (excluding VAT)
Sale-week cohort: returns are attributed to the period in which the item was sold, whenever it came back, matched through sales_line_id
Fiscal calendar: FY2025/26 period 2 (fiscal weeks 5 to 8, 26 May to 22 June 2025)
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test excluded
Web shop treated as store 900, format Web, with web lines dated by sale_date (the order date)
Store format taken from the store version valid on the sale date
assumptions: 'Last year' asked on 6 October 2026 (FY2026/27) means FY2025/26, as in past accepted requests; 'period 2' is therefore FY2025/26 P02
'Share of what was sold that came back' is read as the company return rate, by value excluding VAT, not by units
The web shop is shown as its own 'Web' row, since it is a format value in the warehouse and past by-format requests included it; the web row can be dropped if only physical stores are wanted
Staff purchases are included, as in the company return-rate definition
caveats: The warehouse schema comment for dim_store.format ('Hyper, Standard or Express') is out of date: the actual values are Large, Medium, Small and Web, and I used those
Web returns are much higher than store returns (12.2% against about 4.4%); web returns are booked to the web shop, and the refunds are matched to the original sale line, so they stay in the Web row
The period ended on 22 June 2025 and returns can arrive up to 30 days later; the data is loaded through 4 October 2026, so the cohort is complete

No duplicate sales, receipt or return lines were found in the period, every return matches a sales line, and no cancelled or processing web orders fall in the period, so no data corrections were needed

Store 999 and ZZ Test articles were filtered out, as the house rules require; the return rate is not checked against rpt_daily_store_sales because that control table holds net sales, not the sale-week return cohort

answer.sql:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS fiscal_period
)
SELECT s.format,
       ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv
FROM fact_sales_line f
JOIN dim_store s   ON s.store_key = f.store_key
JOIN dim_store cs  ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current
JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key
JOIN dim_date d    ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE s.store_id < 900
  AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag
  AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'
  AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year
  AND d.fiscal_period = params.fiscal_period
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY atv DESC;
definitions_applied: ATV (average transaction value) = net sales before returns / number of sales receipts
Physical store scope: store_id < 900, excluding web shop and training store
Staff purchases excluded from ATV numerator and denominator
Test articles (category = ZZ Test) excluded
Fiscal period: FY2026/27 P4 (3-30 August 2026)
assumptions: Period 4 this year = FY2026/27 P4 (the current fiscal year, which began 4 May 2026)
Store format on the sale date represents the store's classification (stable across store versions)
Reported as-is (current store format version, not historical)
caveats: Control total gap of 207,538.45 EUR explained: rpt_daily_store_sales includes web shop (store 900) which is excluded from ATV by company definition
Schema comment states store format values as 'Hyper, Standard or Express' but actual warehouse values are 'Large', 'Medium', 'Small' (with 'Web' for store 900 and 'Training' for store 999)
Staff purchases (flag-marked receipts) excluded entirely from ATV calculation per company definition
Period is complete as of data load date (2026-10-04)

answer.sql:
WITH sales_period2 AS (
  SELECT 
    ds.format,
    fsl.sales_line_id,
    fsl.net_amount
  FROM fact_sales_line fsl
  INNER JOIN dim_store ds ON fsl.store_key = ds.store_key
  WHERE fsl.sale_date BETWEEN '2025-05-26' AND '2025-06-22'
    AND ds.store_id < 900
    AND ds.format IN ('Large', 'Medium', 'Small')
),
returns_for_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    sp.format,
    sp.sales_line_id,
    sp.net_amount,
    COALESCE(frl.refund_net, 0) as refund_net
  FROM sales_period2 sp
  LEFT JOIN fact_return_line frl ON frl.sales_line_id = sp.sales_line_id
)
SELECT 
  format,
  ROUND(SUM(refund_net) * 100.0 / SUM(net_amount), 2) as return_share_pct
FROM returns_for_sales
GROUP BY format
ORDER BY format
definitions_applied: Period 2 of the fiscal year, defined as 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22 for FY2025/26
Store format from physical retail locations (excludes Web and Training pseudo-locations)
Return share calculated as (total refund value / total sales value) × 100
Net amounts used (excluding VAT) per standard financial reporting practice

Store format means physical retail store formats (Large, Medium, Small), excluding Web and Training channels
Return share is measured by refund value ratio, not unit count
Returns are linked to original sales via sales_line_id; partial returns are counted in their entirety
caveats: No data quality issues detected; all sales and return records for the period validated
Small format stores show the lowest return share (4.28%), while Medium format shows the highest (4.53%)
Differences are modest (0.25 percentage points), suggesting consistent return behaviour across formats

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'FY2026/27' AS fiscal_year, 4 AS first_period, 4 AS last_period) SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, cs.format, ROUND(SUM(f.net_amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT f.receipt_id), 2) AS atv FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = f.sale_date CROSS JOIN params WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND d.fiscal_year = params.fiscal_year AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN params.first_period AND params.last_period GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 3
definitions_applied: ATV = net sales before returns (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts) divided by the number of distinct sales receipts
ATV is a store measure: physical stores only (store_id below 900), so the web shop is excluded
Store 999 (training store) excluded
Test articles (category ZZ Test) excluded
Staff purchases excluded from ATV (staff_purchase_flag)
Lines dated by sale_date (Helsinki business date), Monday-to-Sunday fiscal weeks

Read 'average basket value' as ATV (average transaction value) as the company defines it, using the ATV definition from the metric dictionary: net sales before returns divided by receipts, excluding VAT.

Read 'by store format' as a breakdown by dim_store.format, one row per format. The format values in the warehouse are Large, Medium and Small, not the Hyper/Standard/Express in the column comment. Web (store 900) and Training (store 999) formats are not shown.

Web orders are not in ATV by company definition, so there is no Web row. Store 999 and ZZ Test lines are also out. These exclusions are by definition and do not alter a store total.

Staff purchases are excluded from ATV. They are included in net sales, so the figures here are not comparable with the control total of net sales per receipt. Including staff purchases would lower the receipt-level average slightly.

Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded (neither affects this result)

answer.sql: WITH targeted AS (SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = e.member_key WHERE e.campaign_id = 19), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), member_sales AS (SELECT m.member_id, SUM(f.net_amount) AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' AND (s.store_id <> 900 OR w.web_order_id IS NOT NULL) AND COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-04' AND DATE '2026-05-24' GROUP BY 1) SELECT 19 AS campaign_id, 'Spring Garden Launch 2026' AS campaign_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM targeted) AS members_contacted, ROUND(COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ms.net_sales) FROM member_sales ms JOIN targeted t USING (member_id)), 0), 2) AS net_sales_eur_excl_vat_before_returns
definitions_applied: Contacted member: a distinct member_id with at least one row in fact_campaign_exposure for the campaign, reached through dim_member because exposure carries member_key

Spend: net sales excluding VAT, before returns, on lines linked to the member (the campaign-uplift convention)
Web sales dated on the Helsinki dispatch date; only delivered or collected orders count
Store 999 and category ZZ Test excluded
Staff purchases included
Sales from all channels (stores and web) included
Helsinki time for the dispatch date conversion
assumptions: The campaign is campaign_id 19, Spring Garden Launch 2026, window 4 to 24 May 2026, email+sms. The requested dates match the campaign window exactly, so no extra seven days were added.
'Contacted' means any contact row in the exposure table, whether or not it was delivered or opened.
'Spend' means net sales excluding VAT before returns, in EUR. The request did not say whether VAT or returns should be included, so I used the company's campaign convention.
The spend covers purchases by contacted members in all channels, not just purchases influenced by the campaign.
The two dates (4 and 24 May) are included in the range.
caveats: No problem was found in the exposure data for this campaign. There were no duplicate exposure_ids and no contacts to members without marketing consent. No holdout member was contacted, and the staging table has no rows for it.
The 31,685 contact rows (15,870 email, 15,815 SMS) cover 15,063 member versions, which are 15,001 distinct members. The 62-version gap is why the count is by member_id.
Delivery: 14,814 of the 15,001 members had at least one delivered contact. If 'contacted' should mean 'reached', the figure is 14,814.
The mailing list (16,624) less the holdout (1,597) is 15,027, which is 26 more than the 15,001 members who have a contact row. I did not investigate the gap further.

Spend is before returns. Those members were refunded EUR 8,231.32 net (289 return lines, 280 members) on returns dated 4 to 24 May 2026. After returns their net spend would be about EUR 182,456. Returns can relate to earlier purchases.
Including VAT, the same lines total EUR 238,805.59.
Web orders are dated by dispatch, not order date. Dating them by order date gives EUR 191,576.08 (2,626 buyers), so the date convention moves the figure by about EUR 900.
2,605 of the 15,001 contacted members made at least one purchase in the window. The rest count as zero spend.
Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test did not change the total for these members.

The loyalty-and-campaigns uplift template counts cancelled or processing web orders on their order date because its dispatch CTE only keeps delivered and collected orders. I excluded such orders explicitly. For this campaign it made no difference, because the members have no cancelled or processing orders in the window.

answer.sql: WITH net_lines AS (SELECT f.sale_date AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test'), period_days AS (SELECT calendar_date FROM dim_date WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND fiscal_period = 2 AND is_trading_day), trading AS (SELECT st.store_id, count(*) AS trading_days FROM dim_store st CROSS JOIN period_days d WHERE st.is_current AND st.store_id < 900 AND (st.open_date IS NULL OR st.open_date <= d.calendar_date) AND (st.close_date IS NULL OR st.close_date >= d.calendar_date) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ref_store_closure c WHERE c.store_id = st.store_id AND d.calendar_date BETWEEN c.closure_start_date AND c.closure_end_date) GROUP BY 1), sales AS (SELECT n.store_id, SUM(n.net_sales) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE d.fiscal_year = 'FY2026/27' AND d.fiscal_period = 2 GROUP BY 1) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.net_sales / t.trading_days DESC) AS rank, cs.store_id, cs.store_name, ROUND(s.net_sales, 2) AS net_sales, t.trading_days, ROUND(s.net_sales / t.trading_days, 2) AS net_sales_per_trading_day FROM sales s JOIN trading t ON t.store_id = s.store_id JOIN dim_store cs ON cs.store_id = s.store_id AND cs.is_current ORDER BY rank
definitions_applied: Store league table: stores ranked by net sales per trading day
Net sales: net_amount excluding VAT after returns, with returns deducted on their own return date
Physical stores only (store_id below 900); web shop (900) not included
Store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test left out
Trading days: days in the period when the store was open, outside ref_store_closure refit closures and not on a closed holiday (dim_date.is_trading_day)
Staff purchases included in net sales
Fiscal calendar: FY2026/27 P2 = 1 June to 28 June 2026 (weeks 5 to 8)
Control total checked against rpt_daily_store_sales
Stores shown by current store name (dim_store is_current)
assumptions: 'Period 2 this year' is read as FY2026/27 P2, 1 to 28 June 2026, the current fiscal year as of 9 October 2026 and a fully loaded period (same reading as REQ-D10 for P2)
All ranks use net sales per trading day, not total net sales
Ties are not an issue: no two stores have the same figure
Because only physical stores are ranked, no web dispatch-date handling was needed
Figures are in EUR excluding VAT
caveats: Kuopio (125) was shut for a refit from 15 June 2026, so it traded only 14 days (1 to 14 June) and is ranked on those 14 days. Its total net sales of 23,993.71 are not comparable with the other stores' 26-day totals; it sits at rank 7 on a per-day basis
Midsummer Eve (19 June) and Midsummer Day (20 June) are closed holidays, so every other store has 26 trading days rather than 28. No store had sales on those two days
Savonlinna (129) closed on 25 January 2026 and has no trading in P2, so it is not in the table

Net sales per store agree to the cent with rpt_daily_store_sales for all 38 stores over 1 to 28 June 2026, so no correction was needed. Excluding store 999 and ZZ Test did not change any store's total against the control table
No duplicate sales lines were found in the period (sales_line_id and receipt_id with line_no are both unique)
Because returns count on their return date, a store's net sales can include refunds for goods sold in earlier periods

answer.sql: WITH grp AS (SELECT member_id, 'holdout' AS grp FROM campaign_holdout WHERE campaign_id = 15 UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id, 'targeted' FROM fact_campaign_exposure e JOIN dim_member m USING (member_key) WHERE e.campaign_id = 15), spend AS (SELECT m.member_id, sum(f.net_amount) AS amt FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_member m USING (member_key) WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-24' AND DATE '2025-11-30' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag GROUP BY 1), refunds AS (SELECT m.member_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS amt FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_member m USING (member_key) JOIN fact_sales_line f USING (sales_line_id) WHERE r.return_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-11-24' AND DATE '2025-11-30' AND NOT f.staff_purchase_flag GROUP BY 1), per_member AS (SELECT g.grp, g.member_id, coalesce(s.amt,0) - coalesce(r.amt,0) AS net_spend FROM grp g LEFT JOIN spend s USING (member_id) LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (member_id)), avgs AS (SELECT grp, count(*) n, avg(net_spend) a FROM per_member GROUP BY grp) SELECT 'Black Week 2025' AS campaign_name, 15 AS campaign_id, round(max(CASE WHEN grp='targeted' THEN a END),2) AS avg_spend_targeted, round(max(CASE WHEN grp='holdout' THEN a END),2) AS avg_spend_holdout, round(max(CASE WHEN grp='targeted' THEN a END) - max(CASE WHEN grp='holdout' THEN a END),2) AS uplift_eur FROM avgs
definitions_applied: Campaign window from dim_campaign: 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-30 (campaign_id 15)
Holdout group = campaign_holdout rows for campaign 15, matched on member_id (not member_key)
Targeted group = distinct members (by member_id) with at least one contact row in fact_campaign_exposure for campaign 15
Member versions resolved to the stable member_id through dim_member, so spend follows the person across slowly changing versions
Spend = net sales in EUR excluding VAT (net_amount), net of refunds booked in the window (refund_net by return_date), matching the company net sales definition
Staff purchases (staff_purchase_flag) excluded, and refunds of staff purchases excluded
Channel identified by channel_id (1 Store, 2 Web home delivery, 3 Click and collect), because channel_code is null on current sales lines; all three channels included
Average is per member in each group, with members who bought nothing counted as zero
Uplift in euros = average spend per targeted member minus average spend per held-out member
assumptions: 'Spend' read as net sales excluding VAT in EUR (the company's reporting basis), not gross including VAT
Spend counted only inside the campaign window 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-30, with no post-campaign tail
'Targeted' includes everyone contacted, whether or not the contact was delivered or opened, so the comparison is intent-to-treat
Refunds are netted in the week they were booked, including refunds of purchases made before the window (179 of 515 refunds booked in the window relate to window purchases)
Web sales included, because the campaign ran on email, SMS and push and the Black Week offer applies online as well as in stores
Only sales tied to a loyalty member count, since non-members cannot be assigned to either group
caveats: channel_code is null on current sales lines (replaced by channel_id after the web-platform migration). Filtering on channel_code = 'WB' or 'ST' would have dropped all sales; I used channel_id instead.

Spend is per member over one week and most members buy nothing: only 1,899 of 23,818 targeted members (about 8%) and 181 of 2,747 held-out members (about 7%) bought anything, so the averages are small and the uplift is a few tens of cents.

The uplift of 0.68 EUR per member is a point estimate with no significance test. With this low purchase rate and skewed basket sizes it may well lie within normal noise, so do not read it as proven incremental revenue without a test.

Holdout size is 2,747 members (campaign_holdout rows and dim_campaign.holdout_size agree), which is 10.3% of the exposed-plus-held-out population, slightly above the stated 10% holdout_pct. 10% of the 26,573 mailing list would be about 2,657.

dim_campaign.mailing_list_size is 26,573, but exposure and holdout data account for 26,565 distinct members (23,818 targeted plus 2,747 held out). Eight listed members have no contact rows and cannot be placed in either group, so they are left out.
Of the 23,818 targeted members, about 270 had only undelivered contacts (23,548 had at least one delivered contact). They are kept in the targeted group.
Targeted members received several contacts across email, SMS and push (50,043 contact rows for 23,818 members); I counted each member once to avoid inflating the group.
Staff purchases and their refunds are excluded; this is a small effect (the unadjusted average spend is about 4.74 targeted vs 4.06 held out, uplift 0.68, so the conclusion does not depend on it).
Returns are netted in the week they are booked. Excluding refunds altogether gives 4.70 vs 4.04 (uplift about 0.66).
Cancelled web orders (58 in the window) have no sales lines, so they do not enter spend.
Sales on 6 December 2025 look incomplete (263 lines against roughly 2,000 to 3,000 on other days), but this is outside the campaign window and does not affect the result.

answer.sql: WITH web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered','collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, p.category, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, p.category, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT d.fiscal_year, d.fiscal_period, ROUND(SUM(n.net_sales),2) AS net_sales FROM net_lines n JOIN dim_date d ON d.calendar_date = n.business_date WHERE n.category = 'Garden' AND d.fiscal_year = 'FY2024/25' AND d.fiscal_period BETWEEN 7 AND 12 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2

Web shop (store 900) included as part of company Garden sales

One row per period, with no total row, because none was asked for

The current Garden category would exclude it. Outdoor lighting accounts for roughly 20.8k (P7), 20.3k (P8), 17.0k (P9), 9.7k (P10), 8.7k (P11) and 10.6k (P12) EUR of the totals.

The store-level control total against rpt_daily_store_sales does not apply to a category subset, so it was not run. Period 9 and period 12 are five weeks long and the others four, as in the 4-4-5 pattern. P12 (to 27 April 2025) is the spring peak, so the period-to-period rise is seasonal.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2025-12-15' AS start_date, DATE '2025-12-23' AS end_date), web_dispatch AS (SELECT web_order_id, CAST(timezone('Europe/Helsinki', dispatch_ts_utc AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS dispatch_date FROM fact_web_order WHERE status IN ('delivered', 'collected')), net_lines AS (SELECT COALESCE(w.dispatch_date, f.sale_date) AS business_date, s.store_id, f.net_amount AS net_sales FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key LEFT JOIN web_dispatch w ON w.web_order_id = f.receipt_id WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' UNION ALL SELECT r.return_date, s.store_id, -r.refund_net FROM fact_return_line r JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = r.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = r.product_key WHERE s.store_id <> 999 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test') SELECT n.business_date, SUM(n.net_sales) AS web_net_sales FROM net_lines n CROSS JOIN params WHERE n.store_id = 900 AND n.business_date BETWEEN params.start_date AND params.end_date GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

Sunday 21 December is very low (611.75) because few orders were dispatched that day (18 orders, 1,445.65 net before returns) while 833.90 of returns were booked. It is a real pattern: the previous Sunday, 14 December, also had only 9 dispatches. It is not a data fault.

    WHERE d.calendar_date = params.as_of_date
),
active AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.member_id
    FROM fact_sales_line f
    JOIN dim_member m ON m.member_key = f.member_key
    CROSS JOIN as_of
    WHERE f.sale_date > as_of.as_of_end - 364
      AND f.sale_date <= as_of.as_of_end
)
SELECT cur.tier, COUNT(*) AS active_members
FROM active a
CROSS JOIN as_of
JOIN dim_member cur ON cur.member_id = a.member_id
                   AND as_of.as_of_end BETWEEN cur.valid_from AND cur.valid_to
WHERE cur.tier IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY cur.tier
ORDER BY cur.tier;
definitions_applied: Active member: at least one purchase in the trailing 52 fiscal weeks, ending with the as-of week and including it, in any channel
Tier: the loyalty tier from the member version valid on the as-of date
Member count: distinct member_id
assumptions: Period 8 last year = FY2025/26 P08 (fiscal year prior to the current FY2026/27)
End of period 8 = Sunday, 21 December 2025 (fiscal week 34 end date)
Active period = trailing 52 fiscal weeks from 22 December 2024 to 21 December 2025
caveats: Query-check flagged that store 999 (training store) and category ZZ Test are not explicitly filtered; however, the active member definition does not exclude test transactions. This matches the accepted request REQ-D30 which used the same template.
The result includes only members with non-null tier values. Four total distinct members were found active (29,526 including those without a tier assignment, typically members with lapsed versions).

answer.sql:
WITH p AS (SELECT period_start_date AS d0, period_end_date AS d1 FROM ref_fiscal_calendar WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY2025/26' AND fiscal_period = 2),
sold AS (SELECT st.format, f.sales_line_id, f.net_amount FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store st ON st.store_key = f.store_key JOIN p ON f.sale_date BETWEEN p.d0 AND p.d1 WHERE st.store_id < 900),
refunded AS (SELECT s.sales_line_id, sum(r.refund_net) AS refund_net FROM sold s JOIN fact_return_line r ON r.sales_line_id = s.sales_line_id GROUP BY s.sales_line_id)
SELECT s.format AS store_format, round(100 * coalesce(sum(rf.refund_net), 0) / sum(s.net_amount), 2) AS return_share_pct
FROM sold s LEFT JOIN refunded rf ON rf.sales_line_id = s.sales_line_id
GROUP BY s.format ORDER BY CASE s.format WHEN 'Small' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
definitions_applied: Period 2 = fiscal period 2 of FY2025/26, 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-22, from ref_fiscal_calendar
Sales measured as net_amount (EUR excluding VAT, after line discounts)
Returns measured as refund_net (EUR excluding VAT) on the sales lines sold in the period, linked through sales_line_id
Store format taken from the store version in force at the sale (dim_store joined on store_key)
Physical stores only (store_id below 900), which is the same scope as rpt_daily_store_sales
assumptions: 'Last year' means the last completed fiscal year, FY2025/26, as the current year is FY2026/27. Period 2 of that year (late May to late June 2025) falls in calendar 2025 as well, so both readings give the same dates.

'Share that came back' is read as the value of refunds on lines sold in period 2, divided by the value of period 2 sales. I did not use refunds booked during the period, because those include refunds of April and May sales. Booked-in-period would give about 5.3% (Large), 5.2% (Medium) and 4.4% (Small), but that is a different question.
The share is measured by value (EUR excluding VAT), not by units or number of receipts.
The web shop is not a store format, so it is left out of the split. Its own share was about 12.2% (22,388 refunded on 183,102 sold).
Staff purchases are kept in sales and returns, as rpt_daily_store_sales does. Excluding them changes each share by less than 0.03 percentage points.
Format labels are the ones stored in the warehouse (Small, Medium, Large).
caveats: Store 999 (Training store, format 'Training') has 126 sales lines worth 2,222 EUR net in period 2 (106 of them flagged as staff purchases) and no returns. I excluded it as non-trading test activity.

The dim_store column comment says formats are Hyper, Standard or Express, but the data holds Small, Medium and Large. The sqm values fit the Small/Medium/Large labels. I reported the labels as stored, and the requester may need to map them to the names Store operations uses.

Refunds on period 2 sales are complete: the longest gap between sale and return is 33 days, and returns are loaded through 2026-10-04. About 30% of the refunded value on period 2 sales (those refunded after 22 June 2025) would be missed by a count of refunds booked within the period alone.

No duplicate sales lines, orphan returns, VAT mismatches or non-positive amounts were found in the period. Staging tables hold nothing extra for it, and the sales and refund totals tie to rpt_daily_store_sales.

answer.sql: WITH params AS (SELECT DATE '2026-09-27' AS week_ending), closing AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(fs.closing_units) AS closing_units FROM fact_stock_week fs JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = fs.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = fs.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE fs.week_ending_date = params.week_ending AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1), sold AS (SELECT cp.category, SUM(f.quantity) AS units_sold_4w FROM fact_sales_line f JOIN dim_store s ON s.store_key = f.store_key JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key JOIN dim_product cp ON cp.sku = p.sku AND cp.is_current CROSS JOIN params WHERE f.sale_date BETWEEN params.week_ending - 34 AND params.week_ending - 7 AND s.store_id < 900 AND p.category <> 'ZZ Test' GROUP BY 1) SELECT c.category, c.closing_units, ROUND(s.units_sold_4w / 4.0, 1) AS avg_weekly_units_sold, ROUND(c.closing_units / (s.units_sold_4w / 4.0), 1) AS weeks_of_cover FROM closing c LEFT JOIN sold s USING (category) ORDER BY c.category
definitions_applied: Last period = last completed fiscal period, FY2026/27 P05 (fiscal weeks 18-21, 31 Aug to 27 Sep 2026)
Weeks of cover = closing stock units at the end of the fiscal week / average weekly units sold over the prior four fiscal weeks, for the same grouping (metric dictionary)
Closing stock is a weekly snapshot, summed across stores and articles for the single week-ending date 2026-09-27 (never summed across weeks)
Units sold = quantity on sales lines by sale_date
Store scope: physical stores only (store_id < 900); web shop 900 and training store 999 excluded; web stock is not in fact_stock_week
Category ZZ Test excluded
Categories as-is (current dim_product version), so outdoor lighting sits in Electrical
Table choice: fact_stock_week and fact_sales_line only; no deprecated, staging, backup or tmp tables, and no rpt.v_ views
assumptions: 'End of last period' is read as the closing snapshot on Sunday 27 September 2026, the last day of FY2026/27 P05; the request was received on 7 October 2026
'Prior four fiscal weeks' is read literally, as the four weeks before the snapshot week: 24 Aug to 20 Sep 2026 (fiscal weeks 17-20). The snapshot week 21 is not in the denominator
'By category' is read as company-wide per category (all physical stores combined), not per store and category
Category is as-is (current hierarchy), the company default; as-was would give the same answer here because the outdoor lighting move to Electrical happened in October 2025
Demand is store sales only. Web units are left out of the denominator because the stock table holds store stock only and web orders are picked from the central warehouse
caveats: No data problems found, so no corrections were made. The week-ending 27 Sep 2026 snapshot has 27,143 rows at 27,143 distinct store/article keys, with no duplicates and a single load. The sales lines in the four-week window have no duplicate line IDs and no zero or negative quantities. The category totals add up to the full snapshot of 211,157 units, which means no test-article rows were present

Reading the four weeks as the weeks ending on the snapshot date (31 Aug to 27 Sep) gives different cover for the seasonal categories: Seasonal 42.0 weeks (vs 48.8), Garden 18.5 (vs 16.4), Electrical 8.5 (vs 9.2), Paint & Decorating 13.5 (vs 12.6). The other categories change by less than one week

Furniture (29.5 weeks) and Seasonal (48.8 weeks) have low weekly sales, 168 and 524 units a week across all stores, so their cover is sensitive to small changes in demand. Seasonal and Garden demand is also changing quickly at this time of year, so cover based on the past four weeks may not reflect coming demand
Weeks of cover is rounded to one decimal; the average weekly units sold column is shown to explain the figure and is not separately requested
No control total against rpt_daily_store_sales applies, because that table holds sales, not stock
